map:donors.subsystem: Donor read handling: extract.rs, reference.rs, bam_stats.rs, read_name.rs, census.rs, and the parts of main.rs that wire them (windows, pool, census, duplicates, merge-by-name)
map:donors.summary: For each event, spike reads event ± --flank (default 10 kb, at least HAP_FLANK 2 kb) plus any --region window. It keeps a pair only when both mates pass every filter: primary, mapped, not a duplicate, not QC-fail, MAPQ at or above --min-mapq (20), proper pair (0x2), mate mapped, first or last segment, and a usable quality string. Pass 1 reads the window, chunked across threads for BAM. Pass 2 re-reads the window widened by max|TLEN|+200 (at least 1 kb) to find missing mates. Pairs are deduplicated by name; fewer than 30 stops the run. The pool then sets three things: the fragment-length CDF (|TLEN| between read length or 1 and 1500), the tiling depth (pool fragment depth in a 2 kb window at the first covered breakpoint, applied to the whole haplotype), and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD (worst 1 kb bin against that depth). Pairs fully inside event ± 2 kb are suppressed by copy; every other pool pair is passed through. merge.sh removes every pool name with `samtools view -N`. The census counts records over the event at any MAPQ that are not in the pool; it writes SIM_RESIST, warns above 0.10 and refuses above 0.5. In clean mode, duplicate families of removed pairs are found by their 5' ends and removed too. Library traits come from the first 50,000 primary non-duplicate records of the file: read length (the mode), the trimming verdict (share of full-length reads ending in A below 0.05), read-name shape, SM and bwa options. The quality model takes its own 20 × 50 kb index-placed sample through the same extraction filters. Contig names come from the FASTA .fai, and HLA names that contain colons are handled. CRAM is detected by extension, its index is pruned to the region, and records from other contigs are dropped. Measured here: in mappable windows 98–99% of non-duplicate reads are editable; the reads left out crash at 5–50%; learning only from pool reads lowers the crash share by about 4% among MAPQ≥20 reads.

algorithms.name: Record filter for donor material
algorithms.how: Drops a record that is unmapped, secondary, supplementary, a duplicate or QC-fail, or below min_mapq (missing MAPQ counts as 0). It also requires is_properly_segmented, a mapped mate, and first or last segment. The CRAM path also requires both mates on the queried contig. A pair enters the pool only when both mates' records pass.

algorithms.name: Two-pass pair extraction
algorithms.how: Pass 1 queries [start,end), chunked on the rayon pool for BAM (fold_bam_region gives each record to the chunk holding its start; there is one chunk per 100 kb at most, and one chunk per thread at most). It stores R1 and R2 partials in name-keyed HashMaps. Pass 2 re-queries the WHOLE window widened by max(max|TLEN|+200, 1000), in one sequential pass, and only completes pairs whose other mate pass 1 stored. Reverse-strand mates are reverse-complemented back to sequencing order. ref_start is min(pos), ref_end is ref_start+|TLEN| (positions + seq length when TLEN=0), and the compacted CIGAR is kept in MateAlignment.

algorithms.name: CRAM handling
algorithms.how: A file is CRAM when its path ends in '.cram'. The .crai entries are pruned to slices that intersect the region, so noodles does not decode every container on the chromosome (M15). Records from multi-contig slices are dropped by reference id (L2). A missing quality string shows up as an empty array when the sequence is not empty. noodles-cram 0.74 itself checks each slice's reference MD5 against the FASTA.

algorithms.name: Unusable-quality drop (M14)
algorithms.how: A record whose quality is all 0xFF or '*', or holds a byte above Q93, is left out of the pool and tallied by (name, mate). main adds those names to replaced_reads.txt, so merge.sh removes them without replacing them.

algorithms.name: Extraction windows and pool assembly
algorithms.how: Each event gets event ± flank, merged with --region only when the two overlap or touch (M8). A fusion gets both breakpoints ± flank and its pool chromosome is chrom_a. Pairs are deduplicated by name (first copy kept), MIN_DONOR_PAIRS=30 is enforced, and the pool is sorted by (ref_start, name) so the run is deterministic.

algorithms.name: Fragment length model
algorithms.how: An empirical CDF of the pool's |TLEN| within [min_fragment_len, 1500]. min_fragment_len is 1 for an adapter-trimmed library and read_length otherwise. With no usable sizes it falls back to N(400,80) clamped into the range.

algorithms.name: Coverage estimate for tiling
algorithms.how: Fragment depth from the pool, as the mean of up to 50 points over a 2 kb window, counting only pairs on the same chromosome (M9). It is taken at the first covered breakpoint side (or the SNV position). A single-locus event is refused only when no side is covered; a fusion needs every side covered. The tiling count is cov × VAF, spread uniformly over the haplotype.

algorithms.name: Depth fold (SIM_DEPTH_FOLD, CR2 option B)
algorithms.how: Each reference interval of a haplotype segment is cut into bins of about 1 kb. The fold is max((D+1)/(C+1), (C+1)/(D+1)) over the bins, with D the pool depth in the bin and C the anchor depth. It is measured only; a warning fires above 1.5.

algorithms.name: Suppression geometry
algorithms.how: Only pool pairs entirely inside the haplotype footprint (event ± 2 kb) can be suppressed, at copy_rate (phased by the LOH copies when available). All other pool pairs are kept, written to R1/R2.fq.gz and listed for removal by name.

algorithms.name: Resistant-read census (CR4/RF8)
algorithms.how: Counts primary, mapped, non-duplicate, non-QC-fail records at any MAPQ over the event's changed span: the DEL/DUP/INV span, the 2 bases around an INS point, the REF of a small variant, or the 2 bases around each fusion cut. A record is resistant when its name is not in the pool or the unusable-quality set (under origin, also not removable). The share goes into SIM_RESIST; spike warns above 0.10 and refuses above 0.5 unless --allow-resistant.

algorithms.name: Duplicate families of removed pairs (clean mode)
algorithms.how: Re-reads every extraction window ± MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN. A family is keyed by both mates' unclipped 5' ends. A pair flagged duplicate on both mates is removed when an unflagged pair in its family was removed and not written back.

algorithms.name: Library characterisation (bam_stats)
algorithms.how: Reads the first 50,000 primary, mapped, non-duplicate, non-QC-fail records from the HEAD of the file, with no MAPQ filter. cycles is the mode of SEQ length (a tie goes to the longer). adapter_trimmed means at least 1,000 full-length reads, of which under 5% end in A at the 3' end in sequencing orientation. A library is refused as single-end when no sampled record has 0x1. The scan also learns the read-name shape, picks SM from the first @RG that has one, and copies alignment options from the bwa @PG CL.

algorithms.name: Read naming
algorithms.how: Names are classed as 7-field, 5-field or other (Picard's tile/x/y rule), and the majority class wins. The most common RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE becomes the middle, with the tiles and x/y ranges seen alongside it. A synthetic read is named SPIKE_<internal>:<middle>:<tile>:<x>:<y>, with tile, x and y drawn from FNV+splitmix on the internal name, never from the RNG.

algorithms.name: Reference access and contig naming
algorithms.how: The .fai is looked up first as <stem>.fa.fai, then <path>.fai. A bgzip file that is not named .gz/.bgz is refused. Coordinates are read 0-based half-open and uppercased. SharedReference loads whole chromosomes, and fetches are silently clamped to the contig. split_contig matches the longest FASTA name followed by ':' (L13, HLA names). Events are validated against .fai lengths, and SNV REF against the reference.

algorithms.name: Startup quality sample
algorithms.how: Takes the 16 kb BAI leaf bins (or CRAI slices) that hold reads, and places 20 × 50 kb blocks at window floor((2k+1)W/40). It extracts them through extract_read_pairs (the same donor filters) and deduplicates by name.

algorithms.name: Merge by name
algorithms.how: merge.sh runs `samtools view -N replaced_reads.txt -U outside.bam` and checks ACTUAL >= NAMES. It then merges sim.bam (RG ID:sim SM:<sample> PL:ILLUMINA, no LB) with outside.bam and sorts. Removing by name also removes the secondary and supplementary records of every listed pair.

limitations.what: Selection bias: whatever fails the pool filter cannot be edited and stays as old-allele evidence. In mappable DNA this is small; at real SV sites in repeats it is large.
limitations.evidence: MEASURED on the 35x HG002 BAM, chr20:10,000,001-11,000,000, 131,744 primary non-dup R1: 98.86% pool-eligible, 0.71% mate on another chromosome, 0.25% mate unmapped, 0.12% with a low-MAPQ mate or own record, 0.06% same-chromosome |TLEN|>1000 (samtools view -F 0xF04 -f 0x41 | awk on flags/MQ). LDLR window chr19:11,080,001-11,140,000: 98.2% of non-dup primary records editable on the 35x BAM and 98.5% own-record-eligible on the hospital BAM D24-14230 (no MQ tag there). DOCUMENTED: 6 of 20 real HG002 deletions in validate_pipeline are above 0.5 resistant (case file, RF8); 0.93-0.95 at chr20:7119236.

limitations.what: Survivorship in what is learned: quality strings, error tables, the class mix and the fragment CDF all come only from pool-eligible pairs, and the excluded reads crash far more often. Effect on reads a caller sees at MAPQ≥20 is small (~4% relative).
limitations.evidence: MEASURED, 35x HG002 chr20:10-12 Mb, crash = >=10 of last 20 quals <Q15. Crash share by class: pool-eligible 0.80% (516,922 reads); own MAPQ<20 5.1%; not proper 11.1%; mate unmapped 9.1%; unmapped 49.9%; all non-dup primary 0.98%. Among all mapped MAPQ≥20 reads: crash 0.83% vs 0.80% pool, soft-clip 2.39% vs 2.31%; the non-pool 0.68% of reads crash at 5.4% and clip at 13.7%. DOCUMENTED (v2 plan K2b): spike is still ~15% short on crash within pool-eligible held-out pairs (0.90% vs 1.06%), so survivorship is not the main cause.

limitations.what: One anchor depth: pool fragment depth in 2 kb at the first breakpoint side scales a flat tiling over the whole haplotype. Local depth shape (GC, capture, mappability) is lost, and depth measured at a repeat breakpoint is depth after MAPQ filtering.
limitations.evidence: DOCUMENTED (REVIEW CR2): a het DUP over an 18.75x interior made 81.09x vs 28.13x expected; C4 fold across 40 real chr20 spans had median 1.27 and max 2.46, with 6/40 above 1.5. MEASURED here, LDLR chr19:11.08-11.14 Mb on 35x: pool fragment depth per 1 kb bin min 21.8 / p10 26.2 / median 31.9 / p90 37.2 / max 43.4, while pool/any-MAPQ proper-pair depth is ≥0.980 in every bin. At LDLR the variation is sampling noise plus GC, not mappability. INFERRED: an exome or panel BAM would get coverage islands from uniform tiling at a single anchor depth.

limitations.what: Pass 2 re-reads the WHOLE widened window, single-threaded (not chunked), when only two edge strips of about max|TLEN|+200 bp can hold missing mates. On multi-Mb events this is a serial floor under the threaded pass 1.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code: the pass 2 region is [start-pad, end+pad] (extract.rs:119-133, 454-465), and pass 1's union already covers every record overlapping [start,end). Scale reference: chr20:14.55-17.55 Mb holds 894,131 records (samtools view -c, 0.37 s with htslib). DOCUMENTED: the 3 Mb DEL takes 24.0 s at 1 thread and 9.9 s at 16 (README:1358).

limitations.what: Each event's region is read about 6 times: pass 1, pass 2, the LOH pileup and its phasing pass, the census over the span, and the clean-mode duplicate scan (windows ± 1.5 kb). The pool already holds seq and CIGAR for most of the data these passes need.
limitations.evidence: DOCUMENTED: the duplicate re-read alone costs 5-6 s at 1 thread (2.5-3 s at 4) on a 3 Mb event (README:1365). INFERRED: the other passes from code (loh.rs:176-220 count_alleles, census.rs:109-171, main.rs:919-932).

limitations.what: bam_stats learns read length, trimming verdict and name shape from the head of a coordinate-sorted file: one subtelomeric, mostly low-MAPQ locus. The verdicts hold on the BAMs tested, but the A share depends on base composition. A mixed-length library (multiple runs, or R1 and R2 of different length, review finding 6) is reduced to one mode, and quality-trimmed (not adapter-trimmed) libraries are not modelled.
limitations.evidence: MEASURED on the 35x BAM: the first 50,000 primary non-dup records span chr1:9,996-183,555 and 79.8% have MAPQ<20. All are 151 bp. The 3' A share is 0.258 at the head vs 0.314 in chr20:30-31 Mb, both far above the 0.05 cut. Hospital LDLR: mode 151, but only 65% of reads are 151 (trimmed library). INFERRED: the mixed-length and quality-trimming cases.

limitations.what: Untrimmed libraries: fragments shorter than a read are left out of the fragment model (min = read_length), so synthetic reads never show adapter read-through or the soft clips it causes.
limitations.evidence: MEASURED: on the untrimmed 35x BAM, chr20:10-11 Mb, 1,083 of 130,401 proper R1 pairs (0.83%) have |TLEN|<151. DOCUMENTED: adapter read-through is 0.48% of reads and about 26% of real soft clips (case file 2026-10-06; soft-clip-causes memory). The hospital library is sequencer-trimmed, so it is not affected (read-length-fix memory).

limitations.what: No check that the BAM was aligned to the given FASTA: @SQ LN and M5 are never compared with the .fai. A same-named wrong build (BAM path) would run silently; only SNV REF validation and odd error tables would hint at it. CRAM is protected by noodles' slice MD5 check.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code: grep finds no comparison of @SQ lengths against the .fai, and the only header reads are names, @RG and @PG. MEASURED: the 35x BAM @SQ lines carry no M5 (samtools view -H), so only LN could be compared there.

limitations.what: read_fai first tries <stem>.fa.fai, so for genome.fasta it would use a genome.fa.fai belonging to another FASTA in the same directory. The CRAM repository instead uses noodles' <path>.fai, so one run can open two different indexes.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code (Path::with_extension replaces the last extension).

limitations.what: SharedReference::load holds two copies of every loaded chromosome until it returns: ReferenceReader's FIFO cache (256 entries) stores a clone of each whole-chromosome fetch. Peak memory is about 2x the loaded sequence (~6 GB for a genome-wide VCF).
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code: fetch_sequence inserts seq.clone() into the cache, and load keeps one reader across the whole loop.

limitations.what: The main run never checks that the input is duplicate-marked. On an unmarked BAM, PCR duplicates enter the pool as independent fragments: cov includes them, synthetic reads are made without them, and family members are suppressed independently. After downstream re-marking, the alt allele would be over-represented by about the duplication rate.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code: no markdup or dup-flag detection exists in main.rs, bam_stats.rs or extract.rs (grep), while validate.rs has one (DOCUMENTED, REVIEW L15). MEASURED duplicate rates: 12.9% of primary records in the 35x LDLR window, 3.8% on the hospital BAM.

limitations.what: Synthetic reads carry no PCR or optical duplicates, so spiked regions have a lower raw duplicate share.
limitations.evidence: DOCUMENTED (duplicates memory, K-run): 0.008 duplicate share in spiked regions vs 0.036 real. Callers skip duplicates, so raw-count CNV tools are the ones exposed.

limitations.what: BAM route: about 94% of R1.fq.gz is passthrough originals from event ± 10 kb. They are realigned by align.sh into RG ID:sim, which has no LB, so their read group changes and their alignment may change far beyond the 2 kb footprint. If the input carries LB, Picard re-marking would treat them and their flagged copies as different libraries.
limitations.evidence: DOCUMENTED: a 10 kb DEL wrote 13,800 unchanged originals vs 815 new pairs (REVIEW.md:359). MEASURED headers: the 35x BAM @RG has LB:HG002; the hospital @RG has no LB. INFERRED: the Picard behaviour. The FASTQ route is not affected: kept originals stay raw.

limitations.what: RF8's refusal text recommends lowering --min-mapq. In a segmental duplication, clean mode at MAPQ 0 removes the MAPQ-0 reads placed at the event, while the paralog keeps its half of the event copy's molecules. A hom DEL in a 2-copy segdup would read about CN0 at the event and 100% at the paralog, where reality is about 50% at each.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from the clean suppression logic. DOCUMENTED: origin mode exists for exactly this (edit-model-origin memory: physics SUPPORTED).

limitations.what: Huge events: the pool and the pass 1 maps grow linearly with event size and depth, and there is no size cap or warning.
limitations.evidence: DOCUMENTED: a 3 Mb DEL peaks at 1231/1380/1711 MB and a 3 Mb DUP at 1493/1787/2028 MB at 1/4/8 threads (README:1358-1360). INFERRED: about 10 GB for a 20 Mb event by linear extrapolation.

limitations.what: The pool assumes the aligner sets 0x2 and that MAPQ means what bwa's does. A BAM with 0x2 never set yields an empty pool, and the MIN_DONOR_PAIRS error names coverage, --region, MAPQ and quality but not the proper-pair flag. --min-mapq 20 is not calibrated for aligners with other MAPQ scales.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code. DOCUMENTED: bam_stats accepts a BAM whose pairs are all improper (test_paired_bam_without_proper_pairs_is_not_mistaken_for_single_end).

limitations.what: Synthetic pairs never have a mate on another chromosome or a large-insert mate, while real libraries carry this chimeric background. The original background stays untouched, so the alt-haplotype molecules are slightly cleaner than real ones.
limitations.evidence: MEASURED: 0.71% of non-dup R1 in chr20:10-11 Mb have a mate on another chromosome and 0.06% have |TLEN|>1000. Proper-pair max |TLEN| is 1,227, so MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN 1500 never binds.

limitations.what: Read names are assumed unique per template across the whole BAM. The pass 1 maps, dedup_pairs_by_name, duplicates_of and `samtools view -N` all key on QNAME alone, so renumbered names that collide across read groups would mis-pair mates and remove extra records.
limitations.evidence: INFERRED from code (SAM-spec assumption; no check).

open_issues: Pass 2 edge strips. Query only [start-pad, start) and [end, end+pad), or each stored partial's own mate position, instead of the whole widened window. Falsifier: byte-identical R1/R2/truth.vcf/replaced_reads on the 15 identity sets plus a time drop on the 3 Mb DEL/DUP at t8/t16. If the time does not move, pass 2 was not the serial floor.

One streaming pass per event. Collect pool pairs, census counts, dup-family records and LOH allele counts in a single read of window ± 1.5 kb, instead of about 6 re-reads. Falsifier: byte-identical outputs; the documented 5-6 s duplicate re-read on 3 Mb should disappear. Care point: the LOH pileup's filter is per record, not per pair.

Anchor vs footprint-wide depth (a cheap step toward CR2 option A, which stays open). Score the anchor estimator against the median of the 1 kb pool-depth bins depth_fold already computes. Falsifier: on CR2's 40 seeded spans (scripts/cr4_placements.py), the across-event spread of realised event-average depth ratio against 1+VAF should shrink. Units rule from the case file: both estimators are pool fragment depth.

Refuse a BAM/FASTA build mismatch. Compare @SQ LN (and M5 when present) with the .fai for every event contig, before extraction. Falsifier: a reheadered or other-build BAM must be refused; the 35x, hospital and NA18488 backgrounds must pass.

Warn on unmarked input. Reuse validate.rs's L15 logic (dup flags plus a markdup @PG) in the main run. Falsifier for the harm: plant the same het SNVs on the 35x BAM and on a `samtools view --remove-flags 1024` copy, re-mark with Picard, and compare realised VAF. The prediction is a rise of about the dup rate (12.9% there) on the unmarked copy.

Adapter read-through for untrimmed libraries. Admit fragments shorter than a read and append the adapter (AGATCGGAAGAGC...) as the sequencer reads it. Falsifier: the adapter-clip share after bwa-mem2 on the untrimmed 35x BAM against real (documented 0.48% of reads). The user leans to modelling bad ends only, so ask first.

RF8 message. The clean-mode suggestion to lower --min-mapq is probably wrong inside segdups (it over-deletes at the placement, see limitations). Consider pointing at --edit-model origin instead. Falsifier: a hom DEL in a 2-copy segdup with clean at --min-mapq 0, against origin, against the expected ~50/50 MAPQ-0 depth.

BAM route seam. Consider leaving pool pairs entirely outside the 2 kb footprint in the BAM (not listed, not realigned), and copy LB into align.sh's @RG. Falsifier: merged.bam records outside the footprint become identical to the original; count Picard re-mark flips at het SNVs on the 35x BAM (LB:HG002) before and after.

Synthetic duplicates (open since the duplicates run). Draw family sizes from the pool's own duplicate-family distribution, with optical copies at a nearby tile and x/y. Falsifier: the spiked-region duplicate share (0.008) should approach the real 0.036 without moving MarkDuplicates-filtered VAF.
ReferenceReader cache. Do not cache whole-chromosome fetches in SharedReference::load (or drop the clone). Falsifier: peak RSS on a multi-chromosome VCF run halves, with byte-identical output.
read_fai lookup order. Prefer <path>.fai and only then <stem>.fa.fai, matching what noodles uses for CRAM.
Exome or panel input. Uniform tiling at one anchor depth would create coverage islands. Either document it as unsupported or gate it on SIM_DEPTH_FOLD.
refuted_or_done: DONE M5: merge.sh removes originals by name (samtools view -N) instead of by region. In-BED records lost went from 13.7% to 0%, and the merged BAM keeps a single SM (REVIEW.md).
DONE M8: --region and event windows are merged only when they overlap or touch; M9: windows deduplicated by name and coverage made chromosome-aware.

DONE M14: records with unusable quality are dropped from the pool and removed by name; M15: the CRAM .crai is pruned to the region; L2: CRAM reads from foreign contigs are dropped; L13: HLA contig names that contain colons; L19: single-end input detected from flag 0x1 with the scan capped; N6: bam_stats' unused insert-size and coverage estimates removed.
DONE CR8: unmatched R1 reads are kept for pass 2 (extract.rs:98-104). CR-FRAG: the fragment model is limited to the range the generator samples.
DONE CR4 option B: resistant census, SIM_RESIST, warning above 0.10. RF8: refusal above 0.5 with --allow-resistant. Measure-and-warn only; which reads get edited is unchanged.
DONE CR2 option B: SIM_DEPTH_FOLD with a warning above 1.5. CR2 option A (a learned fragment-start intensity) is still OPEN and was never built.
REFUTED/RETRACTED T3: 'mappability dominates 5 of 6 depth-fold warnings' became 3 of 6 at --min-mapq 0, inconclusive (case file 2026-09-26). The lesson: thresholds and units must match.

REFUTED as a blanket warning, T7/CR3 option B: a footprint scan for the sample's own non-SNP variants fires on 38 of 40 footprints. The CR3 fail-closed part for --gvcf is done; the indel model is open.
DONE duplicates (clean mode): duplicates of removed pairs are removed with them. Old-allele reads at hom SNVs went from 3.4% to 0 (duplicates memory). Synthetic reads still have no duplicates (open).
DONE read length and trimming (master 3684f74, K1 pass); read names in the input's Illumina shape (master 50c75b6, K1/K1b/K2 supported); align.sh copies the bwa @PG options (master 97aa3b4).

REFUTED quality model v1 (bccc43a: one event's pool of ~2,800 pairs is too thin). v2, learned from a 20-block startup sample, was merged locally (7f28bb0) and is still ~15% short on crash. Copying whole quality strings (quality-tails, de806dd) was refuted as a fix for soft clips.

MEASURED here, new: learning only from the pool explains about 4% relative of the crash and soft-clip gap among MAPQ≥20 reads (0.83% vs 0.80% crash; 2.39% vs 2.31% clip; chr20:10-12 Mb, 35x). It is not the main cause of the documented 15% crash shortfall, which K2b already shows within pool-eligible pairs.

map:events.subsystem: Event model and haplotype editing (simulate.rs, haplotype.rs, origin.rs, loh.rs, carried.rs, exon.rs, vcf_input.rs, types.rs, plus the parts of main.rs, synth.rs, census.rs and truth.rs these call)
map:events.summary: Each event becomes one linear VariantHaplotype: an ordered list of segments, each from the reference (possibly reverse-complemented) or novel sequence, with a fixed 2 kb reference flank on each side (HAP_FLANK, main.rs:241). Junctions are segment boundaries, so read pairs tiled across the haplotype become split or discordant on their own. Before tiling, loh::sample_copies finds the sample's SNPs over the footprint (by pileup, or from --gvcf), phases the het SNPs into blocks, and flips one coin per block to pick the event copy. The haplotype then takes that copy's alleles (SNPs only). Above VAF 0.5, a second haplotype takes the other copy's alleles. In clean mode (the default), donor-pool pairs lying wholly inside the footprint are removed per copy: min(1,2v) on the event copy, max(0,2v−1) on the other, v when the copy is unknown. The same number is then tiled back uniformly as n = cov·v·starts/f, with one coverage taken from the first breakpoint. Fusions and legacy junction DUPs are additive: they keep every original and tile only across breakpoints, n = cov·v/(1−v). Under --edit-model origin, every primary read at the spot and at its XA look-alikes gets p_origin × copy_rate, and one draw is made per duplicate family. Before any event runs, three guards apply. Carried small alleles are refused (≥10 reads and ≥20% carrying another allele). SIM_RESIST above 0.5 is refused (RF8). Event footprints closer than 7 kb are refused (CR1). The truth GT comes from VAF alone. The design is general and honest about its limits, and validation supports it for DELs and SNVs/small indels. The biggest gaps are in what happens around the edit. Every event remakes ±2 kb of the event copy. That erases the sample's own indels and SVs there, because only SNPs are carried over (CR3). It also drops duplicates and the local depth pattern. For an SNV, about 88% of the remade pairs never touch the variant (inferred). Beyond that, insertions use iid random sequence, there is no ploidy, cis/trans is not controlled, exon specs put breakpoints exactly at exon edges, and there are no complex events, STR expansions or MEIs.

algorithms.name: Event parsing (CLI specs)
algorithms.how: del/dup/inv by coordinates (start used as the 0-based start, VCF-style) or by exon range. An exon range spans min(exon start) to max(exon end) of the affected exons, so breakpoints sit exactly on exon edges. Fusion breakpoints are an exon end and an exon start, and the join (Forward/LeftLeft/RightRight) is inferred from exon-number order. ins takes a length (random sequence) or explicit bases. snp takes 1-based REF/ALT (any SNV/MNV/indel/delins). af= takes a number, het (exactly 0.5) or hom (1.0).

algorithms.name: VCF ingest
algorithms.how: Records with one ALT only (multi-allelic records are dropped). The SVTYPE base type decides the event: DEL and INS take any subtype (INS:ME:* only for shape), DUP takes bare or :TANDEM only, plus INV and BND. Records with no SVTYPE and DNA alleles become SmallVariant. A DEL/DUP/INV span comes from END, then SVLEN, then the alleles. A sequence-resolved INS is trimmed to the bases it adds. BND mates are paired by MATEID into one Fusion. VAF comes from SIM_VAF, then VAF, then AF only with --vcf-info-af. GT and FILTER are counted, never used.

algorithms.name: Haplotype constructors
algorithms.how: DEL = left|right. Full DUP = left|copy|copy|right. Junction DUP = ref[E-F..E]|ref[S..S+F]. INV = left|revcomp|right. INS = left|novel|right. Fusion = one piece from each partner, one reverse-complemented for LeftLeft/RightRight. Small variant = left|ALT|right, where the ALT segment keeps a reference origin only when REF and ALT have equal length. junctions() keeps only boundaries where the reference does not continue straight on.

algorithms.name: Sample copies and phasing (LOH)
algorithms.how: Pileup SNP calls need ≥10 reads: het when the top two alleles are each 20-80%, hom-alt when one allele is ≥90% and differs from the reference. The gVCF path takes biallelic SNPs with GT/PS, and a het SNP inside a carried deletion is folded to hom-alt. A second BAM pass collects each fragment's alleles at the het SNPs. Phasing is union-find with parity over cis/trans votes, where gVCF PS links weigh 1e6. One coin per block picks the event copy. Each fragment is classified by majority vote (ties are left unknown). apply_variants writes single-base alleles into the segments (complemented in reversed segments). own_bases keeps the sample's alleles off a small variant's own REF span.

algorithms.name: Copy-aware suppression (clean)
algorithms.how: Only donor-pool pairs are candidates: proper pairs, both mates at --min-mapq or above, not duplicate/secondary/supplementary/QC-fail. A pair is removed only if it lies wholly inside the haplotype's ref_range. The removal rate is copy_rate(copy, v), which averages v over the two copies. Pairs that overlap the footprint edge are kept, and the synthetic taper matches them.

algorithms.name: Tiling count and placement
algorithms.how: Non-additive events: n = round(cov·v·(L − f − novel_only)/f), floored at 2 (SIM_VAF records a raised count). Starts are uniform over the starts whose fragment overlaps reference, so no fragment ever lies wholly inside novel sequence. Additive events: n = cov·v/(1−v) per breakpoint, with v capped at 0.95, and every start is drawn so the fragment crosses a breakpoint. cov is the pool's fragment depth in a 2 kb window at the first covered breakpoint side. Above VAF 0.5, a fragment comes from the other-copy haplotype with probability 1 − 1/(2v).

algorithms.name: Coverage guards and depth fold
algorithms.how: A fusion needs donor coverage on every breakpoint side. Other events need it on any one side, and the bare sides are reported. SIM_DEPTH_FOLD is the worst 1 kb bin's (D+1)/(C+1) against the single scaling depth. It is measured only and changes nothing.

algorithms.name: Planted-evidence count (SIM_ALT_FRAGS)
algorithms.how: Small variant: a mate must cover the changed ALT bases plus one base on each side. SV: the fragment must cover the base on each side of a real junction.

algorithms.name: Legacy junction-DUP depth copies
algorithms.how: For each pool pair at least 50% inside the DUP, a copy is made at copy_rate. Its start is the original start jittered ±20 bp, it gets a new fragment length, and its sequence comes from the reference plus the copy's SNP alleles.

algorithms.name: --edit-model origin
algorithms.how: p_here = 1 − 10^(−MAPQ/10). At MAPQ 0 it is 1/(1+n_XA), or 1/6 when there is no XA. The rest is split evenly over the XA hits. p_origin is the surest mate's placement sum inside the footprint. Look-alike regions are XA hits outside the footprint, merged within 1 kb, kept when at least 2 reads point there, and padded by one read length. A fragment is removable (R4) only when every mate has a placement inside the footprint. The removal chance is p_origin × copy_rate, where copy uses the family's phase call at the spot and is unknown at look-alikes. Chances are summed over events and capped at 1, with one draw per duplicate family. Origin depth, in fragment units through f = span/bases, replaces pool depth.

algorithms.name: Refusals and guards before simulation
algorithms.how: Carried small allele: refused when ≥10 spanning reads and ≥20% carry any non-reference allele, all such events listed in one error. Overlap: footprints of span ± 3500 bp must not intersect, so spans need at least 7 kb between them. RF8: refused when SIM_RESIST (the share of primary reads at any MAPQ over the census span that are not editable) is above 0.5, unless --allow-resistant. The donor pool needs at least 30 pairs.

algorithms.name: Combining events and the truth record
algorithms.how: An original suppressed by any event is dropped. Synthetic sets from different events are concatenated, with no composition between them. Clean also removes the duplicates of removed originals. The truth GT is 1/1 when VAF ≥ 0.9 and 0/1 otherwise, unphased. The phase choice is not written anywhere.

limitations.what: The sample's own indels, SVs and STR alleles are erased on the remade event copy. SampleCopies is one base per position (HashMap<u64,u8>), and the gVCF path keeps SNPs only. So within ±2 kb of every event, a het indel on the event copy disappears (half the time), and a hom indel becomes about (1−v) ALT.
limitations.evidence: Measured by me: of 2,000 random small-variant footprints (pos ± 2 kb) inside HG002's v5.0q small-variant benchmark on chr20, 978 (48.9%) hold a carried het non-SNP and 546 (27.3%) a carried hom non-SNP in GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1_chr20.vcf.gz, mean 1.54 per window (scratchpad evmodel/foot.py). Documented: the CR3 probe (a hom 2 bp DEL under a het DUP) went from AF 1.0 to 0.360, and T7 found 38/40 chr20 10 kb footprints with a carried non-SNP (docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR3/T7). The effect on raredisease calls (GT flips of nearby background indels) has not been measured.

limitations.what: Collateral remake. Every event removes and re-synthesises the whole 2 kb flank on each side, even for an SNV. The remade pairs lose the originals' real quality strings and errors, their duplicates (clean removes the dup copies and spike emits none) and the local depth pattern, and they carry the SPIKE_ names. Only fragments that overlap the changed bases need to differ.
limitations.evidence: Arithmetic from simulate.rs:817 with HAP_FLANK 2000, mean fragment 421 bp (README:1856) and 150 bp reads: L = 4001, starts = 3580. About 11.8% of the remade fragments for an SNV overlap the site and about 8.4% show it in a read, so roughly 88-92% are remade without touching the variant. Documented: 'no duplicates among spike reads' is open (memory realism-inspection-20261006.md, item C). Astra's point (c): replacing half the reads in the ±2 kb window with uniform ones flattens half of the local depth pattern (memory validation-plan.md).

limitations.what: One depth for the whole event, and uniform placement. The interior depth of a DUP follows the anchor's depth, not the local depth.
limitations.evidence: Documented. The CR2 probe gave 81.09x where the expected value is 28.13x. On 40 chr20 10 kb DUPs the fold was 1.11-2.46 (median 1.27), and 6 of 40 were above 1.5. T3 (whether mappability is the cause) is inconclusive: 3 of 6 still warn at --min-mapq 0 (README:1860-1866; CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR2/T3).

limitations.what: Exon-spec events put their breakpoints exactly on exon edges, in unique sequence. Real exon DEL/DUP breakpoints lie in introns, often in Alus, which makes exon-spec events systematically easier to call than real ones (and less often refused by RF8). Exon-spec fusions likewise join an exon end straight to an exon start: an RNA-like junction at DNA level.
limitations.evidence: Measured by me: 0 of 36 LDLR exon edges (data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed) lie inside an Alu (UCSC rmsk, cnv_validation/resources/mobile_elements/rmsk.txt.gz). Of the 62 ends of 31 ClinVar pathogenic LDLR DELs ≥50 bp (cnv_validation/resources/clinical/clinvar_pathogenic_sv_ge50.bed), 19 lie inside an Alu. Only 3 of those 62 ends sit exactly on an exon edge, and 1 of 31 has both ends there; the median distance to the nearest edge is 75.5 bp (scratchpad evmodel/ldlr_bp.py). Caveat: some ClinVar coordinates are imprecise.

limitations.what: Inserted sequence is unrealistic. A length-only INS, or a symbolic <INS>/<INS:ME:ALU> from a VCF, gets iid uniform ACGT: no tandem-repeat structure, no MEI, no poly-A tail, no target-site duplication. Real ≥50 bp insertions are mostly tandem-repeat expansions plus MEIs, whose reads map to other copies at MAPQ 0, which is the evidence RetroSeq and Manta use.
limitations.evidence: Measured by me on HG002 Q100 chr20 carried INS ≥50 bp: 630 of 765 sit in or next to a tandem repeat (the TR BED covers 7.4% of chr20). 36 of 765 are at least 50% mobile-element 13-mers (Alu 25, L1 11), and 17 of 765 have a poly-A/T run of 10 or more at one end. Spike-style random sequence of the same lengths: 0 ME and 0 poly-A (scratchpad evmodel/sv_shape.py, mei.py). Documented: a real AluY insertion in the hospital BAM had 14 of 15 mates placed on other contigs at MAPQ 0 (cnv_validation/analytical_performance_report_sv.md:382).

limitations.what: No fragment is ever placed wholly inside novel sequence, and those starts are left out of the count. Long insertions therefore lack their internal read pairs. For STR expansions longer than a fragment, that removes the in-repeat read pairs ExpansionHunter relies on (raredisease runs ExpansionHunter/stranger), and the full FASTQ lacks the unmapped or elsewhere-mapping pairs a real insertion yields.
limitations.evidence: Read from the code: novel_only starts are subtracted from the count, and sample_ref_overlapping_start excludes them. That the hospital uses ExpansionHunter/stranger is documented in cnv_validation/config/config.yaml:177. The effect on ExpansionHunter has not been measured.

limitations.what: Junctions are blunt cuts at the stated coordinates. Junction microhomology and repeat context are realistic only when the coordinates come from a real event. A DEL/DUP/INV record carrying END or SVLEN silently drops any inserted junction bases in a sequence-resolved ALT (a delins).
limitations.evidence: Measured by me. HG002 Q100 chr20 carried pure DELs ≥50 bp: 372 of 442 have at least 2 bp of junction homology, 51 are blunt, median 16 bp, and 367 of 442 have an end in a tandem repeat. 442 random-position chr20 DELs of 50-5000 bp: 80 have at least 2 bp, 238 are blunt, median 0 (scratchpad evmodel/sv_shape.py, randdel.py). That the delins bases are dropped is read from the code; Q100 had 0 such ≥50 bp records, so it was not measured.

limitations.what: No ploidy or sex-chromosome model, and input GT is ignored. On male non-PAR X/Y the default af 0.5 gives a half-depth, mosaic-like event recorded as GT 0/1. af=hom writes diploid 1/1. A VCF GT=1/1 is simulated at --allele-fraction (default 0.5). FILTER and hom-ref records are simulated too.
limitations.evidence: grep -i 'chrX|chrY|ploidy|hemizyg|haploid' finds 0 hits in src/ and README. CR7(a) measured GT=1/1 → SIM_VAF 0.500 and GT 0/1; CR7(b) is the ploidy finding (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR7).

limitations.what: Compound and complex events. Two events closer than 7 kb are refused, so a compound-het pair inside one exon or gene region cannot be built. With --allow-overlap, each event is simulated against the original donor and the synthetic sets add up. If both coins pick the same copy, the overlap reaches about 1+v depth and each ALT drops to about v/(1+v), with no read carrying both. Events further apart flip independent coins per phase block, even inside one gVCF PS, so cis/trans is random and is not recorded (the truth GT is unphased). Not supported at all: DEL-INV, inverted or dispersed DUPs, CPX records, CNV SVTYPE, multi-allelic records, CN≥4 per haplotype (a tandem DUP is exactly one extra copy), copy-neutral LOH/UPD events, and trio-consistent (inherited/de novo) spikes.
limitations.where: src/main.rs:1088-1188, 1248-1292; src/simulate.rs:410-428; src/loh.rs:924-941; src/truth.rs:468-474; src/vcf_input.rs:221-224, 870-883; src/haplotype.rs:216-276
limitations.evidence: Depth and VAF in an overlap are inferred from the code paths. The refusal and the 7 kb rule are documented (README:1603, CR1). The phase coin per call is confirmed in code (memory validation-plan.md, Astra point (b)).

limitations.what: Fusions are additive, and so is the legacy junction DUP. Each adds about cov·v/(1−v) junction fragments on top of every original, giving a depth bump at the junction (about 2x at v=0.5), with no reciprocal join and no copy-number conservation.
limitations.evidence: Documented: CR6, 'C junction fragments added on top of C retained originals' (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR6; README:1788-1798).

limitations.what: Reads in look-alikes and low-MAPQ reads resist clean edits. RF8 refuses real SV sites in repeats. origin is validated only in the exact-twin, one-XA-hit regime.
limitations.evidence: Documented. 6 of 20 pipeline HG002 DELs have SIM_RESIST above 0.5 (memory rf8-refusal.md). The transplant run refused 13 of 300 events forward and 17 of 300 reverse (memory validation-plan.md). On the origin physics gate, L was 0.739 and P 0.763, inside the bands; at the RF14 look-alikes origin removed 0 fragments (R4 kept 25 of 52; memory edit-model-origin.md).

limitations.what: Phase blocks get independent coins. With short-read phasing only, a multi-block event copy is a mosaic of both haplotypes. That is invisible to a single-sample caller but inconsistent for trio, UPD or long-range phasing. Pileup het calls (20-80%, MAPQ≥20) are the only phase source unless a phased gVCF is supplied.
limitations.evidence: Read from the code. No trio or UPD consequence has been measured.

limitations.what: ref_range() takes min and max over all reference segments regardless of chromosome. That is harmless today, because only additive fusions span two chromosomes, but it blocks any multi-chromosome non-additive (complex or balanced) event from reusing the suppress-and-tile path.
limitations.evidence: Read from the code.

limitations.what: At very low VAF the floor of 2 tiled fragments overstates the planted fraction, and a planted event can have no supporting read at all.
limitations.evidence: Documented: low-AF table on 20 hospital sites, AF 0.001 gives 16 of 20 sites with 0 ALT reads, and AF 0.05 gives 2 of 20. SIM_ALT_FRAGS and SIM_VAF now record this (memory independent-review-20261004.md).

open_issues: P1 (highest leverage, new mechanism): a minimal edit that keeps positions. Remake only the event-copy fragments that overlap the changed bases or junction, instead of the whole ±2 kb. Each replacement keeps its suppressed original's reference start, length and duplicate family, mapped through the haplotype; fragments that start in deleted sequence are dropped, and DUP copies get one replacement per copy. The 1:1 replacement fixes CR2 by construction, keeps the sample's indels, duplicates and real qualities in the flanks, and needs no learned intensity, so it avoids CR2-A's mappability double count. Novel-sequence molecules (P3) still need new starts at local density. Falsifiers: the CR2 dup_variable probe interior must read about 28.13x (today 81.09x); binned output/donor depth on real HG002 DUPs must be flat at 1+v in mappable bins, and a sham run must give 1.0; transplant rounds 1b/2b/3 must keep their verdicts; the duplicate rate in the footprint must equal the unspiked rate; reads outside the remade set must be byte-identical. A cheaper first step for small variants: reuse the breakpoint_only zone sampler (simulate.rs:1032-1043) non-additively, suppressing only event-copy pairs that overlap the changed span and tiling the same number crossing it.

P1b (SNVs/MNVs, possibly small indels): edit the base inside the original event-copy reads that cover the site, keeping each read's quality, errors, name and duplicate family. Falsifier: transplant round 2b SNV/indel A and E metrics stay supported, and FASTQ records outside the edited reads are byte-identical.

Measure first, before CR3 option A: spike 20 SNVs into HG002 at sites with a carried hom or het indel within 2 kb (expected from the 27.3% and 48.9% exposure measured here). Compare background calls against the unspiked BAM; a nearby hom indel flipping to het, or a het indel lost, would confirm the predicted artifact. If confirmed, either P1/P1b, or a per-copy variant list built from a phased VCF (indels included). The CR3 falsifier stands: dup_homdel must return to AF 1.0 with input phase preserved.

Grouped-event composition (the CR1 prerequisite): apply several edits to one VariantHaplotype per copy, with explicit cis/trans, and write phase into the truth (GT 0|1 with PS) and the chosen copy into the README. Falsifiers: two SNVs 300 bp apart planted cis come out cis in at least 95% of the read-backed phase-informative reads, and trans comes out trans; two events closer than 7 kb show no 1+v depth inflation. This also unblocks CR6-A (balanced translocation) and complex SVs, after the ref_range per-chromosome fix.

Realistic insertion content: MEI insertions from a consensus library (AluY/L1HS/SVA, with poly-A tail and a target-site duplication), STR/VNTR expansions as unit repeats of an existing repeat, and emitting the fragments wholly inside the insertion at local density. Falsifiers: the MAPQ-0 elsewhere-mate fraction should match the real AluY's (14 of 15); a transplant of HG001-only Alu insertions into HG002 should match real-vs-real; ExpansionHunter genotypes and IRR counts should track the planted length. VCF <INS:ME:*> should at least warn that it becomes random sequence.

Ploidy and genotype mode (CR7 a/b): a sex or contig-ploidy map, haploid GT on male non-PAR X/Y, an input-GT reproduction mode that honours FILTER and hom-ref, and a refusal of af=het on haploid contigs. Falsifier: a male chrX DMD exon DEL with af=hom gives about 0x in non-PAR and writes GT 1; a PAR event behaves as diploid.

Exon-spec breakpoints: either document that exon specs give exon-edge, unique-sequence junctions (0 of 36 LDLR edges in an Alu against 19 of 62 ClinVar ends), or add an option to draw intronic breakpoints from real junction classes (Alu-Alu, TR, microhomology). Falsifier: SIM_RESIST and caller-recall distributions for exon-spec events move toward those of ClinVar-coordinate events in LDLR.
VCF delins SVs: a DEL/DUP/INV with END or SVLEN plus a sequence ALT carrying extra bases should be honoured (as segments plus novel bases) or counted and refused, not silently simplified.

New event types the existing machinery could support: copy-neutral LOH/UPD (suppress other-copy reads and tile from the event-copy haplotype with no structural change); trio-consistent spiking (the same transmitted haplotype into parent and child, de novo into the child only), relevant because raredisease is trio-aware (external knowledge, not verified here); triplication and CN≥4 per haplotype; inverted and dispersed DUPs.

Still open from earlier runs: CR2 option A, CR3 option A plus the footprint scan (the T7 threshold decision), CR4 option A, CR6 option A, CR7 (a)/(b), the RF8 scoring of refused events in validate_pipeline.sh, the origin thresholds (PD-29, SIM_RESIST 0.5 not checked for origin), RF15 (spike's short insertions cleaner than real), DUP 50-299 reverse inconclusive in round 3 (rho 2.81), pileup failure without --gvcf only warns (README:1628-1632).
refuted_or_done: DONE CR7(c): af=het is exactly 0.5; it used to be a Beta(40,40) draw that moved the event itself (main.rs:303-310, commit 8dca8d0).
DONE CR3 fail-closed half: an unreadable --gvcf stops the run. The footprint non-SNP scan is not done: T7 found a blanket warning would fire on 38 of 40 chr20 loci, a decision still pending.
DONE CR6 relabel: fusion mode is announced as additive and not balanced (main.rs:316-332). The balanced/derivative model is not built.
DONE CR4 option B: SIM_RESIST is in the truth VCF with a warning above 0.10. RF8 (merged c0c9614) refuses above 0.5 unless --allow-resistant; 6 of 20 real pipeline DELs are above 0.5.

DONE CR2 option B: SIM_DEPTH_FOLD with a warning above 1.5. T3 'mappability dominates, 5 of 6' was RETRACTED as a units error; the direct counterfactual gave 3 of 6, inconclusive (judgment-gate-cases.md 2026-09-26).
DONE CR1 gate: footprints must sit 7 kb apart. Grouped-event composition is NOT built.
DONE CR5: insertion fragments are drawn only from reference-overlapping starts, so 494 of 500 pairs are anchored at 1 Mb. CR7 INS sequence in the truth and the AF caps (SIM_VAF/SIM_REQ_VAF) are done.
DONE carried-allele refusal (review finding 3, carried.rs): it refuses 99.3% het and 100% hom SNVs the sample carries, and 0.2% of random SNVs.
DONE gVCF hom-alt fix (finding 4, RegionSnps::with_hom_alt_from), origin conservation (finding 2, OriginSite::depth scaling), low-AF SIM_ALT_FRAGS (180 of 180 equal to an independent locator).
DONE --edit-model origin (experimental): the physics gate is SUPPORTED only in the exact-twin regime (L 0.739, P 0.763); look-alike removal is held small by R4 (memory edit-model-origin.md).

SUPPORTED: transplant round 1b, DELs ≥50 bp in all 6 bins x directions; round 2b 13 of 16 (SNV, small DEL/INS); round 3 5 of 16 supported, 0 refuted, DUP 50-299 reverse moved from refuted to inconclusive.

REFUTED: RF6 junction probe built from the reference (spike writes the sample's SNPs into junction reads); RF11 lower clip floor; RF13 2-mismatch tolerance for short INS (fixed by ins_planted); RF14 split_reads/ins_reads as planted-ness checks (fixed by del_planted/ins_planted).

map:history.subsystem: History and known-gaps inventory (whole spike project: review findings, the judgment-gate case file, owner notes, merge/push state)

algorithms.name: Quality model v2 (fqzcomp context as a generator, plus an error table learned once from a sample of the input)
algorithms.how: At startup it reads 20 blocks of 50 kb, placed from the index. Each quality is drawn in a context of: the last 5 Q values, cycles to the 3' end, a changes bit, one of 8 read-mean classes, the lows among the last 16 qualities, and the longest one-letter run so far (read from the template, not the called bases). Errors are drawn per (Q, class, lows, run, distance to the 3' end, errors in the last 30 bases), with backoff below 200 counted bases. A pair's two classes are drawn jointly, given each mate's run and the event's class mix. It warns below 50,000 sampled pairs.
algorithms.where: src/quality.rs:92 (SAMPLE_BLOCKS), src/quality.rs:501 (learn), src/quality.rs:726 (draw_classes), src/quality.rs:859 (error_rate), src/synth.rs:31 (MIN_PROFILE_PAIRS=50_000), README.md:1905-1955

algorithms.name: Library cycles and adapter-prefix trimming (read-length fix)
algorithms.how: The cycle count is the most common read length, pooled over both mates. A library counts as adapter-trimmed when at least 1,000 full-length reads were sampled and under 5% of them end in A. For a trimmed library, a mate's length is min(cycles, fragment), and a 3' suffix that spells the start of AGATCGGAAGAGC is trimmed.

algorithms.name: Illumina-shaped read names
algorithms.how: The name shape (7-part, 5-part or other) is learned from 50,000 records. Each read is named SPIKE_<internal>:<middle>:<tile>:<x>:<y>. Tile, x and y come from an FNV+splitmix hash of the internal name, never from the RNG.

algorithms.name: Carried-allele refusal (review finding 3)
algorithms.how: A small variant is refused when at least 10 reads span it and at least 20% of them carry another allele (a mismatch, deletion or insertion at its bases). All refused events are listed in one error before extraction. Structural events are not checked.

algorithms.name: Resistant-read census and refusal (CR4 option B plus RF8)
algorithms.how: SIM_RESIST is the share of reads over the event that are not in the donor pool. It warns above 0.10 and refuses above 0.5 unless --allow-resistant is given.

algorithms.name: Depth-fold census (CR2 option B), on top of a single-depth tiling count
algorithms.how: Tiling count n = round(C*VAF*starts/mean_frag), where C is the pool's fragment depth in a 2 kb window at the first breakpoint, applied to the whole event. SIM_DEPTH_FOLD is the worst 1 kb bin's max((D+1)/(C+1), (C+1)/(D+1)). It warns above 1.5 and corrects nothing.

algorithms.name: Sample copies and phasing
algorithms.how: SampleCopies is two HashMap<u64,u8> SNP maps, so it cannot hold indels or SVs. Het SNPs from a pileup (at least 10 reads, 20-80%) or from a gVCF are phased by fragment links or PS sets. One coin flip per phase block picks the event copy. gVCF hom-alts are layered on top of the pileup when the gVCF has no het call.

algorithms.name: Duplicate-family removal in clean mode (duplicates fix)
algorithms.how: Once the removal list is final, spike re-reads the event windows +/- 1,500 bp. Duplicates of every removed kept pair, matched by both mates' unclipped 5' ends, are added to replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt.

algorithms.name: --edit-model origin (experimental)
algorithms.how: Reads are removed by placement chance, from MAPQ and XA. The surest mate decides for the fragment. There is one draw per duplicate family, and look-alike regions come from XA hits. The origin depth counts each read at its family's p_origin (review finding 2 fix).

algorithms.name: validate rows that decide INS and DEL (RF13, RF14)
algorithms.how: These rows count only spike's own reads for the event. ins_planted needs a 31-base junction probe with the inserted bases exact and at most 2 flank substitutions. del_planted needs ref[S-15,S)+ref[E,E+16) within 2 substitutions, within START/END +/- 500. split_reads and ins_reads are now advisory.

algorithms.name: SIM_ALT_FRAGS (low-AF note)
algorithms.how: Counts the planted pairs that show the event. For a small variant: a read over the changed bases plus one base each side. For an SV: a fragment across a junction. spike warns at 0, and the reads are unchanged.

algorithms.name: Full-FASTQ assembly (fastq.sh, --into-fastq)
algorithms.how: Every raw record is kept byte for byte except the listed originals, in order. spike's SPIKE_ pairs are appended in the raw file's header style. Both mates are read together, and the script refuses on mismatched mates or aliased outputs. Results are written beside the target and published only on success.

algorithms.name: align.sh copies the input's bwa-mem2 options
algorithms.how: The alignment options are parsed from the input BAM's bwa @PG (for example -M -K 100000000). -t -R -o -v -H -p -C are not copied.

limitations.what: RF15: spike's 20-39 bp insertions align as one clean I, while real ones are split, shortened or clipped. Cause not measured; site vs content not separated.
limitations.evidence: ins_reads fails spike's het INS 0/16 at 20-39 bp against HG002's real ones 47/112. Of the 60 real ones under 40 bp that fail, 23 have no I in any read. 40/90 real insertions that copy no neighbour also fail.

limitations.what: Independent review finding 6, still open: different R1/R2 cycle counts collapse into one 'cycles' value. Both mates come out at the longer length, and the extra R1 cycles get the Q20 fallback.
limitations.evidence: A BAM with R1 100 / R2 150 gives synthetic reads of 150/150. BamStats has one `cycles` field, computed over both mates. The owner notes it is not relevant for 151/151 data.

limitations.what: spike makes no PCR or optical duplicates of its own reads.
limitations.evidence: Duplicate share in the spiked regions is 0.008 against 0.036 real. Reported only, not fixed. Callers skip duplicates.

limitations.what: CR2: one breakpoint depth scales the whole event, so the donor's local depth profile is flattened. SIM_DEPTH_FOLD only warns. Option A (spatial start intensity) is not built.
limitations.evidence: A het DUP over an 18.75x section gave 81.09x where local CN3 predicts 28.13x. 6 of 40 ordinary chr20 DUPs warn (median fold 1.27, max 2.46).

limitations.what: CR3: synthetic copies carry SNPs only, so the sample's own indels and SVs are rewritten as reference. A failed pileup still only warns, and neither the footprint scan nor the indel model exists.
limitations.evidence: A hom 2 bp DEL under a het DUP comes out at AF 0.360 instead of 1.0. Any non-SNP record lies in 38/40 seeded chr20 footprints (95%); a >50 bp one in 4/40.

limitations.what: CR4: reads outside the donor pool (low MAPQ, discordant, unmapped mate) are never edited. Only the census, the warning and the refusal above 0.5 exist; option A is not built.
limitations.evidence: At AF=1 with half the pairs at MAPQ 0, 37.5x stays inside the deletion. 6/20 of validate_pipeline.sh's real HG002 DELs have SIM_RESIST above 0.5; at --min-mapq 0, 5 of the 6 drop below.

limitations.what: CR1: there is no grouped-event composition. Events less than 7,000 bp apart are refused, and --allow-overlap merges independent simulations only approximately. This also blocks CR6 option A.
limitations.evidence: Two adjacent DELs at AF=1 read 67.05x/67.03x inside under --allow-overlap.

limitations.what: CR6: fusion mode is additive junction evidence, not a balanced reciprocal translocation. It was relabelled, not modelled.
limitations.evidence: n = C*v/(1-v) junction fragments are added on top of C retained originals, and only one derivative junction is built.

limitations.what: CR7(a)/(b): input GT is ignored and the truth GT comes from AF alone (>= 0.9 gives 1/1). There is no ploidy (male X/Y), no baseline CN, and FILTER/hom-ref are not used as gates.
limitations.evidence: An input GT=1/1 DEL with no AF wrote SIM_VAF=0.500;GT=0/1.

limitations.what: CR9, the rest: no per-window depth profiles, no strand- or CIGAR-aware junction checks, and no donor-relative global checks (validate is not given the donor BAM). --strict's composed false-failure rate is non-zero.
limitations.evidence: --strict exits 1 on 8/64 correct real runs (12.5%), against 4/64 by default before RF14.

limitations.what: Quality model v2 residuals: crashed reads about 15% short on 35x; run-free reads on the hospital BAM clip too little; the hospital K2 pass is narrow; master is 1.27x slower until the quality-speed branch is merged.
limitations.evidence: Crash 0.88% vs 1.16% (z -2.49). K2 bad-end clips 0.94% vs 1.38% (z -2.64). Run-free hospital reads clip 0.26% vs 0.73%. Speed 11.86 s vs 9.37 s; the unmerged speed fix measured 1.18x.

limitations.what: Soft clips that are not bad ends are not reproduced: adapter read-through, chimeric fragments and sequence not in the reference. An untrimmed library never draws a fragment shorter than the read. A fragment longer than 1,500 bp is never generated.
limitations.evidence: Of HG002 chr20 reads: adapter 0.71%, sample's own variant 0.54%, chimeric 0.13%, not in reference 0.10%. The fragment range is [read_length, 1500], or [1, 1500] when trimmed. The adapter can be learned from pairs with TLEN < 150: the consensus equals TruSeq for 33 bp, then the index. Not built.

limitations.what: Errors: a wrong base is drawn uniformly among the other three, so the lean of wrong calls to A/G (two-colour chemistry) is missing. Sequence-specific errors such as GG were never measured. PCR errors are not modelled. Offline, the fqzcomp-style model made about 15% too many errors per read. Homopolymer slips were left out.
limitations.evidence: Wrong calls lean to A and G (minor). Errors per read: model 0.575 vs real 0.505. Slips add about 0.04 points.

limitations.what: The pileup het/hom caller and read-to-copy assignment ignore base quality. Phase blocks that no read links get independent coin flips, so a new seed also changes which copy carries the event.
limitations.evidence: A grep of src/loh.rs finds no base-quality reference. REVIEW.md design note: 'Pileup het caller has no base-quality filter'. Astra's point (b) was confirmed in code.

limitations.what: --edit-model origin is unvalidated on real data. The physics verdict covers only the exact-twin, one-XA-hit regime. The look-alike half is inert in practice, the census thresholds are borrowed from clean, and main() could pass a subset of events to draw_origin_removals without any test failing.
limitations.evidence: 0 fragments removed at the 14 look-alikes on the whole-genome 35x BAM: of 52 candidate fragments, R4 keeps 25 and 18 have a mate outside the regions read. PD-29: fold 1.24 -> 1.47 under origin at chr20:14548422.

limitations.what: Real-vs-fake validation is incomplete. Round 3 left 11 of 16 inconclusive. The reverse 50-299 bp DUP was not cleared. The real-vs-real yardstick sits below counting noise, which is unexplained. The phased-neighbour check never ran. Not tested at all: a low-VAF mixture, read-level 'can you tell', origin mode, callers, DUP >= 300 bp, INV, fusions, INS >= 50 bp.
limitations.evidence: rho for reverse DUP 2.81 (1.50-5.06), n=33 shared. R_c 0.61 (DUP J), 0.50 (INS20-49 A), 0.69 (INS1-4 A). 0/142 DUP windows lie fully inside the small-variant beds.

limitations.what: Hospital path not exercised end to end. SNVs, small indels, exon DELs/DUPs and LDLR have never been spiked into real hospital data. fastq.sh was tested only on a 478,815-pair stand-in. Lanes must be concatenated first. The effect of a second fastp pass on synthetic reads is unmeasured. The quality model learns from post-fastp BAM reads, which are cleaner than raw.
limitations.evidence: fastp dropped 2.82% of reads. The stand-in lacks pairs whose mate maps to another chromosome; a real FASTQ adds about 1 point of old allele at hom sites (the SIM_RESIST share). F3's 33 min for 380 M pairs is a prediction, not a measurement.

limitations.what: LDLR in particular: its SV breakpoints often sit in Alus, where RF8 may refuse them. Manta misses ClinVar 4845403 (a 2,136 bp Alu-Alu DEL) even on the full BAM; whether it would miss a real carrier is unknown.
limitations.evidence: Of 39 LDLR pathogenic SVs, 6 have both ends in an Alu and 9 have one. spike's Alu-Alu junctions clip like real ones.

limitations.what: Slices are refuted as a shortcut for testing Manta and CNVnator. TIDDIT is inconclusive because it varies so much between runs. One whole-BAM event takes about 2 h 55 min.
limitations.evidence: CNVnator: both slices miss the B1/B2 DELs that FULL finds. Manta: S1 equals FULL 3/3 at the events, but 2 background calls vanish. TIDDIT: FULL runs differ by about 2,400 calls. Manta --callRegions on chr19: 245/279 calls identical, all 34 missing are BNDs to other chromosomes.

limitations.what: Low AF: at 30x, most SNVs at AF 0.001-0.02 get no planted pair showing them. SIM_ALT_FRAGS records this, but the reads are not conditioned on it.
limitations.evidence: 12-16 of 20 sites have 0 ALT reads at AF 0.001-0.02; 0/20 at AF 0.1.

limitations.what: Open validate and harness defects: RF3, RF4, RF5, RF7, RF9, RF10, RF11, NF1, NF5 and NF7 (detailed in the evidence). validate_pipeline.sh has no scoring for its 6 RF8-resistant events, and its 4 depth-only background DELs stay counted.
limitations.evidence: RF3: summary.fail counts advisory rows (counted_* fields added in 27625d3). RF4: a negative SIM_RESIST passes. RF5: --help never explains '(advisory)'. RF7: the depth fold's worst bin is discarded. RF9: ins_sequence is not evaluable below 12 bp, a false fail under --strict. RF10: validate opens the BAM 9x instead of 6x (+43%). RF11: ins_reads fails 40-49 bp insertions (now advisory). NF1: a small --region aborts at MIN_EVENTS=5. NF5: split_reads pools both ends. NF7: Truvari version is not pinned. Recall outside the background: 0.7692 / 0.5385 / 0.4615.

limitations.what: Docs drift since quality v2, 4 instances: (1) README.md:1968 says a donor pool under 1,000 pairs warns, but the code warns below 50,000 sampled pairs (src/synth.rs:31). (2) README.md:1955 still says a 31-value alphabet over-crashes (24% vs 14%), which quality-speed 75a8d73 withdraws as a run-bin composition artifact. (3) docs/analysis/soft-clips/README.md:29 and :31 still say first-order Markov chain and 'nothing to simulate'. (4) REVIEW.md:2867's CR2 status says T3 found 5 of 6 mappability, retracted at REVIEW.md:4705.

Review text. Sizes now: main.rs 5,975 lines and validate.rs 8,591 (wc -l, tests included). pick_sample_name is at src/bam_stats.rs:281.

limitations.what: AF has no single meaning. It is an edit or replacement fraction for DEL/DUP/INV and an added-junction fraction for additive modes. SIM_VAF is a model expectation, not an observed fraction.
limitations.evidence: Independent review model assessment.

limitations.what: Long novel insertions get no reads lying wholly inside the inserted sequence, so there are no unmapped or assembly-style reads for big INS.
limitations.evidence: Fragment starts are restricted to fragments that overlap reference.

limitations.what: Adapter-trimming detection is a dataset-specific heuristic: under 5% of full-length reads ending in A, and the TruSeq prefix. It is not configurable and was verified only on HG001/HG002/hospital NovaSeq libraries.
limitations.evidence: Review text, plus read-length K0 measured on 3 libraries.

limitations.what: Threads step 2 (per-chunk RNG streams) was not chosen, so work that draws random numbers stays single-threaded. --threads 1 is 3.8-4.3% slower than before threading.
limitations.evidence: Threads step 1 result.

map:outputs.subsystem: Outputs and pipeline integration: src/main.rs (CLI, orchestration, the generated align.sh/merge.sh/fastq.sh and run README), src/fastq.rs, src/truth.rs, and the README sections Output files, CLI reference, What spike refuses and Pipeline validation examples
map:outputs.summary:
main() (main.rs:455-1024) checks the CLI first. The prefix and --into-fastq paths are checked before the output folder is made (main.rs:485-489). It then learns a few things from the BAM: read length, trimming, name shape, SM and bwa @PG options (main.rs:540-584). It refuses carried alleles, builds one quality profile (main.rs:654-664) and runs the events one at a time, in order, on a single StdRng seeded from --seed (main.rs:614, 704-860). For each event it extracts reads, runs the census with its RF8 refusal, builds the haplotype and simulates. After the loop it puts together the removal list: the originals it consumed, origin's removals, the pairs with unusable qualities and the duplicates of removed pairs (main.rs:898-932). It then writes R1/R2.fq.gz, truth.vcf, align.sh, events.bed, replaced_reads.txt, merge.sh, fastq_removed_reads.txt with fastq.sh, and README.md (main.rs:935-1002). If asked, it runs align.sh and then fastq.sh (main.rs:1014-1021).

Users take one of two routes. (1) The BAM route: align.sh makes sim.bam, tagged @RG ID:sim SM:<input SM>, using the bwa options copied from the input. merge.sh then makes merged.bam: samtools view -N/-U drops the listed names, a count check guards against the wrong BAM, then come merge, a full re-sort and an index. This route is used for the preliminary SV-caller tests. (2) The FASTQ route, which is how raredisease is run at the hospital. fastq.sh, or --into-fastq, streams both raw mates through one awk pass. It drops the names in fastq_removed_reads.txt and appends the SPIKE_ reads at the end of each file, in the raw header style. It refuses, and writes nothing, on any mismatch.

truth.vcf is uncompressed VCFv4.3, with a sample column named SAMPLE. INFO carries SIM_VAF, SIM_REQ_VAF, SIM_ALT_FRAGS, SIM_RESIST and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD. GT is 1/1 when the requested fraction is 0.9 or more. Output does not change with --threads (rayon only runs work that draws no random numbers). It does change with event order, with the date, and with which gzip is installed.

Hot spots, measured. merge.sh took 1 h 42 min on a 742 M-record BAM for one 2.1 kb DEL. fastq.sh runs at about 150k pairs/s; for 380 M pairs that predicts about 42 min (not measured). Big events have a serial floor: the 3 Mb DUP takes 26.5 s even at 16 threads.

algorithms.name: Run orchestration and output order
algorithms.how: The CLI is checked first; --into-fastq and --fastq-prefix are checked before create_dir_all, so a refused run leaves a fresh folder empty. Events are processed one after another on one RNG stream. The RF8 refusal checks every event before anything is written. The outputs are then written in a fixed order. --align runs before --into-fastq.
algorithms.where: src/main.rs:455-1024 (create_dir_all 489, RNG 614, event loop 704-860, writes 935-1002, align/fastq 1014-1021)

algorithms.name: Removal list (replaced_reads.txt)
algorithms.how: The list holds four kinds of names: the originals each event consumed (kept and suppressed), origin's removals, the pairs dropped for unusable quality, and, in clean mode, the duplicates of removed pairs, found by reading the windows again (± MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN). It is a sorted BTreeSet, one name per line.

algorithms.name: FASTQ-route removal list
algorithms.how: fastq_removed_names = replaced minus the names written to R1/R2. The originals spike kept therefore stay in the raw FASTQ as raw records.

algorithms.name: fastq.sh (whole-sample spiked FASTQ)
algorithms.how: The script first refuses output/input clashes by inode (-ef) and by realpath. One awk then reads RAW_R1 on stdin and RAW_R2 through a FIFO, record by record. It checks that names match and that the 4-line structure holds, and drops the listed names, counting found against wanted and catching repeats. It copies the first record's header comment as the style for spike's reads. A second awk appends the SPIKE_ records from R1/R2.fq.gz. Outputs are written to hidden temp files beside their names and moved into place with mv -T only after both mates pass the checks. Compression uses pigz -p THREADS/2 per mate, or gzip if pigz is missing.
algorithms.where: src/main.rs:2193-2454 (identity check only at END 2362-2373; append 2424-2428)

algorithms.name: --into-fastq pre-checks and runner
algorithms.how: Before any work, spike checks that both raw paths are files and are not the same inode, and that neither is a file the run writes (RUN_OUTPUT_FILES plus the prefix pair). At the end it runs bash fastq.sh, and its exit status becomes spike's.

algorithms.name: align.sh generator
algorithms.how: Presets for bwa-mem2, minimap2 and bowtie2, or a custom command run verbatim. The @RG is ID:sim SM:<input's first SM> PL:ILLUMINA, quoted with sh_quote. The bwa-mem2 preset copies the input's bwa @PG options (fix B). Default paths are canonicalized and single-quoted. Output goes through samtools sort into sim.bam, which is then indexed.

algorithms.name: merge.sh generator
algorithms.how: samtools view -b -N replaced_reads.txt -U outside.bam writes removed.bam, which is used only to count records; with no -@ it runs on one thread. The script aborts if fewer records come out than names are listed (the wrong-BAM guard). It then merges sim.bam with outside.bam into merged_tmp.bam, re-sorts all of it into merged.bam, and indexes. Temp files go in $DIR and are not cleaned up on failure.

algorithms.name: Paired FASTQ writer
algorithms.how: Every pair's quality is checked first (length equal to SEQ, bytes 33-126), so a refusal creates no file. Records are written as @name/1 and @name/2 with flate2 Compression::fast. The two mates are written side by side with rayon::join, or in turn on one thread, with the same bytes either way. Both streams are finished and flushed before an error is reported.

algorithms.name: Truth VCF writer
algorithms.how: The header has contigs from the .fai, the ALT/INFO definitions, and, under origin only, ##spike_edit_model. There is one record per event (two BND records for a fusion, with MATEID). POS uses the preceding-base convention, and INS carries the full sequence. Records are sorted by .fai contig rank, then POS. GT is 1/1 if SIM_REQ_VAF >= 0.9, else 0/1. IDs are sim_<type>_<event index>. The ID of an input VCF record is dropped, and SIM_GENE falls back to 'unknown'.

algorithms.name: Run README (run log)
algorithms.how: The log holds the command line, joined with spaces and not quoted; the input paths; and an events table (requested and simulated VAF, kept, chimeric, suppressed, dropped, resistant, depth fold). Paragraphs on resistant reads, depth folds, VAF changes and bare breakpoint sides appear only when they apply. It ends with the output file table and the workflow. The version comes from CARGO_PKG_VERSION.

algorithms.name: Determinism controls
algorithms.how: There is one global rayon pool sized by --threads, used only for work that draws no random numbers. One StdRng (rand 0.8) seeded from --seed (default 42) is passed by &mut through the events in input order and then through origin's single removal draw. Read-name tiles come from a hash, not from the RNG.

algorithms.name: spike validate dispatch
algorithms.how: argv[1]=='validate' is caught before clap parses anything, so the subcommand has its own parser and a --json output (JSON written by hand). It never appears in spike --help.

limitations.what: merge.sh dominates the BAM route: 1 h 42 min to replace 2,820 read names in a 742 M-record (37 GB) whole-genome BAM at 16 threads. spike itself took about 1 s and align.sh about 46 s. merge.sh re-sorts the whole merged BAM even though samtools merge of two coordinate-sorted inputs is already sorted, and its view -N step has no -@.
