limitations.what: In merged.bam, kept originals come back from sim.bam with RG:Z:sim and without the original PG:Z:MarkDuplicates tag. The 'sim' read group is therefore mostly real reads, all inside the event regions. Tools that keep statistics per read group (BQSR, Delly's per-library insert sizes, per-RG QC) see a small separate group. Manta is not affected: it pools stats per BAM file.
limitations.evidence: Measured: 4,870 of 4,870 kept-original primary records in B1 sim.bam have the same chrom, POS, CIGAR, MAPQ and pair flags as in the original 37 GB BAM, and only the RG and PG tags differ (scratchpad keptcmp/). The original has a single @RG with ID ...S17_L002_R1_001_2. Manta's alignmentStatsSummary.txt reads 'group: .../merged.bam'. The effect on per-RG tools is inferred.

limitations.what: truth.vcf is not bgzipped or indexed, so the harness bgzips, tabix-indexes and re-heads it before Truvari. The input VCF's ID (a ClinVar ID, for example) is dropped, gene falls back to 'unknown' unless SIM_GENE is set, the sample column is 'SAMPLE' rather than the BAM's SM, and no benchmark-regions BED is written. Scoring has to match on coordinates.
limitations.evidence: Code read. The harness block 'needs contig headers + bgzip + tabix' is at validate_pipeline.sh:946.

limitations.what: Output depends on event order and on the other events. One RNG stream runs through every event in input order, so adding, removing or reordering one event changes the reads and the realised fractions of all events after it. Output also differs by date (fileDate, README timestamp) and by gzip vs pigz bytes in fastq.sh.
limitations.evidence: Commit bccc43a: 'K7 FAIL by rule (2 allele_freq flips from the reordered random stream)'. The date and gzip effects are read from the code.

limitations.what: Big events have a serial floor. Tiling, phasing and the removal draw run on one thread, so a 3 Mb DUP takes 44.3 s at 1 thread, 29.8 s at 4 and 26.5 s at 16. Events run in sequence even when they are independent.
limitations.evidence: README.md:1354-1361 run-time table (35x HG002).

limitations.what: fastq.sh throughput is capped by a single awk pass and pigz -p THREADS/2 per mate. A raw FASTQ from the wrong run is caught only at END, after the whole file has been read.
limitations.evidence: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-fastq-safety.md:136: 478,815 pairs in 3.18 s at 8 threads, about 150k pairs/s. That predicts about 42 min for the hospital's 380 M pairs (not run; F3's 33 min was before the one-awk fix, full-fastq.md:146-148).

limitations.what: Machine use is awkward. Refusals and I/O errors share exit status 1. There is no machine-readable run summary: per-event kept, chimeric, suppressed, resistant, depth fold and ALT fragments are only in the Markdown table and the truth INFO. Harnesses grep logs and awk the truth VCF.
limitations.evidence: sv_slice_test run.sh:122-127 treats any non-zero exit as a refusal and greps '^Error' from spike.log; validate_pipeline.sh:798 awks SIM_RESIST out of truth.vcf.

limitations.what: spike validate is hidden: argv is intercepted before clap, so spike --help and the README's CLI reference ('Usage: spike [OPTIONS] --bam <BAM> --reference <REFERENCE>') never mention the subcommand.
limitations.evidence: Code and README text.

limitations.what: merge.sh disk use and failure cleanup. outside.bam, removed.bam, merged_tmp.bam, the sort temp files and merged.bam all sit in $DIR at once, and nothing removes them if the script fails. merged.bam is written in place, not atomically, and the output is BAM even when the input is CRAM.
limitations.evidence: Code. The user's loop deletes the temp files by hand (run.sh:131). The peak of about 3x the BAM size is inferred from the steps.

limitations.what: Events must sit at least 7 kb apart (span ± 3,500 bp footprints) unless --allow-overlap is given, and with it one event's synthetic flank writes reference over the other's edit. Compound hets or cis/trans pairs within one LDLR-sized gene cannot be planted.
limitations.evidence: CLI help text and README.md:1603 refusal row.

limitations.what: Every event's pairs stay in memory until the end, so peak memory grows with the total of all events.
limitations.evidence: Measured per single event: 1.2-2.5 GB for 3 Mb events (README.md:1358-1361). Growth with many events is inferred from the code.

limitations.what: --align runs before --into-fastq, so an align failure (for example no bwa-mem2 index under the reference's exact name, README:439-445) aborts the run before the whole-sample FASTQ is built, although that FASTQ does not need sim.bam.
limitations.evidence: Code order.

limitations.what: In the FASTQ route, all SPIKE_ reads go at the end of each file and all take the input's most common RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. They are therefore one block in one lane, and in a run that big would fill whole bwa -K batches by themselves.
limitations.evidence: Harmless for a small event (see refuted_or_done, F2). Big events and multi-lane per-lane processing are not measured.

open_issues: Faster merge.sh: add -@ to view -N; count with view -c instead of writing removed.bam; drop the full re-sort; write the index during the merge (samtools merge --write-index). A further step would splice: copy the untouched BGZF blocks verbatim and re-encode only the edited windows plus the mates' spans. Falsifier: on the B1 inputs, the decoded records (samtools view | md5, ignoring the order of ties at one position) and the header (minus @PG) equal the current merged.bam. Then time each step. Current: 1 h 42 min (measured). The owner's sv-caller-slices note already lists a faster spiked-BAM build as an untested idea.

Stale outputs: at startup, delete the files in RUN_OUTPUT_FILES plus merged.bam (or refuse a non-empty -o without --force), and write a run ID into a run.json that align.sh stamps into sim.bam (@CO) and merge.sh checks. Kill test: run spike twice in one folder with different events, skip align.sh, run merge.sh; it must refuse.

Provenance and a machine-readable summary: embed the git commit (build.rs or option_env) and write ##spike_version, ##spike_seed and ##spike_command (shell-quoted with sh_quote) to truth.vcf. Add a run.json with per-event stats, refusals, input sizes and mtimes, and output checksums, written last as a completion marker. Use exit 2 for policy refusals and 1 for errors, so loops like run.sh's fallback can tell them apart.
Shell-quote the logged command (sh_word at main.rs:1303 already exists). Falsifier: paste the README command for an af=0.05 event into bash; truth.vcf must again show SIM_REQ_VAF=0.050.

Truth VCF for benchmarking: write truth.vcf.gz plus .tbi (noodles bgzf is already a dependency; tabix would need a feature). Carry the input record's ID (e.g. SIM_SRC_ID) and the gene from GENEINFO. Use the BAM's SM as the sample column. Write a benchmark-regions BED (event spans plus a margin) for hap.py -f or truvari --includebed. Left-normalize small indels or warn when they are not left-aligned. Check: validate_pipeline.sh's fix-up block (944-959) becomes a no-op.

Clinical safety: require -o, or default to ./spike_out and warn when -o is under /tmp. Make the scripts' mode follow the umask (0o777 & !umask). Add an option to drop absolute paths and the SM from README.md and the scripts' comments. State in the README and the log that R1/R2.fq.gz are mostly real patient reads (about 91% kept pairs in B1). Optional, against the user's 2026-10-04 choice of names that can be told apart: a blinded-names mode with a private key file, for blinded proficiency testing.

Read group in the BAM route: either give spike's reads the input's own @RG (single-RG input), or keep the kept originals in place by merging with fastq_removed_reads.txt and only the SPIKE_ records of sim.bam. Alignment realism does not motivate this (4,870/4,870 identical, measured). The motive is per-RG tools. Test first whether Delly's or GATK's per-RG statistics change between merged.bam with RG sim and with the original RG; if nothing changes, drop it.

Per-event RNG streams seeded from (seed, hash of the event spec), or counter-based draws per fragment. Output would then not depend on event order, a panel run would equal its one-at-a-time runs, and independent events, and tiling inside a big event, could run in parallel (serial floor 26.5 s at 16 threads for a 3 Mb DUP). This changes the bytes once, so it needs a K7-style equivalence gate against master's seed spread.

Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ: compare the first raw header's RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE with the BAM's learned name shape before simulating (the check costs one record), instead of finding found != want only after a scan of about 42 min. Optional: a native Rust fastq route with parallel compression, held to byte-identical decompressed output against fastq.sh on the F1 stand-in.

Multi-lane FASTQ input: accept one pair per lane and write per-lane outputs, putting each SPIKE_ read in the lane its name claims. The hospital sample is a single pair today (full-fastq.md), so this is low priority.

Big events in the FASTQ route: measure whether SPIKE_ reads appended at the end (several bwa -K batches made only of event reads) align as they do in sim.bam, for example a 1-3 Mb DUP compared with F2's 1,296/1,296 for a small event. If they differ, write each spike pair in place of a removed original.

Compound het or multi-variant haplotypes inside one footprint (several small variants assigned to copies, with cis/trans, tiled in one pass) for FH-style demos in LDLR, where the 7 kb rule refuses neighbouring exonic variants.

Under --into-fastq, the quality model learned from the BAM reflects reads after fastp --correction, and fastp dropped 2.82% of raw reads (hospital-demo-plan.md). At the hospital, measure the share of bases and qualities that differ between BAM and raw records of the same names. If it is under about 0.5%, leave it alone.
Expose spike validate in --help (clap subcommands kept compatible with the current argv form). Run --into-fastq before --align, or keep going when --align fails.
refuted_or_done: Already measured harmless for small events: placing the SPIKE_ reads at the end of the FASTQ. F2 realigned with raredisease's bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000; 1,296 of 1,296 spike records were identical to sim.bam (full-fastq.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-full-fastq.md).

Measured here, so 'keep the kept originals in place' has no alignment-realism benefit: re-aligning them in sim.bam does not change their alignment. 4,870 of 4,870 kept-original primary records in B1 sim.bam match the original 37 GB BAM in chrom, POS, CIGAR, MAPQ and pair flags; only RG:Z:sim and the missing PG:Z:MarkDuplicates differ (scratchpad keptcmp/).

Refuted for Manta: the concern that the separate 'sim' read group skews per-RG fragment statistics. Manta 1.6 pools stats per BAM file (B1 FULL manta alignmentStatsSummary.txt reads 'group: merged.bam', 799,600 fragment observations).

Done: fastq.sh no longer clobbers an input with an output and refuses mates in different orders (review findings 1 and 7, merged 658baa4). Outputs are published with a temp file and mv only after the checks pass.
Done: align.sh copies the input's bwa @PG options (-M, -K), so split reads get SECONDARY and not SUPPLEMENTARY (fix B, 97aa3b4).
Done: spike's read names take the input's Illumina shape with a SPIKE_ machine field, so Picard optical-duplicate detection works and FastQC's per-tile module runs (50c75b6).
Done: in clean mode the duplicates of removed pairs are removed with them, closing the FASTQ-route leak of old-allele reads (2eb9309; hom-SNV old allele went from 0.034 to 0).
Done: output does not change with --threads (threads step 1, byte-identical; fastq.rs test_each_file_holds_the_same_bytes_at_any_thread_count).
Done: generated-script defaults are made absolute and quoted against shell metacharacters (L12), and the SM in the RG is sanitized for tab, newline and backslash.
Done: merge.sh aborts when it gets fewer removed records than listed names, which guards against merging onto the wrong BAM.
Done: SIM_ALT_FRAGS says when no planted pair shows a low-fraction event (bdd568a).
Done: --raw-fastq was renamed --into-fastq, with --fastq-prefix, and its path refusals run before the output folder is made (2764dbc).

Refuted for Manta and CNVnator, with TIDDIT inconclusive (cnv_validation 4bd707b): sliced BAMs as a stand-in for full spiked BAMs. Any faster BAM build must therefore still produce whole-genome merged.bam.

map:synth.subsystem: Read synthesis and the quality/error model (src/synth.rs, src/quality.rs, src/stats.rs, plus tiling in src/simulate.rs). State: master b901339, local only; v2 model 7f28bb0. The quality-speed branch is not merged.

algorithms.name: Startup quality sample
algorithms.how: Lists the input's windows that hold reads from its index (BAI 16 kb leaf bins with chunks, or CRAI slice spans). Places 20 blocks of 50 kb at window floor((k+0.5)W/20), pushing a block forward where it would overlap the previous one. Extracts pairs as donor pools are extracted (proper pairs, non-duplicate, MAPQ >= --min-mapq), dedups by name, and fetches the reference with 1 kb of padding. Warns below 50,000 pairs and stops below 30. Measured K4: 113,938-143,080 pairs, read in 0.3-2.8 s, learned in 1.2-3.3 s.

algorithms.name: Template and run bin
algorithms.how: A donor mate's template is the reference from its 5' end, with soft clips included (reverse mates are reverse-complemented). A synthetic mate's template is the haplotype or reference with the sample's SNP alleles, taken in sequencing order. run_bin maps the longest one-letter run read so far to bins 0-3. The bin edges are hard-coded from HG002 35x: A/G/T 7-8, 9-11 and 12+; C 5-6 and 7+. Runs are always read from the template, never from the called bases.

algorithms.name: fqzcomp-style quality generator
algorithms.how: Counts are learned per mate. The context key packs: the last 5 qualities (4-value alphabet), or for larger alphabets the last one exact plus 2 binned; the position min(7, cycles_left>>pshift), with pshift = round(log2(rl/8)) = 4 at 151 cycles, so one bin covers 16 cycles; a flag for >= 2 bin changes; the class; the lows below Q15 among the last 16; and the run bin. There are 6 backoff levels, each needing 20 observations. The draw is categorical over the learned alphabet.

algorithms.name: Read classes and the pair class draw
algorithms.how: There are 8 classes, cut on a read's mean Phred at the 1/3/8/20/40/60/80% quantiles. The pair's two classes are drawn with weight joint(c1,c2) x P(c|run)/P(c) for each mate, shrunk toward P(c) by 8 reads, times the event's class mix r_m(c) = (n_m(c)+0.5)/(sum_h n_m(h)P(c|h)+0.5) from its donor pool. A run-ratio cache is on the unmerged quality-speed branch.

algorithms.name: Error table learning
algorithms.how: Each sample block is walked base by base in alignment order (walk). Aligned bases count as error or not. Inserted bases and Ns are left out. A soft-clipped end is placed where it would align and counted only if it is 1-4 bp or matches the reference at >= 50% of its bases. Positions where >= 5 reads align and >= 10% differ are masked as the sample's variants. The verdicts are flipped into sequencing order and counted in cells of (symbol, class, lows incl. the base itself, end bin 1-10/11-30/31-60/61+, run, errors among the last 30: 0/1/2-3/4+). Backoff happens at fewer than 200 bases: to (Q, lows, run, errors), then (Q, class), then (Q), then 10^(-Q/10). There is no mate dimension and no record of which base was called.

algorithms.name: Base-by-base read generation
algorithms.how: For each cycle, a quality is drawn from the context with cycles_left = rl - c. A template N emits N at Q2 and skips the error draw. Otherwise p_err comes from the error table. On an error: with probability indel_error_rate the error is an indel (50/50 insertion of a uniform random base, or deletion of the template base); otherwise it is a uniform substitution to one of the other 3 bases. The emitted quality, the template base and the error flag go into the read state. Reads are padded with N/Q2 only when the template runs out.

algorithms.name: Pair layout, read length and adapter trimming
algorithms.how: mate_length returns read_length for an untrimmed library (no fragment shorter than one read). For a trimmed library it returns min(cycles, frag). trim_adapter_start cuts any 3' end that spells a prefix of AGATCGGAAGAGC, but only when frag >= cycles. Whether a library is trimmed is learned in bam_stats: >= 1000 full-length reads and < 5% of them ending in A. The coin flip for F1R2/F2R1 comes before either mate. Haplotype pairs map their ends back to reference and return PairSpans.

algorithms.name: Fragment length distribution
algorithms.how: The empirical sorted CDF of |TLEN| of the event's donor proper pairs, kept only in [min_fragment_len, 1500]. The fallback is 400+/-80 clamped into that range. Draws are uniform from the sorted vector, by rejection into [min, 1500]; after 1000 tries the draw is clamped. Lengths are independent of position, GC and template.

algorithms.name: Tiling and suppression
algorithms.how: Non-additive events: pairs entirely inside the haplotype footprint (event +/- 2 kb) are suppressed at copy_rate (event copy min(1, 2v); other copy max(0, 2v-1); unknown copy v). Then n = round(cov x vaf x (hap_len - mean_frag - novel_only) / mean_frag) fragments are tiled at uniform starts, or at starts overlapping reference when there is novel sequence. Additive events (fusion, junction DUP): n = cov x v/(1-v) per breakpoint, with v capped at 0.95, placed only across breakpoints. The junction DUP adds depth copies jittered +/-20 bp. There is a floor of 2 fragments. cov is the pool's fragment depth in 2 kb at the first breakpoint, and that one depth scales the whole event. The CR2 depth fold is measured, not corrected.

algorithms.name: Read names
algorithms.how: SPIKE_<internal>:<input RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE>:<tile>:<x>:<y>. The tile and x/y come from an FNV-1a + splitmix64 hash of the internal name, not from the RNG. Picard optical-duplicate detection works on them, but spike makes no duplicates.

limitations.what: Substitution errors are uniform over the other 3 bases. In real data, errors at low quality go mostly to one base per true base, and the pattern differs by library.
limitations.evidence: Measured on mismatches at Q<15 in 151M proper MAPQ>=20 reads, chr20:10.0-11.5 Mb, in sequencing orientation (scratchpad map/spectrum.py). Hospital (NovaSeq X): A->C 0.91, T->C 0.89, C->A 0.74, G->A 0.64; C is 59% of wrong calls (n=23,349). HG002 35x: C->A 0.92, G->T 0.84, A->C 0.62, T->A 0.63 (n=101,990). spike: 1/3 each by code. Inferred consequence: real error alleles pile onto one alt base and one strand, which feeds callers' strand-bias filters. spike's are spread about 3x thinner. block_errors already sees (ref, called) for every counted base but does not store the called base.

limitations.what: spike emits Q2 on called bases and never emits N. In real binned NovaSeq data, Q2 occurs only on N.
limitations.evidence: K2b FASTQs (quality-speed-run/evidence/k2b, scratchpad map/fqstats.py): real R1 has 297 Q2 bases (R2 198), all N; spike seed 21 has 302 (R2 140), none of them N, and no N at all. Hospital chr20:10.0-11.5 Mb: 1,341 Q2 bases, all N. Cause: next_quality can draw Q2 at a non-N template base. The error table holds no counted Q2 bases, because Ns are left out at quality.rs:971, so the rate falls back to nominal 0.63. Real N rate: 2-3e-5 per base.

limitations.what: The last cycle is missing its quality and error rise. The position bins lump the last 16 cycles together, and the error end bin lumps the last 10.
limitations.evidence: Low-quality share at the last cycle against cycles 2-8 from the end: 35x real R1 5.76% vs 4.0-4.2% and R2 7.46% vs 5.3-6.1%; spike R1 3.95% vs 3.9-4.1% and R2 5.56% vs about 5.5%, flat (map/fqctx.py). Hospital: 2.13% at cycle 151 vs 1.42% at cycle 150. Mismatch rate (MD tags, 151M reads, the sample's SNP floor about 0.08 points included): hospital 0.354% vs 0.242%, 35x 0.802% vs 0.481% (map/mdcycle.py). Cycles 1-10 also err more on the hospital BAM (0.20-0.23% vs 0.178% mid-read).

limitations.what: In trimmed libraries, a read cut short by its fragment gets end-of-read quality and error contexts at its artificial end. Physically, its last base was a mid-run cycle.
limitations.evidence: Hospital chr20:10.0-11.5 Mb (map/trimends.py): reads of 90-130 bp with length = |TLEN| (n=4,124) have a low share of 0.73% over their last 10 cycles (0.63% at their last), against 1.55% over the last 10 cycles of 151 bp reads. spike uses cycles_left = rl - c with rl = min(cycles, frag) when generating, and qual.len() when learning, so the spike side is inferred from code. It affects about 1-3% of pairs.

limitations.what: There are no homopolymer slips. The default indel error rate is 0. With --indel-error-rate on, indels fall wherever a substitution would (mostly in poor tails), insert a uniformly random base and split 50/50, so they are not shaped like run-length changes. There is also a nit: an insertion pushes the unconsumed template base into the run tracker, and a deletion skips it.
limitations.evidence: From the v2 gate: slips with Q100 variants masked are 1.0% (A) and 1.6% (T) at runs of 12-14. Slips add only about 0.04 points to the clip share, so v2 left them out. Their effect on indel callers at homopolymers inside planted windows (where up to 100% of reads are synthetic) was never measured.

limitations.what: spike's qualities ignore the bases and their context, except one-letter runs.
limitations.evidence: 35x R1 low share, relative to overall, after the preceding trinucleotide: real GGA 1.62x, CCC 1.45x, AAA 1.25x; spike 1.01-1.10x for those. spike reaches 1.5-1.6x only at CpG trinucleotides, probably through the regional class mix (inferred) (map/fqctx.py). K5, by called base: real A .0189, C .0185, G .0156, T .0124; spike flat at .016-.017. The bases carry about 1% of bits per quality, so this was left out on purpose.

limitations.what: spike has no fragment-end (library-prep) motif. Starts are uniform, but the hospital library's read starts show strong composition bias over the first 11 cycles.
limitations.evidence: Hospital, chr20:10.0-11.5 Mb, n=345,632 (map/startcomp.py). Cycle 1: C .308 and G .269 against the background .198. Cycle 2: T .348 and G .160. Cycle 6: A .353 against .303. The pattern looks like Tn5 tagmentation (inferred). 35x HG002 shows only a mild bias (cycle 1 A .331). spike's reads take the background composition by construction, since their starts are uniform.

limitations.what: spike makes no duplicates, PCR or optical, of its own reads.
limitations.evidence: Hospital Picard metrics: 17,385,340 of 369,010,019 pairs are duplicates (4.71%), and 10,361,338 of those are optical (59.6%). In spiked regions, the duplicate share is 0.008 against 0.036 real. Callers skip duplicates, so the effect is mainly on QC.
limitations.where: src/synth.rs:418-439 (only junction-DUP depth copies are jittered, on purpose); memory duplicates.md

limitations.what: Untrimmed libraries get no adapter read-through: no fragment is shorter than the read length.
limitations.evidence: In the 35x untrimmed slice, 0.71% of all reads, 25.7% of clipped reads, have adapter clips; spike has 0. The adapter is learnable: past TLEN, the consensus equals TruSeq R1/R2 for 33 bp and then the index.

limitations.what: Some real soft clips are not modelled: chimeric fragments, sequence not in the reference, and simple repeats. Overall, any-clip share is spike 0.94% against 2.42% real at K2.
limitations.evidence: Chimeric 0.13% of reads, not in reference 0.10%, repeats 0.04%. Leaving them out was the user's decision.

limitations.what: Synthetic templates carry the sample's SNPs only, not its own indels or SVs (CR3), so planting removes the background indels from the replaced share of reads.
limitations.evidence: 38 of 40 seeded footprints hold at least one HG002 non-SNP record (median 4.5). A hom 2 bp deletion under a het DUP comes out at AF 0.360 instead of 1.0.

limitations.what: One depth and uniform starts for the whole event, so local depth structure is lost (CR2). GC bias itself is small in the hospital library.
limitations.evidence: Depth fold on 40 DUPs: 1.11-2.46, median 1.27; 6 of 40 above 1.5, mostly mappability. Event 39 (GC 0.593) is at 28.2x against an anchor of 45.4x. Hospital GC curve, measured this session (map/gcbias.py, observed/uniform): 0.88-1.08 over GC 0.25-0.75 on chr19:10-13 Mb (LDLR region), and 0.90-1.02 on chr20:10-13 Mb. Het DEL depth inside: spike 0.47, real carriers 0.52.

limitations.what: The error table has no mate dimension, but real R2 errs more than R1 at the same quality.
limitations.evidence: Mismatches in 151M aligned reads, with a sample-SNP floor of about 0.1%: hospital Q9 R2 10.47% vs R1 8.53%, Q24 0.43% vs 0.32%; 35x Q11 9.12% vs 7.13%, Q25 0.39% vs 0.23% (map/mateq.py). Whether spike's class dimension absorbs this is not measured.

limitations.what: spike's crashed reads are about 15% short, and run-free reads clip too little on the hospital BAM.
limitations.evidence: K1: crashed 0.88% vs 1.16%. K2b: 0.90-0.91% vs 1.06% (z -3.7 to -3.9). Hospital K2, bad-end clips in run bin 0: spike 0.26% vs own 0.73%. Mismatches per 100 aligned bases: 0.270 vs 0.308.

limitations.what: 5' soft clips: real reads clip at their sequencing start in about 0.4% of reads. spike's first cycles have no error excess beyond what their quality gives.
limitations.evidence: Measured: 5' clips 0.42% hospital, 0.41% 35x (1-4 bp: 0.125% and 0.106%) (map/clipends.py). spike's 5'-clip share is not measured.

limitations.what: The run-bin edges are constants fitted on one NovaSeq 6000 dataset. There is no detection of BQSR-recalibrated input (OQ tags or @PG BaseRecalibrator).
limitations.evidence: Hard-coded at quality.rs:126-135. grep finds no OQ or BQSR handling in src/. In v1, raw qualities were checked by hand from @PG. Portability to 4-colour, DNBSEQ or AVITI chemistries is unmeasured.

limitations.what: In the FASTQ route, reads go through two rounds of processing. The model is learned from the post-fastp BAM (with --correction on overlaps and a quality filter that drops 2.82%), and spike's reads then pass fastp again.
limitations.evidence: The hospital pipeline's fastp flags and drop rates are recorded in the hospital-demo-plan memory. The effect on spike's reads is not measured.

limitations.what: spike does not model tile- or cycle-correlated events (bubbles), index hopping, or library errors shared by both mates or by duplicates (PCR, 8-oxoG, deamination).
limitations.evidence: Not measured. Tiles are assigned by hash, independent of quality. At hom SNVs, real data shows 0.17% ref reads; spike's planted hom sites have 0 old-allele reads.

open_issues: Learn the substitution matrix P(called | true, quality symbol, mate) inside block_errors, which already compares every counted base with the reference (quality.rs:979), and use it in place of random_different_base. Falsifier: after bwa-mem2, spike's Q<15 mismatch spectrum in sequencing orientation against the sample's (hospital A->C 0.91, T->C 0.89). Also report the alt-allele concentration per error site and strand.

Tie Q2 to N: learn P(N | quality symbol) from the sample, and emit N when the drawn quality is N-only. Falsifier: Q2 bases that are not N in spike's output must be 0, and the N rate must be within 2x of real (2-3e-5 per base).

Final cycle: add one dedicated last-cycle position in the quality key and in end_bin. Do not refine the bins in general: 19 position bins lost in bits per quality (0.3858 vs 0.3826). Falsifier: the last-cycle low share and mismatch rate against real (35x R1 5.76% / 0.802%; hospital 2.13% / 0.354%). Cheap to test, and worth checking whether it moves the 15% crash shortfall.

Physical cycle axis for trimmed libraries: use cycles_left = read_length - c in both learning and generation. Falsifier: the last-10-cycle low share of fragment-limited reads (real 0.73% against 1.55% for full reads).

Homopolymer slip model: ReadState already tracks run_base and run_len. Learn slip rates by run length, base and strand from the sample's aligned indels at reference runs, with a pileup variant mask. Falsifier: indel-caller FP/FN at 8-14 bp runs in windows planted with a hom SNV, spike against unplanted. The v2 gate measured slips only for clips.

Fragment-end motif: learn a 5'-start k-mer enrichment from the startup sample's read starts, and weight the uniform starts by it (by rejection or importance). Falsifier: the composition of SPIKE_ reads at cycles 1-11 against the hospital sample's.

Replace-in-place tiling for non-additive events: remake each suppressed pair at its own start and length mapped through the haplotype, and draw only the junction or novel fragments fresh. This keeps local depth, GC, mappability, fragment lengths and the end motif without a coverage estimate. Falsifier: the depth fold goes to 1, the depth correlation per 100 bp with the unspiked BAM, and the AF dispersion at planted het SNVs against real hets. Never proposed or refuted in the plans or case file.

Duplicates of spike's own reads at the sample's Picard rates: optical (same tile, nearby x/y, independent sequencing errors) and PCR (same fragment). Falsifier: the Picard duplicate share in spiked regions (now 0.008 vs 0.036).
Adapter read-through for untrimmed libraries, from a learned per-mate adapter consensus. Falsifier: the adapter-clip share after alignment (0.71% real vs 0% spike on 35x).
CR3: synthetic templates carry the sample's SNPs only. Option B (fail closed / label) or option A (sample haplotype model) is still the user's decision.
BQSR/OQ detection: warn or refuse when the input carries OQ tags or @PG BaseRecalibrator/ApplyBQSR, or learn from OQ.

Unexplained: crashed reads are about 15% short (K1/K2b), and hospital run-free bad-end clips are 0.26% vs 0.73% (K2). Cheap diagnostic: split K2's bad-end clips by 5' vs 3' end and by clip length. Real 5' clips are about 0.42% of reads.

Docs drift, found while reading. README.md:1968 says 'A pool under 1,000 read pairs gets a warning', but the warning is now on the startup sample at 50,000 (synth.rs:31). README.md:1972, the main.rs:1912-1913 error text and the synth.rs:8-9 module doc still say the base qualities come from the event's pool. docs/analysis/soft-clips/README.md:29 still says 'first-order Markov chain'. README.md:1955 still claims the 31-value alphabet over-crashes (24% vs 14%), which the unmerged quality-speed branch corrects as a test artifact.
The quality-speed branch (1.18x, byte-identical, K3/K6 corrections) is not yet merged. Merging it needs a merge or rebase, because master moved to b901339.

map:validate.subsystem: Validation and measurement tooling: spike validate (src/validate.rs), the census (src/census.rs), truth.rs's own checks, the realism yardsticks in scripts/ (transplant, realism probe, origin physics, real_events, validate_pipeline.sh) and the records in docs/review/*
map:validate.summary: `spike validate` (src/validate.rs:154-211) loads a spike truth VCF (load_truth_events, :893-1095) and runs per-event checks chosen by type in check_event (:540-693), plus three [global] library heuristics read from a sample of the event windows (:2546-2926). Each row is either gating (counted in the exit status) or advisory (left out unless --strict; counted_rows :290). A check that cannot run, or cannot measure, is a FAIL, never a silent pass (check_outcome :128, event_not_evaluable :2822, event_checked :674-689). Since RF13 and RF14 the deciding rows for INS and DEL are provenance checks: spike's own SPIKE_evNNNN_hap_ reads carrying a 31-base junction probe (:1571, :1651). Rows that depend on how the aligner writes the event (split_reads for DEL, ins_reads) were made advisory after the realism probe showed they fail real HG002 variants. DUP, INV and BND are still decided by split_reads, which has never been measured on real variants (:582-583). Small variants are graded by allele_freq: a binomial central-99% test with a power floor and one vote per fragment, using haplotype-distance voting for indels (N15, N18). census.rs computes SIM_RESIST and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD at simulation time, warning at 0.10 and 1.5 and refusing above 0.5. truth.rs asserts that its parallel slices line up, in release builds too. Realism is judged outside validate. The main yardsticks are the HG001<->HG002 transplant rounds (read-count metrics J, E1, A, E against real carriers, with a real-vs-real control and broken-dose controls), the realism probe (validate's own rows run on real variants) and the quality-model K tests against held-out real reads. validate_pipeline.sh is a Delly-only, DEL-only test of gain over the background. No measurement anywhere asks whether a variant caller calls a spiked variant the way it calls the real one. Every transplant plan lists callers as out of scope.

algorithms.name: Gating vs advisory row policy and exit status
algorithms.how: Every row carries an advisory flag, set at one place (check_outcome). failure_message and the JSON counted_* trio both read one filter: strict || !advisory. An event covered only by advisory rows still gets a failing event_checked row. A row that errored keeps its advisory standing.

algorithms.name: coverage_ratio / coverage_any_mapq (DEL, DUP)
algorithms.how: Mean aligned-base depth (M/=/X only, since review finding 5) over [start,end) divided by the mean of the two flank windows of --flank bp each (default 5000). PASS if |ratio - (1-VAF)| < 0.3 for a DEL, or |ratio - (1+VAF)| < 0.3 for a DUP. Fewer than 1x of flank depth is a FAIL. The any-MAPQ copy is advisory. One mean over the whole span (CR9).

algorithms.name: del_planted (DEL, gating, RF14)
algorithms.how: Reads named SPIKE_evNNNN_hap_ (N from the truth ID sim_del_N) within 500 bp of START or END. Any record that is not secondary or supplementary counts, whatever its MAPQ or duplicate flag. A read carries the event if a window matches ref[START-15,START)+ref[END,END+16) in either orientation with at most 2 mismatches. One carrier is enough.

algorithms.name: ins_planted (INS, gating, RF13)
algorithms.how: The same name filter, within 150 bp of POS. There are two 31-base junction probes, one per end of the insertion: 15 reference bases, then 16 bases past the junction. Every inserted base must match exactly, and at most 2 flank bases may differ. One carrier is enough. Without a sim_ins_N ID, or with a symbolic <INS> ALT, the row is a not-evaluable FAIL.

algorithms.name: split_reads / split_reads_each_end (DUP/INV/BND gating; DEL advisory)
algorithms.how: Counts primary reads at MAPQ >= --min-mapq within 500 bp of each breakpoint whose SA:Z names the partner contig at a position within 500 bp. Pooled: at least 2 distinct names over both ends. Each-end (advisory): at least 2 at each end. Only the SA contig and position are parsed, never strand, CIGAR or sequence. The each-end row is blind for spans of 500 bp or less.

algorithms.name: ins_reads / ins_sequence (INS, advisory)
algorithms.how: ins_reads: at least 2 reads with an I of at least min(SVLEN,50) bp, or a soft clip of at least 50 bp once SVLEN >= 50, within 100 bp of POS. Reads the CIGAR only. ins_sequence: at least 2 reads holding the first or last k=min(len,31)-mer of the ALT, in either orientation. Not evaluable when k < 12 or when the k-mer occurs in the reference within 1 kb.

algorithms.name: allele_freq (SNV/MNV/small indel, gating)
algorithms.how: Votes are per fragment (mates that disagree cast no vote). The model is Binomial(n, p_obs), with p_obs = VAF*(1-0.01) + (1-VAF)*0.001. The row is not evaluable when power to clear the error floor (at least 3 alt reads, tail 0.005) is below 0.99, or when depth is below 5. PASS requires the count to be inside the central 99%. Indels vote by Levenshtein distance between the read's bases and the reference haplotype with and without the edit, combined with up to 10 nearby truth records (N15 third attempt). A read votes only if it reaches 10 bp past the repeat region on both sides (N18). MNVs are read jointly. Complex alleles are a FAIL.

algorithms.name: Global library heuristics
algorithms.how: Up to 200k primary mapped records, an equal share per event window (the head of each window). insert_size: mean 50-1000 and SD 5-300. dup_rate: below 50%, and needs either duplicate flags or an @PG markdup step (otherwise not evaluable). mean_mapq: above 20. Fixed ranges, never compared with the donor.

algorithms.name: Census rows (advisory, read back from the truth VCF)
algorithms.how: Prints SIM_RESIST against <= census::WARN_ABOVE (0.10) and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD against <= 1.5. A missing field or '.' gives no row. An unparseable value is an advisory FAIL. Nothing is recomputed from the BAM.

algorithms.name: Resistant-read census and RF8 refusal (simulation time)
algorithms.how: Counts primary, non-duplicate, non-QC-fail reads at any MAPQ over census_spans. A read whose name is not in the editable donor pool is resistant. Warns above 0.10 and refuses above 0.5 unless --allow-resistant. Depth fold warns above 1.5. All thresholds are documented as unchecked for --edit-model origin.

algorithms.name: Truth-writer invariants
algorithms.how: Release-mode assert_eq! that the adjusted_afs, resistant, depth_folds and alt_frags slices have the same length as events (RF1). Writes SIM_VAF (simulated), SIM_REQ_VAF, SIM_ALT_FRAGS (planted pairs that show the event), SIM_RESIST and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD. GT = 1/1 iff VAF >= 0.9.

algorithms.name: Transplant realism test (HG001<->HG002)
algorithms.how: Spike donor-only het variants into the other sample using the hospital aligner command (-M -K 1e8). Read evidence with code independent of spike, from recipient minus replaced_reads plus sim.bam. Deletions: J = n_any/flank_depth and E1 = interior/flank depth. Small variants: A (exact carriers) and E (any form). DUPs: J. Compare d = fake - real against c = real - real at shared het sites. Controls: B1 (VAF 0.25) and B2 (200 bp off) must fail, and a sham must show 0. Round 3 judges rho = R_f/R_c with split-half per-site noise, pass if the bootstrap 95th percentile is <= 2.25.

algorithms.name: Realism probe (validate's rows on real variants)
algorithms.how: Writes isolated T2T-Q100 chr20 INS of 20-49 bp and DEL of 500 bp or more as spike-format truth, runs spike validate --json on HG002's own BAM, and compares with spike's runs at the same or similar events.

algorithms.name: End-to-end harness
algorithms.how: GIAB HG002 het DELs of 500-50,000 bp, spiked into the NA18488 chr20 background at several VAFs, then align.sh and merge.sh, spike validate (step 5 needs at least one non-advisory PASS), Delly -t DEL, and Truvari --passonly -r 500 -p 0.5 -P 0.5. A background control gives Recall_outside_bg and the --min-gain gate.

algorithms.name: Other real-data harnesses and probes
algorithms.how: slice_loop.sh and real_events.sh run spike, align, merge and validate per event on a ±PAD slice, and real_events_score.py scores the JSON. low_af/locate.py places reads on the haplotype by 20-mer seeds, independently of spike, to check SIM_ALT_FRAGS. carried/probe.py is the kill test for the carried-allele refusal. duplicates/measure.py measures the old-allele leak after re-marking duplicates. origin_physics.py is a synthetic exact-twin genome with wgsim truth. The quality-model K1/K2/K2b runs compare spike reads with held-out real reads (crash share, SD ratio, bad-end clips).
algorithms.where: scripts/slice_loop.sh:1-31, scripts/real_events.sh, scripts/real_events_score.py, scripts/low_af/locate.py, scripts/carried/probe.py, scripts/duplicates/measure.py, scripts/origin_physics.py:1-31, docs/analysis/quality-model-v2/clipscore.py, docs/analysis/soft-clips/

limitations.what: Caller-level equivalence has never been measured for any variant type: whether a caller (DeepVariant/GATK for small variants; Manta, TIDDIT, CNVnator or gCNV for SVs) makes the same call, genotype, QUAL/GQ and breakpoint on a spiked variant as on the real carrier.
limitations.evidence: Every transplant plan scopes callers out: round 1 lists 'SV callers (round 2)' under 'Not in this round' (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:115), and round 2 lists 'Callers' (2026-09-28-transplant-round2.md:185). The transplant metrics are read counts only. validate_pipeline.sh compares no genotype (README.md:2354-2360) and measures gain over background, not equivalence to a real carrier. Manta missing ClinVar 4845403 even on the full BAM has no real-carrier comparison (memory sv-caller-slices.md, hospital-demo-plan.md).

limitations.what: DUP, INV and BND are still decided by split_reads, a rule about what the aligner writes, which has never been checked on real variants. For DELs and INS the same kind of rule failed most real variants. It reads only the SA contig and position, so it never checks that an INV's segments are on opposite strands.
limitations.evidence: Comment 'DUP, INV and BND were not measured and are unchanged' (validate.rs:582-583). The realism probe found split_reads failing 12 of 20 and 9 of 15 real DELs (REVIEW.md:5570-5583). The SA parser stops after two fields (validate.rs:3383-3394; README.md:852-857).

limitations.what: The deciding INS and DEL rows are provenance checks only. A single SPIKE_ read with the join passes, which proves neither the AF nor that a caller sees realistic evidence. Where the join is already reference sequence, they show presence, not removal.
limitations.evidence: MIN_PLANTED_READS = 1 (validate.rs:338). README.md:938-947: 9 of 12 and 10 of 12 RF14 real sites have a reference-spelled join. The independent review says the same (2026-10-04-independent-review.md:129).

limitations.what: coverage_ratio is one mean over the whole span with a fixed ±0.3 tolerance. A large local depth error passes it.
limitations.evidence: A het DUP over an interior read at 4.32x passed at 1.32 against an expected 1.50 (README.md:812-818; REVIEW.md CR2/CR9:3243-3246). SIM_DEPTH_FOLD only warns and does not correct.

limitations.what: The [global] checks are fixed heuristics, not compared with the donor library, and the spike-in barely moves them. validate cannot read the donor BAM, so a donor-relative insert-size check is impossible today.
limitations.evidence: insert_size 50-1000/5-300, dup <50%, MAPQ >20 (validate.rs:2841-2926). On NA18488 they moved by 0.4 MAPQ and all passed on the unspiked background (REVIEW.md:417-427). CR9 'What remains' says this needs the donor BAM (REVIEW.md:3275-3280). parse_validate_args_from takes only bam, truth, reference, min-mapq, flank, json and strict (validate.rs:708-792).

limitations.what: validate has no background baseline or delta mode. N1's requirement that each check be read as spiked minus unspiked is only in external harnesses. spike has no pre-flight check that the donor already carries a requested SV; carried.rs covers small variants only.
limitations.evidence: N1: 7 of 8 truth DELs were already depleted in NA18488, and the background scored 7/19 against 6/19 spiked (REVIEW.md:379-401, :450-463). README.md:1604 limits the carried-allele refusal to small variants.

limitations.what: validate never reads SIM_ALT_FRAGS, the planted pairs that show the event, so it cannot tell reads lost in align, merge or the FASTQ route from an event that was simply sparse.
limitations.evidence: CensusInfo reads only SIM_RESIST and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD (validate.rs:83-101). Grep: SIM_ALT_FRAGS does not appear in validate.rs outside a test fixture string at :3985.

limitations.what: The transplant yardstick covers SNVs, 1-49 bp indels, DELs of 50 bp to 10 kb and DUPs of 50-299 bp in clean mode on chr20-scale benchmark regions. It excludes DUPs of 300 bp or more, INV, BND/fusion, non-tandem INS of 50 bp or more, MNV/complex, origin mode, and base quality, MAPQ and strand of carrying reads. Round 3 is 5/16 supported, 0 refuted and 11 inconclusive.
limitations.evidence: round2 plan 'Not in this round' (2026-09-28-transplant-round2.md:179-185). Round 3 result table (2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:165-188).

limitations.what: Real-vs-real agreement is better than counting noise at DUP J, INS20-49 A and INS1-4 A (R_c < 1). This is unexplained, and it inflates rho, keeping those groups inconclusive.
limitations.evidence: R_c of 0.61, 0.50 and 0.69. Split-half calibration 1.2165, thought to be mate double-counting, which is an inference (round3 plan :222-232).

limitations.what: spike's short insertions are cleaner than real ones (RF15). The cause is unmeasured, and transplant INS20-49 cannot settle it.
limitations.evidence: ins_reads fails spike's 20-39 bp INS 0 of 16 against 47 of 112 real HG002 ones (CLINICAL_SV_NEW_FINDINGS.md:451-469). INS20-49 is inconclusive in both directions in rounds 2b and 3.

limitations.what: Read-level realism gaps that callers may notice remain: crashed reads about 15% too few, too few soft clips on run-free reads on the hospital BAM, and no synthetic duplicates in spiked regions.
limitations.evidence: Commit 7f28bb0: crash 0.88% vs 1.16% and bad-end clips 0.94% vs 1.38%. Memory quality-model-run.md: run-free reads clip 0.26% vs 0.73%. Memory duplicates.md: duplicate share 0.008 vs 0.036.

limitations.what: Background non-SNP variants in the event footprint are erased (CR3). They are near-universal, and their effect on calls is quantified by one number only.
limitations.evidence: T7: 38 of 40 footprints hold a carried non-SNP record (REVIEW.md:4634-4651). The only impact measurement is a hom 2 bp deletion falling to AF 0.360 under a het DUP.

limitations.what: Truth GT ignores input GT and ploidy: GT is 1/1 iff VAF >= 0.9. This limits any genotype-concordance test with callers.
limitations.evidence: genotype_from_vaf (truth.rs:468-474). CR7 input-GT and ploidy parts are open (REVIEW.md:3159-3164, :3196).

limitations.what: The allele_freq error model uses fixed constants (ALT 0.001, REF 0.01) rather than the sample's learned error table. Its false-FAIL rate on real data is known only for HG002 35x.
limitations.evidence: Constants at validate.rs:1747-1750. Real GIAB out-of-range: 2.6% of indels (8.7% near other records) and 0.6-0.8% of SNVs (README.md:1137-1157).

limitations.what: The census thresholds (0.10 warn, 0.5 refuse, 1.5 fold) have not been calibrated for --edit-model origin.
limitations.evidence: origin_thresholds_note (census.rs:269-277).

limitations.what: All realism evidence comes from one or two NovaSeq libraries (HG002 35x and the hospital HG001/HG002 30x) and mostly from chr20. The adapter-trimming heuristic is specific to these datasets, and the FASTQ route has not been run on the real raw FASTQ through the full raredisease pipeline.
limitations.evidence: Deck limitations slide: 'one sample (HG002, 35x), chromosome 20, BAM route' (docs/presentation/slides/next.html). Independent review, library trimming row (2026-10-04-independent-review.md:124). Memory hospital-demo-plan.md: the FASTQ route was tested on a stand-in.

Run the hospital's own callers on (a) the donor's real BAM and (b) the recipient spiked BAM, aligned with the hospital command. ideas.title: Coverage-preserving edit: remap each event-copy donor fragment through the haplotype instead of uniform re-tiling
ideas.problem: Non-additive events suppress every event-copy pool pair inside event +/- 2 kb and tile n = cov*v*starts/f fragments at uniform starts, scaled by one anchor depth. The footprint's local depth shape, duplicates, real quality strings and background indels are discarded, and the work done and the removal list grow with the footprint instead of with the changed bases.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED this session (scratchpad perf/dup1; current-master code = binary quality-speed-run/bin/spike-new; 35x HG002 BAM, dup:chr20:14550000-15550000, seed 1, 1 thread): 63,390 pairs suppressed, 120,046 tiled, 72,263 pairs listed for removal from the raw FASTQ (8,873 of them duplicates), SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 4.69 (bin chr20:14862000-14863000 at 9.9x against a 50.3x scaling depth). Only 17 of the 120,046 tiled pairs show the junction (SIM_ALT_FRAGS=17). DOCUMENTED: CR2 probe read 81.09x where 28.13x was expected; 40 chr20 DUPs had folds of 1.11-2.46 (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR2; README.md:1858-1866). INFERRED from simulate.rs:817 with HAP_FLANK 2000 and a 421 bp mean fragment: about 88% of an SNV's remade pairs never touch the site. Code: suppression at simulate.rs:249-264, uniform starts at simulate.rs:1062-1065, one anchor depth at simulate.rs:266-280. The coverage-preserving primitive already exists. The legacy junction model makes one depth copy per original inside the DUP, with +/-20 bp jitter and a new length (synth.rs:418-510, jitter at :434-436).
ideas.proposal: Replace uniform re-tiling for non-additive events with an exact image map from reference fragments to haplotype fragments. Each pool pair is drawn for the event copy with the same copy_rate coin as today. Then: (a) If its fragment overlaps no changed base or junction, leave the original untouched: not removed, not rewritten. (b) If it crosses a changed span, remove it and emit one synthetic pair at its image start on the haplotype, with its own fragment length. For a DEL, starts inside [S,E) vanish and starts left of S extend across the join; for INV, INS and SNV only boundary-crossing fragments are remade. (c) For sequence that appears twice in the haplotype (a DUP), emit one extra fragment per event-copy original. Give it a fresh nearby start and a new length, reusing generate_depth_pair's jitter, so Picard sees no exact positional duplicates. Keeping the same start would make the copy-2 image a positional duplicate of the original. (d) For novel sequence longer than a fragment, draw interior fragments at the local start density measured from pool starts beside the insertion point. (e) Optionally give each remade pair its original's duplicate-family size. Per base, depth becomes donor depth x (1 - v + v*copies) by construction. These events then no longer need cov, the floor of 2 (except in novel interiors) or SIM_DEPTH_FOLD. Work and removal lists scale with the fragments over the change. A DUP removes only the ~cov*v pairs that cross the first copy's end.
ideas.simplest_version: DUP only. Full-model DUPs keep every original and add the legacy depth copies (synth.rs:454) for the interior. Only event-copy pairs that cross E are replaced, with haplotype pairs at their own start and length. Other event types are unchanged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 BAM, after align.sh and merge.sh: (1) The CR2 dup_variable probe interior must read 28.13x +/- 5% (today 81.09x). (2) On the 40 seeded chr20 DUPs and on chr20:14.55-15.55 Mb, take bins of 1 kb where at least 95% of reads have MAPQ >= 20. In at least 95% of them, the merged/donor depth ratio must lie inside the Poisson 99% band around 1+v. A uniform-tiling build fails this where the fold is 4.69. (3) A sham run (v=0) leaves the merged.bam records identical to the input. (4) Transplant rounds 1b, 2b and 3 keep every supported verdict. (5) The Picard duplicate share inside the footprint stays within the 95% CI of the unspiked rate. Kill if (1), (2) or (4) fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No build is needed. Run the existing binary twice, with --dup-model junction (its interior is per-original depth copies) and with --dup-model full. Use the 1 Mb chr20 DUP above and the CR2 dup_variable probe. Align both and compute the per-1 kb-bin output/donor depth inside the DUP with samtools depth. If junction-mode interiors track 1+v bin by bin while full mode shows the 4.69 fold, the coverage-preserving principle holds on real reads. If junction mode is off too, the cause is alignment or mappability, and the idea dies for DUPs.
ideas.impact: CNV callers in raredisease (gCNV, CNVnator, TIDDIT coverage) would see the donor's own depth shape times the copy number instead of a flat anchor depth. Outside the remade fragments, flank indels, duplicates and real qualities survive, which covers most of CR3's +/-2 kb exposure for SNVs. There would be fewer synthetic reads to align and much shorter removal lists for the FASTQ route; a DUP becomes nearly append-only.
ideas.risks: Copy assignment still comes from the same phase coin, so CR3 remains inside remade fragments. Resistant reads (CR4) are unchanged. A jittered DUP copy can still hit a real fragment's 5' ends by chance. Output bytes change for every non-additive event, so the transplant rounds must be re-run. The novel-interior density for long INS still needs an estimate.
ideas.history_check: Never tried. The map lists it as OPEN P1 (event-model reader) and as 'Replace-in-place tiling ... never proposed or refuted' (synthesis reader). CR2 option A, a learned start intensity, was never built. CR2 option B (SIM_DEPTH_FOLD, measure only) is done. T3's mappability attribution was retracted (judgment-gate-cases.md 2026-09-26), which is why this falsifier uses mappable bins only. The DUP jitter primitive already exists in the legacy junction model. The design notes advise against that model only because its junction reads are additive (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:303).

ideas.title: merge.sh: stream the original through `samtools view -N ^list` into `samtools merge --write-index`, with no outside.bam and no full re-sort
ideas.problem: merge.sh makes five full passes over a whole-genome BAM. The biggest runs on one thread: `view -N list -U outside.bam` compresses the 37 GB outside.bam single-threaded. Then come a merge, a full re-sort of data that is already sorted, a single-threaded index and a single-threaded `view -c` for a log line. Temp files reach 3-4x the BAM on a disk that is 88% full.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: B1 merge.sh took 1 h 42 min (sim.bam at 22:14:03, merge.log at 23:56:10) on a BAM of 37,083,621,094 bytes and 741,918,308 records (/home/parlar_ai/sv_slice_test/data/B1, logs/run.log). MEASURED this session on a real slice (scratchpad perf/bam): 35x HG002 chr20:10-30 Mb, 387 MB, 6,765,353 records, 1,496 listed names. Today's steps at 16 threads: view -N -U 36.77 s, merge 3.82 s, sort 4.92 s (in memory, no spill), index 2.17 s, view -c 2.10 s, total 49.8 s. Scaled x96-110, that is 80-91 min, consistent with B1. Adding -@16 to the view does NOT help (34.80 s): samtools 1.23 threads only the -o output, not -U (view -@16 -b -o /dev/null took 2.33 s, against 35.76 s on one thread). The replacement is a guard `view -@16 -c -N list` (0.92 s) plus `view -@16 -u -N ^list | merge -@16 --write-index -o merged.bam##idx##merged.bam.bai sim.bam -`. It took 4.04-4.25 s and gave the same records in the same order: md5 c809e24a for today's merge+sort, for merge alone and for the stream. The RG tag was stripped for this comparison only because my stand-in sim.bam shared the input's RG ID. It wrote a BAI directly (magic BAI\1). Code: src/main.rs:2516, 2538, 2542, 2543, 2546. df: /home is 88% full.
ideas.proposal: Generate merge.sh as three steps. (1) Guard: ACTUAL=$(samtools view -@T -c [-T REF] -N replaced_reads.txt ORIGINAL), abort if ACTUAL < NAMES (the same rule as today). (2) samtools view -@T -u [-T REF] -N ^replaced_reads.txt ORIGINAL | samtools merge -@T --write-index -o "merged.bam##idx##merged.bam.bai" sim.bam - . (3) Report the total from samtools idxstats, not from a full view -c. Write under a temp name and mv on success. Check that samtools supports `-N ^`; on older versions, say so clearly or fall back to today's path. For CRAM input, write CRAM against the same reference. A later step could splice at the BGZF level: copy untouched blocks verbatim and re-encode only the event windows and the blocks holding the listed names' SA-located records. Measure the streamed version first.
ideas.simplest_version: Two edits to the generated script: replace the view, merge and sort steps with the `-N ^` pipe into `merge --write-index`, and replace the final view -c with idxstats.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Use the B1 inputs: the 37 GB D24-14230 resample BAM, B1 sim.bam and replaced_reads.txt. (1) samtools view of the new merged.bam must md5-match today's merged.bam, record for record and in order. Headers must be equal apart from @PG. (2) The guard must still abort when ORIGINAL is another BAM (the 35x HG002 BAM). (3) Manta must open merged.bam with its BAI. (4) Wall time must be at most 20 min at 16 threads. A build that inverts the selection (-N without ^) fails the md5 and the record count. A build without the guard accepts the wrong BAM. Kill if the md5 differs or time is above 30 min.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done on the 387 MB real slice: 49.8 s became 4.0-4.25 s with the same record stream. Next, at the scale of hours: run today's and the new merge.sh on the 2.7 GB HG002 chr20 BAM with a real spike run's sim.bam, whose RG ID is 'sim' so nothing collides. Compare md5 and time, then do one B1-size run.
ideas.impact: The full-BAM SV-caller route drops from ~2 h 55 min per event to roughly Manta's 72 min plus ~8 min for the merge (inferred, x96-110 from the slice). This is the user's open choice between a locked fast route and the full route (memory sv-caller-slices.md). Peak disk falls from ~3-4x to ~1x the BAM. Every spike -> merged.bam loop (validate_pipeline.sh, the slice and real_events loops) gains in proportion.
ideas.risks: `-N ^FILE` needs a recent samtools. It is present in 1.23 here, but the minimum version is unchecked and the hospital container may be older. samtools merge renames colliding @RG/@PG IDs exactly as today. Without the ##idx## suffix, --write-index writes a CSI, and some callers want a BAI. The order of ties at one position must be re-checked on B1 (it was identical on the slice).
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map ('add -@ to view -N; count with view -c; drop the full re-sort; write the index during the merge'). The owner's sv-caller-slices note lists 'a faster spiked-BAM build' as an untested idea. This session corrects that plan: -@ alone gains nothing (34.8 s vs 36.8 s) because the -U output is unthreaded, and inverting the selection is what makes the pass parallel. Never built or refuted. Related measurement: realigning kept originals costs almost nothing. B1 align.log shows 0.30 s of compute against 43 s of index and reference loading for 5,326 reads, so leaving kept originals out of align.sh has no speed motive.

ideas.title: Whole-sample FASTQ: filter the two mates in parallel, keeping the per-record pairing check, then optionally splice natively with BGZF block copy
ideas.problem: fastq.sh sends both mates through one gawk process, reading R2 with getline from a FIFO. That caps throughput at ~165k pairs/s. With THREADS at 8 or below, pigz -6 on THREADS/2 per mate is close to a second bottleneck. Every raw record is decompressed, parsed in awk and recompressed, although only hundreds to tens of thousands of the ~380 M pairs change.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED this session (scratchpad perf/fq, perf/run). Input: 2,000,000 real HG002 NovaSeq pairs (the head of HG002.novaseq.chr20.R1/R2.fastq.gz) and 2,999 removed names, through the B1-generated fastq.sh. Times: 11.95 s at THREADS 8 and 12.22 s at THREADS 16 (~165k pairs/s). With pigz -1 at 16 threads: 12.24 s, unchanged, so awk is the cap (output 167 MB vs 137 MB). mawk instead of gawk: 19.21 s (worse). One gawk filter per mate, in parallel, with pigz -p8 -6 each: 5.41 s with identical content (no cross-mate check yet). Components: pigz -dc 1.52 s per mate (691 MB); compression 10.22 s with pigz -p4 -6 and 1.57 s with -p4 -1. The GIAB raw 40x FASTQ is BGZF: its first 8 MB are 651 BGZF blocks, 12,873 B compressed and 65,280 B uncompressed on average. DOCUMENTED: the hospital sample is one pair of 380 M reads per mate, lengths 35-151, and F3 predicted ~33 min (memory full-fastq.md). bwa infers the insert-size distribution per batch from the reads in that batch (B1 align.log: 'Inferring insert size distribution ... n: 5326'). Code: src/main.rs:2264 (ZIP threads), :2327 (getline from the FIFO), :2412 (the one awk), :2424-2428 (append at the end).
ideas.proposal: Stage 1 (shell, byte-identical): run one filter per mate in parallel, each with its own decompressor and pigz -p THREADS/2. Keep the per-record pairing guarantee: each awk writes its record names to a FIFO, and `cmp` reads both FIFOs, so any difference aborts. found/want and repeat counts are checked per mate. Stage 2 (native, optional): spike does the splice itself, with memchr record parsing, a HashSet of removed names, one thread per mate with a lock-step name check, and noodles' multithreaded BGZF writer. When the input is BGZF, it copies verbatim every compressed block that holds no removed record. It re-encodes only the blocks that do, plus a neighbour when a record spans a block boundary. Also: check the first raw header against the BAM's learned RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE before reading the whole file. Optionally write each SPIKE_ pair in a removed original's slot instead of all at the end, so a big event does not fill whole bwa -K batches on its own.
ideas.simplest_version: Stage 1 only: two awks, two pigz processes, a cmp over the two name FIFOs, and the same END checks as today.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Use real raw FASTQ: HG002.novaseq.chr20.R1/R2 with a removal list from a spike run on the matching chr20 BAM, then the hospital pair. (1) Decompressed outputs must be byte-identical to today's fastq.sh output for both mates. (2) Every refusal today's script makes must be reproduced: mates in different order, a listed name missing, a duplicated name, a truncated record, a raw FASTQ from another run. (3) Wall time at 16 threads must fall at least 2x for stage 1 and at least 5x for stage 2. A version without the cross-mate check accepts a swapped-order pair and fails. Kill stage 2 if it is not at least 2x faster than stage 1.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Add the cmp-over-FIFOs check to the per-mate script in the scratchpad and re-time the 2 M-pair test (today 12.22 s; 5.41 s without the check). Then run both on the full 0.85 GB chr20 raw pair. Before planning stage 2's block copy, check at the hospital whether the raw FASTQ starts with the BGZF 'BC' extra field (head -c 18 | xxd).
ideas.impact: Building each hospital sample's spiked FASTQ drops from ~33-39 min to ~15-17 min with stage 1 (inferred from the measured 2.25x). Stage 2 brings it to a few minutes (inferred): decompression-bound at ~1.5 s per 2 M-pair mate, or I/O-bound with BGZF block copy. The owner runs many samples. The fail-fast check saves a full scan of a wrong FASTQ. Slot interleaving removes the appended-batch question for big events.
ideas.risks: Per-mate filters must still give exactly today's refusals and its atomic publish. Stage 2 changes the compressed bytes (BGZF instead of pigz gzip), though not the content. Block copy works only on BGZF input. Interleaving changes record order (the same multiset of records), so its effect on alignment must be measured before it becomes the default.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map: 'Optional: a native Rust fastq route with parallel compression, held to byte-identical decompressed output', 'Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ' and 'Big events in the FASTQ route'. The one-awk design came from review finding 7 (mates in different orders, merged 658baa4), so stage 1 keeps a per-record check. F2 measured appended SPIKE_ reads as harmless for a small event (1,296/1,296). Not tried: the per-mate split, a native splice, BGZF block copy. New here: compression level does not move the wall time at 16 threads, mawk is slower, and the GIAB raw FASTQ is BGZF.

ideas.title: Per-event and per-fragment random streams: a panel run equals its single-event runs, and tiling can use every thread
ideas.problem: One StdRng seeded from --seed runs through every event in input order: haplotype building, suppression draws, tiling, then origin's draw. Adding, removing or reordering one event changes every later event's reads and realised fractions. The tiling loop cannot run in parallel without changing bytes.
ideas.evidence: Code: one StdRng at src/main.rs:614, passed by &mut through the events at :795 and :807-822. src/simulate.rs:259 draws only for replaceable pairs, so the stream also depends on the pool. Tiling at :1018-1086 is serial. DOCUMENTED: commit bccc43a, 'K7 FAIL by rule (2 allele_freq flips from the reordered random stream)'. README.md:1354-1361: a 3 Mb DUP takes 44.3 s at 1 thread and 26.5 s at 16. MEASURED this session (scratchpad perf/dup1): tiling plus synthesis of 120,046 pairs took 3.52 s of a 19.21 s run on a 1 Mb DUP at 1 thread, and that step is serial at any --threads. scripts/transplant/transplant.py:243-266 re-runs the remaining events after each RF8 refusal, so every accepted event's reads change between attempts.
ideas.proposal: Derive each event's stream from (seed, hash of the event's canonical spec). Derive each tiled fragment's draws from (event stream, fragment index), e.g. StdRng::seed_from_u64(splitmix(seed ^ hash(spec) ^ index)) or ChaCha's stream and word position. Draw the suppression coin per pool pair from (event, hash of the pair name) instead of the shared stream. Then tile fragments in parallel with rayon, collect them in index order, and run independent events in parallel. origin's final draw keys on (seed, family). Output stays independent of --threads; it changes once relative to today's bytes.
ideas.simplest_version: Per-event streams only (seed ^ hash(spec)), with each event's internal order kept serial. This gives order independence without parallel tiling.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 BAM: (1) Invariance: take two events 100 kb apart. Each event's SPIKE_ reads, suppressed names and truth INFO in the 2-event run must be byte-identical to its 1-event run and to the reversed-order run. Today's binary fails this. (2) Equivalence: on the docs/presentation round-trip events (K7's set), SIM_ALT_FRAGS, the validate verdicts (allele_freq, del_planted, ins_planted) and realised AF must fall inside master's 5-seed spread. (3) --threads 1, 4 and 16 give identical bytes. (4) With per-fragment streams, the 3 Mb DUP wall time at 16 threads drops below today's 26.5 s. Kill if (1), (2) or (3) fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Before building: time the tiling step of the 3 Mb DUP at 16 threads from log timestamps, as done here at 1 thread for 1 Mb, to bound the parallel gain. Count, in the transplant logs, how many accepted events RF8 retries re-drew. If tiling is under ~15% of the wall time at 16 threads, build only the per-event stream.
ideas.impact: Hospital panels (many genes in one sample) become composable: adding or dropping a variant does not change the others' reads, so caller results can be compared across reruns. Transplant retries and the B1/B2 arms stop re-drawing accepted events. K7-style gates stop failing on stream reordering. The serial floor of big events shrinks, by up to the ~10 s tiling share of a 3 Mb DUP (inferred).
ideas.risks: Every output changes once, so all locked byte-identity baselines must be re-cut. Seeding per fragment adds a small cost per fragment. Two identical specs in one run would share a stream; the overlap rule already refuses them. origin's single draw must keep its per-family meaning.
ideas.history_check: On 2026-09-27 the user chose threads step 1 (only work that draws no random numbers, byte-identical) and not step 2 (memory threads-step1.md). The map keeps per-event RNG streams OPEN. New evidence since then: the v1 quality-model K7 failure was attributed to stream reordering (bccc43a), the transplant retry loop re-draws accepted events, and the serial tiling share is now measured. Not refuted, but it needs the user's word because the bytes change.

ideas.title: Reuse the learned quality profile across runs on the same input (save and load), byte-identical
ideas.problem: Every run re-reads 20 blocks of 50 kb and re-learns the fqzcomp contexts and error tables, even for a single SNV. Since v2 this is the largest fixed cost of a small run.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED this session (scratchpad perf/dup1/log.txt): 'Quality sample: 20 blocks ... 126228 pairs; read in 2.6 s, learned in 4.1 s', i.e. 7.0 s of a 19.21 s run at 1 thread on the 35x BAM. DOCUMENTED: K4 measured reads of 0.3-2.8 s and learning of 1.2-3.3 s (plan 2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md, as summarised in the map). Before v2, a 1 kb DEL took 0.55 s in total (README.md:1354). Code: src/main.rs:659-664, src/quality.rs:476-506. Harnesses run spike many times per BAM: the transplant.py spike_run loop (:243-266), the slice loop and the real_events loop. Note: master is now 4a5672d, with the quality-speed run-ratio table merged and pushed (memory quality-speed-run.md), not b901339 as the map says.
ideas.proposal: Serialise the learned profile to a versioned binary file: alphabet, class cuts, joint and class_run counts, both ContextMaps and the error tables. Key it by spike version, canonical input path, size, mtime, index mtime, --min-mapq, read length and reference identity. --quality-profile FILE loads the file when the key matches and refuses otherwise, or writes it when it does not exist. learn's fill step recomputes the run-ratio table.
ideas.simplest_version: A --save-quality-profile / --quality-profile pair with a hand-written length-prefixed format and a strict key check. No automatic cache directory.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 and hospital BAMs, three cases: 35x dup+snp at seed 1, threads 8; the K6 events; 35x del at seed 7, threads 1. (1) Every output file must be md5-identical between a fresh run and a run that loads the saved profile. (2) A profile saved at --min-mapq 20 must be refused at --min-mapq 0 and on another BAM. A build that ignores the key loads it, and its md5 differs from the fresh run. (3) Wall time drops by about the logged read+learn time. Kill on any md5 difference.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Sum the 'read in X s, learned in Y s' log lines over one transplant or slice campaign's spike logs to get the total time at stake. If it is under ~10 minutes per campaign, do not build.
ideas.impact: Removes 1.5-7 s from every run, which is most of a small event's run time. Helps harness loops and repeated hospital runs on the same demo BAM. No output changes.
ideas.risks: A stale profile could be reused silently if the key misses something, e.g. a BAM rewritten in place with the same size and mtime. The format must follow every change to the profile struct. The gain is small for one-off runs.
ideas.history_check: Not proposed before. The startup sample itself replaced per-pool learning after v1 was refuted (bccc43a). The last speed step, the run-ratio cache (quality-speed, merged as 4a5672d), was also byte-identical. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Drop the pass-2 edge-strip and one-pass re-read plans: per-event time goes to compute in the LOH and duplicate scans, not to re-reading the BAM
ideas.problem: Two open plans in the map target BAM re-reads: pass 2 re-reading the whole widened window, and the ~6 reads of each region. Measured, re-reads are cheap. The time sits in per-record work: the LOH pileup and phasing, and the clean-mode duplicate scan, which builds an OriginRecord with an owned name for every record before filtering.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED this session (scratchpad perf/dup1/log.txt, the 1 Mb DUP on the 35x BAM at 1 thread): pass 1 0.79 s, pass 2 0.30 s (1.6% of 19.21 s), census 0.44 s, LOH pileup 1.71 s plus phasing 0.85 s, duplicate scan 2.07 s, FASTQ write 1.74 s. Plain htslib decoding of the same 1 Mb window (300,045 records) took 0.14-0.21 s (samtools view -c, and view > /dev/null). So each extra read costs ~0.2-0.3 s, and the scans cost seconds. Code: src/origin.rs:1033-1054 (scan_long, then filter by duplicate flag or name), src/loh.rs:600-720 and :1036-1061, src/extract.rs:118-180 (pass 2). DOCUMENTED: on a 3 Mb event the duplicate re-read costs 5-6 s at 1 thread (README.md:1365).
ideas.proposal: Do not build pass-2 strips or a unified streaming pass. Instead, run perf on the LOH pileup and the duplicate scan on the 1 Mb and 3 Mb events and fix what dominates. In the duplicate scan, test the flag bit and a name lookup on the raw record before building an owned record. In the LOH passes, avoid allocating and hashing per base, e.g. a dense Vec over the window instead of HashMaps. Keep byte identity.
ideas.simplest_version: In removed_duplicates, skip any record that is neither flagged duplicate nor named in `removed`, before allocating its name or decoding its CIGAR.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 BAM, 3 Mb DEL and DUP in clean mode at 1 and 4 threads: every output must be md5-identical to master, and the duplicate-scan step (from log timestamps) must fall by at least 50%. If a perf profile shows that decoding, not per-record work, dominates the scans, the idea is wrong and the one-pass plan comes back.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: One perf record of the 1 Mb DUP run at 1 thread (~20 s of CPU), to see which functions dominate the LOH and duplicate-scan intervals.
ideas.impact: A few seconds per Mb at 1 thread off spike's own time for big events. Mostly it saves building two plans that the measurement says cannot pay off.
ideas.risks: Small absolute gains. spike's own run time is far below merge.sh's and fastq.sh's, so this ranks after them.
ideas.history_check: The map lists 'Pass 2 edge strips' and 'One streaming pass per event' as OPEN, both inferred. This measurement (pass 2 0.30 s, decoding 0.14-0.21 s per window) contradicts the inferred 'serial floor' for pass 2 at this size. Threads step 1 already chunked the census and LOH passes over threads (census.rs:138, loh.rs:640 and :1061).

ideas.title: Bound peak memory: no whole-chromosome copies in the reference cache, and no clone of every kept pool pair
ideas.problem: SharedReference::load fetches each chromosome through ReferenceReader, whose FIFO cache stores a clone of every whole-chromosome fetch, so loading holds about two copies. Each event also clones every kept pool pair, and every event's outputs live until the end of the run.
ideas.evidence: Code: src/reference.rs:183-191 (cache.insert(key, seq.clone())) and :223-231 (one reader for the whole load loop); src/simulate.rs:262 (kept.push(pair.clone())); src/main.rs:666, :855 and :913 (outputs held, then combined). MEASURED: MAXRSS 704 MB for the 1 Mb chr20 DUP at 1 thread (scratchpad perf/dup1). DOCUMENTED: 3 Mb events peak at 1.2-2.5 GB (README.md:1356-1361). INFERRED: a genome-wide VCF panel loads ~3.1 GB of sequence and peaks near ~6 GB during the load.
ideas.proposal: In SharedReference::load, fetch whole chromosomes without the FIFO cache, or move the sequence out instead of cloning it. Keep kept originals as indices into the pool, or move pairs out of the pool, instead of cloning them. Optionally write each event's SPIKE_ pairs to the FASTQ streams as soon as the event finishes, since names are unique per event.
ideas.simplest_version: Bypass the cache for whole-chromosome fetches in load (a one-line change) and nothing else.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 BAM with a VCF of one random SNV per autosome plus chrX: peak RSS (/usr/bin/time %M) must fall by at least half the loaded reference size, and every output must stay md5-identical. A build that drops the sequence too early fails to fetch or changes outputs.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Run the current binary on that 23-SNV VCF under /usr/bin/time and read the reference-load log line. If peak RSS minus the loaded size is small, the cache copy is not the problem and only the pool clone is worth touching.
ideas.impact: Hospital panels across many chromosomes, and multi-Mb events, fit on smaller machines. No output changes.
ideas.risks: Low. The gain matters only for genome-wide panels or very large events.
ideas.history_check: Listed in the map as an OPEN, inferred limitation ('peak memory about 2x the loaded sequence'). Never measured or changed.

ideas.title: Carry the sample's own phased haplotypes, indels included, onto every remade copy (CR3 option A, now with read-level evidence)
ideas.problem: Remade event-copy reads (event +/-2 kb) are built from reference plus the sample's SNPs only: SampleCopies is two HashMap<u64,u8> SNP maps (src/loh.rs:34-43), the gVCF parser returns on any non-SNP (src/loh.rs:554-557), and apply_variants writes single bases (src/haplotype.rs:661-697). Every spike therefore erases the sample's own nearby indels from the replaced share of reads: hom indels near a planted variant fall to about het, and het indels on the event copy vanish. In the hospital VCF this would show as new het indels next to each spiked variant: a spike signature and wrong background genotypes. The event copy is a coin per phase block and is not recorded.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED by me, read-only, on the EXISTING transplant round-2 forward run0 (HG001-only small variants spiked into hospital HG002 D24-14230; view = recipient minus replaced_reads.txt plus sim.bam), first 80 events (scratchpad cr3probe/cr3_existing.py, cr3_het.py): 17 HG002 Q100 hom-alt indels 400-1,921 bp from 12 planted events went from recipient AF median 0.95 to spiked AF median 0.48 (range 0.35-0.85); 0 of 211 synthetic _hap_ reads covering them carry the indel; all 17 are 1/1 in the hospital's own DeepVariant call (call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz). 49 het indels: 0 of 596 synthetic reads carry them. LDLR exposure (measured, Q100 vs data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed +/-2 kb): 18 of 18 exon footprints hold a carried non-SNP, 9 of 18 a hom one. DOCUMENTED: CR3 probe hom 2 bp DEL under a het DUP AF 1.0 -> 0.360; T7 38/40 footprints (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:122-196, REVIEW.md:4634-4651). Both GIAB truth sets are fully phased (memory validation-plan.md).
ideas.proposal: Add a sample-haplotype source (--sample-vcf: phased VCF or gVCF with GT|PS, indels included). Build each copy's template from it: SNPs as today, and small indels as segment splits marked 'background', so they are never junctions and are never counted by SIM_ALT_FRAGS, own_bases or the validate probes. Pick the event copy per PS block, by coin or explicit hap=1/2. Write the choice to the truth as phased GT plus PS and to the run README. Keep the pileup path when no VCF is given. This complements P1 (minimal remake): P1 shrinks the remade set, and this makes the remade reads right.
ideas.simplest_version: Read biallelic SNPs plus indels of 50 bp or less from a phased VCF over the footprint. Apply them to the event-copy and other-copy haplotypes by splitting reference segments, and refuse when a background indel overlaps the event's own REF span. No SVs and no STR alleles yet.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (a) Value kill: run the hospital's DeepVariant (container) on the spiked view and on the unspiked BAM over +/-2 kb of the 12 events in round-2 forward run0. If at most 1 of the 17 hom indels and at most 5% of the 49 het indels change GT, the read loss does not reach the caller, so shelve the idea. (b) Mechanism kill after build: re-plant the same events. Background hom indels must return to median AF >= 0.9, with >= 90% of SPIKE_ reads over them carrying the allele. Het indels must stay within binomial noise of the recipient AF. The CR3 dup_homdel probe must return to AF 1.0, and transplant 2b's SNV/indel verdicts must not change. Today's code fails this (0.48; 0/211).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: bcftools mpileup | call (or the DeepVariant container) on the recipient and the spiked view at the 66 background-indel sites already found in round-2 forward run0. Count GT flips. About 2 hours, with no spike run.
