ideas.impact: Hospital demo: removes a systematic, visible artefact around every spiked LDLR variant (background hom indels turned het) and gives phased truth. Benchmarkers get unbiased FP/FN counts in the 4 kb around each spike.
ideas.risks: Segment bookkeeping (junctions(), SIM_ALT_FRAGS, own_bases, del_planted/ins_planted probes) must ignore background breaks, or every background indel becomes a 'junction'. The VCF must belong to the BAM's sample: GIAB truth works for demo backgrounds, while a DeepVariant+WhatsHap VCF elsewhere carries its own errors. Output bytes change for every run, so it needs a K7-style seed-spread gate. It overlaps P1/P1b and CR7(b), and the design notes say to design these together.
ideas.history_check: CR3 option A has been open since the Codex review (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:122-196: 'large, overlaps CR7'). Option B's fail-closed half is done (--gvcf unreadable stops the run). The blanket footprint warning was refuted by T7 (38/40). The map's 'measure first' step is answered at read level by the measurement above. It has never been built or refuted.

ideas.title: Sex- and ploidy-aware genotypes: hemizygous chrX/chrY in males, haploid truth GT, input GT honoured
ideas.problem: spike has no ploidy: grep for chrX|chrY|ploid|hemizyg|haploid|PAR in src/ finds only a chrM test line. The default --allele-fraction is 0.5 (src/main.rs:102), the truth GT is only 0/1 or 1/1 (src/truth.rs:468-474), and VCF GT is counted but never used (src/vcf_input.rs:262-271). On male non-PAR chrX/Y the default gives a half-dose 'het' written 0/1, a genotype a male cannot carry, and DeepVariant would call it 0/1. The hospital demo background, HG002, is male.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: the hospital raredisease ngsbits_samplegender for D24-14230 says male (ratio_chry_chrx 0.2832), and HG001 D25-7403 female (0.0123). idxstats chrX/autosome read density is 0.499 (HG002 hospital), 0.501 (HG002 35x) and 0.977 (HG001); chrY is 0.444, 0.468 and 0.075. Real hemizygous SNVs (scratchpad cr3probe/chrx_af.py): 200 Q100 GT=1 SNVs in chrX:20-30 Mb on the hospital BAM have median depth 16, median AF 1.0, and 4.5% below 0.8; chr20 hets have median AF 0.512 at 33x. Q100 chrX:10-60 Mb holds 41,317 haploid GT '1' records and 64 DELs >= 50 bp. ClinVar P/LP: 24,472 of 339,976 records (7.2%) are on chrX non-PAR (cnv_validation resources/clinical/clinvar.vcf.gz). DOCUMENTED: CR7(a), an input GT=1/1 gives SIM_VAF 0.500 and GT 0/1, and CR7(b) is open (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404). cnv_validation docs/findings/2026-08-31-chrx-male-ploidy.md: a diploid model makes gCNV call about 99% of male chrX CN=1.
ideas.proposal: (1) Infer sex from idxstats chrX/chrY density, or take --sex M|F, with a GRCh38 PAR1/PAR2 table. (2) Build a contig ploidy map: male non-PAR X and Y are haploid; chrY in a female is refused. (3) On haploid contigs the default becomes af=1 (hemizygous) and the truth GT '1'; af below 1 is refused unless --mosaic is given. (4) An opt-in VCF genotype mode (CR7 option B): GT drives the dosage (0/1 -> 0.5, 1/1 -> 1, haploid 1 -> 1), phased GT and PS are carried, and FILTER/hom-ref gates are opt-in. (5) The sex call and ploidy go into the run README.
ideas.simplest_version: --sex flag plus the PAR table. On male non-PAR chrX/Y, the default af becomes 1.0 and the truth GT '1', and an explicit af<1 is refused without --mosaic. Automatic sex inference comes later.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Spike 30 SNVs at Q100-reference positions in chrX:20-30 Mb into hospital HG002 with defaults, BAM route with the hospital aligner command (-M -K 100000000). The realised AF distribution must match HG002's own hemizygous SNVs (median 1.0, at most 10% below 0.8; real 4.5%). Today's default predicts a median of about 0.5 and must fail. 10 PAR1 SNVs must stay near 0.5. Spiked chrX DELs >= 50 bp must show interior/flank depth (E1) near HG002's real Q100 chrX DELs (about 0). The inferred sex must agree with ngsbits/peddy on all 3 local BAMs. Kill the idea if realised AF stays below 0.8 at more than 10% of sites, or if the inference disagrees with ngsbits on any BAM.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: idxstats sex inference on the 3 local BAMs (done: 0.499/0.501 against 0.977). Then one spike run of a single chrX non-PAR SNV into HG002 at the default and at af=hom, with a pileup of realised AF in sim.bam plus the kept reads (minutes).
ideas.impact: X-linked disorders (DMD, OTC, F8, F9, GLA, ABCD1...; 7.2% of ClinVar P/LP) can be demoed on the male GIAB background without biologically impossible het calls. The truth GT then matches what DeepVariant, genmod and hap.py see. Benchmarkers get correct haploid truth.
ideas.risks: PAR coordinates are build-specific. The X-transposed region and X-Y homologous genes give low MAPQ, so RF8 may refuse there. Male X has no het SNPs, so the copy is unknown and copy_rate = v, which is right at af=1. A truth GT of '1' may break consumers that assume diploid. CR7's design notes ask for the old behaviour to stay the default for one release.
ideas.history_check: CR7(b) has been open since the Codex review. Option B (two explicit modes) was recommended but not chosen (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404). CR7(c) af=het=0.5 is done (8dca8d0). No ploidy code has ever existed, and nothing here was refuted.

ideas.title: Grouped events on one haplotype pair: compound hets and cis/trans with phased truth
ideas.problem: Footprints must sit at least 7 kb apart (FOOTPRINT_MARGIN = HAP_FLANK + MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN = 3500, src/main.rs:1188). --allow-overlap simulates each event against the original donor and concatenates the sets (src/simulate.rs:410-428), so no read carries both events and the overlap reads about 1+v. Events further apart flip independent coins per phase block (src/loh.rs:924-949), so cis/trans is random and is not recorded, and the truth GT is unphased (src/truth.rs:468-474). Compound hets are the usual form of autosomal-recessive diagnoses, and of FH homozygous/compound cases in LDLR.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: 52 of 153 LDLR exon pairs (34%) are less than 7 kb apart edge to edge (data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed), so two exonic LDLR variants in those exons are refused. DOCUMENTED: two adjacent DELs at AF=1 under --allow-overlap read 67.05x/67.03x inside (REVIEW.md:2930-2939). The phase coin per call is confirmed in code (memory validation-plan.md, Astra point (b)). Grouped composition is listed as not built (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:297-301, :490-505).
ideas.proposal: An event group (--event '...;group=g1;hap=1', or VCF records sharing a PS with phased GT) is applied to one VariantHaplotype per copy. Cis members edit the same copy and trans members the other. One suppression pass runs at copy_rate per copy, and one tiling pass covers the union footprint. The truth writes phased GT (0|1, 1|0) with PS, and the README says which sample copy was used. It reuses idea 1's per-copy templates, and a later per-chromosome ref_range fix opens multi-chromosome groups (CR6-A).
ideas.simplest_version: Small variants only (SNV/MNV/indel), two or more on one chromosome inside one union footprint, explicit cis/trans, VAF 0.5 or 1.0, with no SVs in groups.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real yardstick: HG002's own Q100-phased het SNV pairs 100-400 bp apart on the hospital BAM. Among ALT-carrying fragments that cover both sites, measure the share carrying both ALTs (real cis near 1, real trans near the error rate). Plant 30 cis and 30 trans pairs at the same distances at Q100-reference positions. Spiked co-carry rates must fall inside the real cis and trans distributions, and depth over the union must stay within binomial noise of the unspiked BAM. Today's --allow-overlap is predicted to give 0 cis co-carry and about 1+v depth, and must fail. Kill if cis co-carry is below 95% of the real rate, or trans co-carry is more than 2x the real rate.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: A pysam script over Q100 phased het pairs in the hospital HG002 BAM gives the real cis/trans co-carry rates (about 1 hour). One spike --allow-overlap run with two SNVs 300 bp apart records the broken baseline (minutes).
ideas.impact: FH/LDLR and autosomal-recessive compound-het demos reach genmod's compound models. Benchmarkers can test phasing and compound-het logic. It also unblocks CR6-A (balanced translocation) and complex SVs.
ideas.risks: Union footprints mixing SVs and small variants complicate the tiling count. raredisease does not read-phase by default (inferred from the outputs on disk: no phasing step), so cis/trans matters mostly for trio-based inheritance logic. Phase must agree with the sample's own phase blocks, which depends on idea 1. It changes truth output for grouped runs only.
ideas.history_check: The CR1 gate is done (7 kb refusal). Grouped-event composition is explicitly open and was never built (REVIEW.md:2930-2939; CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:490-505). The outputs map lists compound hets in LDLR as open. Never refuted.

ideas.title: Repeat-expansion (STR) events with the real motif and in-repeat read pairs, judged by ExpansionHunter
ideas.problem: There is no STR or expansion event type: no such spec in src/exon.rs or src/main.rs. An expansion can only be written as an INS with explicit bases, and its fragments that lie wholly inside the inserted sequence are never drawn and are left out of the count (src/simulate.rs:801-817, 888-946). A length-only ins draws random bases (src/main.rs:2017-2024). Pathogenic full expansions longer than a fragment (FMR1 >= 200 CGG = 600 bp, C9orf72, DMPK, CANVAS RFC1) therefore lack the in-repeat pairs ExpansionHunter relies on. The hospital pipeline runs ExpansionHunter + stranger, and spike cannot produce that result class.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: hospital raredisease_results/repeat_expansions holds an EH VCF of 66 loci and a stranger VCF. HG001 and HG002 EH calls differ at about 40 of 66 loci. Q100 HG002 carries a 520 bp AAAAG insertion at RFC1 chr4:39348424 (hap 1). Hospital EH calls HG002 RFC1 13/51 (CI 43-85; ADSP 13/0, ADFL 20/23, ADIR 0/9) and HG001 9/13 SPANNING. In EH's evidence BAM all 9 in-repeat reads at RFC1 have an anchored mate on chr4, and bwa-mem2 placed the in-repeat read itself at chr2:162,752,903, another AAAAG array. 0 pure in-repeat reads sit at the locus in the main BAM (scratchpad cr3probe/rfc1_irr.py). EH also calls HG002 RAPGEF2 TTTTA 7/158 (CI 48-230) where Q100 has only a 16 bp insertion, so EH's long-allele calls carry off-target noise. DOCUMENTED: the ExpansionHunter/stranger path in raredisease (cnv_validation config/config.yaml:177).
ideas.proposal: A str: event (a catalog locus, or chr:start-end:MOTIF:units) that rewrites one copy's tract to N units, pure or keeping the reference's interruption pattern, on a chosen copy (idea 1/2). Fragment starts wholly inside an inserted repeat are admitted, with the count taken over all starts so in-repeat depth equals local depth. The truth carries RU/units plus the sequence ALT. In the FASTQ route bwa-mem2 then scatters the in-repeat reads as it does for real ones.
ideas.simplest_version: str:chr:pos:MOTIF:N becomes an INS of MOTIF x N at the tract's end, plus an event-level switch that drops the novel-only start exclusion for that event.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Transplant Q100 HG002's RFC1 520 bp AAAAG allele into HG001 (EH 9/13) with the hospital aligner command. EH, with the hospital catalog, on spiked HG001 must call a long allele whose CI overlaps HG002's real 43-85, with ADIR within Poisson noise of 9 and ADFL within noise of 20/23, and the in-repeat mates placed off-locus as in real. A broken version (random sequence of the same length, or in-repeat reads not realigned) must fail by giving no INREPEAT call. For expansions longer than a fragment there is no real carrier on disk. That half needs a public carrier WGS (for example Coriell FMR1/C9orf72), and until then it is judged only against EH's own consistency, labelled as such.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No code needed: run today's spike with the Q100 RFC1 record (explicit sequence, --vcf) into HG001 over RFC1 +/-10 kb, align with -M -K, and run EH from a biocontainer with that catalog entry (hours). If 520 bp already matches real, the remaining work is only the longer-than-a-fragment half and the spec.
ideas.impact: The hospital can demo repeat-expansion disorders (FMR1, HTT, C9orf72, ATXNs, RFC1) through the EH/stranger path, a result class spike cannot make today. EH callers get a benchmark with planted lengths.
ideas.risks: EH's in-repeat read recovery depends on its catalog's off-target regions and on where bwa places pure-repeat reads, which is realistic only in the realign/FASTQ route. GC-rich CGG tracts are under-covered in real libraries, and uniform tiling would over-cover them. FMR1 on male X needs idea 2. CR3 and the 7 kb rule apply.
ideas.history_check: Never proposed in spike: grep finds no ExpansionHunter in docs/ or README. CR5 (REVIEW.md:3119-3131) only made placement honour the existing exclusion, a consistency fix, not a test of in-insert fragments. The map lists STR expansions as unsupported. RF15 (short INS too clean) is open and a different size class.

ideas.title: Homology-aware breakpoints for approximate and exon-spec CNVs (snap to NAHR / microhomology junctions)
ideas.problem: Exon specs cut exactly at exon edges (src/exon.rs:421-427), and approximate coordinates are cut bluntly where stated (src/haplotype.rs:122-161). Real LDLR DELs and DUPs are often Alu-mediated: two same-orientation Alus join at homologous positions, giving a hybrid Alu, long junction homology and low-MAPQ junction reads, the class Manta missed at ClinVar 4845403. The repo's own LDLR demo events carry junction classes that no real FH carrier has.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED by me. The repo demo VCF data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_known_deletions_hg38.vcf has both ends on a multiple of 100 in 15 of 22 records. Junction homology (scratchpad cr3probe/junction_homology.py, GRCh38 no-alt): 19 demo DELs have median 0 bp, 1/19 >= 2 bp and 12/19 blunt; 31 ClinVar LDLR-region DELs have median 1 bp and 14/31 >= 2 bp. 20 of 22 demo records have a same-orientation Alu pair within 500 bp of both ends, and 13/22 already have both ends inside an Alu (UCSC rmsk; 356 Alus in chr19:11.0-11.2 Mb). From the map, measured by another reader: 0/36 LDLR exon edges lie in an Alu against 19/62 ClinVar ends; HG002 Q100 chr20 DELs >= 50 bp have 372/442 >= 2 bp homology (median 16), against 80/442 for random positions. DOCUMENTED: spike's precise-coordinate Alu-Alu junctions clip like real carriers in 16/18 events (memory realism-inspection-20261006.md).
ideas.proposal: Opt-in bp=nahr / --snap-breakpoints W for DEL/DUP (exon or coordinate specs). Search +/-W of each stated end for same-orientation Alu (or segdup/LCR) pairs, align them, and put the junction at a homologous position inside their longest identical stretch, so the haplotype holds a hybrid element. Otherwise fall back to the best 2-20 bp microhomology position. Exon specs take intronic ends that keep the stated exons inside. The truth gets the snapped POS/END, CIPOS/CIEND for the original, and SIM_SNAP=class.
ideas.simplest_version: DEL only, Alu pairs only (rmsk), W=1 kb, junction at the midpoint of the longest exact match of 10 bp or more between the two Alus; otherwise unchanged with a warning.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Yardstick: round-1b HG001-only Alu-Alu DELs with real carriers in the HG001 hospital BAM. Per event, measure junction homology, junction-read MAPQ, split/clipped-read count and clip offset. Snapped versions of the 22 demo LDLR records planted into HG002 must fall within the real-vs-real spread on these metrics, and today's rounded versions must fall outside it. If the rounded versions already match real, the cut position inside Alus does not matter to the aligner or callers: kill the idea and only document it. Secondary: SIM_RESIST and Manta call/no-call for snapped exon-spec events move toward those of ClinVar-precise events.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Reference arithmetic only (minutes): snap the 22 demo records offline and report homology and hybrid-Alu identity. Then compare junction-read MAPQ in an existing rounded-LDLR spike (sv_slice_test B1-B3 runs) with the realism-inspection Alu-Alu events (scratchpad inspect/).
ideas.impact: LDLR exon CNV demos that look like real FH carriers to Manta, TIDDIT and gCNV. SV benchmarks lose a systematic easy bias in exon-spec events.
ideas.risks: Snapping changes the user's stated event, so it must be opt-in and recorded. Several Alu pairs may qualify, which makes the snap seed-dependent. Junctions inside repeats raise SIM_RESIST and may trip RF8. Many real LDLR SVs are not Alu-mediated (24 of 39 have neither end in an Alu, memory hospital-demo-plan.md), so the microhomology fallback matters as much.
ideas.history_check: The map lists 'exon-spec breakpoints: document or add an option' as open. It was never built or refuted. The realism inspection supports that precise coordinates give real-like clips, which is the premise here.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and mtDNA deletions, judged against a real HG001/HG002 mito mixture
ideas.problem: spike has no chrM handling (chrM appears in src/ only in a loh test). chrM is circular, so pairs spanning 16569->1 are improper and a linear haplotype cannot make them. It is multi-copy, so the quantity is heteroplasmy, not diploid copies. Depth is in the thousands. The 7 kb footprint rule allows only about 2 events on a 16.5 kb genome. Whether today's clean mode gives Mutect2-MT and eKLIPse the same evidence as real heteroplasmy is untested, although the hospital pipeline runs them.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: the hospital raredisease_results holds call_snv/mitochondria (Mutect2 FilterMutectCalls on a liftunlift reference), call_sv/mitochondria (eKLIPse) and haplocheck (HG002 coverage 5895, haplogroup H5a7). idxstats chrM read density against autosomes is 321x (HG002 hospital), 479x (HG001) and 562x (HG002 35x). Within 300 bp of either chrM end, 33% of reads are not proper pairs (chrM:1-300 0.331, chrM:16300-16569 0.336), against 0.8-0.9% mid-chrM; MAPQ<20 is 0-5%. Mutect2-MT shows 8 homoplasmic (AF>0.9) SNVs only in HG001 and 6 only in HG002 (for example 2259C>T, 4745A>G, 7337G>A, 13326T>C). HG002 has no 20-80% heteroplasmic SNV, so the pileup's het phasing does not fire there. ClinVar has 187 P/LP MT records. INFERRED from code: with no het SNP, copy_rate(None, v) = v, which already gives heteroplasmy semantics.
ideas.proposal: (1) Validate today's behaviour first against a real mixture. (2) A chrM mode: the copy is always unknown (a fraction of molecules), with no diploid phasing; the truth records AF as heteroplasmy; several events per chrM run through grouped composition (idea 3) or a relaxed footprint rule, since depth is huge. (3) A circular-aware haplotype that wraps the flank across the origin, so synthetic pairs span 16569->1. (4) mtDNA deletion presets (the common 4,977 bp m.8470-13447) at heteroplasmy levels for eKLIPse.
ideas.simplest_version: No code: run today's spike on single chrM SNVs at af 0.05 and 0.2 into HG002 and compare with the real mixture. Build only what fails.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Build a real mixture: HG001's chrM reads at f=0.05 and 0.2 (name-hash subsample), merged with HG002's chrM reads at 1-f. At the 8 HG001-only homoplasmic sites this is real heteroplasmy at f. Spike the same 8 SNVs at af=f into HG002 (several runs, since the 7 kb rule applies) and run the hospital's Mutect2 mitochondria steps on both. Per-site AF and call/FILTER status must agree within the split-half noise of the real mixture. A broken version (af doubled by a diploid copy_rate, or the unknown-copy suppression off) must fail. Kill the idea if spike's AF error at f=0.05 exceeds the real split-half noise at 3 or more of the 8 sites. eKLIPse deletion levels have no real carrier on disk: label them as checked against eKLIPse only.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: samtools view -s on chrM of both hospital BAMs to build the mixture, then a pileup at the 8 sites (minutes). One spike run of chrM:7337G>A at af=0.1 into HG002 gives SIM_RESIST, pool size, memory and realised AF (minutes).
ideas.impact: Mito disease demos (MELAS m.3243A>G, LHON, KSS deletions) through the hospital's MT path. It also gives, nearly for free, a low-VAF realism yardstick at very high depth (concept test 2, 'mixture', open in validation-plan memory).
ideas.risks: NUMT reads and the liftunlift realignment differ by route. raredisease subsamples MT reads (mt_subsample_rd 150) for eKLIPse. haplocheck will rightly flag contamination for multi-site mixtures, so pathogenic demos should use single sites. A whole-chrM pool at about 10,000x is large in memory (inferred about 650k pairs). The 7 kb rule limits events per run.
ideas.history_check: Never examined: mito appears in docs only as a read-name pairing note (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-read-names.md:139) and one chrM mate in the duplicates plan. The mixture test is open in memory validation-plan.md. Nothing was refuted.

ideas.title: Mobile-element insertions from a consensus library with poly-A tail and target-site duplication
ideas.problem: Symbolic <INS:ME:ALU/L1/SVA> records and ins:...:len specs get iid uniform random bases (src/main.rs:2017-2024; src/vcf_input.rs:363-391), with no poly-A, no TSD and no fragments wholly inside. Real MEI evidence is mates that map to the element's many genomic copies at MAPQ 0, plus clipped poly-A. Random sequence gives unmapped mates instead (inferred). HGVS and ClinVar describe MEIs symbolically (for example BRCA2 c.9342_9343insAluY), so a clinical MEI spike today is random DNA.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED/MEASURED in cnv_validation config/frozen_evidence/mei_evidence.tsv: the real AluY in BRCA2 carried by the hospital HG002 SeraCare construct (chr13:32394774) has a 343 bp insert, a 15 bp TSD and a 40 bp homopolymer; 26 clipped and 72 spanning reads; 15/15 support mates off-contig, 14 at MAPQ 0, over 10 contigs; the NA12878 control has 0 clipped. From the map (measured by another reader): 36/765 HG002 Q100 chr20 INS >= 50 bp are >= 50% ME 13-mers and 17/765 end in a poly-A/T of 10 or more, against 0 and 0 for spike's random sequence. MEASURED: the hospital params have skip_me_calling true, so RetroSeq is off there, and the effect is on Manta/TIDDIT and on what a reviewer sees.
ideas.proposal: A bundled ME consensus set (Dfam AluY/AluYa5, L1HS with a 5'-truncation length draw, SVA_E/F), with random strand, a poly-A length draw (10-60 bp), a TSD of drawn length (7-20 bp) duplicated from the target site, and optional per-base divergence. An ins:...:alu spec and VCF <INS:ME:*> use it, and anything else that falls back to random bases warns. The truth already carries the built sequence (CR7).
ideas.simplest_version: AluY consensus plus a 30 bp poly-A plus a 15 bp TSD, for <INS:ME:ALU> only, with a warning for other ME types.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Plant AluY (consensus + poly-A + 15 bp TSD) at chr13:32394774 into HG001 (D25-7403, which lacks it) and align with the hospital command. The share of support mates placed off-contig and at MAPQ 0 must match the real SeraCare AluY (15/15 and 14/15) within binomial noise, and the clipped-per-spanning-read share must fall within noise. The random-sequence version (today's symbolic path) must fail, with mates unmapped. Kill the idea if the consensus version also fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No code needed: write AluY consensus + poly-A + TSD as an explicit-sequence VCF INS (that path already works), run today's spike into HG001 at that locus, align, and count mate placement (hours).
ideas.impact: MEI demos and SV benchmarks where Manta and TIDDIT see MEIs as they see real ones. Spiked symbolic MEIs stop being detectable as random DNA.
ideas.risks: The SeraCare AluY is an engineered construct at unknown AF, so compare shares, not counts. Divergence between the consensus and real elements changes MAPQ. Long L1/SVA need in-insert fragments (idea 4's change). ME calling is skipped at the hospital, so the value there is indirect.
ideas.history_check: The map lists 'realistic insertion content' as open. RF15 (short INS cleaner than real) is open but concerns 20-39 bp. Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Trio-consistent spiking: inherited variants on the transmitted haplotype, de novo in the child only
ideas.problem: spike takes one BAM (src/main.rs:47) and picks the event copy by a coin per phase block (src/loh.rs:924-949). Spiking a family member by member cannot put an inherited variant on the haplotype the child actually received from the carrier parent, and a de novo needs child-only spiking. raredisease is pedigree-aware: genmod inheritance models, UPD and peddy use trios (external knowledge; the pedigree/ and peddy/ outputs are on disk).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: the hospital raredisease_results holds pedigree/ and peddy/ folders (a single-sample run here). DOCUMENTED: cnv_validation config/samples.ped lists the CEPH-1463 family sequenced at the hospital (NA12877 father, NA12879/81/82/85, HG001 = NA12878); those BAMs are index-only on this machine (memory validation-plan.md). Code: a single --bam and one coin per block. INFERRED: independent runs put the child's allele on a random haplotype, so it co-segregates with the carrier parent's linked SNPs only about 50% of the time.
ideas.proposal: spike trio --parent1 --parent2 --child. Phase the child's het SNPs by transmission (Mendelian). For an inherited event, choose the parental haplotype (explicit or coin) and the child's copy inherited from it, and spike both using idea 1's copy templates. A de novo goes to the child only. Write a truth per sample plus a PED-aware summary.
ideas.simplest_version: Inherited small variants only, one carrier parent, transmission phase from the three BAMs' het SNPs inside the footprint.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real yardstick on the CEPH trio NA12877/NA12878 -> NA12879 at the hospital: for real transmitted het variants, linked het SNPs within one fragment co-segregate in about 100% of phase-informative fragments. Spiked inherited variants in the child must sit in cis with the transmitting parent's alleles in at least 95% of phase-informative fragments. Independent runs (today) are predicted at about 50% and must fail. De novo spikes must show 0 alt reads in both parents, and genmod must classify at least 90% as designed.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: At the hospital: for 50 Platinum-truth transmitted het SNVs, count phase-informative fragments in NA12879 to fix the real co-segregation rate (pysam, hours).
ideas.impact: Realistic family demos for raredisease's trio analysis: inheritance filters, de novo, and compound hets across parents.
ideas.risks: The data exist only at the hospital. Within one fragment, short reads rarely cover both the variant and a linked SNP. It depends on ideas 1 and 3, and three BAMs triple the run time.
ideas.history_check: The map lists trio-consistent spiking under new event types (inferred, unverified). Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: ClinVar-native VCF ingest: route sequence-resolved ≥50 bp records to the SV path, keep ClinVar ID, gene and HGVS
ideas.problem: ClinVar is the obvious source for the hospital demo, but no ClinVar record of 50 bp or more carries SVTYPE. vcf_input.rs:226-241 therefore turns every one of them into a SmallVariant. The run log and README label it 'SNV', the truth ID is sim_var_N, and it gets no SVTYPE/END/SVLEN. The ClinVar ID and GENEINFO are dropped, and SIM_GENE falls back to 'unknown' (vcf_input.rs:430-432, truth.rs:430). Planted deletions come out physically right, but on the small-variant path. A sequence-resolved tandem DUP becomes an insertion of 'novel' sequence. Fragments that lie wholly inside the copy are never tiled, so the duplicated region gets no extra depth. SIM_ALT_FRAGS cannot count a junction when the ALT is longer than a read, so it reads 0. The warning then wrongly blames rarity ('a real variant this rare can go unseen', simulate.rs:320). ClinVar's contig names ('19') are also refused outright. Separately, a DUP given by coordinates with a 1 bp span is planted as SVTYPE=DUP SVLEN=1 without a word.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED with the prebuilt release binary (target/release/spike, built 2026-10-06; vcf_input.rs/truth.rs/exon.rs unchanged since 0a00caf, checked with git diff) on the 35x HG002 BAM, outputs in scratchpad cv/ and rf8/. (1) ClinVar VCF (cnv_validation/resources/clinical/clinvar.vcf.gz) as-is gives 'Error: chromosome '19' not found in FASTA index'. (2) Renamed to chr19, ClinVar 251409 (a pathogenic 7,636 bp LDLR DEL) is labelled 'SNV chr19:11106493 <7.6kb REF>>C', ID sim_var_1, no SVTYPE, SIM_GENE=unknown. R1 md5 54443603 differs from the del:chr19:11106493-11114129 spec's 26ccc768. (3) ClinVar 251140 is a pathogenic 8,119 bp DUP (CLNHGVS g.11104774_11112892dup), and ALT[1:] equals the downstream reference exactly (samtools faidx). As a VCF record it gives 313 synthetic and 280 suppressed pairs, SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 at AF 0.5, and the 'this rare' warning. dup:chr19:11104770-11112889 gives 1,540 synthetic and 888 suppressed pairs, SIM_ALT_FRAGS=30, DEPTH_FOLD 1.51. (4) With only SVTYPE=DUP or SVTYPE=DEL added to the same two records, R1.fq.gz is byte-identical to the coordinate specs (md5 5bfadff3, 26ccc768). The fix is therefore pure routing: README:328 already documents the anchor+copy DUP form. (5) Scale, from bcftools over clinvar.vcf.gz (fileDate 2026-05-03): P/LP records with an allele difference of 50 bp or more number 2,602 Deletion, 285 Duplication, 448 Insertion, 356 Indel and 305 Microsatellite genome-wide. In LDLR they are 31 DEL, 3 DUP, 3 INS and 2 Indel. For comparison, the GIAB Q100 chr20 VCF has SVTYPE on 1,712 of 1,712 such records, so only clinical-style VCFs hit this. (6) cnv_validation's clinvar_pathogenic_sv_ge50.bed stores the 4 LDLR ClinVar DUPs as 1 bp intervals, and dup:chr19:11104769-11104770 was planted as SVTYPE=DUP;SVLEN=1 with no warning (rf8/e8).
ideas.proposal: vcf_input.rs: when a record has no SVTYPE, both alleles are DNA and |len(ALT)-len(REF)| >= 50 with a shared anchor, classify it as follows. A pure deletion becomes DEL. A pure insertion whose inserted bases equal the adjacent reference on either side (after shifting across the repeat), or that carries CLNVC=Duplication, becomes DUP (the existing anchor+copy form). Any other insertion becomes INS with its sequence. Anything else goes to the existing delins/complex handling or a counted refusal. Records under 50 bp keep today's SmallVariant path byte for byte. If a VCF contig is missing from the .fai but chr+name / name-minus-chr (MT<->chrM) is present, and only one of the two is, use it and log it once. Carry ID to SIM_SRC_ID, GENEINFO's symbol to SIM_GENE and CLNHGVS to SIM_HGVS in the truth and the run README. Add --vcf-ids 251409,251140 to pick records out of a big VCF. Reword the SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 warning for an ALT longer than a read. Warn when a coordinate-spec DEL/DUP/INV is shorter than 50 bp. Possible later extension: HGVS g. specs (hgvs:NC_000019.10:g.11104774_11112892dup), which ClinVar and lab reports use and which avoid the 0/1-based ambiguity of del:chr:S-E.
ideas.simplest_version: Map CLNVC=Deletion/Duplication/Insertion to SVTYPE=DEL/DUP/INS for no-SVTYPE records of 50 bp or more (exactly what the bcftools-edited gate records did), plus the chr-prefix alias and SIM_SRC_ID from the ID column.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x HG002 BAM, take all 39 LDLR P/LP sequence-resolved ClinVar records of 50 bp or more, renamed only by the alias. (a) Every DEL and DUP fed by --vcf must give R1/R2 byte-identical to its coordinate spec (del:/dup: at the stated span). Today none does (the DEL md5 differs, and the DUP has 313 vs 1,540 synthetic pairs). (b) After align.sh+merge.sh, spike validate on the 3 DUPs must give coverage_ratio |ratio-1.5|<0.3 and the DELs del_planted PASS. The idea is refuted if the shape classifier labels any of the 31 DELs other than DEL, or fewer than 3 of 3 Duplications as DUP. The same holds if any record under 50 bp in a 500-record ClinVar sample changes bytes against master.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 hour: a 30-line Python classifier over the 39 LDLR records writes SVTYPE into a copy of the VCF. Run the existing release binary on each record and compare md5 against the matching del:/dup:/ins: spec. Two of the 39 are already done and byte-identical (cv/delsvt, cv/dupsvt).
ideas.impact: The hospital user can spike pathogenic ClinVar variants by ID straight from the ClinVar VCF. Today a pathogenic LDLR duplication fed that way plants no extra depth, which CNV callers (gCNV, CNVnator) need, and every SV is reported as an 'SNV' with its ClinVar ID lost. With the ID in the truth VCF, demo results can be matched back to ClinVar records.
ideas.risks: vcf_input has no reference today (it is loaded later). Shape-based DUP detection needs either the reference or CLNVC, so start with CLNVC plus allele shape. ClinVar 'Microsatellite' expansions (305) should become INS with their sequence, not DUP, and RF15/CR5 limits on long insertions still apply. Contig aliasing must refuse when both spellings exist. VCF runs with records of 50 bp or more will change bytes, so the gate must show identity for records under 50 bp.
ideas.history_check: Not proposed or refuted before (no ClinVar entry in .claude/judgment-gate-cases.md; the map has no item for SVTYPE-less ≥50 bp records). Related OPEN map items: 'VCF delins SVs' and 'carry the input record's ID (SIM_SRC_ID) and gene from GENEINFO'. L7 (an SVTYPE record with no END/SVLEN becoming 1 bp) was fixed but is a different path. CR5 handled long sequence-resolved insertions' anchoring only. The hospital-demo-plan memory assumed RF8 would be LDLR's obstacle; it was not (0/35 refused, see the plan-mode evidence below), and this ingest gap is the real one.

ideas.title: A per-variant demo receipt: score truth.vcf against raredisease's DeepVariant, SV and ranked outputs
ideas.problem: After spike, fastq.sh (about 42 min predicted) and raredisease (hours), nothing tells the owner, variant by variant, how the spiked variants came out. The missing facts are: whether the pipeline called it, with what GT and AD-VAF, which SV callers supported it, whether it passed the clinical filter, and where it ranked. spike validate checks reads, not calls. validate_pipeline.sh covers Delly DELs only. Caller-level behaviour has never been measured for any class, and SNVs, indels and exon DEL/DUPs have never been run through the hospital pipeline. The truth VCF is also awkward to score: it is not bgzipped, its sample is 'SAMPLE' and its IDs are sim_*.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: the hospital raredisease run on HG002 (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results) has these outputs. call_snv/genome holds the DeepVariant VCF (params: variant_caller=deepvariant, aligner=bwamem2). call_sv/genome carries INFO svdb_origin/set/FOUNDBY. rank_and_filter has *_ranked_clinical.vcf.gz with RankScore, Compounds and GeneticModels (114 records at LDLR). repeat_expansions has the stranger VCF. Real yardstick, exact-key matching of GIAB v4.2.1 HG002 records in chr19:10-13 Mb against that DeepVariant VCF: het SNV GT match 1,845/1,850 (99.73%), het indel 402/406 (99.01%), hom SNV 793/794, hom indel 199/205. The 29 multi-allelic 1/2 records match 0 by exact key, so splitting and normalising are needed. grep over spike scripts/ src/ README finds no reader of raredisease or DeepVariant outputs (README mentions DeepVariant only as a --gvcf source). DOCUMENTED: transplant plans scope callers out (2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:115, round2.md:185).
ideas.proposal: A scorer taking truth.vcf plus standard VCFs: --snv (DeepVariant), --sv (svdb-merged), --ranked (genmod clinical) and --repeats (stranger). Per truth record it reports call/no-call. Small variants match on left-normalised, split alleles. SVs match on type plus reciprocal overlap of at least 0.5 or both breakpoints within 500 bp, and SVTYPE-less ClinVar-style records are classified as in the first idea. It also reports called GT (with 1 ≡ 1/1 on a male haploid X), AD-VAF against SIM_VAF, QUAL/GQ, supporting callers from svdb_origin, presence in the clinical ranked VCF, and RankScore with its rank among the sample's ranked variants. Output is a TSV plus a one-line summary. Given a GIAB truth for the same background, it prints the real-variant rate in the same table, so a spiked miss can be read against real misses. Following the owner's 2026-10-05 split, generic VCF scoring goes in spike (public) and the raredisease path wiring stays in cnv_validation. A side fix: write truth.vcf.gz plus .tbi with the BAM's SM as the sample column.
ideas.simplest_version: One Python script: bcftools-norm both VCFs, exact-key match for SNV/indel, 50% reciprocal overlap for SVs, then grep RankScore from the ranked VCF. Print one row per truth record.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run the scorer on the unspiked hospital HG002 raredisease output with the GIAB v4.2.1 records in a 3 Mb window as pseudo-truth. It must report at least 99.5% GT match for het SNVs (the awk measurement gives 99.73%) and at least 98.5% for het indels. A sham truth of 200 random benchmark-region positions with no variant must give at most 1% 'called'. If representation differences push the real-variant match below 95% even after normalisation, the scorecard cannot tell a spike failure from matching noise, which kills or redesigns it. The scorecard then makes the idea's real test possible: spiked ClinVar het SNVs (genes where HG002 is reference) should be called 0/1 at a rate inside the binomial band of the real 99.7%. A rate clearly below it is a spike realism gap.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 2-3 hours. Turn the awk join done here into the script and add SV matching. Then score the existing sv_slice_test FULL Manta/CNVnator VCFs against the B1-B3 truth.vcfs; it must reproduce score.py's verdicts (Manta misses ClinVar 4845403 on FULL).
ideas.impact: The owner gets a receipt per demo run and the first caller-level measurements for the classes never tested at the hospital (SNV, indel, exon DEL/DUP, LDLR SVs). It doubles as a regression check across spike versions and raredisease updates.
ideas.risks: Where it lives: the owner decided caller loops belong in cnv_validation, so keep spike's part generic. 'Called' is not 'called like real', so the real-variant rate must sit beside it. ClinVar's left-shifted VCF and right-shifted HGVS need normalisation. Rank position depends on what else is in the sample. DeepVariant writes male X as 1/1.
ideas.history_check: Never built. The map's biggest validation gap is caller equivalence. validate_pipeline.sh is Delly/DEL-only, and RF12 added Recall_outside_bg there. The cnv_validation slice-safety run (4bd707b, unmerged) has an SV scorer (score.py) that can be reused, but slices were refuted, so this scores full raredisease runs. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Exon specs from MANE (GFF + transcript choice), and fix the bundled LDLR exon BED whose exon 1 is in intron 1
ideas.problem: Exon-level events (del:LDLR:exon4-exon8) are the natural clinical spec, but the inputs behind them are broken or unusable. (1) The bundled data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed has the wrong exon 1, so any event naming exon 1 (promoter/exon-1 deletions are a known FH class) lands about 1 kb into intron 1. (2) The bundled ldlr_known_deletions_hg38.vcf names alleles like real published ones ('_ClinVar', '_Danish', '_Czech'), but its breakpoints are round-number approximations. (3) The hospital's own exon BED (Scout: 7 columns, exons merged across transcripts, no exon numbers, no strand) cannot be used. spike reads column 5 (a transcript list) as the gene. (4) spike cannot read a GFF/GTF, so the user has to hand-make a single-transcript BED for every gene.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED. MANE v1.0 GFF (prime_radiant/data/work/MANE.GRCh38.v1.0.refseq_genomic.gff.gz) puts NM_000527.5 exon 1 at chr19:11089462-11089615 (0-based). The bundled exon1 is 11090578-11090919: no overlap, starting 963 bp downstream. The 8 ClinVar initiator-codon records (around 11089548) fall in MANE exon 1, while the 5 ClinVar records inside the bundled exon1 are annotated intron_variant (or missense in another transcript). 16 of 18 exons match MANE exactly, and exon 18's end differs by 4 bp. In the known-deletions VCF, 20 of 22 POS and 15 of 22 END are multiples of 100, against 0 of 37 starts/ends in cnv_validation's ClinVar LDLR SV BED. Only 1 of its 19 DELs matches a ClinVar record by length (251409, 7,636 bp), and it is shifted by 193 bp (11106300 vs 11106493). Running the release binary with --exon-bed set to the Scout BED (scout_hgnc_all_exons_grch38p14_260122.bed.gz) and del:LDLR:exon2-exon3 exits 1: 'gene 'LDLR' not found. Available: ENST00000450305, ENST00000488147, NR_106918, ...', in a 13 MB log. Code: exon.rs:64-138 groups by (column 5, chrom), and exon.rs:149-160 falls back to genomic numbering when names carry no number.
ideas.proposal: (1) Replace the bundled LDLR BED with a MANE-derived one, and ship the script that regenerates it. Relabel the known-deletions VCF as 'approximate breakpoints, not observed alleles', or replace it with ClinVar IDs at exact coordinates. (2) Add --exon-gff FILE [--transcript ID]: read exon features from a GFF3/GTF, choose the MANE Select transcript by default (tag, or the only NM in a MANE file), take exon numbers from exon_number or the ID suffix and the strand from column 7, and name exons GENE_exonN so SIM_EXONS stays as today. (3) Make the 'gene not found' error print at most 10 near matches, not the whole catalogue. Later: c. HGVS for SNVs/indels (snp:NM_000527.5:c.682G>A) once transcripts are loaded.
ideas.simplest_version: Correct the two lines of the bundled BED, and put a 6-line awk recipe in the README that turns the public MANE GFF into spike's BED (chrom, start-1, end, GENE_exonN, GENE).
ideas.falsifying_measurement: With the corrected annotation, del:LDLR:exon1-exon1 must span all 8 ClinVar initiator-codon records (around 11089548) and end at the exon-1 splice donor (11089615). The bundled BED's exon1 contains 0 of 8. del:LDLR:exon4-exon8 on the 35x BAM must give truth.vcf/R1/R2 byte-identical to the bundled BED's (no regression on matching exons). As a minus-strand check, exon 1 of DMD from the GFF reader must contain DMD's ClinVar initiator-codon records. A reader that numbers by position fails this.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1 hour. The awk MANE->BED diff against the bundled BED is done (2 lines differ). Repeat it for DMD (minus strand) and 5 other panel genes, and check ClinVar initiator-codon positions inside each derived exon 1.
ideas.impact: LDLR exon-level demos (and any gene) land on the right exons. The hospital can use public MANE rather than its own unusable Scout BED. The public repo stops shipping an LDLR resource that misplaces exon 1 and mislabels approximate deletions as real ones.
ideas.risks: Transcript choice (a lab's legacy exon numbering against MANE). The GFF parser has to handle GENCODE as well as RefSeq attributes. Exon-spec breakpoints stay exactly on exon edges, which are easier to call than real intronic/Alu breakpoints (map OPEN). Do not ship hospital-derived files in the public repo.
ideas.history_check: Not in the map or case file. L14 fixed BED6 score columns, and number_exons refuses duplicate exon numbers. The map's measurement '0 of 36 LDLR exon edges lie inside an Alu' used this bundled BED, so its exon-1 edges were the wrong ones and should be re-measured. The BED has been unchanged since the initial commit a63115e.

ideas.title: Sex-aware defaults: detect a male background and stop the half-depth 'het' on haploid X/Y
ideas.problem: The demo background HG002 is male. X-linked demos are a core raredisease use: DMD exon deletions are the classic CNV demo. On non-PAR chrX/chrY, the default --allele-fraction 0.5 or af=het removes and replaces half of a single-copy chromosome's reads. That plants a mosaic-like half-depth event, and the truth records it as a germline GT 0/1. af=hom is physically right on a haploid X but writes diploid 1/1. Nothing warns. spike has no notion of sex or ploidy, and the truth GT comes from the VAF alone.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: samtools view -c -F 0xF04 -q 20 counts over 500 kb windows give HG002 35x chrX:100.0-100.5 Mb 65,377 against chr7:100.0-100.5 Mb 153,806 (0.425), and HG001 CRAM 105,545 against 116,682 (0.905). idxstats on HG002 gives chrX at 157k reads/Mb against chr7 at 316k (0.498). So one index-level ratio separates male from female. raredisease itself runs ngsbits samplegender (a results folder exists). DOCUMENTED: grep for chrX|ploidy|hemizyg finds 0 hits in src/ and README; CR7(b) ploidy is open (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR7). Code: truth.rs:468-474 genotype_from_vaf; main.rs:102 default AF 0.5.
ideas.proposal: At startup, estimate sex from the index (reads per Mb on X and Y against autosomes), or take --sex male|female. On a male's non-PAR X/Y (GRCh38 PAR1/PAR2 hard-coded; refuse to guess for other builds): (a) af=het or the default AF warns, or refuses with --strict-ploidy, saying that a germline variant on one X is af=hom and anything lower is mosaic; (b) af=hom writes GT 1 (haploid); (c) an explicit fractional af runs, labelled mosaic in the README. Female samples and autosomes are unchanged byte for byte.
ideas.simplest_version: A warning, not a refusal, when an event lies on non-PAR chrX/chrY and the X/autosome ratio is below 0.65, plus GT '1' for af=1.0 there.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On HG002 35x, an exon-level DMD deletion (non-PAR X) at af=hom must read about 0x inside after align.sh+merge.sh (validate coverage_ratio ≈ 0) and write GT 1. The same event at af=het must warn or refuse. On the HG001 CRAM (X ratio 0.905), af=het must run byte-identical to master. On HG002, a PAR1 event (chrX:10,001-2,781,479) must be treated as diploid. Master fails: no warning, and 0/1 is written for the half-depth event. The guard is refuted if the ratio misclassifies either GIAB sample, or a female's X ratio overlaps the male band on the hospital BAMs.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1 hour. Compute the X/autosome ratio from idxstats or windowed counts on every local BAM/CRAM and on the hospital HG002/NA12878 BAMs; done for two. Check that the gap stays wide (male 0.43-0.50 against female 0.9).
ideas.impact: X-linked demos on the male GIAB background are right by default, and the truth GT matches what a hemizygous call is.
ideas.risks: The owner prefers measure-and-warn to new refusals (only RF8 refuses), so default to a warning. Sex-chromosome aneuploidy and loss of Y in old samples. DeepVariant reports male X calls as 1/1, so the scorecard must treat 1 ≡ 1/1. The DMD exon-spec breakpoints sit on exon edges (separate open gap).
ideas.history_check: CR7(b) (ploidy) has been OPEN since the Codex review and was never built or refuted. CR7(c) (af=het exactly 0.5) is done and does not touch ploidy.

ideas.title: Provenance you can paste back: commit-stamped version, shell-quoted command, recorded seed and defaults, a run.json, and no stale outputs
ideas.problem: A demo dataset cannot be traced to the code and settings that made it. The version is always 0.1.0. truth.vcf says only ##source=spike. The seed and defaults appear only if they were typed. The README's command is joined without quoting, so pasting it into bash splits at the ';' of a per-event af= and drops every argument after it, including --seed and -o. A reused -o keeps an old sim.bam, and merge.sh checks only that sim.bam exists, so it merges the previous run's reads. A refused run leaves the previous truth.vcf and FASTQ in place. Refusals and I/O errors share exit status 1.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED, B1 run (sv_slice_test/data/B1/spike): README.md says 'spike version: 0.1.0'. The binary was renamed spike-bdd568a by hand to keep the commit. The command block shows --event del:chr19:11127041-11129177;af=het --seed 1 unquoted, and the truth header has ##source=spike with no version, seed or command. Code: main.rs:989 is args.join(" "); Cargo.toml version 0.1.0 and no build.rs; merge.sh only tests that $DIR/sim.bam exists (main.rs:2505-2508); main.rs has no remove_file or remove_dir outside tests. INFERRED from bash semantics: pasting the B1 command runs spike with af 0.5, seed 42 and default -o /tmp/spike.
ideas.proposal: Embed `git describe --dirty` at build time (build.rs or option_env, falling back to 'unknown'). Write ##spike_version, ##spike_command (each argv through the existing sh_quote), ##spike_seed and ##spike_settings (every effective default) into truth.vcf, plus an input identity (BAM size, mtime and an @SQ hash rather than the path). Write run.json last, as a completion marker: per-event stats, refusals, output md5s and a run ID. align.sh stamps the run ID into sim.bam (@CO), and merge.sh/fastq.sh refuse a mismatch. Refuse an -o that holds RUN_OUTPUT_FILES or merged.bam unless --force, and clear them under --force. Use exit 2 for policy refusals (RF8, carried, overlap) and 1 for errors.
ideas.simplest_version: Shell-quote the logged command, print the effective seed, and add the commit hash to the README version line and a ##spike_version header.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (1) On the 35x BAM, run a command with --event 'snp:chr19:11113291:C:A;af=0.05' --seed 3, then paste the README's command block into bash. truth.vcf must be byte-identical apart from fileDate. Master fails, giving SIM_REQ_VAF=0.500, seed 42 and output in /tmp/spike. (2) Stale kill test on a chr20-only BAM: spike event X into -o D, then align.sh. Spike event Y into the same D, then merge.sh without align.sh. This must refuse. Master passes its count guard and merges X's sim.bam. (3) Two binaries from different commits must write different ##spike_version lines.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1 hour. Reproduce (1) with the current release binary (about 1 s per run). Reproduce (2) on data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.GRCh38.chr20.bwamem2.bam with two small chr20 events, since align.sh takes about a minute and merge.sh runs on a 2.7 GB BAM.
ideas.impact: Every demo dataset can be traced to a commit and exact settings, which hospital validation documentation needs. Stale-output mix-ups cannot silently produce a wrong merged.bam or FASTQ. Loops such as sv_slice_test run.sh can tell refusals from crashes.
ideas.risks: Truth and README bytes change, so identity tests need updating. Builds from tarballs have no git. Deleting files in a user folder is risky, so refusing a dirty -o is safer than clearing it. Input identity must not hash a 54 GB BAM (use size, mtime and header).
ideas.history_check: Listed OPEN in the map (Outputs: provenance and machine-readable summary, stale outputs, shell-quote the logged command). Never built or refuted. sh_quote/sh_word already exist (main.rs:1297-1303).

ideas.title: Composable demo panels: per-event random streams and stable event IDs, so adding or dropping one event leaves the others byte-identical
ideas.problem: A hospital demo sample is built in steps: plant a panel, find a refused or unwanted event, drop it, add another gene. One StdRng runs through all events in input order, and read names and truth IDs carry the event index. So any change to the panel rewrites every later event's reads, ALT counts, IDs and names, even for events tens of kb apart. Each change forces a full fastq.sh plus raredisease rerun (hours) and re-checking variants already confirmed.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED with the release binary on 35x HG002 (scratchpad ord/). snp:chr19:11113291:C:A (B) was run alone and after snp:chr19:11100231:A:T (A, 13 kb away, separate footprints). 0 of B's 276 SPIKE R1 records are identical (sequence+quality), SIM_ALT_FRAGS is 22 alone and 19 with A, the ID is sim_var_1 vs sim_var_2, and the names are SPIKE_ev0001 vs SPIKE_ev0002. Code: main.rs:614 is a single StdRng::seed_from_u64(args.seed), threaded through main.rs:795/808/821/871; simulate.rs:174 builds name_prefix ev{:04} from the event index; events are concatenated (--event then --vcf) and never sorted. DOCUMENTED: K7 FAIL in bccc43a came from the reordered random stream.
ideas.proposal: Seed each event's RNG from a hash of (seed, canonical event key: type, contig, coordinates, alleles, af, dup_model). Give origin's joint removal draw a stream of its own. Derive the read-name prefix and the truth ID from a short stable hash of the key, or a user label (;id=LDLR_ex4), keeping sim_<type>_N only for display. Update validate's planted-read prefix mapping to match. Truth records keep their positional sort.
ideas.simplest_version: Per-event StdRng seeded from FNV(seed, spec string), and the event index taken from the sorted canonical keys rather than input order. Names stay in today's format.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On 35x HG002, B's SPIKE R1/R2 records (matched by stable ID) and its truth INFO must be byte-identical across the panels {B}, {A,B} and {B,A}. Master fails (0 of 276 identical). K7-style check: over 5 seeds, validate verdicts on the 15 identity sets must stay within master's seed spread. The idea is refuted if B still changes because of hidden coupling (the shared duplicate-family scan, a pool window shared between events, origin's joint draw).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1-2 hours of code reading plus one run. List every &mut rng consumer, and check whether B's replaced_reads subset and suppressed set are already identical between {B} and {A,B} (they should be if only RNG couples events). That tells whether per-event streams alone suffice.
ideas.impact: Demo panels can be extended or trimmed without re-validating events already checked. A panel run equals its one-event-at-a-time runs. This also opens running independent events in parallel later (3 Mb DUP serial floor 26.5 s at 16 threads).
ideas.risks: Every output byte changes once, so this needs the owner's explicit word and a K7 gate. The byte-identity rule applies to speed-ups, not to this. Stable names must stay unique and Illumina-shaped. validate's sim_number to SPIKE_evNNNN mapping must change in step.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'Per-event RNG streams seeded from (seed, hash of the event spec)'). Threads step 2 (per-chunk RNG streams) was not chosen (threads-step1 memory). Never refuted.

ideas.title: Compound-het and cis/trans small-variant groups inside one footprint, with phased truth
ideas.problem: Recessive and compound-het demos (homozygous FH in LDLR, or any AR gene, ranked by genmod's compound model in raredisease) need two variants in one gene on chosen copies. Small variants closer than 7 kb are refused. With --allow-overlap they are simulated independently and add up: when both coins pick the same copy, depth is about 1+v and each ALT about v/(1+v), and no read ever carries both alleles. Cis/trans is a coin per phase block, and the truth GT is unphased 0/1.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: of 1,095 ClinVar P/LP SNVs in LDLR (clinvar.vcf.gz, chr19:11089000-11134000), 295,948 of 598,965 pairs (49.4%) are closer than 7 kb, so half of all LDLR compound-het pairings are refused today. The hospital ranked clinical VCF has Compounds/CompoundsNormalized INFO (header measured), so the pipeline scores compound pairs. DOCUMENTED: two adjacent DELs at AF=1 under --allow-overlap read 67.05x/67.03x inside (REVIEW.md:2930-2939, CR1). Code: main.rs:1088-1188 (overlap refusal), loh.rs:924-949 (one coin per block), truth.rs:468-474 (unphased GT). INFERRED from code: under --allow-overlap no synthetic read carries both ALTs, because each event's haplotype holds only its own edit.
ideas.proposal: A group spec, for example --event 'snp:chr19:P1:A:T;group=fh1;copy=1' --event 'snp:chr19:P2:C:A;group=fh1;copy=2', or copy=1 on both for cis. All members of a group go onto one VariantHaplotype per copy: each copy's haplotype gets its own small edits through the existing allele-application path, plus the sample's SNPs. Suppression runs once over the union footprint at per-copy rates, and tiling is done once per copy, reusing the existing two-haplotype machinery for v > 0.5. The truth gets GT 0|1 or 1|0 with a PS, plus SIM_GROUP. 'Copy' is defined within the phase block holding the sites. Refuse, or mark 'phase unknown', when the sites span blocks that no gVCF PS links.
ideas.simplest_version: SNV-only groups (equal-length edits, so coordinates do not shift) within one footprint, each member at het. Copy 1 and copy 2 are each fully remade from their own haplotype.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On 35x HG002, plant two ClinVar P/LP SNVs in LDLR exon 4 (chr19:11105220-11105600, so one fragment covers both). In trans, fragments covering both sites with both ALTs must be at most 1% of covering fragments. In cis, at least 95% of ALT-carrying covering fragments must carry both. Each site's AF must sit in validate allele_freq's 99% band at 0.5, and footprint depth must stay within ±10% of unspiked. Today's --allow-overlap fails: 0% cis, an ALT share near 0.33 when the coins match, and 1+v depth. Downstream, the scorecard must show DeepVariant calling both 0/1 and genmod listing them as compounds.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1-2 hours. Run today's --allow-overlap on the two exon-4 SNVs with the release binary plus align.sh. Measure the AF at each site, the depth, and the fragments carrying both ALTs. This fixes the broken baseline the gate must beat.
ideas.impact: Compound-het, homozygous-FH and AR demos become possible, along with cis/trans teaching cases. This is the CR1 prerequisite, and it later unblocks complex events.
ideas.risks: Phase across unlinked blocks cannot be observed in short reads, so truth phase is defined only within a block. Groups with indels shift coordinates. Bigger footprints magnify CR3 (the sample's own indels erased). Overlapping footprints of SV and small-variant members need the ref_range per-chromosome fix.
ideas.history_check: Grouped-event composition has been OPEN since the Codex review (CR1; CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:297-301, 501-502). The 7 kb gate is DONE. Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ before simulating, not after a 40-minute stream
ideas.problem: --into-fastq checks only that RAW_R1/RAW_R2 are distinct files that the run will not overwrite. fastq.sh finds out the pair belongs to another run only at END, when found != want, after streaming the whole file. For the hospital's 380 M pairs that is about 42 min (predicted) per mistake, on top of the multi-lane trap (lanes must be concatenated first).
ideas.evidence: Code read: main.rs:1534-1559 (validate_into_fastq: is_file, same inode, output aliasing only). The fastq.sh identity check sits at END (main.rs:2362-2373). MEASURED: the first headers of the local raw FASTQs separate runs. HG002.novaseq.pcr-free.40x.R1 starts A00744:46:HV3C3DSXX:2, the same RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE as the 35x BAM's read names. HG002.chr20_R1 starts D00360:94:H2YT5BCXX:2, a different instrument and run. DOCUMENTED: about 150k pairs/s puts 380 M pairs at about 42 min (fastq-safety plan:136; full-fastq memory).
ideas.proposal: Before the quality sample and the event loop, read the first record of each raw mate. Check that the R1 and R2 base names match. Check that RUN:FLOWCELL (ignoring lane) is among the middles bam_stats saw in its 50,000-name sample. Check that read length ≤ cycles. Refuse (exit 2) with a message naming both values. Skip the check, with a notice, when the names have no Illumina shape. Optionally run the check also inside fastq.sh before streaming.
ideas.simplest_version: Compare the first RAW_R1 header's instrument:run:flowcell with the BAM's learned name middle, and refuse on a mismatch.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x BAM plus the HiSeq HG002.chr20 FASTQ pair must be refused in under 5 s, before any simulation. 35x BAM plus the NovaSeq 40x pair must proceed. Master proceeds with both. The check is refuted if, on the hospital BAM, the 50k-name sample shows several RUN:FLOWCELL values and the raw FASTQ's first record is not among them (false refusal). Measure the distinct middles there first.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 30 min: zcat|head -1 on each local raw FASTQ against samtools view|head names on each local BAM (done for 3). At the hospital, count distinct RUN:FLOWCELL values in 50k BAM names.
ideas.impact: Saves about 40 min plus a confusing late failure per wrong pair at the hospital, with a message saying which run the files are from.
ideas.risks: A sample sequenced over several flowcells. SRA-renamed reads with no Illumina shape. A BAM made from a subset of the FASTQ, which passes the check correctly.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ'). The fastq-safety fixes (658baa4: aliasing, mate order) did not add an identity pre-check. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Portable, share-safe outputs: no specimen IDs or absolute paths in README/scripts, a umask-following script mode, and no /tmp default
ideas.problem: A demo bundle (truth, README, scripts) is meant to be shared with trainees, other labs or in public-repo issues. Today it embeds the input BAM's absolute path and the SM, which carry hospital specimen IDs, in README.md, align.sh, merge.sh and sim.bam's header. The default -o is /tmp/spike, which is shared on multi-user servers. Scripts are always 0755 while data follow the umask. Nothing says that R1/R2.fq.gz are mostly real patient-sample reads.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED on the B1 run outputs (sv_slice_test/data/B1/spike). The specimen token 'D24-14230' appears 2 times in README.md, once in align.sh, once in merge.sh, 0 times in fastq.sh/truth.vcf/events.bed, and 2 times in sim.bam's header. align.sh is -rwxr-xr-x and truth.vcf is -rw-rw----. B1 kept 2,435 original pairs against 228 synthetic, so about 91% of R1/R2 is real reads. Code: main.rs:106 (default -o /tmp/spike). DOCUMENTED: a pre-push scan already had to rewrite 3 commits with filter-branch to remove a hospital storage path (full-fastq memory).
ideas.proposal: Add --portable. Paths are written relative to -o, or as basenames plus a header hash. README and script comments show a user label instead of the SM (sim.bam's @RG SM is unchanged, so raredisease sample matching still works). Script mode is 0o777 & !umask. Require -o, or warn when it is under /tmp. The README states that R1/R2 are mostly real reads from the input sample.
ideas.simplest_version: Drop the /tmp default (require -o), make script mode follow the umask, and add one README sentence about real reads in R1/R2.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: With --portable on a run whose BAM path contains a token (a symlink to the 35x BAM named FAKEID-123.bam), `grep -r FAKEID-123` over every text output in -o must return 0 hits. align.sh, merge.sh and fastq.sh must still run, and sim.bam must be identical apart from @PG. Master gives hits in README.md, align.sh and merge.sh (the B1 pattern).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 10 min: the token grep on B1 outputs is done (4 text hits, 2 header hits). Repeat on a fresh release-binary run with a symlinked BAM.
ideas.impact: Demo bundles can leave the lab without leaking specimen IDs, and pushes to the public gmc-norr/spike repo need less manual scrubbing.
ideas.risks: Relative paths break if the output folder is moved. Read names stay SPIKE_ by the owner's 2026-10-04 choice, and this proposal does not touch them. The background should already be GIAB, not patient data, so this mainly protects LIMS IDs and paths.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'Clinical safety: require -o..., script mode follows umask..., drop absolute paths and the SM'). Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Sex/ploidy-aware events: haploid truth and dosage on male chrX/chrY (the hospital HG002 demo sample is male)
ideas.problem: spike assumes two copies everywhere. On a male sample an event on non-PAR chrX/chrY at the default af (0.5) is planted at half dose, a mosaic-like state, and written GT 0/1. af=hom writes diploid 1/1. A VCF GT of '1' is ignored and simulated at --allele-fraction. The pipeline it feeds treats male X as haploid, so X-linked demo genes (DMD, F8, F9, OTC, GLA, ABCD1) give an event the pipeline cannot call the way it calls a real hemizygous variant, plus a truth GT that cannot match the caller's GT.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED this session on the hospital raredisease output for D24-14230 (HG002; samplesheet sex=1): the DeepVariant/GLnexus VCF (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results/call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz) has 105,196 chrX non-PAR records, all GT 1/1, and 4,073 PAR records, also all 1/1: 0 het. Female HG001 (NA12878_snv.vcf.gz) has 88,860 0/1 + 3,066 1/0 in non-PAR X. Of 74,867 male non-PAR SNV calls with depth >=10, only 334 (0.45%) have a ref fraction of 0.2-0.8; chr20 has 54,420 of 84,636 (64%) (zcat | awk on AD). ExpansionHunter reports a single REPCN at the 6 chrX catalog loci in HG002 (repeat_expansions/*_repeat_expansion.vcf). CODE: grep -iE 'ploidy|haploid|chrX|PAR' over src/ finds nothing. genotype_from_vaf is 1/1 iff vaf>=0.9 (src/truth.rs:468-474). resolve_af_spec maps het to 0.5 (src/main.rs:303-310). DOCUMENTED: CR7(b) (docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:343-346, 382-383). cnv_validation excludes chrX because gCNV calls male X under a diploid model (cnv_validation/config/config.yaml:43-48).
ideas.proposal: Add --sex male|female. Print an X/autosome pool-depth check beside it and warn when the two disagree. Ship a built-in GRCh38 PAR map. On haploid regions (male non-PAR X, Y) the event has one copy: af=hom means the single copy (copy_rate 1), an omitted af defaults to 1.0, and af<1 is flagged as mosaic (warn by default, matching the owner's measure-and-warn preference). Truth writes GT '1', or optionally '1/1' to match the pipeline's GLnexus convention, plus SIM_PLOIDY and ##spike_sex. A VCF GT '1' is honoured. DEL af=hom gives 0 copies; DUP gives CN 2. Female and autosomes are unchanged. PAR follows a declared policy, because this pipeline calls PAR as haploid too (measured).
ideas.simplest_version: A --sex male flag that (a) defaults af to 1.0 on non-PAR chrX/chrY, (b) warns when af<1 there, and (c) writes GT 1 (or 1/1) there with SIM_PLOIDY=1. Dosage code needs no change: af=1 already removes all event-copy and other-copy pool pairs (copy_rate min(1,2v) and max(0,2v-1), src/synth.rs:694-700) and tiles the full depth.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: In the male hospital HG002 BAM, plant 20 non-PAR chrX SNVs at af=0.5 and 20 at af=hom. Realign with the hospital command (bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000) and call with DeepVariant as raredisease runs it. KILL the idea if the af=0.5 spikes already look like real male X calls: ref fraction outside 0.2-0.8 as in >=99.5% of real calls, and GQ matching real 1/1 calls (KS p>0.01). Support needs two things. The af=0.5 spikes must fall inside the 0.2-0.8 band, where real male calls sit 0.45% of the time, with low GQ or no call. The af=hom spikes, and the flag's default, must match real hemizygous calls. Also plant a DMD exon DEL at af=hom: CNVnator/gCNV must call CN0, as at a real hemizygous chrX deletion in the HG002 Q100 SV truth. A build without the flag writes GT 0/1 and fails the GT-concordance check against the pipeline's 1/1.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Minutes: pull the AD/GQ distribution of HG002's real non-PAR X 1/1 calls (ref-fraction part done here: 334/74,867 in 0.2-0.8). Read raredisease's DeepVariant arguments (haploid_contigs/par_regions) from the run's pipeline_info. Hours: with the existing binary, plant 5 SNVs at af=0.5 and 5 at af=hom on HG002 chrX (BAM route, one region), realign, run DeepVariant on the region with the same contig settings, and compare.
ideas.impact: Hospital demos on the male HG002 background, and on any male demo sample, can carry X-linked disease variants (DMD exon deletions, F8/F9, OTC) that DeepVariant, EH and gCNV call as they call real hemizygous variants. Truth GT then equals the pipeline's GT, so concordance tables work. Landscape: NEAT and VISOR take a ploidy setting; spike is the outlier.
ideas.risks: What is 'correct' in PAR depends on the pipeline: this one calls PAR haploid in males (4,073 PAR calls, all 1/1), so follow the pipeline rather than biology, or make PAR configurable. GT '1' vs '1/1' conventions differ across hap.py, Truvari and GLnexus. A wrong --sex silently gives the wrong dosage, which the X/autosome depth check mitigates. The full CR7 genotype model is large and tied to CR3 (DESIGN_NOTES:391-396). Ship the flag first.
ideas.history_check: CR7(b) is OPEN (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:343-396; sized 'large'). CR7(c) af=het=0.5 is done (main.rs:303-310). Nothing refuted. New evidence: the hospital pipeline's own behaviour on the male demo background (0 het calls on chrX; haploid EH calls on X) shows that today's default output is unrepresentable there. That justifies the small flag ahead of the full model.

ideas.title: Phased-truth templates for GIAB backgrounds: the remade copy keeps the sample's own indels and SVs (CR3 option A without a learned model)
ideas.problem: Synthetic templates carry only the sample's SNPs. SampleCopies holds one base per position, and the gVCF path keeps SNPs only. So every event re-synthesises +/-2 kb of the event copy without the sample's own indels and SVs (and of both copies at v>0.5). For a het SNV, a hom background indel inside the window should read about AF 0.5 and be called 0/1 (inferred). A clinician comparing the demo calls with the GIAB truth would see holes around every planted variant.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED: the CR3 probe, a hom 2 bp DEL under a het DUP, went from AF 1.0 to 0.360 (docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR3). T7: 38/40 chr20 footprints hold a carried non-SNP. MEASURED in the map: of 2,000 random chr20 footprints in HG002 Q100, 48.9% hold a carried het non-SNP and 27.3% a hom non-SNP. CODE: src/loh.rs:34-43 (SampleCopies), src/loh.rs:554-557 (the gVCF parser returns early on any non-SNP), src/haplotype.rs:661-697 (apply_variants writes single bases). DOCUMENTED: backgrounds will be GIAB/demo data, never patient data (memory hospital-demo-plan.md:22). The HG002 Q100 and HG001 Platinum truths are fully phased, indels included (memory validation-plan.md). MEASURED here: the first 200,000 NA12878 Platinum v1.2 records hold 55,919 1|0, 59,748 0|1 and 84,333 1/1, with no unphased het. LANDSCAPE: VISOR (HACk), VarSim, NEAT and simuG all build haplotypes from a phased VCF of every variant type.
ideas.proposal: Add --phased-truth VCF [--truth-bed BED]. For each event, build each copy's template from the reference plus that copy's phased records: SNVs, MNVs, indels, and SVs lying wholly inside the footprint. Build it with the existing segment machinery (haplotype.rs constructors already splice DEL/INS/ALT segments), then apply the event on top. Refuse when the event overlaps a truth record on its copy, as carried.rs does for small alleles. Copy identity comes from the VCF's GT order, shared with the hap= idea. Outside the truth BED, or at unphased records, fall back to today's pileup path and record SIM_TEMPLATE=truth|pileup per event. Suppression and tiling are unchanged.
ideas.simplest_version: Indels of 50 bp or less only, small-variant events only, inside the truth BED. Every other event and region behaves exactly as today (byte-identical without the flag).
ideas.falsifying_measurement: This is the map's 'measure first' test, on real data, and it decides whether the build is needed. Plant 20 het SNVs into the hospital HG002 BAM at sites with a Q100 hom indel within 2 kb, and 20 with a het indel. Read each background indel's AF from recipient minus replaced_reads plus sim.bam, as the transplant scripts do, and call GT (DeepVariant, or bcftools as a proxy) against the unspiked BAM. KILL if today's SNP-only build already leaves >=95% of background indel GTs unchanged. The prediction is that hom indels read about 0.5 and flip to 0/1. With phased-truth templates, >=95% must be unchanged and the CR3 dup_homdel probe must read AF of about 1.0. The SNP-only build must fail both.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours, no code: run the 40 SNV spikes above with the existing binary on the HG002 hospital BAM (BAM route, hospital aligner; evidence read as in scripts/transplant/small_evidence.py). Measure background indel AF in the footprints. If nothing flips, stop.
ideas.impact: Every spiked event on a GIAB background stops leaving a +/-2 kb hole in the sample's indel and SV calls, so concordance against the GIAB truth outside the event stays clean. It is also the prerequisite for realistic STR events on the sample's own allele and for copy-neutral LOH/ROH events. Unique pairing: real reads plus a complete haplotype. BAMSurgeon has no haplotype model; VISOR and VarSim have no real reads.
ideas.risks: Truth BEDs exclude the hard regions where CR3 may matter most. Truth errors become spike errors. The SeraCare-engineered HG002 (D24-14230) differs from Q100 in 7 genes, so mask them +/-2 kb (memory validation-plan.md). Indel representation and left-alignment vs reads need care. SVs inside footprints complicate segment arithmetic (ref_range across chromosomes). Patient backgrounds have no truth and fall back to today's path.
ideas.history_check: CR3 option A is OPEN and awaiting the user (DESIGN_NOTES:122-200, 490-505). Option B as a blanket footprint warning was REFUTED by T7 (38/40 fire); this is not a warning. Fail-closed for an unreadable --gvcf is DONE. A phased-truth template was never tried. New evidence: the owner committed to GIAB/demo backgrounds, for which a complete long-read phased truth already exists. That turns option A from a learned sample-haplotype model into reading a file.

ideas.title: Haplotype-addressed events (hap=1|2): chosen cis/trans, compound hets across a gene, trio-consistent spikes
ideas.problem: Which copy carries an event is a coin per phase block, flipped separately for every event, even when --gvcf supplies phase. The truth GT is unphased. A compound het in trans (FH in LDLR, any AR gene) cannot be requested: it comes out trans or cis by chance. Inherited and de novo patterns across a family cannot be built consistently. A new seed also moves the event to the other copy.
ideas.evidence: CODE: pick_target_alleles flips rng.gen::<bool>() per block (src/loh.rs:924-941, coin at :937). The gVCF orientation is parsed (src/loh.rs:566-583) but used only as GVCF_LINK votes (src/loh.rs:874-883), never to choose a copy. Truth writes '/' (src/truth.rs:468-474). MEASURED: LDLR has 101 of 153 exon pairs >=7 kb apart (data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed; edge distance >=7,000 clears the CR1 footprint rule). So most exon-pair compound hets are allowed today, but each lands in trans with probability 1/2 (inferred). MEASURED: the Platinum NA12878 v1.2 truth is phased (first 200k records: 0 unphased het). MEASURED: raredisease samplesheets have paternal_id/maternal_id columns, and the hospital has raredisease runs of 7 CEPH-1463 members (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_fix-gatk-cnv/Seq25-160*/samplesheet.csv). DOCUMENTED: 'the seed-2 replant changed copy choice too' (memory validation-plan.md, Astra point b). LANDSCAPE: VISOR places each variant on a named haplotype.
ideas.proposal: Add a per-event hap=1|2, and honour VCF input GT 0|1 / 1|0. When the event's footprint holds a phased --gvcf SNP, take the haplotype carrying the GT's first allele (hap=1) or second (hap=2) instead of the coin. Refuse hap= when the block has no phased anchor. Write a phased GT with PS (the gVCF PS) to truth.vcf. Always log the chosen copy, coin events included. Family use: run spike once per member with the same event and the transmitted haplotype from a pedigree-phased VCF; a de novo is the child alone.
ideas.simplest_version: hap= only together with a --gvcf whose GT is phased. Replace the coin for blocks containing a phased SNP and write a '|' GT. Without hap=, the coin path and RNG draw order stay byte-identical.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the hospital HG001 BAM, with the Platinum v1.2.1 phased VCF as --gvcf, plant 20 het SNV pairs >=7 kb apart: 10 requested cis and 10 trans. For each planted ALT-carrying fragment, read its alleles at truth-phased het SNPs on the same fragment. The share matching the requested haplotype must be within 2 points of the real rate for all 40 events. Measure the real rate first: the share of real HG001 fragments at real het SNVs whose linked SNP alleles agree with the Platinum phase (expected about 98-99%). The coin build puts about half the events on the wrong haplotype, with near-0% agreement for those, and fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Minutes to hours. Measure the real agreement rate on 200 HG001 het SNVs with pysam/samtools (whatshap is installed at ~/.pixi/bin). Run the existing binary with --seed 1 and --seed 2 at one event with the Platinum --gvcf, and confirm from the reads that the copy flips with the seed.
ideas.impact: Compound-het demos (LDLR FH, AR genes) get the right phase for raredisease's genmod compound model. Trio demos (inherited vs de novo) become possible on the CEPH family the hospital already runs. Copy choice is reproducible and written down. The variant stays in real reads, which VISOR's named haplotypes do not offer.
ideas.risks: Platinum phase may not be parent-of-origin ordered: check whether hap1 is paternal before making trio claims, and parents' truths are needed for inherited spikes. Blocks phased from short reads only cannot be anchored. The 7 kb rule still blocks close pairs; those need CR1 grouped composition. PS semantics differ between gVCF producers.
ideas.history_check: Cis/trans being random and unrecorded is in the map (inferred, confirmed in code by Astra point b). Grouped-event composition (CR1) and trio-consistent spiking are listed as OPEN or new types. Nothing refuted. This is the cheap subset that needs no composition and covers every pair >=7 kb apart.

ideas.title: STR expansion/contraction events with in-repeat read pairs, judged by ExpansionHunter against real HG001/HG002 alleles
ideas.problem: There is no repeat-expansion event. An explicit 'ins:' of unit repeats approximates one, with three gaps. (a) Fragments lying wholly inside inserted sequence are never drawn, and their starts are subtracted from the count. An expansion longer than a fragment therefore lacks the in-repeat read pairs (IRRs) that ExpansionHunter uses to size long alleles. (b) The event copy's own repeat allele is rewritten to reference length plus the insertion (CR3). (c) The truth carries no repeat unit or count. Repeat-expansion disorders (HTT, FMR1, C9orf72, RFC1, ATXNs, DMPK) are a central rare-disease class, and raredisease reports them through EH/stranger.
ideas.evidence: CODE: novel_only starts subtracted (src/simulate.rs:801-817). ref_overlapping_start_intervals skips novel segments (src/simulate.rs:888-946). The ins spec accepts explicit bases (src/exon.rs:554-600). MEASURED on the hospital raredisease outputs (repeat_expansions/*_repeat_expansion.vcf; 66 catalog records per sample): 42 of 60 autosomal records differ between HG001 and HG002, and 8 have an INREPEAT allele in at least one sample. Examples: HG002 RFC1 13/51 (ADIR 9) and RAPGEF2_TTTTA_3P 7/158 (ADIR 13); HG001 SAMD12_TTTTA_3P 1/76 (ADIR 7; reference 12 units). MEASURED: the hospital library's chr20 proper pairs have mean |TLEN| 388, with 52.3% <=380 bp and 15.8% <=255 bp. Inference: most IRR fragments for a 76-unit TAAAA allele would lie wholly in inserted sequence and be excluded. DOCUMENTED: clinical repeat variation goes through EH/stranger in raredisease (cnv_validation/config/config.yaml:177).
