The Platinum v1.2 NA12878 TR truth is on disk (413,558 TR sites; platinum_pedigree_truthset_v1.2/README.md). LANDSCAPE: VISOR simulates TR expansions only in synthetic reads; I found no tool that plants them into a real sample's reads (inferred from search).
ideas.proposal: Add an event str:CHR:START-END:UNIT:COUNT[;af=..][;hap=..]. The event copy's haplotype replaces the reference repeat interval with UNIT x COUNT (an absolute count, optionally with an interruption pattern). For this event type, allow fragment starts inside novel sequence at the same density, so in-repeat pairs exist; their placement (MAPQ 0 elsewhere, or unmapped) is left to the real aligner, as in reality. The truth carries SIM_RU and SIM_REPCN, and the run README states the expected EH genotype.
ideas.simplest_version: No new spec. For an explicit 'ins:' whose sequence is a pure repeat of the reference unit at that position, include novel-only starts in tiling and in the count, and write SIM_RU/SIM_REPCN.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run a transplant at EH catalog loci. Plant HG001's allele into HG002 at af=hom, to avoid copy ambiguity, at about 10 spanning loci where they differ (e.g. HTT 16/18 vs 17/24, ATXN2 23/24 vs 23/31) and at the long ones (SAMD12_TTTTA_3P 76 units; RFC1 51-unit length in reverse). Run the raredisease EH version and catalog on the spiked data. Spanning loci: EH REPCN must fall within REPCI of the planted count at least as often as EH agrees with the TR truth on the real samples (measure that first). Long alleles: ADIR on the spike must sit within the real spread (HG001 SAMD12 76 units gives ADIR 7). Today's build, with no novel-only starts, is predicted to give ADIR near 0 and a low REPCI there, and must fail. KILL if today's 'ins:' already gives real-like ADIR.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours, no EH needed. With the existing binary, plant 'ins:' of 64 x TAAAA at the SAMD12_TTTTA_3P locus (chr8:118,366,817) into HG002 at af=hom (BAM route). Count reads that are >=90% TAAAA in sim.bam, and compare with real HG001 at the same locus (it carries 76 units). EH is available from bioconda if the gate needs it.
ideas.impact: The hospital can demo the EH/stranger path (HTT, FMR1, C9orf72, RFC1, ATXN loci) with planted expansions of chosen length, the way it demos SNVs and SVs. The real HG001 and HG002 EH calls already on disk give a yardstick with no new sequencing.
ideas.risks: GC-extreme repeats (CGG, GGGGCC) show depth dropout and quality collapse that a quality model learned on ordinary DNA will not reproduce. Real expansions are somatically unstable, so EH sees a length spread. Off-target IRRs need the whole-sample FASTQ route to land where reality puts them. RF15 (short insertions cleaner than real) may apply to unit-repeat inserts. Kb-scale expansions inflate fragment counts. The hap=/phased-truth ideas are needed to edit the sample's own allele rather than the reference length.
ideas.history_check: Map: STR expansions listed as unsupported. The novel-only exclusion is listed as an inferred limitation (README:1872). The OPEN item 'Realistic insertion content' already names STR/VNTR unit repeats with an EH falsifier. Never built or refuted. New evidence: the real EH outputs for both GIAB samples on disk (42/60 differ, 8 INREPEAT) and the hospital fragment-length shares make the transplant yardstick concrete.

ideas.title: SMN1/SMN2 paralog copy-number events for SMNCopyNumberCaller (SMA demos), as the first real-data test of --edit-model origin
ideas.problem: SMN1 sits in a near-identical segmental duplication with SMN2. Clean mode edits only MAPQ>=20 pool reads, so an SMN1 deletion is refused by RF8, or under --allow-resistant leaves most reads unedited. raredisease runs SMNCopyNumberCaller as a dedicated step, and SMA is among the most requested rare-disease results, but spike cannot plant SMN1 copy-number changes today.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED on the hospital HG002 BAM (samtools view -F 0xF04): SMN1 gene chr5:70,924,941-70,953,012 holds 6,733 primary non-dup reads, 14.4% at MAPQ>=20 and 84.4% at MAPQ 0. SMN2 (chr5:70,049,669-70,077,595) is 16.5%/82.2%. The SMN1 exon 7-8 end (chr5:70,946,000-70,953,012) is 39.8% at MAPQ>=20. LDLR is 99.6%. At c.840 (chr5:70,951,946 C in SMN1; chr5:70,076,526 T in SMN2; bases checked with samtools faidx), 32/32 reads at SMN1 carry C and 30/30 at SMN2 carry T, all at MAPQ>=20 (samtools mpileup -q 20). So reads that cover a paralog-specific base are placed by sequence. MEASURED: raredisease SMNCopyNumberCaller (smncopynumbercaller/out/*.json) gives SMN1 2, SMN2 2, Total_CN_raw 3.838, Coverage_MAD 0.076 (HG002), and 2/2, 3.898 (HG001). HG002's per-site SMN1_CN_raw spans 1.73-2.51. INFERRED: SIM_RESIST is about 0.86 over SMN1, above RF8's 0.5. DOCUMENTED: origin is validated only in the exact-twin, one-XA regime and is untested on real data (memory edit-model-origin.md).
ideas.proposal: Add an SMN recipe on top of --edit-model origin. (a) SMN1 deletion (het/hom) = DEL over SMN1, with origin removal by placement chance at SMN1 and at its XA look-alike SMN2. Make origin sequence-informed: a read carrying an SMN1 paralog-specific base is assigned to SMN1 with p of about 1 and one carrying an SMN2 base to SMN2; others split by XA as today. (b) SMN1-to-SMN2 gene conversion = the SMN1 paralog bases on one copy rewritten to SMN2's, as one grouped edit. The truth carries SMN1/SMN2 CN.
ideas.simplest_version: No code. A het and a hom SMN1 whole-gene DEL with today's --edit-model origin --allow-resistant, scored with SMNCopyNumberCaller. Reads at paralog bases already sit at their true locus with MAPQ>=20 (measured), so today's MAPQ/XA model may already be right.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run SMNCopyNumberCaller (the raredisease version) on spiked HG002. A het SMN1 DEL must give SMN1 CN 1, SMN2 CN 2 and Total_CN_raw of about 2.9 (+/-0.2; real Coverage_MAD 0.07-0.08). A hom DEL must give SMN1 0 and isSMA True. Per-site SMN1_CN_raw must fall within the real per-site spread (HG002 1.73-2.51 at CN2). Real-carrier yardstick: per-site SMN1 fractions and Total_CN_raw of public 1000G NYGC 30x CRAMs of known SMN1 CN1 carriers (Chen et al. 2020), fetched as region slices. Clean with --allow-resistant edits only about 14% of reads, keeps Total_CN_raw near 3.7 and SMN1 at 2, and must fail. KILL the sequence-informed refinement if plain origin already passes.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours. Install smncopynumbercaller (bioconda) in a scratch env and run it on the hospital HG002 BAM; it reads only the SMN and normalisation regions by index. Then run the existing binary in origin mode for a het SMN1 DEL, merge only the touched regions, and re-run the caller. Also count how many SMN-region MAPQ-0 reads carry XA, since origin needs it.
ideas.impact: SMA diagnosis and carrier demos (SMN1 0 or 1 copies) through the pipeline's dedicated caller. It also gives --edit-model origin the real-data test the map says it lacks, in exactly the twin regime it was built for. No simulator in the landscape (BAMSurgeon, VISOR, NEAT) handles paralog-specific copy number in real reads (inferred).
ideas.risks: Origin's look-alike half has been inert in practice (R4 kept 25 of 52 and removed 0 at the RF14 look-alikes). bwa's random MAPQ-0 placement between SMN1 and SMN2. SMN2 delta7-8 and the SMN1 2+0 silent-carrier haplotype. The caller's normalisation regions must stay untouched. No real SMA carrier reads are on disk (public 1000G only). Clinical stakes of a wrong demo.
ideas.history_check: SMN was never attempted (no hit in the repo docs). Origin: physics SUPPORTED only for exact twins; a real-GIAB origin test with its own locked plan is OPEN (REVIEW.md:6390-6393). RF8's suggestion to lower --min-mapq is flagged as probably wrong in segdups (map). Not refuted.

ideas.title: In-read base editing for SNVs/MNVs (BAMSurgeon/SomatoSim style), keeping real qualities, errors, duplicates and flanks
ideas.problem: For an SNV, spike suppresses and re-synthesises every event-copy pair in +/-2 kb. Most remade pairs never touch the site, yet they lose real qualities, errors, duplicates, local depth and the sample's indels. The landscape's standard for SNVs is to edit the base inside the real reads that cover it.
ideas.evidence: INFERRED (map): with HAP_FLANK 2000 (src/main.rs:241) and the tiling count at src/simulate.rs:817, about 88-92% of the remade fragments for an SNV do not show the variant. DOCUMENTED: the duplicate share in spiked regions is 0.008 vs 0.036 real (memory duplicates.md). Real hom SNVs keep 0.17% ref reads; spike's keep 0. CR3 erasure as in the phased-truth idea. LANDSCAPE: SomatoSim introduces variants directly into experimentally generated reads, which 'preserves error profiles' (Hawari et al. 2021, BMC Bioinformatics, PMC7936459). BAMSurgeon's addsnv edits existing reads. The AMP/API/CAP in-silico validation recommendations (Duncavage et al., J Mol Diagn 2022) treat 'manipulated data files in which variants are inserted into existing data files' as a main category. DOCUMENTED: raredisease runs fastp --correction (memory hospital-demo-plan.md:23), which rewrites mismatching bases in overlapping mates.
ideas.proposal: For SNV/MNV events, select the event-copy fragments covering the changed bases at copy_rate, using the same copy assignment and rate as today but only on fragments that cover the site. Rewrite the base in both mates when they overlap the site, and identically in every member of the fragment's duplicate family (origin::duplicates_of keys families). Keep each read's quality string, other bases and errors. A read whose base at the site was a sequencing error keeps an error. Rename edited records SPIKE_ (the owner wants spiked reads identifiable). In the FASTQ route, edit the raw record at the same 5'-anchored offset in sequencing orientation; fastp trims only 3'. Pairs elsewhere in the window are untouched, and non-pool reads over the site stay in the census.
ideas.simplest_version: Het SNVs only, BAM route, pool pairs only. Edit both mates and the duplicate family. Leave everything else untouched, so the R1/R2 output contains only the edited pairs.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Rerun transplant round 2b/3's SNV group with in-read edits on the hospital HG002/HG001 pair, using the same scripts and controls. The A metric must stay supported (rho rule). Background indel GTs within 2 kb must be unchanged vs unspiked in >=95%. The Picard duplicate share in the footprints must equal the unspiked share (about 0.036-0.047) instead of 0.008. Base-quality-at-site distribution of ALT reads vs real HG001 carriers must give KS p>0.01. A broken variant that edits only one mate of overlapping pairs must lose ALT after fastp --correction in the FASTQ route: realised AF below planted by about the overlapping-pair share. KILL if the A metric becomes refuted, or if no flank metric (duplicates, background GTs) moves.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours: a pysam prototype outside spike edits 20 transplant SNV sites in the hospital HG002 BAM (both mates, duplicate families), realigns the edited pairs with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000, and scores with scripts/transplant/small_evidence.py against real HG001 carriers.
ideas.impact: SNV/MNV spikes, the most common clinical class, become nearly indistinguishable from real data outside the edited base. Duplicates, depth shape and background indels are all kept. Low-AF and mosaic spikes edit exactly k real reads, with no floor of 2 synthetic fragments. This brings spike to the landscape standard for small variants, while keeping its unique whole-sample FASTQ route.
ideas.risks: Indels cannot be edited in place without changing read length, so this covers SNV/MNV only. The edit position must survive fastp's 5' end (true for raredisease's flags) and --correction. Reads with soft clips over the site. Transplant 2b already SUPPORTS SNVs, so the gain is in the flanks rather than at the site. Renaming real reads to SPIKE_ changes Picard optical keys unless tile/x/y are kept.
ideas.history_check: P1b in the map is OPEN (never built or refuted). Fix A, copying whole donor quality strings onto synthetic reads (de806dd), was REFUTED as a soft-clip fix; that was a different mechanism, applied to synthetic reads. Transplant rounds 2b/3 support SNVs today, so this proposal rests on the flank gaps (documented duplicates 0.008 vs 0.036, CR3), not on the site evidence.

ideas.title: Multi-lane whole-sample FASTQ route for the hospital's family samples (one pair per lane, SPIKE_ reads in their named lane)
ideas.problem: --into-fastq/fastq.sh takes a single R1/R2 pair, and SPIKE_ reads all take the input's most common RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. The hospital's CEPH-1463 family samples, the natural trio background, arrive as 7 lane pairs. Concatenating them (the documented workaround) turns 7 per-lane alignments and read groups into one. The demo samplesheet then differs from a real run, and a SPIKE_ read's name can claim a lane its file does not hold.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: each of the 7 family runs (Seq25-16020, 16022, 16025, 16028, 16030, 16032, 16150) has 7 samplesheet rows, lanes 1-7 with L001-L007 FASTQs (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_fix-gatk-cnv/*/samplesheet.csv). The nextflow log shows BWAMEM2_MEM run per lane (Seq25-16020_LNUMBER1..7) and one MARKDUPLICATES per sample. The HG002 BAM's @RG ID is built from file and lane ('..._S17_L002_R1_001_2'). HG001/HG002 are single-lane. DOCUMENTED: 'Lanes must be concatenated first' (memory full-fastq.md). fastq.sh is one awk over one pair (src/main.rs:2193-2454; validate_into_fastq src/main.rs:1534). Names come from the majority lane (src/read_name.rs:98-165).
ideas.proposal: Let --into-fastq take a lane list or a raredisease samplesheet.csv. Remove listed names from whichever lane holds them, with the found-vs-wanted check summed over lanes. Distribute SPIKE_ pairs across lanes in proportion to the removed originals' lanes, naming each with that lane's RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. Write a ready spiked samplesheet.csv with sex and pedigree columns carried over.
ideas.simplest_version: Loop fastq.sh per lane with a cross-lane total check, and append all SPIKE_ pairs to the lane holding the most removed originals, renamed to that lane. Emit the samplesheet.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On one 7-lane family sample at the hospital, four checks must hold. (a) Every unlisted raw record is byte-identical in its lane's output. (b) The removed totals over lanes equal the list. (c) SPIKE_ pairs per lane vs removed originals per lane give chi-square p>0.01; the all-in-one-lane version fails this. (d) Each SPIKE_ name's lane field equals its file's lane. KILL the per-lane work if raredisease on the concatenated layout gives the same DeepVariant and SV VCFs as the per-lane layout on an unspiked sample (per-lane bwa -K batches and RGs then make no difference).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours, not a full raredisease run. Take one 2 Mb region's reads from all 7 lanes of a family sample. Align per lane vs concatenated with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000, MarkDuplicates, and diff the primary records and duplicate flags. If identical, keep the concatenation workaround and drop this idea.
ideas.impact: Trio and family demos on the CEPH data the hospital already sequences, with spiked FASTQs and samplesheets shaped exactly like their real runs. Pairs with the hap= idea for inherited and de novo patterns.
ideas.risks: Proportional lane assignment is a model choice (by removed originals vs by lane size). Per-lane fastp adds QC differences. The gate may show concatenation is harmless, which would make this idea pure convenience. Hospital raw FASTQs are not on this machine.
ideas.history_check: The map lists multi-lane input as OPEN, low priority, because 'the hospital sample is a single pair' (full-fastq.md). New evidence: the family samples the hospital runs through raredisease are 7-lane, with per-lane alignment (measured from their samplesheets and nextflow log). Not refuted.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial mode: copy-less heteroplasmy SNVs and mtDNA deletions for the raredisease MT path (Mutect2, eKLIPse)
ideas.problem: spike treats chrM like a diploid autosome. The pileup calls 20-80% heteroplasmies 'het' and phases them with a coin, copy_rate assumes two copies (min(1,2v) on the 'event copy'), and truth writes 0/1 or 1/1 instead of a heteroplasmy level. Pairs that span the circular junction are improper on the linear reference and fall out of the pool. raredisease calls MT SNVs (Mutect2) and deletions (eKLIPse), but spike has never been checked there.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (hospital HG002 BAM): chrM holds 1,305,882 mapped reads (samtools idxstats), about 10,000x. Mid-genome windows are 99% MAPQ>=20 and proper (chrM:3000-3500, 8400-8500, 13400-13500). The junction ends are 64-66% proper (chrM:1-300 and 16300-16569), so census resistance there is about 0.35 (inferred). MEASURED: raredisease's MT VCF for HG002 has 50 records with AF from 0.0009 to 1, e.g. 6210 T>C at AF 0.085 PASS, and eKLIPse outputs exist (0 deletions). rank_and_filter holds only SNV/SV files, and params.yaml sets skip_mt_annotation: true, so MT calls are not ranked at the hospital today. CODE: no chrM-specific handling in src (grep finds chrM only in a loh.rs test). Pileup het thresholds 20-80% (src/loh.rs:87-121).
ideas.proposal: Mark chrM copy-less. Every fragment is removed at v, with no pileup phasing or coin, and af means heteroplasmy. Truth writes SIM_VAF as heteroplasmy, with GT as Mutect2 writes it. Refuse or handle events within one fragment of the circular junction. Subsample the pool to a cap, since chrM depth is about 10,000x. Add an mtDNA deletion recipe at real direct-repeat breakpoints (the common 4,977 bp deletion).
ideas.simplest_version: Force copy=unknown and skip phasing on chrM, document af as heteroplasmy, and warn for events within 500 bp of either chrM end.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Plant m.3243A>G and 4 other MT SNVs at 2/5/10/30% into HG002, and the common deletion at 20%. Run raredisease's MT steps. Mutect2 AF must fall within the binomial 99% interval of the planted level at the observed depth. FILTER and strand-bias flags must occur at the rate of real heteroplasmies of similar AF in HG001/HG002 and the CEPH samples (e.g. HG002 6210 T>C at 0.085 PASS). eKLIPse must report the deletion within +/-5 points. KILL (documentation only) if today's binary already passes everything. Find a real 20-80% heteroplasmy in the on-disk MT VCFs and plant next to it: the diploid copy logic should distort that level, and the copy-less mode must not.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours: plant one chrM SNV at af 0.1 with the existing binary on the HG002 BAM (BAM route), then run GATK Mutect2 --mitochondria-mode on chrM of the merged region (GATK via pixi/docker) and compare AF and filters with real low-level calls.
ideas.impact: Mitochondrial-disease demos (MELAS m.3243A>G, LHON, single large deletions) through the pipeline's own MT callers. Low until the hospital enables MT annotation, because MT is not in the ranked output today.
ideas.risks: raredisease's MT calling uses a shifted reference and NUMT handling that spike does not model. NUMT reads with low MAPQ. The quality model is learned on nuclear DNA. Memory at about 10,000x. Demo value depends on skip_mt_annotation.
ideas.history_check: Not in the map, docs or memory (grep). Never tried or refuted.

ideas.title: Golden per-read truth (NEAT/VarSim style): write each SPIKE_ pair's true haplotype spans and what it shows, plus an alignment scorer
ideas.problem: spike knows each synthetic pair's true haplotype and reference spans (PairSpans), but uses them only to count SIM_ALT_FRAGS. Nothing is written per read. After raredisease realigns, nobody can tell whether a missed spike is an aligner misplacement or a caller miss. Harnesses rebuilt this information several times (an independent 20-mer locator, junction probes).
ideas.evidence: CODE: PairSpans (src/synth.rs:670-673) is used only in pairs_showing (src/simulate.rs:1111) via tile_haplotype_reads (src/simulate.rs:974). grep finds no writer. DOCUMENTED: scripts/low_af/locate.py was built as an independent placer that agrees with SIM_ALT_FRAGS in 180/180 runs (memory independent-review-20261004.md). Manta missed ClinVar 4845403, a 2.1 kb Alu-Alu DEL, even on the full BAM, cause unknown (memory hospital-demo-plan.md:28, sv-caller-slices.md). LANDSCAPE: NEAT writes a 'golden' BAM recording where each read originated; VarSim does the same for aligner evaluation.
ideas.proposal: Write spike_reads.tsv.gz: name, event, copy/haplotype, each mate's true reference spans (or 'novel'), junctions crossed, and whether the pair shows the ALT. Add 'spike validate --alignment' to report, per event, the share of SPIKE_ reads the aligner placed within 10 bp of truth, their MAPQ and their clip state.
ideas.simplest_version: The TSV only, gzipped, written next to truth.vcf. No change to reads or RNG.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On 20 transplant DEL events plus ClinVar 4845403 in hospital HG002, the TSV's ALT-shown flags must agree with scripts/low_af/locate.py on >=99.5% of reads. A mutant with an off-by-one in reverse-complemented segments must fail that. KILL the scorer part if bwa-mem2 places >=99.9% of junction-carrying SPIKE_ reads within 10 bp of truth at every event, 4845403 included: per-read truth would then explain no miss.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours: on the existing B1 run (4845403), recompute each SPIKE_ read's true origin with locate.py and compare it with its sim.bam placement. If misplacement is near zero, keep only the TSV.
ideas.impact: Attributes caller misses (Manta at Alu-Alu junctions, EH on long repeats) to alignment or to calling. It feeds the caller-equivalence work and makes demo post-mortems quick.
ideas.risks: Adds an output file to the stale-output and provenance surface. It must not change bytes of existing outputs. It is a diagnostic, not realism. Landscape scope note: long-read (VISOR, Sim-it, PBSIM), exome capture (NEAT BED), UMI, somatic purity (BAMSurgeon, VISOR), RNA fusion and methylation (Mason) modes were considered and not proposed. The hospital runs short-read WGS raredisease (params analysis_type: wgs), has no long-read data (memory validation-plan.md), and skips ME calling (skip_me_calling: true).
ideas.history_check: Not proposed or refuted before. SIM_ALT_FRAGS (bdd568a) and the planted rows (RF13/RF14) use the same geometry at event level only.

ideas.title: Carry each site's own strand-specific systematic errors into the synthetic reads
ideas.problem: spike makes every synthetic error independent of where the read sits on the genome. The error draw depends only on the quality, the read state and the cycles left (src/synth.rs:208-234; src/quality.rs:894-921), and no reference position enters it. Real Illumina errors recur at the same base, on the same strand, with the same wrong base. These are sequence-specific errors, and callers see them as candidate alleles and as strand bias. Inside a remade footprint (+-2 kb, half of the pairs at het and all of them at hom), that error structure disappears. In addition, block_errors masks any position where at least 5 reads align and at least 10% differ (quality.rs:963). That removes the strongest recurrent sites from learning altogether.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me on the K2b sets: 62,682 held-out pairs of the HG002 35x PCR-free BAM over the 20 index-placed blocks, real against spike remade at the same 5' positions (scratchpad qtq2/k2b/{real,spike21,spike22}.bam). Restricted to the Q100 v5.0q small-variant BED, with Q100 records masked +-5 bp, BQ>=10, MAPQ>=20 and reads without indels (script /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/phys/recur.py, output recur_35x.out).
- Sites where 3 or more reads on one strand show the same wrong base: real 181, spike 2 and 2. Only 9 of the 181 real sites show that base on the other strand.
- Caller-style candidate sites (at least 2 alt reads and AF>=0.12): real 453 (500 per Mb), of which 366 are one-strand; spike 85 and 74 (93 and 81 per Mb).
- Share of mismatches that fall at a site with 2 or more same-strand, same-alt reads (phys/errproc.py): real 6.27%, spike 1.35%. On the hospital HG002 30x BAM, same blocks: 13.47%, with 543 sites of 3 or more.

The effect belongs to the SITE. I split the full 35x BAM's reads into two halves by name hash (phys/splithalf.py, split_both.out, 20 blocks):
- When half A has 3 or more same-strand same-alt reads at a site, half B has 2 or more at that site with P=0.372 (n=191), against a base rate of 0.000228. It has at least one with P=0.613, against 0.0081.
- A single error in half A raises half B's chance of one to 0.044, against 0.0081 (n=41,641).
- The other strand repeats it only 3.7% of the time.
- Hospital BAM (Q9 bases fall below BQ 10 there): P(B>=1 | A==1) is 0.0169 against 0.00057 (30x, n=2,729).

These sites are not duplicates. At full 35x depth, 690 of 757 sites with 3 or more reads have reads with all-distinct 5' ends (phys/dupcheck.py).

One-letter runs explain only part of it. 48 of the 181 sites (26.5%) have a run of 7 or more within 15 bp upstream in sequencing orientation, against 2.0% of background positions. 111 (61%) have no run of 5 or more, so v2's run bin cannot place them.
ideas.proposal: Learn a per-site, per-strand error map from the event's own donor pool. spike already extracts those pairs with their CIGARs (ReadPair.align, used by class_mix at quality.rs:816). For each reference position, strand and alt base, count the alt reads and the strand depth. Shrink the counts toward the sample's iid rate by empirical Bayes, calibrated on the split-half curve above, and keep only the excess over what the v2 error table already predicts. When a synthetic read reads a reference-origin template base at that position on that strand, emit the site's alt with the excess probability. Positions come from template_at's ref_start and orientation for flank reads, and from hap_to_ref inside reference segments for haplotype reads. Novel sequence, and bases within about 10 bp downstream of an edit (where the sequence context changed), fall back to the iid model. This copies what the sample's reads do at that very site, with no motif model needed.
ideas.simplest_version: Use only sites with at least 2 same-strand same-alt reads in the pool and 0 on the other strand. Apply rate = (k_alt - expected_iid) / n_strand, floored at 0 and capped at 0.5, in flank reads only (reference-origin segments). No shrinkage beyond the subtraction, and no change to haplotype or novel segments.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Offline injection, no Rust. From the 35x BAM reads in the 20 blocks that are NOT in real.bam (the training half), compute the site map. Inject the site alt into spike21.bam's aligned reads at the learned excess rate (by position and strand). Then re-run recur.py: count sites, candidates and the overlap with real.bam. About 2-3 hours with the existing phys/ scripts.
ideas.impact: DeepVariant is raredisease's SNV caller at the hospital (pipeline_info params: variant_caller deepvariant). External knowledge, not verified here: its candidate generator needs 2 alt reads and AF>=0.12. Real data feeds it about 5x more error-driven candidates per Mb than spike's reads over the same DNA. So precision and strand-bias filtering inside every spiked window are tested on data that is too clean. For low-VAF benchmarks (af=0.05 and below, SIM_ALT_FRAGS cases), site-specific noise sets the detection floor, and spike's iid errors overstate sensitivity. This also covers the 61% of recurrent sites that v2's run-bin context cannot reach.
ideas.risks:
- The pool holds about 15-17 reads per strand at 30-35x, so single-error sites are noisy; the shrinkage must be calibrated on split halves, or spike copies noise.
- Unlisted low-fraction variants and paralog mismapping would be copied too. That is arguably realistic, since it is what reads there show, but it must not touch the planted allele: exclude the event's own changed bases.
- Double counting with the iid table, which already includes weaker recurrent sites: learn the table with the same site mask.
- Output bytes change, so a K7-style validate gate against master's seed spread is needed.
- The sequence context changes downstream of an edit; there the map does not apply.
ideas.history_check: Never proposed or measured here: grep finds no 'systematic error', 'site-specific' or 'recurrent error' in docs, src or the case file. It is related to, but distinct from, the REFUTED or corrected copying of a donor pair's error positions (case file 2026-10-06; fix A de806dd, quality-tails). That copied read-relative cycles onto another pair, and its failure was about clip totals that counted adapter and foreign tails. This proposal keys errors to genomic site plus strand, and its evidence (split-half reproducibility) is new. quality.rs:963 deliberately masks strong recurrent sites as 'the sample's variants'.

ideas.title: Per-mate error emission: the wrong base the sample calls (and N at Q2), learned in block_errors
ideas.problem: The error table has no mate dimension (quality.rs:253-264), so it averages R1 and R2. Every error picks one of the other three bases uniformly (synth.rs:719-728). block_errors sees the called base but stores only `base != r` (quality.rs:1014). Ns are left out of learning (quality.rs:1006), so a drawn Q2, which real data uses only for N, emits a called base with an error rate that falls back to nominal (0.63). spike therefore never writes an N. The table also counts the sample's own variants near indels as high-quality errors: the >=10% mask misses positions next to the sample's indels.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me (phys/errproc.py; outputs errproc_35x.out and errproc_hosp.out). Q100 records masked +-5 bp, reads without indels, sequencing orientation.

Share of Q<15 errors going to the most common wrong base:

| Set | R1 | R2 |
|---|---|---|
| 35x real | 0.747 | 0.692 |
| hospital HG002 30x, same 20 blocks | 0.837 | 0.819 |
| spike21, same templates | 0.337 | 0.338 |

The pattern belongs to the library. On 35x, C->A is 0.92 and G->T 0.84. On the hospital BAM, A->C is 0.92 and T->C 0.91.

Mismatch rate by mate:

| Set | Q25 (Q24) R1 | Q25 (Q24) R2 | Q37 (Q40) R1 | Q37 (Q40) R2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35x real | 0.184% | 0.425% | 0.0084% | 0.0155% |
| spike21 | 0.351% | 0.402% | 0.0186% | 0.0234% |
| hospital real | 0.264% | 0.389% | 0.0072% | 0.0149% |

spike's R1 errs 1.9-2.2x the real R1 at Q25 and Q37.

Q2 and N:
- 35x real: 495 Q2 bases, all N (2.6e-5 per base).
- hospital real: 782 Q2 bases, all N.
- spike21: 441 Q2 bases, none of them N; 0 N in total.

Spike's learning rule counts high-quality errors that are not errors. Of the high-Q errors it counts on real reads, 11.3% (475 of 4,202) lie within 5 bp of a Q100 record (phys/learnmask.py).
ideas.simplest_version: A 2 (mate) x 4 (true base) x 4 (called base) matrix for Q<15 and one for Q>=15. A mate bit on the existing full and mid error cells. Q2 -> N. That is about 40 lines in quality.rs and synth.rs.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Check that the matrix can be learned from 20 blocks. Compute it on the even-numbered blocks and on the odd-numbered blocks of real reads (errproc.py restricted to each set). If the top-alt shares differ by less than 0.05 and the R1/R2 ratios by less than 15% between the two halves, build. Then confirm that the per-mate Q25 excess of spike's R1 disappears when its learning is split by mate (offline recount with learnmask.py). About 1-2 hours.
ideas.impact: This is the cheapest broad fix. When independent errors pile onto one alt base (75-84% go to one base, against 33% today), random error reads add up to alt counts at a site twice as often (sum p^2 of 0.6 against 0.33), which is what DeepVariant's candidate thresholds count. R1 stops over-erring 2x at high quality, which is the quality range callers trust. FastQC and fastp see N where real reads have them; fastp's n_base_limit filter fired on 275,690 hospital reads (hospital fastp.json). The fix is learned per library, so it carries over to other chemistries.
ideas.risks:
- Output bytes change (K7 gate).
- Emitting N changes bwa's scoring at those bases (minor).
- The hospital BAM is post-fastp --correction (13,917,960 corrected bases, hospital fastp.json), so its overlap tails are partly healed. The emission learned from it then passes fastp again in the FASTQ route; this is minor (about 1.2e-4 corrections per base).
- More cells: the mate split halves the counts, but the backoff exists.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (substitution matrix; Q2 tied to N; mate dimension), never built or refuted. Code confirmed: synth.rs:719-728 is uniform; quality.rs:1014 drops the called base; quality.rs:253-264 has no mate key. The v2 plan left the mate dimension out without measuring it. My K2b numbers (spike R1 1.9-2.2x real) are new evidence that the class dimension does not absorb it.

ideas.title: Homopolymer slips learned per library, as run-length changes
ideas.problem: At the default --indel-error-rate 0 (main.rs:178-182), spike's reads never slip at homopolymers. When the option is turned on, indels fall wherever a substitution would (synth.rs:210-226), with a uniform random inserted base. They are not shaped as plus or minus one unit of a run, and they do not depend on run length. Real reads slip at long runs at rates that depend on the library. Indel callers and STR genotypers see that stutter at every homopolymer inside a remade footprint, and spike's reads lack it.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me (phys/errproc.py). The measure is the number of 1-2 bp I/D per read pass over a reference homopolymer run, by run length. Runs touching a Q100 record +-5 bp are excluded, MAPQ>=20.

| Run length | 35x real (K2b held-out) | hospital HG002 30x, same 20 blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 4-5 | 0.0044% | 0.011% |
| 6-7 | 0.024% | 0.032% |
| 8-9 | 0.21% (11/5,176) | 0.30% |
| 10-11 | 0.97% (14/1,440) | 1.95% |
| 12-14 | 0.59% (6/1,018) | 2.59% |
| 15+ | 2.2% (15/680) | 7.20% (83/1,153; 57 ins, 26 del) |

spike21 on the same templates: 0 at every run of 8 or more.

The same sample (HG002) gives 2-3x different rates in two libraries at the same sites. The slips are therefore a process, not the sample's variants. Indels outside runs: 35x real 7.6e-6 per base, hospital 1.7e-5, spike 2.6e-6 (alignment artifacts).

DOCUMENTED: the v2 gate measured slips at 1.0% (A) and 1.6% (T) at 12-14 runs and dropped them because they add only 0.04 points to the clip share (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md:84,105,167). Their effect on indel calling was never measured.
ideas.proposal: Learn slip rates from the startup sample's CIGARs. For each read pass over a reference run (in sequencing orientation), record whether the read shows a +-1 or +-2 unit change at that run. Mask runs where the pool pileup shows the sample's own indel (at least 10% of reads, as block_errors does for SNVs). Key the rates by run length bin (6-7, 8-9, 10-11, 12-14, 15+), base, mate and insertion versus deletion. At generation, ReadState already tracks run_base and run_len (quality.rs:209-212). When the template run ends, draw a slip with the learned probability and emit the run one unit shorter or longer, keeping the qualities drawn as usual. Retire the uniform indel branch, or keep it for non-run errors at the sample's measured off-run rate. Dinucleotide STR stutter is the natural next step (not measured here).
ideas.simplest_version: Homopolymers only. Five length bins x 2 (ins/del), pooled over bases and mates, from the 20 sample blocks with a pileup mask. Apply a +-1 base slip at the end of the run.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Measure the slip table on the startup-sample-sized data (20 blocks) split into two halves by hash. Check that the 10-11, 12-14 and 15+ bins have at least 30 events each, and that the halves agree within 1.5x. The 35x is thin: 6-15 events per long bin over 1 Mb, so 40 blocks may be needed for a PCR-free library. About 1 hour with errproc.py.
ideas.impact: Clinically, many frameshifts sit in homopolymers. Today a planted indel at a run shows exactly two clean alleles, where real carriers show 2-7% stutter around both. So DeepVariant's indel GQ, its het/hom split and its filtering are tested on data that is too easy. The background homopolymer indels in every remade window lose their stutter too. raredisease also runs ExpansionHunter and stranger (cnv_validation config), which read repeat-region reads.
ideas.risks:
- Q100 may miss some real indels in hard homopolymers outside the bench BED. The 2-3x library difference argues the bulk is process, but restrict learning to the bench BED.
- Slips change bwa's alignments and may add soft clips. That is the realistic direction, but K2b's bad-end clip share must stay |z|<3.
- Output bytes change.
- The PCR-free library (35x) is thin per bin.
ideas.history_check: Slips were measured in the v2 gate only as a clip-share contributor (+0.04 points) and left out (v2 plan:84,105,167). They are not refuted for indel realism; the map lists them as OPEN. The new evidence is per-pass rates up to 7.2% and the 2-3x library dependence on the same sample. --indel-error-rate exists, but it is shaped wrongly (synth.rs:210-226).

ideas.title: Molecule-level errors shared by both mates (library damage and PCR errors)
ideas.problem: spike draws every error per read, so the two mates of a synthetic fragment never agree on a wrong base beyond chance. Real libraries carry errors in the molecule itself: DNA damage, end-repair errors and polymerase errors before clustering. Both mates (and every PCR or optical duplicate) read those errors as the same wrong base at high quality. Overlap-aware callers and duplicate or UMI consensus cannot remove them. spike's errors are all removable that way, while real ones are not.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me (phys/mateconc.py, mateconc2.py, mateconc3.py). The measure is overlapping proper pairs, at positions both mates align with BQ>=10, Q100 records masked +-5 bp.

K2b 35x held-out pairs, real against spike21 on the same templates:
- Real: 1,049,176 overlapped bases. Both mates show the same wrong base at 104 positions, against about 1.7 expected under independence; 44 of them have both bases at Q>=30. Changes in R1 orientation: T>C 30, G>T 21, A>G 17, C>A 12.
- Spike21: 20 positions, none at Q>=30, about a third of its 65 both-wrong positions as uniform draws predict.

Hospital HG002 30x, same 20 blocks:
- 155 same-base positions in 1,537,431 overlapped bases, 141 with both mates at Q>=30, and 0 where both are wrong with different bases.
- Transitions dominate: A>G 39, T>C 21, C>T 20, G>A 15.
- 135 of the 155 sites have no other read carrying that alt, so they are molecule errors, not variants.

The hospital reads went through fastp --correction: 13,917,960 bases corrected in 6,354,765 reads (raredisease trimming/*.fastp.json). That removes overlap disagreements, so in that BAM concordant errors are about half of all overlap errors.
ideas.proposal: Learn the molecule-error rate and spectrum from the startup sample's overlapping pairs. The pairs and their MateAlignment are already there. Take the R1-orientation 4x4 change table per overlapped base where both mates agree on a non-reference base and no other read shares it. Subtract this share from the per-read error table's high-Q cells so it is not counted twice. At generation, apply molecule errors to the fragment sequence once, before the two mate templates are cut from it, in generate_read_pair, generate_haplotype_read_pair and generate_depth_pair. Then both mates, and any future synthetic duplicates (see the duplicates idea), carry them. Qualities stay as the model draws them; real ones are mostly Q>=30.
ideas.simplest_version: One global rate m and a 12-cell change table in R1 orientation, from overlaps in the 20 blocks. Mutate the haplotype or reference slice of the fragment with probability m per base before template_at and template_from_seq.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
K2b same templates (mateconc2.py), concordant same-base overlap errors with both mates at Q>=30, per overlapped base:
- 35x: real 44/1.05M; spike must land at 31-59 (Poisson 95%); today 0.
- Hospital blocks: real 141/1.54M.
- The top R1-orientation changes must keep their order (T>C and G>T first on 35x; A>G and T>C on the hospital BAM).
- Total high-Q aligned mismatches per base must not rise by more than 10%.

Broken versions:
- errors drawn per mate at rate m: concordance near 0, fails;
- the fragment mutated in reference rather than R1 orientation: the G>T/C>A asymmetry flips, fails;
- no subtraction from the per-read table: high-Q mismatch rate +>10%, fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Repeat mateconc3.py on a third library and region: the NA18488 chr20 background (data/validation/background) or HG001 30x. Check that the rate is within 3x across libraries and that most sites are singletons. Then inject molecule errors post hoc into the spike21 FASTQ pairs and re-align one set to check that bwa keeps them as aligned mismatches. About 2 hours.
ideas.impact: This is decisive for low-VAF benchmarking (af=0.05 and below, a case spike documents). Real high-quality false alleles that survive mate-overlap and duplicate consensus come from molecule errors; spike has none. So spike overstates the precision of callers that combine overlapping mates or use duplicate or UMI consensus (external knowledge: GATK fragment likelihoods, Mutect2). For germline DeepVariant at 30x the effect is small: a concordant pair gives 2 alt reads at AF ~0.07, under 0.12. It also sets up realistic duplicates.
ideas.risks:
- Hospital counts are confounded by fastp --correction, which can turn a discordant error into a concordant one when the high-quality mate is the wrong one. Learning from a fastp'd BAM and then running fastp again in the FASTQ route double-applies it, so prefer learning from bases fastp could not touch, or from the 35x-style raw libraries.
- About 13% of concordant sites carried the alt in other reads (unlisted or mosaic variants); learn only from singleton sites.
- Molecule errors are about 1/3 of real high-Q errors, so the subtraction matters.
- Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: Never measured or proposed. The map only lists 'library errors shared by both mates or by duplicates (PCR, 8-oxoG, deamination)' as not modelled and unmeasured. grep finds no concordant or molecule-error analysis in docs or the case file. Nothing refuted applies.

ideas.title: A standing same-template read-physics panel, the shared gate for every read-model change
ideas.problem: Read realism is gated today by K1 (quality strings) and K2/K2b (bad-end clips, crash share). They score a few summary shares. Every gap in ideas 1-4 and 6-7 passed them unnoticed: the substitution spectrum, R1/R2 error rates, recurrent strand-specific sites, concordant molecule errors, slips, terminal cycles, and the placement of high-Q errors. The case file's K6 entry shows that comparing spike against all reads in a window misleads through composition. K2b's design (real held-out pairs against spike remade at the same 5' positions) avoids that, but it scores only clips.
ideas.simplest_version: One script that runs the six existing phys/*.py measurements on k2b real/spike BAMs plus a hash-split of real.bam, and prints one table with z-scores against the real-vs-real spread.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Run the existing scripts on a hash split of real.bam (real-vs-real) to get the calibration spread for each metric today. About 1 hour; it tells whether 62k pairs is enough depth for the recurrence and slip rows.
ideas.impact: Every read-model change (ideas 1-4, 6-10) gets a locked, composition-safe falsifier in one command. Regressions in realism are caught before merge, and the owner's measure-first process gets a cheap standard instrument. A classifier AUC is a single release-to-release realism number that catches gaps nobody thought to list.
ideas.risks:
- The K2b spike reads are made from the reference without the sample's SNPs, so the classifier and every metric must mask Q100 sites, or spike must use the sample-copy template.
- The recurrence and slip rows are depth-limited (17x per half).
- A panel can turn into a target that is tuned to; keep a held-out region set.
ideas.history_check: 'Read-level can-you-tell' is concept test 3 in memory validation-plan.md, never built. K2b exists (docs/analysis/quality-model-v2/k2b.sh) but scores clips only. Nothing refuted applies. The K6 case-file rule (compare over the same templates) is why the panel must use the K2b design.

ideas.title: Dedicated first- and last-cycle bins, and the physical cycle axis for trimmed reads
ideas.problem: The quality key's position bins are 16 cycles wide (pshift 4 at 151 cycles, quality.rs:547 and 718). The error table's end bin lumps the last 10 cycles (quality.rs:162-169), and nothing marks the first cycles. Real reads err sharply more at the very last cycle and at the first few. Their terminal errors also cluster: two or more in the last 4 bases, which bwa then soft-clips. spike spreads the same number of terminal errors, so they stay as aligned high-quality mismatches. In trimmed libraries, a read cut short by its fragment gets end-of-read contexts at a cycle that was mid-run physically, because generation uses rl = min(cycles, frag) (synth.rs:140, 187).
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me, mismatch % by cycle with Q100 masked (phys/errproc.py):

| Set | Read | Cycle 151 | Cycles 146-150 | Cycles 1-5 | Cycles 6-10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35x real | R1 | 0.538 | 0.324 (1.66x) | 0.085 | 0.057 |
| 35x real | R2 | 0.841 | 0.535 (1.57x) | | |
| hospital real | R1 | 0.249 | 0.125 (2.0x) | 0.153 | 0.088 |
| spike21 | R1 | 0.392 | 0.414 (flat) | 0.087 | 0.082 |

Aligned Q>=30 mismatches in the last 10 cycles of reads with mean Q>=35 (phys/hiq.py): real 9.0e-5, spike 3.77e-4 (4.2x). Spike's excess, about 270 errors, matches the 272 real high-Q errors found in 2-4 bp 3' clips (phys/learnmask2.py).

Clips by end (phys/clipends.py), real vs spike: 5' 1-4 bp 0.112% vs 0.021-0.029%; 3' 1-4 bp 0.182% vs 0.130%.

DOCUMENTED in the map: on the hospital BAM, reads cut to their fragment have a 0.73% low share over their last 10 cycles, against 1.55% for full-length reads.
ideas.proposal: In both the quality context key and the error table, replace the coarsest terminal bins with dedicated ones: the 3' end as cycle 1, cycles 2-4 and cycles 5-10 from the end, plus a 5'-start flag for cycles 1-5. Keep the rest as is; the refuted 19-bin refinement was general, not terminal. Measure cycles_left from the library's cycle count, not the trimmed length, in both learning (count_read and block_errors use qual.len(), quality.rs:737 and 1023) and generation. A read cut short by its fragment then stops mid-run, as the sequencer's read did.
ideas.simplest_version: Add a last-cycle bin to end_bin (cycles_left == 1) and to the quality key's position, plus a first-5-cycles flag in the error table. Make it a one-line change of the cycles_left source for trimmed reads.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Count how many sample bases and errors fall in each new terminal cell at 120k pairs; each needs at least 200 bases (MIN_ERROR_BASES). Check that real train and held-out halves agree on the last-cycle ratio within 10%. About 1 hour.
ideas.impact: bwa clips terminal error clusters. Today they become isolated high-quality mismatches inside the alignment, which is 4x the real rate in the cleanest reads at their ends. Those are what callers count. This fixes the last-cycle quality and error rise the map lists, and the start-of-read excess behind real 5' clips. It is cheap and may also move the 15% crash shortfall.
ideas.risks:
- More cells means thinner counts at the extremes; backoff covers it.
- It may trade bad-end clip share against aligned mismatches, so K2b must stay in band.
- 5' clips are partly caused by the sample's variants and chimeras, which this does not model.
- Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: The final-cycle bin is OPEN in the map, never built. REFUTED offline: 19 general position bins as a quality model, on bits per quality (0.3858 vs 0.3826; memory quality-model-options). That was a general refinement measured on bits, not on errors or clipping at the extremes. The trimmed-read cycle axis is OPEN in the map.

ideas.title: Put high-quality errors in the reads that crash: a per-read dead-tail state
ideas.problem: spike learns about the right number of high-quality errors, but puts them in the wrong reads. In real data more than half of all high-Q errors sit in the clipped tails of crashing reads. spike spreads them over poor and good reads alike, so they stay aligned. As a result spike's reads carry 1.8x the real aligned high-Q mismatch rate, while crashing about 15% too rarely. The v2 contexts (lows in the last 16, errors in the last 30) carry memory only backwards, base by base. They cannot represent a read whose tail is dead from some cycle on.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me on K2b same templates, Q100 masked:
- Aligned Q>=30 mismatch rate: real 1.19e-4, spike 2.10e-4 (phys/errproc.py).
- Reads with at least 1 aligned Q>=30 mismatch: real 1.42%, spike 2.21%. With 6 or more: 0.003% vs 0.017% (phys/hiq.py).
- In poor classes (mean Q<30 and 30-35), spike is about 2x real in every distance-to-3'-end bin, for example 3.31e-3 vs 1.46e-3 at more than 60 cycles from the end.
- Spike's learning rule counts high-Q errors at 2.41e-4 per base; 53% of them (2,226 of 4,202) sit in clipped ends (phys/learnmask.py).

DOCUMENTED:
- K2b crash share 0.90-0.91% vs 1.06% (z -3.7 to -3.9; qtq2/k2b/k2b.txt).
- In bad tails Q11 errs at 12% (mild) vs 51% (bad), and even Q37 errs at 7%; the per-read tail rate SD is 0.16 vs 0.108 if every read erred alike (memory bad-tails-20261007).
ideas.proposal: After the mate-aware table (idea 2) and the terminal bins (idea 6), re-measure. If the excess remains, add an explicit latent per-read state. Learn from the startup sample, per read, the onset cycle of a dead tail: the start of a bad-end clip, or of a burst of lows. That gives P(onset | class, run bin, cycle) and separate quality and error tables for dead and alive bases. At generation, draw the onset at the start of the read (jointly for mates through the existing class draw), and condition both the quality and the error draws on the state.
ideas.simplest_version: A two-state flag per read: 'dies at cycle c' drawn from the sample's empirical onset distribution per class. The error table gets one extra binary key (dead or alive), learned with the onset rule.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: On real K2b reads, check whether onset is identifiable: is the per-read tail error rate bimodal given class and lows (dead against alive), and does onset given class carry enough reads per cell? Compare with spike21's distribution under the same rule. About 2-3 hours with hiq.py extended.
ideas.impact: This addresses the oldest unexplained residuals: crashes 15% short, and hospital run-free reads under-clipping (0.26% vs 0.73%). It also removes the 1.8x excess of trusted aligned errors that callers count. Read-level discriminators would find it easily (more reads with an isolated Q37 mismatch).
ideas.risks:
- Earlier latent-state attempts failed as quality models: a 4-class hidden chain gave crash 0.05%.
- It interacts with the run bin and class mix, and the onset definition from clips mixes in non-error clips (the K2b masking rule is needed).
- It may move K1's SD and perfect-read shares.
- Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: REFUTED nearby: a 4-class hidden-state chain as a QUALITY model (SD 1.41, crash 0.05%; memory quality-model-options), and 12 finer classes or lows at every level (no gain, v2 gate). 'An explicit bad-tail process (a crash state that stays): not tested' (memory quality-model-options-20261006). The new evidence is the aligned high-Q excess localised by class and end bin (hiq.py) and the 53% clip share of learned high-Q errors.

ideas.title: Synthetic PCR and optical duplicate families at the sample's own rates
ideas.problem: spike makes no duplicates of its own reads (only junction-DUP depth copies, which are jittered on purpose; synth.rs:414-439). After raredisease re-marks duplicates, spiked windows show a lower duplicate share than real ones. Each synthetic molecule is also sequenced exactly once, so nothing a real PCR family shares (molecule errors, idea 4) is ever repeated. Picard's optical detection works on SPIKE_ names, but no optical pair exists. Read names take tile and x/y from a hash of the internal name (read_name.rs:154-161).
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me, hospital MarkDuplicates metrics: 17,385,340 of 369,010,019 pairs are duplicates (4.71%), and 10,361,338 of them are optical (59.6%).

DOCUMENTED: in spiked regions the duplicate share is 0.008 against 0.036 real (memory duplicates.md, realism-inspection item C). Clean mode removes the duplicates of removed originals (origin.rs:997-1054), so spiked windows lose them and gain none.
ideas.proposal: From the donor pool and the duplicate scan spike already does (5'-end family keys, duplicate flags), learn the family-size distribution, the optical share, and the optical pairs' tile and x/y distances (from the input's read names). For each synthetic pair, draw a family size. Emit PCR copies (the same fragment and template with the same molecule errors, independent sequencing errors, a new name) or optical copies (a name on the same tile with x/y within the learned distance) in the learned proportion. Keep the copies in fastq_removed_reads and merge logic as ordinary SPIKE_ reads. They must be flagged by Picard and dropped by callers.
ideas.simplest_version: A single duplicate probability per pair equal to the pool's duplicate share, and an optical flag at the sample's optical share. An optical copy reuses the tile and offsets x/y by up to 100 px. Copies share the fragment and draw new sequencing errors.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Route: FASTQ to bwa-mem2 -M -K 1e8 to Picard MarkDuplicates, on the hospital BAM's 20 K2 events.
- Duplicate share inside spiked windows within +-25% of the unspiked BAM's share in the same windows (today 0.008 against 0.036).
- Picard's optical fraction within +-0.10 of 0.596.
- Duplicate-filtered het VAF at planted SNVs unchanged within +-0.02.
Broken versions fail: copies with jittered 5' ends (Picard does not flag them, share stays about 0.008); optical names on random tiles (optical fraction near 0); copies that are not removed by callers (VAF rises).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hand-make 50 synthetic pairs plus copies (same fragment, an optical name near the original), align, run Picard MarkDuplicates with raredisease's flags, and check every copy is flagged with the right optical call. About 1-2 hours; it settles the naming question before any Rust.
ideas.impact: Spiked regions pass duplicate QC and look like the rest of the library in MultiQC/Picard (the owner wants FASTQs that Picard and FastQC treat as real). It is a prerequisite for realistic family-shared errors at low VAF. Raw-count CNV tools and coverage QC that do not drop duplicates see real-like depth composition. Callers skip duplicates, so the effect on calls is small.
ideas.risks:
- More reads per event, and family-size estimates from one pool are noisy (use the startup sample).
- Interaction with the removal list and fastq.sh accounting (found vs wanted).
- Picard's pixel distance on patterned flow cells must match raredisease's settings.
- Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: OPEN since the duplicates run (memory duplicates.md: 'spike makes no duplicates of its own reads ... reported only'). Never built. The duplicate-leak fix (2eb9309) is done and separate.

ideas.title: Fragment-end (tagmentation) motif: weight synthetic fragment starts by the library's own end preference
ideas.problem: Synthetic fragment starts are uniform (simulate.rs:1043 and 1064, gen_range). The hospital library's real read starts carry a strong composition signature over the first cycles, which looks like Tn5 tagmentation (inferred). spike's reads start at background composition. A single base tells them apart statistically, and the local start-site pattern (and hence fine-scale coverage and duplicate structure) differs.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED by me at the 22 hospital K2 events (phys/startcomp2.py; scratchpad qtq2/k2v2), first cycles in sequencing orientation:
- Sample reads (n=227,849): cycle 1 A .182, C .337, G .291, T .190; cycle 2 T .318, G .182; cycle 6 A .322.
- SPIKE_ reads (n=9,559): cycle 1 A .272, C .226, G .222, T .281, and flat at these values through cycle 11.

DOCUMENTED in the map: the 35x PCR-free library shows only a mild bias (cycle 1 A .331), so this belongs to the library.
ideas.proposal: From the startup sample, learn a position weight matrix over -5..+10 bp around each read's 5' end, on the read's own strand, against background k-mer frequencies. When drawing a fragment, accept a uniform start with probability w(left end) x w(right end) / w_max^2 (rejection sampling), or use importance weights over the candidate starts. Apply the same weighting to junction-crossing zones for additive events.
ideas.simplest_version: A position-specific mononucleotide PWM for 3 bases on each side of the cut. Rejection sampling of fragment starts on both ends, with the acceptance rate logged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
At the hospital K2 events, the SPIKE_ reads' composition at cycles 1-6 must be within +-0.02 of the sample reads' in every base (C .337 and G .291 at cycle 1). On 35x, spike must stay within +-0.02 of its mild bias.
Broken versions fail: the PWM applied on the reference strand instead of the read strand (the cycle-1 C/G excess appears as G/C mirrored on reverse reads), and master (flat .22-.28).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Learn the PWM on even blocks and test its likelihood gain on odd blocks of hospital reads. Compute the rejection acceptance rate to know the speed cost. About 1 hour with a Python script.
ideas.impact: This removes a per-read tell that a classifier or FastQC per-base content would see in the SPIKE_ block of a FASTQ, and gives synthetic reads the library's own start-site structure. The effect on variant calls is likely small. The owner wants FASTQs that downstream tools treat as real.
ideas.risks:
- Rejection sampling costs speed, and the owner cares about speed.
- It changes which fragments cross junctions, so SIM_ALT_FRAGS and the realised VAF shift slightly.
- It is library-specific: it must be learned, never hard-coded.
- A minimal-edit or replace-in-place tiling (event-lens P1) would inherit real starts for free, except for novel or junction fragments.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (fragment-end motif, measured on the hospital BAM). Never built or refuted. The GC bias, a related start-placement effect, was measured small (0.88-1.08) and left alone.

ideas.title: Adapter read-through and sub-read-length fragments for untrimmed libraries
ideas.problem: For an untrimmed library spike never draws a fragment shorter than one read (min_fragment_len = read_length, synth.rs:128-134; stats.rs:34-41). Synthetic reads therefore never read into the adapter and never form fully overlapping, dovetailed pairs. Real untrimmed libraries carry adapter clips and short fragments that aligners and callers handle as noise.
ideas.evidence:
DOCUMENTED:
- On the 35x untrimmed slice, 0.71% of all reads (25.7% of clipped reads) have adapter clips; spike has 0 (memory soft-clip-causes-20261006).
- 0.83% of proper R1 pairs in chr20:10-11 Mb have |TLEN|<151 (map).
- The adapter can be learned from the sample: past TLEN, the consensus equals TruSeq R1/R2 for 33 bp and then the library's index (memory soft-clip-causes).

Code confirmed: mate_length returns read_length for an untrimmed library and refuses shorter fragments (synth.rs:138-142). The hospital library is sequencer-trimmed, so it is not affected (memory read-length-fix).
ideas.proposal: For libraries bam_stats calls untrimmed, admit the pool's own |TLEN| below read length into the fragment CDF. Append the per-mate adapter consensus, learned from the startup sample's short pairs (bases past TLEN in sequencing order, including the index), past the fragment end, and run the quality and error model over the adapter bases as over any other bases.
ideas.simplest_version: The TruSeq R1/R2 adapter strings plus the learned 8-10 bp index from the short pairs in the startup sample, with the fragment CDF floor lowered to 1 for untrimmed libraries.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Re-extract the adapter consensus from 20 blocks of the 35x BAM and check per-position agreement of at least 0.76 over 33 bp on both halves, as before. Ask the user whether adapter clips are in scope before any code.
ideas.impact: It matters for users with untrimmed libraries (GIAB-style data, other sites). Adapter-clipped short fragments are about 26% of real soft clips there, and their absence makes spiked windows cleaner for SV callers' clip-based evidence. It does not matter for the hospital demo.
ideas.risks:
- The user leans toward modelling only bad ends (memory soft-clip-causes: 'maybe we can skip all softclips except for those generated by bad ends'), so ask first.
- Index barcodes are sample-specific: copying the input's index is realistic, but it should be documented.
- Output bytes change for untrimmed inputs only.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map and in the soft-clip analysis (learnable adapter, not built). The user leans away from it. Never refuted. Read-length trimming for trimmed libraries is done (3684f74).

ideas.title: Sex and ploidy context: refuse impossible 'het' events on a male's non-PAR X/Y and write haploid GTs
ideas.problem: spike has no sex, ploidy or PAR model. On male non-PAR X/Y, the default af 0.5 builds a 50% mosaic and writes GT 0/1, and af=hom writes diploid 1/1. The pileup's spurious 'het SNPs' on a haploid X are phased, and a coin picks the event copy among them. The hospital's own demo sample is male, and X-linked genes (DMD above all) are a core clinical use. The run raises no warning.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED. HG002 35x BAM, samtools view -c -F 0xF04 -q 20 per 1 Mb: chrX:50-51 Mb gives 128,171 and chrX:31-32 Mb (DMD) 137,311, against chr7:50-51 Mb at 290,897 (0.44-0.47). PAR1 chrX:1-2 Mb gives 264,805 (0.91, diploid) and chrY:3-4 Mb 127,939. idxstats per kb: chrX 157.1 vs chr7 315.6 (0.498). HG001 CRAM (female): chrX:50-51 Mb 200,244 vs chr7 226,630 (0.88). raredisease's own output for the hospital sample (cnv_validation/from_rv/.../ngsbits_samplegender/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_ngsbits_sex.tsv) reads 'male', ratio_chry_chrx 0.2832. Spike runs (v2 binary 7f28bb0; master 4a5672d changed only quality.rs's run-ratio cache, per git diff --stat) used del:chrX:31500000-31502000 on HG002 35x (scratchpad robust/chrx_het, chrx_hom). af=het exits 0 with 0 WARN lines and writes SIM_VAF=0.500, GT 0/1. af=hom writes GT 1/1. The log reads 'chrX:31498000-31504000: 1 het SNPs, 3 hom-alt SNPs; phased 1 het SNPs into 1 block(s)', which is a het call on a haploid X. A chrM run (snp:chrM:3243:A:G;af=0.3, robust/chrm) worked numerically: realised 5073/(5073+3+12334)=0.291 by an exact 25-mer count, but it took 52 s wall and 2.64 GB RSS (938,703-pair pool, cov 29,056) and still wrote GT 0/1. Code: grep for chrX|chrY|ploidy|haploid|PAR|chrM in src/ finds only one gVCF test (loh.rs:1480). genotype_from_vaf is truth.rs:468. DOCUMENTED: CR7(b) (docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404).
ideas.proposal:
Give each event a ploidy context.
(1) Sex comes from the BAI's per-contig mapped-record counts: chrX density against the autosomes, with a cut near 0.7 (measured 0.44-0.50 male, 0.88 female). A --sex flag overrides it and is cross-checked. CRAM indexes carry no counts, so a CRAM needs --sex, or the estimate comes from the quality sample's chrX block.
(2) A built-in GRCh38 PAR table (chrX:10,001-2,781,479 and 155,701,383-156,030,895), plus --ploidy-bed for other builds.
(3) On haploid regions: refuse af<1 unless --allow-mosaic, write GT '1', skip het phasing, and treat every fragment as the one copy (copy_rate = v).
(4) Later: chrM without phasing, and its truth written in the mitochondrial convention.
ideas.simplest_version: From BAI counts, call a sample male when chrX density is below 0.7x the autosomes. Then refuse any event in non-PAR chrX/chrY with af<1, and write GT '1' for af=1 there. Nothing else changes.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
On real data:
(a) Inferred sex must be male for HG002 35x and for the hospital BAM (raredisease says male), and female for HG001.
(b) HG002 del:chrX:31500000-31502000 af=het must be refused.
(c) With af=hom, after align.sh and merge.sh, depth inside the DEL must be only the resistant share (SIM_RESIST 0.027), and the truth GT must read '1'.
(d) A PAR1 event at chrX:1.5 Mb (measured diploid depth) must behave as today, with af=het allowed and GT 0/1. A classifier that ignores PAR fails here.
(e) On HG001, the same DMD event at af=het must be allowed and byte-identical to master.
Kill the design if (d) is refused or (e) moves.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Mostly done this session: region counts on three samples and the two DMD runs. What remains takes under an hour: run samtools idxstats on every whole-genome BAM here (HG002 35x, the HG002 strobealign BAM, the hospital BAM). Confirm that one cut separates them by chrX/autosome density, and that a chr20-only slice gives 'unknown', not 'female'.
ideas.impact: Hospital demo: a DMD exon deletion in the male GM24385/HG002 sample currently becomes a biologically impossible half-depth 'het', and its truth GT is wrong for hap.py/vcfeval haploid scoring. With the fix it is refused, or built as a hemizygous loss with GT '1'. The fix also stops phasing on alignment artifacts.
ideas.risks: Inference fails on slices without chrX reads, so 'unknown' must refuse X events unless --sex is given. Truth GT changes for male X runs, a deliberate byte change. Mosaic studies legitimately want af<1 on X, hence --allow-mosaic. The full CR7(b) copy-number model is large, and this is only its refusal-plus-GT slice.
ideas.history_check: CR7(b) has been open since the Codex review, rated 'large' (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404). CR7(c), exact af=het, is done (8dca8d0). The idea was never built or refuted. New this session: raredisease's own sex call says the hospital sample is male, a measured silent run on DMD, and the haploid het-phasing artifact.

ideas.title: --gvcf sample identity: pick the BAM's sample and check that the VCF describes these reads
ideas.problem: load_snps_from_gvcf hard-codes the first sample column (loh.rs:396, `let sample_col: usize = 9`). Its comment claims the index comes from the header, but it does not. Nothing compares the VCF's sample with the BAM's SM or with the reads. When the file has any het SNP in the footprint, it replaces the pileup outright (loh.rs:189-216), the sample's own hom-alt calls included. A multi-sample family VCF, or a mixed-up GIAB file, therefore writes another person's alleles onto spike's reads with exit 0.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED. HG002 35x BAM with HG001's v4.2.1 benchmark VCF as --gvcf, del:chr20:44999900-45000100 (scratchpad robust/gv2_HG001): exit 0, 0 WARN lines. spike took HG002's 6 hom-alt SNPs (HG001 is het at the same 6) as '6 het SNPs' in 3 blocks and 'classified 234 fragments'. At chr20:45,000,494 (HG002 1/1 G>A), 15 of 15 SPIKE_ reads carry REF, against 0 of 32 kept originals. With HG002's own VCF, 15 of 15 carry ALT (robust/allele_count.py).
Exposure over 200 random 4 kb footprints inside both benchmark beds on chr20 (robust/wrong_gvcf.py; HG002 Q100 vs HG001 v4.2.1):
- The wrong VCF has at least one het in 65.5% of windows, so it replaces the pileup there.
- Only 211 of HG002's 736 het SNPs are het in HG001.
- HG001 brings 641 hets.
- 12% of windows lose a HG002 hom-alt.
The control (HG002 v4.2.1 in the wrong-file slot) gives 734/736 shared and 0 lost.
Sample names: the HG001 VCF says 'HG001' and the BAM SM says 'HG002'. The hospital raredisease VCF's sample, 'D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x', equals its BAM SM (bcftools query -l, samtools view -H), so a name match passes the hospital's correct case. DOCUMENTED: README.md:386 describes using the hospital's own DeepVariant calls with --gvcf.
ideas.proposal:
(1) Choose the VCF column whose sample name equals the BAM SM. If there is one sample under a different name, warn. If there are several samples and none matches, refuse and name a --gvcf-sample flag.
(2) Add a data gate that reuses the second BAM pass spike already makes at the gVCF het positions (collect_snp_alleles). It computes the share of gVCF het sites with at least 8 reads where both alleles each reach 15% or more. Below a locked cut, refuse with 'this VCF does not describe this BAM'. The share is reported in the run log either way.
ideas.simplest_version: Refuse a multi-sample VCF without --gvcf-sample. Warn when a single sample's name differs from SM. Log the het-concordance share, without gating on it yet.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Concordance over 100 random footprints must be at least 0.9 for HG002 35x with HG002's VCF, and for the hospital BAM with its raredisease VCF. It must be at most 0.5 for HG002 35x with HG001's VCF (benchmark overlap predicts about 211/641). At chr20:44.998-45.002 Mb the HG001 file must be refused; today it puts REF on 15/15 SPIKE reads. If correct-VCF runs fall under the cut in more than 1% of footprints (pileup noise at 30x), the gate is wrong. Every correct-VCF run must stay byte-identical to master.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Under an hour: bcftools mpileup -R at the HG001 and HG002 het sites in 100 footprints of the 35x BAM gives the two concordance distributions before any code is written. The hospital BAM with its own VCF is the specificity check.
ideas.impact: A user who passes the hospital's case VCF (multi-sample for a trio) or the wrong GIAB file gets a refusal. Today the background around every event quietly carries another person's alleles. By inference that is about one false-allele site per footprint: 430 HG001-only hets over 200 windows, with one coin per block. The sample's own hom-alts also turn het.
ideas.risks: Low-MAPQ footprints give few concordance sites, so the gate must abstain below a minimum count. Calls from another caller on the right sample still disagree at some sites, which is why the cut is locked only after the gate B distributions. Benchmark VCFs name samples 'HG002' while lab BAMs use other SMs, so a single-sample name mismatch only warns.
ideas.history_check: Not in the case file or any review finding (grep finds only the hard-coded column). Review finding 4 (gVCF hom-alt, 2ab9fc7) and CR3 fail-closed (an unreadable --gvcf stops) touched this path but never sample identity. It was never proposed or refuted.

ideas.title: Refuse a BAM/CRAM aligned to another build: compare @SQ LN/M5 with the FASTA, plus a data tell
ideas.problem: spike never compares the alignment's @SQ lengths or M5 with the FASTA. header.reference_sequences() is used only for name lookups (extract.rs:330, 385, 468; quality.rs:1093). A BAM aligned to another build with the same contig names (T2T-CHM13 uses chr1..chrX) runs to exit 0 with a normal-looking truth VCF. It removes the wrong reads and learns the quality model against the wrong sequence.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED. /home/parlar_ai/dev/telotyper/aligned/ERR3239334.dedup.bam is a CHM13 alignment (bwa-mem2 @PG 'reference/chm13v2.0.fa'; @SQ chr19 LN 61,707,364 against GRCh38's 58,617,616). spike run with the GRCh38 no-alt FASTA and del:chr19:11100000-11102000 (scratchpad robust/chm13): exit 0, 0 WARN lines, truth SIM_RESIST 0.011 and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 1.11. But the log reads 'chr19:11098000-11104000: 10 het SNPs, 4483 hom-alt SNPs' and 'Applied 3012 het SNP variants'; the same event on HG002 35x gives 13 het and 0 hom-alt. The quality sample masked 20,623,489 of 29,768,724 bases (69.3%) as 'the sample's own variant sites', against 83,841 of 38,120,856 (0.22%) on HG002 35x.
Headers: HG002 35x and hospital @SQ are identical to the .fai (diff of name and LN). NA18488.chr20.bam has 3,171 extra alt/decoy/HLA contigs, with LN and M5 equal on shared contigs (chr19 M5 85f9f4fc... in both the .dict and the BAM). The HG001 CRAM's M5 also matches.
DOCUMENTED: validate_pipeline.sh had to add its own contig check (check_background_contigs, scripts/validate_pipeline.sh:464-480) because Delly refused an alt-aware background.
ideas.proposal:
Before extraction, check every contig spike reads: event contigs, --region and the quality-sample contigs. Each needs @SQ LN equal to the .fai length, and M5 equal to the .dict (or a computed MD5) when both exist. Otherwise refuse with a policy exit code. Warn when the BAM names contigs the FASTA lacks: that is an alt-aware alignment, and align.sh will realign spike's reads to a different reference than the originals.
A second, header-independent layer catches reheadered files: refuse when the quality sample's masked share exceeds a locked cut (0.22% correct vs 69.3% wrong, measured).
ideas.simplest_version: Compare LN for the event contigs only, in one loop over header.reference_sequences() against the .fai lengths spike already loads.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: ERR3239334 with the GRCh38 FASTA must be refused before extraction. HG002 35x, the hospital BAM, NA18488.chr20.bam (a superset) and the HG001 CRAM must pass with outputs md5-identical to master. For the data layer, a scratch copy of the CHM13 BAM reheadered with GRCh38 LNs (samtools reheader) must still be refused by the masked-share rule, while all GRCh38 backgrounds stay under the cut. Kill it if any correct background is refused.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done here: two runs and the header diffs. What remains, under 10 minutes: one spike run each on the hospital BAM and NA18488 to read their masked shares from the 'Error table from' log line. NA18488 is African ancestry and more polymorphic, so it sets the specificity margin for the cut.
ideas.impact: Users with T2T or hg19 BAMs that share chr names get a refusal instead of a silently wrong spike, which removes unrelated reads and learns errors from 69%-masked data. Harnesses no longer need their own contig checks.
ideas.risks: Many BAMs carry no M5 (HG002 35x has none), so the check is LN-only there. The masked-share cut must not fire on a highly polymorphic sample or on low-MAPQ-heavy input. Compare only the contigs spike reads, so that analysis-set naming differences in chrUn contigs do not cause false refusals.
ideas.history_check: The map lists it as inferred ('No check that the BAM was aligned to the given FASTA'). It was never built or refuted. CR-BUILD was about bcftools test dependencies and is unrelated. This session gives the first measured silent run.

ideas.title: v2 regression: the startup quality sample aborts on alt/decoy-aware inputs (GIAB HG001 CRAM)
ideas.problem: quality::sample_input spreads 20 blocks over every indexed window of every @SQ contig (quality.rs:1091-1199), and any block failure is fatal. On a GRCh38 full-analysis-set plus decoy alignment (the 1000G/NYGC layout, and GIAB's NA12878.final.cram in data/), the last block lands on a decoy contig. With the no-alt FASTA, the run aborts before any event with a cryptic error. The pre-v2 binary runs the same command fine.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED. NA12878.final.cram (data/giab_hg38/HG001) has 3,366 @SQ. 4,605 of its 79,637 CRAI slices (5.8%) are on non-primary contigs. Block 19, at window floor(39W/40), lands on chrUn_JTFH01000280v1_decoy (scratchpad robust/crai_sorted.txt).
The v2 binary (7f28bb0; master 4a5672d differs only in quality.rs's run-ratio cache, per git diff --stat 7f28bb0 4a5672d -- src) with the no-alt FASTA and del:chr19:11100000-11102000 exits 1 after 7 blocks: 'Error: invalid reference sequence name: chrUn_JTFH01000277v1_decoy' (robust/hg001cram/log.txt).
The pre-v2 binary (target/release, built 2026-10-06 at about master 97aa3b4) exits 0 on the same command: 2265 kept, 228 chimeric (robust/hg001cram_old).
INFERRED from code: a BAM with reads on a contig absent from the .fai would reach fetch_window (quality.rs:1190, reference.rs:66-73) and fail with 'chromosome ... not found in FASTA index'.
ideas.proposal: Choose quality blocks only from windows on contigs that are in the FASTA with a matching length (shared with the build check). A block on a contig the FASTA lacks is skipped with a warning and counts toward the 50,000-pair thin-sample warning. It no longer aborts the run. Whether to restrict to primary assembled chromosomes is a separate, byte-changing decision.
ideas.simplest_version: In indexed_windows, keep only names present in the .fai (one HashSet lookup) before choose_blocks.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: HG001 CRAM with the no-alt FASTA must exit 0 with all 20 blocks on .fai contigs. On HG002 35x and the hospital BAM, whose @SQ equal the .fai (measured), R1/R2, truth.vcf, replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt must be md5-identical to master, because the window list is unchanged. The log line 'from chr1:73644223 to chrX:119028195' on HG002 must not move. A mutant without the filter must reproduce the abort.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done this session: the abort and the pre-v2 success on the same command. The fix plus the three md5 comparisons take about an hour.
ideas.impact: Public GIAB and 1000G CRAMs (the HG001 CRAM in data/) work again with the no-alt FASTA, instead of dying on an unexplained decoy name. This matters before v2 is pushed, since public master does not yet have the regression.
ideas.risks: Restricting to primary contigs would change bytes for BAMs with reads on chrUn/random/EBV, so keep the minimal filter. Skipping blocks must cover only 'contig not in FASTA', never decode or I/O errors, or real faults get hidden.
ideas.history_check: Introduced by quality model v2 (7f28bb0, 2026-10-07). Its K4 measured only HG002 35x and the hospital BAM, both with @SQ equal to the .fai. Nothing on decoys appears in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model*.md or the case file (grep). It was never reported.

ideas.title: A refused or partial run leaves the previous run's outputs in a reused -o: clear them, stamp a run id, distinct exit codes
ideas.problem: spike creates -o (main.rs:489) but never removes stale files. A run refused after the CLI checks (carried allele, RF8, too few donors) exits 1 and leaves the previous run's truth.vcf, R1/R2, replaced_reads.txt, merge.sh and fastq.sh in place. merge.sh checks only that sim.bam exists. A loop that ignores the exit code, or a user who runs fastq.sh afterwards, spikes the wrong event. Refusals and I/O errors share exit status 1 (main.rs:862-864).
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED (scratchpad robust/stale). Run 1, del:chr19:11100000-11102000 on HG002 35x into one -o, exited 0 (truth.vcf md5 a5538b6f2fa9). Run 2 into the same -o, snp:chr20:45000494:G:A, was refused at exit 1 with 'the sample already carries another allele ... (42 of 43 reads)'. Afterwards truth.vcf (still a5538b6f2fa9, the chr19 DEL), R1.fq.gz (84851d3db490), merge.sh and fastq.sh are all run 1's.
DOCUMENTED: the owner's loop works around this with rm -rf before every run (sv_slice_test/wt/slice_safety/run.sh:121, 131 per the map), and validate_pipeline.sh:947 reuses an existing truth.vcf.gz.
ideas.proposal: At startup, after the CLI checks, refuse when -o holds any of RUN_OUTPUT_FILES, sim.bam or merged.bam, unless --overwrite is given, which deletes them first.
