Write run.json last as a completion marker; it holds the run id, seed, shell-quoted command and per-event stats. align.sh stamps the run id into sim.bam's @CO. merge.sh and fastq.sh refuse when run.json is missing or the id differs. Policy refusals exit 2 and errors exit 1.
ideas.simplest_version: Delete RUN_OUTPUT_FILES plus sim.bam, sim.bam.bai and merged.bam at startup, before any work, and publish truth.vcf last via temp file and rename.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Repeat the two-run sequence above. Afterwards no run-1 truth.vcf, R1 or fastq.sh may remain, or merge.sh/fastq.sh must refuse. With --overwrite, a run 1 then run 2 sequence must leave run 2's outputs byte-identical to run 2 in a fresh folder. A fresh single run must be byte-identical to master (apart from the new run.json). Kill it if a harness in scripts/ (validate_pipeline.sh, slice_loop.sh, real_events.sh) breaks.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done: two runs, 5 minutes. Before building, grep the harnesses for reuse of -o and for '-ne 0' exit handling, to list what exit code 2 would change.
ideas.impact: Hospital loops over many genes, and the user's own SV loops, can no longer pick up a stale truth or stale reads after a refusal. Machine harnesses can tell a refusal from a crash.
ideas.risks: Deleting files in a user-chosen folder must touch only spike's own names. Exit code 2 changes what existing harnesses see, though run.sh treats any non-zero exit as a refusal already.
ideas.history_check: In the map's OPEN list ('Stale outputs', inferred from code) together with provenance/run.json. It was never built or refuted. This session measured it.

ideas.title: Detect duplicate-unmarked input before simulating (unmarked BAMs inflate the planted VAF after re-marking)
ideas.problem: The main run never checks that the input is duplicate-marked. On an unmarked BAM, PCR and optical duplicates enter the donor pool as independent fragments. Coverage counts them, members of a family are suppressed independently, and spike's reads carry no duplicates. After raredisease re-marks duplicates, the kept originals lose their duplicates and spike's reads do not, so the alt share rises. validate.rs already has the detector (L15), but main does not use it.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED. data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.GRCh38.novaseq-40x.strobealign-sv.two-pass.bam has no markdup @PG and no @RG. In chr20:10-10.5 Mb, 0 of 149,768 primary records are flagged duplicate, against 12.10% of 149,273 on the bwa 35x BAM. samtools fixmate+markdup on the strobealign BAM's proper MAPQ≥20 pairs in chr19:11.0-11.2 Mb marks 9,276 of 70,881 reads (13.1%).
spike on the strobealign BAM (robust/strobe) exits 0. Its only warning is the missing SM ('tagging simulated reads SM:SIM'), and it reports 'Duplicates of the removed originals: 0 pair(s)', against 54 on the 35x BAM.
The detector would stay quiet on NA18488.chr20.bam (8.47% flagged, markdup @PG), the hospital BAM (3.76%, markdup @PG) and the CHM13 BAM (10.6%). It lives at validate.rs:2713-2749.
INFERRED harm: at v=0.5 and d=0.131, VAF after re-marking ≈ v/(v+(1-v)(1-d)) ≈ 0.535.
ideas.proposal: Run the L15 rule (duplicate flags present, or a markdup @PG) in main on the index-placed quality sample, not the file head. When neither holds, refuse unless --unmarked-ok, or warn, as the user chooses. Print the expected VAF bias from the pool's own duplicate-family share, which spike can compute by 5' ends as duplicates_of already does.
ideas.simplest_version: A single warning line when the quality sample has zero duplicate flags and the header has no markdup @PG.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Detector: it must fire on the strobealign BAM and stay silent on HG002 35x, the hospital BAM, NA18488, the HG001 CRAM and CHM13.
Harm: plant 100 het SNVs into the strobealign BAM and into the 35x BAM, run samtools markdup on each merged BAM, and compare realised VAF. The prediction is about +0.03 on the unmarked input. If the difference is under 0.01 with a 95% CI excluding 0.03, the harm claim dies and a log line is all that is warranted.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Detector side done (flag counts, @PG, region markdup). For the harm side, run the 100-SNV plant plus markdup on chr20 of both BAMs: a few hours of compute, and no code change.
ideas.impact: Users who bring aligner output straight from strobealign or minimap2, or any pre-markdup BAM, get told, instead of a planted fraction about 3 points high once their pipeline marks duplicates.
ideas.risks: Some PCR-free libraries legitimately have very few duplicates, so a zero-flag check alone could false-fire on a marked file with no duplicates in the sample. The @PG check covers that. Refusing would break users who intentionally feed unmarked BAMs, so warn by default.
ideas.history_check: The map's OPEN list has 'Warn on unmarked input' (inferred; REVIEW L15 exists only in validate). New here: a real unmarked BAM sits in spike's own data directory, and its duplicate share is measured at 13.1%. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Per-event RNG streams, so an event's reads do not depend on which events came before it
ideas.problem: One StdRng seeded from --seed runs through every event in input order (main.rs:614, 795, 807-822). Adding, removing or reordering an event changes the reads and realised fractions of every event after it. A gene panel's result for one variant therefore depends on the rest of the panel. It also blocks running independent events in parallel.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (scratchpad robust/order): event B = del:chr20:44999900-45000100 on HG002 35x, seed 42. Alone it gives SIM_ALT_FRAGS=34. After A (del:chr19:11100000-11102000), the same B gives SIM_ALT_FRAGS=42, and only 11 of B-alone's 277 SPIKE_ R1 sequences appear in the A+B run. DOCUMENTED: commit bccc43a 'K7 FAIL by rule (2 allele_freq flips from the reordered random stream)'. The documented serial floor is a 3 Mb DUP at 26.5 s even at 16 threads (README.md:1354-1361).
ideas.proposal: Derive each event's StdRng from hash(seed, canonical event spec, occurrence index). The random insertion sequence (build_haplotype) and tiling draw from it, and so does origin's removal draw, per event or keyed per family. Name SPIKE reads by the event's stream id, or compare by sequence only.
ideas.simplest_version: Seed one StdRng per event from (seed, event index in sorted canonical-spec order) and use it for everything that event draws. origin keeps its single draw for now.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
On HG002 35x, runs of [A,B], [B] and [B,A] must give event B identical SPIKE read sequences and qualities and identical truth INFO.
Across 20 seeds on 10 real HG002 events, the distributions of SIM_ALT_FRAGS and of realised VAF in the merged BAM must match master's (KS p > 0.05), which kills a biased stream derivation.
Output must remain the same at --threads 1 and 16.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done for the dependence itself (two runs). Before building, list every rng call site (grep rng in main.rs, simulate.rs, synth.rs, origin.rs) to confirm each draw belongs to exactly one event. The global origin draw is the known exception.
ideas.impact: A hospital panel run equals its one-at-a-time runs, so adding an LDLR variant no longer perturbs the DMD one. It also opens the way to parallel independent events and parallel tiling inside a big event.
ideas.risks: It changes every run's bytes once. The owner's rule keeps --seed output byte-identical when speeding up, so this needs an explicit word and a K7-style seed-spread gate. Two identical specs need distinct occurrence indices.
ideas.history_check: In the map's OPEN list ('Per-event RNG streams'). Threads step 2 (per-chunk RNG) was considered and not chosen (memory threads-step1.md). It was never refuted. New: a measured order dependence on real HG002 events.

ideas.title: N-aware tiling: never place spike fragments over reference gaps or past contig ends
ideas.problem: Fragment starts are uniform over every reference-overlapping start of the haplotype (simulate.rs:926-946). A reference N emits N at Q2 (synth.rs:189-202), and bases past a contig end are N-padded (synth.rs:51, test at synth.rs:1561). So an event within 2 kb of a gap or contig end tiles whole reads of N at full depth, where real data has no reads at all. Count and depth are scaled as if those starts were real.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (scratchpad robust/ngap): del:chr20:61000-61400 sits beside the chr20 p-arm gap, whose N run ends at 60,000. Without --allow-resistant it is refused by RF8 (SIM_RESIST 0.814). With it: 644 SPIKE_ reads, 123 entirely N (19%) and 149 at least half N. SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 76.88 warns, but the reads are still written. DOCUMENTED: real NovaSeq N rate is 2-3e-5 per base, with Q2 only on N (the map, K2b FASTQs).
ideas.proposal: Treat reference N runs (for example, 10 bp or longer) and positions past a contig end as non-placeable, the way novel_only sequence is. Exclude fragment starts whose fragment overlaps them, and drop those starts from the count.
ideas.simplest_version: In sample_ref_overlapping_start, reject a start whose fragment covers 10 or more consecutive reference N, and subtract those starts in compute_tiling_count.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the chr20:61000-61400 event, all-N SPIKE reads must go from 123 to 0, and spike's per-base N rate must come within 2x of the real 2-3e-5. On the 15 identity sets (no N in their footprints) and a near-contig-end unit fixture, outputs must be byte-identical to master. A fix that also drops starts at isolated single Ns would move bytes there and fail.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done (one run). Before building, scan GRCh38 for N runs within 2 kb of the exons in the user's clinical gene list (bedtools window on the .fai gaps). If there are none, rank this as hygiene only.
ideas.impact: No impossible all-N reads in the spiked FASTQ, and correct counts for events near gaps or contig ends. The impact is modest, because RF8 already refuses most of these sites.
ideas.risks: Changes counts near gaps, which is intended. The N-run threshold must not remove starts at isolated IUPAC/N bases inside real sequence.
ideas.history_check: CR5 (insertion fragments drawn only from reference-overlapping starts) is the same mechanism, applied to novel sequence and never to N. Contig-end coordinate handling is unit-tested (haplotype.rs:1413-1500), but read placement over N is not. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Code health: one EventOutcome per event, plus an end-of-run audit of the output name contract
ideas.evidence: MEASURED on the two-event HG002 run (scratchpad robust/order/AB): 6,396 R1 and 6,396 R2 names, identical sets; 0 duplicate names; fastq_removed ∩ written = 0; fastq_removed ⊄ replaced = 0; replaced minus written minus fastq_removed = 0. The invariants hold today, so an audit would not false-alarm. Line counts from wc -l and the location of #[cfg(test)] at main.rs:2938. DOCUMENTED: the independent review lists missing EventPlan/EventResult and run manifest as unaddressed debt (docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:131-142). RF1 was an index-alignment defect in exactly these slices.
ideas.proposal: Replace the parallel vectors with one EventOutcome struct (adjusted_vaf, resistant, depth_fold, alt_frags, kept, suppressed, chimeric). Separately, add an audit pass just before outputs are published that checks the name contract and records the result in run.json. On a violation, the outputs are not published.
ideas.simplest_version: Only the audit: four set checks over names spike already holds in memory, bail! before publishing on a violation.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done: the four invariants checked by awk/comm on a real run. Next, an hour: run the same awk check over the outputs of the 15 identity sets and the transplant runs, to confirm none violates them today.
ideas.impact: Catches silent output corruption in the FASTQ route at write time, not 42 minutes into fastq.sh or after a raredisease run. It also removes the class of index-misalignment bugs RF1 belonged to.
ideas.risks: A large diff in main.rs, so keep the refactor and the audit in separate commits, each byte-identical. The audit costs a little memory for name sets on huge events.
ideas.history_check: The independent review (2026-10-04) named this architecture debt and it is unaddressed. RF1 fixed the symptom with release asserts. Nothing here was refuted.

ideas.title: Background-integrity yardstick: measure what each spike does to the sample's own variants in its footprint, first in the reads and then in the calls
ideas.problem: Every realism yardstick spike has looks only at the planted allele: transplant J/E1/A/E, the K quality tests and validate's rows. None of them asks whether the sample's own variants in the remade event ±2 kb survive. A real carrier's footprint keeps its background. spike remakes the event copy from a template that carries SNPs only (CR3), so the sample's indels and SVs there are lost. Until now that harm rested on one probe (AF 1.0 -> 0.360) and on the T7 count of exposed footprints. Its size on real transplanted events was never measured.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED here, read-only, on round 2b's existing forward normal-arm outputs (session scratchpad transplant2/full/forward/normal/run0-2: sim.bam plus replaced_reads.txt, made by the 2026-09-28 master binary). SampleCopies is still SNP-only in current master (src/loh.rs:33-41 at 4a5672d), so the effect should carry over. Reads counted: MAPQ>=20, non-duplicate, spanning; recipient = hospital HG002 BAM; after = recipient minus replaced plus sim.bam; truth = HG002 v4.2.1. Results:
- 297 of 754 forward footprints hold at least one HG002 non-SNP within ±2 kb (153 het, 145 hom, 476 records).
- 198 hom indels: median read AF 0.934 before, 0.479 after. 187 of 198 sit below 0.75 after, against 28 before.
- 233 het indels: median 0.448 before, 0.240 after. 109 dropped by more than 0.2.
- 214 of 752 events (28.5%) damage at least one background indel.
- Control, same footprints and code: background SNPs are preserved. Hom 1.000 -> 1.000 with 0 of 198 changed; het 0.500 -> 0.484 with 8 of 201 changed by more than 0.2.
Scripts: /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/valid_lens/cr3_bg.py and snp_bg.py. DOCUMENTED: the CR3 probe (hom 2 bp DEL 1.0 -> 0.360) and T7 (38/40 footprints exposed) in docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md. The transplant metrics read only the planted site (scripts/transplant/small_evidence.py:1-30).
ideas.proposal:
Make background integrity a standing metric in every realism round and in the hospital acceptance run.
- For each event, take the footprint (event ±2 kb plus a 500 bp margin) and leave out the planted allele.
- Measure (a) read AF for every background benchmark variant before and after, as cr3_bg.py does, and (b) the hospital caller's calls (DeepVariant in region mode) on the recipient before and after.
- Report per footprint and per variant class (SNP, indel, SV): GT changes, lost calls and new calls.
- A sham run (realigned unchanged reads, as the transplant already makes) gives the null.
The metric then serves as the locked falsifier for any CR3 work: P1 minimal edit, P1b in-place base edit, or a per-copy variant list from a phased VCF. It also settles the pending T7 decision with a number rather than a warning.
ideas.simplest_version: Add the read-AF comparison (cr3_bg.py logic) as a seen-not-judged column of every transplant run. It needs no caller and costs about 10 s per 750 events.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Run DeepVariant on the 137 forward footprints whose hom background indel fell below AF 0.75, before and after spiking.
- The idea dies at caller level if DV still calls 1/1 at 95% or more of those indels after spiking, and the sham shows the same change rate. Read-level damage would then not reach the calls, and the metric is not worth a standing slot.
- The metric must also fail a broken version: a mutant that empties the SNP carry-over (SampleCopies maps empty) must show background-SNP GT changes in roughly half of the footprints that hold a het SNP. Today's SNP control shows 8 of 201.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Pick 50 of the 137 hom-indel footprints. For each, build a small BAM: recipient reads over ±5 kb, minus that run's replaced names, plus sim.bam's reads over the same span. Build the same slice from the unspiked recipient as a sham. Run DeepVariant 1.9.0 (cached at ~/.singularity/cache/docker.io-google-deepvariant-1.9.0.img) with --regions on both. The sham slice's calls must match raredisease's genome-wide DV calls at those positions. Then count GT flips after spiking. About 1 h, and no spike run is needed.
ideas.impact: Hospital demo: a spiked LDLR variant would turn nearby common hom indels into hets and drop het ones from the event copy. raredisease would then report spurious calls and GT errors next to every planted variant, and a GIAB-based benchmark would score them as FP/FN. The metric gives CR3 option A and P1 a locked real-data falsifier, and makes 'indistinguishable from real' cover the whole footprint rather than one base.
ideas.risks:
- The carrier detector is crude (same-length indel within 25 bp). It under-counts in repeats: hom 'before' AF is 0.934, not 1.0.
- The round 2b binary predates the read-length fix and quality v2. The CR3 code is unchanged, but the numbers must be re-measured on 4a5672d.
- DV version: 1.9.0 is cached, while the hospital runs 1.6.1.
- Calling DV on footprint slices must be shown equal to whole-BAM calling by the sham.
- Excluding the planted allele by distance (60 bp) may let some interaction through.
ideas.history_check: CR3 is documented with one probe (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR3). T7 refuted a blanket footprint WARNING because it fires on 38 of 40 footprints. This proposal is a measurement yardstick, not a warning, so T7 does not cover it. The map's 'measure first, before CR3 option A' proposed 20 SNV sites. This session measured it at read level on 752 real transplant events. Nothing similar was built or refuted.

ideas.title: Caller-equivalence round for SNVs, indels and short DUPs: DeepVariant on the transplant's real carriers against the spiked recipients, judged against real-vs-real at shared sites
ideas.problem: No measurement asks whether the hospital's small-variant caller calls a spiked variant as it calls the real one: same call, GT, GQ/QUAL and AD-VAF. The transplant judges read counts only. Its plans explicitly leave out base quality, MAPQ, strand and callers (2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:115, round2.md:179-185). DeepVariant's pileup images include exactly those features. RF15 (short INS cleaner than real) has never been checked at the caller level.
ideas.proposal:
Reuse round 2b's event draw: forward, reverse and shared sets, the B1/B2 arms and the sham.
- Re-spike with current master (4a5672d) using the hospital aligner command.
- Call DeepVariant in region mode, pinned to the hospital's 1.6.1 image, at each site ±1 kb on: the donor's real BAM, the spiked recipient (recipient minus replaced plus sim.bam), the sham, and both shared samples.
- Per site, record: call made (normalized, representation-aware matching), GT, GQ, QUAL and AD-VAF.
- Judge per group and direction:
  - call-status discordance, fake vs real, against the same discordance real vs real at shared sites;
  - paired GQ/VAF differences against shared-site differences with the round-3 bootstrap rule.
- Controls: B1 must shift GT or GQ, B2 must lose the call at the true position, and the sham must add 0 calls.
- Stratify by homopolymer/TR context.
ideas.simplest_version: Forward INS20-49 and SNV only (200 events), DeepVariant 1.9.0, current spike. Compare the call rate and GQ distribution of the fake calls with the donor's existing raredisease calls.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Fail per group:
- If spiked INS20-49 is called het at a rate outside the real-vs-real band, spike's insertions are not caller-equivalent there. Example: 95/100 or more fake against 78/100 real, Fisher p<0.01 and a gap above the shared-site discordance of 6/100. The same rule applies to every group.
- If fake GQ sits systematically above real (paired median ΔGQ beyond the shared-site 3-6), the group fails.
The harness itself must break on broken controls: B1 (VAF 0.25) must change DV's GT or GQ distribution. If B1 cannot be told from the normal arm by any DV metric, the round has no power, and the round is dropped rather than read as a pass.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b:
1) Run DeepVariant 1.9.0 in region mode on the donor HG001 BAM at the 100 forward INS20-49 sites and compare call status with raredisease's 1.6.1 calls. 95% or more must agree, otherwise the 1.6.1 image must be pulled. About 20 min.
2) Run it on round 2b's existing fake slices at the same sites (old binary) for a seen-not-judged first look at whether fake INS20-49 is called more often than 78/100.
ideas.impact: This answers the hospital's actual question for SNVs and indels, the variant types the demo most needs and that are untested at the hospital. It tests RF15 at the level that matters, and it gives the GQ/QUAL distributions that drive raredisease rank scores. Region-mode DV over about 10 Mb per BAM is minutes of CPU (inferred from DV's whole-genome cost).
ideas.risks:
- DV version mismatch (1.9.0 cached vs 1.6.1 at the hospital).
- GLnexus re-genotyping may shift GQ, so run GLnexus too or compare at gVCF level.
- DUP representation: exact-POS lookup found only 24/54 real DUP calls. Part of that is representation, so matching must be normalized (bcftools norm, or vcfeval-style).
- Slicing for DV must be checked by the sham.
- 100 events per group detect only call-rate differences of about 15-20 points (inferred).
ideas.history_check: Listed as the biggest OPPORTUNITY in the map and in memory validation-plan.md ('which callers' is still open with the user). Never run. Every transplant plan scopes callers out. Not refuted. New here: the real-side call rates and the shared-site discordance yardstick, measured from existing raredisease outputs.

ideas.title: Manta equivalence on round 1b DELs, stratified by Alu context: the real-carrier yardstick for 'Manta misses spiked LDLR Alu-Alu deletions'
ideas.problem: Manta missed the spiked ClinVar 4845403 (a 2.1 kb Alu-Alu DEL in LDLR) even on the full BAM. Nobody knows whether a real carrier would also be missed, so that result cannot be read as a spike defect or as a caller fact. No SV caller has been run on spiked vs real carriers of the same events. Round 1b's verdicts are read counts only, and LDLR's breakpoints often sit in Alus.
ideas.proposal:
For each round-1b run, build one whole-genome spiked BAM with current master: 3 runs per direction, plus the B1/B2 arms and the sham. Events sit 7 kb apart, so one BAM carries about 280 events.
- Run Manta 1.6.0 with --callRegions over all event windows, on the spiked recipient and on the donor's real BAM, in the same mode.
- Compare call status, GT, breakpoint offset, and PR/SR support.
- Judge per size bin × Alu stratum against shared-site real-vs-real discordance.
- Then add TIDDIT and CNVnator, whole-genome on one BAM per arm, with a repeated-run noise floor (TIDDIT differs by about 2,400 calls between runs).
This puts the LDLR question on a measured footing: spiked Alu-Alu DELs should be called at about the real 42%, not at about 0% or 90%.
ideas.simplest_version: Forward run0 only: 276 events, whose old sim.bam is already in the scratchpad (transplant/full/forward/normal/run0). Build one merged BAM, run Manta callRegions on donor HG001 and on spiked HG002, and tabulate the call rate per bin × Alu stratum against the numbers above.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Build the run0 merged BAM with samtools view -@16 -N/-U and samtools merge (both inputs are sorted, so no re-sort), then run Manta --callRegions over the 276 windows on that BAM and on the HG001 BAM. Roughly 3-4 h of wall time, mostly the BAM build. It also times a faster merge route.
ideas.impact: This answers the open LDLR question (would a real Alu-Alu carrier be missed?) with GIAB real carriers, and tells the hospital which spiked SV classes behave like real ones in Manta, the raredisease caller with the best breakpoint resolution. It also prepares the full SVDB-merged comparison.
ideas.risks:
- The BAM build is slow: merge.sh took 1 h 42 min, and the faster route is untested.
- --callRegions can differ from a full run at inter-chromosomal BNDs (not relevant for DELs).
- Shared-site n is 78-100 per bin, so only large differences can be seen.
- RF8-refused events (13-17 per 300) drop out and must be reported.
- Using the old sim.bam for the gate predates quality v2.
ideas.history_check: Slices were refuted for Manta (narrowly, background calls) and for CNVnator (cnv_validation 4bd707b). This design uses whole-genome BAMs plus region calling on both arms, which slice-safety measured as identical except at inter-chromosomal BNDs. Caller equivalence is an open OPPORTUNITY in the map and was never run. New here: real call rates, shared discordance and the Alu stratification.

ideas.title: A name-free, same-locus 'can you tell' classifier, tracked per release, whose feature ranking finds the next realism gap
ideas.problem: spike's read realism is checked one hand-picked statistic at a time (SD, crash share, clip share). Each new gap (last-cycle drop, Q2 not on N, the substitution spectrum) was found by someone thinking to look. A joint discriminator would give one number per release and list what gives spike's reads away. The idea was concept test 3 in the validation plan, but was never built.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED here.
(1) On K2b held-out 35x pairs (/home/parlar_ai/quality-speed-run/evidence/k2b; spike reads made on the same templates as the real ones): a gradient-boosted classifier on 14 quality-string features, with pair-grouped 5-fold CV and 20,000 reads per class, gives AUC 0.572 (R1) and 0.569 (R2).
- The null controls give 0.499 (real vs real) and 0.500 (spike seed 22 vs seed 23).
- No single feature exceeds 0.519. The top one is the last-cycle quality (real 34.57, spike 35.28), which is the missing last-cycle drop the map found by hand.
(2) On the 14 hospital K2 events (session scratchpad inspect/ and qtq2/k2v2/): SPIKE_ reads against real reads over the same footprints, with event-grouped CV:
- pre-v2 binary (bdd568a): AUC 0.958 (6,266 spike reads, 85,510 real);
- v2: AUC 0.582 (6,254 spike reads).
The test detects the known big gap and follows its fix. Scripts: scratchpad valid_lens/disc.py and disc_k2.py.
ideas.simplest_version: The existing quality-only script, run on the K2b FASTQs and the K2 event folders for every new binary: two AUCs and a feature ranking, under 1 min of wall time each.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Two checks:
(a) Sensitivity: an old binary with a known large gap must score clearly higher than v2. This already passed here, at 0.958 against 0.582.
(b) Usefulness as a gap-finder: a branch that fixes the top-ranked feature (for example, a dedicated last-cycle position in the quality key and end_bin) must lower AUC on held-out data. If AUC does not move, the ranking does not point to real gaps.
If the aligned-feature AUC for v2 is 0.5 ± 0.01 with nulls at 0.5, the classifier has nothing left to find at that feature set. Then keep it only as a regression guard.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Add 10 aligned features (NM, MD mismatch cycles, clip ends, MAPQ, TLEN) to disc_k2.py on the K2 event folders (spiked.bam/real.bam already exist), and read the top 3 features. About 1 h, no spike run.
ideas.impact: One realism number per release that catches gaps nobody has thought to measure (the K tests only check what they were written for). Its feature ranking points future quality/error work at the biggest giveaway, and it guards against regressions when the model changes.
ideas.risks:
- A quality-feature AUC is not caller relevance. A gap the classifier finds may not matter to DeepVariant or Manta, so pair it with the caller round.
- With rich enough features any simulator becomes separable, so AUC thresholds need the null and an old-binary anchor.
- Composition effects (K6) can masquerade as model gaps unless templates are matched.
- The hospital comparison is footprint-matched, not template-matched.
ideas.history_check: Concept test 3 in memory validation-plan.md ('read-level can you tell'), never built; listed as an OPPORTUNITY in the map. Nothing refuted. New here: a working positive control (0.958 against 0.582) and the null at 0.50.

ideas.title: Re-run the locked realism yardsticks on current master, then pin them as a pre-merge realism suite
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED: git ls-files shows no .github, CI config, Makefile or rust-toolchain. The transplant scripts were last touched in c87ab53/e58738d (2026-09-28).
DOCUMENTED:
- Round 3 ran on round 2b's reads (2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:167).
- The read-length K2 re-run flipped one verdict, and a later look showed that was the seed draw (memory read-length-fix.md, 3684f74). Single-seed verdicts are fragile.
- Quality v2's K7 was 'no validate regressions' only (memory quality-model-run.md).
- Round 1b's full run took 26 min (12:13-12:39); round 3 scoring took 3 min 43 s.
MEASURED here: the discriminator (0.958 pre-v2, 0.582 v2) and the background-integrity metric are both cheap enough to add to such a suite.
ideas.simplest_version: Re-spike round 2b's forward and reverse events with 4a5672d and score them with round3.py unchanged. Report the 16 verdicts beside the 2026-09-28 ones.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Run the suite on three historical binaries: the 2026-09-28 master (148 bp, Markov chain), 3684f74 and 4a5672d.
- If no metric separates the 148 bp/Markov binary from 4a5672d beyond the 2-seed spread, the suite is blind to known large gaps and is not worth its 1-2 h per merge.
- If 4a5672d turns any group from supported to refuted beyond the seed spread, the suite has found a real regression that current gates missed.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Re-spike round 2b's SNV, DEL5-19 and INS5-19 events, both directions, with 4a5672d, then run round3.py. This covers the 5 currently supported group×direction cells. About 40-60 min.
ideas.impact: It protects the realism claims the hospital demo will rest on, and makes 'keep the transplant verdicts' an executable falsifier for P1, CR3 and quality work. It also catches silent regressions from model changes such as quality v2.
ideas.risks:
- 1-2 h of compute per merge clashes with the owner's 'speed matters'. Run it on request or nightly, not on every commit.
- Groups at their power limit (11 of 16 are inconclusive) will flicker, so gate only on clear flips.
- Event lists drawn from GIAB benchmark regions don't cover hard clinical regions.
- Each run needs disk (round 2b is 3.6 GB).
ideas.history_check: Byte-identity gates (threads step 1, quality-speed B1) and K7 exist, but they guard output identity or validate rows, not realism against real carriers. No realism regression suite exists. Nothing refuted. The read-length look (3684f74) shows why 2 seeds are needed.

ideas.title: Graded broken-control ladder and power table: give every 'supported' verdict a minimum detectable dose and offset
ideas.problem: The only broken controls are B1 (VAF 0.25, a half dose) and B2 (200 bp off). A 'supported' verdict therefore only says spike is not as wrong as a half dose, and in some metrics not even that. Nobody knows the smallest error each metric can see, so the verdicts cannot be read quantitatively or used to size future rounds. Shared-site n (33 DUPs) caps several verdicts.
ideas.evidence:
DOCUMENTED:
- Round 3: B1 is only 'unsure' on E for DEL1-4, DEL20-49, INS1-4 and INS20-49, and on A of DEL20-49 (rho 1.89-2.72). The rule cannot tell half dose from full there (2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:191-201).
- Round 1b 50-299 bp: B1 failed by only 0.001 (memory validation-plan.md).
- DUP50-299 reverse: rho 2.81 with an interval of 1.50-5.06 on 33 shared DUPs.
- The read-length K2 flip was a seed draw (3684f74).
MEASURED here from round3/run/evidence3.tsv: the across-site variance divided by per-site counting noise is:
- 2.51-4.01 for INS20-49 A;
- 3.36-5.85 for DUP J;
- 0.78-1.28 for SNV and DEL5-19 A.
Site effects therefore dominate the INS20-49 and DUP metrics, and only paired same-site designs have power there. A second whole-genome HG002 library exists (/home/parlar_ai/dev/sv_caller/data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.novaseq.pcr-free.35x.bwamem2.dedup.grch38_no_alt.bam). It could serve as a cross-library real-vs-real yardstick at every HG002 site, not just the 33 shared DUPs.
ideas.proposal:
Add control arms at VAF 0.45, 0.40 and 0.35 (0.25 exists) and at offsets of 10, 25, 50 and 200 bp, each with 2 seeds.
- For each metric × group, estimate the dose and offset at which the locked rule fails at least 80% of bootstrap draws: the minimum detectable effect (MDE).
- Publish an MDE table and report each verdict as 'supported within ±X% dose / Y bp'.
- Drop metrics that cannot see a half dose (E in four groups).
- Use the table to size n per group, for example how many shared DUPs are needed for an interval inside 2.25.
- Report a cross-library HG002-vs-HG002 c alongside. It is looser, since it includes library differences, so use it only to widen n_c, never to replace the same-run yardstick.
ideas.simplest_version: One extra arm at VAF 0.40 for the 5 currently supported cells (SNV both directions, DEL5-19 both, INS5-19 reverse), scored with round3.py unchanged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Two outcomes:
- If the VAF 0.40 arm already fails every counted metric in every supported cell (rho's 5th percentile above 2.25), the current tests resolve a 20% dose error, the ladder adds little, and the work stops there.
- If VAF 0.40 passes in supported cells, 'supported' only bounds the dose error to between 20% and 50%. That is a documented limit on every current verdict, and the ladder must be run.
A wrong analysis must also fail: the ladder's fail probability must rise with the dose error. A non-monotone curve means the rule is noise-dominated.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Spike round 2b's forward SNV and DEL5-19 events (200) at VAF 0.40 with current master, then score with round3.py. About 30-45 min.
ideas.impact: It makes every realism verdict quantitative ('spike's SNVs are indistinguishable from real ones within ±X% evidence'), which the hospital can quote. It also lets future rounds be sized rather than guessed, and stops low-power metrics from producing perpetual inconclusives.
ideas.risks:
- Compute per arm.
- The MDE depends on the binary, so recompute it when the realism suite runs.
- A dose ladder misses shape errors such as quality or strand, which the discriminator and caller rounds cover.
- A cross-library yardstick, if misused, would make passing easier.
ideas.history_check: B1 and B2 exist since round 1 but were never graded. R_c < 1 is still unexplained (round3 plan :222-232), and the across-site spread measured here shows why rho intervals are wide where site effects dominate. Nothing refuted. Astra's 2x2 design (memory) needs complete local haplotypes and is separate.

ideas.title: Whole-sample acceptance test for the hospital route: spiked against unspiked raredisease outputs, with a FASTQ-route sham that sets the pipeline's own noise floor
ideas.problem: The owner's product is raredisease run on a full spiked FASTQ. Nothing measures what else changes genome-wide, and the pipeline is not reproducible to the call, so a raw diff cannot be read. TIDDIT runs differ from each other by thousands of calls. The FASTQ route also removes originals from the middle of the file and appends SPIKE_ reads at the end. That shifts bwa-mem2's -K 100000000 batch boundaries, which carry per-batch insert-size estimates, for every later read. Some alignments far from any event could therefore change (inferred, unmeasured). fastp and MarkDuplicates may also remove planted evidence, and nothing checks the per-event survival of SPIKE_ fragments in the final BAM.
ideas.evidence:
DOCUMENTED (memory sv-caller-slices.md):
- Two TIDDIT FULL runs differ by about 2,400 calls genome-wide; Manta and CNVnator FULL runs are deterministic.
- raredisease aligns with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000 (memory validation-plan.md).
MEASURED here, fastp with the hospital flags (--detect_adapter_for_pe --length_required 40 --correction) on the K2b 35x sets:
- reads dropped: real 0.77% (964/125,364), spike 0.88% (seed 21) and 0.80% (seed 22);
- too-many-N: real 32, spike 0.
The differences are small.
MEASURED: the hospital's unspiked raredisease outputs exist for both GIAB samples (cnv_validation/from_rv/.../raredisease_results/call_snv, call_sv, repeat_expansions). validate never reads SIM_ALT_FRAGS (src/validate.rs:83-101).
DOCUMENTED: F2 checked only the SPIKE_ records (1,296/1,296 identical to sim.bam), not the rest of the genome.
ideas.simplest_version: An order-sensitivity check, run here: align a 2M-pair hospital-like FASTQ subset with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000 twice, once in original order and once with 1% of pairs moved to the end. Count records whose position, MAPQ or flags change. If none change, the sham is needed only for TIDDIT.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
If sham-vs-baseline differences are zero for DeepVariant and Manta, and spiked-vs-baseline differences outside the footprints are zero too, the sham adds nothing for those callers; keep it only for TIDDIT/gCNV.
The protocol must fail a broken build: a spiked FASTQ made with an empty removal list (originals left in beside their replacements) must show footprint discordance and old-allele calls above the sham floor. If it does not, the protocol cannot see real mistakes.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Run the bwa-mem2 order-sensitivity check above on the K2b FASTQs or a chr20 slice of the hospital reads. Loading the index dominates; about 1 h.
ideas.impact: Gives each demo sample a documented, defensible statement: what changed in the raredisease output, and that nothing else changed beyond the pipeline's own run-to-run noise. This is the evidence a clinical team needs before using spiked data for training or proficiency testing.
ideas.risks:
- It needs hospital compute and the user's access: about 3 full raredisease runs per sample.
- GLnexus and rank-score steps add their own variation.
- The sham must mimic the spike's removal pattern (clustered at events, not random) to be a fair floor.
- It must use GIAB/demo data only, never patient data.
ideas.history_check: F2 measured alignment identity of the SPIKE_ records only. The FASTQ route has never been run on the real raw FASTQ (memories full-fastq.md and hospital-demo-plan.md). A second fastp pass on spike's reads is listed as unmeasured; this session's K2b numbers suggest it is small. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Benchmark-ready composite truth: the background benchmark plus the planted events, with footprint stratification BEDs, so hap.py, vcfeval or truvari can score the whole spiked sample
ideas.problem: truth.vcf holds only the planted events. It is uncompressed, its sample column is 'SAMPLE', and its GT comes from VAF; no regions BED is written. On a GIAB background, which is what the hospital will use, the natural benchmark is the GIAB truth plus the planted variants. But spike changes the background's non-SNPs in many footprints, so a naive 'GIAB + planted' truth scores spurious FN/GT errors around every event. There is also no stratification that separates planted / footprint / untouched results, and every harness rebuilds the truth by hand.
ideas.evidence:
MEASURED here (first idea): 214 of 752 transplant events change at least one background indel's read AF (hom median 0.934 -> 0.479).
DOCUMENTED / code read:
- truth.rs:115-117 writes ##fileformat and ##source=spike only.
- truth.rs:205 names the sample column SAMPLE.
- truth.rs:468-474 sets GT from VAF.
- No normalization code was found in truth.rs, vcf_input.rs or exon.rs (grep).
- validate_pipeline.sh:944-959 adds contig headers, bgzips and tabix-indexes by hand before Truvari.
MEASURED: truvari 5.4 and 4.2.2 exist in cnv_validation's pixi environments; hap.py and rtg are not installed (command -v).
ideas.simplest_version: A 30-line bash script: bedtools subtract plus bcftools view -T ^footprints, then bcftools concat and norm, then tabix.
ideas.falsifying_measurement:
Score the unspiked HG002 DeepVariant calls against GIAB as a baseline, and the spiked sample's calls against the composite truth.
- In the 'rest' stratum, TP/FP/FN must equal the baseline to within the sham noise floor. A difference means either spike changed something outside the footprints or the composer is wrong.
- A broken composer that keeps background records inside the footprints must show the footprint FN/GT errors the first idea predicts, about 0.48 AF at former hom indels.
- If the composite and naive truths give the same footprint scores, the footprint handling is unnecessary. Keep only bgzip, name and normalize.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Compose the truth for round 2b forward run0 (700 events) from its truth.vcf and events.bed with HG002 v4.2.1. Run vcfeval (rtg container) or bcftools isec against DeepVariant calls on 50 footprints from the first idea's gate. About 2 h.
ideas.impact: The hospital and other users get a standard GA4GH-style benchmark of the whole spiked sample: recall of the planted events, and proof that precision elsewhere is unchanged. Background damage becomes visible as its own stratum instead of hiding in genome-wide numbers, and the hand-made truth fix-ups in harnesses go away.
ideas.risks:
- Removing the footprints hides CR3 rather than fixing it, so the removed fraction must always be reported.
- hap.py and vcfeval need containers.
- GIAB confident regions exclude parts of clinical genes such as LDLR's Alus, so a planted event may fall outside the bed and must be scored separately.
- Normalizing planted indels may move their POS against SIM_* bookkeeping.
ideas.history_check: The map lists 'truth VCF for benchmarking' as OPEN (bgzip/tbi, SIM_SRC_ID, SM, a benchmark-regions BED, left-normalization). Composing with the background truth and stratifying footprints is new. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Carry each site's own strand-specific systematic errors into the synthetic reads
ideas.problem: spike makes every synthetic error independent of where the read sits on the genome: the error draw depends only on quality, read state and cycles left (src/synth.rs:208-234; src/quality.rs:894-921), and no reference position enters it. Real Illumina errors recur at the same base, on the same strand, with the same wrong base (sequence-specific errors), which callers see as candidate alleles and strand bias. Inside a remade footprint (+-2 kb; half the pairs at het, all at hom) that structure disappears. block_errors also masks any position with >=5 reads and >=10% differing (quality.rs:963), removing the strongest recurrent sites from learning.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R1) on K2b sets: 62,682 held-out pairs of the HG002 35x PCR-free BAM over 20 index-placed blocks, real vs spike remade at the same 5' positions (scratchpad qtq2/k2b/{real,spike21,spike22}.bam), Q100 v5.0q small-variant BED, Q100 records masked +-5 bp, BQ>=10, MAPQ>=20, reads without indels (scratchpad phys/recur.py -> recur_35x.out). Sites with >=3 reads on one strand showing the same wrong base: real 181, spike 2 and 2; only 9 of the 181 show it on the other strand. Caller-style candidates (>=2 alt reads, AF>=0.12): real 453 (500/Mb; 366 one-strand), spike 85 and 74 (93 and 81/Mb). Share of mismatches at a site with >=2 same-strand same-alt reads (phys/errproc.py): real 6.27%, spike 1.35%; hospital HG002 30x same blocks 13.47%, 543 sites with >=3. Site effect (phys/splithalf.py, split_both.out, name-hash halves of the full 35x BAM): when half A has >=3 same-strand same-alt reads, half B has >=2 with P=0.372 (n=191) vs base 0.000228, >=1 with P=0.613 vs 0.0081; a single error in A raises B's chance of one to 0.044 vs 0.0081 (n=41,641); the other strand repeats only 3.7%. Hospital: P(B>=1|A==1)=0.0169 vs 0.00057 (n=2,729). Not duplicates: 690 of 757 sites with >=3 reads have all-distinct 5' ends (phys/dupcheck.py). Runs explain part: 48/181 (26.5%) have a run >=7 within 15 bp upstream (background 2.0%); 111 (61%) have no run >=5, so v2's run bin cannot place them.
ideas.proposal: Learn a per-site, per-strand error map from the event's own donor pool (pairs with CIGARs already extracted; ReadPair.align used by class_mix at quality.rs:816). For each reference position, strand and alt base, count alt reads and strand depth; shrink toward the sample's iid rate by empirical Bayes calibrated on the split-half curve; keep only the excess over what the v2 error table predicts. When a synthetic read reads a reference-origin template base at that position on that strand, emit the site's alt with the excess probability. Positions come from template_at's ref_start/orientation (flank reads) and hap_to_ref inside reference segments (haplotype reads). Novel sequence and bases within ~10 bp downstream of an edit fall back to the iid model.
ideas.simplest_version: Only sites with >=2 same-strand same-alt pool reads and 0 on the other strand; rate = (k_alt - expected_iid)/n_strand, floored at 0, capped at 0.5; flank reads only (reference-origin segments); no shrinkage beyond the subtraction; haplotype and novel segments unchanged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b design: learn the map from even-hash pool reads, generate the odd-hash pairs at their own positions, align with bwa-mem2, score with recur.py inside the Q100 bench BED with Q100 masked. Sites with >=3 same-strand same-alt reads must reach 0.7-1.3x real (181 -> 127-235); candidates (>=2 alt, AF>=0.12) 0.7-1.3x real (453); >=40% of spike's >=3-read sites must coincide (position, strand, alt) with a real site having >=2. Broken versions must fail: master (2 sites, 74-85 candidates); map at shuffled positions (overlap near 0.0002 base rate); no subtraction/shrinkage (candidates >1.3x); strands swapped (overlap near 0). If even a perfect copy of the pool's counts cannot beat 20% overlap with held-out real reads at pool depth, the idea is dead.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Offline injection, no Rust: from the 35x BAM reads in the 20 blocks NOT in real.bam (training half) compute the site map; inject the site alt into spike21.bam's aligned reads at the learned excess rate by position and strand; re-run recur.py for sites, candidates and overlap with real.bam. About 2-3 h with the existing phys/ scripts.
ideas.impact: DeepVariant is raredisease's SNV caller at the hospital (pipeline_info: variant_caller deepvariant); external knowledge (unverified here): its candidate generator needs 2 alt reads and AF>=0.12. Real data feeds it ~5x more error-driven candidates per Mb than spike's reads over the same DNA, so precision and strand-bias filtering inside every spiked window are tested on too-clean data. For low-VAF benchmarks (af<=0.05) site-specific noise sets the detection floor and iid errors overstate sensitivity. Covers the 61% of recurrent sites v2's run bin cannot reach.
ideas.risks: Pool holds ~15-17 reads per strand at 30-35x, so single-error sites are noisy; shrinkage must be calibrated on split halves or spike copies noise. Unlisted low-fraction variants and paralog mismapping would be copied (arguably realistic) but must not touch the planted allele: exclude the event's changed bases. Double counting with the iid table (learn it with the same site mask). Output bytes change (K7-style gate vs master's seed spread). Context changes downstream of an edit, where the map does not apply.
ideas.history_check: Never proposed or measured: grep finds no 'systematic error', 'site-specific' or 'recurrent error' in docs, src or the case file. Related to but distinct from the REFUTED/corrected copying of a donor pair's error positions (case file 2026-10-06; fix A de806dd quality-tails), which copied read-relative cycles onto another pair and failed on clip totals counting adapter and foreign tails. This keys errors to genomic site plus strand, with new split-half evidence. quality.rs:963 deliberately masks strong recurrent sites as 'the sample's variants'.

ideas.title: Per-mate error emission: the wrong base the sample calls (and N at Q2), learned in block_errors
ideas.problem: The error table has no mate dimension (quality.rs:253-264), so it averages R1 and R2. Every error picks one of the other three bases uniformly (synth.rs:719-728). block_errors sees the called base but stores only base != r (quality.rs:1014). Ns are left out of learning (quality.rs:1006), so a drawn Q2 (which real data uses only for N) emits a called base with the nominal error rate (0.63); spike never writes an N. The >=10% variant mask misses positions next to the sample's indels, so the table counts the sample's own variants there as high-quality errors.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R2; scratchpad phys/errproc.py -> errproc_35x.out, errproc_hosp.out; Q100 masked +-5 bp, reads without indels, sequencing orientation). Share of Q<15 errors going to the most common wrong base, R1/R2: 35x real 0.747/0.692; hospital HG002 30x same 20 blocks 0.837/0.819; spike21 same templates 0.337/0.338. Pattern is library-specific: 35x C->A 0.92, G->T 0.84; hospital A->C 0.92, T->C 0.91. Mismatch rate R1/R2 at Q25 (hospital Q24): 35x real 0.184%/0.425%, spike21 0.351%/0.402%, hospital 0.264%/0.389%; at Q37 (Q40): 35x real 0.0084%/0.0155%, spike21 0.0186%/0.0234%, hospital 0.0072%/0.0149%. spike's R1 errs 1.9-2.2x real R1. Q2 and N: 35x real 495 Q2 bases, all N (2.6e-5/base); hospital 782, all N; spike21 441 Q2 bases, none N, 0 N total. Of high-Q errors spike's rule counts on real reads, 11.3% (475/4,202) lie within 5 bp of a Q100 record (phys/learnmask.py).
ideas.proposal: In block_errors: key cells by mate (R1/R2); for each counted base also store the called base including N in an emission table P(called in {A,C,G,T,N} | true base, quality symbol, mate), backed off to (true, mate) then uniform; stop excluding N calls. In generate_from_template: after an error fires, draw the called base from the emission table instead of random_different_base; when the drawn quality symbol is one the sample emits as N >=99% of the time, emit N and skip the error draw (Q2 -> N). Widen the learning-time variant mask to +-5 bp around positions where pool reads show the sample's indels (I/D in CIGAR, or a shared clip boundary).
ideas.simplest_version: A 2 (mate) x 4 (true) x 4 (called) matrix for Q<15 and one for Q>=15; a mate bit on the existing full and mid error cells; Q2 -> N. About 40 lines in quality.rs and synth.rs.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b same-template sets scored with errproc.py: Q<15 top-alt share per mate and per true base within +-0.05 of real (35x 0.747/0.692); per-mate mismatch rate at Q25 and Q37 within +-20% of real (0.184/0.425% and 0.0084/0.0155%); 0 Q2 bases that are not N and an N rate within 2x of 2.6e-5. Repeat on the hospital 20-block sample (0.837/0.819; Q24 0.264/0.389%). Broken versions: mates swapped (R1/R2 ratio inverts), matrix transposed (spectrum fails), master (0.34 and R1 at 1.9x) must all fail.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Learnability: compute the matrix on even- and odd-numbered blocks of real reads (errproc.py on each set); build if top-alt shares differ <0.05 and R1/R2 ratios <15% between halves. Then confirm the per-mate Q25 excess of spike's R1 disappears when learning is split by mate (offline recount with learnmask.py). About 1-2 h.
ideas.impact: Cheapest broad fix. With 75-84% of errors on one alt base (vs 33% today), random error reads add up to alt counts at a site about twice as often (sum p^2 0.6 vs 0.33), which is what DeepVariant's candidate thresholds count. R1 stops over-erring 2x at the qualities callers trust. FastQC/fastp see N where real reads have them (fastp's n_base_limit filter fired on 275,690 hospital reads, hospital fastp.json). Learned per library, so it carries to other chemistries.
ideas.risks: Output bytes change (K7 gate). Emitting N changes bwa scoring at those bases (minor). Hospital BAM is post-fastp --correction (13,917,960 corrected bases), so overlap tails are partly healed and the emission learned from it passes fastp again in the FASTQ route (minor, ~1.2e-4 corrections/base). Mate split halves the counts (backoff exists).
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (substitution matrix; Q2 tied to N; mate dimension), never built or refuted. Code confirmed: synth.rs:719-728 uniform; quality.rs:1014 drops the called base; quality.rs:253-264 has no mate key. The v2 plan left the mate dimension out without measuring it; the K2b numbers (spike R1 1.9-2.2x real) are new evidence that the class dimension does not absorb it.

ideas.title: Homopolymer slips learned per library, as run-length changes
ideas.problem: At the default --indel-error-rate 0 (main.rs:178-182) spike's reads never slip at homopolymers. When enabled, indels fall wherever a substitution would (synth.rs:210-226) with a uniform random inserted base, not as +-1 unit of a run and not dependent on run length. Real reads slip at long runs at library-dependent rates; indel callers and STR genotypers see that stutter at every homopolymer inside a remade footprint, and spike's reads lack it.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R3; scratchpad phys/errproc.py): 1-2 bp I/D per read pass over a reference homopolymer, by run length, runs touching a Q100 record +-5 bp excluded, MAPQ>=20. 35x real (K2b held-out) vs hospital HG002 30x same blocks: 4-5: 0.0044% vs 0.011%; 6-7: 0.024% vs 0.032%; 8-9: 0.21% (11/5,176) vs 0.30%; 10-11: 0.97% (14/1,440) vs 1.95%; 12-14: 0.59% (6/1,018) vs 2.59%; 15+: 2.2% (15/680) vs 7.20% (83/1,153; 57 ins, 26 del). spike21 same templates: 0 at every run >=8. Same sample in two libraries gives 2-3x different rates at the same sites, so slips are a process, not the sample's variants. Off-run indels: 35x 7.6e-6/base, hospital 1.7e-5, spike 2.6e-6 (alignment artifacts). DOCUMENTED: the v2 gate measured slips at 1.0% (A) and 1.6% (T) at 12-14 runs and dropped them for adding only 0.04 points to clip share (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md:84,105,167); their effect on indel calling was never measured.
ideas.proposal: Learn slip rates from the startup sample's CIGARs: for each read pass over a reference run (sequencing orientation) record whether the read shows a +-1 or +-2 unit change; mask runs where the pool pileup shows the sample's own indel (>=10% of reads, as block_errors does for SNVs). Key rates by run-length bin (6-7, 8-9, 10-11, 12-14, 15+), base, mate and ins vs del. At generation, ReadState already tracks run_base/run_len (quality.rs:209-212): when the template run ends, draw a slip and emit the run one unit shorter or longer, qualities drawn as usual. Retire the uniform indel branch or keep it for off-run errors at the measured off-run rate. Dinucleotide STR stutter next (not measured).
ideas.simplest_version: Homopolymers only: five length bins x 2 (ins/del), pooled over bases and mates, from the 20 sample blocks with a pileup mask; apply a +-1 base slip at the end of the run.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b same templates, errproc.py slip table: spike's per-pass slip rate within 2x of real in every bin from 8-9 up (35x 0.21/0.97/0.59/2.2%) and within 2x on the hospital blocks (0.30/1.95/2.59/7.2%); ins/del share within +-0.15; 4-7 bins no more than 2x real. Broken versions fail: master (0); today's --indel-error-rate 0.05 (15+/4-5 ratio collapses); learned rate ignoring run length (bin shape). Caller check: on 20 spiked het SNVs within 100 bp of runs >=10, DeepVariant's background indel calls and GQ at those runs must match the unspiked BAM within its run-to-run spread.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Measure the slip table on 20 blocks split into two halves by hash; check the 10-11, 12-14 and 15+ bins have >=30 events each and halves agree within 1.5x. The 35x is thin (6-15 events per long bin over 1 Mb), so 40 blocks may be needed for a PCR-free library. About 1 h with errproc.py.
ideas.impact: Many clinical frameshifts sit in homopolymers. Today a planted indel at a run shows exactly two clean alleles where real carriers show 2-7% stutter around both, so DeepVariant's indel GQ, het/hom split and filtering are tested on data that is too easy; background homopolymer indels in every remade window lose their stutter. raredisease also runs ExpansionHunter and stranger on repeat-region reads.
ideas.risks: Q100 may miss real indels in hard homopolymers outside the bench BED (the 2-3x library difference argues the bulk is process; restrict learning to the bench BED). Slips change bwa alignments and may add soft clips (realistic direction, but K2b bad-end clip share must stay |z|<3). Output bytes change. PCR-free 35x is thin per bin.
ideas.history_check: Measured in the v2 gate only as a clip-share contributor (+0.04 points) and left out (v2 plan:84,105,167); not refuted for indel realism; map lists slips OPEN. New: per-pass rates up to 7.2% and 2-3x library dependence on the same sample. --indel-error-rate exists but is shaped wrongly (synth.rs:210-226).

ideas.title: Molecule-level errors shared by both mates (library damage and PCR errors)
ideas.problem: spike draws every error per read, so the two mates of a synthetic fragment never agree on a wrong base beyond chance. Real libraries carry errors in the molecule itself (DNA damage, end-repair and polymerase errors before clustering); both mates and every PCR/optical duplicate read them as the same wrong base at high quality, so overlap-aware callers and duplicate/UMI consensus cannot remove them. All of spike's errors are removable that way; real ones are not.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R4; scratchpad phys/mateconc.py, mateconc2.py, mateconc3.py): overlapping proper pairs, positions both mates align with BQ>=10, Q100 masked +-5 bp. K2b 35x held-out, real vs spike21 same templates: real 1,049,176 overlapped bases, both mates same wrong base at 104 positions vs ~1.7 expected under independence, 44 with both at Q>=30; R1-orientation changes T>C 30, G>T 21, A>G 17, C>A 12. spike21: 20 positions, none at Q>=30, ~1/3 of its 65 both-wrong positions as uniform draws predict. Hospital HG002 30x same 20 blocks: 155 same-base positions in 1,537,431 overlapped bases, 141 with both mates Q>=30, 0 both-wrong with different bases; transitions dominate (A>G 39, T>C 21, C>T 20, G>A 15); 135/155 sites have no other read carrying that alt (molecule errors, not variants). Hospital reads went through fastp --correction (13,917,960 bases corrected in 6,354,765 reads, raredisease trimming/*.fastp.json), which removes overlap disagreements, so concordant errors there are about half of all overlap errors.
ideas.proposal: Learn the molecule-error rate and spectrum from the startup sample's overlapping pairs (pairs and MateAlignment already there): the R1-orientation 4x4 change table per overlapped base where both mates agree on a non-reference base and no other read shares it. Subtract this share from the per-read table's high-Q cells to avoid double counting. At generation, mutate the fragment sequence once, before the two mate templates are cut from it, in generate_read_pair, generate_haplotype_read_pair and generate_depth_pair, so both mates (and any synthetic duplicates, M7) carry them. Qualities stay as drawn (real ones are mostly Q>=30).
ideas.simplest_version: One global rate m and a 12-cell change table in R1 orientation from overlaps in the 20 blocks; mutate the haplotype or reference slice of the fragment with probability m per base before template_at and template_from_seq.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b same templates (mateconc2.py): concordant same-base overlap errors with both mates Q>=30 per overlapped base: 35x real 44/1.05M, spike must land at 31-59 (Poisson 95%; today 0); hospital real 141/1.54M; top R1-orientation changes keep their order (T>C, G>T first on 35x; A>G, T>C on hospital); total high-Q aligned mismatches per base rise no more than 10%. Broken versions fail: errors drawn per mate at rate m (concordance ~0); fragment mutated in reference orientation (G>T/C>A asymmetry flips); no subtraction (high-Q mismatch +>10%).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Repeat mateconc3.py on a third library/region (NA18488 chr20 background in data/validation/background, or HG001 30x): rate within 3x across libraries and most sites singletons. Then inject molecule errors post hoc into spike21 FASTQ pairs and re-align one set to check bwa keeps them as aligned mismatches. About 2 h.
ideas.impact: Decisive for low-VAF benchmarking (af<=0.05, a documented spike case): real high-quality false alleles that survive mate-overlap and duplicate consensus come from molecule errors; spike has none, so it overstates precision of callers that combine overlapping mates or use duplicate/UMI consensus (external knowledge: GATK fragment likelihoods, Mutect2). Small for germline DeepVariant at 30x (a concordant pair gives 2 alt reads at AF ~0.07 < 0.12). Sets up realistic duplicates (M7).
ideas.risks: Hospital counts are confounded by fastp --correction (can turn a discordant error concordant when the high-quality mate is wrong); learning from a fastp'd BAM then running fastp again double-applies it, so prefer bases fastp could not touch or raw libraries like 35x. ~13% of concordant sites carried the alt in other reads (unlisted/mosaic variants): learn only from singletons. Molecule errors are ~1/3 of real high-Q errors, so the subtraction matters. Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: Never measured or proposed. The map lists 'library errors shared by both mates or by duplicates (PCR, 8-oxoG, deamination)' only as not modelled and unmeasured; grep finds no concordant or molecule-error analysis in docs or the case file. Nothing refuted applies.

ideas.title: Dedicated first- and last-cycle bins, and the physical cycle axis for trimmed reads
ideas.problem: Quality-key position bins are 16 cycles wide (pshift 4 at 151 cycles, quality.rs:547, 718); the error table's end bin lumps the last 10 cycles (quality.rs:162-169) and nothing marks the first cycles. Real reads err sharply more at the very last cycle and the first few, and terminal errors cluster (>=2 in the last 4 bases) so bwa soft-clips them; spike spreads them so they stay as aligned high-quality mismatches. In trimmed libraries, a read cut short by its fragment gets end-of-read contexts at a cycle that was mid-run physically (rl = min(cycles, frag), synth.rs:140, 187).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R6; scratchpad phys/errproc.py, Q100 masked), mismatch % by cycle: 35x real R1 cycle151 0.538, 146-150 0.324 (1.66x), 1-5 0.085, 6-10 0.057; 35x R2 0.841 vs 0.535 (1.57x); hospital R1 0.249 vs 0.125 (2.0x), 1-5 0.153, 6-10 0.088; spike21 R1 0.392 vs 0.414 (flat), 1-5 0.087, 6-10 0.082. Aligned Q>=30 mismatches in the last 10 cycles of reads with mean Q>=35 (phys/hiq.py): real 9.0e-5, spike 3.77e-4 (4.2x); spike's excess (~270 errors) matches the 272 real high-Q errors found in 2-4 bp 3' clips (phys/learnmask2.py). Clips by end (phys/clipends.py), real vs spike: 5' 1-4 bp 0.112% vs 0.021-0.029%; 3' 1-4 bp 0.182% vs 0.130%. DOCUMENTED (map): on the hospital BAM reads cut to their fragment have 0.73% low share over their last 10 cycles vs 1.55% for full-length reads. Corroborated by M40's classifier: top feature is last-cycle quality (real 34.57, spike 35.28).
ideas.proposal: In both the quality context key and the error table, replace the coarsest terminal bins with dedicated ones: 3' end cycle 1, cycles 2-4 and 5-10 from the end, plus a 5'-start flag for cycles 1-5. Keep the rest (the refuted 19-bin refinement was general, not terminal). Measure cycles_left from the library's cycle count, not the trimmed length, in both learning (count_read and block_errors use qual.len(), quality.rs:737, 1023) and generation, so a read cut short by its fragment stops mid-run as the sequencer's did.
ideas.simplest_version: Add a last-cycle bin to end_bin (cycles_left == 1) and to the quality key's position, a first-5-cycles flag in the error table, and a one-line change of the cycles_left source for trimmed reads.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b same templates plus the hospital 20-block sample: last-cycle ratio (151 vs 146-150) within +-25% of real (1.66x/1.57x 35x; 2.0x hospital R1); cycles 1-5 vs 6-10 within +-25% (1.5x 35x R1; 1.74x hospital); aligned Q>=30 mismatch in the last 10 cycles of class>=35 reads within +-30% of 9.0e-5; 5' 1-4 bp clip share >=0.5x real; K2b bad-end clip share still |z|<3. Broken versions fail: bins added to the quality key only (error ratio stays flat); master (0.95x, 4.2x).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Count sample bases and errors per new terminal cell at 120k pairs (each needs >=200 bases, MIN_ERROR_BASES); check real train and held-out halves agree on the last-cycle ratio within 10%. About 1 h.
ideas.impact: bwa clips terminal error clusters; today they become isolated high-quality mismatches inside the alignment at 4x the real rate in the cleanest reads, which callers count. Fixes the last-cycle quality/error rise and the start-of-read excess behind real 5' clips; cheap; may also move the 15% crash shortfall.
ideas.risks: Thinner counts at the extremes (backoff covers it). May trade bad-end clip share against aligned mismatches, so K2b must stay in band. 5' clips are partly the sample's variants and chimeras, not modelled here. Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: Final-cycle bin OPEN in the map, never built. REFUTED offline: 19 general position bins as a quality model on bits per quality (0.3858 vs 0.3826; memory quality-model-options) - a general refinement scored on bits, not on errors or clipping at the extremes. Trimmed-read cycle axis OPEN in the map.

ideas.title: Put high-quality errors in the reads that crash: a per-read dead-tail state
ideas.problem: spike learns about the right number of high-quality errors but puts them in the wrong reads. In real data more than half of high-Q errors sit in the clipped tails of crashing reads; spike spreads them over poor and good reads alike, so they stay aligned. Result: 1.8x the real aligned high-Q mismatch rate while crashing ~15% too rarely. v2 contexts (lows in the last 16, errors in the last 30) carry memory only backwards base by base and cannot represent a read whose tail is dead from some cycle on.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R7) on K2b same templates, Q100 masked: aligned Q>=30 mismatch rate real 1.19e-4 vs spike 2.10e-4 (phys/errproc.py); reads with >=1 aligned Q>=30 mismatch real 1.42% vs spike 2.21%, >=6: 0.003% vs 0.017% (phys/hiq.py); in poor classes (mean Q<30 and 30-35) spike is ~2x real in every distance-to-3'-end bin, e.g. 3.31e-3 vs 1.46e-3 at >60 cycles from the end; spike's learning rule counts high-Q errors at 2.41e-4/base, 53% (2,226/4,202) in clipped ends (phys/learnmask.py). DOCUMENTED: K2b crash share 0.90-0.91% vs 1.06% (z -3.7 to -3.9; qtq2/k2b/k2b.txt); in bad tails Q11 errs at 12% (mild) vs 51% (bad), even Q37 at 7%; per-read tail rate SD 0.16 vs 0.108 if every read erred alike (memory bad-tails-20261007).
ideas.proposal: After M2 (mate-aware table) and M5 (terminal bins), re-measure. If the excess remains, add an explicit latent per-read state: learn per read from the startup sample the onset cycle of a dead tail (start of a bad-end clip, or of a burst of lows), giving P(onset | class, run bin, cycle) and separate quality and error tables for dead and alive bases. At generation draw the onset at read start (jointly for mates through the existing class draw) and condition quality and error draws on the state.
ideas.simplest_version: A two-state flag per read, 'dies at cycle c', drawn from the sample's empirical onset distribution per class; the error table gets one extra binary key (dead/alive) learned with the onset rule.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: K2b same templates with bad-end clip share |z|<3 as a constraint: reads with >=1 aligned Q>=30 mismatch within +-15% of real (1.42%; spike 2.21% today); aligned Q>=30 mismatch rate within +-20% of 1.19e-4; crash share |z|<3 vs 1.06%. Broken versions fail: onset drawn independently of class (crashes go to good reads); master. Kill condition: if M2 and M5 alone bring the aligned high-Q rate within +-20%, drop this idea.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: On real K2b reads check whether onset is identifiable: is the per-read tail error rate bimodal given class and lows (dead vs alive), and does onset-given-class carry enough reads per cell? Compare with spike21 under the same rule. About 2-3 h with hiq.py extended.
ideas.impact: Addresses the oldest unexplained residuals (crashes 15% short; hospital run-free reads under-clipping 0.26% vs 0.73%) and removes the 1.8x excess of trusted aligned errors callers count; read-level discriminators would otherwise find it easily (more reads with an isolated Q37 mismatch).
ideas.risks: Earlier latent-state attempts failed as quality models (4-class hidden chain gave crash 0.05%). Interacts with run bin and class mix; onset defined from clips mixes in non-error clips (K2b masking rule needed). May move K1's SD and perfect-read shares. Output bytes change.
ideas.history_check: REFUTED nearby: a 4-class hidden-state chain as a QUALITY model (SD 1.41, crash 0.05%; memory quality-model-options) and 12 finer classes or lows at every level (no gain, v2 gate). 'An explicit bad-tail process (a crash state that stays): not tested' (memory quality-model-options-20261006). New: aligned high-Q excess localised by class and end bin (hiq.py) and the 53% clip share of learned high-Q errors. Gated behind M2/M5 by its own kill condition.

ideas.title: Synthetic PCR and optical duplicate families at the sample's own rates
ideas.problem: spike makes no duplicates of its own reads (only junction-DUP depth copies, jittered on purpose; synth.rs:414-439). After raredisease re-marks duplicates, spiked windows show a lower duplicate share than real ones. Each synthetic molecule is sequenced once, so nothing a real PCR family shares (molecule errors, M4) is repeated. Picard's optical detection works on SPIKE_ names but no optical pair exists (tile and x/y from a hash of the internal name, read_name.rs:154-161).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R8): hospital MarkDuplicates metrics: 17,385,340 of 369,010,019 pairs duplicates (4.71%), 10,361,338 of them optical (59.6%). DOCUMENTED: in spiked regions the duplicate share is 0.008 vs 0.036 real (memory duplicates.md, realism-inspection item C); clean mode removes the duplicates of removed originals (origin.rs:997-1054), so spiked windows lose them and gain none.
ideas.proposal: From the donor pool and the existing duplicate scan (5'-end family keys, duplicate flags), learn the family-size distribution, optical share and optical pairs' tile and x/y distances (from input read names). For each synthetic pair draw a family size; emit PCR copies (same fragment and template, same molecule errors, independent sequencing errors, new name) or optical copies (same tile, x/y within the learned distance) in the learned proportion. Keep copies in fastq_removed_reads/merge logic as ordinary SPIKE_ reads; they must be flagged by Picard and dropped by callers.
ideas.simplest_version: One duplicate probability per pair equal to the pool's duplicate share, and an optical flag at the sample's optical share; an optical copy reuses the tile and offsets x/y by up to 100 px; copies share the fragment and draw new sequencing errors.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: FASTQ -> bwa-mem2 -M -K 1e8 -> Picard MarkDuplicates on the hospital BAM's 20 K2 events: duplicate share inside spiked windows within +-25% of the unspiked BAM's share there (today 0.008 vs 0.036); Picard optical fraction within +-0.10 of 0.596; duplicate-filtered het VAF at planted SNVs unchanged within +-0.02. Broken versions fail: copies with jittered 5' ends (not flagged, share stays ~0.008); optical names on random tiles (optical fraction ~0); copies not removed by callers (VAF rises).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hand-make 50 synthetic pairs plus copies (same fragment, optical name near the original), align, run Picard MarkDuplicates with raredisease's flags, and check every copy is flagged with the right optical call. About 1-2 h; settles the naming question before any Rust.
ideas.impact: Spiked regions pass duplicate QC and look like the rest of the library in MultiQC/Picard (owner wants FASTQs Picard and FastQC treat as real). Prerequisite for family-shared errors at low VAF. Raw-count CNV tools and coverage QC that do not drop duplicates see real-like depth composition. Effect on calls small (callers skip duplicates).
ideas.risks: More reads per event; family-size estimates from one pool are noisy (use the startup sample). Interaction with the removal list and fastq.sh found-vs-wanted accounting. Picard pixel distance on patterned flow cells must match raredisease's settings. Output bytes change. Partly overlaps M10/M21 (in-read edit or remap would keep real duplicates for free).
ideas.history_check: OPEN since the duplicates run (memory duplicates.md: 'spike makes no duplicates of its own reads ... reported only'); never built. The duplicate-leak fix (2eb9309) is done and separate.

ideas.title: Fragment-end (tagmentation) motif: weight synthetic fragment starts by the library's own end preference
ideas.problem: Synthetic fragment starts are uniform (simulate.rs:1043, 1064, gen_range). The hospital library's real read starts carry a strong composition signature over the first cycles (Tn5-like, inferred); spike's reads start at background composition. A single base separates them statistically, and fine-scale start-site pattern (coverage and duplicate structure) differs.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R9) at the 22 hospital K2 events (scratchpad phys/startcomp2.py; qtq2/k2v2), first cycles in sequencing orientation: sample reads (n=227,849) cycle 1 A .182, C .337, G .291, T .190; cycle 2 T .318, G .182; cycle 6 A .322. SPIKE_ reads (n=9,559) cycle 1 A .272, C .226, G .222, T .281, flat through cycle 11. DOCUMENTED (map): the 35x PCR-free library shows only mild bias (cycle 1 A .331), so this belongs to the library.
ideas.proposal: From the startup sample learn a position weight matrix over -5..+10 bp around each read's 5' end, on the read's own strand, against background k-mer frequencies. When drawing a fragment, accept a uniform start with probability w(left) x w(right) / w_max^2 (rejection sampling) or use importance weights over candidate starts; apply the same weighting to junction-crossing zones for additive events.
ideas.simplest_version: Position-specific mononucleotide PWM for 3 bases each side of the cut; rejection sampling of fragment starts on both ends with the acceptance rate logged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: At the hospital K2 events, SPIKE_ composition at cycles 1-6 within +-0.02 of the sample reads' in every base (C .337, G .291 at cycle 1); on 35x spike stays within +-0.02 of its mild bias. Broken versions fail: PWM applied on the reference strand instead of the read strand (cycle-1 C/G excess appears mirrored on reverse reads); master (flat .22-.28).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Learn the PWM on even blocks and test its likelihood gain on odd blocks of hospital reads; compute the rejection acceptance rate for the speed cost. About 1 h with Python.
ideas.impact: Removes a per-read tell a classifier or FastQC per-base content would see in the SPIKE_ block of a FASTQ, and gives synthetic reads the library's start-site structure. Effect on variant calls likely small; owner wants FASTQs downstream tools treat as real.
ideas.risks: Rejection sampling costs speed (owner cares). Changes which fragments cross junctions, so SIM_ALT_FRAGS and realised VAF shift slightly. Library-specific: must be learned, never hard-coded. M10/M21 (in-read edit, remap) would inherit real starts for free except for novel or junction fragments.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (fragment-end motif, measured on the hospital BAM); never built or refuted. GC bias, a related start-placement effect, was measured small (0.88-1.08) and left alone.

ideas.title: Adapter read-through and sub-read-length fragments for untrimmed libraries
ideas.problem: For an untrimmed library spike never draws a fragment shorter than one read (min_fragment_len = read_length, synth.rs:128-134; stats.rs:34-41; mate_length refuses shorter fragments, synth.rs:138-142). Synthetic reads never read into the adapter and never form fully overlapping or dovetailed pairs; real untrimmed libraries carry adapter clips and short fragments that aligners and callers handle as noise.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED: on the 35x untrimmed slice 0.71% of all reads (25.7% of clipped reads) have adapter clips; spike has 0 (memory soft-clip-causes-20261006). 0.83% of proper R1 pairs in chr20:10-11 Mb have |TLEN|<151 (map). The adapter is learnable from the sample: past TLEN the consensus equals TruSeq R1/R2 for 33 bp, then the library's index (memory soft-clip-causes). Code confirmed (R10). The hospital library is sequencer-trimmed and unaffected (memory read-length-fix).
ideas.proposal: For libraries bam_stats calls untrimmed, admit the pool's |TLEN| below read length into the fragment CDF; append the per-mate adapter consensus learned from the startup sample's short pairs (bases past TLEN in sequencing order, including the index) past the fragment end; run the quality and error model over adapter bases as over any other.
ideas.simplest_version: TruSeq R1/R2 adapter strings plus the learned 8-10 bp index from short pairs in the startup sample; fragment CDF floor lowered to 1 for untrimmed libraries.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the 35x untrimmed BAM (K2b design without the TLEN>=151 filter): adapter-clip share after bwa-mem2 within +-25% of real (0.71% of reads); share of pairs with |TLEN|<151 within +-0.2 points of 0.83%; hospital (trimmed) output byte-identical to master. Broken versions fail: adapter on the wrong mate (clip spectra and consensus check differ); floor lowered without adapter bases (clips stay ~0).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Re-extract the adapter consensus from 20 blocks of the 35x BAM and check per-position agreement >=0.76 over 33 bp on both halves. Ask the user whether adapter clips are in scope before any code.
ideas.impact: Users with untrimmed libraries (GIAB-style data, other sites): adapter-clipped short fragments are ~26% of real soft clips there, and their absence makes spiked windows cleaner for SV callers' clip evidence. Does not matter for the hospital demo.
ideas.risks: User leans toward modelling only bad ends (memory soft-clip-causes: 'maybe we can skip all softclips except for those generated by bad ends'), so ask first. Index barcodes are sample-specific (copying the input's index is realistic but should be documented). Output bytes change for untrimmed inputs only.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map and in the soft-clip analysis (learnable adapter, not built); user leans away; never refuted. Read-length trimming for trimmed libraries is done (3684f74).

ideas.title: In-read base editing for SNVs/MNVs (BAMSurgeon/SomatoSim style), keeping real qualities, errors, duplicates and flanks (P1b)
ideas.problem: For an SNV spike suppresses and re-synthesises every event-copy pair in +-2 kb. Most remade pairs never touch the site yet lose real qualities, errors, duplicates, local depth and the sample's indels. The landscape standard for SNVs is to edit the base inside the real reads that cover it.
ideas.evidence: INFERRED (map): with HAP_FLANK 2000 (src/main.rs:241) and the tiling count at src/simulate.rs:817, ~88-92% of remade fragments for an SNV do not show the variant.
