DOCUMENTED: duplicate share in spiked regions 0.008 vs 0.036 real (memory duplicates.md); real hom SNVs keep 0.17% ref reads, spike's 0; CR3 erasure as in M11/M41 (198 hom background indels 0.934 -> 0.479 after spiking). LANDSCAPE: SomatoSim introduces variants directly into experimental reads, preserving error profiles (Hawari et al. 2021, BMC Bioinformatics, PMC7936459); BAMSurgeon addsnv edits existing reads; AMP/API/CAP in-silico validation recommendations (Duncavage et al., J Mol Diagn 2022) treat 'manipulated data files in which variants are inserted into existing data files' as a main category. DOCUMENTED: raredisease runs fastp --correction (memory hospital-demo-plan.md:23), which rewrites mismatching bases in overlapping mates.
ideas.proposal: For SNV/MNV events select event-copy fragments covering the changed bases at copy_rate (same copy assignment and rate as today, only on fragments covering the site). Rewrite the base in both mates when they overlap the site, and identically in every member of the fragment's duplicate family (origin::duplicates_of). Keep each read's quality string, other bases and errors; a read whose base at the site was a sequencing error keeps an error. Rename edited records SPIKE_. In the FASTQ route edit the raw record at the same 5'-anchored offset in sequencing orientation (fastp trims only 3'). Pairs elsewhere in the window are untouched; non-pool reads over the site stay in the census.
ideas.simplest_version: Het SNVs only, BAM route, pool pairs only; edit both mates and the duplicate family; leave everything else untouched, so R1/R2 contain only edited pairs.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Rerun transplant round 2b/3's SNV group with in-read edits on the hospital HG002/HG001 pair, same scripts and controls: A metric stays supported (rho rule); background indel GTs within 2 kb unchanged vs unspiked in >=95%; Picard duplicate share in footprints equal to unspiked (~0.036-0.047) instead of 0.008; base-quality-at-site distribution of ALT reads vs real HG001 carriers KS p>0.01. A broken variant editing only one mate of overlapping pairs must lose ALT after fastp --correction (realised AF below planted by about the overlapping-pair share). KILL if A becomes refuted or no flank metric (duplicates, background GTs) moves.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours: a pysam prototype outside spike edits 20 transplant SNV sites in the hospital HG002 BAM (both mates, duplicate families), realigns edited pairs with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000, scores with scripts/transplant/small_evidence.py against real HG001 carriers.
ideas.impact: SNV/MNV spikes, the most common clinical class, become nearly indistinguishable from real data outside the edited base: duplicates, depth shape and background indels kept. Low-AF and mosaic spikes edit exactly k real reads with no floor of 2 synthetic fragments. Brings spike to the landscape standard while keeping its whole-sample FASTQ route.
ideas.risks: Indels cannot be edited in place without changing read length (SNV/MNV only). Edit position must survive fastp's 5' end and --correction. Reads with soft clips over the site. Transplant 2b already SUPPORTS SNVs, so the gain is in flanks. Renaming real reads to SPIKE_ changes Picard optical keys unless tile/x/y are kept.
ideas.history_check: P1b in the map, OPEN, never built or refuted. Fix A (copying whole donor quality strings onto synthetic reads, de806dd) was REFUTED as a soft-clip fix - a different mechanism on synthetic reads. Rests on flank gaps (duplicates, CR3), not site evidence. Sibling of M21 (P1, remap for all non-additive events).

ideas.title: Carry the sample's own phased haplotypes, indels included, onto every remade copy (CR3 option A via a phased/truth VCF)
ideas.problem: Remade event-copy reads (event +-2 kb; both copies at v>0.5) are built from reference plus the sample's SNPs only: SampleCopies is two HashMap<u64,u8> SNP maps (src/loh.rs:34-43), the gVCF parser returns on any non-SNP (src/loh.rs:554-557), and apply_variants writes single bases (src/haplotype.rs:661-697). Every spike erases the sample's nearby indels and SVs from the replaced share of reads: hom indels near a planted variant fall to about het, het indels on the event copy vanish. In the hospital VCF this would show as new het indels next to each spiked variant (a spike signature and wrong background genotypes), and a clinician comparing with GIAB truth would see holes around every planted variant. The event copy is a coin per phase block and is not recorded.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R11) read-only on existing transplant round-2 forward run0 (HG001-only small variants into hospital HG002 D24-14230; view = recipient minus replaced_reads.txt plus sim.bam), first 80 events (scratchpad cr3probe/cr3_existing.py, cr3_het.py): 17 HG002 Q100 hom-alt indels 400-1,921 bp from 12 planted events went from recipient AF median 0.95 to 0.48 (range 0.35-0.85); 0 of 211 synthetic _hap_ reads covering them carry the indel; all 17 are 1/1 in the hospital's DeepVariant call. 49 het indels: 0 of 596 synthetic reads carry them. LDLR exposure (Q100 vs data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed +-2 kb): 18/18 exon footprints hold a carried non-SNP, 9/18 a hom one. Larger measurement in M41 (R26): 198 hom indels median 0.934 -> 0.479, 214/752 events damage >=1 background indel, SNPs preserved. MEASURED in the map: of 2,000 random chr20 footprints in HG002 Q100, 48.9% hold a carried het non-SNP, 27.3% a hom non-SNP. DOCUMENTED: CR3 probe hom 2 bp DEL under a het DUP AF 1.0 -> 0.360; T7 38/40 footprints (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:122-196; REVIEW.md:4634-4651). Both GIAB truths fully phased (memory validation-plan.md); first 200,000 NA12878 Platinum v1.2 records hold 55,919 1|0, 59,748 0|1, 84,333 1/1, no unphased het (R53). Backgrounds will be GIAB/demo data, never patient data (memory hospital-demo-plan.md:22). LANDSCAPE: VISOR (HACk), VarSim, NEAT, simuG build haplotypes from phased VCFs of every variant type.
ideas.proposal: Add a sample-haplotype source (--sample-vcf / --phased-truth VCF with GT|PS, indels included, optional --truth-bed). Build each copy's template from reference plus that copy's phased records: SNPs as today, small indels (and later SVs wholly inside the footprint) as segment splits marked 'background' via the existing segment machinery, so they are never junctions and never counted by SIM_ALT_FRAGS, own_bases or the validate probes; then apply the event on top. Pick the event copy per PS block (coin or explicit hap=1/2, shared with M16); refuse when the event overlaps a truth record on its copy (as carried.rs does). Write the choice to truth as phased GT plus PS and to the run README. Outside the truth BED or at unphased records fall back to today's pileup path and record SIM_TEMPLATE=truth|pileup per event. Suppression and tiling unchanged. Complements M21/M10 (which shrink the remade set; this makes remade reads right).
ideas.simplest_version: Biallelic SNPs plus indels <=50 bp from a phased VCF over the footprint, small-variant events only, inside the truth BED; split reference segments for the event-copy and other-copy haplotypes; refuse when a background indel overlaps the event's REF span; no SVs or STR alleles; every other event and region byte-identical without the flag.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (a) Value kill (shared with M41's gate): run DeepVariant (hospital container) on the spiked view and the unspiked BAM over +-2 kb of round-2 forward run0's events (or plant 20 het SNVs near Q100 hom indels and 20 near het indels in the hospital HG002 BAM). If >=95% of background indel GTs are unchanged (R11: at most 1 of 17 hom and <=5% of 49 het), the read loss does not reach the caller - shelve. (b) Mechanism kill after build: re-plant the same events; background hom indels must return to median AF >=0.9 with >=90% of SPIKE_ reads over them carrying the allele; het indels within binomial noise of the recipient AF; CR3 dup_homdel probe back to AF ~1.0; transplant 2b SNV/indel verdicts unchanged; >=95% background GTs unchanged. Today's code fails (0.48; 0/211).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 2 h, no spike run: bcftools mpileup|call (or the DeepVariant container) on the recipient and the spiked view at the 66 background-indel sites already found in round-2 forward run0; count GT flips. If nothing flips, stop.
ideas.impact: Hospital demo: removes a systematic visible artefact around every spiked LDLR variant (background hom indels turned het) and gives phased truth; benchmarkers get unbiased FP/FN in the 4 kb around each spike. Prerequisite for realistic STR events on the sample's own allele (M18), grouped events (M15) and LOH/ROH events. Unique pairing of real reads plus a complete haplotype (BAMSurgeon has no haplotype model; VISOR/VarSim have no real reads).
ideas.risks: Segment bookkeeping (junctions(), SIM_ALT_FRAGS, own_bases, del_planted/ins_planted probes) must ignore background breaks or every background indel becomes a junction. The VCF must belong to the BAM's sample (see M30): GIAB truth works for demo backgrounds; a DeepVariant+WhatsHap VCF elsewhere carries its own errors. Truth BEDs exclude hard regions where CR3 may matter most; truth errors become spike errors. SeraCare-engineered HG002 (D24-14230) differs from Q100 in 7 genes - mask them +-2 kb. Indel representation/left-alignment vs reads. SVs in footprints complicate segment arithmetic (ref_range across chromosomes). Output bytes change with the flag (K7-style seed-spread gate). Overlaps P1/P1b and CR7(b); design notes say to design these together.
ideas.history_check: CR3 option A open since the Codex review, awaiting the user (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:122-200, 490-505: 'large, overlaps CR7'). Option B's blanket footprint WARNING was REFUTED by T7 (38/40 fire); this is not a warning. Fail-closed for an unreadable --gvcf is DONE. The map's 'measure first' step is now answered at read level (R11, R26). New: the owner committed to GIAB/demo backgrounds with complete phased truths, turning option A from a learned model into reading a file. Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Sex- and ploidy-aware events: detect a male background, hemizygous dosage and haploid truth GT on non-PAR chrX/chrY, VCF GT honoured
ideas.problem: spike has no sex, ploidy or PAR model: grep for chrX|chrY|ploid|hemizyg|haploid|PAR in src/ finds only one chrM/gVCF test line (loh.rs:1480). Default --allele-fraction 0.5 (main.rs:102), af=het maps to 0.5 (main.rs:303-310), truth GT is only 0/1 or 1/1 from VAF (genotype_from_vaf, truth.rs:468-474), and VCF GT is counted but never used (vcf_input.rs:262-271). On a male's non-PAR chrX/Y the default plants a half-dose, mosaic-like event written 0/1 (a genotype a male cannot carry); af=hom is physically right but writes diploid 1/1; the pileup's spurious 'het SNPs' on a haploid X are phased and a coin picks the event copy among them. Nothing warns. The hospital demo background HG002 is male, and X-linked genes (DMD exon deletions above all, OTC, F8, F9, GLA, ABCD1) are core raredisease demos.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED sex signal: idxstats chrX/autosome density 0.499 (hospital HG002), 0.501 (HG002 35x), 0.977 (HG001); chrY 0.444/0.468/0.075 (R12); idxstats chrX 157.1 vs chr7 315.6 reads/kb (0.498). Windowed MAPQ>=20 counts (R37, R43): HG002 35x chrX:50-51 Mb 128,171, DMD chrX:31-32 Mb 137,311 vs chr7:50-51 Mb 290,897 (0.44-0.47); chrX:100.0-100.5 vs chr7 0.425; PAR1 chrX:1-2 Mb 264,805 (0.91, diploid depth); HG001 CRAM 0.88-0.905. raredisease ngsbits_samplegender: D24-14230 male (ratio_chry_chrx 0.2832), HG001 D25-7403 female (0.0123). Hospital pipeline behaviour (R52): DeepVariant/GLnexus VCF (call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz) has 105,196 non-PAR chrX records all 1/1 and 4,073 PAR records all 1/1; of 74,867 male non-PAR SNVs at depth >=10 only 334 (0.45%) have ref fraction 0.2-0.8 vs 64% on chr20; female HG001 has 88,860 0/1 + 3,066 1/0 on non-PAR X; EH reports a single REPCN at the 6 chrX loci. Re-checked by the merger: bcftools view -r chrX:10001-2781479 on that VCF gives 3,794 records, all 1/1 (this pipeline calls PAR1 haploid in this male, although read depth there is diploid). Real hemizygous SNVs (R12, scratchpad cr3probe/chrx_af.py): 200 Q100 GT=1 SNVs in chrX:20-30 Mb on the hospital BAM, median depth 16, median AF 1.0, 4.5% below 0.8; chr20 hets median AF 0.512 at 33x. Spike runs (R43, scratchpad robust/chrx_het, chrx_hom; v2 7f28bb0, master 4a5672d differs only in quality.rs's run-ratio cache): del:chrX:31500000-31502000 on HG002 35x af=het exits 0 with 0 WARN, SIM_VAF 0.500, GT 0/1; af=hom writes GT 1/1; log 'chrX:31498000-31504000: 1 het SNPs, 3 hom-alt SNPs; phased 1 het SNPs into 1 block(s)' (a het call on a haploid X). Q100 chrX:10-60 Mb holds 41,317 haploid GT '1' records and 64 DELs >=50 bp. ClinVar P/LP: 24,472 of 339,976 (7.2%) on chrX non-PAR (cnv_validation resources/clinical/clinvar.vcf.gz). DOCUMENTED: CR7(a) (input GT=1/1 gives SIM_VAF 0.500 and GT 0/1) and CR7(b) open (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404); cnv_validation docs/findings/2026-08-31-chrx-male-ploidy.md (diploid model makes gCNV call ~99% of male chrX CN=1); cnv_validation config.yaml:43-48 excludes chrX.
ideas.proposal: (1) Sex: --sex male|female, else inferred from BAI per-contig mapped counts (chrX density vs autosomes, cut ~0.65-0.7; measured male 0.43-0.50, female 0.88-0.98), with a warning when flag and depth disagree; CRAM (CRAI has no counts) needs --sex or an estimate from the quality sample's chrX block; a chr20-only slice gives 'unknown', which refuses X/Y events unless --sex is given. (2) Built-in GRCh38 PAR table (PAR1 chrX:10,001-2,781,479; PAR2 155,701,383-156,030,895), --ploidy-bed for other builds, refuse to guess for unknown builds. (3) Haploid regions (male non-PAR X, Y): one copy; omitted af defaults to 1.0; af=hom means the single copy (copy_rate 1); af<1 warns by default as mosaic (owner's measure-and-warn preference) and is refused under --strict-ploidy unless --mosaic; skip het phasing (every fragment is the one copy, copy_rate = v); truth GT '1' (option '1/1' to match GLnexus) plus SIM_PLOIDY and ##spike_sex; DEL af=hom = 0 copies, DUP = CN 2; chrY in a female refused. (4) Opt-in VCF genotype mode (CR7 option B): GT drives dosage (0/1 -> 0.5, 1/1 -> 1, haploid 1 -> 1), phased GT/PS carried, FILTER/hom-ref gates opt-in. (5) PAR follows a declared policy: read depth there is diploid (0.91) but this pipeline calls PAR haploid in males (3,794/3,794 1/1), so dosage stays diploid while the truth GT convention in PAR is configurable. Female samples and autosomes byte-identical. Sex call and ploidy written to the run README. chrM handled in M19.
ideas.simplest_version: A --sex male flag (inference later) that on non-PAR chrX/Y (a) defaults af to 1.0, (b) warns when af<1, (c) writes GT '1' (or '1/1') with SIM_PLOIDY=1. Dosage code needs no change: af=1 already removes all event-copy and other-copy pool pairs (copy_rate min(1,2v) and max(0,2v-1), src/synth.rs:694-700) and tiles full depth. Alternative minimal guard (R37): a warning when an event lies on non-PAR X/Y and the X/autosome ratio is below 0.65.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (a) Inference: male for HG002 35x and the hospital BAM (agreeing with ngsbits), female for HG001, 'unknown' for a chr20-only slice; kill if it misclassifies any local BAM or a female's X ratio overlaps the male band. (b) Spike 30 SNVs at Q100-reference positions in chrX:20-30 Mb into hospital HG002 with defaults (BAM route, bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000): realised AF must match HG002's real hemizygous SNVs (median 1.0, <=10% below 0.8; real 4.5%); today's default predicts median ~0.5 and must fail; kill if AF stays below 0.8 at >10% of sites. (c) DMD del:chrX:31500000-31502000 at af=hom after align.sh+merge.sh: interior depth only the resistant share (SIM_RESIST 0.027, validate coverage_ratio ~0), GT '1'; at af=het it warns (refuses under --strict-ploidy). (d) PAR1 events (e.g. chrX:1.5 Mb): read-level AF stays diploid-like (~0.5); a classifier that ignores PAR fails; kill the design if PAR events are refused. (e) HG001 same DMD event at af=het byte-identical to master. (f) Caller level (R52): DeepVariant as raredisease runs it on 20 af=0.5 and 20 af=hom male non-PAR SNVs: kill the caller-level claim if af=0.5 spikes already look like real male X calls (ref fraction outside 0.2-0.8 as in >=99.5% of real calls and GQ matching real 1/1, KS p>0.01); support needs af=0.5 inside 0.2-0.8 (real 0.45%) and af=hom/default matching real hemizygous calls; a DMD exon DEL at af=hom must give CN0 in CNVnator/gCNV as at a real hemizygous Q100 chrX DEL.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Under 1 h: idxstats on every local whole-genome BAM (HG002 35x, HG002 strobealign, hospital; done for 3: 0.499/0.501 vs 0.977) to confirm one cut separates them and a slice gives 'unknown'. Minutes: read raredisease's DeepVariant haploid_contigs/par_regions from pipeline_info. Minutes: one spike run of a single non-PAR chrX SNV into HG002 at default and af=hom, pileup of realised AF in sim.bam plus kept reads; optionally DV on that region (hours).
ideas.impact: X-linked disorders (DMD, OTC, F8, F9, GLA, ABCD1; 7.2% of ClinVar P/LP) can be demoed on the male GIAB background without biologically impossible het calls; truth GT matches what DeepVariant, genmod and hap.py/vcfeval haploid scoring see; stops phasing on haploid-X alignment artifacts. Landscape: NEAT and VISOR take a ploidy setting; spike is the outlier.
ideas.risks: PAR coordinates are build-specific; X-transposed region and X-Y homologous genes give low MAPQ (RF8 may refuse). GT '1' vs '1/1' conventions differ (hap.py, Truvari, GLnexus; DV writes male X as 1/1), so scorers must treat 1 == 1/1. A wrong --sex silently gives wrong dosage (depth cross-check mitigates). Aneuploidy, loss of Y. Mosaic studies need af<1 on X. Owner prefers warnings over new refusals (only RF8 refuses); CR7 notes ask to keep old behaviour as default for one release. Truth bytes change for male X runs. Full CR7 model is large and tied to CR3 (M11).
ideas.history_check: CR7(b) open since the Codex review, sized 'large'; option B (two explicit modes) recommended but not chosen (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:330-404). CR7(c) af=het exactly 0.5 done (8dca8d0) and does not touch ploidy. No ploidy code has ever existed; nothing refuted. New: the hospital pipeline's own haploid calls on X and PAR, a measured silent DMD run, the haploid het-phasing artifact.

ideas.title: Homology-aware breakpoints for approximate and exon-spec CNVs (snap to NAHR / microhomology junctions)
ideas.problem: Exon specs cut exactly at exon edges (src/exon.rs:421-427) and approximate coordinates are cut bluntly where stated (src/haplotype.rs:122-161). Real LDLR DELs/DUPs are often Alu-mediated: two same-orientation Alus join at homologous positions, giving a hybrid Alu, long junction homology and low-MAPQ junction reads (the class Manta missed at ClinVar 4845403). The repo's own LDLR demo events carry junction classes no real FH carrier has.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R15): data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_known_deletions_hg38.vcf has both ends on a multiple of 100 in 15/22 records. Junction homology (scratchpad cr3probe/junction_homology.py, GRCh38 no-alt): 19 demo DELs median 0 bp, 1/19 >=2 bp, 12/19 blunt; 31 ClinVar LDLR-region DELs median 1 bp, 14/31 >=2 bp. 20/22 demo records have a same-orientation Alu pair within 500 bp of both ends; 13/22 have both ends inside an Alu (UCSC rmsk; 356 Alus in chr19:11.0-11.2 Mb). Map (another reader): 0/36 LDLR exon edges in an Alu vs 19/62 ClinVar ends (note: that used the bundled BED whose exon 1 is wrong, M29); HG002 Q100 chr20 DELs >=50 bp have 372/442 >=2 bp homology (median 16) vs 80/442 random. DOCUMENTED: spike's precise-coordinate Alu-Alu junctions clip like real carriers in 16/18 events (memory realism-inspection-20261006.md). Many real LDLR SVs are not Alu-mediated: 24 of 39 have neither end in an Alu (memory hospital-demo-plan.md).
ideas.proposal: Opt-in bp=nahr / --snap-breakpoints W for DEL/DUP (exon or coordinate specs): search +-W of each stated end for same-orientation Alu (or segdup/LCR) pairs, align them, put the junction at a homologous position inside their longest identical stretch so the haplotype holds a hybrid element; otherwise fall back to the best 2-20 bp microhomology position. Exon specs take intronic ends that keep the stated exons inside. Truth gets snapped POS/END, CIPOS/CIEND for the original, SIM_SNAP=class.
ideas.simplest_version: DEL only, Alu pairs only (rmsk), W=1 kb, junction at the midpoint of the longest exact match >=10 bp between the two Alus; otherwise unchanged with a warning.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Yardstick: round-1b HG001-only Alu-Alu DELs with real carriers in the HG001 hospital BAM; per event measure junction homology, junction-read MAPQ, split/clipped-read count and clip offset. Snapped versions of the 22 demo LDLR records planted into HG002 must fall within the real-vs-real spread on these metrics and today's rounded versions outside it. If the rounded versions already match real, the cut position inside Alus does not matter to aligner or callers: kill and only document. Secondary: SIM_RESIST and Manta call/no-call for snapped exon-spec events move toward ClinVar-precise events.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Minutes of reference arithmetic: snap the 22 demo records offline and report homology and hybrid-Alu identity. Then compare junction-read MAPQ in an existing rounded-LDLR spike (sv_slice_test B1-B3 runs) with the realism-inspection Alu-Alu events (scratchpad inspect/).
ideas.impact: LDLR exon CNV demos that look like real FH carriers to Manta, TIDDIT and gCNV; SV benchmarks lose a systematic easy bias in exon-spec events.
ideas.risks: Snapping changes the user's stated event: opt-in and recorded. Several Alu pairs may qualify (seed-dependent snap). Junctions inside repeats raise SIM_RESIST and may trip RF8. Microhomology fallback matters as much as Alu (24/39 real LDLR SVs not Alu-mediated).
ideas.history_check: Map lists 'exon-spec breakpoints: document or add an option' as open; never built or refuted. The realism inspection supports that precise coordinates give real-like clips, the premise here. Related: M29 fixes the bundled exon BED and relabels the approximate-deletion VCF; M43 measures real Manta behaviour at Alu-Alu DELs.

ideas.title: Mobile-element insertions from a consensus library with poly-A tail and target-site duplication
ideas.problem: Symbolic <INS:ME:ALU/L1/SVA> records and ins:...:len specs get iid uniform random bases (src/main.rs:2017-2024; src/vcf_input.rs:363-391), with no poly-A, no TSD and no fragments wholly inside. Real MEI evidence is mates mapping to the element's many genomic copies at MAPQ 0 plus clipped poly-A; random sequence gives unmapped mates instead (inferred). HGVS/ClinVar describe MEIs symbolically (e.g. BRCA2 c.9342_9343insAluY), so a clinical MEI spike today is random DNA.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED/MEASURED in cnv_validation config/frozen_evidence/mei_evidence.tsv: the real AluY in BRCA2 carried by the hospital HG002 SeraCare construct (chr13:32394774) has a 343 bp insert, 15 bp TSD and 40 bp homopolymer; 26 clipped and 72 spanning reads; 15/15 support mates off-contig, 14 at MAPQ 0, over 10 contigs; NA12878 control 0 clipped. Map (another reader): 36/765 HG002 Q100 chr20 INS >=50 bp are >=50% ME 13-mers and 17/765 end in poly-A/T >=10, vs 0 and 0 for spike's random sequence. MEASURED: hospital params skip_me_calling true (RetroSeq off), so the effect is on Manta/TIDDIT and on what a reviewer sees.
ideas.proposal: A bundled ME consensus set (Dfam AluY/AluYa5, L1HS with a 5'-truncation length draw, SVA_E/F) with random strand, poly-A length draw (10-60 bp), TSD of drawn length (7-20 bp) duplicated from the target site, optional per-base divergence. An ins:...:alu spec and VCF <INS:ME:*> use it; anything else falling back to random bases warns. Truth already carries the built sequence (CR7).
ideas.simplest_version: AluY consensus + 30 bp poly-A + 15 bp TSD for <INS:ME:ALU> only, with a warning for other ME types.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Plant AluY (consensus + poly-A + 15 bp TSD) at chr13:32394774 into HG001 (D25-7403, which lacks it), align with the hospital command: share of support mates off-contig and at MAPQ 0 must match the real SeraCare AluY (15/15 and 14/15) within binomial noise, and clipped-per-spanning-read share within noise. The random-sequence version (today's symbolic path) must fail with mates unmapped. Kill if the consensus version also fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No code (hours): write AluY consensus + poly-A + TSD as an explicit-sequence VCF INS (that path works), run today's spike into HG001 at that locus, align, count mate placement.
ideas.impact: MEI demos and SV benchmarks where Manta and TIDDIT see MEIs as they see real ones; symbolic MEIs stop being detectable as random DNA.
ideas.risks: The SeraCare AluY is an engineered construct at unknown AF: compare shares, not counts. Consensus-vs-real divergence changes MAPQ. Long L1/SVA need in-insert fragments (M18's change). ME calling is skipped at the hospital, so value there is indirect.
ideas.history_check: Map lists 'realistic insertion content' as open. RF15 (short INS cleaner than real) is open but concerns 20-39 bp. Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Grouped events on one haplotype pair: compound hets and cis/trans small-variant groups inside one footprint, with phased truth
ideas.problem: Recessive and compound-het demos (homozygous/compound FH in LDLR, any AR gene ranked by genmod's compound model) need two variants in one gene on chosen copies. Footprints must sit >=7 kb apart (FOOTPRINT_MARGIN = HAP_FLANK + MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN = 3500, src/main.rs:1188; refusal main.rs:1088-1188). With --allow-overlap each event is simulated against the original donor and the sets concatenated (src/simulate.rs:410-428): when both coins pick the same copy depth is ~1+v and each ALT ~v/(1+v), and no read carries both alleles. Events further apart flip independent coins per phase block (src/loh.rs:924-949), so cis/trans is random and unrecorded; truth GT is unphased (src/truth.rs:468-474).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: 52 of 153 LDLR exon pairs (34%) are <7 kb apart edge to edge (data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed; consistent with M16's 101/153 >=7 kb), so two exonic variants in those exons are refused (R13). Of 1,095 ClinVar P/LP SNVs in LDLR (clinvar.vcf.gz, chr19:11089000-11134000), 295,948 of 598,965 pairs (49.4%) are <7 kb apart, so half of LDLR compound-het pairings are refused today (R40). The hospital ranked clinical VCF has Compounds/CompoundsNormalized INFO (header measured), so the pipeline scores compound pairs. DOCUMENTED: two adjacent DELs at AF=1 under --allow-overlap read 67.05x/67.03x inside (REVIEW.md:2930-2939, CR1); phase coin per call confirmed (memory validation-plan.md, Astra point b); grouped composition listed as not built (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:297-301, 490-505). INFERRED from code: under --allow-overlap no synthetic read carries both ALTs.
ideas.proposal: An event group (--event 'snp:chr19:P1:A:T;group=fh1;copy=1' --event '...;group=fh1;copy=2', copy=1 on both for cis; or VCF records sharing a PS with phased GT) is applied to one VariantHaplotype per copy: cis members edit the same copy, trans members the other, each copy's haplotype gets its own edits via the existing allele-application path plus the sample's SNPs (or M11's phased templates). One suppression pass over the union footprint at per-copy rates, one tiling pass per copy (reusing the two-haplotype machinery used for v>0.5). Truth writes phased GT (0|1, 1|0) with PS plus SIM_GROUP; README says which sample copy was used. 'Copy' is defined within the phase block holding the sites; refuse or mark 'phase unknown' when sites span blocks no gVCF PS links. A later per-chromosome ref_range fix opens multi-chromosome groups (CR6-A).
ideas.simplest_version: SNV-only groups (equal-length edits, no coordinate shifts), two or more on one chromosome inside one union footprint, explicit cis/trans, each member het (VAF 0.5) or 1.0; copy 1 and copy 2 each fully remade from their own haplotype; no SVs in groups.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real yardstick (R13): HG002's Q100-phased het SNV pairs 100-400 bp apart on the hospital BAM - among ALT-carrying fragments covering both sites, the share carrying both ALTs (real cis ~1, real trans ~error rate). Plant 30 cis and 30 trans pairs at the same distances at Q100-reference positions: spiked co-carry rates inside the real cis and trans distributions; kill if cis co-carry <95% of real or trans >2x real. Concrete LDLR check (R40): two ClinVar P/LP SNVs in LDLR exon 4 (chr19:11105220-11105600) on 35x HG002: in trans <=1% of covering fragments carry both ALTs, in cis >=95% of ALT-carrying covering fragments carry both; each site's AF inside validate allele_freq's 99% band at 0.5; union depth within +-10% of unspiked (or binomial noise). Today's --allow-overlap must fail (0% cis, ALT share ~0.33 when coins match, 1+v depth). Downstream, the M48 scorer should show DeepVariant calling both 0/1 and genmod listing them as compounds.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 h: pysam script over Q100 phased het pairs in the hospital HG002 BAM for real cis/trans co-carry rates. 1-2 h: run today's --allow-overlap on the two exon-4 SNVs (or two SNVs 300 bp apart) with the release binary plus align.sh, measuring per-site AF, depth and fragments carrying both ALTs - the broken baseline.
ideas.impact: Compound-het, homozygous-FH and AR demos reach genmod's compound models; cis/trans teaching cases; benchmarkers can test phasing and compound-het logic. CR1 prerequisite; unblocks CR6-A (balanced translocation) and complex SVs.
ideas.risks: Phase across unlinked blocks cannot be observed in short reads, so truth phase is defined only within a block. Groups with indels shift coordinates. Union footprints mixing SVs and small variants complicate tiling counts and magnify CR3 (M11). raredisease does not read-phase by default (inferred: no phasing step in outputs), so cis/trans matters mostly for trio inheritance logic. Changes truth output for grouped runs only.
ideas.history_check: Grouped-event composition OPEN since the Codex review (CR1; CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:297-301, 490-505; REVIEW.md:2930-2939); the CR1 7 kb refusal gate is DONE; the outputs map lists compound hets in LDLR as open. Never built or refuted. M16 (hap=) covers the cheap >=7 kb case; this covers close pairs.

ideas.title: Haplotype-addressed events (hap=1|2): chosen cis/trans across a gene, reproducible copy choice, phased truth GT
ideas.problem: Which copy carries an event is a coin per phase block, flipped separately for every event, even when --gvcf supplies phase; truth GT is unphased. A compound het in trans (FH in LDLR, any AR gene) cannot be requested - it comes out trans or cis by chance; inherited/de novo patterns across a family cannot be built consistently; a new seed moves the event to the other copy.
ideas.evidence: CODE: pick_target_alleles flips rng.gen::<bool>() per block (src/loh.rs:924-941, coin at :937); gVCF orientation parsed (src/loh.rs:566-583) but used only as GVCF_LINK votes (src/loh.rs:874-883), never to choose a copy; truth writes '/' (src/truth.rs:468-474). MEASURED: LDLR has 101 of 153 exon pairs >=7 kb apart (data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed), so most exon-pair compound hets are allowed today but land in trans with probability 1/2 (inferred). Platinum NA12878 v1.2 truth phased (first 200k records: 0 unphased het). raredisease samplesheets have paternal_id/maternal_id columns, and the hospital ran raredisease on 7 CEPH-1463 members (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_fix-gatk-cnv/Seq25-160*/samplesheet.csv). DOCUMENTED: 'the seed-2 replant changed copy choice too' (memory validation-plan.md, Astra point b). LANDSCAPE: VISOR places each variant on a named haplotype.
ideas.proposal: Per-event hap=1|2, and honour VCF input GT 0|1 / 1|0. When the footprint holds a phased --gvcf SNP, take the haplotype carrying the GT's first allele (hap=1) or second (hap=2) instead of the coin; refuse hap= when the block has no phased anchor. Write phased GT with PS (gVCF PS) to truth.vcf; always log the chosen copy, coin events included. Family use: run once per member with the same event and the transmitted haplotype from a pedigree-phased VCF; a de novo is the child alone (full trio tool in M17).
ideas.simplest_version: hap= only together with a --gvcf whose GT is phased: replace the coin for blocks containing a phased SNP and write a '|' GT. Without hap=, the coin path and RNG draw order stay byte-identical.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On the hospital HG001 BAM with the Platinum v1.2.1 phased VCF as --gvcf, plant 20 het SNV pairs >=7 kb apart, 10 requested cis and 10 trans. For each planted ALT-carrying fragment read its alleles at truth-phased het SNPs on the same fragment: the share matching the requested haplotype must be within 2 points of the real rate for all 40 events. Measure the real rate first (share of real HG001 fragments at real het SNVs whose linked SNP alleles agree with Platinum phase, expected ~98-99%). The coin build puts about half the events on the wrong haplotype (near-0% agreement for those) and fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Minutes to hours: measure the real agreement rate on 200 HG001 het SNVs with pysam/samtools (whatshap installed at ~/.pixi/bin); run the existing binary with --seed 1 and --seed 2 at one event with the Platinum --gvcf and confirm from reads that the copy flips with the seed.
ideas.impact: Compound-het demos (LDLR FH, AR genes) get the right phase for genmod's compound model; trio demos (inherited vs de novo) become possible on the CEPH family the hospital already runs; copy choice reproducible and recorded. Variant stays in real reads, which VISOR's named haplotypes do not offer.
ideas.risks: Platinum phase may not be parent-of-origin ordered (check hap1 = paternal before trio claims; parents' truths needed for inherited spikes). Blocks phased from short reads only cannot be anchored. The 7 kb rule still blocks close pairs (M15). PS semantics differ between gVCF producers. gVCF must belong to the BAM's sample (M30).
ideas.history_check: Random, unrecorded cis/trans is in the map (inferred, confirmed in code by Astra point b). Grouped composition (CR1, M15) and trio spiking (M17) are OPEN. Nothing refuted. This is the cheap subset needing no composition, covering every pair >=7 kb apart.

ideas.title: Trio-consistent spiking: inherited variants on the transmitted haplotype, de novo in the child only
ideas.problem: spike takes one BAM (src/main.rs:47) and picks the event copy by a coin per phase block (src/loh.rs:924-949). Spiking a family member by member cannot put an inherited variant on the haplotype the child actually received from the carrier parent, and a de novo needs child-only spiking. raredisease is pedigree-aware (genmod inheritance models, UPD, peddy use trios; external knowledge; pedigree/ and peddy/ outputs on disk).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: hospital raredisease_results holds pedigree/ and peddy/ folders (single-sample run here). DOCUMENTED: cnv_validation config/samples.ped lists the CEPH-1463 family sequenced at the hospital (NA12877 father, NA12879/81/82/85, HG001 = NA12878); those BAMs are index-only on this machine (memory validation-plan.md). Code: single --bam, one coin per block. INFERRED: independent runs put the child's allele on a random haplotype, so it co-segregates with the carrier parent's linked SNPs only ~50% of the time. Related measured: the family samples are 7-lane (M39).
ideas.proposal: spike trio --parent1 --parent2 --child: phase the child's het SNPs by transmission (Mendelian); for an inherited event choose the parental haplotype (explicit or coin) and the child's copy inherited from it, spike both using M11's copy templates / M16's hap= addressing; a de novo goes to the child only. Write a truth per sample plus a PED-aware summary.
ideas.simplest_version: Inherited small variants only, one carrier parent, transmission phase from the three BAMs' het SNPs inside the footprint (equivalently: M16's hap= run once per member with a pedigree-phased VCF).
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real yardstick on CEPH trio NA12877/NA12878 -> NA12879 at the hospital: real transmitted het variants co-segregate with linked het SNPs within one fragment in ~100% of phase-informative fragments. Spiked inherited variants in the child must sit in cis with the transmitting parent's alleles in >=95% of phase-informative fragments; independent runs (today, ~50%) must fail. De novo spikes must show 0 alt reads in both parents, and genmod must classify >=90% as designed.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: At the hospital: for 50 Platinum-truth transmitted het SNVs, count phase-informative fragments in NA12879 to fix the real co-segregation rate (pysam, hours).
ideas.impact: Realistic family demos for raredisease's trio analysis: inheritance filters, de novo, compound hets across parents.
ideas.risks: Data exist only at the hospital. Short reads rarely cover both the variant and a linked SNP within one fragment. Depends on M11 and M15/M16; three BAMs triple run time; family samples are multi-lane (M39).
ideas.history_check: Map lists trio-consistent spiking under new event types (inferred, unverified). Never built or refuted. M16 provides the cheap per-member path.

ideas.title: Repeat-expansion (STR) events with the real motif and in-repeat read pairs, judged by ExpansionHunter against real HG001/HG002 alleles
ideas.problem: There is no STR/expansion event type (no such spec in src/exon.rs or src/main.rs). An expansion can only be an INS with explicit bases (src/exon.rs:554-600); a length-only ins draws random bases (src/main.rs:2017-2024). Fragments lying wholly inside inserted sequence are never drawn and their starts are subtracted from the count (src/simulate.rs:801-817; ref_overlapping_start_intervals skips novel segments, :888-946). Pathogenic expansions longer than a fragment (FMR1 >=200 CGG = 600 bp, C9orf72, DMPK, RFC1, ATXNs, HTT) therefore lack the in-repeat read pairs (IRRs) ExpansionHunter uses to size long alleles. The event copy's own repeat allele is rewritten to reference length plus the insertion (CR3), and truth carries no repeat unit or count. raredisease runs EH + stranger; spike cannot produce that result class.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R14, R55) on hospital raredisease_results/repeat_expansions (EH VCF of 66 loci + stranger VCF): HG001 and HG002 differ at ~40 of 66 loci (42 of 60 autosomal records); 8 have an INREPEAT allele in at least one sample. Q100 HG002 carries a 520 bp AAAAG insertion at RFC1 chr4:39348424 (hap 1); EH calls HG002 RFC1 13/51 (CI 43-85; ADSP 13/0, ADFL 20/23, ADIR 0/9), HG001 9/13 SPANNING. In EH's evidence BAM all 9 in-repeat reads at RFC1 have an anchored mate on chr4, and bwa-mem2 placed the in-repeat read itself at chr2:162,752,903 (another AAAAG array); 0 pure in-repeat reads at the locus in the main BAM (scratchpad cr3probe/rfc1_irr.py). EH also calls HG002 RAPGEF2_TTTTA_3P 7/158 (CI 48-230, ADIR 13) where Q100 has only a 16 bp insertion (off-target noise in EH's long-allele calls). HG001 SAMD12_TTTTA_3P 1/76 (ADIR 7; reference 12 units). Hospital chr20 proper pairs: mean |TLEN| 388, 52.3% <=380 bp, 15.8% <=255 bp, so most IRR fragments for a 76-unit TAAAA allele would lie wholly in inserted sequence and be excluded (inferred). DOCUMENTED: EH/stranger path in raredisease (cnv_validation config/config.yaml:177); Platinum v1.2 NA12878 TR truth on disk (413,558 TR sites). LANDSCAPE: VISOR simulates TR expansions only in synthetic reads; no tool found that plants them into a real sample's reads (inferred from search).
ideas.proposal: A str: event (a catalog locus, or str:CHR:START-END:UNIT:COUNT[;af=..][;hap=..]) that replaces one copy's repeat interval with UNIT x COUNT (absolute count; pure or keeping the reference's interruption pattern) on a chosen copy (M11/M16). For this event type admit fragment starts wholly inside novel repeat sequence at the same density, with the count taken over all starts so in-repeat depth equals local depth; placement of in-repeat pairs (MAPQ 0 elsewhere, or unmapped) is left to the real aligner, as in reality (FASTQ/realign route). Truth carries SIM_RU and SIM_REPCN plus the sequence ALT; the run README states the expected EH genotype.
ideas.simplest_version: No new spec: for an explicit ins: whose sequence is a pure repeat of the reference unit at that position (str:chr:pos:MOTIF:N becomes an INS of MOTIF x N at the tract end), drop the novel-only start exclusion for that event (include novel-only starts in tiling and in the count) and write SIM_RU/SIM_REPCN.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Transplant at EH catalog loci with the hospital aligner command and EH version/catalog. (1) RFC1: transplant Q100 HG002's 520 bp AAAAG allele into HG001 (EH 9/13): EH on spiked HG001 must call a long allele whose CI overlaps HG002's real 43-85, ADIR within Poisson noise of 9, ADFL within noise of 20/23, in-repeat mates placed off-locus as in real. (2) Spanning loci where HG001/HG002 differ (e.g. HTT 16/18 vs 17/24, ATXN2 23/24 vs 23/31), planted af=hom: EH REPCN within REPCI of the planted count at least as often as EH agrees with the TR truth on real samples (measure first). (3) Long alleles: ADIR within the real spread (HG001 SAMD12 76 units gives ADIR 7). Broken versions must fail: random sequence of the same length, in-repeat reads not realigned, or today's build without novel-only starts (predicted ADIR ~0). KILL if today's ins: already gives real-like ADIR. Expansions longer than a fragment have no real carrier on disk: judge only against EH's own consistency (labelled as such) until a public carrier WGS (e.g. Coriell FMR1/C9orf72) is used.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No code, hours: (a) with the existing binary plant ins: of 64 x TAAAA at SAMD12_TTTTA_3P (chr8:118,366,817) into HG002 af=hom (BAM route), count reads >=90% TAAAA in sim.bam vs real HG001 at that locus (76 units); (b) run today's spike with the Q100 RFC1 record (explicit sequence, --vcf) into HG001 over RFC1 +-10 kb, align with -M -K, run EH from a biocontainer with that catalog entry. If 520 bp already matches real, remaining work is only the longer-than-a-fragment half and the spec.
ideas.impact: The hospital can demo repeat-expansion disorders (FMR1, HTT, C9orf72, ATXNs, RFC1, DMPK) through the EH/stranger path with planted lengths - a result class spike cannot make today; the real HG001/HG002 EH calls on disk give a yardstick without new sequencing. EH callers get a benchmark.
ideas.risks: EH's in-repeat recovery depends on its catalog's off-target regions and where bwa places pure-repeat reads (realistic only in realign/FASTQ route). GC-extreme repeats (CGG, GGGGCC) show depth dropout and quality collapse a model learned on ordinary DNA will not reproduce; uniform tiling would over-cover them. Real expansions are somatically unstable (EH sees a length spread). RF15 may apply to unit-repeat inserts. Kb-scale expansions inflate fragment counts. FMR1 on male X needs M12. CR3 (M11) and the 7 kb rule apply.
ideas.history_check: Never proposed in spike (grep finds no ExpansionHunter in docs/ or README). CR5 (REVIEW.md:3119-3131) only made placement honour the existing exclusion. Map lists STR expansions unsupported, the novel-only exclusion as an inferred limitation (README:1872), and 'realistic insertion content' (naming STR/VNTR unit repeats with an EH falsifier) as OPEN. RF15 (short INS too clean) is a different size class. Never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial mode: copy-less heteroplasmy SNVs and mtDNA deletions, judged against a real HG001/HG002 mito mixture
ideas.problem: spike has no chrM handling (chrM appears in src/ only in a loh test). chrM is circular, so pairs spanning 16569->1 are improper and a linear haplotype cannot make them. It is multi-copy (heteroplasmy, not diploid copies), at thousands-x depth; the pileup's 20-80% thresholds (src/loh.rs:87-121) would call heteroplasmies 'het' and phase them with a coin; copy_rate assumes two copies; truth writes 0/1 or 1/1 instead of a heteroplasmy level; the 7 kb footprint rule allows ~2 events on a 16.5 kb genome. Whether today's clean mode gives Mutect2-MT and eKLIPse the same evidence as real heteroplasmy is untested, though the hospital pipeline runs them.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: hospital raredisease_results holds call_snv/mitochondria (Mutect2 FilterMutectCalls on a liftunlift reference), call_sv/mitochondria (eKLIPse, 0 deletions for HG002) and haplocheck (HG002 coverage 5895, haplogroup H5a7). chrM read density vs autosomes 321x (HG002 hospital), 479x (HG001), 562x (HG002 35x); hospital HG002 chrM 1,305,882 mapped reads (~10,000x). Within 300 bp of either chrM end 33% of reads are not proper pairs (chrM:1-300 0.331, 16300-16569 0.336) vs 0.8-0.9% mid-chrM (64-66% proper at the ends); MAPQ<20 0-5%. Mutect2-MT: 8 homoplasmic (AF>0.9) SNVs only in HG001, 6 only in HG002 (e.g. 2259C>T, 4745A>G, 7337G>A, 13326T>C); HG002 MT VCF has 50 records AF 0.0009-1 (e.g. 6210 T>C at 0.085 PASS) and no 20-80% heteroplasmic SNV, so pileup het phasing does not fire there. ClinVar has 187 P/LP MT records. params.yaml skip_mt_annotation: true (MT calls not ranked at the hospital today). Spike run (R43, scratchpad robust/chrm): snp:chrM:3243:A:G;af=0.3 realised 5073/(5073+3+12334)=0.291 by exact 25-mer count, but 52 s wall, 2.64 GB RSS (938,703-pair pool, cov 29,056), GT 0/1. INFERRED: with no het SNP copy_rate(None, v) = v already gives heteroplasmy semantics.
ideas.proposal: (1) Validate today's behaviour first against a real mixture. (2) chrM mode: copy always unknown (every fragment removed at v, no pileup phasing or coin), af means heteroplasmy, truth records SIM_VAF as heteroplasmy with GT as Mutect2 writes it; subsample the pool to a cap given ~10,000x; several events per chrM via grouped composition (M15) or a relaxed footprint rule. (3) Circular-aware haplotype that wraps the flank across the origin so synthetic pairs span 16569->1; until then refuse/warn within one fragment of the junction. (4) mtDNA deletion presets at real direct-repeat breakpoints (common 4,977 bp m.8470-13447) at heteroplasmy levels for eKLIPse.
ideas.simplest_version: No code first: run today's spike on single chrM SNVs at af 0.05 and 0.2 into HG002 and compare with the real mixture; then the minimal mode: force copy=unknown and skip phasing on chrM, document af as heteroplasmy, warn for events within 500 bp of either chrM end.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real mixture (R16): HG001 chrM reads at f=0.05 and 0.2 (name-hash subsample) merged with HG002 chrM reads at 1-f; at the 8 HG001-only homoplasmic sites this is real heteroplasmy at f. Spike the same 8 SNVs at af=f into HG002 (several runs given the 7 kb rule), run the hospital's Mutect2 mitochondria steps on both: per-site AF and call/FILTER status agree within the real mixture's split-half noise; Mutect2 AF within the binomial 99% interval of the planted level; FILTER/strand flags at the rate of real heteroplasmies of similar AF (e.g. HG002 6210 T>C at 0.085 PASS). Broken versions must fail: af doubled by a diploid copy_rate, unknown-copy suppression off; and plant next to a real 20-80% heteroplasmy (if one exists in the on-disk MT VCFs, e.g. CEPH samples) where diploid copy logic should distort the level. Kill if spike's AF error at f=0.05 exceeds the real split-half noise at >=3 of 8 sites; if today's binary already passes everything, documentation only. eKLIPse deletion levels (no real carrier on disk) are checked against eKLIPse only (+-5 points), labelled as such.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Minutes: samtools view -s on chrM of both hospital BAMs to build the mixture, pileup at the 8 sites. Minutes: one spike run of chrM:7337G>A at af=0.1 into HG002 for SIM_RESIST, pool size, memory and realised AF. Hours: GATK Mutect2 --mitochondria-mode on chrM of the merged region (GATK via pixi/docker) vs real low-level calls.
ideas.impact: Mito disease demos (MELAS m.3243A>G, LHON, KSS single large deletions) through the hospital's MT path (low until MT annotation is enabled). Gives nearly for free a low-VAF realism yardstick at very high depth (concept test 2, 'mixture', open in validation-plan memory).
ideas.risks: NUMT reads and the liftunlift/shifted-reference realignment differ by route; raredisease subsamples MT reads (mt_subsample_rd 150) for eKLIPse; haplocheck flags contamination for multi-site mixtures (use single sites for pathogenic demos); whole-chrM pool at ~10,000x is large (measured 2.64 GB, 52 s); quality model learned on nuclear DNA; 7 kb rule limits events per run; demo value depends on skip_mt_annotation.
ideas.history_check: Never examined: mito appears in docs only as a read-name pairing note (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-read-names.md:139) and one chrM mate in the duplicates plan; not in the map. The mixture test is open in memory validation-plan.md. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: SMN1/SMN2 paralog copy-number events for SMNCopyNumberCaller (SMA demos), as the first real-data test of --edit-model origin
ideas.problem: SMN1 sits in a near-identical segmental duplication with SMN2. Clean mode edits only MAPQ>=20 pool reads, so an SMN1 deletion is refused by RF8, or under --allow-resistant leaves most reads unedited. raredisease runs SMNCopyNumberCaller as a dedicated step and SMA is among the most requested rare-disease results, but spike cannot plant SMN1 copy-number changes.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (hospital HG002 BAM, samtools view -F 0xF04): SMN1 chr5:70,924,941-70,953,012 holds 6,733 primary non-dup reads, 14.4% MAPQ>=20, 84.4% MAPQ 0; SMN2 (chr5:70,049,669-70,077,595) 16.5%/82.2%; SMN1 exon 7-8 end (chr5:70,946,000-70,953,012) 39.8% MAPQ>=20; LDLR 99.6%. At c.840 (chr5:70,951,946 C in SMN1; chr5:70,076,526 T in SMN2; checked with samtools faidx) 32/32 reads at SMN1 carry C and 30/30 at SMN2 carry T, all MAPQ>=20 (mpileup -q 20): reads covering a paralog-specific base are placed by sequence. raredisease SMNCopyNumberCaller (smncopynumbercaller/out/*.json): HG002 SMN1 2, SMN2 2, Total_CN_raw 3.838, Coverage_MAD 0.076; HG001 2/2, 3.898; HG002 per-site SMN1_CN_raw 1.73-2.51. INFERRED: SIM_RESIST ~0.86 over SMN1, above RF8's 0.5. DOCUMENTED: origin validated only in the exact-twin, one-XA regime and untested on real data (memory edit-model-origin.md).
ideas.proposal: An SMN recipe on top of --edit-model origin: (a) SMN1 deletion (het/hom) = DEL over SMN1 with origin removal by placement chance at SMN1 and its XA look-alike SMN2; make origin sequence-informed (a read carrying an SMN1 paralog-specific base assigned to SMN1 with p~1, an SMN2 base to SMN2, others split by XA as today). (b) SMN1-to-SMN2 gene conversion = SMN1 paralog bases on one copy rewritten to SMN2's as one grouped edit. Truth carries SMN1/SMN2 CN.
ideas.simplest_version: No code: a het and a hom SMN1 whole-gene DEL with today's --edit-model origin --allow-resistant, scored with SMNCopyNumberCaller; reads at paralog bases already sit at their true locus with MAPQ>=20, so today's MAPQ/XA model may already be right.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: SMNCopyNumberCaller (raredisease version) on spiked HG002: het SMN1 DEL gives SMN1 CN 1, SMN2 CN 2, Total_CN_raw ~2.9 (+-0.2; real Coverage_MAD 0.07-0.08); hom DEL gives SMN1 0 and isSMA True; per-site SMN1_CN_raw within the real per-site spread (HG002 1.73-2.51 at CN2). Real-carrier yardstick: per-site SMN1 fractions and Total_CN_raw of public 1000G NYGC 30x CRAMs of known SMN1 CN1 carriers (Chen et al. 2020) fetched as region slices. Clean with --allow-resistant (edits ~14% of reads, Total_CN_raw ~3.7, SMN1 2) must fail. KILL the sequence-informed refinement if plain origin already passes.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours: install smncopynumbercaller (bioconda) in a scratch env and run it on the hospital HG002 BAM (reads only SMN and normalisation regions by index); run the existing binary in origin mode for a het SMN1 DEL, merge only touched regions, re-run the caller. Count SMN-region MAPQ-0 reads carrying XA (origin needs it).
ideas.impact: SMA diagnosis and carrier demos (SMN1 0 or 1 copies) through the pipeline's dedicated caller; gives --edit-model origin the real-data test the map says it lacks, in exactly its twin regime. No landscape simulator (BAMSurgeon, VISOR, NEAT) handles paralog-specific copy number in real reads (inferred).
ideas.risks: Origin's look-alike half has been inert in practice (R4 kept 25 of 52 and removed 0 at RF14 look-alikes). bwa's random MAPQ-0 placement between SMN1/SMN2. SMN2 delta7-8 and the SMN1 2+0 silent-carrier haplotype. Caller's normalisation regions must stay untouched. No real SMA carrier reads on disk (public 1000G only). Clinical stakes of a wrong demo.
ideas.history_check: SMN never attempted (no hit in repo docs). Origin: physics SUPPORTED only for exact twins; a real-GIAB origin test with its own locked plan is OPEN (REVIEW.md:6390-6393). RF8's suggestion to lower --min-mapq is flagged as probably wrong in segdups (map). Not refuted.

ideas.title: Coverage-preserving edit: remap each event-copy donor fragment through the haplotype instead of uniform re-tiling (P1)
ideas.problem: Non-additive events suppress every event-copy pool pair inside event +-2 kb and tile n = cov*v*starts/f fragments at uniform starts scaled by one anchor depth. The footprint's local depth shape, duplicates, real quality strings and background indels are discarded, and work and the removal list grow with the footprint instead of with the changed bases.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R19; scratchpad perf/dup1; current-master binary quality-speed-run/bin/spike-new; 35x HG002, dup:chr20:14550000-15550000, seed 1, 1 thread): 63,390 pairs suppressed, 120,046 tiled, 72,263 listed for removal from the raw FASTQ (8,873 duplicates), SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 4.69 (bin chr20:14862000-14863000 at 9.9x vs 50.3x scaling depth); only 17 of 120,046 tiled pairs show the junction (SIM_ALT_FRAGS=17). DOCUMENTED: CR2 probe read 81.09x where 28.13x was expected; 40 chr20 DUPs had folds 1.11-2.46 (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md CR2; README.md:1858-1866). INFERRED (simulate.rs:817, HAP_FLANK 2000, 421 bp mean fragment): ~88% of an SNV's remade pairs never touch the site. Code: suppression simulate.rs:249-264, uniform starts :1062-1065, one anchor depth :266-280. Primitive exists: the legacy junction model makes one depth copy per original inside the DUP with +-20 bp jitter and a new length (synth.rs:418-510, jitter :434-436).
ideas.proposal: Replace uniform re-tiling for non-additive events with an exact image map from reference fragments to haplotype fragments. Each pool pair is drawn for the event copy with today's copy_rate coin; then (a) if its fragment overlaps no changed base or junction, leave the original untouched (not removed, not rewritten); (b) if it crosses a changed span, remove it and emit one synthetic pair at its image start on the haplotype with its own fragment length (DEL: starts inside [S,E) vanish, starts left of S extend across the join; INV/INS/SNV: only boundary-crossing fragments remade); (c) for sequence appearing twice (DUP) emit one extra fragment per event-copy original with a fresh nearby start and new length (generate_depth_pair's jitter) so Picard sees no positional duplicates; (d) for novel sequence longer than a fragment draw interior fragments at the local start density measured from pool starts beside the insertion point; (e) optionally give each remade pair its original's duplicate-family size. Per base, depth = donor depth x (1 - v + v*copies) by construction; cov, the floor of 2 (except novel interiors) and SIM_DEPTH_FOLD become unnecessary; work and removal lists scale with fragments over the change (a DUP removes only ~cov*v pairs crossing the first copy's end).
ideas.simplest_version: DUP only: full-model DUPs keep every original and add the legacy depth copies (synth.rs:454) for the interior; only event-copy pairs crossing E are replaced, with haplotype pairs at their own start and length; other event types unchanged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x HG002 after align.sh and merge.sh: (1) CR2 dup_variable probe interior reads 28.13x +-5% (today 81.09x). (2) On the 40 seeded chr20 DUPs and chr20:14.55-15.55 Mb, in >=95% of 1 kb bins with >=95% reads MAPQ>=20 the merged/donor depth ratio lies inside the Poisson 99% band around 1+v (uniform tiling fails where fold is 4.69). (3) Sham (v=0) leaves merged.bam records identical to input. (4) Transplant rounds 1b, 2b, 3 keep every supported verdict. (5) Picard duplicate share in the footprint within the 95% CI of the unspiked rate. Kill if (1), (2) or (4) fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: No build: run the existing binary with --dup-model junction (interior = per-original depth copies) and --dup-model full on the 1 Mb chr20 DUP and the CR2 dup_variable probe; align both; per-1 kb-bin output/donor depth inside the DUP with samtools depth. If junction-mode interiors track 1+v bin by bin while full mode shows the 4.69 fold, the principle holds on real reads; if junction mode is off too, the cause is alignment/mappability and the idea dies for DUPs.
ideas.impact: CNV callers (gCNV, CNVnator, TIDDIT coverage) see the donor's own depth shape times copy number instead of a flat anchor depth. Outside remade fragments, flank indels, duplicates and real qualities survive, covering most of CR3's +-2 kb exposure for SNVs. Far fewer synthetic reads to align, much shorter removal lists for the FASTQ route; a DUP becomes nearly append-only.
ideas.risks: Copy assignment still uses the same phase coin, so CR3 remains inside remade fragments (M11). Resistant reads (CR4) unchanged. A jittered DUP copy can hit a real fragment's 5' ends by chance. Output bytes change for every non-additive event, so transplant rounds must be re-run (M44). Novel-interior density for long INS needs an estimate.
ideas.history_check: Never tried. Map lists it as OPEN P1 (event-model reader) and 'Replace-in-place tiling ... never proposed or refuted' (synthesis reader). CR2 option A (learned start intensity) never built; option B (SIM_DEPTH_FOLD, measure only) done. T3's mappability attribution was retracted (judgment-gate-cases.md 2026-09-26), hence mappable bins only in the falsifier. Design notes advise against the legacy junction model only because its junction reads are additive (CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:303). Sibling: M10 (P1b in-read edits for SNVs).

ideas.title: merge.sh: stream the original through samtools view -N ^list into samtools merge --write-index, with no outside.bam and no full re-sort
ideas.problem: merge.sh makes five full passes over a whole-genome BAM. The biggest runs on one thread: view -N list -U outside.bam compresses the 37 GB outside.bam single-threaded; then a merge, a full re-sort of already-sorted data, a single-threaded index and a single-threaded view -c for a log line. Temp files reach 3-4x the BAM on a disk that is 88% full.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R20): B1 merge.sh took 1 h 42 min (sim.bam 22:14:03, merge.log 23:56:10) on a 37,083,621,094-byte BAM with 741,918,308 records (/home/parlar_ai/sv_slice_test/data/B1, logs/run.log). On a real slice (scratchpad perf/bam; 35x HG002 chr20:10-30 Mb, 387 MB, 6,765,353 records, 1,496 names) at 16 threads: view -N -U 36.77 s, merge 3.82 s, sort 4.92 s, index 2.17 s, view -c 2.10 s, total 49.8 s; scaled x96-110 that is 80-91 min, consistent with B1. Adding -@16 to the view does NOT help (34.80 s): samtools 1.23 threads only -o output, not -U (view -@16 -b -o /dev/null 2.33 s vs 35.76 s one thread). Replacement: guard view -@16 -c -N list (0.92 s) plus view -@16 -u -N ^list | merge -@16 --write-index -o merged.bam##idx##merged.bam.bai sim.bam - took 4.04-4.25 s with the same records in the same order (md5 c809e24a for today's merge+sort, merge alone and the stream; RG stripped only because the stand-in sim.bam shared the input's RG ID); wrote a BAI directly. Code: src/main.rs:2516, 2538, 2542, 2543, 2546. df: /home 88% full.
ideas.proposal: Generate merge.sh as three steps: (1) guard ACTUAL=$(samtools view -@T -c [-T REF] -N replaced_reads.txt ORIGINAL), abort if ACTUAL < NAMES (today's rule); (2) samtools view -@T -u [-T REF] -N ^replaced_reads.txt ORIGINAL | samtools merge -@T --write-index -o 'merged.bam##idx##merged.bam.bai' sim.bam -; (3) report the total from samtools idxstats, not a full view -c. Write under a temp name and mv on success. Check samtools supports -N ^ (fall back to today's path or say so on older versions). CRAM input writes CRAM against the same reference. Later: BGZF-level splice copying untouched blocks verbatim (measure the stream first).
ideas.simplest_version: Two edits to the generated script: replace view, merge and sort with the -N ^ pipe into merge --write-index, and replace the final view -c with idxstats.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: B1 inputs (37 GB D24-14230 resample BAM, B1 sim.bam and replaced_reads.txt): (1) samtools view of the new merged.bam md5-matches today's merged.bam record for record in order; headers equal apart from @PG. (2) The guard still aborts when ORIGINAL is another BAM (35x HG002). (3) Manta opens merged.bam with its BAI. (4) Wall time <=20 min at 16 threads. Broken builds fail: selection inverted (-N without ^) fails md5 and record count; no guard accepts the wrong BAM. Kill if md5 differs or time >30 min.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done on the 387 MB slice (49.8 s -> 4.0-4.25 s, same record stream). Next (hours): today's and new merge.sh on the 2.7 GB HG002 chr20 BAM with a real spike run's sim.bam (RG 'sim', no collision), compare md5 and time; then one B1-size run.
ideas.impact: Full-BAM SV-caller route drops from ~2 h 55 min per event to roughly Manta's 72 min + ~8 min merge (inferred x96-110) - the user's open choice between a locked fast route and the full route (memory sv-caller-slices.md). Peak disk ~3-4x -> ~1x the BAM. Every spike -> merged.bam loop (validate_pipeline.sh, slice and real_events loops, M43's BAM builds) gains in proportion.
ideas.risks: -N ^FILE needs recent samtools (present in 1.23; minimum version unchecked; hospital container may be older). merge renames colliding @RG/@PG IDs exactly as today. Without ##idx## suffix --write-index writes CSI (some callers want BAI). Tie order at one position must be re-checked on B1 (identical on the slice).
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map ('add -@ to view -N; count with view -c; drop the full re-sort; write the index during the merge'); sv-caller-slices note lists 'a faster spiked-BAM build' as untested. This session corrects that plan: -@ alone gains nothing because -U is unthreaded; inverting the selection makes the pass parallel. Never built or refuted. Related: realigning kept originals costs ~0 (B1 align.log 0.30 s compute vs 43 s index loading for 5,326 reads).

ideas.title: Whole-sample FASTQ: filter the two mates in parallel keeping the per-record pairing check, then optionally splice natively with BGZF block copy
ideas.problem: fastq.sh sends both mates through one gawk process, reading R2 with getline from a FIFO, capping throughput at ~165k pairs/s; with THREADS <=8, pigz -6 on THREADS/2 per mate is close to a second bottleneck. Every raw record is decompressed, parsed in awk and recompressed although only hundreds to tens of thousands of ~380 M pairs change.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R21; scratchpad perf/fq, perf/run): 2,000,000 real HG002 NovaSeq pairs (head of HG002.novaseq.chr20.R1/R2.fastq.gz), 2,999 removed names, B1-generated fastq.sh: 11.95 s at THREADS 8, 12.22 s at 16 (~165k pairs/s); pigz -1 at 16 threads 12.24 s (awk is the cap; output 167 vs 137 MB); mawk 19.21 s (worse); one gawk per mate in parallel with pigz -p8 -6 each: 5.41 s with identical content (no cross-mate check yet). Components: pigz -dc 1.52 s per mate (691 MB); compression 10.22 s with pigz -p4 -6, 1.57 s with -p4 -1. GIAB raw 40x FASTQ is BGZF (first 8 MB: 651 blocks, 12,873 B compressed / 65,280 B uncompressed on average). DOCUMENTED: hospital sample is one pair of 380 M reads per mate, lengths 35-151; F3 predicted ~33 min (memory full-fastq.md). bwa infers insert size per batch (B1 align.log 'Inferring insert size distribution ... n: 5326'). Code: src/main.rs:2264 (ZIP threads), :2327 (getline from FIFO), :2412 (the one awk), :2424-2428 (append at end).
ideas.proposal: Stage 1 (shell, byte-identical): one filter per mate in parallel, each with its own decompressor and pigz -p THREADS/2; keep the per-record pairing guarantee by having each awk write its record names to a FIFO and cmp reading both FIFOs (any difference aborts); found/want and repeat counts checked per mate. Stage 2 (native, optional): spike does the splice itself (memchr record parsing, HashSet of removed names, one thread per mate with lock-step name check, noodles' multithreaded BGZF writer); for BGZF input copy verbatim every compressed block holding no removed record, re-encoding only blocks that do (plus a neighbour when a record spans a boundary). Optionally write each SPIKE_ pair in a removed original's slot instead of all at the end, so a big event does not fill whole bwa -K batches alone. (The raw-header identity pre-check is M37.)
ideas.simplest_version: Stage 1 only: two awks, two pigz processes, a cmp over the two name FIFOs, the same END checks as today.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Real raw FASTQ: HG002.novaseq.chr20.R1/R2 with a removal list from a spike run on the matching chr20 BAM, then the hospital pair. (1) Decompressed outputs byte-identical to today's fastq.sh for both mates. (2) Every refusal today's script makes reproduced: mates in different order, a listed name missing, a duplicated name, a truncated record, a raw FASTQ from another run. (3) Wall time at 16 threads falls >=2x for stage 1 and >=5x for stage 2. A version without the cross-mate check accepts a swapped-order pair and fails. Kill stage 2 if not >=2x faster than stage 1.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Add the cmp-over-FIFOs check to the per-mate script in the scratchpad and re-time the 2 M-pair test (today 12.22 s; 5.41 s without the check); run both on the full 0.85 GB chr20 raw pair. Before planning stage 2's block copy, check at the hospital whether the raw FASTQ starts with the BGZF 'BC' extra field (head -c 18 | xxd).
ideas.impact: Each hospital sample's spiked FASTQ drops from ~33-39 min to ~15-17 min with stage 1 (inferred from the measured 2.25x); stage 2 to a few minutes (inferred; decompression-bound ~1.5 s per 2 M-pair mate, or I/O-bound with block copy). Owner runs many samples. Slot interleaving removes the appended-batch question for big events.
ideas.risks: Per-mate filters must still give exactly today's refusals and atomic publish. Stage 2 changes compressed bytes (BGZF instead of pigz gzip), not content. Block copy works only on BGZF input. Interleaving changes record order (same multiset), so its alignment effect must be measured (see M46's order-sensitivity check) before it becomes default.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map: 'Optional: a native Rust fastq route with parallel compression, held to byte-identical decompressed output', 'Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ' (now M37) and 'Big events in the FASTQ route'. The one-awk design came from review finding 7 (mates in different orders, merged 658baa4), so stage 1 keeps a per-record check. F2 measured appended SPIKE_ reads harmless for a small event (1,296/1,296). New: compression level does not move wall time at 16 threads, mawk is slower, the GIAB raw FASTQ is BGZF.

ideas.title: Reuse the learned quality profile across runs on the same input (save and load), byte-identical
ideas.problem: Every run re-reads 20 blocks of 50 kb and re-learns the fqzcomp contexts and error tables, even for a single SNV. Since v2 this is the largest fixed cost of a small run.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R23; scratchpad perf/dup1/log.txt): 'Quality sample: 20 blocks ... 126228 pairs; read in 2.6 s, learned in 4.1 s', 7.0 s of a 19.21 s run at 1 thread on the 35x BAM. DOCUMENTED: K4 measured reads 0.3-2.8 s and learning 1.2-3.3 s (plan 2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md as summarised in the map); before v2 a 1 kb DEL took 0.55 s total (README.md:1354). Code: src/main.rs:659-664, src/quality.rs:476-506. Harnesses run spike many times per BAM: transplant.py spike_run loop (:243-266), the slice loop, the real_events loop. Master is now 4a5672d (quality-speed run-ratio table merged), not b901339 as the map says.
ideas.proposal: Serialise the learned profile to a versioned binary file (alphabet, class cuts, joint and class_run counts, both ContextMaps, error tables), keyed by spike version, canonical input path, size, mtime, index mtime, --min-mapq, read length and reference identity. --quality-profile FILE loads it when the key matches and refuses otherwise, or writes it when absent; learn's fill step recomputes the run-ratio table.
ideas.simplest_version: A --save-quality-profile / --quality-profile pair with a hand-written length-prefixed format and a strict key check; no automatic cache directory.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On 35x HG002 and hospital BAMs, three cases (35x dup+snp seed 1 threads 8; the K6 events; 35x del seed 7 threads 1): (1) every output md5-identical between a fresh run and a run loading the saved profile; (2) a profile saved at --min-mapq 20 refused at --min-mapq 0 and on another BAM (a build ignoring the key loads it and its md5 differs); (3) wall time drops by about the logged read+learn time. Kill on any md5 difference.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Sum the 'read in X s, learned in Y s' log lines over one transplant or slice campaign's spike logs to get the total time at stake; if under ~10 min per campaign, do not build.
ideas.impact: Removes 1.5-7 s from every run (most of a small event's run time); helps harness loops and repeated hospital runs on the same demo BAM; no output change.
ideas.risks: A stale profile could be reused silently if the key misses something (BAM rewritten in place with same size and mtime). Format must follow every change to the profile struct. Small gain for one-off runs.
ideas.history_check: Not proposed before. The startup sample replaced per-pool learning after v1 was refuted (bccc43a). The last speed step (run-ratio cache, merged 4a5672d) was also byte-identical. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Drop the pass-2 edge-strip and one-pass re-read plans; profile and fix the LOH pileup and duplicate scan instead
ideas.problem: Two open plans in the map target BAM re-reads (pass 2 re-reading the widened window; the ~6 reads of each region). Measured, re-reads are cheap; time sits in per-record work: the LOH pileup and phasing, and the clean-mode duplicate scan, which builds an OriginRecord with an owned name for every record before filtering.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R24; scratchpad perf/dup1/log.txt, 1 Mb DUP on 35x at 1 thread): pass 1 0.79 s, pass 2 0.30 s (1.6% of 19.21 s), census 0.44 s, LOH pileup 1.71 s + phasing 0.85 s, duplicate scan 2.07 s, FASTQ write 1.74 s. Plain htslib decoding of the same 1 Mb window (300,045 records) 0.14-0.21 s (samtools view -c, view > /dev/null): each extra read ~0.2-0.3 s, scans cost seconds. Code: src/origin.rs:1033-1054 (scan_long, then filter by duplicate flag or name), src/loh.rs:600-720 and :1036-1061, src/extract.rs:118-180 (pass 2). DOCUMENTED: on a 3 Mb event the duplicate re-read costs 5-6 s at 1 thread (README.md:1365).
ideas.proposal: Do not build pass-2 strips or a unified streaming pass. Run perf on the LOH pileup and duplicate scan on the 1 Mb and 3 Mb events and fix what dominates: in the duplicate scan test the flag bit and a name lookup on the raw record before building an owned record; in the LOH passes avoid per-base allocation and hashing (e.g. a dense Vec over the window instead of HashMaps). Keep byte identity.
ideas.simplest_version: In removed_duplicates, skip any record that is neither flagged duplicate nor named in removed, before allocating its name or decoding its CIGAR.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x HG002, 3 Mb DEL and DUP in clean mode at 1 and 4 threads: every output md5-identical to master, and the duplicate-scan step (log timestamps) falls by >=50%. If a perf profile shows decoding, not per-record work, dominates the scans, the idea is wrong and the one-pass plan comes back.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: One perf record of the 1 Mb DUP run at 1 thread (~20 s CPU) to see which functions dominate the LOH and duplicate-scan intervals.
ideas.impact: A few seconds per Mb at 1 thread off spike's own time for big events; mostly saves building two plans the measurement says cannot pay off.
ideas.risks: Small absolute gains; spike's own run time is far below merge.sh's (M22) and fastq.sh's (M23), so this ranks after them.
ideas.history_check: Map lists 'Pass 2 edge strips' and 'One streaming pass per event' as OPEN, both inferred; this measurement (pass 2 0.30 s; decoding 0.14-0.21 s per window) contradicts the inferred 'serial floor' for pass 2 at this size. Threads step 1 already chunked census and LOH passes (census.rs:138, loh.rs:640, :1061).

ideas.title: Bound peak memory: no whole-chromosome copies in the reference cache, and no clone of every kept pool pair
ideas.problem: SharedReference::load fetches each chromosome through ReferenceReader, whose FIFO cache stores a clone of every whole-chromosome fetch, so loading holds about two copies. Each event also clones every kept pool pair, and every event's outputs live until the end of the run.
ideas.evidence: Code: src/reference.rs:183-191 (cache.insert(key, seq.clone())) and :223-231 (one reader for the whole load loop); src/simulate.rs:262 (kept.push(pair.clone())); src/main.rs:666, :855, :913 (outputs held, then combined). MEASURED: MAXRSS 704 MB for the 1 Mb chr20 DUP at 1 thread (scratchpad perf/dup1); chrM SNV run 2.64 GB RSS (M19 evidence). DOCUMENTED: 3 Mb events peak at 1.2-2.5 GB (README.md:1356-1361). INFERRED: a genome-wide VCF panel loads ~3.1 GB of sequence and peaks near ~6 GB during the load.
ideas.proposal: In SharedReference::load fetch whole chromosomes without the FIFO cache, or move the sequence out instead of cloning. Keep kept originals as indices into the pool (or move pairs out) instead of cloning. Optionally write each event's SPIKE_ pairs to the FASTQ streams as soon as the event finishes (names unique per event).
ideas.simplest_version: Bypass the cache for whole-chromosome fetches in load (a one-line change), nothing else.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x HG002 with a VCF of one random SNV per autosome plus chrX: peak RSS (/usr/bin/time %M) falls by at least half the loaded reference size, and every output stays md5-identical. A build that drops the sequence too early fails to fetch or changes outputs.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Run the current binary on that 23-SNV VCF under /usr/bin/time and read the reference-load log line; if peak RSS minus loaded size is small, the cache copy is not the problem and only the pool clone is worth touching.
ideas.impact: Hospital panels across many chromosomes and multi-Mb events fit on smaller machines; no output change.
ideas.risks: Low; gain matters only for genome-wide panels or very large events.
ideas.history_check: Listed in the map as an OPEN, inferred limitation ('peak memory about 2x the loaded sequence'); never measured or changed.

ideas.title: Per-event (and per-fragment) random streams and stable event IDs: a panel run equals its single-event runs, and tiling can use every thread
ideas.problem: One StdRng seeded from --seed (main.rs:614) runs through every event in input order (haplotype building, suppression draws, tiling, origin's draw; main.rs:795, 807-822, 871); simulate.rs:259 draws only for replaceable pairs, so the stream also depends on the pool. The read-name prefix ev{:04} and truth ID sim_<type>_N come from the event index (simulate.rs:174); events are concatenated (--event then --vcf) and never sorted. Adding, removing or reordering one event rewrites every later event's reads, ALT counts, realised fractions, IDs and names, even tens of kb apart. Hospital panels are built iteratively (drop a refused event, add a gene), and each change forces a full fastq.sh + raredisease rerun and re-checking of confirmed variants. Tiling (simulate.rs:1018-1086) is serial and cannot be parallelised without changing bytes.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R39, scratchpad ord/): B = snp:chr19:11113291:C:A alone vs after A = snp:chr19:11100231:A:T (13 kb away, separate footprints): 0 of B's 276 SPIKE R1 records identical (sequence+quality), SIM_ALT_FRAGS 22 vs 19, ID sim_var_1 vs sim_var_2, names SPIKE_ev0001 vs SPIKE_ev0002. MEASURED (R49, scratchpad robust/order): B = del:chr20:44999900-45000100 seed 42 gives SIM_ALT_FRAGS 34 alone and 42 after A (del:chr19:11100000-11102000); only 11 of B-alone's 277 SPIKE_ R1 sequences appear in the A+B run. MEASURED (R22, scratchpad perf/dup1): tiling plus synthesis of 120,046 pairs took 3.52 s of a 19.21 s 1 Mb DUP run at 1 thread, serial at any --threads. DOCUMENTED: commit bccc43a 'K7 FAIL by rule (2 allele_freq flips from the reordered random stream)'; README.md:1354-1361 3 Mb DUP 44.3 s at 1 thread, 26.5 s at 16; scripts/transplant/transplant.py:243-266 re-runs remaining events after each RF8 refusal, so accepted events' reads change between attempts.
ideas.proposal: Stage 1: derive each event's StdRng from hash(seed, canonical event key: type, contig, coordinates, alleles, af, dup_model, occurrence index); its random insertion sequence (build_haplotype), suppression coin (optionally keyed per pool pair by hash of the pair name) and tiling draw from it; origin's joint removal draw gets its own stream keyed on (seed, family). Derive read-name prefix and truth ID from a short stable hash of the key or a user label (;id=LDLR_ex4), keeping sim_<type>_N for display; update validate's planted-read prefix mapping; truth keeps its positional sort. Stage 2: per-fragment streams from (event stream, fragment index) (e.g. StdRng::seed_from_u64(splitmix(seed ^ hash(spec) ^ index)) or ChaCha stream/word position), tile in parallel with rayon collecting in index order, and run independent events in parallel. Output independent of --threads; changes once relative to today.
ideas.simplest_version: Per-event StdRng seeded from FNV/splitmix(seed, canonical spec string), event index taken from sorted canonical keys rather than input order; names in today's format; each event's internal order serial; origin keeps its single draw for now.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (1) Invariance on 35x HG002: event B's SPIKE R1/R2 records (matched by stable ID or sequence), suppressed names and truth INFO byte-identical across panels {B}, {A,B} and {B,A}; master fails (0/276, 11/277). Refuted if B still changes through hidden coupling (shared duplicate-family scan, a pool window shared between events, origin's joint draw). (2) Equivalence: on K7's round-trip set and the 15 identity sets over 5 seeds, validate verdicts (allele_freq, del_planted, ins_planted), SIM_ALT_FRAGS and realised AF inside master's seed spread; across 20 seeds on 10 real HG002 events SIM_ALT_FRAGS and realised-VAF distributions match master (KS p>0.05), which kills a biased stream derivation. (3) --threads 1, 4, 16 byte-identical. (4) With per-fragment streams the 3 Mb DUP at 16 threads beats today's 26.5 s. Kill if (1), (2) or (3) fails.
