ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1-2 h of code reading plus one run: list every &mut rng consumer (grep rng in main.rs, simulate.rs, synth.rs, origin.rs) and check whether B's replaced_reads subset and suppressed set are already identical between {B} and {A,B} (they should be if only RNG couples events), telling whether per-event streams alone suffice. Time the 3 Mb DUP's tiling step at 16 threads from log timestamps; if tiling is under ~15% of wall time, build only stage 1. Count in transplant logs how many accepted events RF8 retries re-drew.
ideas.impact: Hospital panels become composable: adding or dropping an LDLR variant no longer perturbs the DMD one, and a panel run equals its one-at-a-time runs, so caller results compare across reruns. Transplant retries and B1/B2 arms stop re-drawing accepted events; K7-style gates stop failing on stream reordering. Opens parallel events and parallel tiling (up to the ~10 s tiling share of a 3 Mb DUP, inferred).
ideas.risks: Every output changes once: needs the owner's explicit word (the byte-identity rule applies to speed-ups, not to this) and a K7-style seed-spread gate; all locked byte-identity baselines must be re-cut. Per-fragment seeding adds a small cost. Two identical specs need distinct occurrence indices (the overlap rule already refuses them). Stable names must stay unique and Illumina-shaped; validate's sim_number -> SPIKE_evNNNN mapping must change in step; origin's single draw must keep its per-family meaning.
ideas.history_check: On 2026-09-27 the user chose threads step 1 (no-RNG work, byte-identical) and not step 2 (per-chunk RNG) (memory threads-step1.md). The map keeps per-event RNG streams OPEN. Never refuted. New since: the v1 K7 failure attributed to stream reordering (bccc43a), measured order dependence on real events (two independent measurements), the transplant retry loop re-drawing accepted events, and the measured serial tiling share.

ideas.title: ClinVar-native VCF ingest: route sequence-resolved >=50 bp records to the SV path, keep ClinVar ID, gene and HGVS
ideas.problem: ClinVar is the obvious source for the hospital demo, but no ClinVar record >=50 bp carries SVTYPE, so vcf_input.rs:226-241 turns every one into a SmallVariant: the run log and README label it 'SNV', truth ID is sim_var_N with no SVTYPE/END/SVLEN, ClinVar ID and GENEINFO are dropped, SIM_GENE falls back to 'unknown' (vcf_input.rs:430-432, truth.rs:430). Deletions come out physically right but on the small-variant path. A sequence-resolved tandem DUP becomes an insertion of 'novel' sequence: fragments wholly inside the copy are never tiled, so the duplicated region gets no extra depth, and SIM_ALT_FRAGS cannot count a junction when ALT is longer than a read (reads 0), with a warning wrongly blaming rarity (simulate.rs:320). ClinVar contig names ('19') are refused outright. A DUP given by coordinates with a 1 bp span is planted as SVTYPE=DUP SVLEN=1 silently.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R34) with the prebuilt release binary (target/release/spike, built 2026-10-06; vcf_input.rs/truth.rs/exon.rs unchanged since 0a00caf per git diff) on 35x HG002 (scratchpad cv/, rf8/): (1) ClinVar VCF as-is: 'Error: chromosome '19' not found in FASTA index'. (2) Renamed to chr19, ClinVar 251409 (pathogenic 7,636 bp LDLR DEL) is labelled 'SNV chr19:11106493 <7.6kb REF>>C', ID sim_var_1, no SVTYPE, SIM_GENE=unknown; R1 md5 54443603 vs the del:chr19:11106493-11114129 spec's 26ccc768. (3) ClinVar 251140 (pathogenic 8,119 bp DUP, CLNHGVS g.11104774_11112892dup; ALT[1:] equals the downstream reference, samtools faidx): as a VCF record 313 synthetic and 280 suppressed pairs, SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 at AF 0.5 and the 'this rare' warning; dup:chr19:11104770-11112889 gives 1,540 synthetic, 888 suppressed, SIM_ALT_FRAGS=30, DEPTH_FOLD 1.51. (4) With only SVTYPE=DUP or SVTYPE=DEL added, R1.fq.gz is byte-identical to the coordinate specs (md5 5bfadff3, 26ccc768): the fix is pure routing (README:328 documents the anchor+copy DUP form). (5) clinvar.vcf.gz (fileDate 2026-05-03) P/LP records with allele difference >=50 bp: 2,602 Deletion, 285 Duplication, 448 Insertion, 356 Indel, 305 Microsatellite genome-wide; in LDLR 31 DEL, 3 DUP, 3 INS, 2 Indel. GIAB Q100 chr20 VCF has SVTYPE on 1,712/1,712 such records, so only clinical-style VCFs hit this. (6) cnv_validation's clinvar_pathogenic_sv_ge50.bed stores the 4 LDLR ClinVar DUPs as 1 bp intervals; dup:chr19:11104769-11104770 was planted as SVTYPE=DUP;SVLEN=1 with no warning (rf8/e8). RF8 was not LDLR's obstacle (0/35 refused).
ideas.proposal: In vcf_input.rs, when a record has no SVTYPE, both alleles are DNA and |len(ALT)-len(REF)| >= 50 with a shared anchor: a pure deletion becomes DEL; a pure insertion whose inserted bases equal the adjacent reference on either side (after shifting across the repeat), or that carries CLNVC=Duplication, becomes DUP (existing anchor+copy form); any other insertion becomes INS with its sequence; anything else goes to delins/complex handling or a counted refusal. Records under 50 bp keep today's SmallVariant path byte for byte. Contig alias: if a VCF contig is missing from the .fai but exactly one of chr+name / name-minus-chr (MT<->chrM) is present, use it and log once. Carry ID to SIM_SRC_ID, GENEINFO's symbol to SIM_GENE, CLNHGVS to SIM_HGVS in truth and run README. --vcf-ids 251409,251140 picks records from a big VCF. Reword the SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 warning for an ALT longer than a read. Warn when a coordinate-spec DEL/DUP/INV is shorter than 50 bp. Later: HGVS g. specs.
ideas.simplest_version: Map CLNVC=Deletion/Duplication/Insertion to SVTYPE=DEL/DUP/INS for no-SVTYPE records >=50 bp (exactly what the bcftools-edited gate records did), plus the chr-prefix alias and SIM_SRC_ID from the ID column.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x HG002, all 39 LDLR P/LP sequence-resolved ClinVar records >=50 bp, renamed only by the alias: (a) every DEL and DUP fed by --vcf gives R1/R2 byte-identical to its del:/dup: coordinate spec (today none does: DEL md5 differs, DUP 313 vs 1,540 synthetic pairs); (b) after align.sh+merge.sh, spike validate on the 3 DUPs gives |coverage_ratio-1.5|<0.3 and the DELs del_planted PASS. Refuted if the classifier labels any of the 31 DELs other than DEL or fewer than 3/3 Duplications as DUP, or if any record under 50 bp in a 500-record ClinVar sample changes bytes against master.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 h: a 30-line Python classifier over the 39 LDLR records writes SVTYPE into a VCF copy; run the release binary per record and compare md5 with the matching del:/dup:/ins: spec (2 of 39 done and byte-identical: cv/delsvt, cv/dupsvt).
ideas.impact: The hospital user can spike pathogenic ClinVar variants by ID straight from the ClinVar VCF. Today a pathogenic LDLR DUP fed that way plants no extra depth (which gCNV/CNVnator need), every SV is reported as 'SNV', and the ClinVar ID is lost; with the ID in truth, demo results match back to ClinVar records (M48).
ideas.risks: vcf_input has no reference today (loaded later), so shape-based DUP detection needs the reference or CLNVC; start with CLNVC plus allele shape. ClinVar Microsatellite expansions (305) should become INS with sequence, not DUP; RF15/CR5 limits on long insertions apply (see M18). Contig aliasing must refuse when both spellings exist. VCF runs with >=50 bp records change bytes; gate must show identity under 50 bp.
ideas.history_check: Not proposed or refuted before (no ClinVar entry in the case file; no map item for SVTYPE-less >=50 bp records). Related OPEN map items: 'VCF delins SVs' and 'carry the input record's ID (SIM_SRC_ID) and gene from GENEINFO'. L7 (SVTYPE without END/SVLEN becoming 1 bp) fixed but a different path. CR5 handled long insertions' anchoring only. The hospital-demo-plan memory assumed RF8 would be LDLR's obstacle; it was not (0/35 refused); this ingest gap is the real one.

ideas.title: Exon specs from MANE (GFF + transcript choice), and fix the bundled LDLR exon BED whose exon 1 is in intron 1
ideas.problem: Exon-level events (del:LDLR:exon4-exon8) are the natural clinical spec, but the inputs behind them are broken or unusable: (1) the bundled data/ldlr_deletions/ldlr_exons_hg38.bed has the wrong exon 1, so events naming exon 1 (promoter/exon-1 deletions are a known FH class) land ~1 kb into intron 1; (2) the bundled ldlr_known_deletions_hg38.vcf names alleles like real published ones ('_ClinVar', '_Danish', '_Czech') but its breakpoints are round-number approximations; (3) the hospital's Scout exon BED (7 columns, exons merged across transcripts, no exon numbers, no strand) cannot be used - spike reads column 5 (a transcript list) as the gene; (4) spike cannot read GFF/GTF, so every gene needs a hand-made single-transcript BED.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R36): MANE v1.0 GFF (prime_radiant/data/work/MANE.GRCh38.v1.0.refseq_genomic.gff.gz) puts NM_000527.5 exon 1 at chr19:11089462-11089615 (0-based); the bundled exon1 is 11090578-11090919 - no overlap, starting 963 bp downstream. The 8 ClinVar initiator-codon records (around 11089548) fall in MANE exon 1; the 5 ClinVar records inside the bundled exon1 are annotated intron_variant (or missense in another transcript). 16/18 exons match MANE exactly; exon 18's end differs by 4 bp. Known-deletions VCF: 20/22 POS and 15/22 END are multiples of 100, vs 0/37 starts/ends in cnv_validation's ClinVar LDLR SV BED; only 1/19 DELs matches a ClinVar record by length (251409, 7,636 bp), shifted by 193 bp (11106300 vs 11106493). Release binary with --exon-bed = Scout BED (scout_hgnc_all_exons_grch38p14_260122.bed.gz) and del:LDLR:exon2-exon3 exits 1: 'gene 'LDLR' not found. Available: ENST00000450305, ENST00000488147, NR_106918, ...' in a 13 MB log. Code: exon.rs:64-138 groups by (column 5, chrom); exon.rs:149-160 falls back to genomic numbering when names carry no number. Corroborated by M13: 15/22 demo records have both ends on multiples of 100.
ideas.proposal: (1) Replace the bundled LDLR BED with a MANE-derived one and ship the regenerating script; relabel the known-deletions VCF as 'approximate breakpoints, not observed alleles' or replace it with ClinVar IDs at exact coordinates. (2) --exon-gff FILE [--transcript ID]: read exon features from GFF3/GTF, choose MANE Select by default (tag, or the only NM in a MANE file), exon numbers from exon_number or the ID suffix, strand from column 7, exons named GENE_exonN so SIM_EXONS stays as today. (3) 'gene not found' prints at most 10 near matches, not the whole catalogue. Later: c. HGVS for SNVs/indels once transcripts are loaded.
ideas.simplest_version: Correct the two lines of the bundled BED, and put a 6-line awk recipe in the README turning the public MANE GFF into spike's BED (chrom, start-1, end, GENE_exonN, GENE).
ideas.falsifying_measurement: With the corrected annotation, del:LDLR:exon1-exon1 must span all 8 ClinVar initiator-codon records (around 11089548) and end at the exon-1 splice donor (11089615); the bundled BED's exon1 contains 0 of 8. del:LDLR:exon4-exon8 on the 35x BAM gives truth.vcf/R1/R2 byte-identical to the bundled BED's (no regression on matching exons). Minus-strand check: exon 1 of DMD from the GFF reader must contain DMD's ClinVar initiator-codon records; a reader numbering by position fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 1 h: the awk MANE->BED diff against the bundled BED is done (2 lines differ); repeat for DMD (minus strand) and 5 other panel genes and check ClinVar initiator-codon positions inside each derived exon 1.
ideas.impact: LDLR exon-level demos (and any gene) land on the right exons; the hospital can use public MANE instead of its unusable Scout BED; the public repo stops shipping an LDLR resource that misplaces exon 1 and mislabels approximate deletions as real ones.
ideas.risks: Transcript choice (a lab's legacy exon numbering vs MANE). GFF parser must handle GENCODE and RefSeq attributes. Exon-spec breakpoints stay exactly on exon edges, easier to call than real intronic/Alu breakpoints (M13). Do not ship hospital-derived files in the public repo.
ideas.history_check: Not in the map or case file. L14 fixed BED6 score columns; number_exons refuses duplicate exon numbers. The map's '0 of 36 LDLR exon edges lie inside an Alu' used this bundled BED, so its exon-1 edges were wrong and should be re-measured. BED unchanged since the initial commit a63115e.

ideas.title: --gvcf sample identity: pick the BAM's sample and check that the VCF describes these reads
ideas.problem: load_snps_from_gvcf hard-codes the first sample column (loh.rs:396, let sample_col: usize = 9); its comment claims the index comes from the header, but it does not. Nothing compares the VCF's sample with the BAM's SM or with the reads. When the file has any het SNP in the footprint it replaces the pileup outright (loh.rs:189-216), the sample's own hom-alt calls included. A multi-sample family VCF or a mixed-up GIAB file therefore writes another person's alleles onto spike's reads with exit 0.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R44): HG002 35x BAM with HG001's v4.2.1 benchmark VCF as --gvcf, del:chr20:44999900-45000100 (scratchpad robust/gv2_HG001): exit 0, 0 WARN; HG002's 6 hom-alt SNPs (HG001 het there) taken as '6 het SNPs' in 3 blocks, 'classified 234 fragments'; at chr20:45,000,494 (HG002 1/1 G>A) 15/15 SPIKE_ reads carry REF vs 0/32 kept originals; with HG002's own VCF 15/15 carry ALT (robust/allele_count.py). Over 200 random 4 kb footprints inside both benchmark beds on chr20 (robust/wrong_gvcf.py): the wrong VCF has >=1 het in 65.5% of windows (replacing the pileup there); only 211 of HG002's 736 het SNPs are het in HG001; HG001 brings 641 hets; 12% of windows lose a HG002 hom-alt; control (HG002 v4.2.1 in the slot) 734/736 shared, 0 lost. Names: HG001 VCF 'HG001' vs BAM SM 'HG002'; hospital raredisease VCF sample 'D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x' equals its BAM SM. DOCUMENTED: README.md:386 describes using the hospital's DeepVariant calls with --gvcf.
ideas.proposal: (1) Choose the VCF column whose sample name equals the BAM SM; one sample under a different name warns; several samples with none matching refuses and names a --gvcf-sample flag. (2) A data gate reusing the second BAM pass spike already makes at gVCF het positions (collect_snp_alleles): share of gVCF het sites with >=8 reads where both alleles each reach >=15%; below a locked cut refuse with 'this VCF does not describe this BAM'; the share is logged either way.
ideas.simplest_version: Refuse a multi-sample VCF without --gvcf-sample; warn when a single sample's name differs from SM; log the het-concordance share without gating yet.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Concordance over 100 random footprints >=0.9 for HG002 35x with HG002's VCF and for the hospital BAM with its raredisease VCF; <=0.5 for HG002 35x with HG001's VCF (benchmark overlap predicts ~211/641). At chr20:44.998-45.002 Mb the HG001 file must be refused (today REF on 15/15 SPIKE reads). If correct-VCF runs fall under the cut in >1% of footprints (pileup noise at 30x), the gate is wrong. Every correct-VCF run stays byte-identical to master.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Under 1 h: bcftools mpileup -R at HG001 and HG002 het sites in 100 footprints of the 35x BAM gives both concordance distributions before code; the hospital BAM with its own VCF is the specificity check.
ideas.impact: A user passing the hospital's case VCF (multi-sample for a trio) or the wrong GIAB file gets a refusal; today the background around every event quietly carries another person's alleles (inferred ~one false-allele site per footprint: 430 HG001-only hets over 200 windows) and the sample's hom-alts turn het. Needed before M11/M16 rely on a supplied phased VCF.
ideas.risks: Low-MAPQ footprints give few concordance sites (gate must abstain below a minimum count). Calls from another caller on the right sample disagree at some sites (lock the cut after gate B). Benchmark VCFs name samples 'HG002' while lab BAMs use other SMs, so a single-sample name mismatch only warns.
ideas.history_check: Not in the case file or any review finding (grep finds only the hard-coded column). Review finding 4 (gVCF hom-alt, 2ab9fc7) and CR3 fail-closed touched this path but never sample identity. Never proposed or refuted.

ideas.title: Refuse a BAM/CRAM aligned to another build: compare @SQ LN/M5 with the FASTA, plus a data tell
ideas.problem: spike never compares the alignment's @SQ lengths or M5 with the FASTA; header.reference_sequences() is used only for name lookups (extract.rs:330, 385, 468; quality.rs:1093). A BAM aligned to another build with the same contig names (T2T-CHM13 uses chr1..chrX) runs to exit 0 with a normal-looking truth VCF, removing the wrong reads and learning the quality model against the wrong sequence.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R45): /home/parlar_ai/dev/telotyper/aligned/ERR3239334.dedup.bam is a CHM13 alignment (bwa-mem2 @PG 'reference/chm13v2.0.fa'; @SQ chr19 LN 61,707,364 vs GRCh38 58,617,616). spike with the GRCh38 no-alt FASTA and del:chr19:11100000-11102000 (scratchpad robust/chm13): exit 0, 0 WARN, SIM_RESIST 0.011, SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 1.11; but log 'chr19:11098000-11104000: 10 het SNPs, 4483 hom-alt SNPs' and 'Applied 3012 het SNP variants' (same event on HG002 35x: 13 het, 0 hom-alt); quality sample masked 20,623,489 of 29,768,724 bases (69.3%) as the sample's variant sites vs 83,841 of 38,120,856 (0.22%) on HG002 35x. Headers: HG002 35x and hospital @SQ identical to the .fai; NA18488.chr20.bam has 3,171 extra alt/decoy/HLA contigs with LN and M5 equal on shared contigs; HG001 CRAM M5 matches. DOCUMENTED: validate_pipeline.sh had to add its own contig check (check_background_contigs, scripts/validate_pipeline.sh:464-480) because Delly refused an alt-aware background.
ideas.proposal: Before extraction check every contig spike reads (event contigs, --region, quality-sample contigs): @SQ LN equals the .fai length, and M5 equals the .dict (or a computed MD5) when both exist; otherwise refuse with a policy exit code. Warn when the BAM names contigs the FASTA lacks (alt-aware alignment; align.sh will realign spike's reads to a different reference than the originals). Second, header-independent layer for reheadered files: refuse when the quality sample's masked share exceeds a locked cut (0.22% correct vs 69.3% wrong).
ideas.simplest_version: Compare LN for the event contigs only, in one loop over header.reference_sequences() against the .fai lengths spike already loads.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: ERR3239334 with the GRCh38 FASTA refused before extraction. HG002 35x, the hospital BAM, NA18488.chr20.bam (superset) and the HG001 CRAM pass with outputs md5-identical to master. Data layer: a scratch copy of the CHM13 BAM reheadered with GRCh38 LNs (samtools reheader) still refused by the masked-share rule while all GRCh38 backgrounds stay under the cut. Kill if any correct background is refused.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done: two runs and the header diffs. Under 10 min: one spike run each on the hospital BAM and NA18488 to read their masked shares from the 'Error table from' log line (NA18488, African ancestry and more polymorphic, sets the specificity margin).
ideas.impact: Users with T2T or hg19 BAMs sharing chr names get a refusal instead of a silently wrong spike; harnesses no longer need their own contig checks.
ideas.risks: Many BAMs carry no M5 (HG002 35x has none), so LN-only there. Masked-share cut must not fire on highly polymorphic samples or low-MAPQ-heavy input. Compare only contigs spike reads, so chrUn naming differences cannot cause false refusals. Shares the contig filter with M32.
ideas.history_check: Map lists it as inferred ('No check that the BAM was aligned to the given FASTA'); never built or refuted. CR-BUILD was about bcftools test dependencies, unrelated. This session gives the first measured silent run.

ideas.title: v2 regression: the startup quality sample aborts on alt/decoy-aware inputs (GIAB HG001 CRAM)
ideas.problem: quality::sample_input spreads 20 blocks over every indexed window of every @SQ contig (quality.rs:1091-1199) and any block failure is fatal. On a GRCh38 full-analysis-set plus decoy alignment (1000G/NYGC layout, and GIAB's NA12878.final.cram in data/), the last block lands on a decoy contig; with the no-alt FASTA the run aborts before any event with a cryptic error. The pre-v2 binary runs the same command fine.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R46): NA12878.final.cram (data/giab_hg38/HG001) has 3,366 @SQ; 4,605 of 79,637 CRAI slices (5.8%) are on non-primary contigs; block 19 at window floor(39W/40) lands on chrUn_JTFH01000280v1_decoy (scratchpad robust/crai_sorted.txt). The v2 binary (7f28bb0; master 4a5672d differs only in quality.rs's run-ratio cache per git diff --stat 7f28bb0 4a5672d -- src) with the no-alt FASTA and del:chr19:11100000-11102000 exits 1 after 7 blocks: 'Error: invalid reference sequence name: chrUn_JTFH01000277v1_decoy' (robust/hg001cram/log.txt). The pre-v2 binary (target/release, built 2026-10-06 at about 97aa3b4) exits 0 on the same command: 2265 kept, 228 chimeric (robust/hg001cram_old). INFERRED: a BAM with reads on a contig absent from the .fai would reach fetch_window (quality.rs:1190, reference.rs:66-73) and fail with 'chromosome ... not found in FASTA index'.
ideas.proposal: Choose quality blocks only from windows on contigs present in the FASTA with a matching length (shared with M31's build check). A block on a contig the FASTA lacks is skipped with a warning and counts toward the 50,000-pair thin-sample warning instead of aborting. Restricting to primary assembled chromosomes is a separate, byte-changing decision.
ideas.simplest_version: In indexed_windows keep only names present in the .fai (one HashSet lookup) before choose_blocks.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: HG001 CRAM with the no-alt FASTA exits 0 with all 20 blocks on .fai contigs. On HG002 35x and the hospital BAM (@SQ equal to .fai) R1/R2, truth.vcf, replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt md5-identical to master (window list unchanged); the HG002 log line 'from chr1:73644223 to chrX:119028195' does not move. A mutant without the filter reproduces the abort.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done this session: the abort and the pre-v2 success on the same command. The fix plus three md5 comparisons take about 1 h.
ideas.impact: Public GIAB and 1000G CRAMs (the HG001 CRAM in data/) work again with the no-alt FASTA instead of dying on an unexplained decoy name. Matters before v2 is pushed, since public master does not yet have the regression.
ideas.risks: Restricting to primary contigs would change bytes for BAMs with reads on chrUn/random/EBV, so keep the minimal filter. Skipping must cover only 'contig not in FASTA', never decode or I/O errors.
ideas.history_check: Introduced by quality model v2 (7f28bb0, 2026-10-07). Its K4 measured only HG002 35x and the hospital BAM, both with @SQ equal to the .fai. Nothing on decoys in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model*.md or the case file (grep). Never reported.

ideas.title: Detect duplicate-unmarked input before simulating (unmarked BAMs inflate the planted VAF after re-marking)
ideas.problem: The main run never checks the input is duplicate-marked. On an unmarked BAM, PCR and optical duplicates enter the donor pool as independent fragments: coverage counts them, family members are suppressed independently, and spike's reads carry no duplicates. After raredisease re-marks duplicates the kept originals lose theirs and spike's reads do not, so the alt share rises. validate.rs already has the detector (L15); main does not use it.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R48): data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.GRCh38.novaseq-40x.strobealign-sv.two-pass.bam has no markdup @PG and no @RG; in chr20:10-10.5 Mb 0 of 149,768 primary records flagged duplicate vs 12.10% of 149,273 on the bwa 35x BAM; samtools fixmate+markdup on its proper MAPQ>=20 pairs in chr19:11.0-11.2 Mb marks 9,276 of 70,881 reads (13.1%). spike on it (robust/strobe) exits 0; only warning is the missing SM ('tagging simulated reads SM:SIM'); 'Duplicates of the removed originals: 0 pair(s)' vs 54 on the 35x BAM. The detector (validate.rs:2713-2749) stays quiet on NA18488.chr20.bam (8.47% flagged, markdup @PG), the hospital BAM (3.76%, markdup @PG) and the CHM13 BAM (10.6%). INFERRED harm: at v=0.5, d=0.131, VAF after re-marking ~ v/(v+(1-v)(1-d)) ~ 0.535.
ideas.proposal: Run the L15 rule (duplicate flags present, or a markdup @PG) in main on the index-placed quality sample, not the file head. When neither holds, warn (default) or refuse unless --unmarked-ok, as the user chooses; print the expected VAF bias from the pool's own duplicate-family share (computable by 5' ends as duplicates_of does).
ideas.simplest_version: A single warning line when the quality sample has zero duplicate flags and the header has no markdup @PG.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Detector fires on the strobealign BAM and stays silent on HG002 35x, the hospital BAM, NA18488, the HG001 CRAM and CHM13. Harm: plant 100 het SNVs into the strobealign BAM and the 35x BAM, samtools markdup each merged BAM, compare realised VAF; predicted ~+0.03 on the unmarked input. If the difference is <0.01 with a 95% CI excluding 0.03, the harm claim dies and a log line is all that is warranted.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Detector side done (flag counts, @PG, region markdup). Harm side: the 100-SNV plant plus markdup on chr20 of both BAMs, a few hours of compute, no code.
ideas.impact: Users bringing aligner output straight from strobealign or minimap2 (or any pre-markdup BAM) are told, instead of getting a planted fraction ~3 points high once their pipeline marks duplicates.
ideas.risks: Some PCR-free libraries legitimately have very few duplicates (zero-flag check alone could false-fire; the @PG check covers that). Refusing would break users who intentionally feed unmarked BAMs, so warn by default.
ideas.history_check: Map's OPEN list has 'Warn on unmarked input' (inferred; REVIEW L15 exists only in validate). New: a real unmarked BAM in spike's own data directory with a measured 13.1% duplicate share. Not refuted.

ideas.title: N-aware tiling: never place spike fragments over reference gaps or past contig ends
ideas.problem: Fragment starts are uniform over every reference-overlapping start of the haplotype (simulate.rs:926-946). A reference N emits N at Q2 (synth.rs:189-202) and bases past a contig end are N-padded (synth.rs:51; test synth.rs:1561). An event within 2 kb of a gap or contig end tiles whole reads of N at full depth where real data has none, and count and depth are scaled as if those starts were real.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R50; scratchpad robust/ngap): del:chr20:61000-61400 beside the chr20 p-arm gap (N run ends at 60,000) is refused by RF8 (SIM_RESIST 0.814) without --allow-resistant; with it, 644 SPIKE_ reads, 123 entirely N (19%), 149 at least half N; SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 76.88 warns but reads are written. DOCUMENTED: real NovaSeq N rate 2-3e-5 per base, Q2 only on N (map; K2b FASTQs; consistent with M2's 2.6e-5).
ideas.proposal: Treat reference N runs (e.g. >=10 bp) and positions past a contig end as non-placeable, like novel_only sequence: exclude fragment starts whose fragment overlaps them and drop those starts from the count.
ideas.simplest_version: In sample_ref_overlapping_start reject a start whose fragment covers >=10 consecutive reference N, and subtract those starts in compute_tiling_count.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On chr20:61000-61400, all-N SPIKE reads go from 123 to 0 and spike's per-base N rate comes within 2x of real 2-3e-5. On the 15 identity sets (no N in footprints) and a near-contig-end unit fixture, outputs byte-identical to master. A fix that also drops starts at isolated single Ns moves bytes there and fails.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done (one run). Before building, scan GRCh38 for N runs within 2 kb of the exons in the user's clinical gene list (bedtools window on .fai gaps); if none, rank as hygiene only.
ideas.impact: No impossible all-N reads in the spiked FASTQ, and correct counts near gaps or contig ends. Modest, since RF8 already refuses most such sites.
ideas.risks: Changes counts near gaps (intended). N-run threshold must not remove starts at isolated IUPAC/N bases inside real sequence.
ideas.history_check: CR5 (insertion fragments drawn only from reference-overlapping starts) is the same mechanism applied to novel sequence, never to N. Contig-end coordinate handling is unit-tested (haplotype.rs:1413-1500) but read placement over N is not. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Code health: one EventOutcome per event, plus an end-of-run audit of the output name contract
ideas.problem: Per-event results travel in four parallel Vec<Option<_>> indexed by event (main.rs:670-677, pushed :851-854, consumed :941-944), guarded only by release asserts in truth.rs:87-110 added after RF1. main.rs is 5,975 lines (~2,940 non-test), validate.rs 8,591. The output contract the FASTQ route relies on (R1/R2 names paired; SPIKE names unique; fastq_removed and written names disjoint; replaced = written originals + fastq_removed) is checked nowhere at run time; fastq.sh (found==want) and merge.sh (ACTUAL>=NAMES) check only counts, and only later.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R51) on the two-event HG002 run (scratchpad robust/order/AB): 6,396 R1 and 6,396 R2 names, identical sets; 0 duplicate names; fastq_removed intersect written = 0; fastq_removed not-subset-of replaced = 0; replaced minus written minus fastq_removed = 0 - invariants hold today, so an audit would not false-alarm. Line counts from wc -l; #[cfg(test)] at main.rs:2938. DOCUMENTED: the independent review lists missing EventPlan/EventResult and run manifest as unaddressed debt (docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:131-142). RF1 was an index-alignment defect in exactly these slices.
ideas.proposal: Replace the parallel vectors with one EventOutcome struct (adjusted_vaf, resistant, depth_fold, alt_frags, kept, suppressed, chimeric). Separately add an audit pass just before outputs are published that checks the name contract and records the result in run.json (M36); on a violation, outputs are not published.
ideas.simplest_version: Only the audit: four set checks over names spike already holds in memory, bail! before publishing on a violation.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Outputs byte-identical to master on the identity sets. On real HG002 runs, seeded mutants make the run refuse: one kept original's name added to fastq_removed_reads.txt; one SPIKE pair's R2 dropped; one duplicate-family member left out of replaced_reads.txt. The audit passes on every real run of the identity sets.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done: the four invariants checked by awk/comm on a real run. Next (~1 h): the same check over the outputs of the 15 identity sets and the transplant runs to confirm none violates them today.
ideas.impact: Catches silent output corruption in the FASTQ route at write time, not 42 minutes into fastq.sh or after a raredisease run; removes the class of index-misalignment bugs RF1 belonged to; prerequisite cleanup for M27's per-event streams.
ideas.risks: Large diff in main.rs: keep refactor and audit in separate commits, each byte-identical. Audit costs a little memory for name sets on huge events.
ideas.history_check: The independent review (2026-10-04) named this architecture debt, unaddressed. RF1 fixed the symptom with release asserts. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Provenance you can paste back and no stale outputs: commit-stamped version, shell-quoted command, recorded seed and defaults, run.json + run id, distinct exit codes
ideas.problem: A demo dataset cannot be traced to the code and settings that made it, and a reused -o can silently mix runs. Version is always 0.1.0 (Cargo.toml, no build.rs); truth.vcf says only ##source=spike; seed and defaults appear only if typed; the README's command is args.join(' ') (main.rs:989), unquoted, so pasting it into bash splits at the ';' of a per-event af= and drops every later argument including --seed and -o. spike creates -o (main.rs:489) but never removes stale files: a run refused after the CLI checks (carried allele, RF8, too few donors) exits 1 and leaves the previous run's truth.vcf, R1/R2, replaced_reads.txt, merge.sh and fastq.sh; merge.sh only tests that sim.bam exists (main.rs:2505-2508), so it can merge the previous run's reads. Refusals and I/O errors share exit status 1 (main.rs:862-864).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R38) on the B1 run (sv_slice_test/data/B1/spike): README 'spike version: 0.1.0' (binary renamed spike-bdd568a by hand to keep the commit); command block shows --event del:chr19:11127041-11129177;af=het --seed 1 unquoted; truth header ##source=spike with no version, seed or command. MEASURED (R47, scratchpad robust/stale): run 1 del:chr19:11100000-11102000 on HG002 35x exit 0 (truth.vcf md5 a5538b6f2fa9); run 2 into the same -o, snp:chr20:45000494:G:A, refused at exit 1 ('the sample already carries another allele ... (42 of 43 reads)'); afterwards truth.vcf (still a5538b6f2fa9, the chr19 DEL), R1.fq.gz (84851d3db490), merge.sh and fastq.sh are all run 1's. Code: no remove_file/remove_dir in main.rs outside tests; sh_quote/sh_word exist (main.rs:1297-1303). DOCUMENTED: the owner's loop works around this with rm -rf before every run (sv_slice_test/wt/slice_safety/run.sh:121, 131 per the map); validate_pipeline.sh:947 reuses an existing truth.vcf.gz. INFERRED from bash semantics: pasting the B1 command runs af 0.5, seed 42, -o /tmp/spike.
ideas.proposal: Embed git describe --dirty at build time (build.rs or option_env, fallback 'unknown'). Write ##spike_version, ##spike_command (each argv through sh_quote), ##spike_seed, ##spike_settings (every effective default) and an input identity (BAM size, mtime, @SQ hash - not the path, see M38) into truth.vcf. Write run.json last as a completion marker (run id, seed, quoted command, per-event stats, refusals, output md5s, M35's audit result). align.sh stamps the run id into sim.bam (@CO); merge.sh and fastq.sh refuse when run.json is missing or the id differs. At startup, after CLI checks, refuse when -o holds any of RUN_OUTPUT_FILES, sim.bam or merged.bam unless --overwrite (which deletes only spike's own names first). Policy refusals (RF8, carried, overlap) exit 2, errors exit 1.
ideas.simplest_version: Two small pieces: (a) shell-quote the logged command, print the effective seed, add the commit hash to the README version line and a ##spike_version header; (b) delete RUN_OUTPUT_FILES plus sim.bam, sim.bam.bai and merged.bam at startup before any work (or refuse on them), and publish truth.vcf last via temp file and rename.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: (1) Paste test on 35x: run --event 'snp:chr19:11113291:C:A;af=0.05' --seed 3, paste the README's command block into bash: truth.vcf byte-identical apart from fileDate; master fails (SIM_REQ_VAF=0.500, seed 42, output in /tmp/spike). (2) Stale tests: repeat R47's two-run sequence - afterwards no run-1 truth.vcf, R1 or fastq.sh remain, or merge.sh/fastq.sh refuse; on a chr20-only BAM spike X into D + align.sh, then spike Y into D and merge.sh without align.sh must refuse (master passes its count guard and merges X's sim.bam). (3) With --overwrite, run 1 then run 2 leaves run 2's outputs byte-identical to run 2 in a fresh folder; a fresh single run byte-identical to master apart from run.json and the new headers. (4) Binaries from different commits write different ##spike_version lines. Kill if a harness in scripts/ (validate_pipeline.sh, slice_loop.sh, real_events.sh) breaks.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Done: the two-run stale reproduction (5 min). About 1 h: reproduce the paste test with the release binary (~1 s/run) and the align/merge stale test on data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.GRCh38.chr20.bwamem2.bam with two small chr20 events; grep the harnesses for -o reuse and '-ne 0' exit handling to list what exit code 2 would change.
ideas.impact: Every demo dataset traceable to a commit and exact settings (hospital validation documentation needs this); stale-output mix-ups cannot silently produce a wrong merged.bam or FASTQ; hospital loops over many genes and the owner's SV loops can tell refusals from crashes.
ideas.risks: Truth and README bytes change (identity tests need updating). Tarball builds have no git. Deleting files in a user-chosen folder must touch only spike's own names; refusing a dirty -o is safer than clearing. Input identity must not hash a 54 GB BAM. Exit code 2 changes what harnesses see (run.sh already treats any non-zero as a refusal).
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'provenance and machine-readable summary', 'Stale outputs' inferred from code, 'shell-quote the logged command'); never built or refuted; the stale case was measured this session.

ideas.title: Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ before simulating, not after a 40-minute stream
ideas.problem: --into-fastq checks only that RAW_R1/RAW_R2 are distinct files the run will not overwrite. fastq.sh finds out the pair belongs to another run only at END, when found != want, after streaming the whole file - ~42 min (predicted) per mistake for the hospital's 380 M pairs, on top of the multi-lane trap (lanes must be concatenated first).
ideas.evidence: Code read: main.rs:1534-1559 (validate_into_fastq: is_file, same inode, output aliasing only); fastq.sh identity check at END (main.rs:2362-2373). MEASURED: first headers of local raw FASTQs separate runs: HG002.novaseq.pcr-free.40x.R1 starts A00744:46:HV3C3DSXX:2 (same RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE as the 35x BAM's read names); HG002.chr20_R1 starts D00360:94:H2YT5BCXX:2 (different instrument and run). DOCUMENTED: ~150k pairs/s puts 380 M pairs at ~42 min (fastq-safety plan:136; full-fastq memory); M23 measures ~165k pairs/s.
ideas.proposal: Before the quality sample and the event loop, read the first record of each raw mate: check the R1 and R2 base names match, RUN:FLOWCELL (ignoring lane) is among the middles bam_stats saw in its 50,000-name sample, and read length <= cycles. Refuse (exit 2) with a message naming both values. Skip with a notice when names have no Illumina shape. Optionally run the check also inside fastq.sh before streaming.
ideas.simplest_version: Compare the first RAW_R1 header's instrument:run:flowcell with the BAM's learned name middle and refuse on a mismatch.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: 35x BAM + the HiSeq HG002.chr20 FASTQ pair refused in under 5 s, before any simulation; 35x BAM + the NovaSeq 40x pair proceeds; master proceeds with both. Refuted if, on the hospital BAM, the 50k-name sample shows several RUN:FLOWCELL values and the raw FASTQ's first record is not among them (false refusal) - measure the distinct middles there first.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 30 min: zcat|head -1 on each local raw FASTQ against samtools view|head names on each local BAM (done for 3); at the hospital count distinct RUN:FLOWCELL values in 50k BAM names.
ideas.impact: Saves ~40 min plus a confusing late failure per wrong pair at the hospital, with a message saying which run the files are from.
ideas.risks: A sample sequenced over several flowcells; SRA-renamed reads with no Illumina shape; a BAM made from a subset of the FASTQ (passes correctly). Multi-lane inputs: see M39.
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'Fail fast on the wrong raw FASTQ'); also listed as a sub-item of R21's native splice. The fastq-safety fixes (658baa4: aliasing, mate order) added no identity pre-check. Not refuted.

ideas.title: Portable, share-safe outputs: no specimen IDs or absolute paths in README/scripts, a umask-following script mode, and no /tmp default
ideas.problem: A demo bundle (truth, README, scripts) is meant to be shared with trainees, other labs or in public-repo issues. Today it embeds the input BAM's absolute path and the SM (which carry hospital specimen IDs) in README.md, align.sh, merge.sh and sim.bam's header. Default -o is /tmp/spike, shared on multi-user servers. Scripts are always 0755 while data follow the umask. Nothing says R1/R2.fq.gz are mostly real patient-sample reads.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R42) on B1 outputs (sv_slice_test/data/B1/spike): the specimen token 'D24-14230' appears 2x in README.md, 1x in align.sh, 1x in merge.sh, 0x in fastq.sh/truth.vcf/events.bed, 2x in sim.bam's header; align.sh is -rwxr-xr-x while truth.vcf is -rw-rw----; B1 kept 2,435 original pairs vs 228 synthetic (~91% of R1/R2 is real reads). Code: main.rs:106 (default -o /tmp/spike). DOCUMENTED: a pre-push scan had to rewrite 3 commits with filter-branch to remove a hospital storage path (full-fastq memory).
ideas.proposal: --portable: paths written relative to -o, or as basenames plus a header hash; README and script comments show a user label instead of the SM (sim.bam's @RG SM unchanged so raredisease sample matching works). Script mode = 0o777 & !umask. Require -o, or warn when under /tmp. README states that R1/R2 are mostly real reads from the input sample.
ideas.simplest_version: Drop the /tmp default (require -o), make script mode follow the umask, and add one README sentence about real reads in R1/R2.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: With --portable on a run whose BAM path contains a token (a symlink to the 35x BAM named FAKEID-123.bam), grep -r FAKEID-123 over every text output in -o returns 0 hits; align.sh, merge.sh and fastq.sh still run; sim.bam identical apart from @PG. Master gives hits in README.md, align.sh and merge.sh (the B1 pattern).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: 10 min: token grep on B1 outputs done (4 text hits, 2 header hits); repeat on a fresh release-binary run with a symlinked BAM.
ideas.impact: Demo bundles can leave the lab without leaking specimen IDs or LIMS paths; pushes to the public gmc-norr/spike repo need less manual scrubbing.
ideas.risks: Relative paths break if the output folder is moved. Read names stay SPIKE_ by the owner's 2026-10-04 choice (not touched). Background should already be GIAB, not patient data, so this mainly protects LIMS IDs and paths. Interacts with M36's input identity (use a hash, not the path).
ideas.history_check: OPEN in the map (Outputs: 'Clinical safety: require -o..., script mode follows umask..., drop absolute paths and the SM'); never built or refuted.

ideas.title: Multi-lane whole-sample FASTQ route for the hospital's family samples (one pair per lane, SPIKE_ reads in their named lane)
ideas.problem: --into-fastq/fastq.sh takes a single R1/R2 pair and SPIKE_ reads all take the input's most common RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. The hospital's CEPH-1463 family samples (the natural trio background) arrive as 7 lane pairs; concatenating them (the documented workaround) turns 7 per-lane alignments and read groups into one, so the demo samplesheet differs from a real run, and a SPIKE_ read's name can claim a lane its file does not hold.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R58): each of the 7 family runs (Seq25-16020, 16022, 16025, 16028, 16030, 16032, 16150) has 7 samplesheet rows, lanes 1-7 with L001-L007 FASTQs (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_fix-gatk-cnv/*/samplesheet.csv); the nextflow log shows BWAMEM2_MEM per lane (Seq25-16020_LNUMBER1..7) and one MARKDUPLICATES per sample; the HG002 BAM's @RG ID is built from file and lane ('..._S17_L002_R1_001_2'); HG001/HG002 are single-lane. DOCUMENTED: 'Lanes must be concatenated first' (memory full-fastq.md). fastq.sh is one awk over one pair (src/main.rs:2193-2454; validate_into_fastq src/main.rs:1534); names from the majority lane (src/read_name.rs:98-165).
ideas.proposal: Let --into-fastq take a lane list or a raredisease samplesheet.csv. Remove listed names from whichever lane holds them, with found-vs-wanted summed over lanes. Distribute SPIKE_ pairs across lanes in proportion to the removed originals' lanes, naming each with that lane's RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. Write a ready spiked samplesheet.csv with sex and pedigree columns carried over.
ideas.simplest_version: Loop fastq.sh per lane with a cross-lane total check, append all SPIKE_ pairs to the lane holding the most removed originals (renamed to that lane), and emit the samplesheet.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: On one 7-lane family sample at the hospital: (a) every unlisted raw record byte-identical in its lane's output; (b) removed totals over lanes equal the list; (c) SPIKE_ pairs per lane vs removed originals per lane chi-square p>0.01 (all-in-one-lane fails); (d) each SPIKE_ name's lane field equals its file's lane. KILL the per-lane work if raredisease on the concatenated layout gives the same DeepVariant and SV VCFs as the per-lane layout on an unspiked sample.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Hours, no full raredisease run: one 2 Mb region's reads from all 7 lanes of a family sample, aligned per lane vs concatenated with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000, MarkDuplicates, diff primary records and duplicate flags; if identical, keep the concatenation workaround and drop this idea.
ideas.impact: Trio and family demos on the CEPH data the hospital already sequences, with spiked FASTQs and samplesheets shaped like their real runs; pairs with M16/M17 for inherited and de novo patterns.
ideas.risks: Proportional lane assignment is a model choice (by removed originals vs by lane size). Per-lane fastp adds QC differences. The gate may show concatenation is harmless (pure convenience then). Hospital raw FASTQs are not on this machine. Interacts with M23 (per-mate parallel filter) and M37 (identity check per lane).
ideas.history_check: Map lists multi-lane input as OPEN, low priority, because 'the hospital sample is a single pair' (full-fastq.md). New: the family samples the hospital runs through raredisease are 7-lane with per-lane alignment (measured). Not refuted.

ideas.title: A standing same-template read-realism panel plus a name-free 'can you tell' classifier: the shared, composition-safe gate for every read-model change
ideas.problem: Read realism is gated today by K1 (quality strings) and K2/K2b (bad-end clips, crash share, mm/100), a few hand-picked summary shares. Every gap in M1-M6 passed them unnoticed: substitution spectrum, R1/R2 error rates, recurrent strand-specific sites, concordant molecule errors, slips, terminal cycles, placement of high-Q errors. Each new gap was found by someone thinking to look. Comparing spike against all reads in a window misleads through composition (case file K6); K2b's design (real held-out pairs vs spike remade at the same 5' positions) avoids that but scores only clips. A joint discriminator would give one number per release and rank what gives spike's reads away.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED: K6 composition error and K3 small-count error (.claude/judgment-gate-cases.md:7-44); K2b reports only bad-end clips, crash share and mm/100 (scratchpad qtq2/k2b/k2b.txt; docs/analysis/quality-model-v2/k2b.sh, clipscore.py). MEASURED (R5): ~600 lines of throwaway Python (scratchpad phys/errproc.py, recur.py, splithalf.py, mateconc*.py, hiq.py, clipends.py), under 2 min CPU on existing K2b BAMs, exposed six gaps no gate reports: recurrent sites 181 vs 2; top-alt share 0.75 vs 0.34; R1 Q25 errors 0.184% vs 0.351%; concordant Q30 mate errors 44 vs 0; slips 2.2% vs 0 at runs >=15; last-cycle ratio 1.66x vs 0.95x. MEASURED (R29): on K2b held-out 35x pairs (/home/parlar_ai/quality-speed-run/evidence/k2b), a gradient-boosted classifier on 14 quality-string features, pair-grouped 5-fold CV, 20,000 reads per class: AUC 0.572 (R1), 0.569 (R2); nulls 0.499 (real vs real) and 0.500 (spike seed 22 vs 23); no single feature >0.519; top feature last-cycle quality (real 34.57, spike 35.28) - the missing last-cycle drop found by hand (M5). On the 14 hospital K2 events (scratchpad inspect/, qtq2/k2v2/) SPIKE_ vs real reads over the same footprints, event-grouped CV: pre-v2 binary (bdd568a) AUC 0.958 (6,266 spike, 85,510 real); v2 AUC 0.582 (6,254 spike). Scripts: scratchpad valid_lens/disc.py, disc_k2.py.
ideas.proposal: Turn the K2b machinery (the ignored test measure_clip_share plus k2b.sh) into a standing panel run on the 35x and hospital BAMs: real held-out pairs vs spike pairs remade at the same templates, plus a real-vs-real hash split of held-out pairs as calibration. Report, with Q100 masking and the bench BED: per-mate spectrum and per-Q error rates; per-cycle mismatch (first 5, last 1); clips by end and length; N/Q2 relation; same-strand recurrent sites and caller-style candidates per Mb with overlap against real sites; concordant mate errors; slips by run length; per-read high-Q error distribution. Each metric gets a pass band from the real-vs-real split, not by hand. Add the name-free classifier, extended to aligned-read features (NM, mismatch positions by cycle, substitution type in sequencing orientation, clip end/length, MAPQ, XA/SA, TLEN, strand, duplicate flag, mate-joint features), excluding every giveaway (names, file order, RG tags); report AUC with event/pair-grouped CV, nulls (real vs real, seed vs seed) and ranked feature importances; track all per release (feeds M44's suite).
ideas.simplest_version: One script that runs the six existing phys/*.py measurements plus the existing quality-only classifier (disc.py/disc_k2.py) on the K2b real/spike BAMs, a hash split of real.bam and the K2 event folders, and prints one table with z-scores against the real-vs-real spread, two AUCs and a feature ranking (under a few minutes).
ideas.falsifying_measurement: The panel must be able to fail and to pass: the real-vs-real split passes every metric (if not, that metric's band is wrong); the pre-v2 binary (quality-speed-run/bin/spike-premaster, e21d282b) fails more metrics than v2; a deliberately broken v2 (mates swapped in the error table) fails the per-mate rows. Classifier: (a) sensitivity - an old binary with a known large gap scores clearly higher than v2 (already passed: 0.958 vs 0.582); (b) usefulness - a branch fixing the top-ranked feature (e.g. M5's last-cycle bin) must lower held-out AUC, else the ranking does not point to real gaps. If the aligned-feature AUC for v2 is 0.5 +-0.01 with nulls at 0.5, keep it only as a regression guard. If real-vs-real cannot pass the recurrent-site metric at K2b depth, that metric needs more blocks before it gates anything.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 h: run the existing scripts on a hash split of real.bam (real-vs-real) to get each metric's calibration spread and learn whether 62k pairs is enough depth for the recurrence and slip rows. About 1 h: add 10 aligned features (NM, MD mismatch cycles, clip ends, MAPQ, TLEN) to disc_k2.py on the K2 event folders (spiked.bam/real.bam exist) and read the top 3 features. No spike run.
ideas.impact: Every read-model change (M1-M9) gets a locked, composition-safe falsifier in one command; realism regressions are caught before merge; the owner's measure-first process gets a cheap standard instrument; a single release-to-release realism number whose feature ranking points work at the biggest giveaway and catches gaps nobody thought to list.
ideas.risks: K2b spike reads are made from the reference without the sample's SNPs, so every metric and the classifier must mask Q100 sites (or spike must use the sample-copy template). Recurrence and slip rows are depth-limited (~17x per half). A quality-feature AUC is not caller relevance (pair with M42/M43). With rich enough features any simulator becomes separable, so thresholds need the nulls and an old-binary anchor. Composition (K6) can masquerade as model gaps unless templates are matched; the hospital comparison is footprint-matched, not template-matched. A panel can become a tuning target; keep a held-out region set.
ideas.history_check: 'Read-level can-you-tell' is concept test 3 in memory validation-plan.md, never built; listed as an OPPORTUNITY in the map. K2b exists (docs/analysis/quality-model-v2/k2b.sh) but scores clips only. Nothing refuted. The K6 case-file rule (compare over the same templates) is why the panel uses the K2b design. New: a working positive control (0.958 vs 0.582) with nulls at 0.50, and six measured unreported gaps.

ideas.title: Background-integrity yardstick: measure what each spike does to the sample's own variants in its footprint, first in the reads and then in the calls
ideas.problem: Every realism yardstick looks only at the planted allele (transplant J/E1/A/E, the K quality tests, validate's rows). None asks whether the sample's own variants in the remade event +-2 kb survive. A real carrier's footprint keeps its background; spike remakes the event copy from an SNP-only template (CR3), so the sample's indels and SVs there are lost. The harm rested on one probe (AF 1.0 -> 0.360) and the T7 count of exposed footprints; its size on real transplanted events was never measured.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R26) read-only on round 2b's existing forward normal-arm outputs (session scratchpad transplant2/full/forward/normal/run0-2: sim.bam + replaced_reads.txt, 2026-09-28 master binary; SampleCopies still SNP-only in 4a5672d, src/loh.rs:33-41). MAPQ>=20, non-duplicate, spanning reads; recipient = hospital HG002; after = recipient minus replaced plus sim.bam; truth HG002 v4.2.1. 297 of 754 forward footprints hold >=1 HG002 non-SNP within +-2 kb (153 het, 145 hom, 476 records). 198 hom indels: median read AF 0.934 before, 0.479 after; 187/198 below 0.75 after vs 28 before. 233 het indels: median 0.448 -> 0.240; 109 dropped by >0.2. 214 of 752 events (28.5%) damage >=1 background indel. Control, same footprints and code: background SNPs preserved (hom 1.000 -> 1.000, 0/198 changed; het 0.500 -> 0.484, 8/201 changed by >0.2). Scripts: scratchpad valid_lens/cr3_bg.py, snp_bg.py. DOCUMENTED: CR3 probe and T7 (38/40) in docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md; transplant metrics read only the planted site (scripts/transplant/small_evidence.py:1-30). Consistent with M11's smaller read-level measurement (17 hom indels 0.95 -> 0.48).
ideas.proposal: Make background integrity a standing metric in every realism round and in the hospital acceptance run. For each event take the footprint (event +-2 kb plus 500 bp margin), excluding the planted allele; measure (a) read AF for every background benchmark variant before and after (cr3_bg.py) and (b) the hospital caller's calls (DeepVariant region mode) before and after; report per footprint and variant class (SNP, indel, SV): GT changes, lost calls, new calls; a sham run (realigned unchanged reads, as the transplant already makes) gives the null. It serves as the locked falsifier for any CR3 work (M11, M21, M10) and settles the pending T7 decision with a number.
ideas.simplest_version: Add the read-AF comparison (cr3_bg.py logic) as a seen-not-judged column of every transplant run; no caller; ~10 s per 750 events.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run DeepVariant on the 137 forward footprints whose hom background indel fell below AF 0.75, before and after spiking. The idea dies at caller level if DV still calls 1/1 at >=95% of those indels after spiking and the sham shows the same change rate (read damage would not reach calls; no standing slot). The metric must also fail a broken version: a mutant emptying SampleCopies must show background-SNP GT changes in roughly half the footprints holding a het SNP (today's SNP control: 8 of 201).
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 h, no spike run: pick 50 of the 137 hom-indel footprints; build small BAMs (recipient reads over +-5 kb minus that run's replaced names plus sim.bam reads over the span) and an unspiked sham slice; run DeepVariant 1.9.0 (cached at ~/.singularity/cache/docker.io-google-deepvariant-1.9.0.img) with --regions on both; the sham's calls must match raredisease's genome-wide DV calls; count GT flips after spiking. This is also M11's value-kill gate.
ideas.impact: Hospital demo: a spiked LDLR variant would turn nearby common hom indels into hets and drop het ones from the event copy, so raredisease reports spurious calls and GT errors next to every planted variant and a GIAB benchmark scores them FP/FN. Gives CR3 option A (M11) and P1 (M21) a locked real-data falsifier and makes 'indistinguishable from real' cover the whole footprint.
ideas.risks: Carrier detector is crude (same-length indel within 25 bp) and under-counts in repeats (hom 'before' AF 0.934, not 1.0). Round 2b binary predates read-length fix and quality v2 (CR3 code unchanged; re-measure on 4a5672d). DV 1.9.0 cached vs hospital 1.6.1. Footprint-slice calling must be shown equal to whole-BAM calling by the sham. Excluding the planted allele by distance (60 bp) may let interactions through.
ideas.history_check: CR3 documented with one probe; T7 refuted a blanket footprint WARNING (fires on 38/40); this is a yardstick, not a warning, so T7 does not cover it. The map's 'measure first, before CR3 option A' proposed 20 SNV sites; this session measured it at read level on 752 real transplant events. Nothing similar built or refuted.

ideas.title: Caller-equivalence round for SNVs, indels and short DUPs: DeepVariant on the transplant's real carriers vs the spiked recipients, judged against real-vs-real at shared sites
ideas.problem: No measurement asks whether the hospital's small-variant caller calls a spiked variant as it calls the real one (call, GT, GQ/QUAL, AD-VAF). The transplant judges read counts only; its plans explicitly leave out base quality, MAPQ, strand and callers (2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:115, round2.md:179-185), all features in DeepVariant's pileup images. RF15 (short INS cleaner than real) has never been checked at the caller level.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R27) from raredisease's own DeepVariant 1.6.1 + GLnexus calls on the donors (exact allele match at POS), real het call rates at round 2b forward sites: SNV 100/100, DEL1-4 99/100, DEL5-19 100/100, DEL20-49 95/100, INS1-4 98/100, INS5-19 97/100, INS20-49 78/100, DUP50-299 24/54; median GQ 25-50; reverse similar (INS20-49 88/100). Real-vs-real at shared sites (HG001 vs HG002 raredisease calls): het-call discordance 0-6 per 100 (INS20-49 6, DEL20-49 4, SNV 0); median |dGQ| 3-6; median |dAD-VAF| 0.074-0.100. Several groups sit off the ceiling, so a test has room to see spike too easy or too hard. DOCUMENTED: hospital DeepVariant 1.6.1, GATK 4.5.0.0 (pipeline_info nf_core_raredisease_software_mqc_versions.yml). MEASURED: DeepVariant 1.9.0 and GATK 4.6.2 containers run locally.
ideas.proposal: Reuse round 2b's event draw (forward, reverse, shared sets; B1/B2 arms; sham). Re-spike with current master (4a5672d) using the hospital aligner command. Call DeepVariant in region mode, pinned to the hospital's 1.6.1 image, at each site +-1 kb on the donor's real BAM, the spiked recipient, the sham and both shared samples. Per site record call made (normalized, representation-aware matching), GT, GQ, QUAL, AD-VAF. Judge per group and direction: call-status discordance fake vs real against real-vs-real discordance at shared sites; paired GQ/VAF differences against shared-site differences with the round-3 bootstrap rule. Controls: B1 must shift GT or GQ, B2 must lose the call at the true position, the sham must add 0 calls. Stratify by homopolymer/TR context. Uses M48's scorer if built.
ideas.simplest_version: Forward INS20-49 and SNV only (200 events), DeepVariant 1.9.0, current spike; compare call rate and GQ distribution of fake calls with the donor's existing raredisease calls.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Fail per group: if spiked INS20-49 is called het at a rate outside the real-vs-real band (e.g. >=95/100 fake vs 78/100 real, Fisher p<0.01, gap above the shared-site discordance of 6/100) spike's insertions are not caller-equivalent there; same rule for every group. If fake GQ sits systematically above real (paired median dGQ beyond the shared-site 3-6), the group fails. Harness must break on broken controls: B1 (VAF 0.25) must change DV's GT or GQ distribution; if B1 cannot be told from the normal arm by any DV metric, the round has no power and is dropped rather than read as a pass.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: (1) ~20 min: DeepVariant 1.9.0 region mode on the donor HG001 BAM at the 100 forward INS20-49 sites vs raredisease's 1.6.1 calls; >=95% must agree, else pull the 1.6.1 image. (2) Run it on round 2b's existing fake slices at the same sites (old binary) for a seen-not-judged first look at whether fake INS20-49 is called more often than 78/100.
ideas.impact: Answers the hospital's actual question for SNVs and indels (the classes the demo most needs, untested at the hospital); tests RF15 at the level that matters; gives the GQ/QUAL distributions that drive raredisease rank scores. Region-mode DV over ~10 Mb per BAM is minutes of CPU (inferred).
ideas.risks: DV version mismatch (1.9.0 cached vs 1.6.1). GLnexus re-genotyping may shift GQ (run GLnexus too or compare at gVCF level). DUP representation: exact-POS lookup found 24/54 real DUP calls, partly representation, so normalize (bcftools norm or vcfeval-style). Slicing must be checked by the sham. 100 events per group detect only ~15-20 point call-rate differences (inferred).
ideas.history_check: Listed as the biggest OPPORTUNITY in the map and in memory validation-plan.md ('which callers' still open with the user). Never run; every transplant plan scopes callers out. Not refuted. New: real-side call rates and the shared-site discordance yardstick from existing raredisease outputs.

ideas.title: Manta equivalence on round 1b DELs, stratified by Alu context: the real-carrier yardstick for 'Manta misses spiked LDLR Alu-Alu deletions'
ideas.problem: Manta missed the spiked ClinVar 4845403 (a 2.1 kb Alu-Alu DEL in LDLR) even on the full BAM. Nobody knows whether a real carrier would also be missed, so the result cannot be read as a spike defect or a caller fact. No SV caller has been run on spiked vs real carriers of the same events; round 1b's verdicts are read counts only, and LDLR's breakpoints often sit in Alus.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R28) from raredisease's SVDB-merged PASS calls on the donors at round 1b's het DELs (reciprocal overlap >=0.5). Real call rates forward, any caller: 50/100 (50-299 bp), 78/100 (300-999), 86/100 (1k-10k); Manta alone 49, 65, 70; reverse 49, 80, 86 (Manta 48, 73, 65). Real-vs-real discordance at shared DELs: any caller 11/100, 4/100, 4/78; Manta 14, 12, 3. By Alu context (UCSC rmsk at cnv_validation/resources/mobile_elements/rmsk.txt.gz, fwd+rev, DELs >=300 bp), Manta calls Alu-Alu DELs 32/77 (42%), no-Alu 179/257 (70%), one-Alu 64/66: a real Alu-Alu het DEL is missed by Manta 58% of the time, so the spiked 4845403 miss is not by itself evidence of unrealism. DOCUMENTED (memory sv-caller-slices.md): Manta --callRegions over LDLR +-1 Mb on the full BAM took 20 s; Manta FULL runs deterministic; slices refuted for Manta and CNVnator, but region calling on a whole-genome BAM differed only at inter-chromosomal BNDs.
ideas.proposal: For each round-1b run build one whole-genome spiked BAM with current master (3 runs per direction, plus B1/B2 arms and sham; events 7 kb apart, ~280 per BAM; M22's streamed merge makes this cheaper). Run Manta 1.6.0 with --callRegions over all event windows on the spiked recipient and on the donor's real BAM in the same mode; compare call status, GT, breakpoint offset, PR/SR support; judge per size bin x Alu stratum against shared-site real-vs-real discordance. Then add TIDDIT and CNVnator, whole-genome on one BAM per arm, with a repeated-run noise floor (TIDDIT differs by ~2,400 calls between runs). Expectation to test: spiked Alu-Alu DELs called at about the real 42%, not ~0% or ~90%.
ideas.simplest_version: Forward run0 only (276 events, old sim.bam in scratchpad transplant/full/forward/normal/run0): build one merged BAM, run Manta callRegions on donor HG001 and spiked HG002, tabulate call rate per bin x Alu stratum against the numbers above.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Per stratum compare fake-vs-real call discordance with shared real-vs-real discordance under a locked rule (e.g. Fisher p<0.01 and >2x the shared discordance); exceeding it refutes caller equivalence there (e.g. spiked Alu-Alu DELs called >=70% while real 42%, or spiked 50-299 bp DELs >=75% vs real 49%). Harness must break on broken controls: B1 (VAF 0.25) lowers Manta's call rate or changes GT; B2 (200 bp off) moves breakpoint offsets by ~200 bp; sham adds 0 calls in the windows.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Build the run0 merged BAM with samtools view -@16 -N/-U and samtools merge (both inputs sorted, no re-sort) - or M22's streamed route - then Manta --callRegions over the 276 windows on that BAM and the HG001 BAM. Roughly 3-4 h wall, mostly the BAM build; also times a faster merge route.
ideas.impact: Answers the open LDLR question (would a real Alu-Alu carrier be missed?) with GIAB real carriers, and tells the hospital which spiked SV classes behave like real ones in Manta (raredisease's best-breakpoint caller). Prepares the full SVDB-merged comparison. Also tells whether M13's breakpoint snapping matters to the caller.
ideas.risks: BAM build slow (merge.sh 1 h 42 min; faster route untested, M22). --callRegions can differ at inter-chromosomal BNDs (not relevant for DELs). Shared-site n 78-100 per bin: only large differences visible. RF8-refused events (13-17 per 300) drop out and must be reported. Old sim.bam for the gate predates quality v2.
ideas.history_check: Slices were refuted for Manta (narrowly, background calls) and CNVnator (cnv_validation 4bd707b); this design uses whole-genome BAMs plus region calling on both arms, which slice-safety measured identical except at inter-chromosomal BNDs. Caller equivalence is an open OPPORTUNITY, never run. New: real call rates, shared discordance and the Alu stratification.

ideas.title: Re-run the locked realism yardsticks on current master, then pin them as a pre-merge realism suite
ideas.problem: Every transplant verdict (rounds 1b, 2b, 3) was produced on 2026-09-28 by a binary with fixed 148 bp reads and the old Markov quality chain. Since then spike gained read-length trimming (only K2 re-run), Illumina names, the duplicates fix, the align-flags fix, and quality v1, v2 and quality-speed. v2 changed every base quality and error, yet its K7 gate checked validate rows only. Future plans (P1 and others) cite 'transplant rounds must keep their verdicts' as their falsifier against a stale baseline. The repo has no CI.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R30): git ls-files shows no .github, CI config, Makefile or rust-toolchain; transplant scripts last touched in c87ab53/e58738d (2026-09-28). DOCUMENTED: round 3 ran on round 2b's reads (2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:167); the read-length K2 re-run flipped one verdict, later shown to be the seed draw (memory read-length-fix.md, 3684f74), so single-seed verdicts are fragile; quality v2's K7 was 'no validate regressions' only (memory quality-model-run.md); round 1b's full run took 26 min (12:13-12:39), round 3 scoring 3 min 43 s. MEASURED: the discriminator (M40: 0.958 pre-v2, 0.582 v2) and background integrity (M41) are cheap enough to add.
ideas.proposal: One script, scripts/realism_suite.sh BINARY, with fixed event lists and 2 seeds, running round 1b (DELs), round 2b/3 (small variants and DUPs), K1 and K2b, M40's panel/discriminator and M41's background integrity. Each part writes JSON; a comparator checks every metric against a locked baseline JSON with tolerances from the 2-seed spread. Gate merges only on a supported -> refuted flip or a discriminator/background regression beyond tolerance; report everything else. First use re-baselines on 4a5672d.
ideas.simplest_version: Re-spike round 2b's forward and reverse events with 4a5672d and score them with round3.py unchanged; report the 16 verdicts beside the 2026-09-28 ones.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run the suite on three historical binaries: the 2026-09-28 master (148 bp, Markov chain), 3684f74 and 4a5672d. If no metric separates the 148 bp/Markov binary from 4a5672d beyond the 2-seed spread, the suite is blind to known large gaps and not worth its 1-2 h per merge. If 4a5672d turns any group from supported to refuted beyond the seed spread, the suite has found a real regression current gates missed.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 40-60 min: re-spike round 2b's SNV, DEL5-19 and INS5-19 events, both directions, with 4a5672d, then run round3.py - covers the 5 currently supported group x direction cells.
ideas.impact: Protects the realism claims the hospital demo will rest on; makes 'keep the transplant verdicts' an executable falsifier for M21, M11 and quality work; catches silent regressions from model changes such as v2.
ideas.risks: 1-2 h of compute per merge clashes with 'speed matters': run on request or nightly. Groups at their power limit (11 of 16 inconclusive) will flicker; gate only on clear flips (see M45). Event lists from GIAB benchmark regions don't cover hard clinical regions. Disk per run (round 2b is 3.6 GB).
ideas.history_check: Byte-identity gates (threads step 1, quality-speed B1) and K7 exist but guard output identity or validate rows, not realism against real carriers. No realism regression suite exists. Nothing refuted. The read-length look (3684f74) shows why 2 seeds are needed.

ideas.title: Graded broken-control ladder and power table: give every 'supported' verdict a minimum detectable dose and offset
ideas.problem: The only broken controls are B1 (VAF 0.25, a half dose) and B2 (200 bp off). A 'supported' verdict only says spike is not as wrong as a half dose - in some metrics not even that. Nobody knows the smallest error each metric can see, so verdicts cannot be read quantitatively or used to size future rounds; shared-site n (33 DUPs) caps several verdicts.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED: round 3: B1 only 'unsure' on E for DEL1-4, DEL20-49, INS1-4 and INS20-49, and on A of DEL20-49 (rho 1.89-2.72) - the rule cannot tell half dose from full there (2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:191-201); round 1b 50-299 bp: B1 failed by only 0.001 (memory validation-plan.md); DUP50-299 reverse rho 2.81 with interval 1.50-5.06 on 33 shared DUPs; the read-length K2 flip was a seed draw (3684f74). MEASURED (R31) from round3/run/evidence3.tsv: across-site variance / per-site counting noise is 2.51-4.01 for INS20-49 A, 3.36-5.85 for DUP J, 0.78-1.28 for SNV and DEL5-19 A - site effects dominate INS20-49 and DUP metrics, so only paired same-site designs have power there. A second whole-genome HG002 library exists (/home/parlar_ai/dev/sv_caller/data/giab_hg38/HG002/HG002.novaseq.pcr-free.35x.bwamem2.dedup.grch38_no_alt.bam), usable as a cross-library real-vs-real yardstick at every HG002 site.
ideas.proposal: Add control arms at VAF 0.45, 0.40, 0.35 (0.25 exists) and offsets 10, 25, 50, 200 bp, each with 2 seeds. For each metric x group estimate the dose and offset at which the locked rule fails >=80% of bootstrap draws (minimum detectable effect). Publish an MDE table and report each verdict as 'supported within +-X% dose / Y bp'. Drop metrics that cannot see a half dose (E in four groups). Use the table to size n per group (e.g. how many shared DUPs for an interval inside 2.25). Report a cross-library HG002-vs-HG002 c alongside (looser; use only to widen n_c, never to replace the same-run yardstick).
ideas.simplest_version: One extra arm at VAF 0.40 for the 5 currently supported cells (SNV both directions, DEL5-19 both, INS5-19 reverse), scored with round3.py unchanged.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: If the VAF 0.40 arm already fails every counted metric in every supported cell (rho's 5th percentile above 2.25), the current tests resolve a 20% dose error, the ladder adds little, and work stops. If VAF 0.40 passes in supported cells, 'supported' only bounds the dose error to 20-50% - a documented limit on every current verdict, and the ladder must be run. A wrong analysis must fail: the ladder's fail probability must rise with dose error; a non-monotone curve means the rule is noise-dominated.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 30-45 min: spike round 2b's forward SNV and DEL5-19 events (200) at VAF 0.40 with current master, score with round3.py.
ideas.impact: Makes every realism verdict quantitative ('spike's SNVs are indistinguishable from real within +-X% evidence'), quotable by the hospital; lets future rounds be sized rather than guessed; stops low-power metrics producing perpetual inconclusives.
ideas.risks: Compute per arm. MDE depends on the binary (recompute when M44 runs). A dose ladder misses shape errors (quality, strand) which M40 and M42/M43 cover. A misused cross-library yardstick would make passing easier.
ideas.history_check: B1 and B2 exist since round 1 but were never graded. R_c < 1 still unexplained (round3 plan:222-232); the across-site spread measured here shows why rho intervals are wide where site effects dominate. Nothing refuted. Astra's 2x2 design (memory) needs complete local haplotypes and is separate.

ideas.title: Whole-sample acceptance test for the hospital route: spiked vs unspiked raredisease outputs, with a FASTQ-route sham that sets the pipeline's own noise floor
ideas.problem: The owner's product is raredisease run on a full spiked FASTQ. Nothing measures what else changes genome-wide, and the pipeline is not reproducible to the call (TIDDIT runs differ by thousands of calls), so a raw diff cannot be read. The FASTQ route removes originals from the middle of the file and appends SPIKE_ reads at the end, shifting bwa-mem2's -K 100000000 batch boundaries (which carry per-batch insert-size estimates) for every later read, so alignments far from any event could change (inferred, unmeasured). fastp and MarkDuplicates may remove planted evidence, and nothing checks per-event survival of SPIKE_ fragments in the final BAM.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED (memory sv-caller-slices.md): two TIDDIT FULL runs differ by ~2,400 calls genome-wide; Manta and CNVnator FULL runs deterministic. raredisease aligns with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000 (memory validation-plan.md). MEASURED (R32): fastp with hospital flags (--detect_adapter_for_pe --length_required 40 --correction) on K2b 35x sets drops real 0.77% (964/125,364), spike 0.88% (seed 21) and 0.80% (seed 22); too-many-N real 32, spike 0 (small differences; N gap is M2's). Hospital unspiked raredisease outputs exist for both GIAB samples (cnv_validation/from_rv/.../raredisease_results/call_snv, call_sv, repeat_expansions). validate never reads SIM_ALT_FRAGS (src/validate.rs:83-101). DOCUMENTED: F2 checked only the SPIKE_ records (1,296/1,296 identical to sim.bam), not the rest of the genome.
ideas.proposal: A locked acceptance protocol per demo sample with three raredisease runs at the hospital: the existing unspiked baseline, the spiked FASTQ, and a sham FASTQ (raw minus a set of original pairs equal in number to the spike's removals and clustered like them, re-appended unchanged at the end). Report per caller: sham vs baseline (noise floor); spiked vs baseline outside footprints (must not exceed the sham); inside footprints background integrity (M41); at planted events call, GT, GQ and rank score against real-carrier distributions from M42/M43. Audit per event the SPIKE_ fragments that survive into the final BAM against SIM_ALT_FRAGS, so losses in fastp, alignment or markdup are visible.
ideas.simplest_version: An order-sensitivity check run here: align a 2M-pair hospital-like FASTQ subset with bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000 twice, once in original order and once with 1% of pairs moved to the end; count records whose position, MAPQ or flags change. If none change, the sham is needed only for TIDDIT.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: If sham-vs-baseline differences are zero for DeepVariant and Manta and spiked-vs-baseline differences outside footprints are zero too, the sham adds nothing for those callers; keep it only for TIDDIT/gCNV. The protocol must fail a broken build: a spiked FASTQ made with an empty removal list (originals left beside replacements) must show footprint discordance and old-allele calls above the sham floor; if not, the protocol cannot see real mistakes.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 1 h: the bwa-mem2 order-sensitivity check above on the K2b FASTQs or a chr20 slice of the hospital reads (index loading dominates). Its result also decides whether M23's slot interleaving matters.
ideas.impact: Each demo sample gets a documented, defensible statement of what changed in the raredisease output and that nothing else changed beyond the pipeline's own noise - the evidence a clinical team needs before using spiked data for training or proficiency testing.
ideas.risks: Needs hospital compute and the user's access (~3 full raredisease runs per sample). GLnexus and rank-score steps add variation. The sham must mimic the spike's clustered removal pattern to be a fair floor. GIAB/demo data only, never patient data.
ideas.history_check: F2 measured alignment identity of the SPIKE_ records only. The FASTQ route has never been run on the real raw FASTQ (memories full-fastq.md, hospital-demo-plan.md). A second fastp pass on spike's reads is listed as unmeasured; the K2b numbers here suggest it is small. Nothing refuted.

ideas.title: Benchmark-ready composite truth: the background benchmark plus the planted events, with footprint stratification BEDs, so hap.py, vcfeval or truvari can score the whole spiked sample
ideas.problem: truth.vcf holds only the planted events; it is uncompressed, its sample column is 'SAMPLE', GT comes from VAF, and no regions BED is written. On a GIAB background (what the hospital will use) the natural benchmark is GIAB truth plus planted variants, but spike changes the background's non-SNPs in many footprints, so a naive 'GIAB + planted' truth scores spurious FN/GT errors around every event. There is no stratification separating planted / footprint / untouched results, and every harness rebuilds the truth by hand.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (M41/R26): 214 of 752 transplant events change at least one background indel's read AF (hom median 0.934 -> 0.479). Code read: truth.rs:115-117 writes ##fileformat and ##source=spike only; truth.rs:205 names the sample column SAMPLE; truth.rs:468-474 sets GT from VAF; no normalization code in truth.rs, vcf_input.rs or exon.rs (grep); validate_pipeline.sh:944-959 adds contig headers, bgzips and tabix-indexes by hand before Truvari. MEASURED: truvari 5.4 and 4.2.2 exist in cnv_validation's pixi environments; hap.py and rtg not installed (command -v).
ideas.proposal: A post-processing script kept outside the core: spike_truth_compose --truth truth.vcf --events events.bed --benchmark-vcf GIAB.vcf.gz --benchmark-bed GIAB.bed, writing truth.composite.vcf.gz + .tbi (background records outside event-copy footprints plus planted events, normalized with bcftools norm, with the background's sample name), confident.bed (GIAB bed minus footprints), strata BEDs and a hap.py stratification TSV (planted = event +-50 bp, footprint = +-2 kb, rest). It prints the fraction of the confident region removed so the exclusion is never silent.
ideas.simplest_version: A 30-line bash script: bedtools subtract plus bcftools view -T ^footprints, then bcftools concat and norm, then tabix.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Score unspiked HG002 DeepVariant calls against GIAB as baseline, and the spiked sample's calls against the composite truth: in the 'rest' stratum TP/FP/FN must equal the baseline within the sham noise floor (M46); a difference means spike changed something outside footprints or the composer is wrong. A broken composer keeping background records inside footprints must show the footprint FN/GT errors M41 predicts (~0.48 AF at former hom indels). If composite and naive truths give the same footprint scores, footprint handling is unnecessary; keep only bgzip, name and normalize.
