ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About 2 h: compose the truth for round 2b forward run0 (700 events) from its truth.vcf and events.bed with HG002 v4.2.1; run vcfeval (rtg container) or bcftools isec against DeepVariant calls on 50 footprints from M41's gate.
ideas.impact: The hospital and other users get a standard GA4GH-style benchmark of the whole spiked sample: recall of planted events and proof that precision elsewhere is unchanged; background damage becomes its own visible stratum; hand-made truth fix-ups in harnesses go away.
ideas.risks: Removing footprints hides CR3 rather than fixing it (always report the removed fraction; M11 fixes it). hap.py and vcfeval need containers. GIAB confident regions exclude parts of clinical genes (LDLR's Alus), so a planted event may fall outside the bed and must be scored separately. Normalizing planted indels may move POS against SIM_* bookkeeping.
ideas.history_check: Map lists 'truth VCF for benchmarking' as OPEN (bgzip/tbi, SIM_SRC_ID, SM, a benchmark-regions BED, left-normalization). Composing with the background truth and stratifying footprints is new. Nothing refuted. Shares the truth-format side fix (bgzip, SM) with M48.

ideas.title: A per-variant demo receipt: score truth.vcf against raredisease's DeepVariant, SV and ranked outputs
ideas.problem: After spike, fastq.sh (~42 min predicted) and raredisease (hours), nothing tells the owner variant by variant how the spiked variants came out: called or not, GT and AD-VAF, which SV callers supported it, whether it passed the clinical filter, where it ranked. spike validate checks reads, not calls; validate_pipeline.sh covers Delly DELs only. SNVs, indels and exon DEL/DUPs have never been run through the hospital pipeline. The truth VCF is awkward to score (not bgzipped, sample 'SAMPLE', IDs sim_*).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED (R35): the hospital raredisease run on HG002 (cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results) has call_snv/genome (DeepVariant VCF; params variant_caller=deepvariant, aligner=bwamem2), call_sv/genome (INFO svdb_origin/set/FOUNDBY), rank_and_filter *_ranked_clinical.vcf.gz (RankScore, Compounds, GeneticModels; 114 records at LDLR), repeat_expansions (stranger VCF). Real yardstick, exact-key matching of GIAB v4.2.1 HG002 records in chr19:10-13 Mb against that DeepVariant VCF: het SNV GT match 1,845/1,850 (99.73%), het indel 402/406 (99.01%), hom SNV 793/794, hom indel 199/205; the 29 multi-allelic 1/2 records match 0 by exact key (splitting/normalising needed). grep over spike scripts/ src/ README finds no reader of raredisease or DeepVariant outputs. DOCUMENTED: transplant plans scope callers out (2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:115, round2.md:185).
ideas.proposal: A scorer taking truth.vcf plus standard VCFs (--snv DeepVariant, --sv svdb-merged, --ranked genmod clinical, --repeats stranger). Per truth record: call/no-call (small variants on left-normalised split alleles; SVs on type plus reciprocal overlap >=0.5 or both breakpoints within 500 bp; SVTYPE-less ClinVar-style records classified as in M28), called GT (1 == 1/1 on a male haploid X, M12), AD-VAF vs SIM_VAF, QUAL/GQ, supporting callers from svdb_origin, presence in the clinical ranked VCF, RankScore and rank among the sample's ranked variants. Output a TSV and a one-line summary; given a GIAB truth for the same background, print the real-variant rate in the same table so a spiked miss reads against real misses. Following the owner's 2026-10-05 split, generic VCF scoring lives in spike (public) and raredisease path wiring in cnv_validation. Side fix: write truth.vcf.gz + .tbi with the BAM's SM as sample column.
ideas.simplest_version: One Python script: bcftools-norm both VCFs, exact-key match for SNV/indel, 50% reciprocal overlap for SVs, grep RankScore from the ranked VCF, one row per truth record.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Run the scorer on the unspiked hospital HG002 raredisease output with GIAB v4.2.1 records in a 3 Mb window as pseudo-truth: >=99.5% GT match for het SNVs (awk measurement 99.73%) and >=98.5% for het indels; a sham truth of 200 random benchmark-region positions with no variant gives <=1% 'called'. If representation differences push real-variant match below 95% after normalisation, the scorecard cannot tell a spike failure from matching noise (kill or redesign). Then the real test: spiked ClinVar het SNVs (genes where HG002 is reference) should be called 0/1 at a rate inside the binomial band of the real 99.7%; clearly below it is a spike realism gap.

reality:C1.better_measurement:
The yardstick needs real large tandem DUPs whose allele matches what spike plants: sequence-resolved, flank identity of 0.99 or more, unique DNA (no segdup, no tandem repeat, single-allelic), with carriers sequenced on the same short-read platform. Do the read-level check first and the caller-level check only after it passes.
(a) Read level, run on the round-3 machinery (J, E1, split-half rho, B1 af 0.25 and B2 200 bp shift controls). Plant the carrier's actual ALT sequence, not a reference copy. Possible sources: HGSVC3/HPRC long-read calls for 1KGP samples with public 30x NovaSeq CRAMs, sliced by region (read level only). Or the Q100 and Platinum sets after an identity filter, though round 2 already found too few events of 300 bp and up there.
(b) For the hospital's actual use (exon-size DUPs in genes such as LDLR), the yardstick is the lab's own archive of orthogonally confirmed exon DUP carriers (MLPA or array) run through raredisease. Compare spiked calls with those carriers. This is inferred; whether such samples exist is not checked.
A first gate costs little: count the candidates that pass identity >= 0.99, outside segdups, in a source with real carriers, before planning anything.
reality:C1.notes:
Gate B, MEASURED read-only. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/c1/ (gateb.py, nosd.tsv, q100.txt, calls_*.tsv, taken from each sample's call_sv/genome/*_sv.vcf.gz).

Selection: TRexclusion <DUP> records of 1-5 kb, with segdups excluded (cnv_validation/resources/segdups.bed.gz, +-500 bp). This leaves 36 records at 31 loci. 5 of those loci are multi-allelic and look like VNTRs (chr8:629514, chr9:93737878, chr10:952386, chr18:79830661, chr20:28754912 x4). Several others are pericentromeric (chr2:94.16M, chr3:91.55M, chr11:54.53M, chr15:17.06M, chr17:21.68M, chr22:15.9M).

Carrier lookup, DUP-type call with reciprocal overlap >= 0.5 or both ends within 500 bp:
- carrier-sample events: 6 of 146 (4.1%);
- non-carrier events: 2 of 106 (1.9%);
- records called in at least one carrier: 2.

Looser rules:
- Any DUP/INS/BND breakpoint within 500 bp: 7 records, with non-carriers 6 of 106.
- Any call of any type within +-1 kb: carriers 63 of 146 against non-carriers 51 of 106. There is no carrier enrichment, so this match is locus noise.

A crude HG002 Q100 check (an INS/DEL of 0.5-1.5x the size within 1 kb) finds 26 of 36 records absent. So at most 2 events pass SIMPLEST's filters, against the 20 required, and the idea's own kill rule fires.

The deeper reason the measurement is unsound is an allele mismatch:
- What spike plants: from_tandem_duplication (src/haplotype.rs:216-229) builds an exact reference copy.
- What the carriers carry: the 80 truth DUPs of 1 kb and up have INS_FLANK_IDENTITY median 0.956 (min 0.903). Outside segdups, only 1 of 40 is 0.99 or higher and 26 of 40 are below 0.95.
- So spike would plant a different allele from the one the carriers carry, at loci where the real alleles are mostly diverged repeat expansions. The carriers' raredisease call rate is about 4%, consistent with the report's 0.008. The report itself says the misses are absent, not mismatched.
- One data point suggests spike's exact-copy DUPs are easy to call: Manta on the full BAM found spike's 6.5 kb B3 DUP (~/sv_slice_test/score.txt).
- A gap between spiked and real call rates is therefore expected, and it would reflect the allele and the locus, not read realism. The comparison cannot license or forbid filling the report's DUP bands.

The read-level arm has the same problem. Its round-3 rho design would also need shared real-vs-real sites, and only about 10 of the 36 have any HG002 Q100 counterpart.

Other checks:
- The gap itself (no realism evidence for DUPs of 300 bp and up) is real and matters for the hospital use, so the question should be kept, with a different yardstick (see better_measurement).
- Manta callRegions on a full BAM was only probed (not locked: 245 of 279 chr19 calls identical, only off-chromosome BNDs lost).
- gCNV was never tested.

2. inv_planted second, with two strand-aware probes: ref[S-15,S)+rc(ref[E-16,E)) and rc(ref[S,S+15))+ref[E,E+16).

reality:M1.notes:
The gap in the code is real. The error draw (synth.rs:208, quality.rs:894-921) has no reference position, and wrong bases are uniform (synth.rs:719). I reproduced the 35x evidence exactly. The split-half result is a genuine, strand-specific site effect, not chance: P(B>=2 | A>=3) is 0.372 against a base rate of 0.000228, and the other strand repeats only 3.7%. v2's run bin does not create such sites: spike's 2+2 sites with >=3 reads have no run >=5 nearby.

Why weaken rather than keep:
(1) The headline "same wrong base" numbers mix in a cheaper, global mechanism, the uniform substitution matrix. Fixing only that closes about a third of the candidate gap, so it should come first or be the control.
(2) On the owner's target data (hospital NovaSeq X, 4-level qualities), 85-93% of recurrence is in Q9 bases. DeepVariant's default min_base_quality of 10 (outside knowledge, not checked here) would discard those. At BQ>=10 there are only 36 sites with >=3 reads and 49 candidates per ~0.95 Mb, against 181 and 453 in the 35x held-out set (which is deeper than this at ~19x of scored depth? no: about 19x, while the hospital is about 32x).
(3) The benchmark effect is small. For germline DeepVariant at 30x, the real-vs-spike difference is about 0.2-2 one-strand candidates per ±2 kb window. At het events the kept half of real pairs (copy_rate) already carries half the site signal. The planted allele is excluded by design.
(4) A fixed 40% overlap threshold sits at about the split-half ceiling (0.372), so the gate could reject even a perfect implementation.
Low-VAF use on 35x-like data is where the idea would matter most. A cheap first step worth its own small gate is a learned substitution matrix (global, about S cost).

This replaces the fastp control: a one-mate-edit mutant must fail it (about the overlapping-pair share discordant vs about 1% real, inferred). reality:M10.notes: REALITY (measured / code-read): for an SNV, spike suppresses every pool pair entirely inside the ±2 kb haplotype footprint at copy_rate (src/simulate.rs:250-263) and re-tiles synthetic fragments over the whole 4 kb haplotype (src/simulate.rs:817). In transplant round 2 forward, 92.3% of the 16,089 remade pairs never reach the site (measured). Synthetic reads carry only SNP background (SampleCopies is a per-base map, src/loh.rs), so background indels are erased. In the probe, hap_carry is 0 in all 17 rows and hom indels drop from mean 0.915 to 0.509; het ones also lose AF (het80.tsv 0.46->0.27, 0.26->0.05; workflow-measured). The gain is in flank realism, and in background calls near every spiked SNV for the hospital raredisease demo. P1b also makes SNV spikes independent of the synthetic quality model (v2 still loses base/context dependence, K5) and far cheaper per event (inferred: a few edited reads instead of about 200 tiled pairs). reality:M13.better_measurement:
Use a paired design at each site and pre-register the gate before any build.

**Step 1: reference only, minutes.** Take the 19 sequence-resolved ClinVar LDLR DELs as the yardstick. Round both ends to 100 bp, apply the snap rule, and require two things:
- (a) the snapped set reproduces the real junction-class mixture: about 3/19 at 10 bp or more, 11/19 at 2 bp or more, and a both-in-Alu rate of about 6/19;
- (b) the snap lands on the real junction haplotype clearly more often than chance.

The proposed SIMPLEST rule already fails this. It snapped 19/19 rounded real events and 22/22 demo records, all to 10 bp or more of homology (10-37 bp), and moved ends by up to 827 bp. It recovered the real junction in at most 1/19 (226298). It also changed the exons covered in 2/22 demo records (ex16-17_partial18 to ex16-18, and ex2-12 to ex2-14).

**Step 2: read level.** Plant into HG002, with the same seed, each real ClinVar event in three forms:
- (a) at its true junction;
- (b) shifted to a nearby blunt junction with the same size and the same exons;
- (c) the same event with its ends rounded, then snapped.

Measure Manta call/no-call and breakpoint error, split-read and discordant-pair counts, and junction-read MAPQ. For the round-1b GIAB HG001 Alu-Alu DELs, also compare against HG001's real reads at the same site.

**Decision.** If (b) differs from (a) by no more than the spread between seeds, the junction class does not matter to the aligner or the callers. Then only document that exon specs cut at exon edges, and kill the snapping.

The proposed measurement does not do this. It compares snapped demo records against real-vs-real spread at other loci. Junction homology is guaranteed by snapping, so it cannot fail, and MAPQ and clip counts depend on the locus.
reality:M13.notes:
**What holds.** Rounded and exon-edge junctions are random-like. Demo DELs: 1/19 have 2 bp or more of homology and 12/19 are blunt. Random same-length events give 16.6% and 56% (measured). Real sequence-resolved LDLR DELs: 11/19 have 2 bp or more and 3/19 have 20 bp or more. So the microhomology-level gap is real and has not been built or refuted.

**What does not hold.** The mechanism is "Alu-first NAHR snapping", and the local data does not support it. Real LDLR DEL ends sit in Alus at about the background rate (6/19 both ends vs 26-29% random). LDLR is so Alu-dense that a ±1 kb search always finds a same-orientation pair (22/22 and 19/19). The SIMPLEST rule would therefore turn every event into a long-homology NAHR junction. That is about 100% against a real share of about 16%, so it over-corrects into the opposite bias and makes the snap position seed-dependent.

**Cheaper fix, in line with "model what really happens".**
1. Replace or relabel the demo VCF with the sequence-resolved ClinVar LDLR DELs and DUPs; that is M29 part 2. VCF input already plants them, as B1-B3 did.
2. Document in the README that exon specs cut exactly at exon edges.
3. Only if Step 2 shows that the junction class changes Manta or MAPQ behaviour: add opt-in intronic ends with a junction class sampled from an empirical mixture (blunt / 2-9 bp microhomology / 20 bp or more homology) measured on real sequence-resolved deletions. Record the original in CIPOS/CIEND and SIM_SNAP.

reality:M15.better_measurement: The co-carry core of the test is nearly tautological. Trans co-carry count must be at or below the 99% binomial upper bound at the per-base mismatch rate measured at those same sites in the real BAM. Cis co-carry share must be at or above the real cis share minus a binomial margin. Lead with what the pipeline actually sees, and lock these checks: (i) each site's AF inside validate allele_freq's 99% band at 0.5; (ii) BINNED depth across the union footprint within binomial noise of unspiked; (iii) DeepVariant calls 0/1 at both sites; (iv) genmod lists the pair (this passes trivially for a singleton, so it does not discriminate; only a trio, M17, would). Report the broken baseline separately for each coin outcome. Choose seeds where the two coins match and where they differ, because --allow-overlap is roughly right in the trans case. Add the single-MNV workaround as a second baseline for cis. A trans group replaces about 100% of reads over the union footprint (roughly 4.3 kb or more). So compare that window's realism metrics against a single AF-1.0 event and against real: duplicate share (0.008 vs 0.036 documented), crashed ends (0.008% vs 1.10% documented) and soft clips.

Editing copy-1 or copy-2 fragments at each site makes cis/trans exact, with no union footprint and no fully remade trans window. - a refusal for hap= with an unphased gVCF;

reality:M2.corrected_claims:
1. "spike never writes an N" is wrong as a general claim. It writes N at Q2 for reference Ns, for padding past a contig end, and for padding after a deletion error uses up the template (synth.rs:189-203 and 245-248; README ~1960). It is true for the 20 K2b blocks: 0 N in spike21 (measured, phys/errproc_35x.out).
2. "spike's R1 errs 1.9-2.2x real R1": the numbers are right, but mate pooling explains them only at Q25. Pooled real Q25 is 0.317% (inferred, computed from errproc_35x.out counts), against spike's R1 0.351% and R2 0.402%. At Q37 pooled real is 0.0119%, yet spike's R1 (0.0186%) and R2 (0.0234%) are both above it, by 1.56x and 1.97x. So about 1.75x of the Q37 excess is not caused by pooling the mates (inferred). phys/hiq_35x.out puts it in the last 10 cycles of class >=35 reads: spike 3.77e-4 against real 9.01e-5, 4.2x (measured). learnmask_35x.out shows 2,226 of the 4,202 high-Q errors the learning rule counts are clipped-end bases (measured). On the hospital data, that band is Q9, which is below the default minimum base quality of 10 in DeepVariant make_examples (min_base_quality=10) and GATK HaplotypeCaller (--min-base-quality-score 10). This is documented in the tools' docs, cited from knowledge, not checked here. Those errors do not enter candidate counts. The bands callers see are Q24, with top-alt 0.864/0.833, and Q40, with 0.625/0.592 (measured, errproc_hosp.out). The gap there is still large against spike's 0.35-0.36. The SIMPLEST version's split at Q15 would merge Q25 (C->A 0.89-0.92) with Q37, whose spectrum is different and mostly transitions (35x R1 Q>=30: A->G 0.58, T->C 0.60). Code citations: quality.rs:253-264 (no mate key; class cuts are shared, ReadState has no mate, error_rate takes none), quality.rs:1006 (N left out), quality.rs:1014 (only base != r is stored), synth.rs:719-728 (alt base drawn uniformly). reality:M2.notes:
Every claim about the code checks out on master 4a5672d:
- The error table has no mate dimension, and mates share the class cuts. ReadState has no mate field and error_rate takes no mate argument, so mates differ in error rate only through class and context.
- A wrong base is drawn uniformly among the other three.
- N is left out of learning, so a drawn Q2 falls back to the nominal 0.63 error rate and is emitted as a called base.

The idea's measured numbers match phys/errproc_35x.out, phys/errproc_hosp.out, phys/learnmask_35x.out and the hospital fastp.json. spike21 comes from the K2b held-out set (learned on 63,040 even-hash pairs, odd-hash pairs written) and is byte-identical to current master.

Real gaps, worth building and cheap:
- the substitution spectrum (top-alt 0.69-0.86 real against 0.34-0.36 spike, in every band);
- Q2 emitted as a called base instead of N;
- the R1/R2 ratio.

Problems:
- The +-20% absolute Q37 gate would fail for a reason the mate split does not touch: spike over-errs at Q37 about 1.75x on both mates, mostly in the last 10 cycles of good reads, and half the high-Q errors the learning rule counts are clipped-end bases.
- The caller-impact argument uses the wrong band for the hospital data (Q9 falls below callers' minimum base quality 10).
- The clip-boundary mask goes against the bad-tails finding.
- The SIMPLEST version's Q15 split merges different spectra.
- The Q>=30 spectrum is mostly transitions in both samples. It may be partly unmasked variants or damage, so learning it from spike's 10% pileup mask may build those variants into the high-Q emission.
- The spectrum closes only part of the candidate-site gap (500/Mb real against 93/Mb spike). Real data's site-recurrent same-strand errors (181 sites against 2) are a separate process.
- Q2 to N affects about 2.3e-5 of bases, so its effect is on FastQC and fastp counts, not on calls.
- Cost is more than about 40 lines once you count a per-symbol matrix, the mate factor, the mask change, tests and the K7 rerun, so a small 2 rather than S.

Recommendation: keep the emission matrix (per quality symbol, true base and mate, with backoff), Q2 to N, and a mate observed/expected factor. Narrow the mask to I/D. Re-lock the gates as described in better_measurement.

The suppression applies to pairs wholly Inside event ±HAP_FLANK (main.rs:241, 2000). 2. The local depth shape is diluted, not "discarded". Outside a DUP's copies, output = (1-v)D + vC, and the (1-v) share keeps the donor's shape. Inside a DUP, output = (1-v)D + 2vC (CR2 formula, CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:66-67). 3. So proposal (a), "leave untouched", also changes merge.sh semantics, not only tiling. 4. The idea's flagship bin would be dropped by its own falsifier (2). I measured it on the 35x BAM with samtools view -c -F 0xF04 [-q 20]: chr20:14862000-14863000 has 82 of 103 reads at MAPQ >= 20 (79.6%, below the 95% bar). Its all-MAPQ count is also thin: 103, against 279 at chr20:14700000-14701000 and 294 at chr20:15000000-15001000. So the thin depth is mostly real, not only mappability. 5. "today 81.09x" was measured on the Codex base binary 4efa0f4 and not re-measured on master. On master's lineage the same probe gives SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 3.88 (9ed9db1). The 40-DUP folds of 1.11-2.46 come from 10 kb DUPs (README.md:1866). 6. The sham falsifier (3) cannot run through the CLI, which refuses allele fractions outside (0.0, 1.0] (main.rs:263-268). 7. Keeping legacy depth copies, which use a >=50%-overlap rule (synth.rs:471-480), and also replacing E-crossing event-copy pairs with their junction image has three effects: (a) the E-crossers' copy-2 image, which matches the reference to the right of E, is lost; (b) the S-crossers get reference-contiguous copies that bleed into the flank left of S; (c) the junction right parts are added on top of the interior copies near S. Each error is about one fragment length (~420 bp) at each end. The ownership rule has to be: an original wholly inside [S,E) gets one jittered copy; an E-crosser keeps its original plus one junction image; an S-crosser gets nothing extra. 8. A DUP still emits about v·N_inside new pairs (~63k for this DUP, against 120k today), so it is not "nearly append-only" in synthetic count; it is only in removals. In the BAM route, alignment work falls from ~186k to ~63k pairs, but only if kept pairs stop being realigned. 9. The SNV inference checks out: with a 4001 bp haplotype and f = 421, about 421/3581 ≈ 12% of starts touch the site, so ~88% do not.
reality:M21.better_measurement: Run Gate B first. It needs no build and the tooling exists: scripts/cr2_probes.py, cr2_run.sh and cr2_score.py, plus the 35x HG002 BAM. Use the master binary with --dup-model junction against full, on the 1 Mb chr20 DUP and the dup_variable probe. Leave out bins within 1 kb of S and E, where junction mode's additive junction reads and the >=50%-overlap bleed sit. (a) The absolute saving is about 2 s per run at default threads. The idea's own Gate B already fails by an order of magnitude on the transplant campaign: about 35 s against a 10-min bar.

reality:M25.notes:
Verdict: weaken. The gap is real and the timings reproduce, but some labels are off, the simplest version probably misses its own gate, and the one-pass plan is lower priority rather than refuted.

**The code (checked on master ba9f4e7):**
- **Duplicate scan.** removed_duplicates (origin.rs:1033-1054) calls scan_long, then Source::scan (origin.rs:751-756). For every record that does three things:
  - converts it fully with RecordBuf::try_from_alignment_record (sequence, qualities, all tags);
  - builds an OriginRecord in origin_record (origin.rs:626-663): name, chromosome and XA strings, parse_xa, placements;
  - pushes it into one growing Vec.
  Only after that is the duplicate-or-named filter applied.
- **LOH count pass.** walk_cigar_count (loh.rs:810) does one SipHash HashMap<u64,[u32;4]> entry per aligned base.
- **LOH collect pass.** It builds a String per record (loh.rs:1088) and does a HashSet<u64> contains per base (loh.rs:1236).
- **Order.** call_snps sorts the het SNPs by position and keeps hom-alts in a map, so a dense Vec should give byte-identical output (inferred).
- **Pass 2.** It is a serial re-read with names built only for records that pass the filter (extract.rs:118-180).

**Gate B, measured.** I copied quality-speed-run/bin/spike-new to scratchpad m25prof (md5 df547601763d). I ran the same 1 Mb DUP (seed 1, 1 thread) under a gdb sampler, one sample every ~0.1 s, 249 samples in all. The outputs were md5-identical to the ideator's run: R1, R2, truth.vcf, replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt.

| Step | Samples | What the samples were in |
|---|---|---|
| Startup quality sample | 1-96 | |
| Event pass 1 + pass 2 | 97-109 | pass 2 about 4 samples |
| Census | 112-115 | |
| class_mix | 116-118 | |
| LOH count pass | 15 | hashing or rehash 6; walk_cigar_count's own time 6 (hash probing inlined); inflate 1 |
| LOH collect pass | 10 | walk_cigar_collect 5; inflate 4 |
| Tiling | about 49 | |
| After the event | 8 | |
| Duplicate scan | 22 | RecordBuf conversion 8; growth of the Vec<OriginRecord> (realloc up to 50 MB) 3; free 1; inflate 2; filter, seen set, duplicates_of grouping and drop 8 |
| FASTQ write | about 23 | |

**What this means:**
- Inflating is a minority of each scan: 2 of 22 samples in the duplicate scan, 1 of 15 in the count pass. So the idea's falsifier, "decoding dominates", does not fire, and the per-record fixes are well aimed.
- Pass-2 strips can save at most about 0.3 s/Mb (about 0.9 s on 3 Mb, inferred), even where it runs serially at 16 threads, against the documented 26.5 s for the 3 Mb DUP at 16 threads. Dropping that plan is justified.
- The simplest duplicate-scan fix would save about 30% of the scan (inferred). The full fix would build the 5' key from the raw record for passing records only, without XA, and use a hashed set; it plausibly reaches 50% or more.
- The dense-Vec pileup is likely the cleanest gain: about 1 s/Mb at 1 thread (inferred).
- Total realistic gain is about 2-3 s/Mb at 1 thread (inferred). The default is 4 threads, where these passes already run in chunks, so the gain is about 1-3 s on a 3 Mb event.
- spike's own time is small next to merge.sh and fastq.sh, and it does not touch the hospital LDLR goal. Value is low.

The one-pass plan should be marked "deprioritized", not "dropped". Once the per-record work is fixed, inflating becomes a larger share of each pass, and the plan may come back.

2. The doubling is a load-time spike only, not a run-long cost. ReferenceReader is a local in load (reference.rs:224) and its cache is freed when load returns. RSS trace of a full 23-SNV run, 1 thread, written by a parallel agent (m26/out2.rss; out2.log: MAXRSS 6,114,252 kB, 2890 MB loaded):

'Indices into the pool' would keep each pool alive, and a pool holds more than its kept set.

reality:M28.notes:
I found no history or refutation against the idea, and its evidence checks out against the files in scratchpad cv/ and rf8/ and against the code.

**What fails today.** Records of 50 bp or more without SVTYPE take the SmallVariant path. A sequence-resolved DUP or insertion longer than a fragment is then tiled only where fragments overlap reference, so the copy gets no extra depth. SIM_ALT_FRAGS is structurally 0 once the insertion is longer than a read, and the warning blames rarity. This hits 2 of the 3 P/LP LDLR DUPs (251140 at 8.1 kb, 976329 at 6.5 kb) plus the 8.1 kb Indel 3767245. DELs are planted almost the same on either path: 306 vs 307 pairs, though SIM_ALT_FRAGS reads 21 vs 41 because the two paths count evidence differently. Their truth record has no SVTYPE/END and is labelled 'SNV'.

**Why it matters for the hospital demo.** In the RF8 census the cnv_validation BED's 1 bp DUP intervals made all 4 DUP rows 1 bp events with no warning. That trap is outside spike, but it shows the coordinate route is error-prone too.

**Priorities.** The core value is DEL/DUP routing plus the ClinVar ID (and gene) in truth. The contig alias, --vcf-ids, HGVS and the under-50 bp warning are conveniences; bcftools rename-chrs already handles the alias, and refusing a contig mismatch is safe. The alias must refuse when both spellings exist.

**Design cautions.**
- Prefer the allele shape plus a reference check over CLNVC alone. CLNVC=Duplication for 403639 is left-aligned (its HGVS position is shifted 5 bp), and the DUP path does not check that the copy matches the reference. All 3 P/LP DUPs pass the downstream-equality check today.
- Do not refuse short delins records the small path already plants correctly.
- Decide on N runs in ALT before the INS route goes live.
- Threshold choice: the physics break is "changed span longer than a read" (about 150 bp), not 50 bp. 50 bp is right for labelling, but routing a 60 bp deletion changes bytes for little physical gain. State this in the plan.

reality:M33.better_measurement:
Isolate the mechanism on the same reads, and predict from data before the run.

1. **Inputs.** Take a chr20 window of the 35x bwa BAM, which is marked. Make a twin with `samtools view --remove-flags 0x400`, reheadered without the samtools markdup @PG. Same reads, aligner, seed and events.

2. **Locked prediction.** Compute it before running, from the window's own markdup family sizes. Expected VAF = vR / (vR + Σ(1−v^k)) for unphased pairs, and the whole-family formula for pairs loh phases. Weight the two by the run's logged phased share.

3. **Runs.** Plant ≥300 het SNVs plus about 5 het 10 kb full-model DUPs. Run `samtools fixmate -m` and `samtools markdup` on both merged BAMs, or better, the full-FASTQ route with bwa-mem2 + Picard, as raredisease does.

4. **Readouts.** Read-level VAF pooled per site: SPIKE_-named non-duplicate reads over all non-duplicate reads, with a bootstrap CI over sites, as a paired difference. Also two depth readouts:
   - footprint depth against outside: predicted 1.11x at v=0.5 and 1.15x at v=1 on the unmarked twin (inferred);
   - het-DUP depth ratio: predicted about 1.65-1.69 against 1.50 (inferred). This is likely the larger, CNV-relevant harm.

5. **Kill rule.** The harm claim dies if the paired VAF difference is under 0.01 and its CI excludes the prediction.

reality:M34.corrected_claims:
1. Wrong placement path. simulate.rs:926-946 (sample_ref_overlapping_start) only runs when the haplotype has novel sequence (has_novel, i.e. an INS; simulate.rs ~1041-1061). DEL, INV, small variants and full-model DUP draw `rng.gen_range(0..=max_start)` over the whole haplotype (simulate.rs ~1063). Junction-DUP and fusion events use breakpoint zones (~1032). So the proposed simplest fix, inside sample_ref_overlapping_start, would not change the measured chr20 DEL at all and would fail its own 123 -> 0 test. The fix has to send every placement through an N-aware interval sampler, and also cut N out of the breakpoint zones. This stays byte-identical on N-free haplotypes: in rand 0.8.5, gen_range(0..n) is gen_range(0..=n-1) (uniform.rs:515), and with no novel sequence the interval union is [0, max_start].
2. Contig ends are not a tiling gap. Haplotype constructors clamp flanks at the contig end (haplotype.rs:134-137, tests at 1413-1500), and generate_haplotype_read_pair returns None when the haplotype is too short (synth.rs:571-573), so a tiled fragment never runs past a contig end. The N padding the idea cites (synth.rs:51, test at 1561) belongs to template_at: generate_read is #[cfg(test)], and generate_read_pair is reached only through generate_depth_pair in the legacy junction-DUP model. Also, all 24 GRCh38 primary contigs start and end in an N run of at least 10 kb (measured: 48 end runs), so a contig end is only reached through an N run.
3. 'Count and depth are scaled as if those starts were real' is misleading. Starts are uniform and n is proportional to starts, so depth over real sequence is already coverage x VAF (inferred from the n formula at simulate.rs:805-817). The cost is wasted all-N fragments, not wrong depth. The fix lowers the count but keeps real-sequence depth the same.
4. 'RF8 already refuses most such sites' is inferred, and it fails at C1R. There is a 1 kb N gap at chr12:7083650-7084650 (checked with samtools faidx; 0 HG002 reads inside it). The C1R exons 1.2-1.9 kb away have 97/98 and 72/73 proper-pair MAPQ>=20 reads, so RF8 would let them through.

reality:M34.notes:
Verdict: weaken. The N half of the gap is real. I recounted the R50 numbers from the run's FASTQ, they match, and the problem can reach a clinical gene: C1R, where RF8 would let it through. Four things weaken it:
- The cited function and the proposed simplest fix do not touch the placement path used by the measured DEL. The fix has to change the main uniform draw at simulate.rs ~1063 and the breakpoint zones, not only the CR5 sampler.
- The contig-end half is not a tiling gap: haplotypes are clamped at the contig end, fragments must fit inside them, and GRCh38 primary contigs end in N runs anyway.
- Depth over real sequence is not inflated; the cost is impossible all-N or mostly-N SPIKE reads. These come out of bwa-mem2 unmapped and their names give the spike away, which matters for the full-FASTQ hospital route.
- The N-rate gate is unsound, because spike has no no-call model.

- Real proper pairs do exist right at the gap edge (HG002: 20 proper MAPQ>=20 reads at chr20:60000-60100). Rejecting fragments that cover N, rather than reads that cover N, fits that. It will also drop real-looking fragments whose unsequenced middle spans a 100-N gap placeholder, which is minor.
- Keep isolated Ns placeable: primary contigs have 144 N runs under 10 bp.
- After the fix, SIM_DEPTH_FOLD should leave N bins out, or it will keep warning on gap bins where no reads are placed.

reality:M39.better_measurement:
Gate B's rule "if identical, keep concatenation" is biased toward building, for three reasons:
- bwa-mem2 -K sets the batch size in bases. Concatenating shifts the batch boundaries for lanes 2-7, and with them the per-batch insert-size estimates, so a byte comparison of primary records will almost surely fail on a handful of reads (inferred).
- Duplicate flags should match apart from ties, because LB is absent in both layouts (measured "Unknown Library").
- A 2 Mb region at 30x is about 1-2 bwa batches in total, against 7 small per-lane batches. That is not the batch makeup of a whole genome.

A better test:
1. Add a null: the same reads concatenated in two lane orders, plus the per-lane layout.
2. Count the reads whose primary alignment, MAPQ, proper-pair flag or duplicate flag differ. Call the layout difference real only if it is clearly above the null.
3. Judge by calls, not records: DeepVariant genotype and GQ, and Manta, at the spiked events and in the background of the region.
4. Report the optical-duplicate metric change on its own, since it is metrics-only under TAGGING_POLICY DontTag.

This can be tried here first on pseudo-lanes: pairs from the HG002 BAM via samtools collate/fastq, split into 7 chunks. That tests the only channel left that can move calls, the bwa batch effect.

Drop check (c), the chi-square on SPIKE_ pairs per lane against removed originals per lane. It only checks that the code follows its own design, and nothing in raredisease is known to read the per-lane share of SPIKE_ reads.
reality:M39.notes:
The gap is real in code but small in consequence:
- --into-fastq takes exactly one pair (num_args = 2).
- fastq.sh is one awk over one pair and refuses a lane that lacks listed names.
- SPIKE_ names take the BAM's most common RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE.

The 7-lane layout of the family runs is measured correctly. But two of the stated harms are wrong (see corrected_claims): the trio/pedigree framing, and the claim that a SPIKE_ read can name a lane its file does not hold. The read-group merge cannot change duplicate flags, because there is no LB and duplicate marking is per library. It is also invisible to DeepVariant. What remains is the bwa per-batch insert-size channel, plus cosmetic MultiQC and samplesheet shape.

There is a cheap alternative that needs no code and should come before any M-sized feature, written as a documented recipe:
1. Run fastq.sh on the concatenated pair.
2. Split each spiked output back into per-lane files by the RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE fields (2-4) of each read name. Raw and SPIKE_ names share that layout, so SPIKE_ reads land in the lane they claim.
3. Write a 7-row samplesheet.

This keeps every raw record byte-identical and in order within its lane, keeps found-vs-wanted exact, and keeps each name's lane equal to its file's lane. That covers checks (a), (b) and (d). Only the proportional spread of SPIKE_ reads is missing, and no consumer of it is known.

Build the full proposal (lane lists, samplesheet parsing, proportional spread, per-lane renaming) only if the null-controlled Gate B above shows layout-dependent call differences at the spiked sites. Hospital use is also not urgent: the current demo backgrounds are single-lane, and the family BAMs and raw FASTQs are not on this machine.

- (iii) Background SNPs in footprints are kept, and only non-SNPs are dropped.
- (iv) Mutant check: a composer whose footprint exclusion is switched off must re-admit the 159 hom indels in the 121 fell-below footprints.

- Take the before calls from the hospital's own DV 1.6.1 calls (call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz).
- Score both against the naive and composite truths.

- a whole-sample spiked FASTQ run through raredisease (M46);
- the hospital's unspiked DV VCF as the baseline;
- a sham whole-sample run (zero events, or the replaced originals put back unchanged) as the noise floor, because realignment and DV are not bit-stable across inputs.

Compare per-variant TP/FP/FN transitions (paired, McNemar-style) in 'rest' against the sham-to-baseline transitions, with the SeraCare mask applied. A pass means the spiked-minus-sham excess is inside the sham's binomial 95% band.

Use vcfeval or hap.py through a pulled container, since neither is on disk. Use bcftools isec only after norm, because it is representation-sensitive.

2. Keep background SNPs in footprints. Spike preserves them: 0 of 198 hom SNPs changed.
3. Compute footprints as span ± HAP_FLANK (2000), not from events.bed (± --flank, 10 kb by default) and not as POS ± 2 kb for SVs.

- Spike HG001-only het SNVs and indels into HG002, using raredisease's own commands.
- Compare the spiked call's DeepVariant GQ, QUAL, AD-VAF and DP with the same variant's real call in HG001's raredisease VCF (D25-7403.../call_snv/genome/NA12878_snv.vcf.gz exists).

- Stratify by GC, mappability and exon status before comparing. The case file's selection/composition rule forbids comparing exonic ClinVar sites to all GIAB records in a 3 Mb window.

Include a broken-spike control that must fail, for example VAF 0.25 or uniform qualities. Without one, a 99.7% call-rate band shows nothing.

For the SV half, Gate B is a regression check against score.py, not a validity test. Add a sham-planted SV (truth record, no edit) that must come out 'missed'.

reality:M49.better_measurement:
1. Make the scorer aware of homology. Count a SPIKE_ read as misplaced only if its true-origin alignment scores better than the aligner's alignment, taking the primary and the SA together (the "equally good alignment" test used by aligner benchmarks). Or allow placements anywhere inside the junction's homology interval, found by extending identity left and right of the join. Lock this rule before running.
2. Check the TSV's per-read flags against an independent placer on INV, tandem DUP, INS and fusion events as well as DELs, so the RC off-by-one mutant can fail.
3. To pin a caller miss on alignment or on calling, use a real yardstick: spiked reads against real carriers of look-alike Alu-Alu DELs (M43 and the transplant events). Compare clip/SA rates and discordant-pair counts per event. Per-read truth on spike reads alone cannot say whether a real carrier would be missed too.
reality:M49.notes:
**What holds up.** The gap is real: no per-read truth file is written. Outputs are R1/R2, truth.vcf, events.bed, replaced_reads.txt, fastq_removed_reads.txt, the scripts and README. PairSpans flows only into pairs_showing, at simulate.rs:299-315 and 1111. A TSV-only version is cheap and would not change bytes or the RNG.

**Gate B, measured now (read-only).** I re-ran it on the existing run of the same event:
- Run: scratchpad inspect/ld1, i.e. /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/inspect/ld1/run/sim.bam. Hospital HG002, spike bdd568a, seed 1, hospital `bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000`. Truth: SIM_ALT_FRAGS=24.
- Script: /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/skeptic_m49/gate_b.py. It places reads with locate.py-style 20-mer seeds on the ±2000 bp DEL haplotype and compares primary records only.

Results:
- 456 primary SPIKE reads placed.
- Reads wholly in a flank: 438 of 438 within 10 bp of truth.
- Junction-crossing reads: 18. Of these, 7 are within 10 bp. The other 11 are off by exactly 2135 bp: their pre-junction bases were aligned onto the right-hand Alu copy.
  - Example: SPIKE_ev0001_hap_000011 has `16S26M1D109M` at 11129150, against a true 11127015.
  - The off reads carry 0-42 bp soft clips and no SA; MAPQ is 60 in 7 of the 11.
- A samtools faidx check shows why. The ~26 bp before each breakpoint are near-identical AluSx sequence, and the bases after them are identical, shifted by 1. So these alignments represent the same junction through its homology; the aligner did not get them wrong.

What this means:
- The idea's kill rule (at least 99.9% within 10 bp) is not met: only 39% are.
- But a "within 10 bp of truth" scorer would flag most junction reads as misplaced at exactly the Alu-Alu junctions it is meant to diagnose, so the metric as written is unsound.
- The useful fact is that bwa explains about 11 of 18 junction reads as a 1-bp deletion plus a short clip, with no split alignment, which leaves Manta little split-read evidence. That came out of existing outputs (read names plus truth.vcf) with a ~70-line script.
- So the TSV saves effort mainly for INV, DUP, INS and fusions, where rebuilding the haplotype is harder. That is a modest diagnostic, not a realism gain, and on its own it still cannot say whether a real carrier would be missed.

**Recommendation.** Keep only the TSV. Record the haplotype spans, each segment's reference mapping, which copy a pair came from, and the ALT-shown flag. Validate it on INV and fusion events too. Drop or redesign the 10-bp scorer as a homology-aware equal-score test. Leave the attribution question to M43's real-carrier comparison.

reality:M5.notes:

(1) Real reads get worse at the very last cycle in both quality and error (35x R1 aligned mismatch 0.538% at cycle 151 vs 0.324% at 146-150, low share 5.76% vs 4.17%), while spike is flat (0.392 vs 0.414, low share 3.95% vs 4.01%). At today's 10- and 16-cycle bins this hardly matters. Under a dedicated last-cycle bin it would mislabel about 27% of the hospital's last-cycle learning bases, and the two groups really differ (last-base mean Q 38.80 vs 38.13, MEASURED). So the axis fix is a prerequisite for the bin on trimmed libraries, not an optional extra. All of this is cheap.

What I cut: the headline impact. The claim was that terminal errors cluster, bwa clips them in real reads, and spike spreads them into 4.2x isolated hi-Q aligned mismatches that the bins would remove. The 3' half is refuted once variants are masked (variant-free short 3' clips match). The "272" number covers both ends and is mostly the sample's own variants. Under independent draws, finer bins only push the learned errors into cycles 1-4 from the end (INFERRED: at a per-base rate near 8e-4, P(two or more in 4 cycles) is about 4e-6 per read). An isolated mismatch there is still not clipped, so the hiq ±30% criterion would most likely fail for reasons the bins do not touch, and would reject a sound change. The 4.2x excess deserves its own idea on the learning side: mask clip-end mismatches caused by variants, or by clip boundaries shared by 3 or more reads, before counting them as errors. Not this one.

The impact on callers is small: one cycle in 151 at about 0.5% error, plus the 5' start. The idea's main value is detectability (the classifier's top feature). I could not find the M40 classifier output; my lastq.py rerun gives real 34.53 vs spike 35.23, close to the quoted 34.57 vs 35.28. Find where the excess comes from before building a latent state. Each step is cheap and offline, and steps 2-4 are mutually exclusive tests:
1. Extend where.py's split (crashed × errors in the previous 30 cycles × lows in the last 16) by end bin and read class. Run it on spike seeds 22 and 23 as well, so the 76% continuation share is not resting on one seed.
2. Re-run learnmask.py, breaking the learned high-Q errors down by error-history bin and lows bin. Count how many of the "after an error, no lows" errors are (a) within 5 bp of a Q100 record or a Q100 indel, (b) in 1-4 bp clips, (c) in bad-end tails of 5 bp or more.
3. Simulate errors along the real held-out qualities, as qm2gate did, then align with bwa-mem2 on the K2b templates. Compare:
   - v2 as it is (must fail);
   - v2 with the error-history fallback keeping class and end bin. Today `mid` drops both (quality.rs:919), so sparse cells with 2+ earlier errors use rates learned from tails;
   - v2 learned with clusters next to Q100 variants and indels masked;
   - the proposed dead/alive key.
   Pass: aligned Q>=30 rate within ±20% of 1.19e-4 and reads with >=1 within ±15% of 1.42%. Constraints: bad-end clip share and crash share each |z|<3. The continuation-cell ratios (5.3x and 3.6x) must come down too, not only the totals.
4. Repeat on hosp_blocks.bam, because the hospital data is the owner's goal and the excess is unshown there.
Build the dead/alive state only if the cheaper fixes in step 3 leave the excess. Gate B's bimodality check should then also show that the excess is at the onset, not in continuation.
reality:M6.notes:
I read the code myself:
- src/quality.rs:255-264: error table levels are full (symbol, class, lows, end, run, errors so far), mid (symbol, lows, run, errors so far), then (symbol, class), then symbol. No mate key. MIN_ERROR_BASES is 200.
- error_cells, quality.rs:908-921, and the learning loop in block_errors, quality.rs:938-1040, which counts 1-4 bp clips and ends with at least 50% reference.
- synth.rs:181-241: errors are drawn per base after the quality draw, and the substitution base is uniform.
- END_BINS is 1-10 / 11-30 / 31-60 / 61+, and ERR_WINDOW is 30.

The gap is real and I reproduced it: 1.188e-4 vs 2.097e-4. But the proposed mechanism is aimed at the smaller part of it. About 13% of the excess is onset in reads that did not crash, and about 10% is in crashed reads. About 76% is spike erring again after an earlier error within 30 cycles in reads that did not crash, mostly at high quality with no lows (5.3x and 3.6x real). That points to two cheaper culprits:
- (a) The error-history fallback. In sparse cells it drops class and end bin, so tail and cluster rates get used in the middle of good reads.
- (b) The sample's own variant clusters leaking into learning: 11.3% of the learned high-Q errors sit within 5 bp of a Q100 record.
A dead/alive key might fix (a) as a side effect. It would not fix (b).

The value to callers is modest (inferred). These excess errors are random, not recurrent. recur_35x.out shows spike has 2 same-strand same-alt sites with 3 or more reads, against 181 in real data, so the missing systematic errors matter more to false calls than this excess.

The cost of L, plus the history of latent-state failures as quality models, argues for doing the cheap ablations first.

   - the breakpoint offset, using a 50 bp window, not 500;
   - call or no-call and SVTYPE.
4. Pass rule: the spiked-minus-real difference falls within the carrier-to-carrier spread for recurrent DUPs (founder alleles), or within split-half read noise where only one carrier exists.
5. Broken controls must fail:
   - af 0.25 must roughly halve PR+SR;
   - a junction shifted 200 bp must give an offset above 50 bp.
   As proposed, B2 cannot fail a call that is matched within 500 bp.
6. Locally there is nothing worth running; at most, check the 3 called satellite loci for a sanity read. A cheaper preliminary is to count how many confirmed DUP carriers the lab holds. If that count is below about 10, the band-filling use stays unlicensed.
value:C1.notes:
The gap is real. No realism evidence covers spike's DUPs of 300 bp or more, and round 3 left DUP 50-299 inconclusive. spike's large DUPs matter for LDLR: B3, a 6.5 kb DUP, was among the slice-safety events.

But the proposed yardstick cannot carry the round:
1. Its own Gate B gives n = 1, not 20.
2. The measurement is unsound in four ways:
   (a) Selecting DUPs "called in at least one carrier" inflates the carriers' rate. A leave-one-out comparison would be needed.
   (b) B2 (a 200 bp shift) cannot fail a call matched within 500 bp, and B1 (af 0.25) is not certain to stop Manta calling. At the caller level the controls are not guaranteed to fail.
   (c) The truth DUPs are long-read INS calls rewritten as <DUP>, and they sit mostly in alpha satellite or possible VNTRs. Planting an exact reference copy of [POS, END] there tests how the truth set represents the allele, not whether spike is realistic. A correct spike could look "too easy" and a broken one could pass.
   (d) The rule "both near 0.008" compares a filtered non-segdup subset with a report figure that includes segdups and satellites.

The cost of L is honest for the full version: whole-BAM merge about 1 h 42 min, callers about 72 min (memory file sv-caller-slices). But the simplest version still needs 20 events, and they do not exist locally.

The value is speculative. Nothing documented says spike will fill report bands, and the hospital use is demo data plus LDLR sensitivity checks.

Keep the gap on the roadmap, re-framed as the hospital confirmed-carrier comparison in better_measurement. The deciding input is the lab's count of MLPA- or array-confirmed DUP carriers.

All numbers here are MEASURED by read-only bcftools/python against cnv_validation files, except where marked DOCUMENTED or INFERRED. Nothing in /home/parlar_ai/dev/spike was touched.

value:C2.already_done_or_refuted: Not done and not refuted. The code says so itself: validate.rs:583 reads "DUP, INV and BND were not measured and are unchanged", and REVIEW.md:5082 and 5861 say the same. No M1-M49 idea and no case-file entry covers it. Some evidence the idea leaves out (my awk replica of split_reads_to_partner, not spike validate, so seen but not judged): spike's own DUP, INV and BND reads already pass split_reads at VAF 0.5, including at a demo site. The merged S1.bam gives the same count. (b) Older spike runs at unique chr20 sites, in scratchpad h8_*/sim.bam, give pooled counts of: a 3.7 kb DUP 12 (5/7), a 4 kb INV 32 and 25, a BND 3 (3/0). All pass the minimum of 2.
value:C2.corrected_claims:
1. Real INVs cannot be measured "on HG002's own BAM". GRCh38_HG2-T2TQ100-V1.1.vcf.gz has 0 SVTYPE=INV records and 0 records with equal-length REF/ALT of 50 bp or more (measured with zcat|grep). The 46 <INV> records are in the Platinum Pedigree VCF /home/parlar_ai/refdata/merged_hg38.svs.TRexclusion.sort.oa.vcf.gz, which is CEPH-1463, so NA12878/HG001. That file has 46 <INV> ALTs and 55 SVTYPE=INV records. NA12878 carries 45 of them, 36 are 300 bp or more, and 41 of the 45 have SUPP=1, mostly a single HiFi sawfish call. These records also write END=POS and put the length in SVLEN, e.g. chr1:181074347 END=181074347 SVLEN=605. A direct conversion would give zero-length INVs, so the truth needs END=POS+SVLEN. The measurement must run on data/giab_hg38/HG001/NA12878.final.cram (bwa 0.7.15 -Y) or the 30x D25-7403 BAM, not HG002.
2. round2.dup_candidates cannot supply DUPs of 300 bp or more. group_of returns None outside 50-299 bp (scripts/transplant/round2.py:58-59). The round-2 plan also documents larger exact duplications as "too few to test: 13 / 13 / 5 at 300-999 bp and 0 / 2 / 0 at 1 kb and up" (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-transplant-round2.md:80-81). The Platinum VCF has no DUP records at all: its types are 9,171 DEL, 15,089 INS and 55 INV.
3. "Exon DUPs and inversions, both demo targets" is half wrong. The demo plan in memory (hospital-demo-plan.md) names SNVs, small indels and exon-level DELs and DUPs. The local ClinVar LDLR SVs of 50 bp or more are 31 DEL, 4 DUP, 2 INS and 0 INV (sv-caller-slices.md).
4. The advisory flag for split_reads is set at validate.rs:622, not 619. The other line citations check out: sa_points_near at 3383, check_del_planted at 1651, junctions at haplotype.rs:581-587.
5. "Before a 20 h raredisease run": validate does not change a single read or call, and nothing in the documented hospital route makes its exit status a gate. A false FAIL costs one look at a report in which coverage_ratio, which still decides a DUP, can be read beside it.
value:C2.better_measurement:
Measure what the user would actually face: false FAILs on correct spike-ins at the target sites, plus kill arms, run before any Rust.
(A) Demo DUPs. Spike the 4 local LDLR ClinVar DUPs into the HG002 30x BAM at VAF 0.5 and 0.1, 3 seeds each. Align with the hospital command (bwa-mem2 mem -M -K 100000000) and run spike validate --json. Rule, locked first: if split_reads FAILs at most 1 of 12 runs at VAF 0.5, build no dup_planted; report VAF 0.1 separately as a power figure (RF14 saw 14 of 30 there for DEL).
(B) Real INVs, the RF14 analogue, in HG001 rather than HG002. Use the 36 NA12878 Platinum INVs of 300 bp or more, with END=POS+SVLEN. Keep the SUPP>=2 set, or the ones pbsv in HG001_GRCh38.pbsv.vcf.gz (49 INV) also calls, apart from the single-caller ones, so that a wrong truth is not scored as an aligner miss. Spike the same coordinates into HG002, which does not carry them, and check verdict agreement between real and spiked at the same site, as RF6 did (19 of 20 for DEL).
(C) Kill arms. Without them, a split_reads that always passed would still meet the proposed "at least 90% pass" rule. Use the same sites with END moved 1 kb, the unspiked BAM, and each real DUP relabelled as an INV. split_reads reads only contig and position, so the relabelled arm should pass and would demonstrate the strand-blindness the PROBLEM claims, at no cost.
(D) A note on the threshold: 90% on n of about 20 cannot be resolved (18 of 20 gives a 95% CI of about 0.68-0.99).
Seen, not judged: a cheap peek with my awk replica on the HG001 CRAM (10 s wall, results in scratchpad invpeek/result.txt) gave pooled split_reads under 2 for 11 of 45 NA12878 INVs, and 8 of 36 at 300 bp or more (about 22%, against about 60% for real DELs). The failures include HLA chr6:31.04M, the chr11:55.6M olfactory cluster, and a SUPP=3 call at chr12:71.55M. So the 90% rule as written would already trigger Step 2, before anyone knows whether these are aligner misses or truth errors.
value:C2.notes:
The gap is real only in the narrow, documented sense that split_reads was never measured on real DUP, INV or BND variants. The harm the idea claims, false alarms on correct DUPs before the demo, has no evidence behind it, and the one demo-site measurement points the other way.

Value. The LDLR 6.5 kb ClinVar DUP spiked at VAF 0.5 passes split_reads with 6 joining reads (3/3, MAPQ 60). That is measured on ~/sv_slice_test/data/B3, but it is n=1 with a replica, not validate. coverage_ratio still decides every DUP, as it does every DEL. INV and BND are not demo targets, and validate rows change no read, call or raredisease result. Where failures would really show up is low VAF and repeat-mediated joins (Alu-Alu in LDLR: 6 of 39 SVs have both ends in an Alu, per memory). RF8 refuses the worst of those anyway. In repeat units a planted row shows only that spike's reads are present, not the event, as RF14 found at 9-10 of 12 sites.

Simplest version. Drop BND: there is no real truth set for it, and fusions sit outside the germline demo. Drop INV until (B) shows that correct spike-ins fail at real INV sites. Run (A) first. Build dup_planted, using del_planted's matcher on ref[E-15,E)+ref[S,S+16), only if demo DUPs fail.

Cost. Step 1 is cheaper than "a few hours": the 45-INV replica peek took 10 s, and validate over about 50 events should take minutes (inferred). Step 2 as proposed is M to L by this project's standards: three rows, strand-aware INV probes, cross-chromosome BND probes, a Python replica, kill tests drawn from real SV sites (the RF8 lesson), mutants, and probably one refuted attempt each, as RF13 and RF14 needed.

Nothing was edited in the repo. Files I wrote are in the scratchpad: invpeek/invs.txt, invpeek/result.txt and inv_bp.bed.

value:C3.already_done_or_refuted:
Not refuted, but partly done or already proposed elsewhere.
(1) Hospital K2b is already proposed. M40 asks to "turn the K2b machinery into a standing panel run on the 35x and hospital BAMs ... clips by end and length". value:M1's better_measurement says "(a) Rerun the K2b design on the hospital BAM". reality:M1, reality:M6 and value:M3 ask for hospital re-measurement too (journal wf_db17a130-4b0).
(2) The 5'/3' clip split was run on the 35x K2b by this workflow (scratchpad phys/clipends.py). Real vs spike: 5' 1-4 bp clips 0.112% vs 0.021-0.029%; 3' 1-4 bp clips 0.182% vs 0.130%.
(3) I have now run the cheap version on the hospital, read-only, in minutes. I re-scored the existing K2 hospital BAMs (scratchpad qtq2/k2v2/*/spiked.bam, v2 binary) with k2runs.py's read set and rule, split by end × clip length × read length × Alu overlap × crash, with Q100 ±10 bp masking. Scripts and outputs are in scratchpad c3fastp/ (k2strata*.py/.out, k2_alu_*.out).
(4) Step 4, the fastp item, is closed by measurement. I ran fastp 0.23.4 with the hospital's exact flags on the 22 K2 events' spike FASTQs:
- SPIKE_ reads: 46 of 9,602 dropped as low quality (0.48%), 8 too short (0.08%), 218 bases corrected (0.015% of bases).
- The 105,218 original reads in the same FASTQs: 0 dropped, 0 corrected.
- Output: c3fastp/syn.json and orig.json.
value:C3.corrected_claims:
1. "None of this is in M1-M49" is wrong. M40 covers hospital K2b plus clips by end and length, and value:M1 proposes hospital K2b (DOCUMENTED, journal).

2. The "unrun 5'/3' diagnostic" has been run on 35x (phys/clipends.py). It is now also run on the hospital K2 data: MEASURED, c3fastp/k2strata.out.

3. The premise that the K2 bin-0 gap may be "small-sample noise" is not supported. MEASURED on the K2 data:
- bin 0: spike 14/5,430 vs own 46/6,313, z −3.57.
- With Q100 ±10 bp masking it barely moves: 0.26% vs 0.70%, z −3.38.
- It is spread over events: own > spike in 12 events, spike > own in 4. Sign-test p ≈ 0.08 (INFERRED from the per-event table), so the cluster-robust evidence is moderate, not nil.

4. "So the clip gap is not a crash gap" does not hold within strata. MEASURED:
- In bin-0 reads overlapping an Alu (UCSC rmsk), own reads crash 30/2,414 (1.24%) vs spike 17/2,163 (0.79%).
- Own non-crashed Alu reads clip 0.88% vs spike 0.23% (z −2.88).
- In non-Alu bin-0 reads spike crashes more (0.43% vs 0.28%).
- The overall 1.49% vs 1.48% match hides strata that offset each other.

5. "k2b.sh with the BAM path swapped" cannot see where the gap sits.
- measure_clip_share needs both mates at 151 bp, and clipscore needs query_length == 151 (code). generate_from_template never trims (reality:C3).
- MEASURED on K2, bin 0:
  - 150-bp reads: spike 5/1,344 (0.37%) vs own 24/1,604 (1.50%), z −3.08.
  - 151-bp reads: 8/3,377 (0.24%) vs 17/3,942 (0.43%), z −1.42.
- About 60% of the bin-0 excess is in 150-bp reads, which the harness drops.
- Read-length mix and crash share by length match: 150-bp share 24.7% vs 25.6%; crash 1.39% vs 1.62%.

6. The kill rule cannot fire. On the 35x K2b, which the v2 plan calls a match, these bins already break |z| < 2 in every seed (computed from qtq2/k2b/k2b.txt):
- bin 1: 0.67-0.75% vs 1.00% (n ≈ 11.8k), z about −2.1 to −2.8;
- bin 3: 11.7-11.9% vs 9.91%, z about +2.5 to +2.9.

7. Step 3, ranking M1-M9 by share of the clip gap, is ill-posed for M1, M4, M7, M8 and M9:
- site and molecule errors show up as aligned mismatches;
- duplicates and start motifs do not clip;
- adapter read-through is excluded by TLEN ≥ 151.

8. Confirmed:
- The fastp figures are exact (MEASURED from the JSON): 13,917,960/113,421,578,824 = 0.0123%; 2.594%; 0.193%.
- D24-14230 is HG002/GM24385, so the Q100 mask is correct. The scratchpad qtq2/plant.sh comment says HG002, and the samplesheet case_id is GM24385_seracare_cancer.
value:C3.better_measurement:
Step 0 is done (MEASURED, c3fastp/): re-scoring the existing K2 hospital BAMs already answers the attribution question, which the proposal put after a new run. The bin-0 gap survives Q100 masking. About 80% of it is in Alu-overlapping reads:
- Alu: spike 9/2,163 (0.42%) vs own 35/2,414 (1.45%), z −3.58.
- Non-Alu: 5/3,267 (0.15%) vs 11/3,899 (0.28%), z −1.15.
- Of the 35 own Alu bad-end reads, 21 are 150 bp. The clips are mostly 3' and 21 bp or longer, with 57% of the clipped bases below Q15.
- They are MAPQ 60 and mostly have no Q100 record within 200 bp.
- 14 of the 35 are crashed.
This looks like sequence-context bad tails beyond homopolymer runs (INFERRED; tens of reads, and 16 of the 22 events were chosen as Alu-flanked). It is not obviously any of M2, M3, M5 or M6.

If the owner wants to go further, use this instead of plain k2b.sh:
(a) Adapt the harness to the trimmed library:
- keep mates of 147 bp or more with frag ≥ cycles;
- apply trim_adapter_start to spike's reads;
- score clipscore by each read's own length;
- report strata of read length (151/150/shorter) × Alu overlap (rmsk) × end × clip length × crash.
(b) Calibrate against real data, not against perfection:
- a real-vs-real hash split, plus the second hospital library D25-7403 (HG001, v4.2.1 mask) as the band;
- kill the "hospital-specific gap" if the Alu-stratum bin-0 spike/real ratio's 95% CI overlaps the 35x ratio (0.90-0.97);
- otherwise report it as a context effect.
(c) Run a value gate before any M build. The bad-end clips are low-quality tails at scattered positions, about 0.6 per kb in K2 flanks (INFERRED from 46 reads over about 75 kb). Count the clusters of 2 or more bad-end clips within ±5 bp in real Alu flanks, LDLR ±50 kb included. If they are rare (for example under 1 per 10 kb), SV callers cannot gain or lose a junction from them, and no read-model build is justified by this gap.
(d) fastp: no further work. SPIKE_ reads are dropped 0.48% low quality plus 0.08% too short, and 0.015% of their bases are corrected, against 0% for the originals. That moves depth at an event by about 0.5% and AF by about 0.002 (INFERRED), which is no call change.
value:C3.notes:
VALUE.
- **Outcomes that matter.** Every value skeptic already rated M1-M9 about 2 on caller impact (M7 and M8 killed), for reasons that do not depend on the size of the clip gap. A ranking by share of the clip gap would therefore not change what gets built.
- **What survives is narrow.** The hospital gap sits in Alu-overlapping reads. LDLR is Alu-rich (DOCUMENTED, hospital-demo-plan), and in the K2 data the LDLR event ld2 shows own 5 vs spike 1 at bin 0. So the gap is in the demo's own territory. But it is about 1 point of reads with scattered low-quality clipped tails, which plausibly changes no DeepVariant, Manta or TIDDIT call (INFERRED, not measured).
- **The fastp half is closed now.** Measured with the pipeline's exact fastp flags on existing spike output. The double pass is benign: spike's overlapping mates get corrected at about the raw rate (0.015% vs 0.0123% of bases), so they end up processed once, like the real reads.

MEASUREMENT. The proposal is unsound as written:
- the kill rule is unfit, because 35x fails it;
- the harness drops 150-bp reads, which carry about 60% of the bin-0 excess;
- the ranking is undefined for 5 of the 9 M ideas;
- the "maybe noise" hypothesis is already contradicted by K2's own data (z −3.4 after Q100 masking).
The reality skeptic (reality:C3) independently found the length-filter and kill-rule faults. My Alu, crash and fastp measurements are new.

COST. S-M, not "under an hour":
- the harness needs Rust test edits for trimming and length;
- k2b.sh runs cargo test --release;
- add 4 bwa-mem2 runs plus stratified scoring.
The simplest useful version, re-scoring the existing K2 BAMs, cost about 5 minutes and is done.

Caveats:
- Small counts: 35 vs 9 Alu bad-end reads.
- Alu overlap is confounded with the Alu-selected events.
- Data: hospital K2 dirs in scratchpad qtq2/k2v2 (v2 binary), events in scratchpad inspect/events.tsv, rmsk at /home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/resources/mobile_elements/rmsk.txt.gz.
- Everything here is read-only. All outputs are in /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/c3fastp/.

value:C4.already_done_or_refuted: The mechanism was already measured, so it is not new. The 2026-09-27 origin physics test (docs/review/REVIEW.md, section "`--edit-model origin`: physics test", around lines 6169-6330) ran a `--min-mapq 0` clean-mode control on a made-up genome with an exact twin. The event was a het DEL. MEASURED: L 0.271 and P 1.296, against a truth of 0.767/0.770 at L and 0.815/0.812 at P. So `--min-mapq 0` over-removes at the event and inflates the twin, because spike's realigned reads spill onto the twin. README.md:516 already says this: "`--min-mapq 0` ... removes each one as if it certainly came from the event. It also never touches the look-alike copy", and it points to origin. The only open gap is that the refusal message (src/census.rs:235, "If most of them are below --min-mapq, lowering it lets spike edit them") and the README bullet at README.md:507 ("Lowering `--min-mapq` often fixes it") do not carry that caveat. The README.md:507 example, chr20:27100000-27110000, sits near the chr20 centromere (INFERRED from coordinates), which is exactly the kind of place where the advice is wrong.
value:C4.corrected_claims:
1) "The hom DEL would read about 0x at the event and full depth at the paralog (INFERRED)": not merely inferred. Its het analogue was MEASURED in the physics test (REVIEW.md: `--min-mapq 0` gives L 0.271, P 1.296; truth L 0.77, P 0.81). Even in an exact twin the true split is not 0.5/0.5 each: truth P exceeds truth L by about 0.05, because bwa-mem2 does not split evenly. A hand-derived "about 0.5 each" is the wrong yardstick.
2) HISTORY says the clean-mode advice was never tested, only origin (M20). In fact the physics test measured the clean-mode `--min-mapq 0` advice as a control, and README.md:516 documents the result.
3) "The exons RF8 refuses are exactly the camouflaged clinical genes": in the idea's own file (scratchpad critic/exons400b.counts, re-read here) only PRODH (37/37 resistant, 1.000) is above RF8's 0.5 threshold, so RF8 refuses 1 of 400 exons. OCLN 0.374 (115 reads, 72 good), TMEM231 0.349, OPN1LW 0.158 and CYP21A2 0.106 (66 reads, 59 good) only trigger the WARN_ABOVE=0.10 warning (src/census.rs:19, warning() at about :280), and that text does not mention --min-mapq.
4) The proposed CYP21A2 test locus would therefore never show the refusal or its advice. CYP21A2 and CYP21A1P are also diverged (about 98% identical per the literature, INFERRED), which fits 89% of reads being MAPQ>=20 proper pairs. Most reads already map to their true copy, so the physical expectation after a hom DEL is nearer 0 at the event and 1.0 at the paralog than 0.5/0.5.
5) "README record any --min-mapq below 20": the run README already echoes the full command line (src/main.rs:989, 2685). Only truth.vcf lacks it.
value:C4.better_measurement:
No new run is needed for the rewording. Cite the physics test, which is already locked and SUPPORTED with the `--min-mapq 0` arm failing both bands. Then add a unit test that the refusal message contains the look-alike caveat and names --edit-model origin.

If real-data evidence is wanted, use the physics-test design on a real camouflaged segment instead of a hand-derived 0.5. Take GRCh38 sequence with a near-perfect paralog, such as PRODH in LCR22 (the only refused exon) or SMN1/SMN2. Simulate truth reads (wgsim, as in scripts/origin_physics.py) from both loci, with and without a hom DEL, for two seeds. Align with bwa-mem2 and draw the band from the two truths at L and P. Kill the rewording only if the `--min-mapq 0` arm lands inside both bands.

The stronger and costlier yardstick is a real carrier. Use a common hom deletion of a segdup copy that one GIAB/1000G sample carries and the other lacks (e.g. UGT2B17, LCE3B/C, GSTM1, RHD; carrier status must be checked first). Plant it in the non-carrier and compare per-locus MAPQ-0 depth at the event and the paralog with the real carrier, as in the transplant method.

To test worth, also check whether any raredisease caller output changes. The physics test suggests the summed depth over event plus twin is about conserved: 0.271+1.296=1.567 vs truth 1.582 (INFERRED from the measured values). So callers that pool paralogs (SMNCopyNumberCaller) and callers that filter on MAPQ may not move. Only per-locus callers that count MAPQ-0 reads (possibly CNVnator, INFERRED) would see the misplacement.
value:C4.notes:
The gap is real but small. The refusal text at src/census.rs:235 gives the --min-mapq advice without conditions, and README.md:507 presents it as a fix. Meanwhile README.md:516 and the physics test already show it misplaces the edit at a look-alike. The fix is a one- or two-sentence change to the refusal message and the README bullet: "at a look-alike copy (MAPQ 0 reads with XA hits), lowering it removes each read as if it surely came from the event and leaves the copy untouched; --edit-model origin (experimental) models that case." This is XS cost and needs no Gate B run.

The SIMPLEST variant (count MAPQ-0 reads with XA in the census) adds code and tests for a branch that fires in about 1 of 400 clinical exons (PRODH only, measured in the idea's own sample). It also misses MAPQ-0 reads without XA, which under bwa's -h 5 rule are the reads with more than 5 hits (README.md, origin section). A plain caveat that always prints is simpler and covers both cases.

The proposed Gate B is not well posed, for four reasons:
- Its CYP21A2 locus is not refused (share 0.106), so it never exercises the advice.
- Its 0.5/0.5 expectation is hand-derived and wrong for diverged paralogs.
- The 5 chr20 DELs may have no single XA paralog, so "depth at its XA paralog" is undefined there.
- It repeats a mechanism already measured on an exact twin.

Value for the hospital LDLR/raredisease demo is low. LDLR is Alu-flanked, not segdup, per hospital-demo-plan.md. In exact twins most raredisease callers ignore MAPQ-0 reads anyway (INFERRED), and the pooled depth looks conserved. The harm is that benchmarks of per-locus callers using MAPQ-0 reads in camouflaged genes could come out over-optimistic; a demo user would be pointed to origin anyway.

Do not point users to origin as validated. It is SUPPORTED only on the toy twin, and on real data its look-alike half removed 0 fragments at RF14's site (README). The message should say "experimental", as the proposal does.

value:C5.already_done_or_refuted: Not done and not refuted. The facts behind it check out. `git ls-files` shows no .github/, no rust-toolchain and no container file (measured). The independent review names the missing CI (docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:142, documented). README "Build" says only `cargo build --release`. Nothing in the memory notes says anything about the hospital host's OS, glibc, Rust, network or PATH. So the claim that this is a blocker has never been measured.
value:C5.corrected_claims:
1. "All dependencies are pure Rust" is wrong (measured, Cargo.lock). noodles-cram 0.74 pulls in bzip2 -> bzip2-sys, and xz2 -> lzma-sys. Both are C code built through `cc`. The existing binary target/release/spike links the system liblzma.so.5 dynamically (measured, `ldd`). A musl static build therefore needs a musl C toolchain (musl-tools, or `cross`/zigbuild), plus a static liblzma (lzma-sys `static`, or LZMA_API_STATIC=1). That makes it more than an S.
2. "The scripts check none of them before a stream of tens of minutes" is mostly wrong for the hospital route (measured, src/main.rs:2257-2440). The hospital route is `spike --into-fastq`, which runs fastq.sh through run_fastq at src/main.rs:1564.
   - fastq.sh never uses samtools or bwa-mem2. Those belong to the BAM route: align.sh and merge.sh, with `samtools view -N` at src/main.rs:2149.
   - `realpath -m` already falls back: `realpath -m -- "$1" 2>/dev/null || printf ...`.
   - pigz is optional and falls back to gzip (src/main.rs:2262).
   - gzip, awk, mktemp and mkfifo are all used before or at the start of the stream, so a missing one fails within seconds.
   - Only `mv -f -T` (src/main.rs:2439) runs after the whole stream.
   - The one external tool spike itself calls, besides bash, is `bcftools` (src/loh.rs:409, for `--gvcf` .vcf.gz). The idea leaves it out.
3. The hospital BAM's @PG (measured: bwa-mem2 2.2.1, samtools 1.19.2, MarkDuplicates 3.3.0) shows the tools inside raredisease's Nextflow tasks. value:C5.notes:
Value is low and speculative, so I'd weaken it.
- **No effect on callers.** It changes no caller's calls on spiked or real variants and no realism result.
- **Unblocks the demo only in one case:** the hospital host cannot run or build spike. Nobody has measured that. The 10-minute host check answers it, so run it first, not after building CI, musl, vendoring and `--check-tools`.
- **Tool list targets the wrong route.** samtools -N and bwa-mem2 are BAM-route tools. value:C6.better_measurement:
The question that decides value is whether any reasonable noise estimator changes a cell's status. That depends on rho, not on R_c alone. A Monte Carlo of E[v]/Var under an exchangeable-fragment binomial or beta-binomial is nearly circular. It can only find the small-sample halving bias, about 1 + 2/n_units, which is roughly 1.05-1.15 at the observed N: median N is 17-24 reads, and the sites that dominate INS20-49 A's noise have N of 8-30 (measured, scratchpad/c6check/top.py). It cannot find a wrong model, and its kill rule tests R_c, which cancels in rho.

The well-posed measurement is to recompute R_f, R_c and rho with the bootstrap under an alternative noise model, locked before the run on the SNV calibration (analytic R_c 1.04 there), and count status changes. Pass/fail: the idea has value only if at least one unsure cell becomes pass or fail. A broken estimator that inflated shared-site noise alone would show up as a move in rho. This has been run (scratchpad/c6check/rho_alt.py, 11 s): 0 of 6 cells change.

For the one real anomaly, INS20-49 A (R_c 0.57 under a binomial, p = 0.001, and shared events are not chosen on reads: round2.py keep = lambda e: True for shared), the next measurement belongs to a different idea. That idea would look at whether the 20-49 bp carrier/ref classification at repeat-extended regions is close to fixed by read geometry, or whether truth records are spelled differently between the samples. It would not look at the estimator.
