value:M1.corrected_claims:
1. The idea uses "hospital HG002 30x same blocks 13.47%, 543 sites with >=3" (from phys/errproc_hosp.out) as hospital support. errproc.py applies no base-quality filter and no bench-BED limit. I re-ran recur.py's own filters (BQ>=10, MAPQ>=20, reads without indels, inside the bench BED, Q100 masked) on phys/hosp_blocks.bam (measured: scratchpad/sk/recur_hosp_bq10.out). The hospital then has only 36 sites with >=3 same-strand same-alt reads at the full 30x, and 10 at a 0.55 subsample (about 17x, the same depth as K2b real.bam, which has 181). With no BQ filter the same data gives 534 and 195 sites (sk/recur_other.out). So about 93% of the hospital's recurrent sites rest on Q9 bases. The hospital quality alphabet is #/*/9/I = Q2/Q9/Q24/Q40, measured. DeepVariant's candidate step drops bases below min_base_quality 10. That default is external knowledge, not checked here; pipeline_info shows deepvariant 1.6.1.

2. "Real data feeds it ~5x more error-driven candidates per Mb" holds only for the 35x NovaSeq 6000 BAM at BQ>=10, where the low bin is Q11 and passes the filter. At BQ>=20 the numbers are real 33 candidates and 13 sites with >=3, against spike21 1 and 0 (sk/recur_other.out). So 420 of the 453 real candidates, and 168 of the 181 sites, rest on Q11 bases. On hospital data at DeepVariant's threshold, real has 49 candidates (51.8/Mb) at 30x and 58 (63.2/Mb) at about 17x. That is no higher than spike's 81-93/Mb on the 35x data. How spike behaves on hospital data was not measured.

3. The outcome that matters is DeepVariant's calls. I took the hospital's own raredisease output (call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz) over the same 20 blocks inside the v5.0q bench and compared it with Q100 (sk/dvfp.py). It has 1351 true-positive SNVs, 8 non-truth calls within 5 bp of a Q100 record, and exactly 1 isolated false positive: chr19:19835502 G>A, 0/1, QUAL 4, AD 19,3. All 3 alt reads are reverse strand, Q40 and MAPQ 60, so it is a genuine site-specific error. Systematic errors therefore give about 1 DeepVariant call per Mb. A ±2 kb footprint then loses about 0.004 calls per event, or about 0.002 at het, where half the pairs are original and still carry the site errors (inferred). One caveat: GLnexus output drops RefCall, so this counts genotyped calls only.

4. The pass rule ">=40% of spike's >=3 sites coincide with a real site with >=2" asks more than a perfect copy can deliver. The split-half oracle measures P(B>=2 | A>=3) = 0.372 (phys/split_both.out, n=191). The threshold has to be set relative to that oracle.

5. The code citations are correct: synth.rs:208 has error_rate(q, &state, rl - c) with no position, and quality.rs:963 is the >=5 reads, >=10% mask. The K2b numbers quoted (181/2/2, 453/85/74, 6.27%/1.35%, the split-half P values, the run shares 48/181 and 111/181, background 2.0%) match the .out files. The dupcheck figure 690/757 has no output file in phys/, so I could not check it.
value:M1.better_measurement:
Use the hospital data and DeepVariant's own filters, report results by base quality, and test whether calls change, not only candidates.

(a) Rerun the K2b design on the hospital BAM: learn from even-hash reads, remake the odd-hash pairs at their own positions, align with the hospital's bwa-mem2 -M -K command, exclude duplicates and the SeraCare gene windows, and score with BQ>=10. Pass if candidates and sites with >=3 reads fall at 0.7-1.3x real at BQ>=20 (hospital real is 49-58 candidates, 10-36 sites). Overlap must reach >=0.6x the split-half oracle measured on the same halves; on 35x the oracle is 0.372.

(b) Add a quality-coupling check. The share of injected or real recurrent alts on low-Q bases must match (real 35x: 93% Q11-carried). A version that emits the site alt at the drawn high quality must fail this check.

(c) The decisive value test. Run DeepVariant 1.6.1 (WGS model) on real vs master-remade reads over at least 20-50 Mb of hospital bench (about 1 isolated false positive per Mb was measured, so fewer Mb gives no power). Count non-truth calls, PASS and RefCall, per Mb. If master's false-positive rate is not significantly below real's, kill the idea for the raredisease goal. Run (c) before Gate B. It needs DeepVariant runs rather than Rust work, and its answer decides whether Gate B is worth doing.
value:M1.notes:
Verdict is weaken: the gap is real at the pileup level, but its value for the owner's goal is close to zero by measurement, and the gate is aimed at the wrong data.

**Value**
- The gap itself is real. The split-half site effect is far beyond a spectrum or duplicate artifact. Even at BQ>=20, real 35x has 33 high-Q candidates against 1 for spike (measured).
- In the target setting, hospital NovaSeq X data through DeepVariant 1.6.1, almost all recurrent errors are Q9. DeepVariant's candidate step drops Q9 bases (external default). The errors that remain give about 1 called false positive per Mb in real data (measured: the chr19:19835502 one-strand Q40 site).
- So for a spiked LDLR demo, the expected change is well under one call over hundreds of events (inferred). The idea's impact claim rests on 35x Q11-bin statistics that do not carry over to the hospital data.
- Value is left only for niche or speculative uses:
  - low-VAF or somatic benchmarking, which the README shows (BCR-ABL1 at 5%, fusions at low VAF);
  - strand-bias filters, e.g. Mutect2, where a panel of normals usually removes recurrent site errors anyway;
  - how the reads look in IGV.

**Measurement**
- BQ>=10 on 35x data mostly scores Q11 coincidences.
- The 40% overlap threshold is above the oracle's 0.372.
- Nothing checks the qualities on emitted errors.
- No step looks at caller output.

**Cost**
- M is too low. Real recurrent errors sit on low-quality bases, so a faithful version must bias the v2 quality draw at the site as well as the base. That touches v2's history and crash state, beyond template_at/hap_to_ref position plumbing and the injection in synth.rs. It also changes output bytes, which needs K7-style gating, and the planted-allele exclusion adds more work.
- Gate B as written (2-3 h, injecting alts into spike21.bam) would also skip the quality coupling.

**Simpler partial step (inferred, unmeasured)**
- Learn the substitution spectrum, true base to called base by quality bin and mate. Real's top-alt share is 0.59-0.84 against spike's uniform 0.34 (phys/errproc_35x.out). That raises same-alt agreement for any 2-3 coincident errors.

Lock the following before any Rust work. All data except the prototype already exists.

**Gate B', a few hours.** Use the 100 forward SNV events of round 2b. Master's outputs are already on disk in scratchpad transplant2/full/forward/normal/run0-2, so the master arm and the sham cost nothing. The pysam prototype, per event:

- list the originals as replaced;
- realign with bwa-mem2 mem -M -K 100000000;
- run Picard MarkDuplicates on the view, because merge.sh has no re-marking.

**(1) Value gate, at caller level.** Run DeepVariant 1.6.1, the hospital's version, available locally as docker google/deepvariant:1.6.1, on footprint slices (±2 kb) of four inputs: unspiked, sham, the master view and the prototype view.

- Metric: the number of Q100 non-SNP records within ±2 kb (excluding ±60 bp of the site) whose GT differs from unspiked.
- Master must exceed sham by at least 5 records over the 100 footprints. If it does not, there is no caller-level flank value: KILL.
- The prototype must stay within sham + 1.

**(2) No regression at the site.** Round 3's SNV A metric with the rho rule, both directions.

**(3) Mate concordance at the site.** This replaces the fastp control.
- Pool all both-cover pairs across events.
- Compare the share of discordant mates with real HG001 carriers (Fisher test).
- The one-mate-edit mutant must fail. Expected: about 100% discordant against about 1-2% real (inferred).

**(4) Duplicate families.**
- Over edited families after Picard, the number of chosen representatives that carry REF must be 0.
- A mutant that skips the duplicate members must give more than 0.
- Score this at hom SNVs (the duplicates plan's K1 yardstick). At het sites it is invisible.

**(5) Quality at the site.** A chi-square or Fisher test over the 4 bins, as a sanity check only.

Drop the kill rule "no flank metric moves": untouched reads are the unspiked reads, so flank metrics move by construction.

M1 (minutes): a guard and its mutants.
- Implement only a warning: an event on non-PAR X/Y, with the background's chrX density at least 0.35 and below 0.65 of the autosomes, measured from 5 windows of 1 Mb each with MAPQ>=20 via index queries. Report "unknown" when the autosome windows are empty or inconsistent.

  - Warns: HG002 35x and the hospital BAM, at the default AF or af=0.5.
  - Silent at af=hom.

M2 (the one that decides whether the defaults or truth bytes should change): DeepVariant 1.6.1, run as raredisease runs it (--haploid_contigs chrX,chrY, no PAR bed, per the measured params), on a 1-2 Mb non-PAR chrX region of the hospital HG002 merged BAM.

- Yardstick: the real Q100 GT=1 sites in the same region.
- Record GT, GQ, FILTER and ref share of AD.

M3 (transplant-style, for the DMD/CNV claim): compare a DMD exon DEL at af=hom and at af=0.5 through Manta and gCNV (the pipeline's ploidy model) with HG002's own real Q100 chrX DELs of 50 bp or more. For real ones, Manta should give 1/1 and gCNV CN0 against a male CN1 baseline. Expect af=0.5 to give Manta 0/1 and an ambiguous gCNV call. That would show the default is unrealistic in practice, not just in principle.

The proposed tests (b) and (c) only check that spike plants what it is told: af=1 already gives AF of about 1 and interior depth equal to the resistant share. Test (f)'s af=0.5 kill rule cannot fire, because the reads' ref fraction is about 0.5 by construction.
value:M12.notes:
Worth: there is a real silent footgun for one class of demo, but the dosage half of it already works.

**Footgun.**
- Measured: on male HG002, del:chrX:31500000-31502000 at the default/het AF exits with no warning and writes SIM_VAF 0.500, GT 0/1, a half-dose mosaic. Log: scratchpad robust/chrx_het/log.txt and out/truth.vcf.
- The VCF route makes this worse. A batch of ClinVar P/LP records has no GT, so every chrX record takes --allele-fraction 0.5 (vcf_input.rs only counts GT, never uses it).
- X-linked demos (DMD exon deletions) are a plausible raredisease use. The owner's demo note names LDLR "and many other genes"; that X-linked genes are on the list is inferred.
- af=hom already gives the correct hemizygous dosage, and its 1/1 label matches what this pipeline's DeepVariant/GLnexus writes for male X (measured, all 1/1). So the outcome only goes wrong through operator error. A cheap guard captures most of the value.

**Keep (S, about 1 day).**
1. A warning on non-PAR X/Y when the background looks male, measured with windowed index counts (works for BAM, CRAM and slices). Built-in GRCh38 PAR table to exempt PAR. Byte-identical output.
2. One README line: on a male background's non-PAR X/Y, use af=hom. This is the owner's measure-and-warn preference.
3. Optional, behind --sex male: omitted af defaults to 1.0 on non-PAR X/Y, and a SIM_PLOIDY=1 INFO tag is added. GT stays '1/1' by default; '1' is opt-in.

**Drop or defer.**
- Automatic sex inference as a decision-maker. All local male BAMs are the same individual (HG002), and there is one female, so the "one cut separates them" test has n=1 per class. Use it as a cross-check only.
- The GT '1' default. It contradicts the pipeline's convention and the owner's cnv_validation finding.
- Skipping phasing. It has no effect at af=1.
- --ploidy-bed for other builds.
- --strict-ploidy refusals.
- The PAR truth-GT policy. PAR depth is diploid, so spike's diploid model is right there, and the pipeline's haploid PAR calls are its own setting (par_bed null). PAR needs only an exemption from the warning.
- CR7(a) VCF genotype mode is a separate medium-sized item and should not ride along.

**Cost.** The proposal as written is L (scored 4); the reduced version is S.

**Not verified by me:** the R52 hemizygous-AF numbers (4.5% below 0.8), the 64 Q100 chrX DELs, and ngsbits ratios. I did verify the idxstats ratios, the GT tallies, par_bed null, DeepVariant 1.6.1, the Q100 '1' encoding, the code lines and the chrx_het/chrx_hom run outputs.

So the SIMPLEST version (W=1 kb) would turn almost every LDLR event into an Alu-Alu hybrid. That contradicts the idea's own risk note that many real LDLR SVs are not Alu-mediated.
4. MINOR: 'both ends inside an Alu 13/22'. I count 15/22, plus 6 with one end, using POS/END as written (convention-dependent). '15/22 both ends on a multiple of 100' is confirmed; 20/22 have at least one end on one.

value:M13.better_measurement:
Use the transplant set that already has real carriers, compare at the same locus, and gate on a caller outcome.

Gate 0 (minutes; offline reference arithmetic):
- Input: the 14 real HG001 Alu-Alu deletions (scratchpad inspect/events.tsv) plus B1. Round both ends to 100 (this measured 0-2 bp homology), then run the snap.
- PASS: the snapped haplotype's junction ±300 bp is byte-identical to the truth haplotype's in at least 10 of 15 (a no-op snap scores 0).
- Also run the snap on the 6 real no-repeat events (nn1-nn6), rounded. Report how often it invents an Alu-Alu junction where reality has none. At W=500 the chance of finding a pair is about 80% (measured), so a false-invention rate above 3 of 6 forces a smaller W or a homology threshold above chance.

Gate 1 (about 1 h with inspect/plant.sh):
- Plant each aa event into HG002 in three arms: T (truth coordinates), R (rounded) and S (rounded, then snapped).
- Per event, compare clipped-read count and SA fraction with HG001's real carrier at the same site.
- KILL (document only): R's clipped count is within the Poisson 95% band of real in at least 10 of 14. That means rounding does not change the read evidence.
- PASS: R falls outside in at least half of the events where T falls inside, and S falls inside wherever T does.

Gate 2 (minutes; the outcome that matters):
- Run Manta and TIDDIT on B1 precise (11127041-11129177), which Manta misses on FULL, and on B1 rounded (11127000-11129200).
- Do the same, rounded and snapped, for two small demo exon deletions (ex5_Danish 1,042 bp, ex4_Taiwanese 1,500 bp), where depth callers are weak.
- Use the S1 slice: it equalled FULL at the planted events 3 of 3 (memory sv-caller-slices.md). Or use Manta --callRegions.
- If Manta calls rounded B1 but misses precise B1, the bias flips a caller's call, and building is justified. If Manta's verdict is the same in both, weaken to documentation.

Why not the idea's own test: it pools spreads across different loci for 22 LDLR records that have no real carriers. Real Alu-Alu clipped counts already span 0-10, so a broken version (the rounded arm, about 15 clips) would sit only marginally outside that spread, and per-event realism cannot be falsified.
value:M13.notes:
Worth: the mechanism is real and measured. Rounding or exon-edge cuts turn 3-40 bp homologous Alu-Alu junctions into 0-2 bp blunt ones. Real carriers of homologous junctions show about 2 clipped reads, against about 15 for blunt ones. README's headline exon example (del:LDLR:exon4-exon8) cuts at exon edges, and 0 of 36 MANE exon edges lie in an Alu.

What is not shown is that this changes an outcome that matters:
- For the hospital demo, raredisease merges callers. Precise B1 was missed by Manta but found by TIDDIT and CNVnator, so the merged VCF would likely report a kb-scale LDLR deletion whatever the junction class.
- The risk lies with small deletions of 1-2 kb, where depth callers are weak, and with single-caller benchmarks. That is untested, which is why Gate 2 comes first: one spike run plus Manta on a slice, a few minutes.

Cheaper alternatives that cover much of the value:
- Use precise ClinVar coordinates where they exist. B1 and B2 are precise, and 14 of 31 ClinVar LDLR deletions have 2 bp or more of homology, so they need no snap.
- Replace demo ex5-10_Czech with ClinVar 251409's real coordinates.
- Document that exon specs and approximate coordinates give blunt, clip-rich, easy-for-split-read-callers junctions.

If built, the simplest version should drop rmsk: no 155 MB dependency, and it covers Alu, segdup and microhomology alike.
- Snap each end within ±W to the longest exact same-orientation match between the two windows. Any cut inside an exact stretch gives the same haplotype.
- Require a threshold above chance. INFERRED: about 11-12 bp is the expected longest match by chance for 2 kb x 2 kb windows, so use about 20 bp or more; otherwise fall back to 2-5 bp microhomology nearest the stated end.
- Record CIPOS/CIEND and SIM_SNAP. Cost: S for DEL only; M with exon-spec intronic constraints and DUP.

Watch out for:
- The snap imposes the Alu-NAHR class rather than discovering it: about 80-97% of LDLR positions qualify. The true Alu-mediated fraction of LDLR SVs is unknown here, because ClinVar's 6 of 39 is contaminated by imprecise coordinates. Present it as an opt-in model, not as finding the real junction.
- Junctions inside repeats raise SIM_RESIST and may trip RF8's refusal.

Files I wrote (read-only probes, scratchpad): skeptic_m13/chance.py, skeptic_m13/hom3.py, skeptic_m13/match.py, skeptic_m13/alu_ldlr.tsv.

value:M14.corrected_claims:
1. "15/15 support mates off-contig" is misread. In mei_evidence.py (lines 261-287), support_mates_off_contig=15 counts the off-contig mates among the 26 supporting clipped reads. 15/15 is the number of those mates that were found. The off-contig share is 15/26 (58%), and the MAPQ 0 share is 14 of the 15 off-contig mates. The proposed pass rule "15/15 and 14/15" therefore compares against the wrong denominator.
2. specimen_spanning_reads=72 is every read covering the breakpoint position, from either allele (spanning() in mei_evidence.py). It is not a count of reads spanning the insertion.
3. The SeraCare AluY is not a genomic MEI. It sits on a construct segment of about chr13:32394259-32395260, with construct seams 515 bp to the left and 486 bp to the right (cnv_validation config/frozen_evidence/construct_seams.tsv). Its AF is unknown. Near it the SV VCF holds a GATK CNV DUP at chr13:32394001-32395000 and a seam BND to chr17:43056563 (measured with zcat of GM24385_seracare_cancer_sv.vcf.gz). It is n=1, with 15 mates.
4. The real AluY was missed by every SV caller (documented in cnv_validation workflow/report/templates/sections/s5_2.md, and confirmed by me: no INS within ±10 kb). That miss is not typical. In the same hospital raredisease run (D24-14230, which is HG002 plus SeraCare), Manta called an INS within ±300 bp of 300 of the 991 real HG002 Q100 insertions of 250-400 bp that carry the Alu 5' 19-mer GGCCGGGCGCGGTGGCTCA (30.3%). It called 152 of 430 (35.3%) insertions that have a poly-A or poly-T but no Alu head, and 200 of 3496 (5.7%) of the rest. (Measured: scratchpad m14/classify.py on ins250_400.tsv and sv_calls.tsv.) So MEIs do reach Manta at the hospital.
5. "HGVS/ClinVar describe MEIs symbolically, so a clinical MEI spike today is random DNA": the local ClinVar VCF (cnv_validation/resources/clinical/clinvar.vcf.gz) has 0 symbolic ALTs and 0 INS:ME records (measured). A clinical MEI never arrives through ClinVar. Someone writes it by hand, and they can paste explicit sequence today.
6. skip_me_calling=true is confirmed: it is in params_2026-09-10/11 json and in all 3 from_rv param/params.yaml.
7. The ME subtype is dropped silently. The truth VCF writes SVTYPE=INS with the random bases (src/truth.rs:402), and sv_type_tag accepts any INS suffix (src/vcf_input.rs:870-877) with no warning. A warning is the cheapest honest fix.
value:M14.better_measurement:
Run Gate 0 first. It needs no code and checks whether insert content changes what a caller does, which is the outcome that matters.
- Draw about 100 HG002-only heterozygous Q100 insertions of 250-400 bp that carry the Alu head and are absent in HG001, using the transplant scripts' selection.
- Plant them into HG001 (D25-7403) with today's spike in two arms. Arm (a) uses the explicit Q100 sequence (the realism ceiling). Arm (b) uses random bases of the same length (today's symbolic path).
- Space the events so that one merged BAM per arm holds them all. Align with the hospital command.
- Run Manta (and TIDDIT) on the whole genome, not with --callRegions. sv-caller-slices.md:57 measured that --callRegions drops inter-chromosome BNDs and adds INS calls, which is exactly the evidence class an Alu changes.
- Score INS recall within ±300 bp. The real-yardstick rate is HG002's 300/991 = 30.3%.
- Pass rule: arm (a) must land within a binomial 95% CI of 30.3%. If arm (b) also lands inside the CI of (a), content does not matter to the hospital's callers and the idea reduces to a warning (value 1). If (b) differs, build the consensus arm (c), AluY + poly-A + TSD + random strand, and require (c) within the CI of (a). Arm (b) is the broken control and must fail.
- Add a second broken control, consensus without poly-A or TSD. If it also passes, those parts are untested decoration and get dropped from the build.
- Use mei_evidence.py on each arm's BAM (tsd_bp, homopolymer_bp, off-contig share over supporting reads, MAPQ 0 share) only as secondary read-level checks, with the correct denominators.
value:M14.notes:
The gap is real in the code: symbolic and length-only INS records get iid bases, and the ME label is dropped silently. The value case as written is weak, and the falsifying measurement is not well-posed:
- **Yardstick:** it rests on one engineered construct, with seams about 500 bp from the insertion and unknown AF, and only 15 mates.
- **Misread number:** it misreads 15/15. The off-contig share is 15/26.
- **Weak discrimination:** mate placement passes for any Alu-derived sequence, so poly-A, TSD and strand are never tested.
- **Wrong outcome:** it does not measure caller output.

What makes the idea worth keeping in weakened form is a number I measured. Manta in the actual hospital pipeline calls about 30% of HG002's real Alu-sized insertions (300/991), so MEI content can matter for SV benchmarks. Whether random content gives Manta a different call rate is unmeasured (inferred). A plausible mechanism is that unmapped shadow mates help Manta's insertion assembly while MAPQ 0 remote mates do not (inferred).

Hospital and LDLR value is indirect for three reasons:
- ME calling is skipped.
- The demo plan names SNVs, indels and exon DEL/DUP, not MEIs.
- ClinVar's VCF carries no MEI records.

Simplest worthwhile version, cost 1-2:
- warn when <INS:ME:*> or ins:...:LEN gets random bases;
- document the explicit-sequence recipe;
- optionally add a helper that writes AluY + poly-A + TSD as an explicit-sequence record (Dfam consensus is CC0).

Build the bundled multi-family library (L1 truncation, SVA) only if Gate 0 shows random and explicit content differ at the caller level. L1 and SVA also need fragments wholly inside the insert, which tiling never draws today (src/simulate.rs:801-803). For Alu this hardly matters at the locus, because those pairs map elsewhere.

Measurement cost: about 3 arms × a whole-genome Manta run (72-103 min each, documented in sv-caller-slices.md) plus merges, roughly half a day. The cost score of 3 reflects that, not the code.

value:M15.already_done_or_refuted:
Not built and not refuted. Nothing in .claude/judgment-gate-cases.md mentions compound, grouped, cis/trans, allow-overlap or MNV (grep returned nothing). This idea is the value:M15 check. The journal (wf_db17a130-4b0/journal.jsonl) shows reality:M15 and value:M15 started twice with no result. CR1 is DOCUMENTED as gated but not composed: REVIEW.md:2934-2939 says "Only the rejection is fixed: ... grouping them, assigning haplotypes, and generating and suppressing molecules once per group -- remains open". CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md:297-301 and 499-501 call it a Phase 2 item that blocks CR6 option A.

Two things partly cover it already:
(a) A cis pair a few hundred bp apart can be written today as one equal-length MNV. `snp:` has no length cap (src/exon.rs:614-670), MNVs keep a 1:1 SegmentOrigin (src/haplotype.rs:466-479), and apply_variants still puts the sample's SNPs inside that span (haplotype.rs:661-697). Its caveats: truth is one MNV record (bcftools norm -a splits it), and validate reads an MNV jointly per read (README:1109), so a span over about 150 bp gets no votes.
(b) Under --allow-overlap, when the two coins land on different copies, a close trans pair already comes out nearly right. That is inferred from simulate.rs:258 (each event suppresses at random with copy_rate) plus synth.rs:694-699 and combine_event_outputs. Depth is about 1+0.25u and each ALT about 0.5/(1+0.25u), where u is the share of fragments not assigned to a copy, and no read carries both ALTs.
value:M15.corrected_claims:
1. "The hospital ranked VCF has Compounds INFO, so the pipeline scores compound pairs." True, but the scoring cannot see phase. MEASURED on .../D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results:
- The execution trace has no phasing process: only DEEPVARIANT, GLNEXUS, GENMOD_ANNOTATE, GENMOD_COMPOUND and the like.
- Every GT in the ranked SNV VCF is one of 0/1 (434,789), 1/1, 1/0 or ./1. None uses '|', and there is no PS.
- The genmod CommandLineOptions show whole_gene=True and no phased option.
- All 114 LDLR records are 'AD|AR_comp', each with 55-153 compound partners (median 120).
So cis and trans give the same genmod output. Even a single spiked P/LP het already becomes a compound with background hets. "Compound-het demos reach genmod's compound models" is true today, with no code.

2. "When both coins pick the same copy depth is ~1+v and each ALT ~v/(1+v)." This holds only when every fragment is assigned to a copy. From copy_rate (synth.rs:694-699: assigned event copy 2v, unassigned v) and per-event random suppression, depth is 1.0+0.5a+0.25u (a assigned, u unassigned, a+u=1). That is 1.25-1.5x, with ALT 0.33-0.40 (inferred). For an AF=1 pair, depth is about 2x and each ALT about 0.5, so the pair would be miscalled 0/1 (inferred).

3. "Today's --allow-overlap must fail" holds for cis (0% co-carry) and for matching coins. With different coins, trans is nearly correct (see above). A trans-only baseline with a lucky seed could therefore pass the AF, depth and co-carry rules. The baseline must force the coin outcome or run several seeds.

4. REVIEW.md 67.05x/67.03x is for two AF=1 DELs on a 75x uniform donor, i.e. the deletions cancel completely. It is not an SNV composition measurement.

5. Reproduced (MEASURED):
- 52 of 153 LDLR exon pairs have an edge-to-edge gap under 7,000 bp. This holds on the post-M29 MANE BED and on the old exon 1 alike.
- 1,095 ClinVar P/LP SNVs (Pathogenic, Likely_pathogenic, Pathogenic/Likely_pathogenic; conflicting excluded; contig '19', 11089000-11134000), giving 295,948 of 598,965 pairs (49.4%) under 7 kb apart.
- Exon 4 alone holds 225 of these SNVs.
Since 50.6% of pairs are allowed, an LDLR compound-het demo is not blocked today. It is only restricted to pairs at least 7 kb apart.

6. Risk the idea leaves out: a trans group remakes both copies over ±2 kb. With today's SNP-only templates (M11/CR3), every background indel in that range is erased on both copies, not just on one. MEASURED in the exon-4 union footprint: Q100 has a het DEL at chr19:11104275 CA>C (0|1), and hospital DeepVariant calls it 0/1 at QUAL 41. Its records and the hospital DV calls match 8/8 (11101794-11108298). The SIMPLEST version would drop that real call from the demo VCF (inferred from code plus M11's measured 0/596 synthetic reads carrying het indels). The proposed LDLR check would still pass.
value:M15.better_measurement:
Step 0, a value gate (about 2 h, no code, release binary plus align.sh on the 35x HG002). Plant two LDLR P/LP SNVs two ways and measure everything at once:
- (a) at least 7 kb apart (e.g. exon 4 with exon 9 or 10), which is allowed today;
- (b) 300 bp apart in exon 4 with --allow-overlap, using seeds whose logged or inferred coins match and seeds whose coins differ.
Measure per-site AF against the validate 99% band, depth in 500 bp bins over the union footprint against the unspiked run, fragments carrying both ALTs, and the AF of every Q100 record in the footprint, chr19:11104275 CA>C included.
If (a) works and (b) with differing coins is within band, the demo need reduces to M16's hap= (cost S) to force trans. Only cis close pairs then need grouping, or the MNV workaround.

Acceptance for the built feature, with absolute rules rather than "2x a near-zero real rate", which 900 fragments cannot resolve:
- (i) Cis: at least 95% of ALT-carrying fragments that cover both sites carry both ALTs. Trans: at most 1%.
- (ii) Each site's AF is inside validate's band at 0.5, or at 1.0 for hom members.
- (iii) Depth in 500 bp bins stays within the binomial band of an unspiked or sham run.
- (iv) Real-haplotype agreement, which is the real phase test: among synthetic fragments covering a planted ALT and a Q100 het SNP, the SNP allele matches the requested Q100 haplotype at or above the real rate minus 2 points. Measure the real rate first on real fragments, as in M16. For trans, the two ALTs sit on opposite Q100 haplotypes.
- (v) Background integrity: every Q100 record inside the union footprint keeps its AF in band, and hospital DeepVariant keeps its GT. The SIMPLEST both-copies remake fails this at chr19:11104275 unless M11 or M10 land first.

Broken controls that must fail:
- today's --allow-overlap with matching coins fails (ii) and (iii);
- a build that ignores copy= fails (iv);
- a build without background indels fails (v).

Drop "genmod lists them as compounds" as a pass criterion, because it cannot fail: every LDLR het is already AR_comp. Replace it with: DeepVariant calls both planted sites 0/1 with GQ in the real-het range, and there is no new SV or CNV call over the union footprint (tests the 1.25-1.5x depth artefact).

Simpler build: put SNV/MNV groups on M10's in-read editing, with one shared per-fragment copy assignment across the group. That avoids the ±2 kb double remake, the 7 kb footprint and the CR3 magnification, at about cost M. Defer SV and indel groups to CR6-A.
value:M15.notes:
On worth, the owner's end goal is a singleton raredisease demo, and that pipeline never sees phase. MEASURED on the hospital HG002 output: no phasing step, no '|' GTs or PS, genmod without phased, and all 114 LDLR hets already AR_comp with 55-153 partners. Choosing cis or trans therefore changes no call, genotype, GeneticModels or Compounds entry.

What phase does change:
- IGV teaching, and only for pairs closer than about one fragment (roughly 500 bp);
- future trio demos (M17);
- external phasing benchmarks;
- the CR6-A prerequisite.

For the demo, the concrete gaps are smaller than the idea suggests:
- Pairs 7 kb or more apart work today, and that is 50.6% of LDLR P/LP SNV pairs (measured).
- Close cis pairs can likely be planted today as a single equal-length MNV (inferred from code; untested).
- Close trans pairs are nearly right under --allow-overlap when the coins differ. M16's hap= (cost S) could force that.

The remaining real defect is the matching-coin or cis case under --allow-overlap: 1.25-1.5x depth, AF 0.33-0.40, and AF=1 members miscalled as het (inferred from synth.rs:694 and simulate.rs:258). Whether that 1.25-1.5x over about 7.5 kb triggers a raredisease CNV or SV call in LDLR has not been measured. It is the strongest value argument for the idea and should be Gate B rather than the near-tautological Q100 co-carry yardstick.

The SIMPLEST version (both copies fully remade from SNP-only templates) would harm the demo. It deterministically erases background indels on both copies over ±2 kb: the exon-4 footprint holds a real het DEL that hospital DeepVariant calls, chr19:11104275 CA>C, QUAL 41 (measured). So it must come after M11, or be built on M10, which reality-checked as "keep" at cost M.

Cost L is honest for the full proposal (VCF PS parsing, group syntax, union-footprint overlap logic, per-copy tiling, phased truth, per-member validate probes). An M10-based SNV-group version is about M.

value:M16.better_measurement:
Gate 0, value (run before any code):
- Take one LDLR exon pair 7 kb or more apart on NA12878.final.cram with Platinum v1.2.1 as --gvcf.
- With the existing binary, find a seed that gives cis and one that gives trans. Tell them apart from the reads: the ALT fragments' alleles at Platinum hets on the same fragment.
- Run DeepVariant and genmod models the way raredisease does: singleton ped, --whole_gene, no --phased. Diff GT, PS, Compounds and RankScore between the two builds.
- PASS (hap= has demo value) only if any of these differ. Predicted (inferred) to be identical; if so, build only the recording.

Gate 1, implementation (only if built):
- Measure the real rate first, on the same CRAM: how often fragments covering two Platinum hets carry Platinum-consistent alleles, with a 95% CI.
- Plant at least 20 events, each with at least 5 informative ALT fragments (a fragment that covers the event and a Platinum het).
- Per-event pass: at least 90% of informative ALT fragments carry the requested haplotype. The pooled rate must sit inside the real-rate CI.
- The proposed "within 2 points per event" cannot work: with 5-15 fragments, one error read moves a single event by 7-20 points.
- Negative control: master's coin build must fail. About 10 of 20 events are expected to fail, and the chance none does is 2^-20.
- With no hap= given, output must be byte-identical to master.
- Gate B as written (seed 1 vs seed 2 at one event) is not a check: the copy matches across two seeds half the time. Use 10 seeds or the new log line.
value:M16.notes:
The gap is real in code. A phased --gvcf only links SNPs; it never chooses the copy. Truth GT is always unphased.

The value is speculative for the stated goal. The cheap subset only covers pairs 7 kb or more apart, and at that spacing phase is invisible to the hospital pipeline: DeepVariant writes no PS, genmod runs without --phased, and every case is a singleton (all measured). So cis vs trans would change no call, no Compounds annotation and no rank in the LDLR demo.

Where phase does change calls is outside this subset:
- Close or overlapping pairs: an SNV inside a het DEL vanishes if cis and looks hemizygous if trans. That is M15/M16 composition.
- Inherited deletions in a family case: which parent's alleles disappear inside the DEL. That needs family-case runs (never run at the hospital), parent-of-origin ordering (Platinum hap order unverified) and phased VCFs for each member (only NA12878 has a per-sample truthset). That is M17.

Simpler version, cost 1, no RNG change: when the block holds a gVCF-phased SNP, log the chosen copy per event and write it to truth (e.g. INFO SPIKE_HAP=1|2 plus a phased GT). Then:
- Users who need a given cis/trans can re-seed until they get it; with two events that takes about two tries on average (inferred).
- The phase-aware benchmarking and provenance (M36) value is captured.
- Seed comparisons like the round-2b replant can be explained after the fact.

value:M17.corrected_claims:
1. "raredisease is pedigree-aware, so trio-consistent haplotypes matter." Wrong for any outcome that phase could change.
- MEASURED: the hospital's VCF carries no phase. In the DeepVariant 1.6.1 + GLnexus VCF for NA12879 (Seq25-16022 .../call_snv/genome/graceful_junk_snv.vcf.gz), the chr20 genotypes are 65,024 0/1, 39,393 1/1, 1,889 1/0 and 207 ./1. Not one is phased ('|').
- MEASURED: genmod 3.9 runs without phase. raredisease 2.4.0 calls GENMOD_MODELS with "--whole_gene --temp_dir ./" and no --phased (~/.nextflow/assets/nf-core/raredisease/conf/modules/rank_variants.config:82-85). The hospital config only overrides cpus and memory.
- MEASURED: nothing in the pipeline phases reads. grep for whatshap, hiphase and phasing over raredisease modules, subworkflows, workflows and conf hits only rtgtools/vcfeval.
- So genmod's AD, AD_dn and AR_comp, UPD, peddy and rhocall all work from genotypes alone. Per-member runs with the right GT per person give the designed labels whichever copy the coin picks.

2. "independent runs co-segregate only ~50% of the time." True per event, not per fragment.
- The copy is one coin per phase block (src/loh.rs:924-941). With a chromosome-wide phased --gvcf, that is one coin per contig (M11 reality check, note 9).
- So each event matches the transmitted haplotype in either about 100% or about 0% of its informative fragments. Only the share of events is ~50%.

3. "Short reads rarely cover both the variant and a linked SNP within one fragment." Overstated.
- MEASURED with scratchpad m17value/informative.py on the hospital HG001 30x BAM, at 60 random Platinum v1.2.1 chr20 het SNVs (MAPQ>=20, duplicates excluded): 844 of 1,868 covering fragments (45%) also cover another Platinum het SNV. 13 of the 60 sites have no informative fragment.
- These sites are themselves het SNVs, which cluster, so the share at arbitrary event positions is likely lower (inferred). The share that is informative for transmission in a trio is smaller again (inferred).

4. "pedigree/ and peddy/ outputs" exist, but the hospital has never run this family as a family.
- MEASURED: every CEPH member was run as its own singleton case. The samplesheets have paternal_id and maternal_id blank, a separate case_id each, and phenotype 2 for everyone.
- pedigree/graceful_junk.ped reads `Seq25-16022 0 0 2 2`.
- A trio demo therefore needs new pipeline setup first: a shared case_id, parent IDs, and parents marked unaffected.

5. The SIMPLEST version names a pedigree-phased VCF, but none is on disk for the children.
- The Platinum v1.2 release on disk is "limited to NA12878" (README.md), so the children's phase would have to be made.

6. "compound hets across parents" need no trio tool when the two footprints are 7 kb or more apart.
- 101 of 153 LDLR exon pairs qualify (M16, measured), and today's per-member runs handle them.
- Pairs closer than 7 kb are M15's problem, not M17's.
value:M17.better_measurement:
Run the value-kill test first. It needs neither the trio tool nor any read-level phase.
- At the hospital, use today's binary once per member:
  - inherited: father het and NA12879 het;
  - de novo: child only;
  - compound: a 7 kb-or-more LDLR exon pair, one variant from each parent, both in the child.
- Run raredisease once as a family case: shared case_id, paternal and maternal IDs set, parents unaffected.
- Pass if the GeneticModels field in *_snv_ranked_clinical.vcf.gz matches the design (AD, AD_dn, AR_comp) for at least 90% of events.
- I expect this to pass (inferred: genmod reads genotypes). If it does, M17 adds nothing for the demo. What remains is a docs recipe plus M39's multi-lane route.

If a phase-aware consumer is added later (WhatsHap --ped, genmod --phased, or a phasing benchmark), test per event, not over pooled fragments:
- For each inherited event with at least 3 transmission-informative fragments, the ALT fragments' alleles at linked SNPs must match the transmitted haplotype in at least 95% of them.
- The coin build fails at about half the events. With 20 events it passes all of them with probability 2^-20.
- Pooling, as proposed, can let a broken build pass when a few deep events dominate. It also cannot tell 50% of events at 100% from all events at 50%.

Two parts of the proposed measurement add nothing:
- Measuring the real "~100%" yardstick: biology fixes it, and M16's HG001 measurement covers it on data already on disk.
- "0 alt reads in parents" for de novo: it holds trivially when the parents are not spiked. Check instead that the parents don't carry the variant, which spike's carried check should already refuse.

The genmod >=90% criterion, as written, cannot tell the trio tool from today's per-member runs.
value:M17.notes:
Verdict: kill the XL trio tool. The code gap is real: one --bam (src/main.rs:47) and a coin per phase block. But it changes no outcome that matters.
- No step in raredisease 2.4.0 reads phase (measured above).
- The hospital's DeepVariant genotypes are unphased.
- Inherited, de novo and 7 kb-or-more compound-het designs come out right at genotype level with today's per-member runs.
- The only realism the tool adds, read-level co-segregation with the transmitting parent's SNPs, would be seen by WhatsHap --ped or a phasing benchmark. Neither is in the owner's path.

Cost XL is honest for the full tool, but the cheapest useful version costs almost nothing.
1. A docs recipe for trio demos with today's tool:
   - spike each member at the designed genotype;
   - de novo in the child only;
   - give inherited `ins:` events an explicit sequence, or copy the ALT from the parent's truth.vcf (CR7 writes the bases).
   - Reason: the random insertion bases come from the shared RNG (src/main.rs:2017-2023). Parent and child runs on different BAMs can therefore get different sequences, and genmod would then see two different variants. This is inferred from the code, not measured.
2. M16 (S), for anyone who does want haplotype addressing.

The real trio blockers at the hospital are elsewhere:
- M39: the family FASTQs are 7-lane.
- The hospital has run raredisease only as singleton cases.

Re-open M17 only if the owner wants phase-aware trio benchmarking, and then as M16 plus whatshap --ped rather than a new subcommand.

value:M18.better_measurement:
Gate 0 needs no code and uses today's binary. It is a transplant, judged EH against EH, at Q100-confirmed long STR alleles.
(a) Loci. RFC1 (520 bp AAAAG) plus the HG002 Q100 insertions that are at least 90% one motif of period 1-6. Measured with scratchpad str_ins_count.py: 47 are 150 bp or longer, 20 are 250 bp or longer, and 9 are 400 bp or longer, among them chr6:156191499 AAGGG 422 bp and chr16:15999866 TTTCT 710 bp. Keep the loci where Platinum v1.2 says HG001 is near reference.
(b) Plant each into the hospital HG001 30x resample BAM (D25-7403_Seq25-7598_30x_sorted_md.bam), which is depth-matched to HG002's D24-14230. Align spike's reads with the hospital bwa-mem2 command against the whole-genome index. A slice reference must not be used: it forces in-repeat reads onto the locus.
(c) Run EH v5.0.0 on spiked HG001 and on real HG002 with a custom catalog: the hospital RFC1 entry as-is, plus one entry per extra locus.
(d) Set the noise floor first. Measure EH replicate agreement on the two existing HG001 runs (resample vs D25-7403 full) and use it as the pass band.
(e) Pass rule, per locus. Spiked ADIR and ADFL fall within the Poisson 95% interval of the real values (RFC1: ADIR 9, ADFL 20/23), and the spiked long-allele REPCI overlaps the real one. Overall, the pass rate must be at least the replicate agreement.
(f) Controls that must fail. A random sequence of the same length must give ADIR ~0 and no INREPEAT. Aligning to a region-only reference must inflate ADIR versus real.
(g) What decides the novel-only change. It earns its keep only if Gate 0 fails at loci of fragment length or longer, and only because real shows locus-placed IRR pairs that spike lacks. If Gate 0 passes, the remaining work is SIM_RU/SIM_REPCN plus a documented ins: recipe. The off-target half then matters only for FMR1 and C9ORF72 full mutations. Label those unvalidated until a public carrier WGS is used, since CGG/GGGGCC dropout is not modelled.
(h) For the demo, a separate no-code check. Plant explicit ins: alleles above the pathogenic thresholds that are shorter than a fragment (HTT 40+ CAG = 120 bp, C9ORF72 30+ = 180 bp, DMPK 50+ = 150 bp, ATXN1/2/3), and confirm that stranger flags them.
value:M18.notes:
Worth: the demo class (repeat expansions through EH/stranger in raredisease) is genuinely missing, and it matters for the hospital goal (documented: memory hospital-demo-plan.md). But the code mechanism the idea proposes, admitting novel-only starts, probably changes EH's output at only 2 of 51 catalog loci: FMR1 and C9ORF72, the ones with off-target regions. It also matters only for alleles longer than a fragment, and no real carrier of such an allele is on disk to judge against. The idea's own evidence points this way. At RFC1, every real in-repeat read EH used belongs to a pair anchored by its mate (I reproduced this: 0 pure reads at the locus, in-repeat mates at chr2:162752904). That is the class today's tiling already draws. So the idea's own KILL condition ("today's ins: already gives real-like ADIR") is likely to fire at RFC1 and at most loci. Run Gate 0 before writing any code.
Most clinically demoable thresholds can probably be reached today with an explicit ins: of MOTIF x N, since the pathogenic sizes are shorter than a fragment (HTT, ATXN1/2/3, C9ORF72 at 30+, DMPK at 50+). That is inferred, not measured.
The proposed measurement has three defects:
- Its long-allele yardstick (HG001 SAMD12 76 units) is EH background, not a real allele.
- It predicts ADIR ~0 for today's build, which contradicts the anchoring evidence above.
- Its spanning-locus test (2) cannot tell the proposal from today's build.
It also rests on a single locus. Q100 offers 47 long pure STR insertions with truth, which a custom EH catalog can genotype; that is a far stronger yardstick, and it is real data.
Cost: the full str: spec (catalog loci, interruption patterns, a choice of copy that depends on M11/M16, a new count formula with CR5's tests to rework, M12 for FMR1 on male chrX) is M to L. The no-code Gate 0 plus a recipe and SIM_RU/SIM_REPCN annotation is S.
Other risks:
- CR3: the event copy's own STR allele is replaced by the reference allele plus the insertion.
- EH underestimates long alleles (RFC1: truth ~116, EH 51), so truth-vs-call scoring must be EH(spiked) against EH(real).
- Admitting novel-only fragments adds pure-repeat reads that bwa scatters to other arrays genome-wide. That is realistic, but it is new background at those arrays.

value:M19.corrected_claims:
1. Claim: "no 20-80% heteroplasmic SNV, so pileup het phasing does not fire there". Wrong: it fires in the idea's own R43 run. The log (scratchpad robust/chrm/log.txt) shows "chrM:1242-5243: 1 het SNPs, 3 hom-alt SNPs", "phased 1 het SNPs into 1 block", "classified 450 fragments (150 event copy, 300 other)". The het is the reference N at chrM:3107. Measured with samtools mpileup -q20 on the HG002 35x BAM: 20,291 of 20,740 reads carry a 1-bp deletion there, and the 461 reads with a base are C 153 / T 271. call_snps (src/loh.rs:101) has no reference-base check in its het branch, so it calls C/T het. On the hospital HG002 BAM: 9,323 of 9,569 reads deleted, C 121 / T 118. By the same rule that would also be called het (inferred).
2. Consequence, measured with an exact 18-mer count on the R43 FASTQs: 12,563 kept real reads carry the 3107 deletion and 0 carry a base; 5,234 spike reads carry C and 0 carry the deletion. So about 29% of reads over 3107 lose a deletion that every real read has. 3107 is 136 bp from MELAS m.3243. The same CR3 mechanism hits HG002's homoplasmic 310 T>TC for any event within 2 kb of it, including the proposed 2259 site.

4. "6 only in HG002 (e.g. 2259C>T, 4745A>G, 7337G>A, 13326T>C)": those four examples are HG001-only. Measured with bcftools on the hospital MT VCFs:
   - HG001-only homoplasmic: 152, 2259, 4745, 7337, 13326, 13680, 14831, 14872.

value:M19.better_measurement:
No code. Use the hospital BAMs and the local broadinstitute/gatk docker image.

1. Build the real mixture by read count, not by sampling fraction. Name-hash subsample HG001 and HG002 chrM pairs so HG001's share of chrM reads is f in {0.05, 0.2}. chrM depth differs between the samples, so sampling at f and 1-f does not give AF f. Measure the mixture's realised AF at the 5 isolated HG001-only sites (2259, 4745, 7337, 13326, 13680) by pileup. That measured value is the yardstick.
2. Spike the same sites into the hospital HG002 BAM at those levels, in groups at least 7 kb apart (about 3 runs of roughly 1 minute each). Align with the hospital command (bwa-mem2 mem -M -K 100000000) and merge. Also make a sham run with unchanged reads.
3. Run Mutect2 --mitochondria-mode and FilterMutectCalls identically on the mixture, spiked and sham chrM, non-control region only.

Pass rules, each against 10-salt split-half noise of both samples (both levels are draws). Compare with the realised SIM_ALT_FRAGS share, not the requested af, and do not use a single-binomial 99% interval.
- (a) AF difference within 2.576 x sqrt(s_spike^2 + s_mix^2).
- (b) Alt-read base quality, position in read, strand and F1R2/F2R1 within the real-vs-real range.
- (c) FILTER agrees, ignoring clustered_events and haplocheck contamination flags. The mixture carries all 14 HG001 differences at once, so those flags differ by design.
- (d) Background integrity in each window, which the proposal lacks:
  - deletion share at 3107 and AF of 310 T>TC, spiked vs mixture and sham, within noise;
  - no new Mutect2 calls in the window.
  - Predicted to FAIL today (inferred from R43: 3107 deletion share about 0.70 vs 0.978 real).

Broken controls:
- B1: af x2 must fail (a).
- B2: synthetic reads with flat quality must fail (b).
- B3: plant within about 300 bp of HG001 16023 (real 0.70 heteroplasmy) and measure the AF distortion from the coin. Only distortion above noise earns the copy-unknown change.

Decision rule:
- If (a)-(c) pass at both f and B3 shows no distortion, write docs (af = heteroplasmy on chrM) plus a warning for events within 1 kb of the chrM ends.
- Separately, fix (d). Two cheap, genome-wide fixes: no het call at a non-ACGT reference base, and carry homoplasmic indels from the pileup into the haplotype (CR3).

eKLIPse: a linear DEL at m.8470-13447 sits mid-chrM and needs no circular code. Test it as-is on the hospital mt_subsample path, labelled self-consistency only (no real carrier).
value:M19.notes:
VALUE. Most of what the proposal would build fixes problems that are measured not to matter:
- copy_rate(None, v) = v already gives heteroplasmy semantics (src/synth.rs:694-699; R43 realised 0.291 at 0.3).
- GT already matches Mutect2's 0/1.
- Only 7 of 187 P/LP sites lie near the circular junction.
- A demo plants one variant per sample, so the 7 kb rule is moot.
- A mid-chrM DEL needs no circular haplotype.

The hospital outcome is also gated: skip_mt_annotation: true in all 3 on-disk params.yaml files, so MT calls are not annotated or ranked today. hospital-demo-plan.md names LDLR and other nuclear genes, not mito. HG002 has 1 PASS heteroplasmy above 1% (6210 T>C at 0.085), so the "real heteroplasmy FILTER rate" yardstick is n=1.

The idea misses the real chrM defect, which is measured. spike's pileup calls a fake het at the reference N chrM:3107. The haplotype then writes C there, so 0 of 5,234 spike reads carry the 3107 deletion that 12,563 of 12,563 real reads carry. The same CR3 mechanism drops the sample's homoplasmic indels (e.g. 310 T>TC) to about 1-v inside each 4 kb window. This affects 19% of P/LP MT sites, MELAS 3243 among them.

The proposed minimal mode (force copy unknown, skip phasing) would remove the coin but leave N at 3107, so the tell stays. The two fixes in better_measurement remove it, and both pay off genome-wide, not only on chrM.

The claim that the mixture gives "nearly for free" the general low-VAF yardstick (concept test 2) is overstated. A chrM mixture tests Mutect2-MT at about 6,000x. Nuclear low-VAF/mosaic realism needs a nuclear mixture.

Cost: M (3) is fair for the full proposal; a circular haplotype alone could be L. The no-code check plus the two small fixes is about 2. Gate B runtime is honest: R43 took 52 s and 2.64 GB RSS, GATK docker is present, the HG001 and HG002 hospital BAMs are on disk, and the CEPH BAMs are not.

value:M2.corrected_claims:
1) The idea says spike's R1 over-erring 1.9-2.2x comes from the missing mate key, so a mate split would stop R1 over-erring at the qualities callers trust. That holds at Q25 but not at Q37. At Q37 spike's R2 also errs 1.5x real (0.0234% vs 0.0155%, errproc_35x.out). With mates pooled, the high-Q (Q>=30) excess is 1.77x (2.10e-4 vs 1.19e-4) and shows up in every read class: class <30 1.7-2.3x, class 30-35 1.5-2.5x, and class >=35 in the last 10 cycles 4.2x (3.77e-4 vs 9.0e-5; phys/recur_35x.out, hiq section). A mate split moves this excess between the mates but does not shrink it. Inferred result: R1 Q37 about 0.015% (still about 1.8x real) and R2 about 0.027% (worse than today). Callers count both mates at a site, so their total error load is unchanged. At Q25 the split would bring R1 to about 1.2x (spike vs real pooled 0.379% vs 0.317%, computed from errproc_35x.out).
2) The fastp impact claim does not hold. The 275,690 too_many_N reads (0.036% of 760M; hospital fastp.json) were removed before alignment, so the BAM spike learns from has none of them. At about 2.4e-5 N per base (about 0.004 N per read), spike's reads would essentially never trip n_base_limit=5. Emitting N changes no fastp filter outcome.
3) The idea says the skew changes what DeepVariant's candidate thresholds count. Its default 0.12 fraction needs about 4-5 alt reads at 30-35x. The measured candidate gap (real 453 vs spike 85, recur_35x.out) is 81% one-strand in real (366/453), and same-strand same-alt sites with >=3 reads are real 181 vs spike 2. That points to recurrent strand-specific errors, not the emission spectrum. From the errproc_35x.out spectra, the skew raises chance pair coincidences about 1.8x (sum p^2 0.64 for R1, 0.59 for R2, vs 0.33) and triples about 4x. Inferred effect: >=2-read sites go from 329 to about 600 (real 1247) and >=3-read sites from 2 to about 8 (real 181). It closes a minority of the gap that callers see.
4) Widening the mask "or a shared clip boundary" conflicts with memory bad-tails-20261007. There, same-strand shared clip spots were measured to be mostly bad ends set off by the sequence (27% vs 3% shuffled; 2.5% on the other strand). Masking ±5 bp there would remove the crash-start errors that K2 depends on, and K2 passed narrowly (z -2.64). Restrict the widening to I/D in the CIGAR or to boundaries shared on both strands.
5) Mask widening is a small lever. The 11.3% within 5 bp of a Q100 record is small next to the clip-counted share of spike-rule high-Q errors: 53% (2226/4202). Overall, spike's learning rule counts high-Q errors at 1.93x the truth-masked aligned rate (2.41e-4 vs 1.25e-4, learnmask_35x.out). Widening addresses at most about 11% of that inflation.
6) "Spike never writes an N" is too broad. It writes N at Q2 wherever the template is N. The claim holds for called bases: spike21 has 0 N.
7) The emission matrix does not need a mate dimension. Per-mate top-alt shares (0.747/0.692 and 0.837/0.819) both fall within ±0.05 of a single pooled value, so the proposed gate cannot tell mate-keyed emission from pooled emission.
8) A mate bit on the full and mid cells is risky. It doubles 10,240 full cells (4 symbols x 8 classes x 5 x 4 x 4 x 4, quality.rs:50-79) under MIN_ERROR_BASES=200. v1 was refuted on exactly this kind of cell thinness, and v2 had only 9 of 16 crash-tail cells at >=200 bases even at about 200k pairs (memory quality-model-run). Halving the counts pushes more cells to back off and risks K2.
value:M2.better_measurement:
Run one check before building (minutes, offline, a Python edit of recur.py). Learn the (true base in sequencing orientation, Q bin) matrix on the even-numbered blocks of the real reads, with mates pooled. On the odd-numbered blocks, redraw spike21's per-site, per-strand alt counts multinomially from that matrix. Then report candidates/Mb and same-strand same-alt sites with >=2 and >=3 reads. Build the emission part only if the redraw closes at least 25% of the >=2-read gap (329 to 1247), a threshold fixed before running. If it does not, ship only Q2 -> N.

Checks after building:
(a) Spectrum on held-out windows, not on the learning blocks (blocks.tsv looks like the 20 learning blocks, so K2b would be in-sample). Use K1's 35x SNV windows and the hospital 20-event windows. Pass if the Q<15 top-alt share per true base is within ±0.05 of real. A transposed matrix must fail, and so must master.
(b) Mate split, gated on the R1/R2 mismatch ratio rather than on absolute levels. Pass if it is within ±15% of real: 35x Q25 0.433 and Q37 0.542; hospital Q24 0.680 and Q40 0.483. Master (0.873/0.795) must fail, and so must a build with the mates swapped (ratio >1). Report absolute levels, R1 and R2 summed, without gating them, because a level excess that has nothing to do with mates is already present.
(c) N: zero non-N Q2 bases, and an N rate per base within 2x of real.
(d) Regression guards, because the change thins cells and changes the random stream: K1 crash share and SD, K2 bad-end clip z, and K7 against master's spread over 5 seeds.
(e) Outcome: recur.py candidates/Mb and >=2-read same-alt sites, reported against the prediction fixed before building (about 1.8x).
value:M2.notes:
The gaps are real as distributions. Measured in phys/errproc_*.out: the Q<15 top-alt share is 0.34 in spike vs 0.69-0.84 in real; spike emits 441 Q2 bases that are not N, against 0 in real; and spike's R1/R2 mismatch ratio at Q25 is 0.87 vs 0.43 in real.

The effect on outcomes is small. Spiked reads already carry SPIKE_ names, so tells such as Q2 on a called base or an odd spectrum carry no indistinguishability value. The planted variants' own calls in the LDLR/raredisease demo are unaffected (inferred). The mate split moves the high-Q error load between the mates but does not reduce the total that callers see. Most of the caller-relevant gap (candidates, recurring sites, one-strand errors) comes from recurrent site-specific errors, which this idea does not address.

The proposed falsifying measurement would fail a correct build. Its absolute per-mate Q37 band (±20%) also picks up a level excess with mates pooled (1.77x high-Q, 4.2x in the last 10 cycles of good reads), which comes from the learning rule (53% of counted high-Q errors are in clips, learnmask_35x.out) and not from the mate key. The scoring is also in-sample (it appears to use the learning blocks), and the per-mate spectrum check cannot tell mate-keyed from pooled emission.

A simpler, safer version:
1) Q2 -> N: about 5 lines in generate_from_template. When q is the symbol the sample uses only for N, emit N and skip the error draw. Gate it on the N check plus K7.
2) A 4x4 emission matrix per Q bin (Q<15 and Q>=15), pooled over mates. It replaces random_different_base at synth.rs:229 and is learned from the called base at quality.rs:1014. Build it only if the offline redraw check passes.
3) For mates, a per-(mate, symbol) multiplier on the existing cell rate, in the spirit of v2's run_ratio, instead of a mate bit that splits the full and mid cells.
4) Drop shared clip boundaries from the mask widening.

The cost of S/40 lines is honest for the code. With K7 random-stream changes, tests, mutants and the K1/K2 guards, it is about a day, hence cost 2.

The bigger lever these measurements point to is a separate idea: the learning rule's high-Q error inflation and the recurrent strand-specific error sites (one-strand candidates: 366 of 453 in real vs 46 of 85 in spike).

value:M20.better_measurement:
Run the no-code version first, and write the predictions down before the run (all INFERRED from my replica):
- het SMN1 DEL: Total_CN_raw 2.92 ±0.15, SMN1 1, SMN2 2.
- hom SMN1 DEL: Total_CN_raw about 1.95, SMN1 0, isSMA True.

Add a test that sees where reads are placed. Measure it on the realigned merged BAM (or the full-FASTQ route), counting primary non-duplicate reads in four bins: MAPQ 0 at SMN1, MAPQ 0 at SMN2, MAPQ>=20 at SMN1, MAPQ>=20 at SMN2. For the het run, the after/before ratio must be:
- MAPQ 0 at SMN1 and at SMN2: 0.75 ±0.04 each.
- MAPQ>=20 at SMN1: 0.50 ±0.06.
- MAPQ>=20 at SMN2: 1.00 ±0.06.

The run must reject clean --min-mapq 0 --allow-resistant, as well as plain clean. My inference is that --min-mapq 0 passes the caller-only rule (about 24.8% removed, and the right shares at the paralog sites) while leaving SMN2's MAPQ 0 depth at 1.0 or above. The caller would hide that, but raredisease's CNV callers would show it as an SMN1 DEL plus an SMN2 DUP.

Test the one premise origin's p=1/2 rests on, on real data: MAPQ 0 reads split 50:50 between the two loci whatever the copy numbers. Use a sample with unequal SMN1:SMN2, such as the hospital's Seq25-16020 or Seq25-16025 (SMN2=3; their BAMs are at the hospital, not here) or 1000G NYGC CN1 carriers sliced to the SMN regions. MAPQ 0 counts should be near 1:1, while MAPQ>=20 reads at the paralog sites follow the copy numbers. If MAPQ 0 placement instead tracks copy number, origin's 1/2 is wrong.

Keep the caller's per-site SMN1 fraction, but test it binomially, not against the CN2 band. Drop the sequence-informed refinement unless the placement test fails.
value:M20.notes:
VALUE:
- SMN results reach clinicians at this hospital. Its Scout fork parses SMNCopyNumberCaller TSVs into SMN1/SMN2 copy numbers and isSMA/isCarrier (scout/parse/smn.py in the hospital's scout-gmc-norr fork, documented in code).
- raredisease runs SMNCOPYNUMBERCALLER 1.1.2 (~/.nextflow/assets/nf-core/raredisease/conf/modules/raredisease.config:31-41, modules/nf-core/smncopynumbercaller/main.nf).
- The owner has never named SMN; the stated targets are LDLR, SNVs/indels and exon-level CNVs. So the SMA-demo value is INFERRED.
- The second payoff is real: this is the cleanest real-data test of origin, in exactly the twin, one-XA regime its physics gate covered (MEASURED, see claim 7).
- Origin's removals do reach the hospital route: they join replaced_names and go into the FASTQ filter (src/main.rs:869-920).

MEASUREMENT FLAW:
- SMNCopyNumberCaller pools SMN1 and SMN2 reads whatever their placement. This is DOCUMENTED in Chen et al. 2020; I did not check it locally because the caller is not installed here.
- So the proposed caller-only rule only shows that about a quarter of the reads from both genes went. It cannot tell origin from --min-mapq 0, which the physics gate showed is wrong (L 0.271 / P 1.296).
- A version where only the look-alike half is broken would give about 3.27 (INFERRED) and fail the Total_CN_raw band. That part of the rule is useful.

COST:
- The honest version is hours to a day:
  - install the caller (pixi or bioconda);
  - run spike origin once on the 37 GB HG002 BAM for one 28 kb DEL;
  - merge, or build a slice of the caller's regions;
  - run the caller;
  - count the four depth bins.
- Split gene conversion (b) off as its own idea. It is a different event (SNVs at the paralog sites on one copy), and real conversions are often partial.

RISKS my replica did not model:
- Sample phase calls (R7, CR3 pileup) inside the twin region could skew the removal chances.
- The junction reads are synthesised in segdup flanks.
The placement test would catch either.

value:M21.corrected_claims:
1. The fold-4.69 bin is real library depth, not mappability, and falsifier (2) as written excludes it.
   - chr20:14862000-14863000 has GC 0.126 (measured: samtools faidx on the no_alt FASTA).
   - It has 103 primary, non-duplicate reads at any MAPQ, against 225-317 in the seven neighbouring 1 kb bins (measured: samtools view -c -F 0xF04 on the HG002 35x BAM).
   - Only 82 of those 103 reads (80%) are at MAPQ 20 or above, so the "≥95% MAPQ≥20" filter drops the very bin the idea leads with.
2. "Work and removal lists grow with the footprint" is true but costs little.
   - The 1 Mb R19 run took 19.2 s wall at 704 MB RSS (measured: perf/dup1/log.txt).
   - fastq.sh scans the whole FASTQ whatever the list size (inferred).
   - The performance framing should be dropped.
3. "Real quality strings survive" applies only to kept originals. A DUP's added copy is still a synthetic read from the reference plus the copy's alleles (synth.rs:418-438, generate_depth_pair → generate_read_pair).
4. In reality a tandem DUP is purely additive (inferred from the haplotype layout L+I+I+R).
   - Every reference-aligned original stays valid: S-crossers are the left flank into copy 1, E-crossers are copy 2 into the right flank.
   - The only new molecules are one extra set of interior fragments plus the copy1→copy2 junction, at about v·D_local.
   - So SIMPLEST's "replace event-copy pairs crossing E" is unneeded bookkeeping. Keeping everything and adding junction fragments at local density is simpler, and it makes the FASTQ route append-only.
5. The CR2 81.09x/28.13x probe is a synthetic chrT BAM from the Codex script (docs/review/REVIEW.md:2941-2949), not real reads. Falsifier (1) is a unit check, not a realism test.
6. The R19 counts check out (measured, log.txt): 63,390 suppressed, 120,046 tiled, 72,263 = 63,390 + 8,873 removed from the FASTQ, cov 50.3, SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 4.69, SIM_ALT_FRAGS 17. The 88%-of-SNV-pairs figure checks out too: 1 - 421/3579 ≈ 0.88.
value:M21.better_measurement:
Use one pooled test whose two predictions are far apart, and run it on today's binary before any code.

**Statistic.**
- Count reads at MAPQ 20 or above, primary and non-duplicate, in both the merged and the donor BAM. Count every interior 1 kb bin at least one fragment (1.5 kb) from either breakpoint, including bins with low-MAPQ reads. Drop only bins under 50 reads.
- Regress added = merged − donor on donor D per bin, pooled over the 40 seeded chr20 DUPs (scripts/cr4_placements.py, md5 8f304862…), the 1 Mb chr20:14.55-15.55 Mb DUP and the 4 LDLR ClinVar DUPs.
- Uniform tiling predicts added = k − (1−v)·D... more precisely added ≈ const − v·D, a slope near −0.5 at v=0.5. A correct image map predicts added = v·D, a slope near +0.5.

**Pass rule.** The slope's 95% CI lies inside [0.4, 0.6] and excludes 0. Today's full mode must fail it, and that failure is a pre-registered precondition. Also report the any-MAPQ ratio in bins with less than 95% of reads at MAPQ≥20. There the image map is expected to undershoot at 1 + v·(1 − f_lowMAPQ), because only pool reads get copies. That is a known CR4-like limit, to be stated rather than hidden by a bin filter.

**A first data point already exists** (measured: ~/sv_slice_test/data/B0 vs B3 S1.bam, ClinVar 976329, a 6.5 kb LDLR DUP, SIM_DEPTH_FOLD 1.35).

| Interior bin | Donor D | Added |
|---|---|---|
| chr19:11106000 | 309 | 152 |
| chr19:11107000 | 286 | 160 |
| chr19:11108000 | 242 | 177 |
| chr19:11109000 | 300 | 124 |
| chr19:11110000 | 277 | 159 |

The synthetic share stays flat at about 296 reads per kb whatever D is. The thin bin gets the most added (177, against v·D = 121), and its ratio is 1.73 against 1.5. That is the uniform-tiling signature on the hospital-relevant locus.

**Gate B.** Run it on existing slices or ±1 Mb windows (depth is local), so it needs no 54 GB merge. Compare --dup-model junction with full under the same slope test. Junction-mode bins within 1.5 kb of a breakpoint must be excluded, because its junction tiling is additive at cov·v/(1−v).

**Keep:** the sham v=0 test (3).

**Replace transplant re-runs (4)** with a DUP-only re-run of the rounds that contain DUPs, since only those outputs change in the DUP-only scope.
value:M21.notes:
**Worth.** The worth is real only for duplications, and it is modest for the owner's hospital goal.

**Where it matters (measured).**
- In a DUP interior spike emits (1−v)·D_donor + 2v·D_anchor. The LDLR B3 DUP and the R19 1 Mb DUP both show this on real reads.
- The 4.69-fold bin is a GC 0.126 library dip, not mappability. Read-depth callers GC-correct, so flat synthetic depth over GC-extreme bins reads as an excess amplification. That can split or inflate CN calls on large DUPs, which is a genuine CNV-caller realism defect.

**Hospital LDLR demo (documented / measured).**
- Only 4 of the 37 LDLR ClinVar SVs are DUPs (sv-caller-slices memory).
- The one measured, B3, has fold 1.35 and a mean interior ratio of about 1.55 against 1.5.
- CNVnator missed B3 on the FULL BAM anyway (score.txt), and Manta found it from junction evidence, which the depth model does not touch.
- A local-dosage fix would make B3 slightly weaker for depth callers. So no outcome flip is expected there (inferred), and gCNV is untested locally.

**Other event types (inferred).**
- DEL interiors are already locally correct by construction: interior pairs are suppressed at the copy rate and nothing is tiled there. Only the ±2 kb flanks are scaled by the anchor.
- For SNVs and indels the reads over the site are still synthetic under remapping, so callers' calls at the site would not change. Restoring real flank reads is cosmetic for calling. M10 (in-read edits) is the right lever for SNVs.

**Scope it to DUPs.** "Keep every original, add one jittered depth copy per event-copy interior pool fragment (generate_dup_depth_copies already does this), add junction fragments at about v·D_local." That is roughly cost 2: mostly junction mode with its junction count fixed, not L. It also makes the DUP FASTQ route append-only, which cuts removal-list risk.

**Kill or defer the full multi-type proposal.**
- The value outside DUPs is speculative.
- Output bytes change for every non-additive event, forcing transplant re-runs.
- The novel-interior density for INS needs a model that does not exist yet.

**Falsifier (2) is not well-posed as written.**
- Its mappability filter excludes the headline bin.
- Its Poisson band is uncalibrated: phased suppression and synthetic draws are not Poisson on the merged count.
- On typical bins (fold 1.1) uniform tiling lands near 1.6, at the edge of a ±0.1 band. So "≥95% of bins in band" was never shown to reject today's binary.
- Replace it with the slope test in better_measurement and run it on master first.

**Known limit to state up front.** Copies are drawn only from the MAPQ≥20 proper-pair pool. In poorly mappable bins the any-MAPQ ratio will undershoot 1+v, the same mechanism as CR4. That is acceptable, but it must be stated, and CR2's design note warns against double-counting mappability.

Rebuilding today's B1 merged.bam (1 h 42 min, already measured and since deleted) adds little, because merge+sort equals merge on samtools-sorted input.
value:M22.notes:
Value: real but conditional. The change does not alter caller calls or the hospital LDLR/raredisease demo, which runs on FASTQ. It removes the measured bottleneck of every whole-genome spike -> merged.bam loop. That loop is now the only valid route for Manta and CNVnator after the slice refutation, and it dominates the --callRegions fast route the user is weighing. So it could decide whether the 37-SV LDLR check is practical.

Cost S-M is honest. It means editing the generated script, rewriting the stub-samtools tests at src/main.rs:3626-3800 (they pin removed.bam being written before counting, and the merge/sort/index calls), and a README version note.

Simpler variant with a smaller test diff: invert the selection inside today's single view (view -@T -N ^list -o outside.bam -U removed.bam). The huge output then goes to the threaded -o, the tiny removed set to unthreaded -U, and the guard and the removed.bam tests stay as they are. Then drop the sort, use merge --write-index and idxstats. It keeps a 37 GB temp file and an extra compress/decompress, so the proposed stream is faster. Or stream with -U removed.bam and guard afterwards: one pass, but it fails late on a wrong BAM. The proposal's separate guard pass costs about 1.5 min on B1 (0.92 s on the slice x about 100, inferred) and fails fast. Acceptable.

Also worth checking that sim.bam's @HD is SO:coordinate before dropping the sort; today align.sh always sorts it.

My test files were removed from the scratchpad, and nothing in the repo was touched.

value:M23.already_done_or_refuted: Not done or refuted. The one-awk design comes from review finding 7 (merged 658baa4). That fix was measured at 1.30x the old time, so its slowdown was known when it was accepted (memory independent-review-20261004.md). F3's ~33 min for 380 M pairs is a prediction, not a measurement: fastq.sh has never been timed on the real hospital pair (memory full-fastq.md).
value:M23.corrected_claims:
1. The idea treats the single awk as the cap. That holds only at high thread counts. spike's default is --threads 4 (src/main.rs:119, default_value_t = 4), and fastq.sh inherits it, so each mate gets pigz -p2. At that setting compression is the bottleneck. Measured on 500k real pairs from perf/fq (scratchpad m23v/run): today's fastq.sh took 6.97 s at THREADS 4 and 5.28 s at THREADS 16, and pigz -6 -p2 alone took 6.41 s per mate. So at the default, stage 1 can gain at most about 1.09x (inferred). The "33-39 to 15-17 min" claim needs THREADS of 16 or more.
2. The R21 timings may be inflated by machine load. This machine had a load average of 63-84 on 72 cores during my checks (uptime); the load during R21 is unknown. My runs were about 1.6x slower than R21's, so only ratios taken in the same session mean anything.
3. Stage 2's ">=5x" needs BGZF block copy. At 16 threads, -6 recompression has a floor of 1.72 s per 500k pairs per mate at pigz -p8 (measured). Against the per-mate awk's 2.75 s, stage 2 would gain only about 1.6x over stage 1 unless blocks are copied (inferred). That would fail the idea's own "kill stage 2 if not >=2x" rule. On plain-gzip input, single-threaded decompression runs at about 280 MB/s (pigz -dc: 0.61 s for 173 MB, measured). For 131 GB per mate (380 M x ~345 B) that is about 8 min, so even stage 2 cannot reach "a few minutes" (inferred). Whether the hospital FASTQ is BGZF is unknown.
4. The scratch prototype perf/run/mate.awk prints only kept records' names. To keep today's refusal parity, every record's name must go to the FIFO; otherwise two swapped removed records pass where today's script refuses.
5. Cost M is too low for stage 2: a native splice with boundary-spanning records and error parity is about L. Stage 1 alone is about S.
Confirmed:
- The line references :2264, :2327, :2412 and :2424-2428 match master ba9f4e7.
- HG002.novaseq.chr20.R1 and the 40x R1 are BGZF: both headers start 1f8b 0804 ... 4243 0200.
- The perf/fq timing input is plain pigz gzip (1f8b 0800), not BGZF, so it cannot test block copy.
value:M23.better_measurement:
Value gate (cheap, at the hospital, first):
- Time today's fastq.sh (or --into-fastq) on the real 380 M pair, with the THREADS actually used.
- Time the raredisease wall-clock for the same sample.
- Run head -c 18 | xxd on the raw R1.
- Build stage 1 only if fastq.sh is at least ~10% of spike-to-VCF time and THREADS is at least 8. At THREADS 4, compression is the bottleneck (measured above).
Correctness gates for stage 1:
- (a) Compressed md5 of both outputs identical to today's script, at THREADS 4 and 16. This is stricter than decompress-and-compare, and it should hold: pigz -6 output was md5-identical across -p 2, 4 and 8 (measured).
- (b) The 13 existing test_fastq_script_* tests pass unchanged.
- (c) Mutant 1 drops the cmp. It must fail test_fastq_script_refuses_mates_in_a_different_order.
- (d) Mutant 2 sends only kept records' names to the FIFO. Add a test that swaps two adjacent removed records: today's script refuses it, so mutant 2 must fail it.
- (e) Fault injection: truncate R2 mid-file, and send SIGTERM mid-run. Afterwards there must be no partial output, no leftover gawk, pigz or cmp process (pgrep), and the error must name the cause. My negative control shows each gawk dies with 'fatal: print ... Broken pipe' when cmp exits. The script must hide that and map cmp's 'line N' to record N.
Timing gate:
- At least 3 interleaved runs per variant, on an unloaded machine or with load reported. Report the median at THREADS 4, 8 and 16.
- Pass if stage 1 at 16 is no more than 1.1 x max(the per-mate awk alone, pigz alone), so the cmp costs at most 10%.
- Replace the flat >=2x rule, which sits on the noise edge. I measured 1.65-2.0x for the filter stage alone (today 4.5-5.5 s vs per-mate+cmp 2.75 s for 500k pairs, outputs identical).
Stage 2 and interleaving: no gate until the hospital file is shown to be BGZF and the value gate passes.
value:M23.notes:
On worth, the outcome barely moves. Documented runtimes:
- raredisease's Manta alone took 7 h 8 min on the full BAM (memory sv-caller-slices.md).
- The user calls raredisease's realignment of the whole genome "slow" (memory hospital-demo-plan.md).
- fastq.sh at a predicted 33-39 min is therefore a small share of each hospital sample's spike-to-VCF time.
- Stage 1 saves about 20 min, and only at THREADS of 16 or more. At the default of 4 it saves nothing (inferred).
- No caller output and no realism result changes. It is a convenience, not a blocker.

The mechanism holds where it applies. On 500k real HG002 NovaSeq pairs (scratchpad m23v), one gawk per mate with every record's name streamed through FIFOs into cmp:
- took 2.75 s, against 4.5-5.5 s for today's single awk, both uncompressed;
- gave md5-identical outputs (38950075, d54ef8ff);
- caught a swapped adjacent pair at record 100001, exiting 1.
The cross-mate check is close to free, so the simplest form of stage 1 is sound.

A paste-joined single awk (one record per pair) was a weaker alternative: 3.2-4.5 s.

Recommendation:
- Keep stage 1 as a small optional change, gated on the hospital's measured fastq.sh share and THREADS.
- Drop stage 2. It is BGZF-only, about L in cost, and capped near 1.6x over stage 1 without block copy.
- Drop interleaving SPIKE_ pairs into removed slots from this idea. There is no evidence of harm: F2 measured 1,296/1,296 appended reads identical to sim.bam. It belongs with M46's order-sensitivity check.

Pairs with M37 (fail fast on the wrong FASTQ). A wrong raw pair today is refused only at END, after the whole pass ('found 0 of N'). At the hospital that costs more than the throughput this idea recovers.

Nothing was written in the repo or worktrees. Scratch files are in /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/m23v.

value:M24.corrected_claims:
(1) Master is ba9f4e7, not 4a5672d. startup-fixes was fast-forwarded onto master on 2026-10-07 (git log). The cited lines src/main.rs:659-664 and src/quality.rs:476-506 are still correct.
