value:M24.better_measurement:
Run Gate B first, on the logs that already exist. Count the spike calls in each campaign (transplant/full: 19; transplant2/full: 14) and multiply by the per-run read+learn cost measured at that campaign's thread count. Then divide by the campaign's wall time. Kill if the saving is under 10 min or under 5% of the campaign. It already fails: about 0.5 min of about 40 min.

If the idea is ever revived, B1 as written (md5 on 3 cases) is necessary but not enough:
- Add a unit round-trip test: `load(save(p)) == p`. QualityProfile derives PartialEq under cfg(test), so this covers every field, including symbol_of, small, pshift, census, n_pairs and n_blocks, which may not move an md5 on 3 cases.
- Add a test that a profile saved by a build with a changed SAMPLE_BLOCKS or learn constant is refused. Keying on the spike version string alone lets dev builds reuse stale tables silently.
- The timing check needs a pass rule, for example 5 alternating runs and median wall time ≤ fresh minus 0.8 × (logged read + learn).
- A safer, simpler key: hash the pairs read from the 20 blocks (the cheap step, 0.6 s with 8 threads) and skip only learning. That removes the in-place-rewrite staleness risk, at the price of keeping about a third of the cost.
value:M24.notes:
VALUE:
- No caller output changes (byte-identical by design) and no realism changes, so the only possible value is runtime.
- Measured, the runtime at stake is about 1.8-2.2 s per run with threads. Across a whole transplant campaign of 14-19 runs that is about 0.5-2 min of about 40 min.
- The two loops the idea says it helps (slice_loop.sh and real_events.sh) never hit the cache, because each run gets a newly cut slice.bam.
- The hospital demo is one run followed by hours of FASTQ building and raredisease.
- Nothing blocks a user.

COST:
- M is honest for the code.
- A hand-written versioned format of two HashMap ContextMaps, the error tables and the class counts would have to track every future change to the profile struct, in a project that is still changing that struct weekly (v1, v2 and the speed fix all landed on 2026-10-07).
- It also creates a new class of silent staleness that the judgment-gate culture would have to guard forever.

SIMPLER, needs no code: put many events in one invocation (repeated --event or --vcf). The profile is learned once per run, and transplant's batches() already does this.

SIDE FINDING, for the reality skeptic or the owner (inferred from code, not measured):
- Under v2, a slice-route run learns its quality profile only from the slice. indexed_windows reads the slice's own BAI (quality.rs:1091-1235), and the slice is event ± 100 kb (slice_loop.sh:35,58).
- That is about 20k pairs at 30x (inferred), against the about 120k the v2 gate found necessary for crashed-tail cells. That is the same thin-sample regime that refuted v1 (bccc43a).
- MIN_PAIRS_TO_LEARN is 30, so the run goes ahead silently.
- That is where loading a profile learned on the parent BAM could matter. It would be a realism change, not a byte-identical one, and would need its own falsifying test: K1/K2 crash share and bad-end clips on slice runs against full-BAM runs of the same events.
- It matters less because the slice route is only for preliminary checks; the hospital runs use full FASTQ (hospital-demo-plan memory).

value:M25.already_done_or_refuted: Not done and not refuted. Threads step 1 split the LOH, census and duplicate-scan reads into chunks with fold_bam_region. Nobody has trimmed the per-record work: removed_duplicates still turns every record into a RecordBuf, and the pileup still does one HashMap entry per base. The two plans this idea would drop ("Pass 2 edge strips" and "One streaming pass per event") are only open_issues that a map reader in this workflow inferred (journal.jsonl). A grep of the repo's README, docs/ and .claude/ for "edge strip", "streaming pass" and "serial floor" finds nothing, so neither plan is in the owner's backlog and dropping them saves no scheduled work. Documented (README.md:1365): the duplicate re-read costs 5-6 s at 1 thread on a 3 Mb event, 2.5-3 s at 4 threads, and under 0.1 s on a 1 kb event.
value:M25.corrected_claims:
1. The cited log cannot give these numbers. perf/dup1/log.txt has whole-second timestamps only ([...T17:26:39Z]; its elapsed column is whole seconds). At 1 s resolution "pass 2 0.30 s" or "duplicate scan 2.07 s" cannot be read from it. I re-ran the same binary and command (spike-new, dup:chr20:14550000-15550000, --threads 1, seed 1) with each stderr line timestamped to the millisecond (scratchpad m25v/run1.log). The machine was loaded (load average about 75 on 72 cores): wall 24.6 s, user 21.5 s. Measured intervals: event pass 1 0.94 s, pass 2 0.34 s, census 0.50 s, LOH pileup 1.94 s, phasing 0.89 s, tiling and simulation 4.33 s, duplicate scan 2.38 s, FASTQ write 2.21 s, startup quality sample about 9.7 s (log: read 4.5 s, learned 5.2 s). The idea's figures hold to within about 15%. All 5 output files are md5-identical to the earlier run.
2. The idea's breakdown leaves out the biggest pieces. Its items add up to about 7.9 s of 19.2 s. The startup quality sample (7 s in the cited log, 9.7 s in mine; that is M24) and tiling (3-4 s) are each larger than anything this idea fixes.
3. The duplicate scan does more than "build an OriginRecord with an owned name before filtering". It first turns every record into a full RecordBuf, decoding sequence, qualities and every tag (origin.rs:754 and :797). Only then does origin_record drop unmapped, secondary and supplementary reads, copy the name and parse XA into placements (origin.rs:626-660). duplicates_of never uses placements or XA.
4. htslib's 0.14-0.21 s is not spike's decoding floor. spike decodes BGZF with noodles-bgzf on flate2's default miniz_oxide (Cargo.toml has flate2 = "1"; Cargo.lock has miniz_oxide 0.8.9 and no libdeflater). noodles-bgzf 0.35 has a `libdeflate` feature that spike does not turn on. The right floor inside spike is pass 2: it reads the same window through the same noodles stack and checks flags first. It takes 0.34 s, against the duplicate scan's 2.38 s, which is 7x. That ratio, not samtools, is what supports the per-record diagnosis.
5. "Pass 2 is 1.6%" was measured at 1 thread. The strip plan's own claim was about a serial floor at 8 and 16 threads, where pass 2 is still unchunked (extract.rs:118-180) and a 3 Mb DEL in clean mode takes 9.9 s in total (README). At about 0.34 s per Mb, pass 2 would be about 1 s, or roughly 10% at 16 threads (inferred). The conclusion (small in absolute terms) still holds, but the 1-thread number does not show it.
6. The simplest version cannot meet the idea's own ≥50% gate. On the 1 Mb DUP's scan window (chr20:14538501-15561500), 163,341 of 299,922 primary mapped records (54.5%) are either flagged duplicate or named in the pre-duplicate removed set of 63,390 names (measured with samtools plus fastq_removed_reads.txt). A filter that only skips the other records saves at most about 45% of the avoidable work, about 39% of the step (inferred). The rest of the records still go through RecordBuf.
7. Gate B cannot run as written. perf_event_paranoid is 4, and `perf stat` is refused for this user (checked).
value:M25.better_measurement:
1. Drop perf, which is blocked here. Timestamp spike's stderr lines to the millisecond with a pipe reader: Rust's stderr is unbuffered, so each line's arrival time is exact. Use pass 2's interval as the decoding floor, since it reads the same window through the same noodles stack. Diagnostic rule, run before any fix: if the duplicate-scan interval is at least 3x pass 2's (now 2.38 / 0.34 = 7x), per-record work dominates and the fix goes ahead. If it is at most 1.5x, decoding dominates and the one-pass plan is back on the table. Apply the same rule to the LOH pileup (1.94 s against 0.34 s).
2. Make the fix the lean version, not the filter-only one. Read the lazy bam::Record, check its flags and the duplicate bit, look up the borrowed name, and build a small record (name, first, duplicate, qc_fail, five_prime from the lazy CIGAR) with no RecordBuf and no XA parse. For the LOH pileup, use a dense Vec<[u32;4]> over the window.
3. Pass rule for timing: run master and new alternately, 3 runs each (A/B/A/B), on 3 Mb DEL and DUP in clean mode at 1 and 4 threads. Use user CPU time and wall time, on a quiet machine or with repeats, since load was about 75 today. Each step must fall to at most 1.5x the pass-2 interval, and total user time must drop by at least 2.5 s at 1 thread on the 3 Mb DEL.
4. Pass rule for identity: R1, R2, truth.vcf, replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt md5-identical to master on those runs.
5. Gate breakers. The gate has to fail a broken version. Two mutants: one that skips duplicate-flagged records (it would lose the 8,873 duplicate pairs) and one that ignores qc_fail; both must break md5 identity. One overlapping two-event run tests the `seen` dedup across spans.
value:M25.notes:
The mechanism holds up. My millisecond re-run puts the duplicate scan at 7x pass 2 over the same window with the same reader. The code shows a full RecordBuf decode on every record, and one SipHash HashMap entry per aligned base in count_alleles_bam: about 45 million entries per Mb at 35x (inferred).

The value is small and lands where nobody is waiting:
- The gain is about 2 s for the duplicate scan plus about 1.5 s for the pileup per Mb at 1 thread, and about half that at the default 4 threads (inferred). A 3 Mb DEL now takes 12.5 s at 4 threads.
- It does not change any output, so callers' calls are untouched.
- The hospital LDLR and raredisease demo uses SNVs, indels and exon-level events, where the duplicate scan costs under 0.1 s (README). The run time the user actually complains about is raredisease realignment, and merge.sh takes hours.
- Ranking: it comes after M24, since the startup quality sample, at 7-9.7 s, is the largest fixed cost per run, and after M22 and M23.

Weaken it to two parts:
- A one-line roadmap decision: do not build the pass-2 strips or the one-pass plan. This is free, since they were never on the owner's backlog.
- An optional cleanup of size S, rated after M22, M23 and M24, gated as described in better_measurement.

A cheaper, separate lever worth a quick A/B (unmeasured): turn on noodles' libdeflate feature, or a faster flate2 backend. Inflating is exact, so the output stays byte-identical by construction, and it would speed up every BAM pass and the quality sample's read.

Risk: a dense Vec for the pileup is no worse in memory than the HashMap on whole-genome data, but size it from the window, since LOH events can span a chromosome arm.

value:M26.already_done_or_refuted: Flagged twice before, never measured and never fixed. docs/review/REVIEW.md:2834 says "SharedReference::load doubles peak memory via the FIFO cache". docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:139 (architecture recommendation 5) says "peak RSS was not benchmarked here". The independent review's "fix 5" in memory is a different item (validate base depth), so this one is still open. Nothing refutes it. I have now measured it (see notes).
value:M26.corrected_claims:
1. The memory doubling at load is now MEASURED, no longer inferred. I ran target/release/spike (built 2026-10-06; src/reference.rs unchanged since 2026-09-25) on the 35x HG002 BAM with 23 SNVs (chr1-22 + chrX, --threads 1 --seed 1 --allow-resistant). Log: "Loaded 23 chromosome(s) ... (2890 MB)", which is 3,031,042,417 bp. /usr/bin/time gave MAXRSS_KB 6114252, about 2.02x the loaded sequence. Sampling RSS every 0.25 s showed it climbing to about 6.0 GB during the load. It then fell to 2.92 GB as soon as load returned and the ReferenceReader was dropped, and stayed at or below 3.0 GB for the rest of the run. Files: scratchpad m26/out2.log, m26/out2.rss, m26/events.txt, m26/run.sh.
2. Two of the cited numbers are the wrong evidence for the reference fix. The chrM run's 2.64 GB came from a 938,703-pair pool at about 29,000x (roadmap journal, M19); chrM is 16.6 kb, so the cache fix cannot change it. In the 1 Mb chr20 DUP run (704 MB), chr20 is 64 MB and memory peaks later, during the simulation step, so the cache fix leaves that peak unchanged (inferred).
3. "One-line bypass" is right, but there is an even simpler version: the cache never gets a hit in production. ReferenceReader is used only by fetch_window, which opens a fresh reader on every call (reference.rs:66-72), and by SharedReference::load, which fetches each chromosome once because chroms_needed is deduplicated through a HashSet (main.rs:633-648). Deleting the cache (reference.rs:79-81, 134-136, 144-147, 182-189) therefore cannot change any output.
4. The optional streaming part conflicts with the idea's own md5 pass rule. combine_event_outputs (simulate.rs:410-427) interleaves each event's kept and chimeric pairs, filters them against the suppressed names of all events, then runs dedup_by_name. Under origin, draw_origin_removals (main.rs:876) rewrites kept_originals after every event has finished (R5). Writing SPIKE_ pairs early would change the FASTQ order, and kept originals cannot be streamed at all.
value:M26.better_measurement:
Gate B has already been run and it passes: the cache is the cause, at 2.02x peak (6.11 GB vs 3.03 GB loaded), with the excess entirely in the load phase (RSS timeline in m26/out2.rss). The remaining gate, for the simplest version only (delete the cache):
(a) Rebuild from master, which adds the v2 startup quality sample and so raises the plateau after the load. Run the same 23-SNV list (scratchpad m26/events.txt; the chr7, chr16 and chr22 positions were replaced because the originals had about 0 reads at MAPQ 20) three times each with old and new builds, interleaved.
(b) Pass if the new MAXRSS divided by the loaded bytes is at most 1.25, against 2.02 measured on the 2026-10-06 build, and the new RSS timeline has no load-phase spike above its post-load plateau plus the largest chromosome (about 250 MB). A build that still caches (for example max_cache_entries left in place) fails (b).
(c) All output files are md5-identical on the 23-SNV panel and on README's 3 Mb del/dup at --threads 1 and 4. A build that loses or truncates the sequence fails here or at fetch.
The pool-clone change needs its own gate, because the 23-SNV panel has pools of only about 2.5k pairs and cannot test it. Measure MAXRSS on the 3 Mb clean DUP and on the chrM 3243 run. Keep the change only if MAXRSS falls by at least 10% with md5-identical outputs. My inferred saving is about 10% at 3 Mb and about 25% on chrM, so it is likely marginal. Drop streaming entirely.
value:M26.notes:
The gap is real and now measured, but the value is low. Peak memory matters only for runs that span many chromosomes. Measured: 23 chromosomes peak at 6.1 GB, against 3.0 GB for the rest of the run. Expected after the fix: about 3.1-3.3 GB (inferred).

None of the following is affected: a caller's calls, the truth VCF, or the reads. Peak memory also does not block the hospital demo. A typical FH panel (LDLR chr19, APOB chr2, PCSK9/LDLRAP1 chr1) loads about 550 MB, so its load peak is about 1.1-1.4 GB (inferred). That is below the peaks of 1.2-2.5 GB documented in README.md:1352-1361 for 3 Mb events, which come from pools and tiling, not from the reference. Any machine that runs nf-core/raredisease has far more than 6 GB. This build machine has 376 GB.

A small possible speed gain: the load phase took about 9 s of 21 s wall time, with 7.8 s of system time spent faulting in about 6 GB. Dropping the clone may save a few seconds per run that spans many chromosomes (inferred, not measured).

What to keep: the simplest version, deleting the ReferenceReader cache outright. It never gets a hit in production, so this removes dead code, cannot change outputs by construction, and halves peak memory for panels covering many chromosomes. Cost: tiny.

What to drop: the pool-clone change, unless the separate 3 Mb/chrM gate shows a saving of at least 10%. Inferred: about 66.6k kept pairs at roughly 1 KB each is about 65 MB of the 704 MB in the 1 Mb DUP run, about 9%. Also drop the "stream SPIKE_ pairs per event" part, which contradicts the idea's own md5 rule (see corrected claims). The "smaller machines" impact is speculative: no user has reported a memory limit.

Also not covered by the idea: for CRAM input, noodles fasta::Repository caches whole chromosomes for each repository instance (extract.rs:20, carried.rs:162, origin.rs:690). This could be a larger copy of the reference for HG001-style CRAM runs and was not measured here.

value:M27.corrected_claims:
Claims I confirmed by reading the code or the run outputs:
- One StdRng is used for the whole run (main.rs:614).
- It is passed through build_haplotype, the simulate_event calls and draw_origin_removals (main.rs:795, 808, 821, 871).
- A suppression draw is made only for replaceable pairs (simulate.rs:259).
- The read prefix comes from the event index (simulate.rs:174), and so do the truth IDs (truth.rs:267, 334, 361, 402, 430).
- Events are concatenated in input order and never sorted (main.rs:617-626).
- R39 (measured, scratchpad ord/): SIM_ALT_FRAGS 22 vs 19; B suppressed 292 vs 278. B's pool is the same in both runs (2885+292 = 2899+278), so in clean mode the RNG is the only coupling here.

Claims that need correcting:
(1) "transplant.py's retries re-draw accepted events" has no consequence. A refused run bails before writing anything (main.rs:785-789, 862-864), and transplant.py deletes the directory before each attempt (rm -rf at :247-248). Only the final accepted attempt's reads exist.
(2) "B1/B2 arms stop re-drawing" is wrong under the proposal's own key. B1 changes af and B2 shifts the coordinates (transplant.py event_spec), so each arm already gets a different key and a different stream.
(3) "K7-style gates stop failing on stream reordering" is already solved by v2's master seed-spread allowance (documented, v2 plan :244-246). Also, stage 1 alone does not keep an event's placement fixed when the quality model changes. Fragment placement and synthesis draws are interleaved in one stream (simulate.rs:1018-1086, synth.rs:371-389). Only the suppression draws, which come first, would stay fixed.
(4) The bccc43a cause, "flips from the reordered random stream", is the author's inference, not a measurement. Later, master run at 5 seeds flipped 0 of the 115 round-trip rows' pass/fail (documented, v2 plan :345). So 2 flips from stream noise alone is less likely than the idea implies, and it is weak evidence here.
(5) Per-event streams do not remove the fastq.sh + raredisease rerun after a panel change. Adding an event changes the FASTQ either way. Only the re-checking of variants already confirmed is saved.
value:M27.better_measurement:
Value check first (cheap, master only, no build):
- Run a hospital-like panel of about 8 LDLR/clinical SNVs, indels and exon DELs at af 0.5 at seeds 42, 2 and 3. A new seed reshuffles the stream the same way a panel edit does.
- Count events whose SIM_ALT_FRAGS or `spike validate` verdict crosses a calling threshold.
- If 0 flip (master already shows 0 of 115 rows across 5 seeds), the gain is reproducibility only, and the idea belongs in low-priority UX work.

Invariance gate (keep (1) of the idea, widened):
- Panels: {B}, {A,B}, {B,A} and {A,B,C}.
- A must lie within the 10 kb default flank (main.rs:140), so the two events' extraction pools overlap and combine_event_outputs and the joint duplicate scan are exercised.
- Cover every place that draws a random number: SNV (suppression and tiling), INS (random inserted bases, main.rs:2022), full DUP, junction DUP (depth copies, simulate.rs:344-351), and an event with phased copies (sample_copies_for_event).
- Pass: B's SPIKE reads (sequence + quality, names stripped), its suppressed names and its truth INFO are byte-identical across all panels.
- Master must fail this gate. A version seeded by event index must also fail it on {A,B}.
- Run origin mode separately and report it. Its joint draw is meant to couple events, so test whether the proposed (seed, family) stream is stable when the events' sites share no families.

Equivalence:
- Drop the KS p>0.05 test over 20 seeds. It has little power, and a pass is only absence of evidence, so most broken derivations would pass it.
- Use v2's K7 rule instead: an allowance from master at seeds 42, 2, 3, 4 and 5 on the 4 round-trip sets.
- Add unit tests that the derived seed changes with --seed and with every key field, and does not change with the event index or the input order.

Speed (stage 2):
- Do not use "beats 26.5 s". Use the means of 3 interleaved rounds against master, with a margin of at least 15%, because master alone varies about 7% (threads-step1.md).
- Pursue stage 2 only if a user needs multi-Mb events to run faster.
value:M27.notes:
Value is low: it does not change any caller's expected results or how real the reads look.
- It only fixes which random realisation each event gets as the panel changes. Every realisation is a valid draw.
- For the hospital demo (mostly af 0.5 germline variants), the measured seed-to-seed spread suggests calls rarely flip. The 19 vs 22 ALT fragments of R39 are called either way at 35x (inferred).
- The real benefit is user experience: an LDLR call does not vanish because a DMD event was added. That is worth having, but it is not an outcome problem.

Runtime is not blocking:
- 26.5 s for a 3 Mb DUP at 16 threads (documented, README:1359) is small next to fastq.sh plus a raredisease run, which takes hours.
- Hospital events are kb-scale.
- Drop stage 2 from this idea.

Cost: the full proposal (stable hash names and IDs, validate's prefix mapping, stage 2) is honestly M to L.
- Stable names and IDs give no caller-relevant gain. Read names only feed Picard's optical-duplicate tile/x/y.
- They do touch validate.rs:384-390, the scripts and the docs. Drop them.

Simplest version worth keeping (cost about 2):
- Seed each event's StdRng from splitmix64(seed, FNV-1a(canonical spec)). FNV-1a and splitmix64 are already used for read names, per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-read-names.md:56.
- Better still, give each event three sub-streams: suppression, placement and synthesis. A quality-model change then moves only the synthesis draws, which pairs future quality-model gates with master, the active development area.
- Origin keeps its single draw on a (seed, "origin") stream. Names and IDs stay as they are. The events' internal order stays serial.

Hidden costs:
- Every output changes once. The 15 identity baselines and every seed-specific number in the README, the case file and the deck must be re-cut or marked as from before the change.
- Needs the owner's explicit consent.

Gate B: one half is already answered by the R39 logs (pool identical, so the RNG is the only coupling in clean mode for this pair). The RF8 retry count is moot, because refused runs write no output.

value:M28.corrected_claims:
1. "3 INS in LDLR": only 1 can be planted. Measured with bcftools on clinvar.vcf.gz: 2004497 and 1069978 carry N runs. is_dna_allele (vcf_input.rs:901) rejects any N, so both are skipped and counted today, not planted wrongly. Only 1074682 (327 bp) can be planted. Genome-wide, 353 of 448 Insertions and 107 of 305 Microsatellites carry N.
2. "2 Indel": neither is a DUP. 3767245 is C>8,118 bp with no shared anchor (ALT starts with T) and no CLNHGVS, and it matches no nearby reference copy (best fit has 1,602 mismatches). 430754 is a 63>1 delinsA.
3. "Deletions come out physically right": close but not exact. Measured from the scratchpad cv/ runs: the VCF-route R1 has 15,044 lines and the del: spec has 15,048, so they differ by one read. The md5 values are confirmed on decompressed FASTQ: 54443603 vs 26ccc768, and dupspec equals dupsvt at 5bfadff3. For DELs, the change is about labels and which check runs, not reads.
4. The labelling harm is bigger than stated. spike validate treats any truth record with no SVTYPE as "SNP" (validate.rs:1069-1079), so del_planted never runs on a ClinVar-route DEL.
5. "exon.rs unchanged since 0a00caf" is out of date. exon.rs has since gained a test (1103835), and main.rs and simulate.rs changed with quality v2. The 2026-10-06 release binary predates v2, so its md5 values only compare runs of that binary. Gates must be re-run on a master build.
6. The shape-based DUP detection adds nothing for ClinVar. Measured over all 3,996 genome-wide P/LP records of 50 bp or more: 2602 of 2602 Deletions are pure deletions with a one-base anchor, and 283 of 285 Duplications are exact copies of the adjacent reference (2 complex). CLNVC alone gives the same labels, and a shape check needs the reference.
7. "Microsatellite should become INS with sequence" is a realism trap. Of the 198 that can be planted, 168 are DMPK expansions and 150 are 151 bp or longer. The tiling never places a fragment wholly inside new sequence (simulate.rs ~1004-1060, CR5), so no read would lie wholly inside the repeat. ExpansionHunter in raredisease looks for exactly those reads (documented in nf-core/raredisease docs, not checked here). These records should be refused and counted until M18.
8. Routing silently drops the REF check that protects against the wrong genome build. Only SmallVariant gets validate_ref_allele (main.rs:1634-1643); the DEL, DUP and INS paths check ranges only. Add the proposed '19'→chr19 alias, and a GRCh37 ClinVar file (also named '19') would plant routed DEL/DUP records at the wrong place with no error.
9. Gate (b) is not cost S. One whole-BAM align+merge takes about 1 h 42 min (documented in the sv-caller-slices memory), so 39 records is about 66 h.
value:M28.better_measurement:
Use a master build throughout.
(1) Routing census, which takes seconds: give the ingest all 3,996 genome-wide P/LP ClinVar records of 50 bp or more. It passes only if the counts per (CLNVC, shape) match these, measured by me:
- 2602 Deletion → DEL
- 283 exact-copy Duplication → DUP
- 95 pure-novel Insertion → INS
- 2 complex Duplications, 351 complex Indels, 465 records with N, and the 198 Microsatellites that can be planted → counted refusals
(2) Byte identity on 35x HG002, against the matching del:/dup:/ins: coordinate spec: R1/R2 md5 must match for 251409 and 4845403 (DEL), 251140 and 976329 (DUP of 1 kb or more), 403639 (96 bp DUP) and 1074682 (327 bp INS). Today all of these fail.
(3) Records under 50 bp: in a sample of 500, R1/R2 must be md5-identical to master. truth.vcf may differ only by the added SIM_SRC_ID, SIM_GENE and SIM_HGVS keys.
(4) Negative controls that a version without the REF check would fail:
- 251140 shifted by 1 kb, or the GRCh37 ClinVar record, after aliasing → refused
- 251140 with one base of the copy mutated and CLNVC=Duplication → refused, not planted as a DUP
- a FASTA holding both 19 and chr19 → alias refused
- `dup:chr19:11104769-11104770` → warns
(5) Replace gate (b). Run spike validate with the new truth on the existing merged B2/B3 BAMs in ~/sv_slice_test/data. The reads are byte-identical, so no new merge is needed. Pass if del_planted and coverage_ratio rows appear where the SNP row was. Do not use |ratio-1.5|<0.3 on a 96 bp DUP: that is ill-posed, and it re-tests the DUP model rather than the routing.
value:M28.notes:
The gap is verified in code and in the scratchpad runs:
- ClinVar has no SVTYPE header at all.
- 251140 by VCF gives 313 synthetic pairs and SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 (shown in dupvcf.log), against 1,540 pairs and DEPTH_FOLD 1.51 from the coordinate spec.
- rf8/e8 truth has SVTYPE=DUP;END=11104770;SVLEN=1 with no warning.
- The cause of SIM_ALT_FRAGS=0 is the small-variant evidence span (Evidence::Bases): no read covers an 8 kb ALT. For a DUP inserted as a small variant, the copy is new sequence, so CR5 places no fragment inside it.

Why weaken rather than keep:
- The fix matters for caller outcomes only for DUPs longer than a fragment. Genome-wide that is 103 of 285 P/LP DUPs (151 bp or more, measured); in LDLR it is 2 (8.1 kb and 6.5 kb).
- For DELs, only the labels change, plus the validate SNP-vs-DEL routing.
- The owner's real LDLR loop already uses correct coordinate specs. The value lies in the hospital "many genes, by ClinVar ID" convenience and in closing a silent trap.

Build this, which is S:
- When there is no SVTYPE and the length difference is 50 bp or more, map CLNVC Deletion/Duplication/Insertion to DEL/DUP/INS.
- Refuse and count Microsatellite, Indel and complex records, naming the reason. Do not route Microsatellites to INS.
- Keep the REF check for routed records: check the REF allele, and for a DUP check the copy against the FASTA in main.rs, where the reference is already loaded. This also verifies DUPs by shape at no extra cost.
- Carry SIM_SRC_ID, plus SIM_GENE from GENEINFO and SIM_HGVS from CLNHGVS, on all VCF records.
- Warn on coordinate-spec DEL/DUP/INV shorter than 50 bp. This catches a real translation error: cnv_validation's BED stores the 4 LDLR DUPs as 1 bp intervals.

Drop or defer:
- shape detection without CLNVC
- --vcf-ids (`bcftools view -i 'ID=...'` already does it)
- HGVS specs

Make the contig alias optional, and add it only together with the REF check. The current error names the contig, and `bcftools annotate --rename-chrs` is a one-liner.

Measured here: counts from bcftools/python on /home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/resources/clinical/clinvar.vcf.gz plus samtools faidx on the GRCh38 no-alt FASTA. The 39 LDLR records are in scratchpad skeptic_ldlr39.txt and the genome-wide set in skeptic_gw.tsv. Inferred: caller outcomes, and the ExpansionHunter effect.

value:M29.better_measurement:
The exon-1 check (all 8 initiator records inside, the old BED holding 0) is well-posed and has effectively been run already (C3, the ATG check). The exon4-exon8 byte-identity check is only a no-regression check. The DMD check tests a reader that the simplest version does not need. A better check targets the README recipe genome-wide, with rules a broken recipe fails:
(a) Exon numbers run in strand order with no gaps for every MANE Select gene. Measured: 9,660 plus-strand and 9,402 minus-strand genes, 0 out of order, 0 gaps, 0 duplicate exon names. A recipe that numbers by position fails on all 9,402 minus-strand genes.
(b) For every gene, the exon holding the CDS start (from the GFF's own CDS features) is the lowest-numbered coding exon. For each ClinVar initiator_codon_variant, it must lie in that exon. Spot checks: LDLR has 8 of 8 in exon 1. DMD's ATG (CDS end 33211312, minus strand) and ClinVar X:33211312 initiator_codon fall inside the derived DMD_exon1 (33211281-33211549).
(c) One spike run with --exon-bed set to the genome-wide file and del:DMD:exon45-exon50. truth.vcf POS/END must equal the outer edges of exons 45 and 50 and SIM_EXONS must list 45-50. This checks that spike reads the 6-column, 19,062-gene file without refusing it.
(d) For the VCF relabel, check that no record ID claims a population or ClinVar origin unless its POS/END matches a ClinVar record exactly.
value:M29.notes:
Verdict: weaken to the SIMPLEST version and drop the built-in GFF reader for now.

**Value (1).**
- The outcome that mattered, LDLR exon-level events landing ~1 kb into intron 1, is already fixed locally (ba9f4e7). What is left for that is a push, which is the user's call.
- Without a reader, MANE already serves any gene. This one awk command, run read-only in the scratchpad, gives a spike-compatible BED for 19,062 genes. Its LDLR rows match the bundled BED exactly, and minus-strand numbering is correct:
  `zcat MANE.GRCh38.v1.0.refseq_genomic.gff.gz | awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' '$3=="exon" && $9~/tag=MANE Select/ {match($9,/gene=[^;]+/); g=substr($9,RSTART+5,RLENGTH-5); match($9,/ID=exon-[^;]+/); n=substr($9,RSTART,RLENGTH); sub(/.*-/,"",n); print $1,$4-1,$5,g"_exon"n,g,$7}'`
  Output: /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/m29v/mane_select_exons.bed.
- The README's exon-BED section never says where to get such a file. That doc gap is real, and the recipe closes it.
- A built-in --exon-gff adds GTF and transcript choice but no correctness over the recipe. It is speculative value at M cost.
- Exon specs are also not the realism-preferred route for the hospital demo. Their breakpoints sit exactly on exon edges: 0 of 36 LDLR exon edges are in an Alu, against 15 of 39 ClinVar LDLR SVs with at least one Alu end (hospital-demo-plan memory). The owner's own LDLR SV testing uses exact ClinVar coordinates (sv-caller-slices memory). So M28 (ClinVar ingest) is the bigger lever. The README should call exon specs idealized breakpoints.

**Keep, as cheap fixes.**
- Relabel or remove ldlr_known_deletions_hg38.vcf. Nothing in code, README or pipeline references it; it only misleads public users with '_ClinVar', '_Danish' and similar names on round-number breakpoints.
- Cap the 'Available:' list at about 10 near matches. With a genome-wide MANE BED, a typo would print 19k names: loud, not blocking.
- The README gVCF example del:chr19:11090000-11133000 misses MANE exon 1 (minor, already noted by the reviewer).

**Don't.**
- Ship hospital or Scout-derived files.
- Add Scout BED support (it holds coding exons only and merges transcripts).

Value 2 because the high-value part is done. Cost 1 for the recipe, the VCF relabel and the error cap.

value:M3.already_done_or_refuted: Partly done, not refuted. The v2 gate learned slips (12-14 runs at 1.0% for A, 1.6% for T) and dropped them because they added only 0.04 points to bad-end clip share (documented: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md:84,105,167; memory quality-model-run.md:88-89). Nobody has measured their effect on indel calling. New evidence from this check counts against the proposed SHAPE. I measured that slips belong to the fragment, not to the read: wherever both overlapping mates pass a run, the two mates either show the same length change or neither does. So the per-read model the proposal describes (sequencing orientation, keyed by mate, drawn in ReadState) is the wrong mechanism.
value:M3.corrected_claims: 1) "35x 15+ = 2.2% (15/680)" is inflated by a sample variant the Q100 ±5 bp mask missed. At chr17:36270887 (A×18), 5 of 12 reads in the 35x and 9 of 21 in the hospital BAM carry a -2. In the hospital BAM, chr17:36241007 (A×17) also shows +1 in 12 of 31 reads. Both sit in the chr17:36.24-36.29 Mb segdup-rich block. With that block left out, per-pass rates are as follows (measured, scratchpad slipval/slipmate.py on slipval/blocks_no17.tsv). 35x: 8-9 0.23% (12/5113), 10-11 0.72% (10/1394), 12-14 0.72% (7/974), 15+ 0.95% (6/632). Hospital: 0.32% (28/8821), 1.84% (46/2498), 2.51% (40/1592), 5.26% (55/1045). So the gap between libraries is about 2.5-3.5x at 10-14 and about 5.5x at 15+, not "2-3x". The 35x process rate at 15+ is about 1%, not 2.2%. 2) "per read pass ... sequencing orientation ... keyed by mate" is the wrong shape. Measured on overlapping pairs where both mates fully span a run of 8 or more, outside chr17: hospital had 3 pairs with both mates slipped (same change every time) and 0 pairs with one mate slipped. Read-independent slips at the measured rates would give about 12.6 one-mate pairs. The 35x had 1 both-slipped pair and 0 one-mate pairs, against about 3.2 expected. With chr17 kept, the hospital had 7 of 7 concordant pairs and 0 discordant. So a slip is a length change in the molecule (inferred: library PCR stutter, consistent with the library dependence), shared by both mates. 3) The IMPACT claims "many clinical frameshifts sit in homopolymers" and "ExpansionHunter/stranger" do not hold for runs of 10 or more. PanelApp green exons (10.0 Mb) hold only 29 runs of 10 or more (2.9/Mb), against 372/Mb in the 20 sample blocks, about 125x fewer. They hold 330 runs of 8-9, where real slip rates are 0.23-0.32% per pass, about 0.1 read at 30x. LDLR's 5,357 exon bp hold 1 run of 8-9 and 1 run of 12-14 (measured, slipval/exonruns.py). ExpansionHunter's catalog is mostly tri- and pentanucleotide loci, not homopolymers, and is unaffected unless a footprint covers one (inferred). 4) "Not dependent on run length" for --indel-error-rate is only partly right. p_err comes from the v2 error table, which includes the read's largest run bin so far (quality.rs ReadState.run; README:1945). Indel errors do rise after long runs, but they land anywhere downstream with a uniform random base, not at the run as a ±1 change (synth.rs:210-226). The claim that the 15+/4-5 ratio collapses at --indel-error-rate 0.05 is inferred, not measured. 5) The code citations check out: main.rs:178-182, synth.rs:210-226, quality.rs:208-211. The slip mix is about 96% ±1. Hospital runs of 12 or more lean to insertions (66 ins vs 30 del); in the 35x it is 8 vs 5 (slipval/signs.py).
value:M3.better_measurement: STEP 0, value probe before any spike code, all on real reads. Pick Q100 1-bp indels in runs of 10 or more inside the benchmark BED, outside segdups and the 7 SeraCare genes ±2 kb, in the hospital HG002 30x BAM. Pick an equal number of runs of 10 or more with no Q100 record. Arm A is the real reads. Arm B is the same reads with every stutter fragment removed: fragments whose run length matches neither Q100 allele, both mates dropped. Arm C removes the same number of random fragments, to control for depth; use 5 draws. Run the raredisease DeepVariant on each arm. Value exists only if B differs from the spread of C in genotype, FILTER or GQ bin at 5% or more of the sites. If not, missing stutter cannot change germline calls, so do not build it for the hospital demo. Repeat once for the low-AF case: plant -1 deletions at 5% and 10% AF at runs of 12 or more, and compare caller TP/FP with stutter present (real flank reads) against stutter removed. STEP 1, if building: model a per-FRAGMENT ±1 edit of the template at each run, drawn once per fragment and read by both mates, not a per-read ReadState draw. Learn from the startup blocks with a mask that looks at direction: exclude a run when one signed change is 30% or more of its passes. The proposed rule of 10% or more of reads would delete the stutter-heavy hospital runs (6/24, 5/21, 4/29, mixed ±1) and bias the rate low. For thin PCR-free libraries, fit log p = a + b·L over runs of 8 or more instead of 10 cells. STEP 2, falsifier: judge the hospital blocks without the chr17 block, plus more blocks for the 35x. Pooled 10-14 and 15+ rates must fall inside the real Poisson 95% CI; "within 2x" on 6-15 events is not usable (the CI for 6 events is 0.37-2.2x). The ins share must be within ±0.15. Add a mate-concordance test: among overlapping pairs over a slipping run, one-mate pairs must stay at 20% or less (real: 0 of 4). A per-read mutant must fail this test (expected about 2pn one-mate pairs), and master and today's --indel-error-rate 0.05 must fail the rate test. Leave the 4-7 bins out of the pass rule; the 35x has 15 and 8 events there. Drop the proposed DeepVariant background check in its current form. It does not separate master from a fix, because 2-5% stutter makes no calls. It is also confounded by CR3: the sample's own indels at those runs are erased to reference on the event copy whatever the slip model does.

(3) The previous gate measured only +0.04 points of clip share (documented). (4) A bigger homopolymer realism gap sits in the same footprints and changes calls: CR3. Use hom-alt sites too: the gate counts one as discordant when 15% or more of its reads carry REF.

Lock everything before code, using gate B (bcftools mpileup -R, under 1 h): the minimum number of sites (e.g. 50), the cut, and a hard-refuse floor (e.g. pooled share below 0.5).

- (2) HG002 35x with HG001's VCF stays at 0.5 or less. Benchmark overlap predicts about 0.33 (inferred).

value:M30.notes:
The gap is real and silent: exit 0, 0 WARN. It only bites when a user hands spike the wrong person's VCF, and nothing shows that has happened. The hospital VCFs are single-sample, and their names match their BAM's SM (measured). So the value is guarding against user error, not fixing outcomes in correct runs.

That error is plausible here. The hospital directory raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample holds both an NA12878 case and a GM24385 (HG002) case, under unrelated sample IDs (measured). The HG001 and HG002 truth VCFs sit side by side in data/giab_hg38. When the error happens the harm is measured and local: a hom-alt site goes het on spike's reads and depth rises about 1.6x. For the LDLR window tested, the harm was zero.

Recommended, simpler build at about S:
- (1) Read the #CHROM header and pick the column whose name equals the BAM's SM. A multi-sample VCF with no match is refused and the message names --gvcf-sample. This also fixes the comment that lies about the column.
- (2) A single sample under another name gives a WARN, never a refusal. GIAB names (HG001/HG002) never match lab SMs (NA12878, D24-...), so a refusal would fire on the README's recommended use.
- (3) Log a run-wide concordance share at startup. Refuse only below a very safe floor, such as a pooled share under 0.5 over 50 or more sites (expected about 0.33 wrong vs about 0.97 right, inferred), with an override.

Drop the per-footprint refusal. It is noisy at about 3 sites a footprint. It would say "this VCF does not describe this BAM" for one event and not the next, with the same file. It also passes footprints like LDLR, where the wrong file happens to agree, while leaving the run's other events unguarded.

The case that "M11/M16 need it" is speculative until those ideas are built. The S cost is honest for the name and column part; the pooled gate is S-M because it hooks into the startup sample. Gate B (bcftools mpileup at about 100 footprints' sites) is cheap, well-posed and should run first. It also settles whether DeepVariant 30x calls on the right sample really clear 0.95.

value:M33.corrected_claims:
1) The detector cannot run "on the quality sample" as written. That sample is extracted with the donor filter, which drops records with the duplicate flag before pairs are built (extract.rs:876/934; README: "Pairs are extracted as donor pools are (--min-mapq, proper pairs, no duplicates)"). So the sample always holds 0 duplicates, and a zero-flag rule computed on it would fire on every input. The flagged records have to be counted while they are skipped, or in a separate count over the same blocks.

2) The predicted bias of +0.035 (VAF 0.535) is an upper bound, not a prediction. It assumes whole duplicate families are removed together. For pairs whose copy is unknown, `copy_rate(None, v) = v` (synth.rs:694-700) removes each family member independently, so a family survives unless every member is removed.

   Measured (scratchpad m33/fam.py) on the marked 35x BAM, data/validation/hg002_novaseq_chr20.bam, chr20:10-10.5 Mb, proper pairs, MAPQ 20 or more:
   - 73,839 pairs fall into 64,870 families keyed by both 5' ends, so 12.15% are duplicates. This matches the duplicate flags exactly (8,969 = 8,969).
   - Family sizes: 1: 56,740; 2: 7,359; 3: 706; 4: 62; 5: 3.

   At v=0.5 the VAF after re-marking is 0.516 if every pair's copy is unknown and 0.532 if every copy is known (inferred from those families). At typical shares of known-copy pairs the shift is about +0.02 (inferred), not +0.03.

3) There are three unmarked BAMs in the data directory, not one:
   - HG002.GRCh38.chr20.bam (novoalign 2x250): 0 of 141,004 primary records flagged in chr20:10-10.5 Mb, no markdup @PG.
   - HG002.GRCh38.chr20.bwamem2.bam: 0 of 140,758 flagged.
   - Both have only 2.8% 5'-end families (measured), so the bias there is at most +0.007 at v=0.5 (inferred). A yes/no "unmarked" warning would fire where the harm is negligible.

4) The hospital BAM is marked (3.76%, markdup @PG), so the LDLR/raredisease demo is not affected.

5) "A few hours of compute" is too high: spike takes about 0.6 s per small event (README run-time table), and re-marking a chr20 slice takes minutes.

Verified as stated: strobealign BAM @PG holds only strobealign plus samtools sort/view, with no @RG; 0 of 149,768 records flagged vs 18,067 of 149,273 (12.10%) on the 35x BAM; the log lines at main.rs:563 and :925 exist.
value:M33.better_measurement:
Use a paired design that changes one thing only.
- Input: a chr20 slice of the marked 35x BAM.
- Unmarked twin: the same slice run through `samtools view --remove-flags 1024`, then reheadered without the markdup @PG.
- Same events and same --seed in both arms.

Comparing the strobealign BAM with the bwa BAM mixes duplicate marking with aligner, MAPQ, pool membership and SIM_RESIST.

A) Mechanism check, no caller noise.
- Per event, take the ratio of planted synthetic fragments (unmarked arm over marked arm).
- Prediction, locked beforehand: the 5'-end family ratio N/U of the pool's own window, about 1.12-1.14 (fam.py on the window).
- Pass: the ratio is within ±0.03 of that prediction.
- Kill: the ratio is below 1.03.

B) Outcome check.
- Run merge.sh, then `samtools fixmate -m` + `markdup` (or Picard, as raredisease runs it) on both merged BAMs.
- Plant 300-500 het SNVs; pool alt/(alt+ref) per arm.
- Lock the prediction as the range 0.516-0.532, narrowed using the run's own share of known-copy pairs (read_copy).
- Harm real: the difference is ≥ +0.012 with a 95% CI that excludes 0.
- Harm dead: the CI's upper end is below +0.008.
- Why not the proposed rule: with 100 sites at about 30x unique depth, the SE of the difference is about 0.012 (inferred), so a true +0.02 lands in neither the pass nor the kill zone.

C) The outcome callers could actually see.
- Plant hom DEL and het DUP events in both arms.
- After re-marking, compare depth across each event and its flanks against background.
- Predicted: about 1.14x footprint depth at v=1, and a het DUP copy ratio of about 1.64-1.67 against 1.5 (inferred).
- Run raredisease's CNV caller (gCNV or CNVnator) on the slice to see whether any copy-number call changes.

D) Detector check.
- It must fire on the stripped twin and on the strobealign BAM.
- It must stay quiet on the original 35x BAM, the hospital BAM, NA18488, the HG001 CRAM and CHM13.
- On the two 2.8% unmarked GIAB BAMs it should report the low family share rather than raise an alarm.
value:M33.notes:
Worth doing only as the cheapest version: a warning that reports a measured share. The harm claim, the predicted size and the falsifying test all need repair.

Value is low:
- The owner's end goal is not touched, because the hospital BAM is marked.
- A het VAF of about 0.52 instead of 0.50 changes no germline genotype call. Binomial noise at 35x is about 0.085 per site (inferred).
- The bias that might matter is relative: about +12% at low AF (v=0.05 becomes about 0.056, inferred from the measured families) and in depth (about +14% over the footprint at v=1; het DUP ratio about 1.65 instead of 1.5). These hit LoD curves and CNV ratios, not het SNVs.
- No doc, script or memory note uses the strobealign BAM as spike input. The novoalign BAM was used for quality-model K6, which is not a VAF measurement.

Simpler and better than the proposal:
1. Count records skipped for the duplicate flag during the startup sample's extraction. Reuse `header_marks_duplicates` (move it to a shared module).
2. If no record carries the flag (and at least 1,000 records were seen) and no @PG names a marker, print one warning. It should give the pool's 5'-end family share (`origin::duplicates_of` already has the key) and the upper bound v/(v+(1-v)(1-d)), worded as "up to", plus the fix: "run samtools markdup first".
3. Do not refuse. Do not add `--unmarked-ok`.

Reporting the share matters because unmarked BAMs here range from 2.8% (harmless) to 12-13% (the NovaSeq strobealign BAM).

Detector caveats:
- biobambam `bamsormadup` and fgbio consensus BAMs are not in `names_a_duplicate_marker`. Consensus BAMs hold no duplicates, so they would trigger the warning wrongly (harmless as a warning).
- A BAM with a markdup @PG whose flags were later stripped stays silent. This is the L15 test's own `unmarked.bam` case.

An alternative that fixes the cause: when the input is unmarked, collapse 5'-end families in the pool's coverage and removal. That is M-sized and wrong for users whose downstream never re-marks, so the warning is the right default.

Cost is honest at S (code plus a test). The repaired measurement takes about 1-2 hours, mostly setup; compute is minutes.

value:M34.already_done_or_refuted: Partly done already. The contig-end half is already handled. Haplotypes are clamped to the contig: the end-of-chromosome tests in haplotype.rs (lines 1413-1500) assert total_len and ref_range stop at the contig end. Tiling draws starts only in [0, hap_len - frag_len] (simulate.rs:1029). So a tiled read never runs past a contig end. The synth.rs:1561 test is on generate_read, the reference-coordinate path, with an overhang of at most INDEL_SLACK (10 bp). Zero coverage already makes compute_tiling_count return 0 (simulate.rs:764). Inferred from that: events on the chrY PAR, which the analysis set hard-masks as N, already plant nothing. Nothing about N placement has been refuted, and no case-file entry covers it.
value:M34.corrected_claims:
1) 'count and depth are scaled as if those starts were real': the depth part is wrong. n = coverage*vaf*effective_len/mean_frag with starts drawn uniformly (simulate.rs:801-816), so depth over non-N sequence is already coverage*vaf. The all-N fragments are extra junk reads. They do not thin or thicken real depth (inferred from code). The count is inflated, the depth is not.
2) 'past contig ends': does not happen in haplotype tiling (see above). GRCh38 contig ends are N runs anyway, e.g. chr20:0-60000 from the bwa .amb.
3) MEASURED, the 'exclude starts whose FRAGMENT overlaps N' rule is unrealistic. The real HG002 chr20 BAM has 51 proper pairs at MAPQ >= 20 whose fragment spans the 100 bp N gap chr20:66235-66335 with both reads outside it (samtools view -q20 -f2 -F0x900 data/validation/hg002_novaseq_chr20.bam chr20:65700-66235, $4+$9>66335). The fragment rule would drop such pairs. The rule has to look at the bases in each read, not the whole fragment.
4) The proposal leaves SIM_DEPTH_FOLD stale. The 76.88 fold is measured over donor depth in the N zone chr20:59000-60000 (log2.txt), and that is independent of tiling. After the fix it would describe fragments that no longer exist, unless the depth-fold zones also skip N.
5) Re-counted the stated evidence: 644 SPIKE reads, 123 all-N (62+61), 149 at least half N, SPIKE per-base N rate 0.23. Counted by zcat|awk on scratchpad/robust/ngap/out/R{1,2}.fq.gz.

(c) A unit fixture with a 100 bp N run inside the insert: pairs whose reads are both N-free are still drawn at master's rate. Real data has 51 such pairs at chr20:66235-66335.

**Gate B, measured now** (bwa .amb of the analysis-set FASTA turned into a BED of N runs; scripts in scratchpad/ngap_skeptic):
- GRCh38 has 800 N runs of at least 10 bp.
- LDLR's nearest N runs are chr19:0-60000 and chr19:24,448,980, millions of bases away.

**Hospital route, measured:** raredisease runs fastp without --n_base_limit, so the default of 5 applies. The fastp.json for D25-7403_Seq25-7598 shows the command with no override and too_many_N_reads 656,664 of 1,165,145,016. Any spike pair with more than 5 N in a read is dropped before bwa-mem2. **Simpler version (cost 1):** at the end of tile_haplotype_reads, after the loop, drop any pair where a read carries more than 5 N. Doing it after the loop matters: the junk pairs have already filled n_frags, so depth over real sequence stays right and the random-number stream is untouched. Haplotypes without N stay byte-identical. Also warn when a haplotype holds 10 bp or more of reference N, and fix SIM_DEPTH_FOLD's N zones. Do not drop whole fragments that overlap N.

VALUE: Neither half would change a caller's calls, the LDLR/raredisease demo, or runtime.

The audit has three problems:
- Three invariants hold by construction: fastq_removed = replaced \ written, kept originals are in consumed_original_names, and both mates come from one ReadPair.
- The fourth (uniqueness) is masked by dedup_by_name.
- It would have caught none of the real output-contract bugs in the project's history:
  - the duplicates leak: hom SNV old-allele 0.034 against 0.0017 (duplicates.md), names that never entered any set;
  - the fastq.sh input clobber and the mate-order pass (review findings 1 and 7);
  - origin conservation: removed 149, added 111.
- What the audit can catch is already caught downstream (fastq.sh ADDED/found checks, bwa on unequal mates) or costs one read pair of depth (a kept original wrongly in fastq_removed).

The refactor is real debt that the independent review names (docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:135), but it is smaller than proposed: EventStat already is the per-event struct. The four pushes are adjacent (main.rs:851-854), and the only `continue` (RF8) skips all of them together and then bails before the truth VCF is written.

Recommendation: do the S-sized EventStat consolidation only when M27 or another change touches the event loop. Swap the audit for the dedup-loss check (a) and the earlier fastq.sh pair check (b), both S.

A possibly more valuable gap to raise separately (inferred, not measured): SPIKE names are deterministic (fnv1a64 of `evNNNN_hap_NNNNNN`, read_name.rs:155-166). If spike is run again on an already-spiked BAM or FASTQ (spiking a second variant into the demo data), new reads can get the same full names as the first run's. Nothing in src refuses or warns on an input that holds SPIKE_ reads. A gate: spike twice into one sample and count the duplicate names in the merged BAM and FASTQ.

Six checks:

1. **Paste test.** Keep it, with two additions. First confirm the chosen site is not already carried, so the original run exits 0 rather than being refused (R47's carried check). Then paste the README block from a different working directory. Pass: truth.vcf (minus fileDate), R1 and R2 are md5-equal to the original run. Master must fail (seed 42, /tmp/spike).

Add a crash case: SIGKILL spike after R1.fq.gz is written. Pass: no truth.vcf exists, because truth.vcf is published last via temp file and rename.

3. **Compatibility gate.** This is the kill rule, actually run:
   - validate_pipeline.sh step 3 on a folder holding only R1, R2 and truth.vcf must re-run without --overwrite;
   - slice_loop.sh on 2 events must give the same spike.exit and validate results as master;
   - two default `-o /tmp/spike` runs in a row must both exit 0.

4. **Version stamp.** This must catch a naive build.rs:
   - Build at commit A, make an empty commit B, then `cargo build --release` with no source change. Pass: the README names B. A build.rs without rerun-if-changed on .git/HEAD and the branch ref keeps A.
   - An uncommitted edit gives `-dirty`.
   - A source copy without .git gives `unknown`.

5. **Cross-binary identity.** On the C2 cases, the md5 of truth.vcf with `^##spike_` lines stripped is equal between master and branch. If provenance lives only in the README, truth.vcf must be byte-equal unstripped.

6. **Exit codes, if kept.**
   - A refusal (carried SNV, RF8) exits a code that is neither 1 nor 2.
   - A missing --bam flag exits 2 (clap).
   - A nonexistent BAM path exits 1.
value:M36.notes:
**Worth.** This does not change any caller's calls on spiked or real variants, and it does not touch runtime. Its value is traceability and safety for the hospital route.
- Clinical validation documentation needs each demo dataset tied to a commit and the exact command. That need is inferred, but a hospital would plausibly require it.
- The hand-renaming of binaries shows the owner already needs it.
- The quoting bug is real and costs one line (map argv through the existing sh_word).
- The stale-output hazard is real in code (R47), but every harness in the repo already guards against it. The realistic victim is a hospital loop over genes that reuses -o with --into-fastq and ignores exit status. That loop would send the previous gene's whole-sample FASTQ through raredisease under the wrong label (inferred, not measured).
- The B1-style scenario, a stale sim.bam merged against new replaced_reads.txt, needs a user who skips align.sh, which the printed next steps tell them to run.

**Recommended scope** (the SIMPLEST version, refined):
a) build.rs with `git describe --dirty`, rerun-if-changed on .git/HEAD and the branch ref, falling back to "unknown". The README gets the commit, the command quoted through sh_word, and the parsed Args, which give the effective seed and every default. truth.vcf gets at most `##source=spike-<version>` and `##spike_seed`, or nothing if the owner wants the md5 checks left alone.
b) After the CLI checks, delete only spike's own names in -o: RUN_OUTPUT_FILES, the whole_sample_paths pair, and merged.bam(.bai). Write truth.vcf last via temp file and rename.

**Defer** these until a real loop shows it needs them: run.json with md5s, the run id and @CO line in sim.bam, refusals in merge.sh and fastq.sh, the input identity hash, and --overwrite.

**Exit codes.** A separate code for refusals is cheap and helps hospital loops tell RF8 refusals at LDLR's Alu breakpoints from crashes. It must not be 2.

**Harness issue outside spike.** validate_pipeline.sh step 3 skips on file presence alone (lines 750-756), and step 7 reuses an existing truth.vcf.gz (line 947). Both are harness-level staleness that no spike-side change fixes unless the harness also reads a run marker.

value:M37.better_measurement:
Put a sample-specific early check in fastq.sh's PAIR awk instead of the RUN:FLOWCELL check. spike passes N_est = (mapped+unmapped)/2 from the BAM index (hospital BAM: 741,918,622 records, so about 371 M, against 380 M raw pairs; measured with samtools idxstats). If no name from fastq_removed_reads.txt has been seen after M = ceil(ln(1e6) * N_est / k) records, where k = want, refuse with "this pair is not the sample the BAM came from". The idea rests on the removed names being spread evenly through a raw FASTQ, and that is measured. On the HG002 40x R1, the 72,263-name list from the 35x BAM (scratchpad m25prof) gave 381, 817 and 1,217 hits by records 2.57 M, 5.14 M and 7.73 M, which is linear and about 458 M pairs in all. Random subsets of about 300 names first hit at records 0.37 M, 2.2 M and 3.1 M (expected about 1.5 M). Subsets of about 30 hit at 0.64 M, 1.77 M and more than about 9 M (scratchpad m37v). Hospital removed lists hold k = 385 to 1,804 names (B1/B2/B3 and m20). So M is about 2.9 to 13.6 M records, roughly 15 to 80 s, against about 35 min now.
Locked tests:
(a) False accept, the case that matters. The hospital D24-14230 BAM with a stand-in FASTQ from D25-7403 (both measured as LH00352:45:227NC2LT1:2) must be refused in under 2 min. Master and the RUN:FLOWCELL version both run to END, so the proposed design fails this test, as a broken version should.
(b) False refusal on several flowcells. HG002.GRCh38.chr20.bam (10 flowcell:lane values over 5 flowcells, measured) with HG002.chr20_R1/R2 (first record D00360:94:H2YT5BCXX:2) must go through.
(c) The right pair must give output byte-identical to master on the F1 stand-in.
(d) A mutant that skips the deadline must fail (a).
Separately, the downsample (superset) trap should become its own idea. At END, compare the raw pair count with the BAM's primary pairs and refuse or warn above about 1.1x. The hospital ratio is 380 M raw / 369.3 M after fastp = 1.03 (measured from fastp.json). Region-subset BAMs, where most contigs have no reads, would be exempt.
value:M37.notes:
Measured from the user's local copy of the hospital data: both raredisease cohort samples at the hospital share one RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE. D24-14230_Seq25-7600 (sample sheet S17_L002) and D25-7403_Seq25-7598 (S18_L002) both read LH00352:45:227NC2LT1:2, from samtools view of their sorted_md BAMs over chr1:10.0-10.1 Mb, chr19 LDLR and other regions; every name had that one middle. The generate3.py docstring says their FASTQs come from one multi-sample samplesheet and sit side by side in one local FASTQ directory. So the likeliest hospital mistake, a neighbouring sample's pair, gets through the proposed check and the SIMPLEST variant. They would only catch cross-run mix-ups. Locally that means the HiSeq HG002.chr20 pair (D00360/HISEQ1, 5 flowcells) against NovaSeq A00744:46:HV3C3DSXX:2 (40x FASTQ, 35x BAM and strobealign BAM all one lane, measured).

The good news from Gate B: the hospital BAM has a single middle, so no false refusal there. The proposed falsifying test, though, only uses a pair where instrument, run and flowcell all differ. An instrument-only or lane-including comparison would pass it too, and the refutation rule checks false refusals only, never false accepts. A late wrong pair is not silent: END refuses with "found X of the N originals". The real cost is about 33-42 min of streaming (predicted) plus a re-run of fastq.sh alone. Against hours of raredisease that is a modest saving (inferred).

The proposed sample-specific deadline check costs about 10 lines of awk plus passing N_est. It is S, and it catches same-flowcell swaps. Keep the header check, if at all, only as a pre-simulation hint naming both runs.

value:M38.notes:
Value is low (2). It changes no caller call on spiked or real variants, adds no runtime, and does not touch the hospital route. That route is spike → --into-fastq/fastq.sh → raredisease, and raredisease takes the sample name from its own samplesheet; fastq.sh carries no token (MEASURED: 0 hits in B1 fastq.sh). The bundle is built and used inside the hospital, and the background is meant to be GIAB or reference material (DOCUMENTED, hospital-demo-plan.md). The B1 token is a SeraCare NA12878 LIMS ID that is already public in 4 tracked files.

The "share-safe" label is risky under the project's realism culture. If the background ever is a patient, R1/R2 are ~91% that patient's real reads (MEASURED: 228 of 2663 R1 headers start with @SPIKE_). Every kept and SPIKE_ read name also carries the input's instrument, run and flowcell (LH00352:45:227NC2LT1, MEASURED in R1.fq.gz, replaced_reads.txt and fastq_removed_reads.txt). Flowcell and run IDs are LIMS keys too. A bundle with no IDs or paths would then look de-identified while it still holds genomic personal data. A --portable/share-safe flag would mislead; a README warning is the honest fix.

Keep only the simple version:
- (a) Scripts follow the umask. One line per script: OpenOptionsExt::mode(0o777) at create time, or chmod 0o777 & !umask. Cost about 1. Impact is near zero (INFERRED): the -o directory is itself created per the umask (B1's directory is drwxrwx---), so the 0755 scripts are usually unreachable to others anyway. It is hygiene.
- (b) Warn, rather than require, when -o is the /tmp/spike default. Requiring it breaks existing invocations. A more concrete hazard, inferred from main.rs:489 (create_dir_all, no non-empty check) and not measured: a reused -o, by default the shared /tmp/spike, keeps the previous run's sim.bam/merged.bam beside the new truth.vcf and replaced_reads.txt. So warn when -o already holds spike outputs.
- (c) One README line: R1/R2 and every read name carry the input sample's real reads and run/flowcell IDs, so a bundle from a patient sample must not leave the lab whatever its labels.

Drop or defer the full --portable. Relative paths and basenames break the zero-argument `bash align.sh` / `bash merge.sh` workflow, which needs REF and the original BAM from outside -o. The SM cannot leave align.sh without changing sim.bam's @RG, and the command-line section, the ##reference header and the stderr log would all need scrubbing too. That is M work for a speculative gain.

Cost S is honest for the simple version, not for the full proposal. Nothing was built or run beyond read-only grep/samtools over B1 and the repo.

value:M39.better_measurement:
1. Settle the runtime question from data already on disk. The pipeline traces are measured: per-lane alignment takes about 1 h of wall time against about 6 h for one pair, but the whole runs take similar spans. Before anything is built, compare whole-pipeline wall time from submit to complete on comparable cluster load. Rule: pursue a split route only if splitting saves at least 3 h end to end.
2. For realism, use a noise floor instead of an identity test. Align the same whole-genome reads three ways: (A) per-lane, (B) concatenated in lane order 1..7, (C) concatenated in order 7..1. B vs C is pure batch and order noise.
3. Kill the per-lane work if both of these hold for A vs B:
   - genome-wide DeepVariant PASS genotype discordance is no larger than for B vs C;
   - at every planted event, the call (DeepVariant GT/FILTER, and Manta/TIDDIT/CNVnator presence and type within 50% reciprocal overlap) matches between A and B.
4. Do not run this on a 2 Mb region. 200k pairs is about 60 Mbp, which is one -K batch when concatenated against seven tiny batches per lane (inferred). The whole genome has about 150 batches per lane, so the region test measures a batch structure the real run never has. Run it whole-genome at the hospital as part of the raredisease runs the user does anyway.
5. Drop check (c), the chi-square on SPIKE_ reads per lane. It tests the design's own model choice, not anything a caller reads. Keep (a), (b) and (d) as file-level checks of a split step.
value:M39.notes:
VALUE (1): would anything that matters change?
- Callers: no evidence they would.
  - The pipeline's dedup is library-wide and there is no LB (measured).
  - DeepVariant uses only SM from the read group; TIDDIT, CNVnator, gCNV and ExpansionHunter ignore read groups (inferred from tool behaviour).
  - Manta keeps fragment-size statistics per read group. Seven near-identical lane distributions versus one pooled one is a negligible change (inferred).
- The only mechanical difference is bwa-mem2's insert-size estimate, which is re-learned per -K batch (documented bwa behaviour; -K is for reproducibility). Shifting the batch boundaries gives tiny differences, the same size as reordering the reads.
- SPIKE_ reads all sitting in one read group is a giveaway only to someone colouring reads by read group in IGV, and the SPIKE_ name prefix already marks them on purpose. So the proportional lane split adds no realism a caller could see.
- The trio motivation is speculative. The 6 CEPH samples were run as singletons, the mother is single-lane, trio events (M16/M17) are unbuilt ideas, and the demo plan names GIAB/demo backgrounds; the single-lane HG001/HG002 are what has been used so far.
- Runtime is the real value the idea misses. In the execution traces, the 7 BWAMEM2_MEM tasks of Seq25-16020 (343M pairs) were all submitted within about 1 min and ran 58-65 min each in parallel. The single-pair HG002 30x (369M pairs) took 6 h 06 min and HG001 30x (387M pairs) took 5 h 45 min, all at about 1140% CPU (measured).
  - The end-to-end spans are similar, though: about 16.4 h to the last task submission for 16020 against about 14 h for HG002's first trace (measured, confounded by different runs and cluster load). Whether splitting shortens a whole run is unproven.
  - If it does, the win does not need lane semantics. Splitting any spiked pair into N rows would also speed up the single-lane HG001/HG002 backgrounds.

MEASUREMENT (2): the proposed rules are not well-posed.
- "Same DeepVariant and SV VCFs" and Gate B's "identical primary records and duplicate flags" will almost surely fail from bwa-mem2 batch noise and MarkDuplicates tie-breaks. The idea would survive on noise, so a harmless layout difference would not be caught. A noise-floor comparison is needed (see better_measurement).
- The 2 Mb gate cannot represent whole-genome batching (inferred above).
- Check (c), the chi-square, measures conformance to the design, not realism.

COST (3): M is honest for the full design (lane list or samplesheet parsing, per-lane accounting, proportional naming, samplesheet writing, tests, plus validation at the hospital). Simplest worthwhile version, about S:
- keep `--into-fastq` on the concatenated pair, which already checks totals across all lanes;
- add an optional split of the output into one pair per RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE taken from each read name, an awk step like the fastq.sh filter;
- SPIKE_ reads land in their named majority lane, so check (d) holds without new naming code;
- print a samplesheet template with one row per lane.
Do even that only after the end-to-end runtime check above shows a saving.

value:M4.corrected_claims:
I re-ran phys/mateconc2.py on qtq2/k2b/{real,spike21}.bam and it reproduces the headline numbers: 35x 104 same-base sites vs 1.71 expected, 44 with both mates Q>=30; spike21 20 of 65. I then split the sites by the lower of the two mates' base quality (new script scratchpad/molerr/strat.py, about 7 s). That changes several claims:
(1) Wrong denominator. The 44 sites come from 913,655 overlapped bases where both mates are Q>=30, not from 1.05M. The rate is 4.8e-5 per base. Hospital: 141 / 1,454,067 = 9.7e-5. The two libraries differ by 2x.
(2) The 35x spectrum in the idea counts sites at every quality. 50 of the 104 sites have one mate below Q15. In that low stratum, real both-wrong positions agree on the base 71% of the time (50 same, 20 different). That fits the sequencer's biased low-Q substitution spectrum: real Q<15 top-alt share is 0.69-0.75 (phys/errproc_35x.out). It does not need molecule errors. spike draws the wrong base uniformly, and its agreement in that stratum is 0.30 (19/63).
(3) At both mates Q>=30 the 35x R1-orientation spectrum is T>C 20, A>G 5, G>T 5, C>T 4, G>A 3 out of 44. 'G>T second' does not hold at high quality, and any order past T>C is noise. Hospital at Q40/Q40: A>G 35, C>T 20, T>C 17, G>A 14, G>T 13.
(4) Molecule errors are not '~1/3' of high-Q errors, at least where mates overlap. With both mates Q>=30, shared-base positions are 49% of erroneous positions on 35x (44 of 90) and 77% on hospital (141 of 183).
(5) fastp --correction only fixes a base of Q<=14 when the other mate's base is Q>=30 (that comes from my knowledge of fastp's code, not checked here). So it cannot account for the Q40/Q40 stratum. My estimate of the shared errors fastp itself creates is about 1e-6 per base (inferred), around 1% of the sites. The hospital counts are therefore not materially confounded.
(6) New, measured: in the overlaps with both mates Q>=30, spike already makes far too many single-mate high-Q errors. 35x: real 23+23, spike21 229+241. Total erroneous mate-bases per mate-base: real 7.3e-5, spike 2.6e-4, 3.5x. Against real's unshared errors alone it is about 10x. phys/hiq_35x.out agrees: in good reads' last 10 cycles, spike 3.77e-4 vs real 9.0e-5. So the 'high-Q mismatches rise <=10%' rule compares against a spike baseline that is already 3-10x off.
(7) 'Decisive for low-VAF benchmarking' is inferred, not measured. See notes.
value:M4.better_measurement:
Run a value test before any Rust (about 2 h).
(a) Inject shared errors after the fact into the spike21 K2b FASTQ pairs. Use one rate taken from the both-mates-Q>=30 stratum and mutate both mates at the same fragment position. Re-align with bwa-mem2.
(b) On real, spike21 and spike21+injected at full depth over the 20 blocks, with Q100 sites +-5 masked, count:
  - DeepVariant-style candidates (alt>=2, AF>=0.12, alt on both strands);
  - LoFreq or Mutect2 tumor-only PASS calls per Mb.
Lock the rule first: if real and spike21 differ by no more than Poisson noise on the PASS-call count, the idea has no caller value at 30x and should not be built for the hospital use. Build only if injection closes at least half of a significant gap.
If it is built, the checks are:
  - Score per stratum, by the lower base quality of the two mates, each with its own denominator. In the both-mates-Q>=30 stratum, spike's shared-site rate must fall inside real's Poisson 95% CI (35x 44/913,655; hospital 141/1,454,067). Its shared share of erroneous positions must match real (0.49 / 0.77; master 0.00). Single-mate high-Q errors must land within +-25% of real (real 46, master 470); this is the subtraction check.
  - Test on 20 blocks that are not the startup sample's learning blocks. Learning and testing on the same blocks only reproduces the fitted number.
  - Replace the 'spectrum order' rule with a binomial test of the R1-orientation strand split (T>C vs A>G), pooled over more pairs. At n=44 the order rule cannot catch a version that mutates the fragment in reference orientation.
value:M4.notes:
Verdict: keep the gap as real, but treat the idea as low-value. Gate it behind a caller-level test before any Rust.

The gap is real and reproduced. In the overlap zone with both mates Q>=30, real reads show shared wrong bases in 49% (35x) and 77% (hospital) of erroneous positions; spike21 shows 0%.

Worth for the owner's goal (inferred from measured rates):
- **How often it happens.** Clean mode replaces the reads only inside each event's window of a few kb. The rest of the sample keeps its real shared errors. From the measured rates (35x about 88 high-Q sites per Mb at full depth, hospital about 150 per Mb), a 4 kb window would hold about 0.3-0.6 shared two-read sites.
- **Hospital germline demo.** Each such site is 2 reads (1 fragment) at AF about 0.07 at 30x. That is below DeepVariant's 0.12 candidate threshold (external knowledge), so I expect no change in PASS calls in the LDLR/raredisease demo.
- **Low-VAF benchmarking.** The effect is limited to false positives inside the windows. events.bed for an SNV covers the event's own bases, so window-restricted scoring would rarely see them. A single high-Q fragment at 30x also seems below Mutect2's TLOD 3 (my rough estimate about 2.6, inferred). Duplicate/UMI consensus value depends on features spike does not have: no UMIs, and synthetic duplicates (M7) are not built.
- So the 'decisive' impact is speculative.

Cost M is honest. The simplest build is a position-to-base overlay on the fragment, like the `alleles` map, drawn once per fragment and read by both template_at calls. Haplotype pairs need the same on their slices. Add a 12-cell R1-orientation table, and scale down the high-Q cells of the per-read error table.

Two things should come first:
- **Spike's single-mate high-Q error excess at read 3' ends** (3.5-10x real in the overlaps). It makes the subtraction step ill-posed.
- **A learned substitution table** (per Q bin x mate x read orientation) in place of uniform random_different_base (synth.rs:719). It is cheaper, it reproduces the low-Q half of the shared-base excess (71% vs 30% agreement), and it may bear on the 5x DeepVariant-candidate gap in phys/recur_35x.out. That last part is inferred: 366 of real's 453 candidates have alt reads on one strand only, while a pair shares its errors across both strands, so molecule errors cannot explain those.

value:M40.better_measurement:
**(A) Gate on change, not on absolute sameness.** For each row, record the distance to real (log-ratio, or JS divergence for spectra) over the three K2b seeds, 21/22/23, which are already on disk.
- A read-model change passes if its target row's distance shrinks by more than 3 seed SDs, and no other row's distance grows by more than 3 seed SDs.
- Run real against real with two independent hash salts, so the bands are not tested on the split that made them. Use it only to mark rows that are already at the noise floor.
- For a "could pass as some real library" scale, use the spread between libraries that is already measured: 35x against hospital, from phys/errproc_35x.out and errproc_hosp.out. Examples: Q<15 top-alt share 0.69-0.84, 15+ run slips 2.2-7.2%, R1 last-cycle ratio 1.66-2.0x.

**(B) Use mutants that v2 currently passes, so a red result means something.**
- Give both mates mate 1's quality tables; the per-mate quality rows must go red.
- Force every template to run bin 0; the K2b bin-3 clip row (11.7% against 9.9%) must go red.

**(C) Add one row a caller actually sees.**
- On real.bam and spike21/22/23.bam over the same 1 Mb, count DeepVariant-rule candidates (alt >= 2 and AF >= 0.12, which recur.py already computes) per Mb away from Q100 sites. Measured: real 500.1/Mb, spike 80.7-92.7/Mb.
- Better still, count DeepVariant or bcftools false-positive calls per Mb.
- This is template-matched, and it says whether spike's reads make calling easier, which a read-level AUC cannot.

**(D) Settings for the classifier.**
- Fix random_state: HGB's early stopping alone moved the AUC by 0.002 between refits.
- Use all 62,682 pairs and a paired bootstrap on the same reads.
- Drop TLEN and the duplicate flag. Both are identical or absent in K2b by construction: spike remakes each pair on the same template, and extract drops duplicates.
- Mask Q100 sites, and require both sets to re-align at MAPQ >= 20, because sample_input pre-selected the real reads at MAPQ 20 (survivorship).

**(E) Size the "fix the top feature" test before running it.** Dropping all three last-cycle features lowers R1 AUC only from 0.571 to 0.564, within about 1.5x the seed range (0.571-0.576). As posed, the test cannot fail reliably.
value:M40.notes:
**Value.** I score this 2. The panel changes no call by itself.
- The read-model changes it would gate (M1-M6) were each scored value 2 by their own value skeptics (journal wf_db17a130-4b0), mostly because no measurement shows them changing a call (M8 was killed).
- So a gate for them inherits that ceiling, unless it has a caller-facing row (C).
- The hospital LDLR demo succeeds or fails on calls, and those are the business of M42 and M43.
- Regressions since v2 were caught by byte-identity (the speed run), not by a realism panel.

**The falsifier as posed cannot discriminate:**
- Bands taken from a real-vs-real split within one sample measure sampling noise only. At 125k reads, v2 already fails most rows: crash z -3.89, any clip 1.33% against 1.95%, top-alt share 0.34 against 0.75, R1 Q25 0.351% against 0.184%, 181 recurrent sites against 2. v2 was merged with those rows failing, so "pre-v2 fails more" just counts two all-red boards.
- "real-vs-real passes every metric" is circular when the bands come from that same split.
- The mate-swap mutant targets a table that has no mate key, on rows v2 already fails.
- The pre-v2 anchor cannot run the K2b harness.

**Cost.** The SIMPLEST version is honestly S, about 2-3 h. Commit phys/*.py and disc.py under docs/analysis, with one runner over the existing K2b seeds and the hospital K2 folders, printing distances with seed SDs and one AUC, and no pass/fail. It runs in about 1 min (measured, 12-23 s per classifier run). The full proposal is M, not S: it needs pass bands, aligned features, K2b sets made on the hospital BAMs, a port of the harness to pre-v2, release tracking and a test on an M5 branch.

**My recommendation:**
- Build the SIMPLEST version as a regression and diagnostic report.
- Gate only with (A), (B) and (C) above.
- Keep the classifier as a regression guard only: alert if AUC rises more than 3 seed SDs.
- Do not use its feature ranking to choose work until a fix has been shown to lower the AUC beyond noise.
