7. "fastq.sh ~42 min predicted" does not appear in README or docs: unverified.
8. Confirmed by measurement:
   - The idea's GIAB-vs-DeepVariant counts reproduce exactly (scratchpad m48/): het SNV 1845/1850, het indel 402/406, hom SNV 793/794, hom indel 199/205, multi-allelic 0/29.
   - truth.vcf is plain text with sample column SAMPLE (truth.rs:205; main.rs:938).
value:M48.better_measurement:
The receipt is a reporting tool, so test it with mutant shams that a broken scorer would fail, and leave realism claims to M42 and M46.

(A) Scorer correctness, using the unspiked hospital HG002 run with GIAB v4.2.1 in chr19:10-13 Mb as truth:
- (a) ALT swap: real het SNV positions with ALT changed to another base must give <=1% called. This catches matching on position alone.
- (b) GT flip: swap het and hom in the truth. GT match must fall to <=2%. This catches a scorer that ignores GT.
- (c) Normalisation: the 29 multi-allelic records, plus a right-shifted copy of the GIAB indels that sit in repeats, must reach >=95% match after split and normalise. Exact-key matching gets 0/29 (measured), so this catches a scorer with no normalisation.
- (d) Random positions with no variant must give <=1% called.
The proposed >=99.5% / >=98.5% thresholds were set from the awk result already measured, so any exact-key join passes them. The 95% kill line cannot be reached on biallelic records.

(B) Replace Gate B. Reproducing score.py on B1-B3 is circular: it uses the same same-type, reciprocal-overlap >= 0.5 rule on n=3, so the two agree by construction. Instead, run truvari bench on GIAB T2TQ100 v1.1 DEL/DUP >= 50 bp on chr19 against the hospital svdb-merged VCF, split by svdb_origin. That gives real-variant recall per caller, which is the yardstick the receipt needs beside spiked SVs. It also tests the parsing of FOUNDBY and svdb_origin (chr19 holds 236 Manta, 276 TIDDIT, 31 CNVnator and 46 gCNV origins, measured).

(C) The realism test as proposed has a ceiling problem. I computed the binomial power (p0 miss = 0.3%, rule "fail on >=2 misses"):
- n=50: alpha 1.0%, power 26% at a 2% miss rate and 72% at 5%;
- n=100: alpha 3.7%, power 60% and 96%.
It therefore detects only gross failures, which spike validate's read-level AF check already catches upstream. The yardstick is also not matched to context: random chr19 hets are not ClinVar coding or CpG sites.
Better:
- Compare GQ, QUAL and AD-VAF (and RankResult's call-quality part) of spiked hets against real GIAB hets in the same genes or coding stratification, at matched depth.
- Most important for the demo, add a footprint diff per event between the spiked and unspiked raredisease runs: non-truth calls gained and baseline calls lost. Score it against a sham set of random footprints without events, which sets the bwa-mem2/DeepVariant noise floor (M46's sham).
value:M48.notes:
Worth: for the hospital demo it is a convenience and regression check, not new evidence. It would confirm that each spiked LDLR variant is called and reaches the clinical ranked VCF with its RankScore. But it produces nothing until a spiked raredisease run exists, and none exists yet (the full route is planned for the hospital). Its realism claims rest on call rates near the ceiling and on rank, which annotation drives.

Verdict: weaken. Build only the simplest version, and only once a spiked hospital run is scheduled:
- small variants: bcftools norm -m-any -f REF on both sides, then exact-key matching (rtg and hap.py are not installed; checked PATH and pixi envs);
- SVs: truvari bench, which is already used by transplant.py and validate_pipeline.sh (binary in ~/dev/sv_caller/.pixi/envs/default/bin);
- bcftools query for RankScore, RankResult and svdb_origin.
Write no custom SV overlap code. The truth "side fix" needs no change to spike: bgzip, tabix and `bcftools reheader -s` inside the script.

Put it in cnv_validation, per the 2026-10-05 decision, unless the owner changes it. Add the per-event footprint diff against the unspiked baseline, which is the most demo-relevant check because spurious or lost calls near a spiked LDLR variant would show in Scout. Fold it in as M46's scoring step, and leave caller-equivalence claims to M42 and M43.

Cost: about half a day for the script plus the mutant shams. The spiked raredisease run itself takes hours at the hospital, but it is the owner's planned run anyway. A local region-limited DeepVariant run is possible, but with 1.9.0 against the hospital's 1.6.1.

All measurements are in scratchpad /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/m48/ (giab.tsv, dv.tsv).

value:M49.already_done_or_refuted: Partly done, and the motivating case is answered without the new file. (1) spike validate already finds each event's own reads by name and checks they are at the breakpoints carrying the join: planted_read_prefix (src/validate.rs:384) feeds check_del_planted (src/validate.rs:1651) and check_ins_planted (src/validate.rs:1571). (2) Measured on the existing B1 run in about a minute, using only read names, sim.bam and the event coordinates: the 4845403 miss happens in the caller, not the aligner. In /home/parlar_ai/sv_slice_test/data/B1/spike/sim.bam, all 456 SPIKE_ev0001 primaries are on chr19 inside the event's +/-2 kb window, and 455/456 have MAPQ >=20. About 10 discordant pairs (TLEN 2493-2761, MAPQ 60) are present and none is duplicate-flagged in the merged slice bams/S1.bam (20 records). About 13 junction reads are soft-clipped 2-42 bp, with no SA tag. Manta FULL work/results/variants/candidateSV.vcf.gz has no candidate in chr19:11120000-11135000 except an unrelated 11 bp DEL at 11122395. So Manta never formed a candidate even though it had about 10 MAPQ-60 discordant pairs. Per-read truth would not change that attribution. RF6's cause (SA pieces on other chromosomes at MAPQ 0) was also found from SA tags alone (memory rf6-junction.md).
value:M49.corrected_claims:
- "nobody can tell whether a missed spike is an aligner misplacement or a caller miss": false. Read names already carry the event (SPIKE_ev0001_hap_NNNNNN), and validate's del_planted/ins_planted already use them. For 4845403 the attribution can be measured from existing files (above).
- "ClinVar 4845403 in hospital HG002": wrong sample. B1 was planted into the SeraCare NA12878 30x resample BAM (D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_sorted_md.bam, per /home/parlar_ai/sv_slice_test/data/B1/merge.log), not HG002.
- "harnesses rebuilt this several times (20-mer locator)": misleading. locate.py was built on purpose as an independent placer, to check SIM_ALT_FRAGS (memory independent-review-20261004.md). A TSV written from the same PairSpans code cannot replace an independent check.
- locate.py cannot run on 4845403 as it stands: it is hard-coded to CHROM='chr20' and handles only DEL and small variants (scripts/low_af/locate.py:20,34).
- The proposed mutant cannot be caught by the proposed test set. A deletion haplotype has no reverse-complemented segment: is_reverse:true appears only in from_inversion (src/haplotype.rs:316) and at :802. An off-by-one in reverse-complemented segments therefore passes on 20 DELs plus 4845403.
- "Manta misses 58% of real Alu-Alu DELs (M43)": not verified here; treat it as an unverified claim from the roadmap.
value:M49.better_measurement:
Value gate, decided before building anything: list the documented misses (4845403 Manta; RF6's 4 chr20 DELs; any M42 DeepVariant misses once they exist). Attribute each one using only names plus the BAM: the event's reads in the window, MAPQ, discordant pairs, clip/SA counts, and del_planted carriers against SIM_ALT_FRAGS. Then attribute each again with per-read truth, built offline by a throwaway locate.py generalised to any contig, or a debug print on a scratch build outside the repo. Build the TSV only if at least one attribution flips; otherwise kill.

Writer-correctness check, if built:
- Per event, the TSV's shows-ALT count must equal SIM_ALT_FRAGS exactly (same code). The independent locator must agree with it on placed pairs, and the denominator must be stated (locate.py drops unplaced pairs and pairs without exactly one forward and one reverse mate).
- The event set must include INV, INS (novel sequence), inverted DUP and a fusion, so a reverse-complement or novel-span mutant actually runs and fails.

Scorer:
- Replace "within 10 bp" with a homology-aware rule: an alignment is consistent when its reference span lies inside the true spans, shifted by up to the junction's homology length. In B1, the junction reads correctly align 20-32 bp past the breakpoint through Alu homology (e.g. 22S26M1D103M at 11129151, 26 bp before END; 121M1D30M at 11126921, ending about 32 bp past POS). A 10 bp rule would score these equivalent representations as misplaced.
- Drop the 99.9%-at-every-event kill bar. With about 20-40 junction reads per event, it requires zero misses at all 21 events, so it is practically never met and never kills. Use a per-event rule with a stated tolerance instead.
value:M49.notes:
The gap is narrow and the payoff low. No per-read file exists (PairSpans reaches only Evidence::shown_by through pairs_showing, src/simulate.rs:1111). But the outcome the idea promises — telling aligner misses from caller misses — is already reachable by name, and for the motivating 4845403 miss the answer is measured now: the miss is in the caller. Manta had about 10 MAPQ-60 discordant pairs and about 13 clipped junction reads, yet produced no candidate. The next step for that miss is Manta's own evidence (its insert-size stats and candidate thresholds in work/), not per-read truth.

Per-read truth does not touch the owner's open question, whether a real carrier would also be missed. Spike reads and real reads meet the same aligner, so knowing that spike reads were placed correctly says nothing about realism; the transplant and M43 comparisons answer that.

Costs:
- The TSV alone is honestly S, though it adds a file to the stale-output and provenance surface (M36).
- 'spike validate --alignment' is not S. It needs truth mapped to reference for split, inverted and novel mates, supplementary handling, and homology-aware tolerance: M at least.
- A cheaper version than the TSV: generalise locate.py into a standalone per-pair placer script, kept outside spike's outputs and used only when a miss can't be attributed. It also stays independent of spike's code.

Possible niche uses:
- Which planted pairs at a het small variant came from the REF copy rather than the ALT copy (other_copy is not in the name).
- Speeding up post-mortems for the hospital demo.
Neither is shown to change a call.

Numbers labelled:
- Measured: placement, MAPQ, discordant, clip and SA counts (samtools view on B1 sim.bam and bams/S1.bam), and the Manta candidate set (zcat candidateSV.vcf.gz).
- Documented: SIM_ALT_FRAGS=24, SIM_RESIST=0.007 (B1 truth.vcf); tiling of 228 pairs (B1 spike.log).
- Inferred: that Manta's thresholds, not alignment, cause the miss.

value:M5.already_done_or_refuted: Not built. The 19-bin result (0.3858 vs 0.3826 bits, quality-model-options memory) was a general refinement scored on bits, so it does not refute a terminal bin. But my measurement below refutes the idea's main impact claim: per-cycle bins cannot remove the 4.2x excess of aligned high-Q mismatches. Measured with scratchpad skeptic_lastcycle/term.py on the qtq2/k2b BAMs (clean reads = mean Q>=35; Q>=30 bases; Q100 +-5 bp masked; clipped bases placed where they would align): over the last 4 cycles spike already makes as many placed errors as real (160 vs 169). Real puts them in few reads: 24 reads have >=2 errors in the last 4, against 0.09 expected if errors were independent at the per-cycle rates. Spike has 11 such reads. Real therefore clips 251 of its 334 last-10 errors; spike clips 68 of 421. Moving the same per-cycle mass into cycle-1 / 2-4 / 5-10 bins keeps the errors as singletons. My estimate is still about 3.4x real aligned (inferred), so the idea's own +-30% rule on 9.0e-5 should FAIL.
value:M5.corrected_claims:
1) "Nothing marks the first cycles" is wrong for the quality key. The empty history slots (EMPTY, quality.rs:698-716) mark the first cycles, and spike's 5' qualities match real (measured, fqend.py): R1 low share at cycle 1 is 2.22% in both, cycle 2 1.79% vs 1.72%. It is right for the error table: error_cells has no start marker. Real clean reads have 4x spike's aligned high-Q mismatches at cycles 1-5 (119 vs 30 and 34 per ~100k clean reads; term2.py, seeds 21/22).
2) The cycle 1-5 vs 6-10 ratio over all reads (1.5x) comes from real being LOWER at 6-10 (0.057 vs spike 0.082). At 1-5 they are equal (0.085 vs 0.087; errproc_35x.out). So a 5' flag would not move that ratio the way the idea says.
3) "Spike spreads terminal errors" is right across reads, not across cycles. Spike's flat per-cycle rate is a smaller effect than missing clumps.
4) The 5' 1-4 bp clip gap is confounded. 43% of real 5' short clips (55 of 128) and 30% of 3' ones have a Q100 record within ~14 bp, against 8-11% for spike. K2b builds spike's reads on reference templates, so spike cannot make these clips.
5) The trimmed-read problem is mostly not fragment-cut reads. On the hospital 20-block BAM (phys/hosp_blocks.bam, MAPQ>=20 primary): 61.0% of reads are 151 bp, 2.6% are cut to their fragment, and 36% are 147-150 bp after adapter-prefix trimming (150 bp: 58,662 reads; full-length forward reads end in A at 0.03%). For those, generation already runs on physical cycles (generate 151, then trim_adapter_start, synth.rs:147). Learning uses qual.len() (quality.rs:737, 1023), so learning and generation already disagree today.
6) The physical last-cycle dip is confirmed on the hospital BAM. Full reads: R1 low share 2.27% at cycle 151 vs 1.58% at 150; R2 2.72% vs 1.83%. The last base of 150-bp reads shows no dip (1.53% / 1.59%). A last-cycle bin learned from qual.len() would therefore be about 39% diluted.
7) The 272 count is unverified: phys/learnmask2.py output was not saved. The M40 classifier claim is also unverified.
value:M5.better_measurement:
Split the work and test each part on what it controls.
(A) Quality key: last-cycle position plus physical cycles_left = read_length - c in count_read and block_errors (and in generation for fragment-cut reads). Metric: the excess low share at physical cycle 151 over cycle 150, per mate. Real values: 35x R1 5.76-4.17 = 1.59 points, R2 1.78 (K2b FASTQs, fqend.py); hospital R1 0.69, R2 0.89 (full-length reads). Pass if spike is within +-25% of real on both BAMs, and the last base of 150-bp hospital reads stays within 0.15 points of physical cycle 150. Master gives about 0 (spike21 R1 3.95 vs 4.05) and fails. A qual.len() version gives about 58% of the hospital excess and fails too. The hospital set must include trimmed reads: measure_clip_share currently drops every pair with insert < rl or a read != rl (synth.rs:2759), and the 35x library is all 151 bp. Use 3 seeds.
(B) Error table: report the placed (aligned + clipped, Q100-masked) high-Q error rate per cycles_left in clean reads. Real rises from about 2.8e-4 at cycles 7-10 to 5.0-5.3e-4 at cycles 1-2; spike is flat at about 4.5e-4. Report the aligned/placed split as well, and do not claim the aligned 4.2x.
(C) Clumping as its own target in a separate idea, for example an 'error in the last 3 bases' context: reads with >=2 high-Q errors in the last 4 cycles, real 3.3e-4 (24 of 72,708) vs spike 1.4e-4. Counts are small, so pool seeds 21-23 and use a Poisson interval.
(D) Drop the 5' 1-4 bp clip criterion, or mask Q100 and use reference templates on both sides. Use aligned high-Q mismatches at cycles 1-5 of clean reads instead (real 119 vs spike about 32).
(E) Gate B should report the share of cycle-1 bases whose full error cell reaches 200 bases. The backoff from the full cell to the mid cell drops the end dimension entirely (quality.rs:900-904), so thin terminal cells lose the effect silently.
value:M5.notes:
The last-cycle quality dip is real and missing from spike. It is cheap to fix, but nothing shows it changes a call. Recommendation: weaken to the quality-key last-cycle bin plus physical cycles_left. Drop the claims about the aligned high-Q mismatch excess and 5' clips.

Measured, scripts in /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/skeptic_lastcycle/ (term.py, term2.py, fqend.py, about 10 s each):
- 35x K2b last cycle: R1 mean Q 34.53 vs 35.16 at the next-to-last cycle and low share 5.76% vs 4.17%; spike is flat at 35.23 / 3.95%. R2 is 7.46% vs 5.68%; spike 5.66%.
- Hospital: the dip sits at physical cycle 151 only.

Why the main impact claim fails: the 4.2x excess of aligned high-Q mismatches in the last 10 cycles of clean reads is a clumping gap, not a gap in the per-cycle rate. Bins redistribute errors over cycles; the clipping comes from how errors gather within reads.

The excess in that cell is the smaller part of spike's aligned high-Q mismatch excess. From hiq_35x.out: class 30-35 reads at cycles 61-200 from the 3' end err at 3.20e-4 vs 1.28e-4; mean Q<30 reads at 3.31e-3 vs 1.46e-3. Summed over all cells that is about 1,140 extra errors outside the clean terminal cell, against about 270 inside it.

Value for outcomes (inferred): no caller outcome found to depend on this.
- The extra errors are random-allele singletons, at roughly 1.4e-5 per base, far below what forms a call.
- raredisease calls SNVs with DeepVariant without BQSR, and as far as I know DeepVariant's pileup carries no cycle channel.
- For the LDLR demo this is invisible to calls; it matters only to a read-level realism check or classifier.

Cost: the code is small. END_BINS or the position value in keys(), the cycles_left source in count_read, block_errors and generate_from_template, roughly 20 lines. Output bytes change, so K1, K2, K2b, K7 and the mutant runs need redoing (about half a day to a day under the project's gates); hence cost 2, not 1.

Risks the idea misses:
- The 36% adapter-prefix-trimmed reads are already handled inconsistently between learning and generation, as described above.
- Five conjunctive pass rules, one of which (the aligned last-10 rate) the mechanism cannot meet, guarantee a FAIL that would hide the part that works. Lock the quality part on its own measurement.

value:M6.already_done_or_refuted: Nothing in the case file or the notes refutes a dead-tail onset state directly. The notes record "an explicit bad-tail process: not tested" (quality-model-options-20261006); the refuted neighbours are the 4-class hidden chain, 12 finer classes and lows at every level. My measurements below refute two of the idea's supporting claims: its premise (where the high-Q errors sit) and its crash-share target. They also put the expected payoff at a small share of the excess. The per-read part of the idea also partly exists already: the read class is drawn once per read, jointly for mates (quality.rs draw_classes), and keys both the quality table (keys, L696-731) and the error table (error_cells, L908-921). Its bottom bins are the 1% and 3% quantiles of read mean quality, which already pick out the reads that crash. ERR_WINDOW=30 with bins 0/1/2-3/4+ is a self-exciting memory that keeps a burst going once it starts. What is missing is only the onset cycle.
value:M6.corrected_claims:
1) "Spike learns about the right number of high-Q errors but puts them in the wrong reads": WRONG. On K2b's same templates, under spike's own counting rule (aligned bases plus bad-end clips; Q100 +-5 bp masked; reads with no indel in the CIGAR, primary, MAPQ>=20, proper pair), spike21 has 4,839 counted Q>=30 errors against real's 3,811 (2.82e-4 vs 2.28e-4 per base, 1.27x). On variant-free templates (no Q100 record within the read +-10 bp) it is 3,684 vs 2,793 (1.32x). MEASURED: scratchpad deadtail_check/where_hiq.py and where_hiq_strat.py on qtq2/k2b/real.bam and spike21.bam.
2) "More than half of high-Q errors sit in the clipped tails of crashing reads": WRONG. Of real's 3,811 counted Q>=30 errors, 1,988 (52%) are aligned. Only 617 (16%) sit in clipped tails of crashed reads (10+ of the last 20 qualities below Q15). The other 1,206 (32%) sit in clipped ends of reads whose quality never crashed. Of those 1,206, 359 (30%) are at clip boundaries within 20 bp of a Q100 record (crashed-read control: 40/617, 6.5%), and 323 (27%) at boundaries shared by 3 or more same-strand reads; together 498 (41%), likely the sample's own variants or site effects rather than sequencing tails. MEASURED: deadtail_check/clip_nature.py. The 53% (2,226/4,202) from learnmask.py is the clipped share over all reads, not over crashing reads.
3) "Crashing ~15% too rarely" as a dead-tail residual: MISATTRIBUTED. Crash share split by what lies under the read (primary, MAPQ>=20):
- no Q100 record: real 0.83% vs spike21 0.78% (z -1.35), spike22 0.82% (z -0.48)
- an SNV only: 0.61% vs 0.63% and 0.57%
- a Q100 indel (6,663 reads): 5.73% vs 3.61% (z -5.81) and 3.37% (z -6.56)
The indel stratum holds about 150 of the roughly 200 missing crashed reads (inferred arithmetic). MEASURED: deadtail_check/crash_by_var.py. The likely cause is that spike's K2b reads are built from the reference, and production templates carry the sample's SNPs only (loh.rs:554; documented as CR3 in docs/review/CLINICAL_SV_DESIGN_NOTES.md). A dead-tail onset drawn from P(onset | class, run, cycle) on the reference template would not reach this.
4) "v2 contexts cannot represent a read whose tail is dead from some cycle on": OVERSTATED (see above). The per-read state exists; only the onset timing is missing.
value:M6.notes:
MEASURED here (read-only Python, under 30 s each; scripts in /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/deadtail_check/; data in scratchpad qtq2/k2b, phys/blocks.tsv, GRCh38 no-alt, HG002 T2T-Q100 v1.1).

The gap is real: on variant-free templates, aligned not-crashed Q>=30 errors are 2,521 (spike21) vs 1,450 (real), 1.74x. That matches hiq.py's 1.8x.

The share a dead tail could fix is a minority:
- Within crashed reads, spike puts high-Q errors too early: aligned 180 vs 93, clipped 337 vs 505. That is the onset effect the idea describes.
- Adding the not-crashed clip deficit (745 vs 646), relocation could remove at most about 186 of the 1,158 excess aligned errors (2,701 vs 1,543), about 16%. This is INFERRED and assumes totals stay fixed; a dead/alive key could also lower the alive cells' rates, and only the Step 0 decomposition settles that.
- Most of the excess is over-generation in reads that never crash, across classes: mean Q<30 633 vs 334, 30-35 777 vs 366, >=35 1,111 vs 750. hiq.py shows the >=35 excess sits mainly in the last 10 cycles (377 vs 90 per 1e6 bases), which is M5's target.

Value to outcomes: low (INFERRED).
- An extra ~0.8e-4 of isolated, independent high-Q errors per base, in donor windows only, will not change germline DeepVariant or GATK calls at 30x.
- False positives come from recurrent errors. Spike has fewer of those than real (1.35% vs 6.27% of mismatches at recurrent sites; phys/errproc_35x.out), and this idea does not touch them.
- SV-caller clip background already matches on K2b (bad-end clips 1.23-1.27% vs 1.26%).
- Nothing links the hospital "run-free reads clip 0.26% vs 0.73%" residual to this mechanism.
- Read-level discriminators would catch cheaper tells first. Spike writes Q2 on 441 called bases where real reads put Q2 only on N (errproc_35x.out), a one-line fix with cost 1. Its low-Q substitution spectrum is uniform (top-alt share 0.34 vs 0.75 real, 0.84 hospital). It makes no homopolymer slips (0% vs 2.2% at runs of 15+).

Cheaper versions to run first:
(i) An S-sized learning-rule change in block_errors: leave out clipped ends within about 20 bp of a pileup variant or indel, or at boundaries shared by 3+ same-strand reads (the user's own conclusion: same-spot clips belong to the sample). That removes up to about 13% of the learned high-Q "errors" (498/3,811, inferred to be non-sequencing).
(ii) M5 terminal bins.
(iii) Step 0 above.

Cost L is honest, and with K1/K2/K7, speed and mutant gates it is more like L+. The speed budget is 1.18x against a 1.25x limit. Risk is high: every crash-share attempt so far has stalled at 13-15% short, and the crash residual turns out to sit at the sample's indels. Build only if Step 0 points at error-table pooling at dead tails and the hospital shows the excess.

value:M7.already_done_or_refuted: Not built and not refuted. The gap is real (measured): /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/dups/run-fix/report.txt gives a duplicate share of 55/6702 = 0.0082 within 300 bp of the 40 spiked SNVs, against 253/7025 = 0.0360 in the baseline. In that run's spiked.bam, only 2 of the 26,990 primary SPIKE_ records carry the 0x400 duplicate flag (measured, samtools view -F 0x900). The proposal's Gate B "naming question" is already settled: read-names K1b (memory read-names.md, master 50c75b6) showed that with the new names a copied SPIKE_ pair gets called optical (+1) and Picard prints 0 warnings.
value:M7.corrected_claims:
1. IMPACT "spiked regions pass duplicate QC and look like the rest of the library in MultiQC/Picard": raredisease has no per-region duplicate QC to fail. MarkDuplicates and MultiQC report whole-library numbers. Even in the dense chr20:9-13 Mb stand-in (43 events, synthetic pairs about 2.8% of 478,611 pairs), PERCENT_DUPLICATION moved only from 0.041689 to 0.040446, and the optical share stayed put: 14017/19937 = 0.703 before, 13575/19300 = 0.703 after (measured, dups/run-fix/{baseline,spiked}.metrics.txt). Across a whole genome (369M pairs) it is diluted out of sight. Inferred: 100 events at about 314 pairs each (measured mean in the stand-in) shift PERCENT_DUPLICATION in the fifth decimal. FastQC's duplication module only reads the start of the file, and fastq.sh appends SPIKE_ reads after the raw reads (main.rs ADD_SPIKE, around lines 2378-2432), so FastQC never sees them.
2. The target "optical fraction 0.596" is one run's whole-genome value, which checks out: 10,361,338 of 17,385,340 (measured, D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_sorted_md.MarkDuplicates.metrics.txt). The same sample's chr20 window gives 0.703, and other hospital runs give 0.43-0.59 (measured: Seq25-16022 0.428, 16020 0.478, 16025 0.477, 16028 0.509, 16030 0.516, D25-7403 0.510/0.586). A fixed 0.596 is the wrong yardstick for a window.
3. "Pixel distance must match raredisease's settings": the hospital runs OPTICAL_DUPLICATE_PIXEL_DISTANCE 100 (Picard's default), TAGGING_POLICY DontTag and REMOVE_DUPLICATES false (measured, the metrics header). With DontTag, optical status is never visible per read in the hospital BAM.
4. "Learn the family-size distribution": 93% of duplicate sets are pairs, 12,989,304 of 13,927,014 sets of size 2 or more (95% of optical and 94% of non-optical sets; measured, histogram in the same metrics file). One copy per pair is enough.
5. "From the donor pool": the pool never holds duplicate-flagged reads (extract.rs:876/934 filter is_duplicate). Any rate has to come from clean mode's removed-duplicates scan (origin::duplicates_of, origin.rs:997-1027), which found 638 pairs in the duplicates K2 (documented, memory duplicates.md).
6. "Same molecule errors" / "prerequisite for family-shared errors": spike has no molecule-level error model (grep for molecule/pcr/damage in src/synth.rs and src/simulate.rs finds none). PCR and optical copies would therefore be built the same way and the distinction means nothing. Also, nothing in a germline raredisease pipeline consumes family errors: no UMI consensus, and callers drop duplicates.
7. "Coverage QC that does not drop duplicates": CollectWgsMetrics in raredisease's qc_bam excludes duplicates (PCT_EXC_DUPE 0.041402, measured). From tool docs, not checked here: DeepVariant, Manta, mosdepth (default exclude flag) and GATK CollectReadCounts (gCNV) skip duplicates by default. Whether CNVnator and TIDDIT count duplicates is unverified. Even if they do, the depth shift is about d/2, roughly 2% (inferred, d = 0.047), below their bin noise and smaller than the depth gap already measured (spike 0.47 against real carriers 0.52 inside DELs, memory realism-inspection-20261006.md).
8. Risk "interaction with fastq.sh found-vs-wanted accounting" is overstated: found-vs-wanted counts only originals listed in fastq_removed_reads.txt (main.rs around 2345-2372). Copies would be SPIKE_ reads passing through ADD_SPIKE, which only checks that the R1 and R2 counts pair up.
9. The VAF arm cannot fail if copies are flagged, and the share arm already covers the unflagged case. Spike's deduplicated het alt share already differs from real (0.4715 vs 0.4964 with 0x400 excluded, measured in report.txt, cause unrelated), so "unchanged" must mean against today's spike, not against real.
10. "20 K2 events on the hospital BAM" is undefined. The existing duplicates harness is 40 SNVs + 3 DELs on chr20:9-13 Mb (scripts/duplicates/run.sh, about 4 min).
value:M7.better_measurement:
Step 0, the value test, needs no Rust and should decide whether this is ever built. Use the existing duplicates harness (scripts/duplicates/run.sh: hospital chr20:9-13 Mb stand-in, bwa-mem2 -M -K 100000000, Picard 3.3.0 with the hospital's options). Copy about 4.7% of the SPIKE_ pairs in spike's R1/R2.fq.gz with awk: same sequence and qualities, new internal name, same tile, x+50 for the optical share and a far tile for the rest. Then run DeepVariant, Manta, CNVnator and TIDDIT on the windows, with and without the copies. Locked rule: if no call, genotype, GQ or SV/CNV boundary at the 43 planted events changes, the feature stays closed. Positive control: the same copies with the 0x400 flag stripped must change CNVnator/TIDDIT read depth, proving the check can see a depth change.
If it is built anyway, three checks:
(a) Duplicate share among SPIKE_ pairs (both mates 0x400) against the share among the originals spike removed for the same events (removed kept pairs' families from origin::duplicates_of, divided by removed kept pairs). Pass if within the wider of the binomial 95% CI and +-25%. Today 2/26,990 records fails; jittered copies fail.
(b) Run Picard with TAGGING_POLICY=All for the test only. Compare the DT:Z:SQ share among SPIKE_ duplicates with the DT:Z:SQ share among the baseline's duplicates in the same windows (about 0.70 there, not 0.596). Pass within +-0.10; random-tile copies give about 0 and fail.
(c) With copies left out, every other output is md5-identical to master. This shows the run's RNG stream and the existing reads are untouched. Draw the copy decision and offsets from a hash of the internal name, as read_name.rs already does.
A whole-library optical-fraction check cannot discriminate and should be dropped. In the stand-in, broken random-tile copies would move it from 0.703 to only about 0.68 (inferred), inside +-0.10.
value:M7.notes:
Verdict kill on worth. The gap is real and measured, but no outcome that matters depends on it. Every caller and coverage QC step raredisease runs either drops duplicates or, for CNVnator and TIDDIT (unverified), would see about a 2% depth shift (inferred), below bin noise. Whole-library Picard and MultiQC numbers cannot show it at the hospital's scale. FastQC never sees SPIKE_ reads, which fastq.sh appends at the end. A local "duplicate depletion" giveaway is moot because SPIKE_ names mark the reads by the owner's design (memory read-names.md). The idea concedes "effect on calls small". The "prerequisite for family-shared errors" has no consumer and no molecule-error model to share.
Cost is honest at M for the full version. But it changes output bytes and the RNG stream, which breaks the byte-identical gates every later change leans on (quality-speed B1, K0 etc.), unless decisions come from a name hash.
If the owner wants it anyway under model-what-really-happens, the simplest faithful version is a per-event replay: rate = removed families' duplicate pairs / removed kept pairs, from the existing clean-mode scan. Use one copy per pair (93% of real sets are pairs). The optical share comes from the removed duplicates' own tile:x:y distance to their representative at Picard's 100 px box. Copies get the same tile and x/y offset at most 100; non-optical copies get another tile. Run step 0 first. Key files checked: src/read_name.rs:146-161, src/synth.rs:414-439, src/simulate.rs:1000-1090, src/origin.rs:982-1054, src/extract.rs:876/934, src/main.rs:2345-2432, hospital metrics at /home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results/alignment/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_sorted_md.MarkDuplicates.metrics.txt, and the stand-in run at /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/dups/run-fix/.

value:M8.already_done_or_refuted: Not built and not refuted. But its value case falls apart once you check what each downstream tool actually reads, and the same pattern already decided GC bias: measured small, left alone. The idea's own "tell" argument also runs against an owner decision. Per memory read-names.md (2026-10-04), the user said "simulated reads must be distinguishable, but all tools must work", and every synthetic read is deliberately named SPIKE_<internal>:<RUN:FLOWCELL:LANE>:tile:x:y. Hiding spike's reads from a classifier is not a goal. The goal is that tools treat them as real, and no tool in raredisease reads where a fragment starts.
value:M8.corrected_claims:
1. The gap is real and reproduces (measured; scratchpad skeptic_motif/tell.py on qtq2/k2v2). Sample reads: n=227,383, cycle 1 A .182 C .337 G .291 T .190. SPIKE_ reads: n=9,541, cycle 1 A .271 C .226 G .222 T .281. SPIKE_ matches the sample's own background at cycles 46 and 51 (A .276 C .226 G .224 T .273).

2. Wrong: "the SIMPLEST version (3 bases each side) fits its cycle 1-6 gate". The bias runs to cycle 10 (measured): cycle 4 A .308, cycle 6 A .322, cycle 7 T .320, cycle 9 T .300, cycle 10 A .302, flat from cycles 11-12 on. That fits Tn5's 9-bp target. A 3-base PWM leaves cycles 4-6 at background, about A .27, so it fails its own ±0.02 gate there (inferred). The same signature is in the whole-genome FastQC of both mates (measured; .../raredisease_results/fastqc/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_LNUMBER1/*_fastqc.zip). R1 cycle 1 is C .317 G .276, R2 is C .313 G .281, and cycle 6 A is .342 in R1 and .339 in R2. So it covers the whole library and both ends.

3. Wrong: "FastQC per-base content would see it". raredisease runs FastQC on the whole FASTQ: 380,000,000 reads per mate (measured, fastqc_data.txt) and 741.9 M mapped reads (measured, idxstats). spike adds about 434 reads per event (9,541 over 22 events, measured), so 100 events are about 6e-5 of the FASTQ. That moves cycle-1 C by about 1e-5 (inferred). The real sample already FAILs "Per base sequence content" for this exact reason (summary.txt, measured), so no module status can change.

4. Overstated: "a per-read tell a classifier would see". A PWM learned on the even K2 events and tested on the odd ones separates sample from SPIKE_ reads with AUC 0.591 using cycle 1 only and 0.624 using cycles 1-15 (measured). That is weak, and the names already say SPIKE_.

5. Misattributed: "the duplicate structure differs". The duplicate gap comes from PCR and optical duplicates. At the 22 K2 events, 3.84% of sample reads are flagged duplicate (9,112 of 236,961, measured). SPIKE_ reads have none (aa1 spiked.bam: 0 of 432, measured). The motif only raises same-start coincidences, by about E[w^2]^2 = 1.49 on a baseline of order 1e-4 (inferred from the measured PWM, assuming independent positions). It barely touches duplicates. Base-pair-scale depth variance rises by about 2% (inferred), well below what any caller notices.

6. Overstated: "rejection sampling costs speed". Acceptance is 1/w_max^2: 0.069 with a 10-cycle PWM on both ends, 0.29 with 3 cycles (inferred from the measured composition). A rejected draw costs a few RNG calls and no read synthesis, so the slowdown is negligible (inferred). The real cost: the RNG stream changes, so every clean-mode output changes and the byte-identical proofs used in past speed work are lost.

7. Gate B ("about 1 h") is already answered, and it passes by construction. Held out by event, mean log-likelihood ratio is +0.135 nats per sample read vs -0.086 per SPIKE_ read (measured, a few minutes of CPU). It shows the bias exists. It cannot show the fix is worth anything.
value:M8.better_measurement:
Run a value gate before building, since the proposed gate is a fit-to-target check. It tests whether the sampler reproduces the composition it was trained on, so a correct sampler passes by construction and no result changes. The checks below cost minutes or are pure arithmetic.

(V1) Run FastQC and fastp on the hospital FASTQ with and without spike (fastq.sh / --into-fastq, about 100 events). Kill the idea if every module status matches and per-base content agrees within 1e-4 at cycles 1-10. Predicted to match from the read fraction alone.

(V2) Find an outcome that depends on where reads start. At SNV/indel sites, compare ReadPosRankSum and DeepVariant GQ/VAF between spiked variants and real look-alike variants moved in from HG001 (the transplant method). Build only if spiked and real differ there, and a motif-weighted prototype, simulated offline in Python on the same haplotypes, closes the gap.

If it is built anyway:
- Learn the PWM on the read's own strand over cycles 1-10, both mates, from bam_stats' first 50k records. Use cycles 40-60 of the same reads as background, so no reference lookup is needed.
- Test held out by region, at the 22 hospital K2 events.
- Pass rule: every base at cycles 1-10, R1 and R2 separately, within ±0.02 of the sample reads (SE about 0.005 at n≈9.5k).
- Broken versions that must fail: reference-strand weighting (the pattern shows mirrored on reverse reads), weighting only one end (R2 stays flat while FastQC shows R1 equal to R2), a 3-cycle PWM (fails cycles 4-6), and master.
value:M8.notes:
Verdict: kill as a build item. Record it in the map as "measured, real, left alone", the same way GC bias was handled.

Why the value is about 1:
- Nothing in raredisease uses the composition of a read's first cycles or the motif at fragment starts: not bwa-mem2, Picard, the callers or fastp.
- Whole-FASTQ FastQC is unaffected, because spike's reads are about 1e-6 of the FASTQ per event and the real sample already FAILs that module for this reason.
- The per-read tell is weak (AUC 0.62) and moot, because the owner deliberately names the reads SPIKE_.
- Start-site structure barely matters: about 1.5x coincidental duplicates on roughly 1e-4, and about 2% more base-pair-scale depth variance (both inferred).
- The idea itself says the effect on variant calls is likely small.

A gap that may be more valuable: real reads at the events carry 3.84% marked PCR/optical duplicates and SPIKE_ reads carry none (measured). Whether that matters depends on whether spike's tiling budget counts depth after duplicate removal. That is worth one check (inferred, not verified here), and the motif would not fix it.

If in-read edit/remap (M10/M21) becomes the default path, real starts come along for free for most reads. That is another reason not to spend M effort here.

Measurements and paths:
- Script: /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/skeptic_motif/tell.py, run on /tmp/claude-1066/-home-parlar-ai-dev-spike/23a35c29-9600-4da2-a2c9-618425a1e0d3/scratchpad/qtq2/k2v2. It gives the composition for cycles 1-15, 46 and 51, and the held-out AUC.
- FastQC of the hospital sample: /home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results/fastqc/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_LNUMBER1/.
- Duplicate counts: samtools view -F 0x900 -q 20 on each event's base.bam.
- Code: start draws at /home/parlar_ai/dev/spike/src/simulate.rs:1043 (breakpoint zone) and :1064 (uniform), plus sample_ref_overlapping_start at :926 for novel sequence. All three are uniform, as the idea says.

value:M9.already_done_or_refuted: Not built and not refuted. Related work already exists. (1) Trimmed libraries already get sub-read-length fragments: master 3684f74 (memory read-length-fix) added SimConfig::min_fragment_len = 1 when trimmed, at types.rs:211, synth.rs:128 and simulate.rs:987, and FragmentDist::from_read_pairs is called with it at main.rs:1930. So the floor is already wired up, and lowering it for untrimmed libraries is a two-line change. (2) spike's realism tests already work around this gap. The K2b held-out clip test keeps only TLEN >= 151 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md:225-230). The soft-clip classifier puts adapter clips in their own group and masks them from model scoring (docs/analysis/soft-clips/README.md; .claude/judgment-gate-cases.md:335-339). So no current measurement is skewed by the missing adapter clips.
value:M9.corrected_claims:
1. Where "0.83% of proper R1 pairs in chr20:10-11 Mb" came from. The 0.83% in the docs is a different count: 38 of 4,595 donor pairs in the del:chr20:38412500-38422500 pool (docs/review/REVIEW.md:3313). I measured chr20:10-11 Mb directly and got the same number. With `samtools view -f 0x42 -F 0xD04 data/validation/hg002_novaseq_chr20.bam chr20:10000000-11000000`, 1,083 of 130,402 primary, non-duplicate proper R1 reads have |TLEN| < 151 (0.831%). Only 0.473% have |TLEN| < 140 (11 or more adapter bases), and 0.042% have |TLEN| < 100. All 617 R1 reads with TLEN < 140 are 151 bp long, and 614 (99.5%) are soft-clipped. So the library really is untrimmed and the read-through really is clipped (measured).
2. The 0.71% adapter-clip share is defined by the classifier. It comes from a different region (chr20:38.5-40.2 Mb, README), and the same analysis gave 0.48% on its first pass (judgment-gate-cases.md:338). The proposed +-25% band (0.53-0.89%) is narrower than that revision. It is only valid if real and synthetic reads go through the identical classifier on the identical blocks.
3. "Output bytes change for untrimmed inputs only" is true but understates the cost. The untrimmed 35x BAM is the main development dataset. Two of the three byte-identity cases in the quality-speed B1 gate are 35x runs (memory quality-speed-run.md:24). A fragment CDF with more entries shifts the random draws, so every 35x seed-based baseline and earlier comparison has to be redone.
4. "Their absence makes spiked windows cleaner for SV callers' clip evidence" has not been measured. My own rough arithmetic (inferred): adapter-clip ends within +-5 bp of a breakpoint come to about 0.0071 x (35/151 read starts per bp) x 10 bp, roughly 0.02 reads. Callers need 2 or more clustered split reads. Common callers also deliberately ignore read-through: GATK HC clips adapter bases using insert size, DeepVariant ignores soft-clipped bases, and Manta/Strelka treat bases past a short fragment's end as adapter. Those are from the tools' documented behaviour; I did not check them here.
5. The owner's pipeline removes real adapters anyway. raredisease runs `fastp --detect_adapter_for_pe` (memory hospital-demo-plan), so even an untrimmed input would have its real adapters trimmed before alignment. The only difference that would remain is the 0.83% of short read pairs.
6. A misfire risk the idea does not mention. bam_stats calls a library trimmed only when fewer than 5% of its full-length reads end in A (bam_stats.rs:31-37, 237). A library trimmed only by software (fastp, cutadapt) has short-fragment reads cut to TLEN, while its full-length reads end in A at the normal base rate, so it is classified untrimmed (inferred). The SIMPLEST version, hard-coded TruSeq, would then add adapter that the real reads do not have. Today's behaviour (no adapter) is the safe failure.
value:M9.better_measurement:
Step 0 (no spike code; decides whether this is worth anything). Make a real-data counterfactual on the 35x chr20 BAM: remove every |TLEN| < 151 pair, or cut its reads to TLEN and realign. Then rerun Manta and one small-variant caller (DeepVariant or GATK HC) on chr20 against GIAB truth, both the original and the counterfactual. Fix the rule in advance: if no Manta call of 50 bp or more changes and the small-variant F1 moves by less than 0.001 / counting noise, the gap has no effect a caller can see. The idea then stays parked as a README limitation note. This is the strongest version of what spike's windows are missing, so a null result here covers the windows too.
Step 1 (only if Step 0 shows calls change, or the user puts adapter clips in scope). Run K2b without the TLEN filter, with the same classifier and the same blocks for real and synthetic reads. Pass rules: (a) adapter-clip share |z| < 3 against the same held-out pairs; (b) for each mate, the clipped-base consensus agrees with the real per-mate consensus at >= 0.9 over the first 33 bp, with R1 clips spelling AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCA and R2 clips AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGT; (c) clip lengths binned 1-5 / 6-20 / 21-50 / >50 within counting noise. Controls that must fail: random bases appended (passes a share-only test), the two mates' adapters swapped (also passes a share-only test), and the floor lowered with no adapter.
Step 2. Software-trimmed control. On a BAM whose short-pair reads were cut to TLEN, as fastp would, spike must add no adapter, and short fragments must be cut the way trimmed mode cuts them.
Step 3. Hospital output byte-identical to master.
Drop the "|TLEN|<151 within +-0.2 points" gate, or only report it. It passes by construction: the CDF is the pool's own lengths, and in the K2b design positions are copied from real pairs. A broken build that omits the adapter would pass it too.
value:M9.notes:
The gap is real and confirmed in the code. In untrimmed mode, mate_length (synth.rs:138-142) refuses fragments shorter than the read length, and min_fragment_len / SimConfig::min_fragment_len hold the floor at the read length. On the 35x BAM the real short pairs make up 0.831% (measured) and carry clipped TruSeq read-through.

The value is low.
- The hospital LDLR/raredisease demo is not affected: that library is sequencer-trimmed (documented, K0 in read-length-fix), and raredisease runs fastp, which removes real adapters even from untrimmed inputs.
- All of the owner's caller-outcome work (SV slices, transplant rounds) uses the trimmed hospital BAMs.
- Adapter read-through is exactly what callers are built to ignore (inferred from tool behaviour). The clip noise near a breakpoint works out to about 0.02 reads (inferred arithmetic).
- spike's own realism measurements already mask adapter clips, so nothing in the current evidence base is skewed.
- The user leaned toward modelling bad ends only (memory soft-clip-causes).
- What remains is realism for GIAB-style untrimmed users who align without trimming, plus closing about 0.7 points of the cosmetic any-clip gap (1.95% real vs 1.33-1.37% spike in K2b; 2.75% real in the slice).

The cost is honestly M, but the risk sits somewhere other than the idea says. The floor is already wired through (types.rs:211, main.rs:1930, simulate.rs:987), so the code is a learner plus the adapter append. The real costs are:
- re-baselining every 35x byte-identity case and seed comparison;
- the software-trimmed misfire: bam_stats would call a fastp-only library untrimmed, and the hard-coded TruSeq "simplest" version would add adapter where there is none.

A simpler version that also holds up better: learn each mate's tail only from short pairs whose reads are actually longer than TLEN, with no hard-coded adapter. If no read-through is seen, fall back to trimmed-mode truncation. That covers sequencer-trimmed, software-trimmed and untrimmed libraries with one rule.

Recommendation: weaken to "park, with a README limitation note, plus the Step 0 counterfactual on real data". Ask the user before any code, as the idea itself says.

ideas.title: C1 Large-DUP realism round from real carriers in the hospital's own CEPH-1463 runs, before spike is used to fill the empty DUP bands of the SV validation
ideas.problem: No yardstick covers spike's DUPs of 300 bp or more. The transplant stops at DUP 50-299, and that class was still inconclusive in round 3. Yet DUPs of 1-5 kb and exon size are where the hospital's own SV validation has no usable truth, so they are where spike is most likely to be used. If spiked DUPs are called much more easily than real ones, a DUP band filled with spiked events would overstate sensitivity, in the very report spike is meant to support.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED. The hospital SV report (/home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/analytical_performance_report_sv.md:202-204) gives raredisease DUP recall 0.008 [0.002-0.030] for 1-5 kb on 240 pooled truth events, and marks 5-10 kb (n=14) and 10-50 kb (n=6) as 'otillräcklig evidens'. cnv_validation/config/config.yaml:517 says the study 'cannot meaningfully measure duplication detection in the size range clinical reporting is concerned with'. The transplant scope excludes DUPs of 300 bp or more (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-transplant-round2.md:179-185), and round 3 left DUP50-299 inconclusive (rho 2.12 forward, 2.81 reverse). MEASURED HERE: the Platinum Pedigree truth with tandem repeats excluded (/home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/from_rv/storage/userdata/cnv_validation/refdata/merged_hg38.svs.TRexclusion.dup_split.vcf.gz) holds 688 <DUP> records of 1-50 kb, none of them 5 kb or longer. Of these, 535 have at least one carrier and one non-carrier among NA12877/78/79/81/82/85/86, and 668 have two or more carriers, so a real-vs-real comparison is possible. The same lab's raredisease outputs for the 7 CEPH members (call_sv, rank_and_filter) are local under from_rv/raredisease_fix-gatk-cnv/Seq25-160xx. Their BAMs are not (only the .bai files). The same lab's HG002 BAM is local.
ideas.proposal: A round-4 transplant for tandem DUPs of 1-5 kb, judged at two levels. (1) Caller level, which can run here. Plant truth DUPs that HG002 lacks (checked against Q100) into the local hospital HG002 BAM with spike's full DUP model, then merge. Run raredisease's SV callers: Manta and TIDDIT, plus CNVnator and gCNV only on whole-BAM runs, since slices were refuted for them. For each DUP, compare call or no-call, type and breakpoint offset with the real carriers' own raredisease SV VCFs. Real-vs-real is two carriers of the same DUP. (2) Read level, at the hospital, where the CEPH BAMs are. Use round 1b's J/E1 metrics on carriers against spiked non-carrier relatives (same lab, shared haplotypes), with B1 (af 0.25) and B2 (200 bp shift) controls and the round-3 rho rule. Only if this is supported, plan a spiked DUP set for the report's empty 5-50 kb bands. INFERRED Wilson arithmetic: when every event is detected, a band needs n of at least 16 to clear a 0.80 lower bound.
ideas.simplest_version: Take 20 truth DUPs: 1-5 kb, not in a tandem repeat, outside segdups, called in at least one carrier, and absent from HG002 Q100. Make one spike run at af=0.5 into the hospital HG002 BAM, run merge.sh, and run Manta with --callRegions on the full merged BAM. The output is a 20-row table: was the spiked DUP called, and was it called in the carriers' raredisease SV VCF?
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Kill the round if fewer than 20 DUPs pass the selection. Also kill it if, in the 20-event pilot, the B1 and B2 arms cannot be told apart from the normal arm (every rho interval crosses 2.25, as with round 3's DUP50-299). Kill the premise that spike's large DUPs need work if the spiked call rate equals the carriers' rate within the carrier-vs-carrier spread, for example if both sit near the report's 0.008.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: About two hours, read-only. Apply the selection filters to the TRexclusion truth VCF. Then look up each selected DUP in the 7 carriers' local raredisease SV VCFs (bcftools or awk, with a 500 bp / reciprocal-overlap window). This gives n and the real carriers' call rate: the target spike must match.
ideas.impact: The hospital's SV validation can use spike to fill its DUP bands only if spiked DUPs are as hard to call as real ones. This measurement licenses that use or forbids it. It is also the first realism evidence for spike's full-DUP model, its CR2 depth fold and the split reads of its DUPs.
ideas.risks: The truth DUPs are long-read INS calls rewritten as tandem DUPs (config.yaml:517), and some may be mistyped. The hospital HG002 run and the CEPH runs differ in run and library. Merging a whole BAM is slow (merge.sh takes 1 h 42 min; M22 would help). The read-level part needs the CEPH BAMs at the hospital. Libraries from one lab may share biases: that is the point for the hospital, but it limits generality.
ideas.history_check: Never proposed. Transplant rounds 1b, 2b and 3 covered only DEL 50 bp-10 kb and DUP 50-299. M42 is DeepVariant on short DUPs, M43 is Manta on DELs, and M46 compares spiked with unspiked runs and has no real carriers. Slices were refuted for Manta and CNVnator (sv-caller-slices memory; cnv_validation 4bd707b), so the caller part must use whole merged BAMs.

ideas.title: C2 dup_planted / inv_planted / bnd_planted rows, after measuring split_reads on real DUPs and INVs (the RF14 analogue)
ideas.problem: For DUP, INV and BND, validate still decides with split_reads: at least 2 primary reads whose SA tag names the partner within 500 bp. That is a rule about what the aligner writes, and it has never been measured on real variants of these types. The same rule failed most real DELs, which is why DEL moved to del_planted. Correctly spiked DUPs and INVs may therefore FAIL validate, a false alarm before a long raredisease run. Or they may pass without carrying the event. An INV's strand is never checked.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED. The comment at src/validate.rs:579-583 reads 'DUP, INV and BND were not measured and are unchanged'. split_reads is advisory only when sv_type == DEL (validate.rs:619). The realism probe found split_reads failing 12 of 20 and 9 of 15 real DELs (docs/review/REVIEW.md:5570-5583). The SA parser reads only the contig and the position (validate.rs:3383-3394), and the each-end row is blind at 500 bp or less. del_planted's design and kill tests (validate.rs:1651-1711; README.md:949-959) gave 33 of 33 correct, 0 of 330 wrong truths and 0 of 200 empty sites. MEASURED HERE: the Platinum truth holds 46 <INV> records genome-wide (TRexclusion dup_split VCF).
ideas.proposal: Step 1, the RF14 analogue. Write spike-format truth for real HG002 tandem DUPs (round2.dup_candidates gives the INS records that copy the reference beside them) and for real INVs. Run spike validate --json on HG002's own BAM and count the split_reads FAILs. Step 2, only if real variants fail. Add gating rows dup_planted, inv_planted and bnd_planted. They look for SPIKE_evNNNN_hap_ reads that carry the haplotype's own junctions (VariantHaplotype::junctions, src/haplotype.rs:581-587, the same junctions SIM_ALT_FRAGS uses), with strand-aware probes for INV and fusion joins. split_reads then becomes advisory for every type.
ideas.simplest_version: dup_planted only: the tandem copy-copy probe ref[E-15,E)+ref[S,S+16), using del_planted's matcher (at most 2 mismatches), as a gating row. INV and BND come later.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: If split_reads passes at least 90% of real HG002 DUPs of 300 bp or more and of the real INVs, against 8/20 and 6/15 for real DELs, the current gating is adequate and no planted row is needed.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Extend scripts/realism_probe.py to DUP and INV records and run spike validate --json on the 35x HG002 BAM: a few hours, with no spike code changes.
ideas.impact: Gives a correct pass or fail for exon DUPs and inversions, both demo targets, before a 20 h raredisease run. It closes the last gating rows that were never measured on real variants.
ideas.risks: In tandem arrays the copy-copy junction is spelled by the reference. RF14 found 9-10 of 12 such joins for DELs, and there the row shows presence, not removal. Real INVs are few. Kill tests must be drawn from real SV sites, not random spots (the RF8 lesson).
ideas.history_check: RF13 and RF14 did this for INS and DEL, each supported after one refuted attempt. RF6's junction probes built from the reference were refuted twice; the planted rows avoid that by reading only SPIKE_ reads. The validation map's OPEN list names '*_planted rows for DUP, INV and BND', but no idea in M1-M49 carries it. M49 is per-read truth plus an alignment scorer, not a validate row.

ideas.title: C3 Size the read-model gap on the hospital library itself (K2b on the hospital BAM, plus a 5'/3' attribution) before choosing among M1-M9; close the fastp double-pass item with existing data
ideas.problem: The hospital library is the one the demo will use, but its read realism rests on one narrow test: K2 on 22 events, which passed at z -2.64 with the shortfall in reads that have no long run. The large held-out K2b test was run on 35x only. Nine read-model ideas (M1-M9) compete for build time, and most were sized on 35x. The open question of whether fastp's second pass over spike's reads matters is also still unanswered.
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED. v2 plan, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-quality-model-v2.md:294-306. Hospital K2: bad-end clips 0.94% vs 1.38%; by run bin, spike 0.26/0.13/0.50/8.62% vs the sample's own 0.73/0.98/0.95/8.16%. The crashed share already matches (1.49% vs 1.48%), so the clip gap is not a crash gap. Mismatches per 100 aligned bases: 0.270 vs 0.308. K2b (:308) was run on the 35x BAM only (1.23-1.27% vs 1.26%). MEASURED HERE from the hospital run's own fastp report (/home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/from_rv/raredisease_seracare_na12878_resample/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results/trimming/D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_LNUMBER1.fastp.json): corrected_bases 13,917,960 of 113,421,578,824 (0.0123%), low_quality_reads 19,711,250 of 760,000,000 (2.59%), too_short_reads 1,463,236 (0.19%).
ideas.proposal: (1) Run docs/analysis/quality-model-v2/k2b.sh on the hospital BAM, with held-out pairs split by even/odd hash, for 3 seeds. (2) Attribute any gap with Q100 and the SeraCare variants masked. Split bad-end clips by end (5'/3'), clip length, mate and cycle, and check for each split which mechanism it points to: Q>=30 mismatches inside the clipped stretch (M6), the wrong-base identity (M2), first and last cycles (M5), one-letter runs (M3). (3) Rank M1-M9 by the share of the hospital gap each mechanism can reach. (4) Close the fastp item. 0.0123% corrected bases is under the open list's 0.5% bar. Check only that fastp's quality filter (more than 40% of bases below Q15) drops SPIKE_ pairs at a rate near that of BAM-eligible real pairs.
ideas.simplest_version: k2b.sh with the BAM path swapped, plus one extra table that splits bad-end clips into 5' and 3' ends.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Kill if hospital K2b puts spike within |z|<2 of real in every run bin over 3 seeds. That would mean K2's run-bin-0 gap was small-sample noise from 22 events and the hospital library has no read-model gap of its own. M1-M9 would then be ranked on the 35x evidence, and the attribution step is dropped.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: One k2b.sh run on the local hospital BAM: about 120k sampled pairs, with bwa-mem2 on about 60k held-out pairs. Under an hour.
ideas.impact: Decides which of M1-M9, if any, matters for the library the owner will actually use, which may save several M-sized builds. It also closes an open hospital-route item with data already on disk.
ideas.risks: The hospital BAM is post-fastp, with the worst 2.59% of reads removed, so 'real' is the filtered set. That is consistent with what spike trains on, but it is not the raw FASTQ. The SeraCare variants must be masked (see C7). Held-out pairs from 20 blocks are not the event regions: K2b's real share was 1.26% against 1.40% in the gate.
ideas.history_check: K2 and K2b are in the v2 plan. The read-model map lists 'split K2's bad-end clips by 5' vs 3' end and by clip length' as an unrun cheap diagnostic. The quality-model-run memory lists 'hospital run-free reads clip 0.26% vs 0.73%' as still off. The fastp question is open in the outputs map ('if it is under about 0.5%, leave it alone'). None of this is in M1-M49; M44 re-runs the existing yardsticks and has no hospital K2b.

ideas.title: C4 RF8 tells users to lower --min-mapq: measure what that does in camouflaged clinical genes, then reword the refusal
ideas.problem: When RF8 refuses an event, its message says that lowering --min-mapq lets spike edit the reads. In segmental duplications this turns a refusal into a silently wrong edit. Clean mode removes the MAPQ-0 reads that bwa placed at the event, which are a random mix of molecules from both paralogs, and keeps the ones placed at the paralog. A hom DEL would then read about 0x at the event and full depth at the paralog, where in reality each would show about half (INFERRED). The exons RF8 refuses are exactly the camouflaged clinical genes.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED HERE. Sample: 400 random PanelApp signed-off green exons (/home/parlar_ai/dev/cnv_validation/resources/clinical/panelapp_signedoff_green_exons_grch38p14_20260901.bed.gz, drawn with awk srand(7)) on the hospital HG002 BAM. Measure: the share of primary non-duplicate reads that are not MAPQ>=20 proper pairs. Pooled it is 1.41%; it is above 0.10 in 5 exons, above 0.25 in 3 and above 0.5 in 1. Those five are PRODH in LCR22 (1.000), OCLN in the chr5 SMA-region segdup (0.374), TMEM231 (0.349), OPN1LW (0.158) and CYP21A2 (0.106) (scratchpad critic/exons400b.counts). DOCUMENTED: the message is at src/census.rs:233-236. 6 of 20 real HG002 DELs are above 0.5, and 5 of those 6 drop below it at --min-mapq 0 (memory rf8-refusal.md).
ideas.proposal: Measure the advice at real camouflaged loci first. Then reword the refusal for the case where most resistant reads are MAPQ 0 with XA hits to a paralog. It should say that in clean mode lowering --min-mapq misplaces the edit, name --edit-model origin as the experimental alternative, and have truth.vcf and the README record any --min-mapq below 20.
ideas.simplest_version: In the census, count the resistant reads that are MAPQ 0 with an XA tag. When they are the majority, drop the '--min-mapq' hint from the refusal message.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Plant an af=1 DEL of one CYP21A2 exon into HG002, and the 5 RF8-refused validate_pipeline DELs into NA18488, at --min-mapq 0 with --allow-resistant. Measure the depth ratio inside the event and at its XA paralog (CYP21A1P) in original minus replaced_reads plus sim.bam. Kill if the event and the paralog both land within 0.1 of the physical expectation, about 0.5 each for a hom DEL in one of two identical copies, because the advice would then be sound.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: One spike run on the local whole-genome 35x HG002 BAM plus align.sh. Count depth at the two loci with samtools, from the original minus the replaced names plus sim.bam, without running merge.sh. About an hour.
ideas.impact: Protects clinical demos in camouflaged genes (CYP21A2 for CAH, the SMA region, LCR22, the opsins) from a silent misplacement that spike itself recommends. The code change is tiny.
ideas.risks: origin is validated only in the exact-twin regime, so pointing users at it may swap one wrong edit for another. For Alu-flanked LDLR SVs the effect may be small, because Alus are diverged. The physical expectation for diverged paralogs depends on how bwa places reads.
ideas.history_check: RF8 (c0c9614) wrote this message. The donor-handling map lists 'RF8 message ... probably wrong inside segdups' as OPEN. It is not in M1-M49: M20 (SMN) tests origin, not the clean-mode advice.

ideas.title: C5 A hospital-installable spike: CI, a static commit-named binary, an offline build path and a tool preflight
ideas.problem: The end goal is to run spike on a hospital host, but there is no release artefact, no CI, no pinned toolchain and no tool check. The generated scripts depend on GNU mv -T, realpath -m, mkfifo, samtools view -N, bwa-mem2 and pigz or gzip, and check none of them before a whole-sample stream that runs for tens of minutes. Hospital hosts are often cut off from crates.io.
ideas.evidence: MEASURED: git ls-files shows Cargo.lock but no .github/, no rust-toolchain and no container file. All dependencies in Cargo.toml are pure Rust (noodles 0.88, flate2, rayon, clap, rand 0.8, anyhow, log, env_logger; 97 packages in Cargo.lock), so a static musl build should work (INFERRED). src/main.rs:2439 uses 'mv -f -T', :2257 'realpath -m' and :2403 mkfifo, with no version checks. The hospital BAM's @PG shows raredisease's tools: bwa-mem2 2.2.1, samtools 1.19.2 and Picard MarkDuplicates 3.3.0. DOCUMENTED: 'No CI workflow or pinned Rust toolchain is present' (docs/review/2026-10-04-independent-review.md:142). Binaries are tracked by renaming them by commit by hand (spike-bdd568a in the sv_slice_test log). A flaky merge-script test was seen once (memory rf13-ins-planted.md).
ideas.proposal: GitHub Actions on the public repo: cargo test --locked on Rust 1.82 and on stable, clippy, and a static x86_64-unknown-linux-musl binary named by commit and published on tags with its SHA256. Add a cargo vendor tarball for offline builds. Add `spike --check-tools`, or a preflight at the top of fastq.sh and merge.sh, that checks the external tools and features the scripts use. Add one tiny end-to-end fixture to the tracked data.
ideas.simplest_version: One workflow file that runs the tests and uploads a musl binary artifact, plus a README paragraph on installing at the hospital.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Drop the packaging half, keeping CI only, if the hospital host already builds with `cargo build --release --locked` (with network access or vendored crates) and has GNU coreutils, a samtools with -N, bwa-mem2 and pigz.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: Ten minutes on the hospital host: rustc -V; cargo fetch --locked; samtools --version; bwa-mem2 version; pigz -V; mv --version | head -1.
ideas.impact: Removes the practical blocker to the owner's end goal and makes runs reproducible across the hospital and the dev machine. It pairs with M36's commit stamp.
ideas.risks: CI on a public repo must never touch hospital data or paths. Only 37 data files are tracked, so tests that need untracked BAMs must be gated before CI is green. musl's allocator may slow the rayon-heavy steps, which needs measuring.
ideas.history_check: This is architecture debt the independent review named and nobody acted on. M36 covers provenance (a commit-stamped version), not distribution, CI or a tool preflight. It is not in M1-M49.

ideas.title: C6 Explain R_c < 1 in transplant round 3 (test the split-half noise estimator) to unlock its unsure cells for small insertions and DUPs
ideas.problem: Round 3 left 11 of 16 cells inconclusive. Six of them are spike's own rho intervals crossing 2.25, pushed up by R_c, real-vs-real mismatch over counting noise, being below 1 at DUP J, INS20-49 A and INS1-4 A. Two independent samples should not agree better than counting noise. That they do suggests the split-half estimator overstates the noise for these metrics. Until this is explained, the yardstick cannot clear spike's small insertions and duplications, which are common pathogenic forms (for example the small dups in LDLR).
ideas.evidence: DOCUMENTED: round 3 plan, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-transplant-round3.md:222-232: R_c 0.61 (DUP J), 0.50 (INS20-49 A) and 0.69 (INS1-4 A); split-half calibration 1.2165; mate double-counting labelled 'an inference'. split_noise is the mean of (x0-x1)^2/4 over salts (scripts/transplant/round3.py:74-77). MEASURED HERE on round 3's evidence3.tsv (session scratchpad round3/run): splitting each group's shared sites by their noise v, R_c in the low-v and high-v halves is DUP50-299 J 1.18 vs 0.47, INS1-4 A 1.08 vs 0.47, INS20-49 A 0.83 vs 0.45 and SNV A 1.22 vs 0.65. Caveat: splitting on the estimated v also selects for that estimate's own errors (regression to the mean), so this only points at the estimator; it does not prove the bias.
ideas.proposal: Test the estimator directly. For each shared site, read its fragment count N and carrier count from the BAM. Monte Carlo the metric at full and at half depth, drawing binomially over fragments with the 1.2165 overdispersion, and compare E[split-half v] with the true full-depth variance. If it is biased, switch to a full-depth fragment bootstrap (pairs resampled with replacement at full N) or an analytic beta-binomial. Then recompute R_f, R_c, rho and the B1/B2 controls, and re-judge the unsure cells under a re-analysis plan locked on the SNV calibration before the run.
ideas.simplest_version: The Monte Carlo on the INS20-49 A and DUP50-299 J shared sites only, with N read from the round-2b BAMs.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Kill if the Monte Carlo bias factor E[v]/Var at the observed N is 1.1 or less for DUP J, INS20-49 A and INS1-4 A. Explaining R_c of 0.50-0.69 would need about 1.5-2.0. The estimator would then not be the cause, and the work moves to how the shared sites are selected.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: A few hours: recount N per shared site from the round-2b BAMs with small_evidence.py, then run a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo in Python.
ideas.impact: May turn the inconclusive INS1-4, INS5-19, INS20-49 and DUP50-299 cells into verdicts without any new spike runs. Small insertions and dups are what an LDLR demo plants most.
ideas.risks: rho = R_f/R_c may not move if the bias hits fake and real sites alike. Re-judging after seeing data breaks the judgment gate unless the new estimator is locked on the SNV calibration first. The round-2b reads must still exist.
ideas.history_check: R_c < 1 was noted after round 2b and again in round 3, and never explained. M45 (the power ladder) deals with broken controls, not with the noise estimator. It is not in M1-M49.

ideas.title: C7 The hospital's 'HG002' is a SeraCare inherited-cancer mix: write its background truth before any truth-based score or demo receipt
ideas.problem: The hospital's HG002 demo and validation background is not plain GIAB HG002. It is a SeraCare inherited-cancer reference mix (sample name GM24385_seracare_cancer) that carries engineered pathogenic variants. Any truth-based score of a spiked run on it will count those variants as false positives or as background damage: background integrity (M41), composite truth (M47) and the per-variant demo receipt (M48). A 'spike LDLR' demo would also show pathogenic cancer-gene variants that spike never planted. And a planted event whose footprint covers one of them would erase it on the event copy (CR3).
ideas.evidence: MEASURED HERE. The hospital's unspiked DeepVariant calls (.../D24-14230_Seq25-7600_30x_resample/raredisease_results/call_snv/genome/GM24385_seracare_cancer_snv.vcf.gz) hold chr17:43124027 ACT>A (BRCA1 c.68_69del, 185delAG) at GT 0/1, AD 38,31, GQ 43. Neither HG002 Q100 v1.1 nor v4.2.1 (data/giab_hg38/HG002/) has a record in chr17:43124000-43124060. On chr20 there are 743 hospital calls with GQ>=30 that Q100 lacks. Their VAF deciles are 0/1/2/42/149/153/86/9/4/297, with no low-VAF excess, so the sample is not a genome-wide blend and the engineered variants are local. DOCUMENTED: the round 1 transplant plan names Seq25-7600 'SeraCare inherited-cancer mix' (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-transplant-round1.md:14). A crude grep finds 230 records containing 'pathogenic' in the unspiked ranked clinical VCF.
ideas.proposal: Build the background truth for each hospital background once: Q100 (or v4.2.1) plus the vendor's variant manifest, with each manifest variant confirmed in the unspiked raredisease calls. Ship it as a VCF/BED that M41, M47 and M48 read. At spike time, warn when an event footprint (±2 kb) covers a manifest variant: carried.rs only catches small variants at the same site, and CR3 erases non-SNP variants on the event copy. Document in the demo notes what the unspiked sample already shows.
ideas.simplest_version: A one-page list: the unspiked raredisease calls with GQ>=30 in PanelApp green exons that Q100 lacks, checked by hand against the SeraCare manifest.
ideas.falsifying_measurement: Kill if the unspiked hospital calls absent from Q100 (VAF 0.3-0.7, GQ>=30, inside PanelApp green exons genome-wide) are, apart from the BRCA1 site, no more than DeepVariant's usual false-positive count there. Estimate that count from chr20, where 743 non-Q100 calls is the baseline. If so, nothing needs curating and a one-line note suffices.
ideas.cheapest_gate_b: An hour: bcftools isec of the unspiked hospital calls against Q100 restricted to PanelApp green exons. List the excess calls and match them to the vendor manifest.
ideas.impact: Keeps every truth-based yardstick on the hospital background honest and the demo story clean, and stops a planted event from silently erasing a SeraCare variant in its footprint.
ideas.risks: Getting the vendor manifest may need the purchase documents. Whether the HG001 background (Seq25-7598) is also a mix is unknown. DeepVariant's false positives differ between libraries, which blurs the excess count.
ideas.history_check: Not raised in the owner's notes or in the panel; the map calls these 'hospital HG001/HG002 30x'. M41, M47 and M48 all assume GIAB truth as the background.
